chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

إذا انقطع الدم على النفساء عاد الخلاف في التلفيق فلو طهرت خمسة عشر
يوما ثم عاد الدم ففي العائد وجهان أحدهما أنه نفاس لوقوعه في الستين
والثاني أنه حيض
قال الصيدلاني هذا الخلاف فيه إذا لم يجاوز العائد ستين فإن جاوز قطعنا
بأنه حيض

### | التفريع

إن قلنا إن العائد نفاس ورأينا ترك التلفيق فالأشهر أن مدة النقاء حيض
وإن بلغ خمسة عشر
ومنهم من قال تستثنى هذه الصورة على قول السحب إذ يبعد تقدير مدة كاملة
في الطهر حيضا
وعليه يخرج ما إذا ولدت ولم تر الدم إلى الخمسة عشر في أن الدم الواقع في
الستين هل هو نفاس أم لا والله أعلم
= كتاب الصلاة = وفيه سبعة أبواب
قال الله تعالى {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة} وقال النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس وقال الصلاة عماد الدين فمن تركها فقد هدم الدين
وافتراض الصلوات الخمس مجمع عليها
وقد كان التهجد بالليل واجبا في ابتداء الإسلام فنسخ إلا في حق رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم
والنظر في الصلاة تحصره أبواب
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في المواقيت وفيه ثلاثة فصول - صلى
الله عليه وسلم -

### | الفصل الأول في وقت الرفاهية للصلوات الخمس

والأصل فيه ما رواه ابن عباس عنه عليه السلام أنه قال أمني جبريل عليه
السلام عند باب البيت مرتين فصلى بي الظهر حين زالت الشمس وصلى بي العصر
حين كان ظل كل شئ مثله وصلى بي المغرب حين أفطر الصائم
وصلى بي العشاء حين غاب الشفق وصلى بي الفجر حين حرم الطعام والشراب على
الصائم ثم عاد فصلى بي الظهر حين صار ظل كل شئ مثله وصلى بي العصر حين صار
ظل كل شئ مثليه وصلى بي المغرب كصلاته بالأمس وصلى بي العشاء حين ذهب ثلث
الليل وصلى بي الصبح حين كاد حاجب الشمس يطلع ثم قال يا محمد الوقت ما بين
هذين
فنبدأ بصلاة الظهر تأسيا بجبريل عليه السلام ويدخل وقتها بالزوال وهو
عبارة عن ظهور زيادة الظل في جانب المشرق بعد تراجعه من جانب المغرب فإذا
صار ظل الشخص مثله من موضع الزيادة خرج وقت الظهر ودخل وقت العصر وتمادى
إلى غروب قرص الشمس
وللظهر وقتان وقت الفضيلة وهو أوله ووقت الاختيار بعد ذلك إلى آخره
وللعصر أربعة أوقات وقت الفضيلة في الأول ووقت الاختيار بعده إلى أن يصير
الظل مثليه
وهو  منتهى بيان جبريل ووقت الجواز بعده إلى الاصفرار ووقت الكراهية عند
الاصفرار
ودليل الزيادة على بيان جبريل قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام من أدرك ركعة من
الصبح قبل أن تطلع الشمس فقد أدرك الصبح ومن أدرك ركعة من العصر قبل أن
تغرب الشمس فقد أدرك العصر
وذهب الإصطخري إلى أن الوقت لا يزيد على بيان جبريل
فإن قيل صلى جبريل العصر في اليوم الأول حين صلى فيها الظهر في اليوم
الثاني فليثبت اشتراك بين الوقتين
قلنا ذهب مالك إلى أن مقدار أربع ركعات مشترك
وحمل الشافعي رضي الله عنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى العصر على انطباق
ابتدائه في المثل الأول وقوله صلى الظهر على انطباق التحلل عليه كما يقال
بلغ البلد إذا دخلها وبلغ إذا قاربها
فأما المغرب فيدخل وقته بغروب الشمس ويعلم في قلل الجبال بإقبال الظلام
وانهزام الضوء وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا أقبل الليل من هاهنا وأدبر
النهار من هاهنا فقد أفطر الصائم وأشار إلى المشرق والمغرب
ثم في وقت المغرب قولان
أحدهما أنه يمتد إلى غروب الشفق وإليه ذهب أحمد بن حنبل لما روي أنه عليه
الصلاة والسلام صلى المغرب عند اشتباك النجوم
والثاني أنه إذا مضى بعد الغروب وقت وضوء وأذان وإقامة وقدر خمس ركعات
فقد انقضى الوقت لأن جبريل صلى في اليومين في وقت واحد وعلى هذا لا بأس
بتناول لقمة أو لقمتين
يسكن بها سورة الجوع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Childbirth; the blood of parturition (dam al-nifās); also "precious/valuable" (nafīs) — the woman in confinement is nufasā'.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Nifās as a juristic category distinct from ḥayḍ (menstruation) — a blood-discharge whose ruling is tied to the 60-day maximum post-partum window.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the act of giving birth. Metaphorical extension: the legal status of the bleeding following delivery, treated as a distinct temporal limit.
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cleanliness, purity; the state of being free from ritual impurity (ṭahārah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭuhr as the interval of purity between two blood discharges — a legally significant "gap" (naqā') that may or may not interrupt the continuity of nifās.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical cleanliness. Metaphorical: the legal presumption that purity continues unless blood returns.
- Root: و-ق-ت (w-q-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A fixed measure of time; a term or deadline (mīqāt).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divinely appointed boundaries for ritual prayer — waqt al-faḍīlah (time of excellence), waqt al-ikhtiyār (time of choice), waqt al-jawāz (time of permissibility), waqt al-karāhah (time of disapproval).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a measured duration. Metaphorical: the legal "window" defined by the angel Gabriel's demonstration — a boundary set by revelation, not by human estimation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Recurring Subject (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — When the protasis (e.g., "if the blood returns") is repeated with a new condition, the apodosis carries a fresh legal ruling, requiring careful parsing of the particle "fa" to distinguish result from continuation.
chapters.translation:
I say — and God knows best:

### | Branch

If the bleeding ceases for a woman in postpartum confinement (nufasā'), the disagreement regarding "piecing together" (talafīq) returns. So if she becomes pure for fifteen days, then the blood returns, there are two views (wajhān) concerning the returning blood: one is that it is postpartum bleeding (nifās), because it occurs within the sixty [days]; the second is that it is menstruation (ḥayḍ).

Al-Ṣaydalānī said: This disagreement applies only if the returning [blood] does not exceed sixty [days total]. If it exceeds [sixty], we rule definitively that it is menstruation.

### | Ramification

If we say that the returning [blood] is nifās, and we adopt the view of abandoning talafīq, then the more famous position (al-ashhar) is that the period of purity is [counted as] menstruation, even if it reaches fifteen [days].

And among them is one who said: This particular case is excepted on the view of "withdrawal" (al-saḥb), for it is improbable to reckon a complete duration within the purity as menstruation.

And upon this [second view] is based the case of a woman who gives birth and does not see blood until the fifteenth [day] — whether the blood occurring within the sixty [days] is nifās or not. And God knows best.

= The Book of Prayer (Kitāb al-Ṣalāh) = And it contains seven chapters.

God Most High said: {«And establish prayer and give zakāh»} (Q 2:43). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five [pillars]." And he said: "Prayer is the pillar of the religion; whoever abandons it has demolished the religion." The obligation of the five prayers is a matter of consensus (ijmāʿ).

And indeed, night vigil prayer (tahajjud) was obligatory at the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated (naskh) — except in the case of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.

The examination of prayer is encompassed by chapters.

— Peace and blessings be upon him — Chapter One: On the Times (al-Mawāqīt). It contains three sections. — Peace and blessings be upon him —

### | Section One: On the Time of Excellence (waqt al-rāḥah) for the Five Prayers

The foundational proof for this is what Ibn ʿAbbās narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, led me in prayer at the Gate of the House [the Kaʿbah] twice. He prayed the Ẓuhr with me when the sun had passed its zenith (zawāl); he prayed the ʿAṣr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to its length; he prayed the Maghrib with me when the fasting person breaks his fast; he prayed the ʿIshā' with me when the twilight (shafaq) had disappeared; and he prayed the Fajr with me when food and drink became forbidden to the fasting person. Then he returned [the next day] and prayed the Ẓuhr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to its length; he prayed the ʿAṣr with me when the shadow of everything was twice its length; he prayed the Maghrib with me as he had prayed it the previous day; he prayed the ʿIshā' with me when one-third of the night had passed; and he prayed the Ṣubḥ with me when the edge of the sun was nearly rising. Then he said: 'O Muhammad, the time is between these two [limits].'"

So we begin with the Ẓuhr prayer, following the example of Gabriel, peace be upon him. Its time enters with the zawāl, which is the appearance of the increase of the shadow on the eastern side after its retreat from the western side. When the shadow of a person becomes equal to his length, measured from the point of increase, the time of Ẓuhr exits and the time of ʿAṣr enters, and it continues until the setting of the solar disk.

The Ẓuhr has two times: the time of excellence (waqt al-faḍīlah), which is its beginning, and the time of choice (waqt al-ikhtiyār) after that until its end.

The ʿAṣr has four times: the time of excellence at its beginning; the time of choice after that until the shadow becomes twice [the object's length] — and this is the limit of Gabriel's demonstration; the time of permissibility (waqt al-jawāz) after that until yellowing [of the sun]; and the time of disapproval (waqt al-karāhah) at yellowing.

The proof for the extension beyond Gabriel's demonstration is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever catches one rakʿah of the Ṣubḥ before the sun rises has caught the Ṣubḥ; and whoever catches one rakʿah of the ʿAṣr before the sun sets has caught the ʿAṣr."

Al-Iṣṭakhrī held the view that the time does not extend beyond Gabriel's demonstration.

If it is said: Gabriel prayed the ʿAṣr on the first day at the same time at which he prayed the Ẓuhr on the second day — so let a shared [portion] between the two times be established.

We say: Mālik held that the measure of four rakʿahs is shared [between them].

And al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, interpreted his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "he prayed the ʿAṣr" as referring to the coincidence of its beginning with the first [day's] equality [of shadow], and his saying "he prayed the Ẓuhr" as referring to the coincidence of its completion (taḥallul) — just as one says "he reached the city" when he enters it, and "he reached [it]" when he approaches it.

As for the Maghrib, its time enters with the setting of the sun, and it is known in the mountain peaks by the advance of darkness and the retreat of light. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: "When the night advances from here, and the day retreats from here, the fasting person has broken his fast" — and he pointed to the east and the west.

Then concerning the time of Maghrib there are two positions (qawlān):

One: that it extends until the disappearance of the twilight (shafaq) — and this is the view of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, due to what was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the Maghrib when the stars were intertwined [thick in the sky].

The second: that when there has passed after sunset the time of an ablution (wuḍū'), an adhān, an iqāmah, and the measure of five rakʿahs, the time has elapsed — because Gabriel prayed on both days at one and the same time. And upon this [view], there is no harm in taking one or two morsels by which the pang of hunger is quieted.

chapters.title_en: Section 33 — On the Expiration of Prayer Times, the Call to Prayer, and Three Foundational Rules
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو شرع في الوقت ومده حتى مضى هذا القدر فإن قلنا إن مثل هذه الصلاة
مقضية في غير المغرب ففي المغرب وجهان
أحدهما أنه مؤداة لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قرأ سورة الأعراف في
المغرب فدل أن آخره غير مقدر
فأما العشاء فيدخل وقته بغيبوبة الشفق وهي الحمرة دون الصفرة والبياض
الذى يزول بعد الحمرة ثم يمتد وقت الاختيار إلى ثلث الليل على قول لبيان
جبريل عليه السلام وإلى النصف على قول لقوله عليه الصلاة
والسلام لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم بالسواك عند  كل صلاة ولأخرت العشاء
إلى نصف الليل فيدل ذلك على الاستحباب
فأما الصبح فيدخل وقته بطلوع الفجر الصادق ويتمادى وقت اختياره إلى
الإسفار ووقت جوازه إلى الطلوع ولا نظر إلى الفجر الكاذب وهو يبدو مستطيلا
ثم ينمحق ويبدو الصادق مستطيرا ثم لا يزال الضوء يزداد قال عليه الصلاة
والسلام لا يغرنكم الفجر المستطيل وكلوا واشربوا حتى يطلع الفجر المستطير
فرع لا يقدم أذان صلاة على وقتها إلا أذان الصبح
قال سعد القرظ كان الأذان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في
الشتاء لسبع بقي من الليل وفي الصيف لنصف سبع
وقيل إذا خرج وقت اختيار العشاء دخل وقت أذان الصبح وهو بعيد
ثم الأولى أن يؤذن مؤذنان أحدهما قبل الصبح والآخر بعده
ولو اقتصر على ما قبل الصبح أجزأه

### | قواعد ثلاثة

الأولى تجب الصلاة عندنا بأول الوقت وجوبا موسعا خلافا لأبي حنيفة
ثم لو مات في أثناء الوقت قبل الأداء هل يلقى الله عاصيا فيه وجهان
ولو أدى في آخر الوقت ووقع بعضه خارج الوقت فهي مؤداة نظرا إلى ابتدائها
على وجه ومقضية نظرا إلى تمامها على وجه والواقع في الوقت مؤدى والباقي
قضاء على وجه ثالث
فإن جعلناه قضاء لم يجز التأخير إليه قصدا ولم يمتنع صحته بنية الأداء
كالمحبوس إذا اجتهد في الوقت ونوى الأداء فكان في غير الوقت لم يلزمه
الإعادة
الثانية تعجيل الصلوات في أوائل الأوقات أفضل عندنا قال عليه الصلاة
والسلام أول الوقت رضوان الله وآخره عفو
الله قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه رضوان الله أحب إلينا من عفو الله
قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه العفو يوشك أن يكون للمقصرين وحيازة فضيلة
الأولية بأن يشتغل بأسباب الصلاة كلما دخل الوقت
وقيل لا بد من بعد تقديم الأسباب حتى ينطبق التكبير على أول الوقت فهي
الأولية
وقيل تتمادى فضيلة الأولية إلى النصف من بيان جبريل عليه السلام
ويستثنى عن فضيلة التعجيل العشاء والظهر ففي العشاء قولان في قول
يستحب التأخير لقوله عليه  الصلاة والسلام لولا أن أشق على أمتي الحديث
وأما الظهر فالإبراد به مستحب في شدة الحر لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
أشتكت النار إلى ربها فقالت قد أكل بعضي بعضا فأذن لها في نفسين نفس في
الصيف ونفس في الشتاء فأشد ما تجدون في البرد من زمهريرها وأشد ما تجدون من
الحر من حرها فإذا اشتد الحر فأبردوا بالظهر فإن شدة الحر من فيح جهنم
ثم قيل إن الإبراد سنة للأمر الوارد وقيل هو
رخصة وحده أن يتمكن الماشون إلى الجماعات من المشي في الظل
واختلفوا في أنه هل يختص بالبلاد الحارة وفي أن من يمشي في كن إلى
الجماعة هل يستحب له
واختلفوا في الجمعة على وجهين وجه المنع أن فواتها خطر ولا بد من تقديم
الخطبة فالبدار أولى
الثالثة من اشتبه عليه الوقت يجتهد ويتبين ذلك بالأوراد وغيرها ثم يصلي
فإن وقع في الوقت أو بعدها فلا قضاء وإن كان قبل الوقت وأدرك الوقت صلى وإن
تبين بعد انقضاء الوقت فقولان وكذا في طلب شهر رمضان
فرع إذا أمكنه أن يصبر إلى درك اليقين ففي جواز الاجتهاد في الحال وجهان
ووجه الجواز أن عمر رضي الله عنه أفطر بالاجتهاد وغلط وكان قادرا على الصبر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-د-د (madda)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Extension, prolongation, stretching forth in time or space
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal extension of a divinely-appointed limit (waqt) as a legal capacity (tawassuʿ)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical stretching; metaphorical (majāz) for the legal extension of a time window
- Root: ش-ف-ق (shafaq)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The redness (ḥumrah) remaining on the horizon after sunset
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The twilight as a sign (ʿalāmah) demarcating the entry of ʿishāʾ
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the red glow; the yellow and white afterglow is excluded as non-indicative
- Root: س-ف-ر (safara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The spreading of light; al-isfār is the illumination of dawn
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The true dawn (al-fajr al-ṣādiq) as opposed to the false dawn (al-kādhib)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for light's diffusion; metaphorical for the legal permissibility window
- Root: ب-ر-د (barada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cooling; al-ibrād is delaying the ẓuhr prayer to the cooler part of the day
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A recommended postponement (taʾkhīr mustaḥabb) rooted in prophetic command
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for temperature; metaphorical for the legal ruling of preference
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab (Coordination on a Causal Basis) — When two clauses are joined by wa, the second may be governed by the cause implicit in the first, as in the Prophet's statement linking the siwāk command to the postponement of ʿishāʾ.
chapters.translation:
### | Sub-Branch

If one enters the time [of prayer] and prolongs it until this measure [of time] has elapsed — then if we hold that such a prayer is made up (maqḍiyyah) in other than the Maghrib, then concerning the Maghrib there are two positions (wajhān):
One of them is that it is performed in time (muʾaddāh), because of what has been related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, recited Sūrat al-Aʿrāf in the Maghrib — and this indicates that its end is not strictly delimited.

As for the ʿIshāʾ, its time enters with the disappearance of the twilight (shafaq) — and that is the redness (ḥumrah), not the yellowness nor the whiteness that vanishes after the redness. Then the time of choice (waqt al-ikhtiyār) extends to one-third of the night according to one saying, based on the declaration of Gabriel (Jibrīl), peace be upon him; and to the half according to another saying, based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Were it not that I would burden my community, I would have commanded them to use the siwāk at every prayer, and I would have delayed the ʿIshāʾ to the middle of the night» — and this indicates recommendation (istihbāb).

As for the Ṣubḥ, its time enters with the rising of the true dawn (al-fajr al-ṣādiq), and its time of choice extends to the illumination (isfār), and its time of permissibility extends to sunrise. No consideration is given to the false dawn (al-fajr al-kādhib), which appears elongated (mustaṭīlan) and then dissipates; and the true dawn appears spreading (mustaṭīran), and then the light continues to increase. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: «Let not the elongated dawn deceive you — eat and drink until the spreading dawn rises.»

### | Sub-Branch

No call to prayer (adhān) is given before its time except the adhān of the Ṣubḥ.
Saʿd al-Qaraẓ said: "The adhān in the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was in winter with seven [parts] remaining of the night, and in summer with half of seven [parts remaining]."
And it was said: when the time of choice for ʿIshāʾ exits, the time for the adhān of Ṣubḥ enters — but this is remote (baʿīd).
Then the preferable practice is that two muʾadhdhins call — one before the Ṣubḥ and the other after it. And if one confines himself to the one before the Ṣubḥ, it suffices him.

### | Three Foundational Rules

**The First:** The prayer is obligatory upon us at the beginning of its time with an expansive obligation (wujūb mūssaʿ) — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. Then if one dies during the time before performing it, is he meeting Allah as a disobedient one? — there are two positions (wajhān).
And if one performs it at the end of the time and part of it falls outside the time, then it is performed in time (muʾaddāh) with consideration to its beginning, on one view; and made up (maqḍiyyah) with consideration to its completion, on another view; and what fell within the time is performed in time, while the remainder is make-up (qaḍāʾ), on a third view.
If we deem it make-up, then delaying to it intentionally is not permissible, yet its validity with the intention of performance (niyyat al-ʾadāʾ) is not precluded — like the imprisoned one who exerts his effort (ijtihād) within the time and intends performance, and it turns out to be outside the time: he is not required to repeat.

**The Second:** Hastening the prayers at the beginnings of their times is more virtuous with us. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: «The beginning of the time is Allah's good pleasure (riḍwān), and its end is Allah's pardon (ʿafw).» Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah's good pleasure is dearer to us than Allah's pardon." Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Pardon is likely to be for the negligent." And the attainment of the virtue of precedence (faḍīlat al-awwaliyyah) is by occupying oneself with the prerequisites of prayer whenever the time enters.
And it was said: there must be a delay in presenting the prerequisites so that the takbīr coincides with the very beginning of the time — that is precedence.
And it was said: the virtue of precedence extends to the half [of the time] from the declaration of Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Excepted from the virtue of hastening are the ʿIshāʾ and the Ẓuhr. Concerning the ʿIshāʾ there are two sayings — on one saying, delay is recommended, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Were it not that I would burden my community...» — the hadith.
As for the Ẓuhr, cooling (ibrād) with it is recommended in intense heat, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «The Fire complained to its Lord and said: 'Parts of me have consumed other parts.' So He granted it two breaths — a breath in summer and a breath in winter. The most severe cold you find is from its zamharīr, and the most severe heat you find is from its heat. So when the heat is intense, cool the Ẓuhr — for intense heat is from the blast (fayḥ) of Hell.»
Then it was said: cooling is a Sunnah due to the command that has come; and it was said: it is a concession (rukhaṣah), its limit being that those walking to the congregations are able to walk in the shade.
And they differed as to whether it is specific to hot lands, and whether it is recommended for one who walks in the shade to the congregation.
And they differed concerning the Friday prayer on two views — the view of prohibition [of delay] is that missing it is perilous, and the sermon (khuṭbah) must be presented beforehand, so hastening is more appropriate.

**The Third:** For one to whom the time is ambiguous, he exerts his effort (ijtihād) and ascertains it by means of the litanies (awrād) and other things, then prays. If it falls within the time or after it, there is no make-up. If it was before the time and he caught the time [in the process], he prays. And if it becomes clear after the time has elapsed, there are two sayings. Likewise in seeking the month of Ramadan.

### | Sub-Branch

If he is able to wait until attaining certainty, then concerning the permissibility of ijtihād in the present moment there are two views. The view of permissibility is that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, broke his fast by ijtihād and erred — while he was able to wait.

chapters.title_en: Section 34 — The Second Chapter on the Time [of Prayer] for Those Possessing Valid Excuses
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في وقت أرباب الأعذار

ونعني بالعذر الجنون والصبى والحيض والكفر ولها ثلاثة أحوال
إحداها أن يخلو عنها آخر الوقت فإن بقي قبل غروب الشمس ما يسع ركعة فزال
العذر وجب العصر وفاقا ولو بقي ما يسع تكبيرة فقولان
أقيسهما وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة أنه يلزم لأن هذا القدر يتسع الإلزام
ولسنا نعتبر وقت الأداء
والثاني وهو اختيار المزني أنه لا يدركه لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام ومن
أدرك ركعة قبل غروب الشمس فقد أدرك العصر وما دونها ليس في معناها فإن مدرك
ركعة من الجمعة مدرك لها بخلاف مدرك التكبيرة هذا حكم العصر
أما الظهر فيلزم أيضا بإدراك وقت العصر لأنه وقته في حق المعذور بالسفر
وهذا العذر أشد ولكنه بكم يصير مدركا  فيه قولان
أحدهما بما يصير به مدركا للعصر
والثاني لا بد من زيادة أربع ركعات على ذلك ليتصور الفراغ من الظهر فعلا
ثم لزوم العصر بعده
وهل تعتبر مدة الوضوء مع ذلك فعلى قولين
وهذه الركعات الأربع في مقابلة الظهر أو العصر فعلى قولين مخرجين
هذا إذا زال العذر قبل أداء الصلاة فإن زال بعده وذلك يتصور في الصبي
يصلي ثم يبلغ والوقت باق فلا يلزمه القضاء خلافا لأبي حنيفة فلو صلى الظهر
فبلغ ووقت الجمعة قائم قال ابن الحداد تلزمه الجمعة وهو غلط عند الأكثرين
ومنهم من وجهه بأن الصبي مضروب على ترك حضور الجمعة والمتعدي بالظهر قبل
الجمعة لا يصح ظهره على وجه ولو بلغ الصبي بالسن في أثناء الصلاة أتمها ولو
بلغ في أثناء يوم من رمضان وهو صائم فلا قضاء عليه
ومنهم من علل بوقوعه عن الفرض
ومنهم من علل بأنه لم يدرك وقتا يتصور فيه الشروع في العبادة
وتظهر فائدة الخلاف في الصبي المفطر إذا بلغ وللعراقيين وجه أن الصبي
تلزمه إعادة الصلاة وإن بلغ بعد الأداء
الحالة الثانية أن يخلو أول الوقت فإذا طرأ الحيض فإن مضى من الوقت قبله
ما يسع الصلاة لزمته وإن كان أقل فلا بخلاف آخر الوقت فإن الشروع في آخر
الوقت يمكن إتمامه بما بعد الوقت وهاهنا لا يمكن في زمان الحيض
وخرج ابن سريج قولا إنه لا تلزمه ما لم يدرك جميع الوقت أو آخره
وأما العصر فلا يلزم بإدراك جزء من أول الظهر لأن وقت الظهر لا يصلح
للعصر ما لم يقع الفراغ من فعل الظهر بخلاف وقت العصر
وذهب أبو يحيى البلخي إلى أن أول الظهر في إدراك العصر كآخر العصر في
إدراك الظهر
الحالة الثالثة أن يعم العذر جميع الوقت فيسقط القضاء بالحيض والجنون
والكفر والصبى ولا تلتحق الردة بالكفر بل يجب القضاء على المرتد نعم الصبي
وإن لم يكن عليه قضاء ولكن يؤمر بالصلاة بعد سبع سنين ويضرب على تركها
بعد عشر سنين والإغماء  في معنى الجنون قل أو كثر
أما الشكر وزوال العقل بسبب محرم كشرب بنج أو تردية من مكان فلا يسقط
القضاء
فرع لو سكر ثم جن فالأصح أنه لا يلزمه إلا قضاء ما فاته في وقت السكر
وقيل يجب قضاء أيام الجنون لاتصاله بالسكر
ولو ارتد ثم جن يلزمه قضاء ما فات في وقت الردة وقيل يجب قضاء ما فات في
الجنون لأن حكم الردة مستمر في الجنون
ولو ارتدت أو سكرت ثم حاضت لا يلزمها قضاء أيام الحيض لأن سقوط القضاء عن
المجنون رخصة وعن الحائض عزيمة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A genuine impediment or hindrance that absolves one from obligation; an excuse that veils culpability.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divinely-recognized concession (rukhṣah) altering the normative demand of worship due to incapacity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for a physical barrier; metaphorical (majāz) for a legal dispensation excusing performance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Temporal Adverbial (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb fī al-ẓarf) — The protasis governs the apodosis via a time-marker, determining legal liability by the extent of elapsed time.
chapters.translation:
I say: By "excuse" (ʿudhr) I mean insanity, childhood, menstruation, and unbelief. These [excused persons] have three states [regarding the prayer time].

The first state: that the end of the time is free of the excuse. If there remains before sunset [enough time] to accommodate one rakʿah, and then the excuse ceases, the ʿAṣr [prayer] becomes obligatory — this by consensus. But if there remains only [enough] for a single takbīrah, there are two opinions [among the scholars]. The one I deem more sound (aqyasuhumā) — and it is the school of Abū Ḥanīfah — is that it is incumbent, because this measure suffices for the imposition of obligation (ilzām); for we do not consider the time of actual performance [but rather the time of valid obligation]. The second opinion — which is the choice of al-Muzanī — is that he does not attain [the prayer], due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«Whoever attains one rakʿah before sunset has attained the ʿAṣr»} — and what is less than that is not in its meaning; for one who attains a rakʿah of the Friday prayer attains it, unlike one who attains only the takbīrah. This is the ruling for ʿAṣr.

As for Ẓuhr, it also becomes obligatory by attaining the time of ʿAṣr, because that time is its [valid] time for the one excused by travel — and this excuse is more severe [than menstruation]. But by what [measure] does one become an attainer [of Ẓuhr]? There are two opinions: One is that he becomes an attainer by the same measure by which he attains ʿAṣr. The second is that an addition of four rakʿahs beyond that is necessary, so that the completion of Ẓuhr can be conceived as an actual act, and then the obligation of ʿAṣr follows after it. And is the duration of the ablution (wuḍūʾ) also considered along with that? There are two opinions. And these four rakʿahs — are they in exchange for Ẓuhr or for ʿAṣr? There are two opinions, derived [from two underlying principles].

This [applies] if the excuse ceases before the performance of the prayer. But if it ceases after performance — and this is conceivable in the case of a boy who prays and then reaches puberty while the time remains — then no make-up (qaḍāʾ) is incumbent upon him, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. If he prayed Ẓuhr and then reached puberty while the time of Friday [prayer] was still standing, Ibn al-Ḥaddād said: The Friday prayer becomes obligatory upon him — but this is an error according to the majority. Among them is one who justified [Ibn al-Ḥaddād's view] by [arguing] that the boy is compelled [by divine command] regarding the abandonment of attending Friday [prayer], and one who performs Ẓuhr before Friday [prayer] — his Ẓuhr is not valid in one respect. And if the boy reaches puberty by age in the midst of the prayer, he completes it. And if he reaches puberty in the midst of a day of Ramaḍān while he is fasting, no make-up is upon him. Among them is one who reasoned [this] by [the fact that] it fell upon the obligatory [act validly]. And among them is one who reasoned that he did not attain a time in which commencing the act of worship could be conceived. The benefit of this disagreement appears in the case of a boy who breaks his fast [in Ramaḍān] and then reaches puberty [mid-day]. And for the Iraqis there is a view that the boy is obligated to repeat the prayer even if he reaches puberty after performance.

The second state: that the beginning of the time is free [of the excuse], and then menstruation supervenes. If there passed from the time before it [enough] to accommodate the prayer, it becomes obligatory upon her; but if it was less, then no — unlike the end of the time, for commencing at the end of the time can be completed beyond the time, whereas here commencement is impossible during the period of menstruation. Ibn Surayj derived a view that it is not obligatory upon her unless she attains the entire time or its end. As for ʿAṣr, it does not become obligatory by attaining a part of the beginning of Ẓuhr, because the time of Ẓuhr is not suitable for ʿAṣr unless the completion of the act of Ẓuhr has occurred — unlike the time of ʿAṣr [which is suitable for Ẓuhr]. Abū Yaḥyā al-Balkhī held that the beginning of Ẓuhr, regarding the attainment of ʿAṣr, is like the end of ʿAṣr regarding the attainment of Ẓuhr.

The third state: that the excuse encompasses the entire time. Then the make-up is dropped by menstruation, insanity, unbelief, and childhood. Apostasy (riddah) is not joined to unbelief; rather, make-up is obligatory upon the apostate. Yes, the boy — even though no make-up is upon him — is nonetheless commanded to pray after seven years and is beaten for abandoning it after ten years. And unconsciousness (ighmāʾ) is in the meaning of insanity, whether little or much. As for intoxication, or the loss of reason due to a prohibited cause — such as drinking a narcotic (bunj) or throwing oneself from a high place — the make-up is not dropped.

A branch [question]: If one became intoxicated and then became insane, the most correct [view] is that only the make-up of what was missed during the time of intoxication is incumbent upon him. And it was said: The make-up of the days of insanity is obligatory, due to its contiguity with the intoxication. And if one apostatized and then became insane, the make-up of what was missed during the time of apostasy is incumbent upon him. And it was said: The make-up of what was missed during the insanity is obligatory, because the ruling of apostasy persists during the insanity. And if a woman apostatized or became intoxicated and then menstruated, the make-up of the days of menstruation is not incumbent upon her, because the dropping of make-up for the insane person is a concession (rukhṣah), whereas for the menstruating woman it is a firm determination (ʿazīmah).

chapters.title_en: Section 35: On the Disliked Times for Prayer, and the Chapter on the Call to Prayer (Adhān)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثالث في الأوقات المكروهة

وهى خمسة اثنان منها يتعلق بالفعل فهما من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لا
صلاة بعد الصبح حتى تطلع الشمس ولا بعد العصر حتى تغرب الشمس
ووجه تعليقها بالفعل أنه يتمادى بالبدار إلى الفرض في أول الوقت
ويقصر بالتأخير
وثلاث منها تتعلق بالوقت وهو وقت طلوع الشمس والاستواء والغروب قال عليه
الصلاة والسلام إن الشمس تطلع ومعها قرن الشيطان فإذا ارتفعت فارقها فإذا
استوت قارنها فإذا زالت فارقها فإذا دنت للغروب قارنها وإذا غربت فارقها
ونهى عن الصلاة في هذه الأوقات
فأما المنوط بالطلوع فمن وقت بدو إشراق الشمس إلى طلوع قرصها وقيل يمتد
إلى استيلاء سلطان الشمس لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام فإذا ارتفعت فارقها
وأما الاستواء فعبارة عن وقت وقوف الظل قبل ظهور الزيادة
أما الغروب فتدخل كراهيته باصفرار الشمس إلى تمام الغروب
ويستثنى من هذه الكراهية من الصلوات ما لها سبب ومن الأيام الجمعة ومن
البقاع مكة
أما الأول فلما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام رأى قيس بن قهد يصلي بعد
الصبح فقال ما هذا فقال ركعتا الفجر فلم ينكر ففي معناهما كل ما له سبب
كالفائتة وصلاة الجنازة وسجود التلاوة وتحية المسجد
وأما ركعتا الإحرام فيكره لأن سببها الإحرام وهو عذر متأخر وفي الاستسقاء
تردد لأن تأخيره ممكن
وأما استثناء الجمعة فلما روى أبو سعيد الخدري أنه نهى عن الصلاة نصف
النهار حتى تزول الشمس  إلا يوم الجمعة فقيل يختص ذلك بمن يغشاه النعاس
فيقصد طرده بركعتين وقيل إنه لا يختص به بل هو خاصية يوم الجمعة
فأما استثناء مكة فلما روي عن أبي ذر أنه أخذ بعضادتي الكعبة وقال من
عرفني فقد عرفني ومن لم يعرفني فأنا جندب سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم يقول لا صلاة بعد الصبح حتى تطلع الشمس ولا بعد العصر حتى تغرب الشمس
إلا بمكة ولذلك لا يكره الطواف في سائر الأوقات لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام
يا بني عبد مناف من ولي منكم من أمور الناس شيئا فلا يمنعن أحدا طاف بهذا
البيت في أي ساعة شاء من ليل أو نهار

### | قاعدة

لو تحرم بالصلاة في وقت الكراهية ففي الانعقاد وجهان
أحدهما نعم كالصلاة في الحمام والدار المغصوبة والثاني لا كصوم يوم العيد
فإن قلنا لا تنعقد لم تلزم بالنذر فأما أداء المنذورة فيها فجائز لأن
النذر سبب كالقضاء
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في الأذان - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
الأذان سنة مؤكدة وقيل إنه فرض كفاية ولو امتنع عنه أهل بلدة يقاتلون
عليه فإنه من شعائر الإسلام والصحيح أنهم لا يقاتلون لأنه سنة
والأصل فيه أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام شاور أصحابه في أمارة ينصبونها
لحضور الجماعات فذكر النار والناقوس فذكر النصارى والمجوس فتفرقوا عن غير
اتفاق رأي فقال عبد الله بن زيد الأنصاري كنت بين النائم واليقظان
إذ نزل ملك من السماء عليه ثياب خضر وبيده ناقوس فقلت أتبيع هذا الناقوس
مني فقال وما تصنع به مني فقلت أضرب به في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم فقال أو لا أدلك على خير من ذلك فقلت بلى
فاستقبل القبلة وقال الله أكبر وسرد الأذان ثم استأخر غير بعيد فأقام
فأصبحت وحكيت الرؤيا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال رؤيا صدق إن شاء
الله ألقه على بلال فإنه أندى صوتا منك فقلت ائذن لي مرة واحدة فأذنت بإذنه
فلما سمع عمر صوتي خرج يجر  رداءه وهو يقول والذي بعثك بالحق لقد رأيت مثل
ما أرى فقال الحمد لله فذاك أثبت ثم أتاه بضعة عشر من الصحابة قد رأي كلهم
مثل ذلك هذا تمهيد الباب ومقصوده يحصره ثلاثة فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ر-ه (K-R-H)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "dislike, aversion, or detestation" — that which the soul turns away from; in legal context, it denotes an act discouraged (makrūh) but not forbidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām and legal theory, karāhah signifies a divine address (khiṭāb) that recommends abstention without imposing a prohibition (taḥrīm); it is a middle category between the obligatory and the forbidden.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage (ḥaqīqah) refers to internal aversion; metaphorical usage (majāz) applies to the legal ruling that labels an act as disliked, transferring the psychological sense to a jurisprudential one.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-Istithnāʾ) — The particle "illā" (except) governs the exclusion of a noun from the scope of a general negative or affirmative predicate, as seen in the prophetic hadith "lā ṣalāta... illā bi-Makkah," where the exception restricts the universal negation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third chapter concerns the disliked times [for prayer]. They are five: two of them pertain to the act [of prayer itself], and these are derived from his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "No prayer after the dawn prayer until the sun rises, and no prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets." The reason for attaching them to the act is that one may hasten to perform the obligatory prayer at the beginning of its time, or delay it to the end; thus the prohibition is linked to the act of praying at those moments.

Three of them pertain to the time itself, namely: the time of sunrise, the time of zenith (when the sun is at its meridian), and the time of sunset. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, the sun rises and with it is the horn of Satan; when it ascends, he separates from it; when it reaches the zenith, he accompanies it; when it declines, he separates from it; when it draws near to setting, he accompanies it; and when it sets, he separates from it." And he forbade prayer during these times.

As for that which is tied to sunrise, it extends from the moment the sun's light begins to appear until the rising of its disk. And it was said: it extends until the sun's dominance prevails, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "When it ascends, he separates from it."

As for the zenith, it is an expression for the time when the shadow stands still before the appearance of its increase.

As for sunset, its dislike enters with the yellowing of the sun until the completion of its setting.

Excepted from this dislike are: from among the prayers, those which have a cause; from among the days, Friday; and from among the places, Mecca.

As for the first [exception], it is due to what was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Qays ibn Qahd praying after the dawn prayer and said: "What is this?" He replied: "The two units of the dawn prayer [i.e., its sunnah]." So he did not disapprove. And in their meaning are all prayers that have a cause, such as the make-up prayer (al-fāʾitah), the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah), the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah), and the greeting of the mosque (taḥiyyat al-masjid).

As for the two units of the iḥrām [upon entering the state of pilgrimage], they are disliked because their cause is the iḥrām itself, which is a delayed excuse [i.e., one could have prayed before entering iḥrām]. And regarding the prayer for rain (al-istisqāʾ), there is hesitation, because its delay is possible.

As for the exception of Friday, it is due to what Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated: that he forbade prayer at midday until the sun declines, except on Friday. So it was said: this is specific to one whom drowsiness overcomes, intending to repel it with two units [of prayer]. And it was said: it is not specific to him, but rather it is a distinctive property of Friday.

As for the exception of Mecca, it is due to what was narrated from Abū Dharr: that he took hold of the doorposts of the Kaʿbah and said: "Whoever knows me, knows me; and whoever does not know me, I am Jundab. I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'No prayer after the dawn prayer until the sun rises, nor after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets, except in Mecca.'" For this reason, the circumambulation (ṭawāf) is not disliked at any other time, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "O sons of ʿAbd Manāf, whoever among you is entrusted with any matter of the people's affairs, let him not prevent anyone from circumambulating this House at any hour he wishes, by night or by day."

### | Rule

If one enters into prayer during a disliked time, there are two views regarding its validity (inʿiqād):
One of them: yes, it is valid, like prayer in the bathhouse or in a usurped house.
The second: no, it is not valid, like fasting on the day of ʿĪd.
If we say it is not valid, then it is not binding by vow (nadhr). As for performing a vowed prayer within such a time, it is permissible, because the vow is a cause, like the make-up prayer.

— Peace and blessings be upon him — The Second Book: On the Call to Prayer (Adhān) — Peace and blessings be upon him —

The call to prayer (adhān) is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah). And it was said: it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). If the people of a town abstain from it, they are fought over it, for it is among the symbols of Islam (shaʿāʾir al-Islām). But the correct view is that they are not fought, because it is a sunnah.

The origin of it is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, consulted his companions regarding a sign they could establish for the gathering of the congregations. He mentioned the fire and the bell (nāqūs), and they mentioned the Christians and the Magians, so they dispersed without agreeing on a single opinion. Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī said: "I was between the sleeper and the wakeful, when an angel descended from heaven wearing green garments, with a bell in his hand. I said: 'Will you sell me this bell?' He said: 'What will you do with it?' I said: 'I will strike it in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.' He said: 'Shall I not guide you to something better than that?' I said: 'Yes.' So he faced the qiblah and said: 'Allāhu Akbar,' and he recited the adhān in sequence. Then he stepped back a short distance and made the iqāmah. So I awoke in the morning and related the vision to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: 'A true vision, if Allah wills. Dictate it to Bilāl, for he has a more penetrating voice than you.' I said: 'Permit me to give the call once.' So I called the adhān with his permission. When ʿUmar heard my voice, he came out dragging his cloak, saying: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I have seen the like of what he saw.' He said: 'Praise be to Allah, for that is more confirmed.' Then a dozen or more of the companions came to him, all of whom had seen the like of that."

This is the preamble of the book, and its purpose is encompassed by three chapters.
