chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في الركوع

وأقله أن ينحني إلى أن تنال راحتاه ركبتيه لو مدهما بالانحناء لا
بالانخناس ويطمئن بحيث ينفصل هويه عن ارتفاعه فلو زاد بالانحناء لم يحسب
ذلك بدلا عن الطمأنينة ولا يجب عندنا ذكر في الركوع خلافا لأحمد لأن الركوع
يخالف المعتاد بصورته لا كالقيام والقعود
وأما في الأكمل فهيئته أن ينحني بحيث يستوي ظهره وعنقه كالصفيحة الواحدة
وينصب ركبتيه ويضع كفيه عليهما ويترك الأصابع على جبلتها منشورة نحو القبلة
ويتجافى عند ذلك مرفقاه عن جنبيه ولا يتجاوز في
الانحناء الاستواء وإذا ابتدأ الهوي وقال الله أكبر رافعا يديه عندنا
خلافا لأبي حنيفة
ثم للشافعي رضي الله عنه قولان
أحدهما أن يمد التكبير إلى أن يستوي راكعا كيلا يخلو هويه عن الذكر
والثاني الحذف  حذارا عن التغيير بالمد وهو جار في تكبيرات الانتقالات
كلها
والذكر المشهور سبحان ربي العظيم وبحمده ثم إن كان إماما لم يزد
على ثلاث وروى أبو هريرة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يقول اللهم لك ركعت
وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت أنت ربي خشع سمعي وبصري ومخي وعظمي
وعصبي وما استقلت به قدمي لله رب العالمين

### | القول في الاعتدال

إذا رفع الرأس من الركوع رفع اليدين فيعدل قائما وقد انتهت يداه إلى
منكبيه ثم يخفض يديه بعد الاعتدال وأقله الاعتدال والطمأنينة
ويستحب أن يقول سمع الله لمن حمده عند الرفع ثم يقول ربنا لك الحمد يستوي
في الإمام والمأموم والمنفرد وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
قال ربنا لك الحمد ملء السموات وملء الأرض وملء ما شئت من شئ بعده أهل
الثناء والمجد أحق ما قال العبد كلنا لك عبد لا مانع لما أعطيت ولا معطي
لما منعت ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد فإن كان في صلاة الصبح
استحب القنوت في الركعة الأخيرة خلافا لأبي حنيفة لما روى أنس بن مالك أن
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يقنت في الصبح حتى فارق الدنيا
ثم كلماته مشهورة وهي متعينة ككلمات التشهد ثم قال العراقيون إذا نزل
بالمسلمين نازلة وأرادوا القنوت في الصلوات الخمس جاز وإن لم تنزل فقولان
وقيل إن لم تنزل لم يجز وإن نزل فقولان وهو أقرب
واختلفوا في الجهر به في الصلاة الجهرية والظاهر أن الجهر مشروع ثم إذا
جهر الإمام أمن المأموم وإن لم يسمع صوته فيؤمن أو يقرأ فيه وجهان
ثم يستحب أن يرفع يديه ويمسح بهما وجهه في آخره
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core sense is "to bow" or "to incline the head and body downward," with a secondary meaning of "to be lowly" or "to humble oneself."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual prayer (ṣalāh), rukūʿ is a prescribed posture of bodily humility (khushūʿ) symbolizing the servant's abasement before divine majesty; it is a physical act of worship (ʿibādah) distinct from mere inclination.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical bending of the torso; metaphorical (majāz) — spiritual submission or humility of the heart.
- Root: ط-م-ن (ṭ-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To be still, tranquil, at rest"; derived from ṭuma'nīnah, meaning "calmness" or "settledness."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prayer, ṭuma'nīnah is the required pause of stillness after each movement, ensuring the body is fully settled — a condition for the validity of the posture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical stillness; metaphorical — inner serenity and presence of heart in worship.
- Root: ا-ع-ت-د-ل (i-ʿ-t-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To be straight, even, balanced"; from ʿadl, meaning "justice" or "equilibrium."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prayer, iʿtidāl is the upright standing after rukūʿ, restoring the body to a state of balance and symmetry as an act of praise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical straightness; metaphorical — moral and spiritual uprightness before God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditionality (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "if he extends them by bowing, not by drawing back" (law maddahumā bil-inḥināʾ lā bil-inkhinās) employs a conditional clause where the protasis (law) sets a hypothetical condition, and the apodosis clarifies the required outcome, governing the legal ruling (ḥukm) of sufficiency.
chapters.translation:
I say: The minimum of the bowing (rukūʿ) is that one incline until his two palms reach his two knees — if he were to extend them (his arms) by bowing, not by drawing back (his body). And he must observe stillness (ṭuma'nīnah) such that his descent (into the bow) is distinct from his rising (from it). If he increases the bowing (beyond the minimum), that is not counted as a substitute for the stillness. And it is not obligatory in our school (al-Shāfiʿī) to recite any invocation (dhikr) during the bowing, contrary to Aḥmad (ibn Ḥanbal), because the bowing differs from the customary (standing posture) by its very form, unlike the standing (qiyām) and the sitting (quʿūd), which require specific recitations.

As for the most complete (form), its description is that one incline until his back and his neck become level, like a single flat board (ṣafīḥah wāḥidah). He straightens his knees, places his palms upon them, and leaves his fingers in their natural state, spread out toward the qiblah. He keeps his elbows apart from his sides (tajāfā) during that, and he does not exceed the level (of straightness) in bowing. When he begins his descent (into the bow), he says "Allāhu Akbar" while raising his hands — in our school, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

Then, for al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him), there are two opinions (qawlān):
One: that he prolongs the takbīr until he is fully settled in the bowing, so that his descent is not devoid of the remembrance (of Allāh).
The second: that he cuts it short (ḥadhf), out of caution against altering (the wording) by prolongation. And this (second opinion) applies to all the takbīrs of the transitions (in prayer).

The well-known invocation (during the bow) is: "Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent, and with His praise" (subḥāna rabbī al-ʿaẓīm wa bi-ḥamdih). Then, if he is an imam, he does not exceed three (repetitions). Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "O Allāh, to You I have bowed, and in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my marrow, my bones, and my nerves have humbled themselves — and whatever my feet carry — for Allāh, Lord of the worlds."

### On the Standing Upright (Iʿtidāl)

When he raises his head from the bowing, he raises his hands, then stands upright, and his hands have reached (the level of) his shoulders. Then he lowers his hands after the uprightness. The minimum (of this posture) is the upright standing and the stillness (ṭuma'nīnah). It is recommended (mustaḥabb) that he say, upon raising (his head), "Allāh hears the one who praises Him" (samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah), then say, "Our Lord, to You is all praise" (rabbanā laka al-ḥamd). This applies equally to the imam, the follower (maʾmūm), and the one praying alone (munfarid). It is narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Our Lord, to You is all praise, filling the heavens, filling the earth, and filling whatever You will after that. O Possessor of praise and glory, the most true thing a servant says — and we are all Your servants — none can withhold what You have given, and none can give what You have withheld, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You."

If it is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ), it is recommended to perform the supplication of qunūt in the last rakʿah, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, based on what Anas ibn Mālik narrated: that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) continued to perform qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world. Then, its words are well-known, and they are specified (muʿayyanah) like the words of the tashahhud. Then the Iraqis (i.e., the Ḥanafīs) said: If a calamity befalls the Muslims and they wish to perform qunūt in the five daily prayers, it is permissible. If no calamity has befallen, then there are two opinions (qawlān). And it was said: If no calamity has befallen, it is not permissible; and if a calamity has befallen, then there are two opinions — and this (latter view) is the more correct (aqrab). They differed regarding reciting it aloud in the audible prayers (al-ṣalāh al-jahriyyah). The apparent (view) is that reciting aloud is legislated (mashrūʿ). Then, if the imam recites aloud, the follower says "Āmīn"; but if he does not hear his voice, then there are two aspects (wajhān): whether he says "Āmīn" or recites (the qunūt himself). Then, it is recommended that he raise his hands and wipe his face with them at the end of it.

chapters.title_en: The Discourse on Prostration and Rising from It
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في السجود والاعتدال عنه

أما أقله فالكلام في الموضوع على الأرض وكيفية الوضع وهيئة الساجد
أما الموضوع فالجبهة ولا يقوم غيرها مقامها ثم يكفي أقل ما ينطلق عليه
الاسم وفي وضع اليدين والركبتين والقدمين قولان
أحدهما يجب لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة آراب
والثاني لا لأن السجود عبارة عن  وضع الجبهة ففيه تمكين أعز الأعضاء من
التراب
فإن أوجبنا فلا يجب كشف القدمين والركبتين ويجب كشف الجبهة وفي اليدين
قولان
أحدهما يجب لقول خباب بن الأرت شكونا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
حر الرمضاء في وجوهنا وأكفنا فلم يشكنا أي لم يزل شكوانا
والثاني لا يجب لأن التواضع حصل بالوضع ثم لا يكفي في الوضع الإمساس مع
إقلال الرأس بل لا بد وأن يرخي رأسه قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها رأيت رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سجوده كالخرقة البالية ثم في كشف
الجبهة يكفي أقل ما ينطلق عليه الاسم ولو سجد على طرفه أو على كور عمامته
أو طرف كمه الذى يتحرك لم يجز
أما هيئة الساجد وهو التنكس بحيث يكون أسافله أعلى من أعاليه فلو سجد على
وسادة وكان رأسه مساويا لظهره فيه وجهان لفوات التنكس
ولو كان به مرض يمنعه من التنكس فهل يجب عليه وضع وسادة ليضع الجبهة
عليها فيها وجهان أظهرهما الوجوب لأن صورة السجود بالوضع لا
بالتنكس
والطمأنينة أيضا واجبة في السجود
أما الأكمل فليكن أول ما يقع على الأرض منه ركبتاه وقال أبو حنيفة بل
يداه
ثم يستحب أن يكبر عند الهوى ولا يرفع اليد ويقول في سجوده سبحان ربي
الأعلى ثلاث مرات
ويضع الأنف على الأرض مع الجبهة مكشوفا ويفرق ركبتيه ويجافي مرفقيه عن
جنبيه بحيث يرى عفرة إبطيه ويقل بطنه عن فخذيه ويضع يديه منشورة الأصابع
على موضعهما في رفع اليدين وأصابعهما مستطيلة في جهة القبلة مضمومة ولا
يؤمر بضم الأصابع إلا هاهنا
ونقل المزني أنه يضع أصابع رجليه بحيث تكون رءوسها في قبالة القبلة
أما المرأة فتترك التخويه والتجافي في الركوع والسجود
ثم يكبر عند الاعتدال ويجلس مفترشا بين السجدتين ويضع يديه قريبا من
ركبتيه منشورة الأصابع ويقول اللهم اغفر لي واجبرني وعافني وارزقني واهدني
ويطمئن في جلوسه
ثم يسجد سجدة أخرى مثلها فإن كان يستعقب ذلك قياما فيجلس جلسة خفيفة
للاستراحة كان رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم لا ينهض حتى يستوي قاعدا
ثم يبتدئ التكبير بحيث ينتهي عند استوائه جالسا أو يستوي جالسا ثم ينهض
مبكرا إلى القيام فيه خلاف
ثم كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام في صلاته وضع يديه على
الأرض كما يضع
العاجن
فرع إذا خر الهاوي إلى السجود على وجهه اعتد به لأن الهوي غير
مقصود وإن خر على جنبه واستد على قصد السجود اعتد به وإن قصد
الاستقامة وصرف فعله عن السجود فلا يعتد بسجوده لأنه غير نية الأصل وإن
لم يخطر له أمر الصلاة وقصد الاستقامة غافلا فالنص أنه لا يعتد به كما لو
صرفه عن السجود ذاكرا
وفيه وجه مخرج يجري نظيره في اتباع الغريم في الطواف ثم إذا لم يعتد
بسجوده فيكفيه أن يعتدل جالسا ثم يسجد ولا يلزمه القيام على الظاهر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To humble oneself, to lower the head in veneration; the physical posture of placing the forehead on the ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of worship (ʿibādah) signifying utter submission (khudhūʿ) to the Divine, both in body and spirit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the physical act; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual humility before God.
- Root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be straight, upright, balanced; to rise evenly from a bent posture.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The restoration of equilibrium (iʿtidāl) in prayer, a pillar (rukn) of the ritual.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bodily straightening; metaphorical for justice and moderation in acts.
- Root: ط-م-أ-ن (ṭ-m-ʾ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be still, tranquil, at rest; to settle firmly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The required stillness (ṭumaʾnīnah) in each posture of prayer, signifying presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical repose; metaphorical for inner serenity.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — governing the legal consequences of intentional vs. unintentional acts in the subsidiary rulings (furūʿ).
chapters.translation:
I say: The discourse on prostration (sujūd) and rising from it (iʿtidāl) comprises two aspects: the minimal obligation and the perfect form.

As for the minimal obligation, the discussion concerns what is placed on the ground, the manner of placement, and the posture of the one prostrating.

Regarding what is placed: it is the forehead (jabhah), and nothing else substitutes for it. Then, the least amount to which the name applies suffices. Concerning the placement of the hands, knees, and feet, there are two opinions (qawlān):

One: They are obligatory, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«أمرت أن أسجد على سبعة آراب»} — "I was commanded to prostrate upon seven bones."

The second: They are not obligatory, because prostration is but the placing of the forehead; therein lies the subjugation of the noblest of limbs to the dust.

If we deem them obligatory, then uncovering the feet and knees is not required, but uncovering the forehead is required. Regarding the hands, there are two opinions:

One: Uncovering them is obligatory, due to the saying of Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt: "We complained to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, of the scorching heat of the sand on our faces and palms, and he did not relieve us" — meaning, he did not remove our complaint.

The second: It is not obligatory, because humility (tawāḍuʿ) is achieved by the placement itself. Then, mere touching with the head raised is not sufficient for placement; rather, one must lower the head. ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in his prostration like a worn-out garment." Then, for uncovering the forehead, the least amount to which the name applies suffices. If one prostrates on its edge, or on the fold of his turban, or on the edge of his sleeve that moves, it is not valid.

As for the posture of the one prostrating — which is the inversion (tanakkus) such that his lower parts are higher than his upper parts — if he prostrates on a cushion and his head is level with his back, there are two aspects (wajhān) due to the loss of inversion.

If a sickness prevents him from inversion, is he obligated to place a cushion to put his forehead upon? There are two aspects; the more apparent (aẓharuhumā) is obligation, because the form of prostration is achieved by placement, not by inversion.

Tranquility (ṭumaʾnīnah) is also obligatory in prostration.

As for the perfect form: let the first of his body to touch the ground be his knees. Abū Ḥanīfah said: Rather, his hands.

Then it is recommended (yustaḥabb) that he say the takbīr upon descending, without raising his hands, and say in his prostration: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" (subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā) three times.

He places his nose on the ground along with the forehead, uncovered; he separates his knees, and distances his elbows from his sides such that the whiteness of his armpits is visible; he draws his belly away from his thighs; he places his hands with fingers spread upon the same position as in raising the hands, with fingers extended toward the qiblah and joined. He is not commanded to join the fingers except here.

Al-Muzanī transmitted that he places his toes such that their tips face the qiblah.

As for the woman, she refrains from spreading and distancing in bowing (rukūʿ) and prostration.

Then he says the takbīr upon rising, and sits with the left foot spread (iftirāsh) between the two prostrations, placing his hands near his knees with fingers spread, and says: "O Allah, forgive me, mend me, grant me well-being, provide for me, and guide me" (Allāhumma ighfir lī wa-jburnī wa-ʿāfinī wa-rzuqnī wa-hdinī). He maintains tranquility in his sitting.

Then he performs another prostration like the first. If he is to rise afterward, he sits a brief sitting for rest (istirāḥah). The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not rise until he was fully seated. Then, whether he begins the takbīr such that it concludes upon his full sitting, or he sits fully and then rises — there is a difference of opinion (khilāf) therein.

Then, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he stood in his prayer, placed his hands on the ground as one who kneads dough places them.

A subsidiary branch (farʿ): If one falling to prostration falls upon his face, it is counted, because the falling is not intended. If he falls upon his side and intends prostration, it is counted. If he intends to straighten himself and diverts his action from prostration, his prostration is not counted, because he did not intend the original act. If the matter of prayer did not occur to him and he intended to straighten himself, heedless, then the text (naṣṣ) holds that it is not counted, just as if he diverted himself from prostration while mindful. There is an aspect (wajh) derived by analogy, paralleled in the case of following a debtor in the circumambulation (ṭawāf). Then, if his prostration is not counted, it suffices for him to sit upright and then prostrate; he is not obligated to stand, according to the apparent view (al-ẓāhir).

chapters.title_en: Section on the Tashahhud and the Sitting Postures
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في التشهد والقعود

أما القعود في التشهد الأول فمسنون على هيئة الافتراش وفي الأخير على
هيئة التورك لأن الافتراش هيئة مستوفز للحركة حتى نقول المسبوق يفترش في
التشهد الأخير للإمام ولو كان على الإمام سجود سهو هل يفترش فيه خلاف
والافتراش أن يضجع الرجل اليسرى ويجلس عليها وينصب القدم اليمني ويضع
أطراف الأصابع على الأرض
والتورك أن يضجع رجله كذلك ثم يخرجها من جهة يمينه ويمكن وركه من الأرض
ثم يضع اليد اليسرى على طرف الركبة منشورة مع التفريج المقتصد وأطراف
الأصابع مسامية للركبة وأما اليد اليمنى فيضعها كذلك لكن يقبض الخنصر
والبنصر والوسطى ويرسل المسبحة وفي الإبهام أوجه قيل يرسلها أيضا وقيل يحلق
الإبهام والوسطى وقيل يضمها إلى الوسطى المقبوضة كالقابض ثلاثة وعشرين ثم
يرفع مسبحته عند قوله لا إله إلا الله مع الهمزة من قوله
إلا الله وهل يحركها عند الرفع فيه وجهان
فأما التشهد فواجب في الأخير خلافا لأبي حنيفة
والصلاة على الرسول واجب معه
وعلى الآل قولان
والتشهد الأول مسنون وفي الصلاة على الرسول فيه قولان لأنه مبني على
التخفيف
فإن أوجبنا الصلاة على الآل في  الأخير ففي كونها سنة في الأول قولان
ثم أكمل التشهد مشهور وكلماته متعينة
وأما الأقل فهو التحيات لله سلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وسلام
علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا
رسول الله وأسقط العراقيون كلمة أشهد في الكرة الثانية
وكان الشافعي رضي الله عنه جعل الأقل ما رآه متكررا في جميع الروايات
وأما ابن سريج فإنه أوجز بالمعنى وقال التحيات لله سلام عليك أيها النبي
سلام على عباد الله الصالحين أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسوله ثم
يقول بعد التشهد اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد ثم يستحب بعده أن يقول كما
صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم وبارك على محمد وآل محمد كما باركت على
إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم إنك حميد مجيد ثم يستحب بعده الدعاء ويختصر إذا كان
إماما
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد تمام للتشهد ثم ليتخير أحدكم من
الدعاء أعجبه إليه والأولى أن يكون سؤاله لأمور الآخرة
فرع العاجز عن التشهد يأتي بترجمته كتكبيرة التحرم والعاجز عن الدعاء لا
يدعو بالعجمية بحال
وتكبيرات الانتقالات وغيرها من الأذكار ففي الإتيان بترجمتها خلاف قيل
بالمنع لأن العجمية مبطلة وترك الذكر ليس بمبطل
والثاني يأتي بها كالتكبير
والثالث ما يجبر تركه بسجود السهو يأتي بترجمته ومالا فلا

### | القول في السلام

لا يقوم مقام التسليم غيره من أضداد الصلاة عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة وأقله
أن يقول السلام عليكم مرة واحدة وهل تشترط نية الخروج وجهان
ولو قال سلام عليكم وجهان في إقامة التنوين مقام الألف واللام
ولو قال عليكم السلام فطريقان كما سبق
أما الأكمل فأن يقول السلام عليكم ورحمة الله
والتسليمة الثانية تسن ونص في القديم على أنه لا تسن
ونقل الربيع أنه إن كان إماما في جمع متعين يقتصر على تسليمة واحدة وإن
كثر الجمع فتسليمتان ثم إن سلم واحدة فتلقاء وجهه وإن سلم تسليمتين فيلتفت
حتى يرى خداه أي يرى من كل جانب  خد واحد
ثم ينوي بالسلام السلام على من على يمينه من الجن والإنس والملائكة وكذا
من الجانب الآخر والمقتدون ينوون الرد عليه ولو أحدث في التسليمة الثانية
لم تبطل الصلاة لأنها واقعة بعد الصلاة تابعة هذا تمام كيفية الصلاة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ر-ش (farasha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To spread out, lay flat, or extend upon the ground; the posture of one who settles upon the ground with limbs outstretched.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A bodily disposition (hayʾah) signifying humility and stillness before the Divine, contrasting with postures of haste or self-assertion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in describing physical placement; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the soul's "spreading" in supplication.
- Root: و-ر-ك (warika)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The hip or haunch; the act of resting upon it (tawarruk) as a seated posture.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A posture of settled repose (ṭumaʾnīnah), symbolizing completion and the cessation of movement in ritual worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical act; no metaphorical extension in juristic usage.
- Root: ش-ه-د (shahida)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify, or attest; presence and bearing witness to a truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The verbal testimony (shahādah) of faith, affirming divine unity and prophethood—a cognitive and verbal act of certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in legal testimony; metaphorical in the heart's "witnessing" of divine realities.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "if the imam has a prostration of forgetfulness" introduces a conditional whose apodosis is governed by juristic disagreement (khilāf), requiring careful parsing of the protasis and its implied ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the sitting in the first tashahhud, it is sunnah (recommended) in the posture of iftirāsh (spreading the left foot and sitting upon it), and in the final [tashahhud] in the posture of tawarruk (resting on the left hip with the right foot upright), because iftirāsh is a posture of readiness for movement—so much so that we hold the one who is preceded (masbūq) spreads [his left foot] in the final tashahhud [performed] behind the imam. And if the imam owes a prostration of forgetfulness (sajdah al-sahw), there is a divergence [among our scholars] as to whether he [the masbūq] spreads [his foot] therein.

The iftirāsh is that one lays flat his left foot, sits upon it, erects the right foot [vertically], and places the tips of his toes on the ground. The tawarruk is that one lays flat his foot likewise, then extends it out from his right side, and settles his hip firmly upon the ground. Then he places his left hand upon the edge of his knee, spread open with moderate parting of the fingers, with the fingertips aligned with the knee. As for the right hand, he places it likewise, but he clenches the little finger, the ring finger, and the middle finger, and releases the index finger. Regarding the thumb, there are [several] views: it is said he releases it also; it is said he forms a ring with the thumb and middle finger; and it is said he joins it to the clenched middle finger, like one grasping twenty-three [beads]. Then he raises his index finger at his saying "lā ilāha illā Allāh"—at the hamzah of his saying "illā Allāh." And whether he moves it upon raising: there are two views.

As for the tashahhud itself, it is obligatory (wājib) in the final [sitting], contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. And the salutation upon the Messenger (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) is obligatory along with it. Regarding [the salutation] upon the family (āl): two views.

The first tashahhud is sunnah. And regarding the salutation upon the Messenger therein: two views, because it is built upon brevity (takhfīf). If we deem obligatory the salutation upon the family in the final [tashahhud], then as to its being sunnah in the first: two views.

Then the complete tashahhud is well-known, and its words are fixed (mutʿayyanah). As for the minimal [form], it is: "al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, salāmun ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa raḥmatu Allāh, wa salāmun ʿalaynā wa ʿalā ʿibād Allāh al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh." The Iraqis dropped the word "ashhadu" in the second [clause]. Al-Shāfiʿī (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) deemed the minimal [form] to be what he saw recurring in all transmissions. As for Ibn Surayj, he abbreviated by meaning and said: "al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, salāmun ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu, salāmun ʿalā ʿibād Allāh al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh wa anna Muḥammadan rasūluh."

Then after the tashahhud he says: "Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā āli Muḥammad." Then it is recommended (mustaḥabb) after that to say: "kamā ṣallayta ʿalā Ibrāhīma wa āli Ibrāhīm, wa bārik ʿalā Muḥammadin wa āli Muḥammad kamā bārakta ʿalā Ibrāhīma wa āli Ibrāhīm, innaka ḥamīdun majīd." Then it is recommended after that to supplicate, and he shortens [the supplication] if he is an imam. The Messenger of Allāh (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said, after completing the tashahhud: "Then let each of you choose from supplication what is most pleasing to him." And the preferable [course] is that his asking be for matters of the Hereafter.

Branch: One incapable of [reciting] the tashahhud performs its translation, like the takbīrah al-taḥrīm. And one incapable of supplication does not supplicate in a non-Arab tongue (ʿajamiyyah) under any circumstance. As for the takbīrāt of transitions and other invocations (adhkār), there is a divergence regarding performing their translation: one view prohibits it, because the non-Arab tongue invalidates [the prayer], and omitting the invocation is not invalidating. The second [view] permits it, like the takbīr. The third [view] distinguishes: what is compensable by the prostration of forgetfulness may be translated, and what is not [so compensable] may not.

### | Section on the Salutation (Salām)

Nothing other than it from the opposites of prayer (aḍdād al-ṣalāh) stands in place of the concluding salutation, in our view, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. Its minimal [form] is that one says "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" once. Whether the intention of exiting [the prayer] is a condition: two views. If he says "salāmun ʿalaykum": two views regarding the substitution of the nunation (tanwīn) for the definite article (alif-lām). If he says "ʿalaykum al-salām": two paths, as previously mentioned.

As for the most complete [form], it is that he says "al-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatu Allāh." The second salutation is sunnah, though it is explicitly stated in the Old [School] (al-qadīm) that it is not sunnah. Al-Rabīʿ transmitted that if he is an imam in a small, fixed congregation, he restricts himself to a single salutation; but if the congregation is large, then two salutations. Then, if he gives one salutation, he [turns] directly toward his face; if he gives two salutations, he turns until his cheeks are seen—i.e., one cheek is seen from each side.

Then he intends by the salutation [to greet] those on his right from among the jinn, humans, and angels, and likewise from the other side. The followers (muqtadūn) intend by it the response to him. If he breaks his ablution during the second salutation, the prayer is not invalidated, because it occurs after the prayer as a subordinate [act]. This completes the modality of the prayer.

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 48: Conclusion on Missed Prayers and the Conditions of Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
### | خاتمة

من فاته صلوات فلا ترتيب عليه في قضائها
وقال أبو حنيفة يلزمه تقديم الأول فالأول إلا إذا زاد على صلاة يوم وليلة
نعم رعاية الترتيب بين الفائتة والمؤداة عندنا مستحبة فيقدم الفائتة إن
اتسع الوقت لهما وإلا قدم المؤداة وسبب التقديم أن لا يتساهل في القضاء
بالتأخير ولو تذكر فائتة وهو في مؤداة أتم التي هو فيها ثم اشتغل بالقضاء
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الخامس في شرائط الصلاة ونواقضها - صلى
الله عليه وسلم -
والشرائط ست
الأول الطهارة عن الحدث فهو شرط في الابتداء والدوام حتى لو
أحدث في الصلاة عمدا أو سهوا بطلت صلاته ولو سبقه الحدث بسبق بول أو مني
أو مذي أو خروج ريح بطلت صلاته على الجديد
وعلى القديم لا تبطل صلاته لما روي مرسلا أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من
قاء أو رعف أو أمذى في صلاته فلينصرف وليتوضأ وليبن على صلاته ما لم يتكلم
ولأنه لو انحل إزاره عن عورته فرده على القرب أو وقعت عليه نجاسة يابسة
فنفضها لم تبطل صلاته قولا واحدا ولو كان ذلك قصدا لبطل مع قصر الزمان
وعلى هذا القول إذا طرأ ناقض بغير قصده ولا تقصيره فله التدارك بخلاف ما
لو انقضت مدة المسح في أثناء الصلاة لأنه مقصر بابتداء الصلاة في آخر مدة
المسح
ولا تخرق خفه فوجهان لأنه قد ينسب إلى تقصير لذهوله عن ضعف الخف
والمتيمم إذا رأى الماء في أثناء صلاته لم تبطل صلاته لأن الصلاة مانعة
من الاستعمال فانتفت القدرة
ثم من سبقه الحدث يطلب الماء ويتوضأ ولا يتكلم ولا يحدث عمدا وبعد وضوئه
لا يعود إلى مكانه الأول فإنه فعل مستغن عنه بل يبني على مكانه خلافا لأبي
حنيفة
ولو سبقه  الحدث في الركوع قبل الطمأنينة فليعد إليه وإن كان بعدها فلا
لأن سبق الحدث لا يبطل ما مضى ولو طير الريح الثوب وافتقر في الإعادة إلى
فعل كثير خرج ذلك على قولي سبق الحدث

### | الشرط الثاني طهارة الخبث

والنظر في أطراف

### | الأول فيما عفي عنه من النجاسات وهي أربعة

الأولى الأثر على محل النجو بعد الاستجمار على الشرط المعلوم
فلو حمل المصلى إنسانا قد استجمر ففيه وجهان
أحدهما الجواز لأنه معفو عنه والأصح المنع لأنه معفو على محل نجو المصلي
للحاجة ولا حاجة إلى الحمل ولو حمل طيرا لم تبطل صلاته لأن ما في البطن
ليس له حكم النجاسة قبل الخروج وما على منفذه لا مبالاة به ومنهم من قطع
بالبطلان لأن منفذ نجاسته لا يخلو عن النجاسة وفي إلحاق البيضة المذرة
بالحيوان تردد فإن النجاسة فيها أيضا مستترة خلقة فلا تفارقه إلا في الحياة
ويطرد ذلك فيمن حمل عنقودا استحال باطن حباته خمرا وكذا في كل استتار خلقي
ولا يجري في القارورة المصممة الرأس خلافا لابن أبي هريرة
الثانية طين الشوارع المستيقن نجاسته يعفي عنه بقدر ما يتعذر الاحتراز
عنه فإن انتهى إلى حد ينسب صاحبه إلى سقطة أو نكبة من دابة لم يعف عنه وكذا
ما
على أسفل الخف من نجاسة لا يخلو الطريق عن مثلها في حق من يصلي مع الخف
الثالثة دم البراغيث معفو عنه إلا إذا كثر كثرة يندر وقوعه وربما يختلف
ذلك باختلاف الأوقات والأماكن فإن الحاجة تختلف به والاجتهاد فيه إلى رأي
المكلف فإن رآه مجاوزا لحد الحاجة فليغسل وإن رآه على حد الحاجة فليصل معه
وإن تردد احتمل أن يقال الأصل العفو إلا فيما علم كثرته أو يقال الأصل
المنع إلا فيما تحققت الحاجة إليه وطريق الاحتياط لا يخفى والميل إلى
الرخصة أليق هاهنا بالفقه
الرابعة دم البثرات وما ينفصل منها من قيح وصديد يعفى عنها للحاجة نقل عن
ابن عمر أنه دلك بثرة على وجهه فخرج منها الدم وصلى ولم يغسل
وإن أصابه من بدن غيره فوجهان أصحهما المنع لإمكان الاحتراز
وأما لطخات الدماميل والقروح والفصد فما يدوم منها غالبا يلحق بدم
الاستحاضة وما لا يدوم يلحق بدم الأجنبي لأن وقوعها نادر
ومال صاحب التقريب إلى إلحقاها بدم البثرات وهو متجه

### | النظر الثاني فيما يطهر عن النجاسة

وهو ثلاثة الثوب والبدن والمكان
أما الثوب فقد ذكرنا كيفية غسله فإن تيقن نجاسة أحد الثوبين اجتهد وقال
المزني يصلي في الثوبين صلاتين وقال في الإنائين إنه يتيمم ولا يجتهد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, execute, or settle a matter; to complete what was owed or decreed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, qaḍāʾ denotes the compensatory performance of an obligatory act after its appointed time has lapsed, as opposed to adāʾ (performance within time).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is 'to decide or finish'; here it is a technical transfer (naql) to the compensatory prayer, retaining the notion of settling a debt owed to God.
- Root: ت-ر-ت-ي-ب (tartīb)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Arrangement, sequence, or orderly succession of things one after another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, tartīb refers to the mandated chronological ordering of prayers, whether between missed prayers themselves or between missed and current ones.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for physical ordering; metaphorically extended to temporal precedence in devotional acts.
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sharṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark, sign, or condition; that upon which something else depends.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A prerequisite (sharṭ) is that whose absence entails the invalidity of the conditioned act, though its presence does not necessitate validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally 'a sign'; technically, a condition precedent — distinct from a pillar (rukn) which is internal to the act.
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭahāra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cleanliness, purity; the removal of filth or ritual impurity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Two types: purification from ḥadath (ritual impurity) and from khabath (physical filth); the former is spiritual-legal, the latter physical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for washing; metaphorical for spiritual cleansing from sin.
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿafw)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pardon, remission, or excusing; that which is overlooked or tolerated.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudence, ʿafw denotes impurities that the Law overlooks due to necessity (ḥājah) or hardship (mashaqqah), rendering them excusable in prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally 'to erase or obliterate'; here, the legal overlooking of minor impurities.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with In (إن) — The particle in introduces a protasis whose apodosis is governed by the conditional implication; when the protasis is past-tense (māḍī) and the apodosis is likewise, the sentence denotes a general rule (taʿmīm) applicable to all instances, as in "if he prays, it is valid."
chapters.translation:
### | Conclusion

Whoever has missed prayers, there is no obligatory order (tartīb) upon him in making them up (qaḍāʾ). Abū Ḥanīfah said: He is obligated to present the first then the first, unless the missed prayers exceed the amount of one day and night.

Yes, observing the order between the missed prayer and the one performed in time (muʾaddāh) is, in our school, recommended (mustaḥabb). So he presents the missed prayer if the time is spacious enough for both; otherwise, he presents the performed one. The reason for this presentation is that one should not be lax in making up the missed prayer by delaying it. And if he remembers a missed prayer while he is in a performed prayer, he completes the one he is in, then occupies himself with the making up.

— Peace be upon him — Chapter Five: On the Conditions of Prayer and Its Nullifiers — Peace be upon him —

The conditions are six:

**The First: Purification from Ritual Impurity (ḥadath).** It is a condition at the beginning and throughout the duration [of the prayer]. Thus, if one commits an act that breaks ritual purity during the prayer, whether intentionally or forgetfully, his prayer is nullified. And if the breaking event overtakes him — whether by the escape of urine, semen, madhy (pre-seminal fluid), or the passage of wind — his prayer is nullified according to the new opinion (al-jadīd). According to the old opinion (al-qadīm), his prayer is not nullified, due to what was related as a mursal report that he — peace be upon him — said: "Whoever vomits, or has a nosebleed, or emits madhy during his prayer, let him depart, perform ablution, and build upon his prayer as long as he has not spoken." And because if his waist-wrapper came loose from his nakedness and he returned it promptly, or dry impurity fell upon him and he flicked it off, his prayer would not be nullified by unanimous agreement. Had that been done deliberately, it would nullify [the prayer] even with the brevity of the time. And upon this [old] opinion, when a nullifier occurs without his intent and without his negligence, he may remedy it — unlike the case where the duration of the wipes (masḥ) expires during the prayer, for he is negligent by beginning the prayer at the end of the wipe's duration. And regarding [the case where] his leather socks (khuff) tear, there are two positions (wajhān), because he may be attributed with negligence due to his heedlessness of the sock's weakness.

And the one performing dry ablution (mutayammim) — if he sees water during his prayer, his prayer is not nullified, because the prayer prevents him from using it, so the ability [to use water] is negated [during that time].

Then, whoever is overtaken by the breaking event: he seeks water, performs ablution, does not speak, and does not deliberately commit another nullifying act. And after his ablution, he does not return to his original place, for that would be an act he has no need of; rather, he builds upon [his prayer] in his [new] place — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

And if the breaking event overtakes him during the bowing (rukūʿ) before attaining tranquility (ṭumaʾnīnah), let him return to it; but if after it, then no, because the overtaking breaking event does not nullify what has already passed. And if the wind carried away his garment and he needed, in restoring it, to perform many actions, that is adjudicated upon the two opinions concerning the overtaking breaking event.

### | The Second Condition: Purification from Physical Filth (khabath)

The examination concerns three aspects:

### | The First Aspect: What is Excused (maʿfūw ʿanhu) of Impurities — and they are four:

**The First:** The trace [of moisture] on the place of excretion after cleansing with stones (istijmār), upon the known condition. If the one praying carries a person who has performed istijmār, there are two positions: One of them is permissibility, because it is excused. The more correct (aṣaḥḥ) is prohibition, because it is excused only on the place of the excretor's own filth due to necessity, and there is no necessity in carrying [another]. And if he carries a bird, his prayer is not nullified, because what is in the belly has no ruling of impurity before its exit, and what is on its exit-passage is of no concern. Among them is one who decisively ruled nullification, because the passage of its impurity is not free of impurity. And regarding the analogy of a dropped egg to the animal, there is hesitation (taraddud), for the impurity in it is also concealed by nature, so it does not separate from it except in [the loss of] life. And this applies analogically to one who carries a grape cluster whose inner berries have turned into wine, and likewise for every natural concealment. But it does not apply to a sealed flask with a narrow mouth — contrary to Ibn Abī Hurayrah.

**The Second:** The mud of roadways whose impurity is certain — it is excused to the extent that avoidance is difficult. But if it reaches a limit where its bearer is attributed with a fall or being struck by an animal, it is not excused. Likewise, what is on the bottom of the leather sock of impurity that the road is not free of its like — in the case of one who prays while wearing the sock.

**The Third:** The blood of fleas is excused, unless it accumulates to an extent whose occurrence is rare. And perhaps this varies with the variation of times and places, for the necessity varies with it. And the exertion of judgment (ijtihād) therein is referred to the opinion of the legally responsible person (mukallaf): if he sees it as exceeding the limit of necessity, let him wash it; if he sees it at the limit of necessity, let him pray with it. And if he hesitates, it may be said: the principle is excusal except where its abundance is known; or it may be said: the principle is prohibition except where the need for it is verified. And the path of caution (iḥtiyāṭ) is not hidden, though the inclination toward concession (rukhṣah) is more fitting here to jurisprudence (fiqh).

**The Fourth:** The blood of pustules (buthrāt) and what separates from them of pus and discharge (ṣadīd) — it is excused due to necessity. It is transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar that he rubbed a pustule on his face, blood came out of it, and he prayed without washing it. And if he is afflicted with it from another's body, there are two positions, the more correct of which is prohibition, due to the possibility of avoidance.

As for the smears of boils, sores, and cupping (faṣd) — what persists from them generally is annexed to the blood of prolonged irregular bleeding (istihāḍah), and what does not persist is annexed to the blood of a stranger, because its occurrence is rare. And the author of al-Taqrīb inclined to annexing them to the blood of pustules, and that is well-directed.

### | The Second Aspect: What is Purified of Impurity

It is three: the garment, the body, and the place.

As for the garment — we have already mentioned the manner of washing it. If he is certain of the impurity of one of two garments, he exerts his judgment (ijtihād). Al-Muzanī said: He prays in the two garments two prayers. And regarding two vessels, he said: He performs dry ablution (tayammum) and does not exert judgment.

chapters.title_en: Three Subsidiary Branches, the Second Locus of Purification (the Body), the Third Locus (the Place), and the Conclusion on the One Who Carries Impurity
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع ثلاثة

الأول لو أصاب أحد كميه نجاسة وأشكل فأدى اجتهاده إلى أحدهما فغسله ففي
صحة صلاته فيه وجهان
ووجه المنع أنه استيقن نجاسة الثوب ولم يستيقن طهارته
وكذا الخلاف لو وقع ذلك في ثوبين ولكن صلى فيهما جميعا
الثاني لو غسل أحد الثوبين وصلى في الآخر من غير اجتهاد ففي صحة صلاته
وجهان ولو أشكل محل النجاسة فغسل نصفه ثم غسل النصف الثاني قال صاحب
التلخيص لم يطهر لاحتمال أن تكون النجاسة على وسط الثوب فإذا غسل النصف
الثاني فينعكس أثر النجاسة على النصف الأول لاتصاله به
الثالث إذا ألقى طرف عمامته على نجاسة بطلت صلاته سواء كان ذلك
الطرف يتحرك بحركته أو لا يتحرك
ولو قبض على حبل أو طرف عمامة فإن كان يتحرك الملاقي للنجاسة بحركته بطلت
صلاته وإلا فوجهان لأنه لا ينسب إليه لبسا بخلاف العمامة ولو شد
على وسطه كان كما لو قبض على طرفه ولو كان تحت رجله فلا بأس لأنه ليس
حاملا ولا متصلا ولو كان طرف الحبل على عنق كلب فهو كما إذا كان على نجاسة
إن بعد منه وإن كان قريبا بحيث لو لم يتعلق بالكلب لكان هو حامله فوجهان
مرتبان وأولى بالمنع ولو كان متعلقا بساجور في عنق الكلب فأولى بالجواز ولو
كان في عنق حمار وعلى الحمار نجاسة فوجهان ويظهر هاهنا وجه الجواز

### | المحل الثاني الذى يجب تطهيره عن النجاسة البدن

وقد ذكرنا كيفية غسله وتتعلق به مسألتان
الأولى إذا وصل عظما نجسا  في محل كسر وجب نزعه فإن كان يخاف الهلاك
فالمنصوص أنه يجب نزعه لأنا نسفك الدم في مقابلة ترك صلاة واحدة وهذا يبطل
الصلاة عمره وفي قول مخرج أنه لا يحب لأن النجاسة تحتمل بالأعذار وخوف
الهلاك عظيم ثم إنما ينقدح النص إذا كان متعديا في الابتداء بأن وجد عظما
ظاهرا وإذا لم يستتر العظم باللحم
فإن استتر بعد إيجاب النزع ثم قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه إذا مات قبل
النزع فقد صار ميتا كله أي لا ينزع وهو إشارة إلى نجاسة الآدمي بالموت وقيل
بوجوب النزع لأنا تعبدنا بغسله فهو كالحي
أما من شرب الخمر وغسل فاه صحت صلاته لأن ما في الجوف لا حكم له

### | المسألة الثانية في وصل الشعر

وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن الله الواصلة والمستوصلة والواشمة
والمستوشمة والواشرة والمستوشرة
الوشر تحديد أطراف السن
والوشم نفر الأطراف بالحديدة وتسويدها
وأما الوصل فإن كان الشعر نجسا فهو حرام وإن كان شعر آدمي
فإن كان شعر امرأة أجنبية فيحرم لأن زوجها ينظر إليها وإن كان شعر رجل
حرم عليها النظر فيه على قولنا بتحريم النظر إلى العضو المبان وإن كان شعر
بهيمة فإن لم تكن ذات زوج فهي متعرضة للتهمة فيحرم عليها وإن كانت ذات
زوج يحرم للخداع ولقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام المتشبع بما لم يعط كلابس ثوبي
زور وإن كان بإذن الزوج فوجهان
أحدهما المنع لعموم الحديث ولأن ذلك تصرف في الخلقة بالتغيير
والثاني الجواز وهو القياس إذ لا معنى للتحريم إلا سبب التزوير
ولا خلاف في جواز تجعيد الشعر وتصفيف الطرة وفي إلحاق تحمير الوجنة بوصل
الشعر تردد للصيدلاني

### | المحل الثالث المكان

فينبغي أن يكون ما يماس بدنه طاهرا وهو موقع الأعضاء السبعة في السجود
وكذا ما يماس ثوبه
ولو كان على طرف البساط نجاسة فلا بأس ولو كان ما يحاذي صدره في السجود
نجسا وكان لا يماسه فوجهان ووجه المنع أنه كالمنسوب إليه
ولو بسط إزارا سخيفا على موضع نجس إن كانت المنافذ  بحيث لا تمنع الملاقاة
لم تصح الصلاة وفي مثله في الفرش على الحرير تردد فإن النظر فيه إلى غالب
ما يلاقي وذلك يحل العتابي الذى قطنه غالب
ومما يصل بمكان الصلاة نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة في
سبعة أماكن المزبلة والمجزرة وقارعة الطريق وبطن الوادي والحمام وظهر
الكعبة وأعطان الإبل
وفي مسلح الحمام تردد بناء على أن العلة خوف رشاش النجاسة أو أنه بيت
الشيطان فعلى العلة الأخيرة تكره
وأما أعطان الإبل فليس المراد بها المرابض التى يكثر فيها البعر فإن ذلك
موجود في مرابض الغنم من النجاسة ولا كراهة ولكن الإبل تزدحم على المنهل
ذودا حتى إذا شربت استيقت فلا يؤمن نفارها وتفرقها في ذلك الموضع قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم في الإبل إنها جن خلقت من جن أما ترى إذا نفرت كيف تشمخ
بأنافها

### | خاتمة

من استصحب النجاسة عمدا بطلت صلاته فإن كان جاهلا ففي وجوب القضاء قولان
ولو علم النجاسة ثم نسيها فقولان مرتبان وأولى بالإعادة
منشأ القولين أن الطهارة عنها من قبيل الشرائط فلا يكون الجهل في تركها
عذرا أو استصحابها من قبيل المناهي فلا يعد الناسي مخالفا
والقول الجديد أنه من الشروط ومعتمد القديم ما روي أنه عليه الصلاة
والسلام خلع نعله في أثناء الصلاة فخلع الناس نعالهم فقال بعد الفراغ
أخبرني جبريل أن على نعلك نجاسة

### | الشرط الثالث ستر العورة

وهو واجب في غير الصلاة وفي وجوبه في الخلوة تستر عن أعين الملائكة والجن
تردد ولكن في غير وقت الحاجة
وأما المصلي في خلوة فيلزمه التستر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing, cleansing by the flow of water over a surface; removal of filth by ablution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ṭahārah) as a condition (sharṭ) for the validity of prayer, distinct from mere physical cleaning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) washing of a garment; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the "washing" of the heart from sin.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Dual Subject (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis ("if he washed one of the two") governs the apodosis ("there are two faces"), with the verb's object elided for brevity.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section comprises three subsidiary branches.

**The First Branch:** If impurity struck one of his two sleeves and the matter became ambiguous, and his juristic effort (ijtihād) led him to one of them, and he washed it, then concerning the validity of his prayer in it there are two faces (wajhān). The face of prohibition is that he was certain of the garment's impurity but not certain of its purity. Likewise, the disagreement applies if this occurred with two garments, but he prayed in both of them together.

**The Second Branch:** If he washed one of the two garments and prayed in the other without juristic effort, there are two faces concerning the validity of his prayer. And if the locus of the impurity was ambiguous, and he washed half of the garment, then washed the second half, the author of *al-Talkhīṣ* said: it does not become pure, because it is possible that the impurity was at the middle of the garment; so when he washed the second half, the trace of the impurity is reflected back onto the first half due to its contiguity with it.

**The Third Branch:** If he cast the end of his turban onto impurity, his prayer is invalidated, whether that end moves with his movement or does not move. And if he grasped a rope or the end of a turban — if what contacts the impurity moves with his movement, his prayer is invalidated; otherwise there are two faces, because it is not attributed to him as a wearing (lubs), unlike the turban. And if he tied it around his waist, it is as if he grasped its end. And if it was beneath his foot, there is no harm, because he is neither carrying it nor connected to it. And if the end of the rope was on the neck of a dog, it is as if it were on impurity: if it is distant from him, [it is invalid]; but if it is close such that were it not attached to the dog, he would be its carrier, then there are two faces, ordered, and the more appropriate is prohibition. And if it was attached to a collar (sājūr) on the dog's neck, then the more appropriate is permissibility. And if it was on the neck of a donkey, and on the donkey there was impurity, there are two faces, and here the face of permissibility is apparent.

**The Second Locus: What Must Be Purified of Impurity — The Body**

We have already mentioned the manner of washing it. Two questions attach to it.

**The First Question:** If a bone that is impure (najis) reached a place of fracture, its removal is obligatory. If he fears destruction [by its removal], the textually stipulated (manṣūṣ) ruling is that its removal is obligatory, for we spill blood in exchange for abandoning a single prayer, and this [impurity] invalidates prayer for his entire lifetime. And in a transmitted opinion (qawl mukharraj), it is not obligatory, because impurity is tolerated under exigencies, and the fear of destruction is grave. Then the textual ruling is only sound if the [bone] was transgressing in the beginning, such as finding a bone exposed and not covered by flesh. If it became covered after the obligation of removal was established, then al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: if he dies before removal, he has become entirely dead, i.e., it is not removed — and this is an indication of the impurity of the human being by death. And it was said: removal is obligatory, because we are commanded to wash him, so he is like the living. As for one who drank wine and washed his mouth, his prayer is valid, because what is in the interior (jawf) has no ruling.

**The Second Question: On the Joining of Hair**

The Prophet — peace be upon him — said: {«لعن الله الواصلة والمستوصلة والواشمة والمستوشمة والواشرة والمستوشرة»} ("May God curse the hair-joiner, the one who asks for joining, the tattooer, the one who asks for tattooing, the tooth-filer, and the one who asks for filing"). Al-Washr is the filing of the tips of the teeth. Al-Washm is the pricking of the limbs with an iron and blackening them. As for the joining (waṣl): if the hair is impure, it is forbidden. And if it is human hair — if it is the hair of an unrelated woman (ajnabiyyah), it is forbidden because her husband looks at her. And if it is the hair of a man, it is forbidden for her to look at it, according to our opinion on the prohibition of looking at a severed limb. And if it is the hair of an animal — if she has no husband, she is exposed to suspicion, so it is forbidden for her; and if she has a husband, it is forbidden for deception, and due to his saying — peace be upon him: "The one who seeks to appear rich with what he was not given is like the wearer of two garments of falsehood." And if it is with the husband's permission, there are two faces: one is prohibition, due to the generality of the hadith and because that is a disposition upon the creation by alteration; the second is permissibility, and that is the analogical (qiyās) view, for there is no meaning for prohibition except the cause of falsification. There is no disagreement on the permissibility of curling hair and arranging the forelock. And regarding the annexation of reddening the cheek to the joining of hair, al-Ṣaydalānī hesitated.

**The Third Locus: The Place**

It is required that what touches his body be pure — namely, the location of the seven limbs in prostration — and likewise what touches his garment. If there is impurity at the edge of the carpet, there is no harm. And if what faces his chest in prostration is impure but does not touch him, there are two faces; the face of prohibition is that it is as if attributed to him. And if he spread a thin garment (izār) over an impure place — if the openings are such that they do not prevent contact, the prayer is not valid. And in its like regarding spreading over silk, there is hesitation, for the consideration therein is of the predominant part that contacts, and that is permissible for the ʿAṭābī cloth whose cotton is predominant.

Among what pertains to the place of prayer: the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — prohibited prayer in seven places: the dunghill, the slaughterhouse, the public road, the valley bottom, the bathhouse, the roof of the Kaʿbah, and the camel resting-places. Regarding the bathhouse's washing-area (musallaḥ), there is hesitation, based on whether the cause is the fear of impurity's splashing or that it is the house of the devil; on the latter cause, it is merely disliked (makrūh). As for the camel resting-places, the intent is not the enclosures where dung abounds — for that exists in sheep enclosures as impurity without dislike — but rather camels crowd at the watering-trough, and when they have drunk they are driven off, so their restlessness and scattering in that place is not safe. The Prophet — peace be upon him — said concerning camels: "They are jinn created from jinn; do you not see how when they are startled, they raise their noses haughtily?"

**Conclusion**

Whoever carries impurity deliberately, his prayer is invalidated. If he was ignorant, there are two opinions (qawlān) on the obligation of making up (qaḍāʾ). And if he knew of the impurity then forgot it, there are two opinions, ordered, and the more appropriate is repetition (iʿādah). The origin of the two opinions is whether purification from it is of the category of conditions (shurūṭ), so ignorance in omitting it is no excuse, or whether carrying it is of the category of prohibitions (manāhī), so the forgetful one is not counted as a violator. The new opinion (al-qawl al-jadīd) is that it is of the conditions; and the basis of the old (al-qadīm) is what was related that he — peace be upon him — removed his sandal during the prayer, and the people removed their sandals, and he said after finishing: "Gabriel informed me that on your sandal there was impurity." {«أخبرني جبريل أن على نعلك نجاسة»}

**The Third Condition: Covering the Private Parts (Satr al-ʿAwrah)**

It is obligatory outside of prayer. Regarding its obligation in seclusion, to be concealed from the eyes of the angels and jinn, there is hesitation — but not at a time of need. As for the one praying in seclusion, covering is incumbent upon him.

chapters.title_en: Section 50 — On the Awrah and the Covering Garment, and the Fourth Condition: Abandoning Speech
chapters.arabic_text:
### | والنظر في العورة والساتر

وأما العورة من الرجل فما بين السرة والركبة ولا تدخل السرة والركبة فيه
على الصحيح
وأما الحرة فجميع بدنها عورة في حق الصلاة إلا الوجه واليدين إلى الكوعين
الظهر والكف وظهر القدم عورة وفي إخمصيها وجهان
أما الأمة فما يبدو منها في حالة المهنة كالرأس والرقبة وأطراف الساق
والساعد فليس بعورة وما هو عورة من الرجل عورة منها وفيما بين  ذلك وجهان
أما الساتر فهو كل ما يحول بين الناظر ولون البشرة فلا يكفي الثوب السخيف
الحاكي للون البشرة ولا الماء الصافي والزجاج
ويكفي الماء الكدر والطين ولو لم يجد ثوبا فهل يكلف التطيين فعلى وجهين

### | فروع أربعة

الأول إذا كان القميص متسع الذيل ولا سراويل صحت الصلاة فإنما يجب التستر
من الفوق ومن الجوانب ولو لم يكن مزرورا بحيث لو ركع انكشفت عورته لم تصح
صلاته فإن كان كثافة لحيته تمنع من الرؤية فوجهان
ووجه المنع أن الساتر ينبغي أن يكون غير المستتر
ويجري الخلاف فيما لو وضع اليد على ثقبة في إزاره
الثاني إذا بدا من عورته قدر يسير بطلت صلاته
وقال أبو حنيفة لا تبطل ما لم يظهر من العورة الكبرى مثل درهم ومن الصغرى
الربع
فلو وجد خرقة لا تفي إلا بإحدى السوأتين قيل يستر القبل فإن السوأة
الأخرى مستترة بانضمام الأليتين
وقيل يستر الدبر لأنه أفحش في السجود والأولى التخيير
ولا ينبغي أن يترك السوأة ويستر الفخد فإن الفخد تابع في حكم العورة
كالحريم له
الثالث في عقد جماعة العراة قولان
أحدهما أنها سنة ثم يغضون البصر ويقف الإمام وسط الصف كإمام النساء
والثاني أن تركها أولى احتياطا للعورة
الرابع لو عتقت الأمة في أثناء الصلاة وكان الخمار بالقرب تسترت واستمرت
وإن كان بعيدا فعلى قولي سبق الحدث فإن فرعنا على القدم فمكثت حتى أتي
بالخمار في مثل تلك المدة التى كانت تمشي إليه فيحتمل أن يقال هذا أولي
لترك الأفعال ويحتمل أن يقال التشاغل بالتدارك أولى من التعطل

### | الشرط الرابع ترك الكلام

فكلام العامد مبطل للصلاة وإن قل فإن كان مفهما فالحرف الواحد مبطل
كقوله ق وع من وقى وعى وإن كان غير مفهم فلا يبطل إلا بتوالي حرفين ولا
تبطل بصوت غفل من غير حرف وهل تبطل بحرف واحد بعدها مدة فيه تردد وفي
التنحنح ثلاثة أوجه
أحدها أنه يبطل صلاته إلا إذا كان مغلوبا أو امتنعت القراءة عليه فتنحنح
وعلى هذا إن  تنحنح لأجل امتناع الجهر فوجهان
الثاني نقله ابن أبي هريرة عن الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن التنحنح لا يبطل
أصلا لأنه ليس من جنس الكلام
الثالث قال القفال لو كان مطبقا شفتيه لا يبطل لأنه لا يكون على هيئة
الحروف وإن كان فاتحا فاه بطل والأول هو الأصح هذا في غير المعذور

### | أما أعذار الكلام فخمسة

الأول أن يتكلم لمصلحة الصلاة فتبطل صلاته خلافا لمالك ويدل عليه أمر
التنبيه على سهو الإمام بالتسبيح والتصفيق مع أن تنبيهه من مصلحة الصلاة
الثاني النسيان وهو عذر في قليل الكلام لحديث ذي اليدين خلافا لأبي حنيفة
وفي كثرة وجهان وتعليل وجه البطلان لمعنيين
أحدهما انخرام نظم الصلاة والثاني وقوع ذلك نادرا وعلى الأخير يبطل الصوم
بالأكل الكثير
الثالث الجهل بتحريم الكلام عذر في حق قريب العهد بالإسلام لأحاديث وردت
فيه وليس عذرا في حق غيره
والجهل بكون الكلام مبطلا مع العلم بالتحريم لا يكون عذرا
والجهل بكون التنحنح مبطلا أو ما يجري مجراه فيه تردد والأصح أنه عذر
الرابع لو التفت لسانه بكلمة بدرت منه فهذا عذر وأبو حنيفة يوافق ذلك
لأنه لا يزيد على سبق الحدث
الخامس لو أكره على الكلام في الصلاة ففي بطلانها قولان كما لو أكره على
الأكل في الصوم

### | فرعان

الأول إذا قال وقد استأذن جمع على بابه {ادخلوها بسلام آمنين} إن قصد
القراءة لم تبطل صلاته وإن قصد الخطاب المجرد بطل وإن قصدهما جميعا لم تبطل
عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة
الثاني السكوت الطويل ذكر القفال فيه وجهين
أصحهما أنه لا يبطل لأنه ليس يخرم نظم الصلاة والثاني أنه يبطل لأنه يقطع
الولاء بين أفعال الصلاة
وعلى هذا لو كان ناسيا فطريقان
أحدهما أنه على الوجهين في الكلام الكثير
والثاني أنه كالكلام القليل وهو الأصح
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿ-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "defect" or "exposure"; the awrah is that part of the body whose exposure is a blemish (ʿawr) upon the person, both physically and ritually.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Sacred Law, the awrah denotes the limit (ḥadd) of what must be concealed for the validity of worship; it is a technical term tied to the notion of ritual inviolability (ḥurmah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, "the vulnerable, exposed part" (e.g., a breach in a wall); metaphorically transferred to the body's parts whose revelation invites moral and ritual harm.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taḍmīn (Implicit Embedding) — When the author says "النظر في العورة" (the consideration is in the awrah), the verb "النظر" governs a suppressed clause of deliberation (taʾammul), requiring the reader to supply "في حكم" (in the ruling concerning) for full syntactic resolution.
chapters.translation:
I say: The consideration now concerns the awrah and the covering garment (al-sātir).

As for the awrah of a man, it is that which lies between the navel and the knee; the navel and the knee themselves are not included therein, according to the soundest (al-ṣaḥīḥ) position.

As for the free woman (al-ḥurrah), her entire body is awrah with respect to the prayer, except the face and the hands up to the wrists. The back of the foot, the palm, and the back of the hand are awrah; concerning the hollows of her two soles (ikhmiṣayhā), there are two faces (wajhān).

As for the slave-woman (al-amah), that which ordinarily appears of her in the state of performing household tasks — such as the head, the neck, the lower parts of the shank, and the forearm — is not awrah. Whatever is awrah for a man is awrah for her as well; concerning what lies between these two categories, there are two faces.

As for the covering garment (al-sātir), it is everything that intervenes between the observer and the color of the skin. Thus, a thin garment that transmits the skin's color does not suffice, nor does clear water or glass. Murky water and clay (ṭīn) do suffice. If one finds no garment, is he obligated to plaster himself with clay? There are two faces on this.

### Four Subsidiary Branches (Furūʿ)

**The First:** If one wears a shirt with a wide hem and no trousers, his prayer is valid; for concealment is required only from above and from the sides. But if the shirt is not buttoned such that, were he to bow (rukūʿ), his awrah would become exposed, his prayer is not valid. If the density of his beard prevents visibility [of the skin through a thin garment], there are two faces. The face of prohibition (manʿ) is that the covering garment ought to be something other than the covered part itself. The same disagreement applies to the case of one placing his hand over a hole in his waist-wrapper (izār).

**The Second:** If a small amount of his awrah becomes visible, his prayer is nullified. Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is not nullified unless what appears from the major awrah is the size of a dirham, and from the minor awrah, a quarter [of a dirham]. If one finds a rag sufficient to cover only one of the two private parts, it is said: he should cover the front (al-qubul), for the other private part is already concealed by the pressing together of the buttocks. And it is said: he should cover the rear (al-dubur), for it is more obscene during prostration. The preferable view is that he has the choice. He should not, however, leave the private part exposed and cover the thigh; for the thigh is subordinate in the ruling of awrah, like the protected precinct (al-ḥarīm) of it.

**The Third:** Concerning the congregational prayer of naked persons, there are two sayings (qawlān). One: it is a sunnah, and they lower their gaze, with the imam standing in the middle of the row, like the imam of women. The second: that abandoning it is preferable, as a precaution for the awrah.

**The Fourth:** If a slave-woman is emancipated during the prayer, and the head-covering (khimār) is near, she covers herself and continues. If it is far away, then [the ruling] follows the two sayings on the precedence of the nullifying event (sabq al-ḥadath). If we build upon the older saying (al-qadīm), and she remains [in prayer] until the head-covering is brought to her in the same duration of time it would have taken her to walk to it, then it is possible to say: this is more appropriate, for abandoning the [extra] actions [of walking]; and it is possible to say: occupying oneself with repairing [the deficiency] is more appropriate than remaining idle.

### The Fourth Condition: Abandoning Speech

Speech, when intentional, nullifies the prayer, however little it may be. If it is intelligible (mufhim), then even a single letter nullifies it — such as one saying "Q" or "ʿA" from waqā (to protect) and waʿā (to comprehend). If it is unintelligible, it does not nullify unless two letters are consecutive. A mere sound of heedlessness (ṣawt ghaflah) without any letter does not nullify. Whether a single letter followed by a prolongation (maddah) nullifies it — there is hesitation (taraddud) therein. Concerning clearing the throat (tanahḥun), there are three faces:

**One:** It nullifies his prayer, unless he is overcome [by necessity] or recitation was prevented for him, so he cleared his throat. Upon this [face], if he cleared his throat because of inability to raise his voice [in recitation], there are two faces.

**The Second:** Ibn Abī Hurayrah transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — that clearing the throat does not nullify at all, because it is not of the genus of speech.

**The Third:** Al-Qaffāl said: If he kept his lips sealed, it does not nullify, because it does not take the form of letters; but if he opened his mouth, it nullifies. The first is the most sound (al-aṣaḥḥ). This [entire discussion] applies to one without a valid excuse.

### As for the Excuses for Speech, They Are Five:

**The First:** That one speaks for the benefit of the prayer (maṣlaḥat al-ṣalāh); his prayer is nullified — contrary to Mālik. Evidence for this is the command to alert [the imam] to forgetfulness through tasbīḥ (glorification) and clapping, even though alerting him is for the benefit of the prayer.

**The Second:** Forgetfulness (nisyān); it is an excuse for little speech, according to the ḥadīth of Dhū al-Yadayn — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. Concerning much speech [under forgetfulness], there are two faces. The rationale for nullification is based on two meanings: one, the disruption of the order (naẓm) of the prayer; the second, that such [much speech] occurs rarely. Upon the latter [meaning], fasting is nullified by eating much [food under forgetfulness].

**The Third:** Ignorance of the prohibition of speech is an excuse for one recently converted to Islam, due to reports (aḥādīth) transmitted concerning this; but it is not an excuse for anyone else. Ignorance of the fact that speech nullifies the prayer, while knowing its prohibition, is not an excuse. Ignorance of the fact that clearing the throat nullifies, or what runs in its course — there is hesitation therein; the most sound is that it is an excuse.

**The Fourth:** If his tongue slips and a word escapes him involuntarily, this is an excuse. Abū Ḥanīfah concurs with this, because it does not exceed the case of the precedence of the nullifying event (sabq al-ḥadath).

**The Fifth:** If one is coerced (ukriha) into speaking during the prayer, there are two sayings on its nullification — just as if he were coerced into eating during the fast.

### Two Subsidiary Branches

**The First:** If, while a group of people seeks permission at his door, he says: {«ادخلوها بسلام آمنين»} ("Enter it in peace, secure" — Qurʾān 15:46): if he intends recitation (qirāʾah), his prayer is not nullified; if he intends mere address (khiṭāb), it is nullified; and if he intends both, it is not nullified with us — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

**The Second:** Concerning prolonged silence (al-sukūt al-ṭawīl), al-Qaffāl mentioned two faces. The more sound of them: it does not nullify, because it does not disrupt the order of the prayer. The second: it nullifies, because it severs the continuity (wilāʾ) between the acts of the prayer. Upon this [second face], if he were forgetful, there are two paths: one, that it follows the two faces concerning much speech; the second, that it is like little speech — and this is the most sound.
