- Root: أ م م (amma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To intend, to repair to, to lead; imām is one whose example is followed (muqtadā bihi).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Leadership in religious matters (imāmah) entails being a model (qudwah) in acts of worship; the imām's validity is conditioned by the congregation's valid intention to follow.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical leading; metaphorical (majāz) extension covers authoritative exemplarity in ritual.
- Root: ق ر أ (qara'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, to recite; qirā'ah is the collected utterance of scripture.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prayer context, it denotes proficiency in reciting the Fātiḥah and requisite Quranic portions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal recitation; here used technically for ritual competence.
- Root: ف ق ه (faqiha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deep understanding, discernment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Juridical acumen (fiqh) in ritual rulings, prioritized over mere recitation skill.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal comprehension; metaphorical extension to applied legal reasoning.
- Root: و ر ع (wari'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Scrupulous avoidance of the unlawful.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Piety as a qualifying trait for leadership, subordinate to fiqh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal abstention; rhetorical usage elevates it as a moral virtue.
- Root: ق د و (qadā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow, to emulate; iqtidā' is the act of following an imām.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual following requires intentional conformity (mutāba'ah) in intention, action, and position.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal tracking; technical sense in prayer is strict sequential imitation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnā') — The text employs conditional clauses (law, in) and exceptions (illā) to delineate juristic rulings; parsing requires identifying the protasis and apodosis, and the exceptive particle's scope over the preceding universal or particular.
chapters.translation:
I say: Two subsidiary issues branch from this.

The first: One who masters the first half of the Fātiḥah may not follow as a ma'mūm one who masters only the latter half, for the latter is illiterate (ummī) in part of what the one being followed (al-muqtadā) masters; and one who is illiterate in a single letter is like one illiterate in all.

The second: If it becomes evident after the prayer that the imām had been illiterate, the ma'mūm is not obligated to repeat the prayer, just as if it became evident that he had been in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) or minor impurity (ḥadath). But if it became evident that he had been a woman or an unbeliever, repetition is incumbent, because such a condition is generally manifest by its signs, and one cannot know from his prayer that he is a Muslim unless one has heard from him the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahādah). And if it became evident that he had been a hypocrite (zindīq), there are two positions, because such a condition is generally concealed.

### The Second Chapter: On Who Is Most Worthy of the Imāmate

The Prophet — peace be upon him — said: «Let the most learned of you in recitation lead you in prayer; if not, then the most knowledgeable of you in the Sunnah; if not, then the eldest of you in age.» However, the more jurisprudent (afqah) is given precedence over the more proficient in recitation (aqra'), because the prayer's need for jurisprudence (fiqh) is greater. Likewise, the jurisprudent is given precedence over one renowned for scrupulous piety (wara'), for that same reason; although scrupulous piety is given precedence over a jurisprudent who is openly sinful (fāsiq). The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — gave precedence to the most proficient in recitation, for in that age the most proficient among them in recitation was also the most jurisprudent among them.

Thus the most deserving of the qualities is jurisprudence, then manifest scrupulous piety, then age and lineage — and concerning these two latter there are two positions:
The first: precedence is given to lineage, due to his saying — peace be upon him — «Give precedence to Quraysh.»
The second: precedence is given to age, due to his saying — peace be upon him — «The eldest of you in age.»

If these qualities are equal, then preference is given by comeliness of appearance and cleanliness of garment. And if the people dislike his leading them, it is disliked for him to lead.

As for consideration of place: the governor (wālī) is more worthy than the owner (mālik); the owner is more worthy than others; the tenant (musta'jir) is more worthy than the owner; the master (sayyid) is more worthy than the resident slave. Concerning the borrower (musta'īr) and the lender (mu'īr), there is hesitation among the companions. And God — exalted — knows best.

### The Third Book: On the Conditions of Following the Imam — peace be upon him —

Its conditions are conformity (mutāba'ah) in intention, in action, and in position. This reduces to six conditions:

The first: That the ma'mūm not advance ahead of the imām in position; if he does so, his prayer is invalidated according to the new position (al-jadīd), contrary to Mālik. Nor is the imām's prayer invalidated by his advancing, nor by a woman's advancing when she follows, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

If he aligns level with him, it is permissible, but slight lagging is more beloved. Then reliance is placed on the equality of the ankles (ka'b), for the instep (mashṭ) may be elongated.

It is recommended, when they are three, that they line up behind him; the single one stands to his right; the two line up behind him according to us. Ibn Mas'ūd said: one stands to his right and the other to his left.

If he leads a man and a woman, the man stands to his right and the woman behind him. If he leads a woman and a hermaphrodite (khunthā), the woman stands behind the hermaphrodite.

Among what is recommended in position: that the one entering [the mosque] not stand alone; if he finds a row, he should join the row, or draw one of them toward himself if the row is cramped. The one drawn has the right to assist him. The prayer of one standing alone in a row is disliked (makrūhah) yet valid; Aḥmad said it is invalid.

### Subsidiary Issue

If they stand around the Ka'bah or inside the House facing one another, their prayer is valid, for no precedence is apparent therein. It has been said that the ma'mūm ought to be closer to the Ka'bah in his direction than the imām.

The second condition: That the ma'mūm and the imām be in a single place, such that no lagging distance intervenes and no barrier (ḥā'il) lies between them, so that the relation of conjunction (nisbat al-ijtimā') is realized.

The places are three:

A place built for prayer — it is a congregating place (jāmi') even if the construction differs, and even with distant lagging it is like the mosque. Thus if the imām stands on the roof while [the ma'mūm is] in a well within the mosque, it is valid. If they are in two houses within the mosque, or in two adjacent mosques with a door between them that is open or shut, it is valid.

The second place: The open ground (sāḥah) not enclosed by a wall. The ma'mūm should therein be within the limit of proximity, which is a bow-shot (ghalwat sahm), between two hundred and three hundred cubits, for when the place is spacious, this constitutes conjunction. It is said this is derived from the distance between the two facing groups in the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqā' from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — for they were following [an imām] and the ruling of the prayer remained continuous upon them. It is possible to define this limit by what the ma'mūm can hear of the imām's voice in customary loud recitation. This applies to estates and spacious houses. It is said that continuity of the row is required within the estate, but this is remote.

### Subsidiary Issue

If between the imām and the ma'mūm there is a traversed thoroughfare or a river that none but a swimmer can ford, there are two positions on whether conjunction is severed thereby. As for a river that a swimmer can ford, it does not sever the connection.

The third place: Owned buildings, to which are annexed the madrasahs and hospices (ribāṭāt). If they stand in two buildings, it is not valid except with a perceptible connection, such as when shoulders touch at an open door between the two buildings. If there remains on the threshold a standing place, it does not suffice. If a gap intervenes that does not accommodate a standing person, the sounder position is validity. If one advances ahead of the connected row in the building where the imām is not, his prayer is not valid; if he stands behind them, it is valid.

As for when the connection is by the contiguity of rows, such that the other building is behind the imām, not on his flanks: if the distance between the two rows exceeds three cubits, it is not valid; if it does not exceed, there are two positions — unlike the connection of shoulders, for that is a verified connection.

The Iraqis said: difference of buildings does not harm if there is no intervening wall between them.

chapters.title_en: Three Subsidiary Branches, the Third Condition (Intention to Follow), and the Fourth through Sixth Conditions (Compatibility, Conformity, and Sequential Following)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع ثلاثة

الأول البحر كالموات فلو كان في سفينتين مكشوفتين وبينهما أقل من غلوة
سهم جاز فإن ما بينهما بحوض السفينة لا كالنهر على الأرض
وقال الإصطخري لا يحوز إلا إذا كانت إحداهما مربوطة بالأخرى بحيث يؤمن من
التباعد
الثاني إذا اختلف الموقف ارتفاعا وانخفاضا فهو كاختلاف البناء فلا بد من
اتصال محسوس وهو أن يلقى رأس المتسفل ركبة العالي تقديرا لو قدر لكل واحد
منهما قامة معتدلة
الثالث إذا اختلف البقاع بأن وقف الإمام في المسجد والمأموم في ملك فهو
كما لو كانا في بناءين مملوكين وإن كان المأموم في موات ولا حائل فيعتبر
غلوة سهم من موقف الإمام على وجه ومن آخر المسجد على وجه ولو كان بينهما
حائل يمنع البصر والوصول كالجدار لم يجز على الأصح وما يمنع الوصول دون
البصر كالشباك أو البصر دون الوصول كالباب المردود فوجهان والباب المغلق
كالجدار

### | الشرط الثالث نية الاقتداء

فلو تابع من غير النية بطلت صلاته ولا يجب على الإمام نية الإمامة ولكن
لا ينال الثواب إذا لم ينو ولا يجب على المأموم تعيين الإمام ولو عينه
وأخطأ بطل بخلاف الإمام إذا عين المقتدي وأخطأ
ولو ربط المقتدي نيته بالحاضر وقال نويت الاقتداء بزيد الحاضر فإذا هو
عمرو ففي الصحة وجهان كما إذا قال بعت هذه الرمكة فإذا هى نعجة
واختلاف نية الإمام والمأموم لا يضر فيجوز اقتداء المتنفل بالمفترض وعكسه
وفي الأداء بالقضاء وعكسه وإن كان أحدهما ظهرا والآخر عصرا خلافا لأبي
حنيفة

### | الشرط الرابع توافق الصلاتين في النظم

فلا يصح الاقتداء في الرواتب بمن يصلي على الجنازة أو صلاة الخسوف لتعذر
المتابعة
وقيل إنه يصح
ثم عند المخالفة ينفرد فراغ الإمام مما يخالف وهو بعيد
نعم لو اختلف عدد الركعات  فإن كان صلاة المأموم أطول جاز ويكون كالمسبوق
إذا أسلم الإمام وإن كان أقصر كما لو اقتضى في الصبح بمن يصلي الظهر فوجهان
أصحهما الصحة ثم إذ قام الإمام إلى الثالثة تخير فإن شاء سلم وإن شاء صبر
حتى
يعود إليه الإمام فيسلم معه ولا يقال يقوم ويوافق ولا يحتسب له لأن ذلك
لا يحتمل في ركعات مستقلة
الشرط الخامس الموافقة وهو أن لا يشتغل بما تركه الإمام من سجود تلاوة أو
قعود للتشهد الأول فإن فعل بطلت صلاته فأما جلسة الاستراحة فلا بأس وأما
القنوت فلا بأس به أيضا إن أدرك الإمام في السجود إذ ليس فيه إلا تخلف يسير
الشرط السادس المتابعة وهو أن لا يتقدم على الإمام ولا يتخلف عنه تخلفا
كثيرا ولا يساوقه بل يتابعه فإن ساوق لم يضر إلا في التكبير فإن ابتداء
تكبيره ينبغي أن يكون بعد فراغ الإمام على العادة
والمستحب أن يكبر الإمام إذا ظن استواء الصفوف بعد قوله استووا رحمكم
الله والناس يسوون صفوفهم بعد فراغ المؤذن من الإقامة وقال أبو حنيفة يسوون
عند قوله حي على الصلاة ويكبر الإمام عند قوله قد قامت الصلاة
والصحيح أن السلام كسائر الأركان فيجوز المساوقة فيه
وقال الشيخ أبو محمد هو كالتكبيرة
أما التخلف إن كان بركن واحدا لم يبطل وإن كان بركنين بطل لو لم يركع حتى
سجد الإمام بطلت صلاته قطعا ولو لم يركع حتى رفع رأسه من الركوع
فوجهان
أحدهما يبطل لأن الاعتدال أيضا ركن فقد سبق بركنين
والثاني لا لعلتين
إحداهما أنه ليس ركنا مقصودا فعلى هذا لا تبطل ما لم يلابس السجود قبل
ركوع المأموم
الثانية أن الاعتدال إنما يكون سابقا به إذا فرغ عنه لا بالشروع فيه فعلى
هذا إذا هوى للسجود قبل ركوعه بطلت صلاته وإن لم يلابس السجود بعد
وحكم التقدم كالتخلف
وقال الشيخ أبو محمد التقدم بركن واحد يبطل لأنه لا يليق بالمتابعة
كالتقدم في المكان وهو بعيد في المذهب هذا كله إذا تأخر بغير  عذر فإن كان
معذورا كالمسبوق إذا أدرك بعض الفاتحة فثلاثة أوجه
أحدها يترك الفاتحة ويركع لأن السبق يسقط كل الفاتحة فبعضها أولى
والثاني يتمم لأنه التزم الخوض
والثالث إن اشتغل بدعاء الاستفتاح فقد قصر فليتدارك وإلا فليركع فإن قلنا
بتدارك فرفع الإمام رأسه من الركوع قبل ركوعه فقد فاتته هذه الركعة وتبطل
صلاته على أحد الوجهين لأن هذا الركوع قائم مقام ركعة فكأنه سبقه بركعة وهو
بعيد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ل-و (gh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, going beyond bounds; a bowshot's range (ghalwah) as a measure of distance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used technically for the permissible spatial limit in congregational prayer linkage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal measure of projectile range; here metaphorical for a fixed juristic standard of contiguity.
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, purpose, resolve directed toward an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heart's determination distinguishing worship (ʿibādah) from mere habit; pivotal in validity (ṣiḥḥah) of acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal resolve; juristically extended to the specific object of following (taʿyīn) in prayer.
- Root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow, pursue, trail behind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sequential adherence (mutābaʿah) as the structural bond between imam and follower.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical following; metaphorical for temporal coordination of ritual movements.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with Hypothetical Estimation (taqdīr) — The phrase "as if one estimated" (ka-anna qaddara) requires positing a counterfactual premise to assess legal equality, akin to grammatical ellipsis (ḥadhf) where the omitted element governs the ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first subsidiary branch: the sea is like dead land (mawāt). Thus, if [the imam and follower] were in two uncovered ships with less than a bowshot's range between them, it is permissible, for what lies between them is like the ship's basin, not like a river on land. Al-Iṣṭakhrī said: It is not permissible unless one of them is tied to the other such that separation is rendered improbable.

The second branch: if the standing positions differ in elevation and lowness, it is like the difference of buildings, so a perceptible connection is required, namely that the head of the lower one be estimated to reach the knee of the higher one, by way of hypothetical estimation (taqdīr) — as if each of them were assigned a moderate stature.

The third branch: if the places differ, such that the imam stands in the mosque and the follower in private property, it is as if they were in two owned buildings. But if the follower is in dead land (mawāt) with no barrier, then a bowshot's range is considered from the imam's standing place on one side, and from the mosque's end on the other. If there were a barrier preventing sight and access, like a wall, it is not permissible on the soundest view. What prevents access but not sight, like a lattice, or sight but not access, like a shut door, presents two views. A locked door is like a wall.

The third condition: the intention of following (niyyat al-iqtidāʾ). If one follows without intention, his prayer is void. The imam is not obligated to intend the imamate, but he attains no reward if he does not intend it. The follower is not obligated to specify the imam [by name]; yet if he specified him and erred, his prayer is void — unlike the imam, who, if he specified the follower and erred, [his prayer is not void].

If the follower tied his intention to the present [person] and said: "I intend to follow Zayd, the present one," and lo, he was ʿAmr, then there are two views on validity — just as if one said: "I sold this mare," and lo, it was a ewe. Divergence of intention between imam and follower does no harm, so it is permissible for one praying voluntarily to follow one praying obligatorily, and the reverse; likewise for one performing an on-time prayer to follow one performing a make-up prayer, and the reverse — even if one is praying ẓuhr and the other ʿaṣr, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

The fourth condition: compatibility of the two prayers in form (naẓm). It is not valid to follow in supererogatory prayers one who prays over a funeral or the eclipse prayer, due to the impossibility of sequential following. It was said that it is valid. Then, upon divergence, the imam's completion of what he differs in is remote [from validity]. Yes, if the number of units (rakʿāt) differs: if the follower's prayer is longer, it is permissible, and he is like one who joined late (masbūq) when the imam concludes. If it is shorter — as when one prays the dawn prayer behind one praying ẓuhr — there are two views, the sounder being validity. Then when the imam rises to the third [unit], he has the choice: if he wishes he may conclude, and if he wishes he may wait until the imam returns to him and conclude with him. It is not said that he should rise and match [the imam], nor is it counted for him, for that is not sustainable in independent units.

The fifth condition: conformity (muwāfaqah), namely that he not occupy himself with what the imam has left behind — whether prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah) or sitting for the first tashahhud. If he does so, his prayer is void. As for the resting sitting (jalsat al-istirāḥah), there is no harm. As for the qunūt, there is also no harm if he catches the imam in prostration, for there is only a slight lag in it.

The sixth condition: sequential following (mutābaʿah), namely that he not precede the imam, nor lag behind him with a great lag, nor move simultaneously with him (musāwaqah), but rather follow him. If he moves simultaneously, it does no harm except in the takbīr, for the beginning of his takbīr should be after the imam's completion, according to custom. It is recommended that the imam pronounce the takbīr when he deems the rows aligned, after saying: "Straighten [your rows], may God have mercy on you," while the people straighten their rows after the muʾadhdhin finishes the iqāmah. Abū Ḥanīfah said: They straighten at his saying "Come to prayer" (ḥayya ʿalā al-ṣalāh), and the imam pronounces the takbīr at his saying "The prayer has commenced" (qad qāmat al-ṣalāh). The correct view is that the salutation is like the other pillars, so simultaneous movement in it is permissible. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: It is like the takbīr.

As for lagging: if it is by one pillar, it does not void; if by two pillars, it voids. If he did not bow until the imam prostrated, his prayer is void definitively. If he did not bow until [the imam] raised his head from bowing, there are two views: One — it voids, because the standing erect (iʿtidāl) is also a pillar, so he has preceded by two pillars. The second — it does not void, for two reasons: One, it is not an intended pillar in itself; on this basis, it does not void unless he touches prostration before the follower's bowing. The second, that erectness is only counted as preceding him when he has completed it, not upon commencing it; on this basis, if he inclined to prostration before his bowing, his prayer is void even if he has not yet touched prostration. The ruling of preceding is like that of lagging. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: Preceding by one pillar voids, because it befits not sequential following — like preceding in place — but this is remote in the school. All this applies when he lags without excuse. If he is excused — like the one who joins late and catches part of the Fātiḥah — then there are three views: One — he abandons the Fātiḥah and bows, because precedence drops the entire Fātiḥah, so a part of it is even more [worthy of being dropped]. The second — he completes it, because he has committed himself to engaging in it. The third — if he occupied himself with the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ), he has fallen short, so let him make up [the Fātiḥah]; otherwise let him bow. If we say he makes up, and the imam raises his head from bowing before his bowing, then this unit has escaped him, and his prayer is void on one of the two views — because this bowing stands in the place of a unit, as if he had been preceded by a unit — but this is remote.

chapters.title_en: Five Subsidiary Branches and the Book of Traveler's Prayer: Abridgment (Qaṣr)
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فروع خمسة الأول المسبوق ينبغي أن يكبر للعقد ثم للهوي فإن اقتصر على واحد وقصد الهوي به لم ينعقد وإن قصد العقد انعقد بشرط أن يقع تكبيره في اعتداله وإن أطلق فالقياس أنه ينعقد لقرينة البداية ونقل العراقيون عن الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه لا ينعقد لأنه قارنته قرينة الهوي ولا مخصص الثاني إذا نوى قطع القدوة في أثناء الصلاة فيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها المنع وفاء بالملتزم والثاني الجواز لأنه نفل فلا يلزم بالشروع والثالث الجواز للمعذور بعذر يجوز ترك الجماعة به وعلى الأقوال إذ أحدث الإمام انقطعت القدوة ولم تبطل صلاة المأموم الثالث المفرد إذا أنشأ القدوة في أثناء الصلاة فالنص الجديد يدل على منعه والقديم على جوازه ويشكل على الجديد جواز الاستخلاف فإن فيه اقتداء بمن لم يقتد به وإنما منع الشافعي رضي الله عنه الاستخلاف في القديم ولكن ليس في الاستخلاف انتقال المنفرد إلى الاقتداء بل هو تبديل المقتدى به الرابع إذا شك المسبوق فلم يدر أن الإمام فارق حد الراكعين قبل ركوعه فقولان أحدهما أنه مدرك إذ الأصل بقاء الركوع والثاني لا إذ الأصل عدم الإدراك الخامس إذا كان مسبوقا فسلم الإمام نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه على أنه يقوم من غير تكبير وعلته أنه كبر في ارتفاعه عن السجود مع الإمام وهو الانتقال في حقه وقال الشيخ أبو حامد يكبر هاهنا للانتقال = كتاب صلاة المسافرين = وفيه بابان الباب الأول في القصر الباب الثاني في الجمع - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في القصر - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو رخصة جائزة عند وجود السبب والمحل والشرط ### | والنظر الأول في السبب وهو كل سفر طويل مباح فهذه ثلاثة قيود ### | الأول السفر وحده الانتقال مع ربط القصد بمقصد معلوم فالهائم وراكب التعاسيف لا يترخص وإن مشى ألف فرسخ وأمر السفر ظاهر وإنما الغموض في بدايته ونهايته أما البداية فهي الانفصال عن الوطن والمستقر ### | والمستقر ثلاثة الأول البلد والانفصال عنه بمجاوزة السور فإن لم يكن له سور فبمفارقة البنيان فإن كان وراء البنيان خراب ففي اشتراط مجاوزته تردد ولا يشترط مجاوزة المزارع والبساتين التى يخرج إليها للتنزه الثاني القرية ولا بد فيها من مجاوزة البساتين والمزارع المحوطة دون التى ليست محوطة وإن اتصلت أبنية قرية بأخرى فالقياس أن يكفيه مجاوزة قريته ونقل العراقيون عن الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن ذلك لا يكفي الثالث الصحراء والانفصال عنها بمجاوزة الخيام والنادي والدمن وإن نزلوا على منهل أو محتطب فلا بد من مجاوزتهما إلا أن يتسع بحيث لا يختص بالنازلين وإن تفرقت الخيام بحيث لا يستعين بعضهم ببعض فلكل حلة حكمها وقد قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه لو نزلوا في واد والسفر في عرضه فلا بد من جزعه وقال الأصحاب إن كانوا على ربوة فلا بد من الهبوط أو في وهدة فلا بد من الصعود ### | ### | فرع إذا رجع المسافر ليأخذ شيئا خلفه فلا يقصر في الرجوع ولا في مستقره فإن لم يكن المستقر وطنا بل أقام بها غريبا فأظهر الوجهين أنه كسفره ### | أما نهاية السفر فتحصل بأحد أمور ثلاثة الأول الوصول إلى عمران الوطن الثاني العزم على الإقامة مطلقا أو مدة تزيد على ثلاثة أيام في موضع تتصور الإقامة به ولو في واد فإن كان لا يتصور فالأصح أنه يترخص لأن العزم فاسد الثالث الإقامة في صورتها إذا زادت على ثلاثة أيام انقطع الترخص ولا يحسب في الثلاث يوم الدخول ويوم الخروج ثم المقيم فوق الثلاثة إذا كان عازما على أن يشغله ألا يتنجز في الثلاثة فلا يترخص كالمتفقه والتاجر تجارة كبيرة إلا إذا كان شغله قتالا ففيه قولان أحدهما يترخص لما روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قصر في بعض الغزوات ثمانية عشر يوما وروي سبعة عشر وروي عشرين والثاني لا لأنه مقيم والقتال المجدد لا يرخص في القصر وفعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحمل على عزمه الارتحال في كل يوم إن تنجز غرضه فإن قلنا يترخص ففي الزيادة على هذه المدة قولان الأقيس الجواز لأنه لو طال القتال على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استمر على القصر ولما روي أن ابن عمر أقام على القتال بأذربيجان ستة أشهر وكان يقصر أما إذا كان عزمه الخروج في كل ساعة لو تنجز غرضه ولكن اندفع بعائق فإن كان غرضه القتال يرخص على الصحيح للخبر ومن منع حمل ذلك على أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتنقل من موضع إلى موضع وإن كان غرضه غير القتال فقولان أحدهما المنع لأن هذا خاصية القتال وإلا فهو مقيم من حيث الصورة والثاني وهو اختيار المزني أنه يترخص لأنه منزعج بالقلب ولا فرق بين القتال وبين غيره في حكم القياس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ب-ق (sabaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To precede, outstrip, come before; the one who is "preceded" (masbūq) is the latecomer who joins the congregational prayer after the imam has already begun.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, precedence implies a temporal gap in the act of worship; the masbūq's state is one of deficiency (nuqṣān) that must be remedied by completing what was missed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is spatial/temporal priority; here it is transferred (majāz) to the ritual status of one who has missed part of the prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result); in legal reasoning, the conditional phrasing "if he intended X, then Y" requires precise parsing of intent (niyyah) as the operative cause.

- Root: ق-ص-ر (qaṣara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shorten, curtail, confine; also to be deficient or to fall short.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, qaṣr is the divinely granted reduction of the four-unit prayers to two units during travel — a concession (rukḥṣah) predicated on the existence of a cause (sabab), a locus (maḥall), and a condition (sharṭ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal meaning is physical shortening; the juristic usage is a technical transfer (naql) denoting a specific legal dispensation, not a mere abbreviation of form.
- Sībawayh Rule: Restrictive Qualification (al-Taqyīd bi al-Sharṭ) — The threefold restriction (cause, locus, condition) functions as a series of nested qualifiers, each delimiting the scope of the ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first of the five branches: The one who is preceded (al-masbūq) ought to pronounce the takbīr (saying "Allāhu Akbar") for the opening consecration (taḥrīmah), then for the bowing (al-hawī). If he confines himself to a single takbīr and intends thereby the bowing, it does not constitute the consecration. But if he intends the consecration, it is valid on the condition that his takbīr occurs while he is in his upright posture (iʿtidāl). If he makes an unqualified utterance (aṭlaqa), then the analogical ruling (al-qiyās) is that it does constitute the consecration, by virtue of the contextual indication (qarīnah) of his commencing the prayer. The Iraqis transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — that it does not constitute the consecration, because the contextual indication of bowing is conjoined with it, and there is no specifying factor (mukhassiṣ) to override it.

The second branch: If he intends to sever his following of the imam (qatʿ al-qudwah) in the midst of the prayer, there are three opinions (aqwāl). One of them is prohibition, in fulfillment of the obligation he has undertaken (al-multazam). The second is permissibility, because it is a supererogatory act (nafl), and one is not bound by mere commencement. The third is permissibility for the one who has an excuse (maʿdhūr) — an excuse for which abandoning the congregation is permissible. And upon all the opinions, if the imam becomes ritually invalidated (aḥdatha), the following is severed, yet the prayer of the follower (al-maʾmūm) is not nullified.

The third branch: If one praying alone (al-mufrad) initiates following an imam in the midst of the prayer, the new textual opinion (al-naṣṣ al-jadīd) indicates its prohibition, while the old opinion (al-qadīm) indicates its permissibility. And it poses a difficulty for the new opinion that deputization (al-istikhāf) is permissible — for therein one follows one whom he had not been following. But al-Shāfiʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — only prohibited deputization in the old opinion; yet in deputization there is no transition of the solitary worshipper to following, but rather a substitution of the one followed (tabdīl al-muqtadā bihī).

The fourth branch: If the one who is preceded doubts, not knowing whether the imam had departed the boundary of the bowers (ḥadd al-rākiʿīn) before his own bowing, there are two opinions (qawlān). One of them is that he has caught the unit (mudrik), for the original presumption (al-aṣl) is the continuance of the bowing. The second is that he has not caught it, for the original presumption is the non-attainment (ʿadam al-idrāk).

The fifth branch: If he is one who is preceded and the imam gives the salutation (sallama), al-Shāfiʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — explicitly ruled that he stands up without a takbīr. And the reason for this is that he had already pronounced the takbīr in his rising from the prostration with the imam, and that constitutes the transition (al-intiqāl) in his case. But Shaykh Abū Ḥāmid said: He pronounces the takbīr here for the transition.

= The Book of the Prayer of Travelers (Ṣalāt al-Musāfirīn) =

It contains two chapters: The first chapter concerns abridgment (al-qaṣr); the second chapter concerns combining (al-jamʿ).

The first chapter on abridgment — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace — and it is a concession (rukḥṣah) that is permissible upon the existence of the cause (al-sabab), the locus (al-maḥall), and the condition (al-sharṭ).

### | The first consideration concerns the cause

And it is every lengthy permissible journey (safar ṭawīl mubāḥ). These are three restrictions (quyūd).

### | The first is the journey (al-safar)

Its definition is the act of moving (al-intiqāl) with the binding of one's intention (rabṭ al-qaṣd) to a known destination (maqṣad maʿlūm). Thus the wanderer (al-hāʾim) and the rider of trackless wastes (rākib al-taʿāsīf) do not avail themselves of the concession, even if he walks a thousand parasangs (farsakh). And the matter of the journey is evident; the obscurity lies only in its beginning and its end.

As for the beginning, it is the separation (al-infiṣāl) from one's homeland (al-waṭan) and place of settled residence (al-mustaqarr).

### | And the place of settled residence is of three kinds

The first is the city (al-balad), and separation from it is by passing beyond its wall (al-sūr). If it has no wall, then by departing from its built-up area (al-bunyān). If there is wasteland (kharāb) beyond the built-up area, there is hesitation (taraddud) concerning the condition of passing beyond it. And it is not required to pass beyond the farmlands and orchards (al-mazāriʿ wa al-basātīn) to which one goes out for recreation (tanazzuh).

The second is the village (al-qaryah), and it is necessary therein to pass beyond the orchards and farmlands that are enclosed (al-muḥawwaṭah), but not those that are not enclosed. And if the buildings of one village are contiguous with another, the analogical ruling is that passing beyond one's own village suffices. The Iraqis transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — that this does not suffice.

The third is the open desert (al-ṣaḥrāʾ), and separation from it is by passing beyond the tents (al-khiyām), the encampment (al-nādī), and the dung-heaps (al-diman). If they have alighted at a watering-place (manhal) or a firewood-gathering spot (muḥtaṭab), it is necessary to pass beyond both, unless the place is so vast that it is not exclusively reserved for those alighting there. And if the tents are so scattered that some do not avail others, then each encampment (ḥillah) has its own ruling. Al-Shāfiʿī — may Allāh be pleased with him — said: If they alighted in a valley and the travel is along its breadth, it is necessary to traverse it (jazʿuhu). And the companions (al-aṣḥāb) said: If they were upon a hillock (rabwah), it is necessary to descend; or in a hollow (wahdah), it is necessary to ascend.

### | A subsidiary branch

If the traveler returns to take something behind him, he does not abridge in the return nor in his place of settling (mustaqarr). But if the place of settling is not his homeland, rather he has taken up residence there as a stranger (gharīb), then the more manifest of the two opinions (aẓhar al-wajhayn) is that it is like his journey.

### | As for the end of the journey, it is attained by one of three matters

The first: arriving at the inhabited area (ʿumrān) of the homeland. The second: the resolve (al-ʿazm) upon residence absolutely, or for a period exceeding three days, in a place where residence is conceivable — even if in a valley. But if residence is not conceivable therein, then the more correct opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that he avails himself of the concession, for the resolve is defective (fāsid). The third: residence in its form (ṣūrah) — when it exceeds three days, the concession is severed. And the day of entry and the day of exit are not counted in the three.

Then the one residing beyond three days, if he is resolved upon an occupation that will not be completed within the three, does not avail himself of the concession — like the student of jurisprudence (al-mutafaqqih) and the merchant engaged in large trade (tājir tijārah kabīrah) — except if his occupation is fighting (qitāl), for therein are two opinions. One of them is that he avails himself of the concession, because it is related that the Messenger of Allāh — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace — abridged in some of the military expeditions for eighteen days; and it is related for seventeen, and related for twenty. The second is that he does not, because he is a resident, and renewed fighting does not permit abridgment; and the act of the Messenger of Allāh — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace — is interpreted as his resolve to depart each day if his purpose were accomplished.

If we say he avails himself of the concession, then concerning exceeding this period there are two opinions. The more analogical (al-aqyas) is permissibility, for had the fighting been prolonged for the Messenger of Allāh — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace — he would have continued abridging; and because it is related that Ibn ʿUmar remained fighting in Azerbaijan for six months and would abridge.

As for the one whose resolve is to depart at every hour if his purpose were accomplished, but he is repelled by an obstacle (ʿāʾiq) — if his purpose is fighting, he avails himself of the concession upon the sound opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ), due to the report (al-khabar). And the one who prohibits interprets that as the Messenger of Allāh — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace — moving from place to place. And if his purpose is other than fighting, there are two opinions. One of them is prohibition, for this is a peculiarity (khāṣṣiyyah) of fighting; otherwise he is a resident in terms of form (ṣūrah). The second — and it is the choice of al-Muzanī — is that he avails himself of the concession, for he is agitated in his heart (munzaʿij bi al-qalb), and there is no difference between fighting and other than it in the ruling of the analogy (ḥukm al-qiyās).

chapters.title_en: Section 61 — On the Conditions of Travel Concessions and the Domain of Shortening Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو خرج من بغداد يقصد الري فبدا له أثناء الطريق العود انقطع سفره فلا
يقصر في الحال ما لم يفارق مكانه كمشي السفر
ثم إن فارق وكان بينه وبين مقصده مرحلتان قصر وإلا فلا
ولو انتقض عزمه في العود وأراد التمادي إلى الري ولم تبق مرحلتان لا يقصر
وكذا لو غير عزيمته من الري إلى همدان انقطع ذلك السفر فليفارق مكانه ثم
ليترخص

### | القيد الثاني الطويل

وحده مسيرة يومين وبالمراحل مرحلتان وبالأميال ثمانية وأربعون ميلا
بالهاشمي كل ثلاثة أميال فرسخ
وقال أبو حنيفة هو مسيرة ثلاثة أيام

### | ثم رخص السفر ثمانية

أربعة منها تتعلق بالقصير والطويل كالصلاة على الراحلة على أصح القولين
وترك الجمعة والتيمم وأكل الميتة
وأربعة تتلعق بالطويل القصر والفطر والمسح ثلاثة أيام والجمع في أصح
القولين
ثم الصوم أفضل من الفطر وفي القصر والإتمام قولان
وقال الصيدلاني  القصر أفضل وفي الفطر قولان لأن بدل الصوم يثبت في الذمة
ونقصان القصر لا يثبت في الذمة

### | ثم لطول السفر أربعة شرائط

الأول أن يعزم عليه في الأول فلو خرج في طلب الآبق على عزم أن ينصرف مهما
لقيه لم يترخص وإن مشى ألف فرسخ إلا إذا علم أولا أنه لا يلقاه قبل مرحلتين
الثاني أن لا يحسب الإياب في طول السفر فلو كان مجموع الإياب
والذهاب مرحلتين لا يقصر لا ذاهبا ولا جائيا
الثالث أن يكون طوله ضروريا فلو ترك الطريق القصير وسلك الطويل لم يقصر
إلا إذا كان فيه غرض من أمن أو سهولة طريق وفي غرض التنزه والتفرج وجهان
الرابع أن لا يعزم على الإقامة في الطريق فلو قصد سفرا طويلا على أن يقيم
في كل مرحلة أربعة أيام لم يترخص

### | القيد الثالث المباح

فالعاصي بسفره لا يترخص كالآبق والعاق وقاطع الطريق لأن الرخصة إعانة ولا
يعان على المعصية ومن عين مقصدا ولا غرض له لم يترخص لأنه عاص بإتعابه نفسه
قال الشيخ أبو محمد من الأغراض الفاسدة طوف الصوفي إذا لم يكن له غرض سوى
رؤية البلاد
وفي جواز أكل الميتة والمسح يوما وليلة للعاص وجهان
الأصح الجواز فإنه ليس من خصائص السفر فأشبه تناول المباحات
أما العاصي في سفره بالشرب وغيره فيترخص

### | فرع

لو أنشأ سفرا مباحا ثم غير القصد إلى معصية فالنص أنه يترخص لأن الشروط
إنما تعتبر عند ابتداء الأسباب وقد انعقد هذا السفر سببا مرخصا وكذا على
العكس الآبق إذا توجه إلى سيده لم يترخص لفقد الشرط في الابتداء وخرج ابن
سريج قولا أن النظر إلى الحال لا إلى الابتداء وهذا أوضح

### | النظر الثاني في محل القصر

وهو كل صلاة رباعية مؤداة في السفر أدرك وقتها في السفر والرباعية احتراز
عن المغرب والصبح فلا قصر فيهما والمؤداة احتراز عن المقضية ولا قصر إذا
قضى في السفر ما فات في الحضر ولو فات في السفر ففي قضائها ثلاثة أقوال
أحدها وهو مذهب المزني  جواز القصر إذ لم يجب إلا هذا القدر
والثاني المنع لأنه هذه رخصة ووقت القضاء متسع
الثالث إن قضى في السفر قصر وأما في الحضر فلا
وإن تحلل حضر بين سفرين فوجهان

### | فرع

نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن المسافر في آخر الوقت يقصر ونص في
الحائض إذا أدركت أول الوقت أنه تلزمها الصلاة
فقيل قولان بالنقل والتخريج
أحد القولين أنه يلزم بأول الوقت الإتمام على المقيم وأصل الصلاة على
الحائض لإدارك وقت الإمكان ولتغليب جانب الوجوب
والثاني لا لأن الوجوب إنما يستقر بكل الوقت أو بآخره
ومنهم من فرق بأن الحيض إذا طرأ كان ذلك القدر من الوقت بالإضافة إلى
إمكانها كل الوقت بخلاف المسافر

### | النظر الثالث في الشرط

وهو اثنان
الأول أن لا يقتدي بمتم فإن اقتدى به ولو في لحظة لزمه الإتمام ولو تردد
في أن إمامة مسافر أو مقيم لزمه الإتمام وإن كلام مسافرا بمجرد التردد
بخلاف ما لو شك أن إمامه هل نوى الإتمام لأن النية لا يطلع عليها وشعار
المسافر ظاهر والظاهر من المسافر أن ينوي القصر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-ر (qa-ṣad-ra) [qṣr]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shorten, curtail, confine; the opposite of elongation (iṭālah); also denotes restraint and limitation of extent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, the reduction of the four-unit obligatory prayer to two units as a divinely legislated concession (rukḥṣah) during travel.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical shortening; metaphorical (majāz) extension to ritual acts where the quantity of units is reduced, not the essence of the prayer.
- Root: ع-ز-م (ʿayn-zāy-mīm) [ʿzm]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm resolve, determination, and binding intention; the knotting of a decision against hesitation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The decisive volitional act that constitutes the legal condition (sharṭ) for the validity of travel concessions; its absence nullifies the concession.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the tightening of a rope; metaphorical: the fixing of intent that distinguishes purposeful travel from aimless wandering.
- Root: ر-خ-ص (rā-khā-ṣād) [rkḥṣ]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, ease, and permissibility after prior restriction; the relaxation of a norm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A legally granted dispensation permitting an act ordinarily prohibited or modified due to exigent circumstance (ʿudhr), contingent upon the absence of sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: tender and pliant; metaphorical: the divine easing of the law for the traveler, which is an aid (iʿānah) and thus cannot be extended to the disobedient.
- Root: م-ض-ي (mīm-ḍād-yā) [mḍy]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pass on, proceed forward, and continue along a path; the elapsing of time or traversing of distance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The actualization of travel by physically departing from one's place, as opposed to mere intention; a condition for the renewal of concession after interruption.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the passing of a thing; metaphorical: the commencement of journeying that legally separates the traveler from his abode.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb) such that legal consequences attach only when the condition is fully realized; in the phrase "if he departs and between him and his destination are two stages," the apodosis (shortening) is suspended on the complete fulfillment of both the departure and the distance, illustrating the principle of taʿlīq (suspension of ruling on condition).
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the subsidiary branch concerning the interruption of travel: If one departs from Baghdad intending [to reach] al-Rayy, and it occurs to him during the journey to return, his travel is severed, and he does not shorten [the prayer] in that very moment unless he departs from his place by walking the distance of travel. Then, if he departs and between him and his destination there remain two stages (marḥalatān), he shortens; otherwise, he does not. And if his resolve to return is broken and he desires to continue on to al-Rayy, yet there do not remain two stages, he does not shorten. Likewise, if he alters his determination from al-Rayy to Hamadhān, that travel is severed, so let him depart from his place and then avail himself of the concession.

As for the second restriction, namely the length [of travel]: Its measure is the journey of two days, and by stages it is two stages, and by miles it is forty-eight miles by the Hāshimī [measure], every three miles being one parasang (farsakh). Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is the journey of three days.

Then the travel concessions are eight: Four of them pertain to both the short and the long [journey], such as praying upon the mount according to the sounder of the two opinions, the abandonment of the Friday prayer, dry ablution (tayammum), and eating carrion. And four pertain specifically to the long [journey]: shortening, breaking the fast, wiping [over the leather socks] for three days, and joining [prayers] according to the sounder of the two opinions. Then, fasting is superior to breaking the fast, and regarding shortening versus completing [the prayer], there are two opinions. Al-Ṣaydalānī said: Shortening is superior. And regarding breaking the fast, there are two opinions, because the substitute for fasting is established as a debt upon the conscience (dhimmah), whereas the deficiency entailed by shortening is not established as a debt upon the conscience.

Then, for the length of travel, there are four conditions: The first is that one resolve upon it at the outset. Thus, if one departs in search of a runaway slave with the resolve to turn back whenever he encounters him, he does not avail himself of the concession, even if he walks a thousand parasangs, unless he knows at the outset that he will not encounter him before two stages. The second is that the return journey not be counted within the length of travel. Thus, if the total of the return and the going is two stages, he does not shorten, neither going nor returning. The third is that its length be necessary. Thus, if one abandons the short route and takes the long one, he does not shorten, unless there is in it some purpose of safety or ease of road. And regarding the purpose of recreation and amusement, there are two faces (wajhān). The fourth is that he not resolve upon residing along the way. Thus, if one intends a long journey on the condition that he reside at every stage for four days, he does not avail himself of the concession.

As for the third restriction, namely the permissible [travel]: The one who is disobedient by means of his travel does not avail himself of the concession, such as the runaway slave, the undutiful child, and the highway robber, because the concession is an aid, and one does not aid in disobedience. And whoever designates a destination while having no purpose therein does not avail himself of the concession, because he is disobedient by wearying himself. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: Among the corrupt purposes is the wandering of the Sufi when he has no purpose other than sightseeing the lands. And regarding the permissibility of eating carrion and wiping [over the socks] for a day and a night for the disobedient, there are two faces. The sounder [opinion] is permissibility, for it is not among the specificities of travel, so it resembles the partaking of permissible things. As for the one who is disobedient within his travel by drinking or otherwise, he does avail himself of the concession.

I say: As for the subsidiary branch: If one initiates a permissible travel and then alters his intention to disobedience, the text (naṣṣ) [of al-Shāfiʿī] is that he avails himself of the concession, because the conditions are only considered at the commencement of the causes, and this travel has been constituted as a concession-granting cause. Likewise, conversely, the runaway slave — if he heads toward his master, he does not avail himself of the concession, due to the absence of the condition at the outset. And Ibn Surayj articulated an opinion that consideration is given to the present state, not to the commencement, and this is the clearer [view].

As for the second consideration, concerning the domain of shortening: It is every four-unit prayer performed in its time during travel, whose time was reached during travel. The phrase "four-unit" is a precaution excluding the sunset (maghrib) and dawn (ṣubḥ) prayers, for there is no shortening in them. And the phrase "performed in its time" is a precaution excluding the made-up prayer (al-maqḍiyyah), for there is no shortening when one makes up in travel what was missed in residence. And if it was missed during travel, then regarding making it up there are three opinions: The first, which is the madhhab of al-Muzanī, is the permissibility of shortening, since nothing was obligatory upon him except this very measure. The second is prohibition, because this is a concession, and the time for making up is expansive. The third is that if he makes it up during travel, he shortens, but as for [making it up] during residence, he does not. And if one is released from residence between two travels, there are two faces.

I say: As for the subsidiary branch: Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, stated in the text that the traveler at the end of the time shortens, and he stated regarding the menstruating woman that if she reaches the beginning of the time, the prayer becomes obligatory upon her. So it was said there are two opinions, by transmission and by derivation. One of the two opinions is that he is bound at the beginning of the time to complete [the prayer] like the resident, and the origin of the prayer upon the menstruating woman is [obligatory] due to her reaching the time of possibility, and to give preponderance to the side of obligation. The second is no, because obligation is only established by the whole of the time or by its end. And among them is one who distinguished by saying that when menstruation supervenes, that measure of time is, relative to her possibility, the whole time, unlike the traveler.

chapters.title_en: Section 62 — Branches on Shortening Prayer (Qaṣr) and Combining Prayers (Jamʿ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع

الأول لو اقتدى بمتم ثم فسدت لزمه الإتمام في الاستئناف لأنه التزم مرة
بالشروع
الثاني لو اقتدى بمن ظنه مسافرا ثم بان كونه مقيما لزمه الإتمام لأنه
مقصر إذ شعار الإقامة ظاهر
ولو بان أنه مقيم محدث قال صاحب التلخيص له القصر لأنه في الظاهر ظنه
مسافرا وفي الباطن لم تصح قدرته
وحكى الشيخ أبو علي وجها أنه يتمم ويلتفت على أن المسبوق هل يصير مدركا
بالركوع إذا بان كون إمامه محدثا
الثالث إذا رعف الإمام المسافر وخلفه المسافرون فاستخلف مقيما أتم
المقتدون وكذا الراعف إذا عاد واقتدى بالمستخلف لأنه لم يكمل واحد صلاته
حتى كان فيها في صلاة مقيم
الشرط الثاني أن يستمر على نية القصر جزما في جميع الصلاة فلم ينو القصر
ولا الإتمام لزمه الإتمام ولو شك في أنه هل نوى القصر ولو في لحظة لزمه
الإتمام ولو قام الإمام على الثالثة ساهيا  فشك أنه هل نوى الإتمام لزمه
الإتمام بخلاف ما إذا شك في نية إمامه لأن النية لا يطلع عليها وحال
المسافر ظاهرة القصر بخلاف ما إذا قام إلى الثالثة فإنه تأكد ظن الإتمام
بالقيام
أما القاصد إذا قام إلى الثالثة والرابعة سهوا فيسجد لسهوه ولا يعتد به
إتماما بل لو قصد أن يجعله إتماما لزمه أن يقوم فيصلي ركعتين أخريين
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في الجمع - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
والجمع بين الظهر والعصر وبين المغرب والعشاء في وقتيهما جائز بسببين
السفر والمطر
ونعني به السفر المباح وقال أبو حنيفة لا يجوز الجمع بالسفر
وفي السفر القصير عندنا قولان
أحدهما نعم فإن أهل مكة يجمعون بمزدلفة وسفرهم قصير
والثاني لا كالقصر وأهل مكة يجمعون بعذر النسك ولذلك يجوز لأهل عرفة أيضا
وليسوا مسافرين
ومن علل بالسفر منع أهل عرفة من الجمع ويخرج أهل مكة على القولين

### | ثم شرائط الجمع ثلاثة

الأول الترتيب وهو تقديم الظهر على العصر مهما عجل العصر فإن أخر الظهر
إلى وقت العصر ففي تقديمه وجهان
ووجه الفرق أن العصر في وقته فلم يفتقر إلى تقديم غيره بخلاف العصر في
وقت الظهر
الثاني الموالاة عند التقديم فلا يحتمل الفصل بأكثر من قدر إقامة لتحقق
صورة الجمع
فأما في التأخير ففي الموالاة وجهان وفائدة اشتراطها في التأخير أن يصير
الظهر فائتة لا يجوز قصرها إذا لم يصل العصر عقيبها
الثالث نية الجمع عند التقديم في أول الصلاة الأولى أو في وسطها فلو نوى
في أول الصلاة الثانية لم يجز
وقال المزني يجوز لأن اتصالها به لا يزيد على اتصال سجود السهو
ومعنى النية في التأخير أن لا يتركها على قصد التكامل والترك فيعصى به
وتصير قضاء وقد تردد الأصحاب في أن الظهر المؤخر مع نية الجمع أداء أو قضاء
والصحيح أنه أداء

### | السبب الثاني المطر

وقد جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة من غير خوف ولا سفر وقال
الشافعي
رضي الله عنه ما أراه  إلا من عذر المطر ولا خلاف أن الأوحال والرياح لا
تلحق بالمطر وفي الثلج خلاف
هذا في الجماعة أما من يصلي في بيته أو كان طريقه إلى المسجد في ركن ففي
حقه وجهان
ثم قال أصحابنا التقديم بعذر المطر جائز وفي التأخير وجهان لأنه بالتقديم
يفرغ قلبه وفي التأخير لا يأمن انقطاع المطر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-ر (qa-ṣad-ra) [qaṣr]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shorten, curtail, limit; a state of being confined or restricted.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, the reduction of the four-unit obligatory prayer (farḍ) to two units during travel — a concession (rukḥṣah) predicated on the license granted by the Lawgiver.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of physical shortening; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the legal dispensation, since the prayer's essence is not diminished but its form is abbreviated.
- Root: ج-م-ع (jīm-mīm-ʿayn) [jamʿ]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bring together, unite, gather; the act of assembling disparate elements into a single whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal union of two obligatory prayers within a single time window, either by advancing (taqdīm) the second to the first's time or delaying (taʾkhīr) the first to the second's time.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical gathering; metaphorical for the temporal conjoining of two acts of worship, as no physical assembly is entailed.
- Root: ن-و-ي (nūn-wāw-yā) [niyyah]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, purpose, resolve; the heart's determination toward an aim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The indispensable condition (sharṭ) distinguishing an act of worship from mere habit; its locus is the heart, not the tongue.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the heart's resolve; metaphorical extension to the legal validity of ritual acts, as intention is unobservable externally.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inversion (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "if he prays behind one he thought a traveler") governs the apodosis ("he must complete"), with the legal ruling (ḥukm) contingent upon the stated condition, requiring careful parsing of hypothetical scenarios.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now I shall expound the branches (furūʿ) pertaining to the shortening of prayer (qaṣr), followed by the chapter on combining (jamʿ).

**Branches:**

**First:** If one prays behind one whom he deems a traveler (musāfir), and then the prayer of the imam becomes invalid (fasadat), it becomes obligatory upon the follower to complete the prayer (itmām) when he recommences (al-istīʾnāf), because he has already committed himself once by virtue of his commencement (al-shurūʿ).

**Second:** If one prays behind a person whom he supposes to be a traveler, but then it becomes evident that he is a resident (muqīm), it becomes obligatory upon him to complete the prayer, because he is deficient (muqaṣṣir) — for the insignia of residence (shiʿār al-iqāmah) are manifest.

But if it becomes evident that he is a resident who is in a state of ritual impurity (muḥdith), the author of *al-Talkhīṣ* (al-Qaffāl) said: He may shorten (qaṣr), because in his outward estimation (fī al-ẓāhir) he supposed him to be a traveler, and inwardly (fī al-bāṭin) his [the imam's] capacity (qudrah) was not validly established.

Shaykh Abū ʿAlī (al-Ṭabarī) related a view (wajh) that he completes the prayer, and this turns upon whether the one who is overtaken (al-masbūq) becomes a perceiver (mudrik) of the bowing (rukūʿ) when it becomes evident that his imam was in a state of ritual impurity.

**Third:** If the traveling imam suffers a nosebleed (raʿafa) while his followers behind him are travelers, and he appoints as his successor (istakhlafa) a resident, then the followers must complete the prayer. Likewise, the one who suffered the nosebleed, when he returns and prays behind the successor, must complete — because neither of them has completed his own prayer, such that he was, during it, within the prayer of a resident.

**The Second Condition:** That one persist in the intention of shortening (qaṣr) definitively (jazman) throughout the entire prayer. Thus, if he did not intend shortening nor completion, completion becomes obligatory upon him. And if he doubts whether he intended shortening, even for a single moment, completion becomes obligatory upon him. And if the imam stands up for the third unit forgetfully (sāhiyan), and he [the follower] doubts whether he [the imam] intended completion, completion becomes obligatory upon him — unlike the case where he doubts the intention of his imam, because intention cannot be discerned, and the traveler's state (ḥāl) manifestly indicates shortening. This differs from the case where he stands for the third unit, for then the presumption of completion is strengthened by the standing (al-qiyām).

As for the one who intends [the full prayer] (al-qāṣid), if he stands for the third and fourth units forgetfully, he prostrates for his forgetfulness (sajdah al-sahw) and it is not reckoned as completion. Rather, if he intended to make it a completion, it would be obligatory upon him to stand and pray two additional units.

**The Second Chapter: On Combining (al-Jamʿ)**

Combining between the noon prayer (ẓuhr) and the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr), and between the sunset prayer (maghrib) and the night prayer (ʿishāʾ), within either of their two times, is permissible by virtue of two causes: travel (al-safar) and rain (al-maṭar).

By travel, I mean permissible travel (al-safar al-mubāḥ). Abū Ḥanīfah said: Combining by virtue of travel is not permissible.

Regarding short travel (al-safar al-qaṣīr), there are two views (qawlān) in our school:

**One:** Yes, it is permissible — for the people of Mecca combine at Muzdalifah, and their travel is short.

**The Second:** No, it is not permissible, like the shortening of prayer. And the people of Mecca combine by virtue of the excuse of the ritual (ʿudhr al-nusuk); for this reason, it is also permissible for the people of ʿArafāt, though they are not travelers.

Whoever reasons by travel [as the sole cause] would prevent the people of ʿArafāt from combining, and would render the case of the people of Mecca subject to the two views.

**Then the conditions of combining are three:**

**First:** Order (al-tartīb) — namely, advancing the noon prayer before the afternoon prayer whenever one hastens the afternoon. But if one delays the noon prayer until the time of the afternoon, there are two views (wajhān) concerning its advancement [within the combined time].

The basis for the distinction is that the afternoon prayer is in its own [proper] time, so it does not require the advancement of another before it — unlike the afternoon prayer [when performed] in the time of the noon prayer.

**Second:** Consecutiveness (al-muwālāh) when advancing — it is not permissible to separate by more than the measure of the ritual purification (qadr al-iqāmah), so that the form of combining (ṣūrat al-jamʿ) is realized.

As for delaying (al-taʾkhīr), there are two views concerning consecutiveness. The benefit of stipulating it in delaying is that the noon prayer would become a missed prayer (fāʾitah), which may not be shortened if one does not pray the afternoon immediately after it.

**Third:** The intention of combining (niyyat al-jamʿ) when advancing, at the beginning of the first prayer or in its midst. If one intends it at the beginning of the second prayer, it is not permissible.

Al-Muzanī said: It is permissible, because its connection to it is no greater than the connection of the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw).

The meaning of intention in delaying is that one does not abandon it with the intent of completion and abandonment (al-tark), whereby one would sin and it would become a make-up prayer (qaḍāʾ). The companions (al-aṣḥāb) have vacillated concerning whether the delayed noon prayer, with the intention of combining, is an on-time performance (adāʾ) or a make-up (qaḍāʾ). The correct view is that it is an on-time performance.

**The Second Cause: Rain**

The Messenger of God {«صلى الله عليه وسلم»} combined in Medina without fear or travel, and al-Shāfiʿī {«رضي الله عنه»} said: "I do not consider it to be anything other than the excuse of rain." There is no disagreement that mud (al-awḥāl) and winds (al-riyāḥ) are not annexed to rain. Concerning snow (al-thalj), there is a difference of opinion.

This [permission] applies to congregational prayer. As for one who prays in his own house, or whose path to the mosque is through a sheltered corner (rukun), there are two views (wajhān) in his case.

Then our companions said: Advancement by the excuse of rain is permissible, and concerning delaying there are two views — because by advancement one's heart is freed [of concern], whereas in delaying one is not secure from the cessation of the rain.

chapters.title_en: Section 63 — On the Conditions of the Friday Prayer (Jumuʿah) and Its Subsidiary Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو نوى الإقامة قبل صلاة العصر بطل الجمع ولو نرى في خلال العصر فوجهان
ولو نوى بعد العصر وأدرك العصر فوجهان مرتبان وأولى بأن لا يبطل
أما انقطاع المطر في أثناء الظهر والعصر بعد اتصاله بأول الصلاتين غير
ضار
وقال أبو زيد ينبغي أن يتصل المطر بالتحلل من الأول والتحرم بالثاني
ليتحقق الجمع والاتصال
هذا إذا كان ينقطع ويعود فلو انقطع ولم يعد فهو كما لو نوى المسافر
الإقامة
= كتاب الجمعة =
وفيه ثلاثة أبواب الباب الأول في شرائطها
الباب الثاني في بيان من تلزمه الجمعة
الباب الثالث في كيفية أداء الجمعة
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في شرائطها - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وهي ستة
الأول الوقت فلو وقعت تسليمة الإمام في وقت العصر فاتت الجمعة
والمسبوق لو وقع آخر صلاته في وقت العصر فيه وجهان
أحدهما أنها تصح لأنه تابع للقوم وقد صحت صلاتهم ولذلك حط شرط القدوة في
الركعة الثانية عنه
والثاني أن الجمعة فائتة لأن الإعتناء بالوقت أعظم بخلاف القدوة وانفضاض
العدد فإنهما يتعلقان بغير المصلي فالأمر فيهما أخف
الشرط الثاني دار الإقامة فلا تقام الجمعة في البوادي ولا عند الخيام
لأنها معرضة للنقل وإن كان لإقامتهم أثر في قطع رخص السفر وإن كانت أبنيتهم
من سعف وخشب جاز لأنهما لا ينقل ولا يشترط أن يعقد الجمعة في ركن أو مسجد
بل يجوز في الصحراء إذا كان معدودا من خطة البلد فإن بعد عن البلد بحيث
يترخص المسافر إذا انتهى إليه لم تنعقد إليه لم تنعقد الجمعة فيها بخلاف
صلاة العيد فإنه لا يشترط فيها دار الإقامة ويشهدها الرجالة والركبان
فالأحب فيها الخروج
وقال أبو حنيفة لا يقام في القرى بل لا بد من مصر جامع بسوق قائم ونهر
جار وسلطان قاهر
الشرط الثالث أن لا تكون الجمعة مسبوقة بأخرى فلا تنعقد في بلد جمعتان
لأنه إذا لم تجز إقامتها في كل مسجد كسائر الجماعات فالمقصود شعار الاجتماع
ثم لا مرد بعد الواحد
وقال أبو يوسف تصح جمعتان ولا تصح ثلاثة وهو تحكم

### | فرعان

أحدهما إذا كثر الجمع وعشر الاجتماع في مسجد واحد إما للزحمة وإما لنهر
لا يخوض إلا السابح كدجلة فيجوز عقد جمعتين كما ببغداد
ومنهم من علل حكم بغداد بأنها كانت قرى متفاصلة فحدثت العمارات الواصلة
فاستمر الحكم القديم
قال صاحب التقريب حكم العلة يقتضي أن يترخص المسافر عن قريته وإن لم
يجاوز هذه العمارات استصحابا لما كان فإن لم يجوز له الترخص نظرا إلى ما
حدث فمقتضاه منع الجمعتين وما ذكره متجه فهو في محل التردد
الثاني لو عقدت جمعتان فالسابقة هى الصحيحة إن كان فيها السلطان وإن كان
السلطان في الثانية فوجهان
وهذا التردد بعيد عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه إذ لا تعلق للجمعة عنده
بالسلطان
ولكن يصح للترجيح إذ لا يعجز كل شرذمة عن المبادرة بعقد جمعة فيفوتون على
الباقين
ثم النظر في السبق إلى تحريمة الصلاة
وقيل إلى التحلل وقيل إلى أول الخطبة وهما ضعيفان
أما إذا وقعتا معا تدافعتا وإن احتمل التساوق والتلاحق تدافعتا أيضا
واستؤنفت الجمعة إذ لم يحصل لأحد براءة الذمة في حال وإن تلاحقا ولكن لم
يعرف السابق فقولان أظهرهما التدافع إذ لم تحصل البراءة
وحكى الربيع بن سليمان أنهم يصلون الظهر إذ صحت جمعة في علم الله تعالى
قطعا
أما إذا تعين السابق ثم التبس فالمذهب أن الجمعة فائتة وقيل بطرد القولين
وهو بعيد
الشرط الرابع العدد فلا تنعقد الجمعة عندنا بأقل من أربعين ذكورا مكلفين
أحرارا مقيمين لا يظعنون شتاء ولا صيفا إلا لحاجة وهل يشترط أن يكون الإمام
زائدا على الأربعين فيه وجهان ومستند العدد أن المقصود الاجتماع ولم  ينقل
في التقدير خبر والأربعون أكثر ما قيل وقال جابر بن عبد الله مضت السنة أن
في كل أربعين فما فوقها جمعة فاستأنس الشافعي به وبمذهب عمر بن عبد العزيز
وبالاحتياط
