- Root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is beauty and embellishment; al-zīnah denotes that which renders something comely, whether intrinsic or acquired.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the religious law, tazayyun (adorning oneself) is licit beautification pertaining to the body and attire, distinct from spiritual adornment (zīnat al-qalb) which is faith and knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of outward physical embellishment, not metaphorical (majāz) adornment of character.
- Root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fear, dread, apprehension of harm; khawf is the agitation of the soul from anticipation of an affliction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṣalāt al-khawf is a legislated concession (rukḥṣah) wherein the obligatory prayer is performed in a state of combat, preserving the essential rites while permitting deviation in sequence due to necessity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal fear of the enemy; the term is transferred to the specific prayer-form (majāz mursal) by naming the prayer after its cause.
- Root: ح-ر-س (ḥ-r-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Guarding, watching, protecting; ḥāris is one who stands sentinel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prayer of fear, ḥirāsah denotes the act of a group remaining in prayer-posture while guarding, deferring a ritual pillar (rukn) due to the exigency of combat.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sentry-duty; metaphorically extended to the ritual deferral in prayer.
- Root: ص-د-ع (ṣ-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To split, cleave, divide into parts; ṣadʿ is a crack or fissure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used figuratively for dividing the companions into two groups (ṣadʿayn), a division necessitated by tactical arrangement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical (majāz) usage of physical splitting for organizational partition.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the author says "النوع الأول صلاة رسول الله" and then specifies "ببطن النخل," the latter is an appositive clarifying the former, requiring the reader to parse the nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) as a definition followed by its qualifier.
chapters.translation:
### | The Third [Matter]: Adornment

It is recommended (yustaḥabb) therein for men to wear white garments, to use perfume (ṭīb), and to walk with dignified composure (haynah). Walking is preferable to riding. There is no objection to the attendance of elderly women, but not in ostentatious clothing, and upon them is the avoidance of perfume.

Abu Hurayrah saw a woman from whom the scent of musk was emanating, so he said: "Have you perfumed yourself for the Friday [prayer]?" She replied: "Yes." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: {«أيما امرأة تطيبت للجمعة لم يقبل الله صلاتها حتى ترجع إلى بيتها وتغتسل اغتسالها من الجنابة»} — 'Any woman who perfumes herself for Friday, Allah will not accept her prayer until she returns to her house and performs a full ablution like her ablution from major impurity (janābah).'"

### | The Fourth [Matter]: It is recommended for the Imam to recite in the first [rakʿah] Surah al-Jumuʿah, and in the second {«إذا جاءك المنافقون»} (When the Hypocrites Come to You).

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: If he forgot al-Jumuʿah in the first [rakʿah], he combines it with Surah al-Munāfiqūn in the second. And in the old [school] (al-qadīm), he said: He recites in the first {«سبح اسم ربك الأعلى»} (Glorify the Name of Your Lord, the Most High), and in the second Surah al-Ghāshiyah.

= The Book of the Prayer of Fear (Ṣalāt al-Khawf) =

It comprises four types. The first type: the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [at Biʾr Maʿūnah]. The second type: his prayer ﷺ at ʿAsfān when the war was not intense. The third type: the prayer of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. The fourth type: the prayer of intense fear.

### | The First Type: The Prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Baṭn al-Nakhl

When he divided his companions into two divisions (ṣadʿayn), he prayed two rakʿahs with one group and gave the salutation, then prayed two rakʿahs with the other group. For him it was supererogatory (sunnah), and for them it was obligatory (farīḍah). There is nothing in this [type] except the following of an obligatory [worshipper] behind one performing supererogatory [prayer], which is permissible even without fear.

### | The Second Type: His Prayer ﷺ at ʿAsfān When the War Was Not Intense

When the enemy was in the direction of the qiblah, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd was still with the disbelievers, the time of ʿAṣr entered. They [the disbelievers] said: "A prayer-time has entered upon them which is dearer to them than their very souls. When they commence it, we shall charge upon them with a single assault." Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and informed him of this. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arranged his companions into two ranks and prayed with them. The first rank guarded him during the first prostration, and they did not prostrate until the second rank stood up. Then the guards prostrated and caught up [with the Imam]. Likewise, the second rank did this in the second rakʿah.

This [arrangement] is only complete when the enemy is facing the qiblah. In it there is nothing except falling behind the Imam in [certain] pillars (arkān), and that is not permissible except with an excuse. Then, if two groups from one of the two ranks are singled out for guarding, it is permissible. And if the second rank initiates the guarding, it is permissible, but guarding by the first rank is more fitting.

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: If the second rank advanced in the second rakʿah to the first rank, and the first rank fell back, without their actions becoming numerous, that would be good.

And regarding whether the guards in the first [rakʿah] should guard in the second [rakʿah], there are two opinions (qawlān):
One of them is prohibition, because falling behind is repeated upon them, and the Law has granted concession only for a single time.
The more analogically sound (al-aqyas) is permissibility, because the effect of the first [deferral] is effaced by the intervening separation (faṣl), and the intent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in that was only to achieve equality between the two ranks.

### | The Third Type: The Prayer of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ

This is when the fighting becomes fierce (yaltaḥim), and the situation cannot bear the falling behind of all [the troops] nor their occupation with prayer. This occurred at Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided his companions into two divisions, and withdrew with one group to a place where the enemy's arrows could not reach them. He prayed one rakʿah with them, then stood with them for the second, and they [the first group] completed the second rakʿah by themselves and gave the salutation. They then took the place of their brothers in the rank. The fighting group (al-fīʾah al-muqātilah) withdrew to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was standing, waiting for them, and they followed him in the second rakʿah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat for the second [tashahhud], they stood up and completed the second rakʿah, caught up with him, and made the tashahhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salutation with them.

This is the narration of Khawwāt ibn Jubayr. In it there is nothing except the separation (infirād) from the Imam in the second rakʿah, and the Imam's waiting for the second group twice — in the standing (qiyām) and in the tashahhud.

Ibn ʿUmar narrated that when he [the Prophet] stood for the second [rakʿah], they did not separate for the rakʿah, but rather took the place of their brothers in the rank while still in prayer. The others withdrew and prayed one rakʿah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salutation with them. They then returned to the place of their brothers, with one rakʿah still upon them. Then the first group returned and completed the second rakʿah separately, and rose to the rank. The others returned and completed likewise.

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, adopted the narration of Khawwāt ibn Jubayr for two reasons:
One: Its transmitters are more numerous, and it is closer to caution (iḥtiyāṭ) and to abandoning actions that are dispensable.
Two: The narration of Khawwāt is restricted (muqayyad) to Dhāt al-Riqāʿ, which was the last of the campaigns, whereas the narration of Ibn ʿUmar is unrestricted (muṭlaq).

Among our companions (aṣḥāb) there are those who say: The prayer is valid according to the narration of Ibn ʿUmar, due to the soundness of both narrations, but the preferable [view] is the narration of Khawwāt. This [latter view] is far-fetched, because it entails choosing among many dispensable actions.

Then the consideration in this prayer concerns two aspects (ṭarafayn):
One: Its modality (kayfiyyah). They have disputed over three points:
First: Al-Muzanī transmitted that the Imam recites with the second group the Fātiḥah and a surah. Its meaning is that he remains silent before it, waiting. The companions (aṣḥāb) corrected him on this — he does not remain silent, but rather when they catch up, he prolongs the recitation such that the recitation of the Fātiḥah is expansive enough for them. This is the transmission of al-Rabīʿ. The justification of al-Muzanī's statement is the equality between the two groups, for he recites the Fātiḥah with the first, so let him recite it with the second.
Second: Does he make the tashahhud before the second group catches up with him, or does he wait until they return? There are two paths (ṭarīqān):
One: It is like the Fātiḥah [i.e., he waits].
The second: He makes the tashahhud, since equality between the two groups is not lost in the tashahhud.
Third: Mālik held that the second group makes the tashahhud with the Imam, then stands at his salutation for the second [rakʿah] as one who has been preceded (al-masbūq) stands. This is an old opinion (qawl qadīm), and there is no doubt of its permissibility. But what Khawwāt narrated is also permissible, contrary to Mālik.

### | الطرف الثاني في تعدية النص إلى صلاة المغرب وصلاة الحضر والجمعة

أما المغرب فليصل الإمام فيها بالطائفة الأولى ركعتين وبالثانية ركعة ثم
إن انتظرهم
في التشهد الأول فجائز وإن انتظرهم في القيام في الركعة الثالثة فحسن لأن
التطويل بالقيام أليق ونقل عن الإملاء أن الانتظار في التشهد أولى
وروى عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه صلى بالطائفة الأولى ركعة وبالثانية ركعتين
في ليلة  الهرير وهو قول نقل عن الإملاء والصحيح الأول لأن في هذا تكليف
الطائفة الثانية زيادة تشهد لا يحسب لهم
أما الرباعية في الحضر فليصلي الإمام في الطائفة الأولى ركعتين وبالثانية
ركعتين فلو فرقهم أربع فرق وصلى بكل فرقة ركعة فهل يحرم الانتظار الثالث
فعلى قولين
فإن قلنا يحرم فهل تبطل به الصلاة فعلى قولين
أحدهما يجوز ذلك كما جاز بالمرة الأولى والثانية والثاني لا لأنه رخصة
فلا يزاد على محل النص فعلى هذا يمتنع الانتظار في الركعة الثالثة وما
قبلها جرى على وجهه
وقال ابن سريج تخريجا المنع يختص بالركعة الرابعة فإن الانتظار في
الثالثة هو الانتظار الثاني للإمام بدلا من انتظاره في التشهد إلا أن
المنتظر في التشهد ثم هو المنتظر في القيام بعينه وهاهنا المنتظر ثانيا غير
المنتظر أولا وهذا لا يقدح في الصلاة وهو متجه
أما الجمعة ففي إقامتها على هذا الوجه وجهان ووجه المنع أن العدد فيها
شرط فكيف ينفرد الإمام بالثانية مع انفضاض الفرقة الأولى إلى عود الفرقة
الثانية

### | فرعان

الأول في وجوب رفع السلاح في هذه الصلاة وصلاة عسفان قولان والوجه أن
يقال إن كان في البعد عن السلاح خطر ظاهر فهو محرم في الصلاة وغيرها وإن
كانت الموضوعة والمحمولة واحدة لتيسر أخذها في الحال فلا يحرم وإن لم يظهر
في تنحية السلاح خلل فهذا محل الجزم ففي وجوب الأخذ به واستحبابه تردد وكيف
ما كان فلا تبطل الصلاة بتركه لأن العصيان لا يتمكن من نفس الصلاة
الثاني في السهو ولا شك أن سهو الطائفة الأولى في الركعة الأولى وسهو
الطائفة الثانية في الركعة الثانية للإمام محمول وسهو الطائفة الأولى في
ركعتهم الثانية غير محمول لانفرادهم
ومبدأ الانفراد آخر الركعة الأولى وهو رفع الإمام رأسه من السجود أو أول
الركعة الثانية وهو اعتداله في القيام فيه وجهان
أما سهو الطائفة الثانية في ركعتهم الثانية وهم على عزم اللحوق بالإمام
فيه وجهان ينظر في أحدهما إلى آخر الأمر وفي الثاني إلى صورة التفرد في
الحال
وهما جاريان في المزحوم إذا سها وقت التخلف وفيمن انفرد ركعة وسها ثم
انشأ القدوة في الثانية على أحد القولين

### | النوع الرابع صلاة شدة الخوف

وذلك إذا التحم الفريقان ولم يحتمل تخلف طائفة عن القتال فلا سبيل إلا
الصلاة رجالا وركبانا مستقبلي القبلة وغير مستقبليها إيماء بالركوع والسجود
ولا تحتمل فيها الصيحة والزعقة للاستغناء عنها ولا تحتمل الضربات الكثيرة
من غير حاجة وتحتمل القليلة مع الحاجة وفي الكثيرة مع الحاجة ينظر فإن كان
في أشخاص فيحمتل ما لا يتوالى منها وإن كان في شخص واحد فلا يحتمل لكونه
عذرا نادرا
وفيه قول إنه يحتمل في الموضعين وهو منقاس لأن الواحد أيضا قد يدفع عن
نفسه في بسلاحه ودرعه فيحتاج إلى الموالاة
وفيه قول ثالث إنه لا يحتمل في الأشخاص أيضا لندور الحاجة وضيق باب
الرخصة
ومما يحتمل أيضا تلطخ السلاح بالدم مهما ألقاه عقيب التلطخ فإن أمسكه
مختارا لزمه
القضاء وإن كابه حاجة إلى الإمساك فظاهر كلام الأصحاب وجوب القضاء أيضا
لنذور العذر
والأقيس أن لا يحب لأن أصل القتال وإن كان نادرا ألحق بالأعذار العامة في
إسقاط القضاء مع الإيماء وترك الاستقبال
هذه كيفية الصلاة

### | والنظر الآن في السبب المرخص

وهو خوف مخصوص ويتبين خصوصه بمسائل
الأولى لو انهزم المسلمون لم يصلوا صلاة الخوف إلا إذا كان الكفار فوق
الضعف فعند ذلك يجوز وإلا فالهزيمة محرمة والرخص لا تستفاد بالمعاصي فأما
إذا انهزم الكفار لم يجز لنا صلاة الخوف في اتباع أقفيتهم لأنه لا خوف
الثانية القتال المباح كالواجب في الترخص وذلك كالذب عن المال وقد نقل عن
الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه لو ركبه سيل ولم ينج ما له إلا بصلاة الخوف لم
يصل وظاهر النصوص الجديدة خلافه
وخرج من هذا أن قتل الصائل على المال لا يجوز وهو بعيد لأن المال كالنفس
قال عليه الصلاة والسلام من قتل دون ماله فهو شهيد
الثالثة لو تغشاه حريق أو غرق أو تبعه سبع أو مطالب بالدين وهو معسر خائف
من الحبس عاجز عن بينة الإعسار فله صلاة الخوف وكذا من هرب من حق القصاص في
وقت يتوقع من التأخير سكون الغليل وحصول العفو هكذا ذكره الأصحاب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع د ل (ʿadala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be straight, to balance, to equalize; the core sense is equilibrium in measure or action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, ʿadl denotes the mean of justice—applying a revealed ruling (naṣṣ) analogically to a parallel case with measured parity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical straightness; metaphorical (majāz) for juridical extension (taʿdiyah) of a text's ratio legis.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (in, 'if') governs the apodosis, requiring the translator to preserve the conditional sequence and its legal consequence without interpolation.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the Sunset Prayer (al-Maghrib), let the imam lead the first group in two rakʿahs and the second group in one rakʿah. Then, if he waits for them during the first tashahhud, that is permissible; and if he waits for them while standing in the third rakʿah, that is commendable, because prolonging by standing is more fitting. It is transmitted from al-Imlāʾ that waiting during the tashahhud is preferable. It is also narrated from ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) that he led the first group in one rakʿah and the second in two rakʿahs on the night of al-Harīr—this being a saying transmitted from al-Imlāʾ. Yet the correct view is the first, because in this [second arrangement] there is an imposition upon the second group of an additional tashahhud that is not counted for them.

As for the four-rakʿah prayer in residence (al-ḥaḍar), let the imam lead the first group in two rakʿahs and the second in two rakʿahs. If he were to divide them into four groups and lead each group in one rakʿah, then is the third waiting prohibited? There are two opinions. If we say it is prohibited, then does the prayer become invalid by it? There are two opinions: one holds that it is permissible, just as it was permissible the first and second time; the second holds it is not, because it is a concession (rukḥṣah), so it may not be extended beyond the locus of the text (maḥall al-naṣṣ). On this view, waiting in the third rakʿah is precluded, while what precedes it proceeds in its proper course.

Ibn Surayj said, as a derivation (takhrīj): the prohibition is specific to the fourth rakʿah, for waiting in the third is the imam's second waiting, in place of his waiting in the tashahhud—except that the one waited for in the tashahhud is the very same person waited for while standing, whereas here the one waited for second is not the one waited for first. This does not vitiate the prayer, and it is sound.

As for the Friday Prayer (al-Jumuʿah), there are two aspects concerning its performance in this manner. The aspect of prohibition is that the requisite number (al-ʿadad) is a condition therein—so how can the imam be alone in the second rakʿah while the first group disperses until the second group returns?

### Two Subsidiary Issues

The first concerns the obligation of setting aside weapons in this prayer and in the Prayer of ʿAsfān: there are two sayings. The sound approach is to say: if there is a manifest danger in distancing oneself from the weapon, then it is prohibited—both in prayer and outside it. If the laid-down and the carried [weapon] are equivalent, due to the ease of seizing it immediately, then it is not prohibited. If no defect appears in setting the weapon aside, then this is a locus of definitive judgment: there is hesitation between its obligation and its recommendation. However it may be, the prayer is not invalidated by omitting it, because disobedience does not take hold within the prayer itself.

The second concerns forgetfulness (al-sahw). There is no doubt that the forgetfulness of the first group in their first rakʿah, and the forgetfulness of the second group in their second rakʿah, are borne by the imam. The forgetfulness of the first group in their second rakʿah is not borne by him, due to their isolation. The beginning of isolation is the end of the first rakʿah—namely, the imam's raising his head from prostration—or the beginning of the second rakʿah, namely, his straightening in the standing posture: there are two aspects.

As for the forgetfulness of the second group in their second rakʿah while they are resolved to catch up with the imam, there are two aspects: one looks to the final outcome, and the second looks to the form of isolation at the present moment. Both apply to the one crowded out (al-mazḥūm) who forgets during the time of lagging behind, and to the one who prays alone for a rakʿah, forgets, then initiates following (al-iqtidāʾ) in the second [rakʿah], according to one of the two sayings.

### The Fourth Type: The Prayer of Extreme Fear

This applies when the two hosts clash and it is impossible for any group to withdraw from combat. Then there is no recourse except prayer on foot and riding, facing the qiblah and not facing it, gesturing (īmāʾ) for bowing and prostration. In it, a shout or a cry is not tolerated, because there is no need for it. Numerous blows are not tolerated without need, but few are tolerated with need. As for numerous blows with need, one looks [to the circumstances]: if they come from multiple persons, then what is not consecutive among them is tolerated; if from a single person, it is not tolerated, because it is a rare excuse. There is a saying that it is tolerated in both situations, and it is analogically derived, because a single person may also defend himself with his weapon and armor, thus needing continuity. There is a third saying that it is not tolerated even from multiple persons, due to the rarity of the need and the narrowness of the door of concession.

Also tolerated is the soiling of the weapon with blood, provided he casts it away immediately after the soiling. If he holds it deliberately, he must make up the prayer (al-qaḍāʾ). If a need compels him to hold it, the apparent wording of the companions (al-aṣḥāb) is that making up is also obligatory, due to the scarcity of the excuse. The more analogically sound view is that it is not obligatory, because the basis of fighting—though rare—is annexed to general excuses in dropping the make-up, along with gesturing and omitting the facing of the qiblah. This is the modality of the prayer.

### Now the Consideration Turns to the Permissive Cause

It is a specific fear, and its specificity is clarified through several issues.

The first: If the Muslims are routed, they do not pray the Prayer of Fear unless the disbelievers are more than double [in number]. At that point it is permissible; otherwise, the rout is prohibited, and concessions are not acquired through acts of disobedience. As for when the disbelievers are routed, it is not permissible for us to pray the Prayer of Fear while pursuing their backs, because there is no fear.

The second: Permissible fighting—like obligatory fighting—licenses the concession, such as defending one's property. It is transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) that if a flood overtook a man and he could not save his property except by the Prayer of Fear, he would not pray it. Yet the apparent wording of the new texts (al-nuṣūṣ al-jadīdah) contradicts this. Derived from this is that killing an aggressor against property is not permissible—but that is far-fetched, because property is like the self. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«مَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ مَالِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ»} — "Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr."

The third: If a fire or a flood engulfs him, or a wild beast pursues him, or a creditor demands payment while he is insolvent, fearing imprisonment and unable to prove his insolvency, then he may pray the Prayer of Fear. Likewise, one who flees from a claim of retaliation (al-qiṣāṣ) at a time when he anticipates that delay will quell the rancor and obtain pardon—thus the companions (al-aṣḥāb) have mentioned it.

chapters.title_en: Section 71 — Fear Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Khawf), Its Branches, and the Two ʿĪd Prayers
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو خاف المحرم فوات الوقوف بعرفة فيصلي مسرعا في مشيه على وجه ويترك
الصلاة على وجه وتلزمه الصلاة ساكنا على وجه ومن ومنشؤ التردد أنه من قبيل
طلب شيء أو خوف فوات في محصل
الرابعة لو رأى سوادا فظنه عدوا لا يطاق فصلى صلاة شدة الخوف فإذا هو إبل
تسرح ففي وجوب القضاء قولان مشهوران ينظر في أحدهما إلى تحقق الخوف وفي
الثاني إلى
الخطأ في السبب
والقولان جاريان في كل سبب جهله ولو عرفه لبطل الخوف كجهله بحصن على
القرب منه أو نهر حائل بينه وبين عدوه

### | فرعان

الأول لو ركب في أثناء صلاته لهجوم خوف فبني على صلاته قال الشافعي لا
يصح ولو انقطع الخوف فنزل وصلى بقية صلاته متمكنا صحت فظن المزني أن الفرق
كثرة أفعال الركوب واعترض بأن ذلك يختلف بالأشخاص
وقيل سببه أنه شرع في صلاة تامة فلا يتممها على النقصان وهو منقوض بمن
مرض في أثناء صلاته فإنه يقعد في البقية ولكن أراد الشافعي رضي الله عنه ما
إذا بادر الركوب أخذا بالحزم مع إمكان إتمام البقية قبل الركوب فإن فرض
تحقق الخوف أو انقطاعه فلا فرق بين النزول والركوب بل إن قل فعله مع الحاجة
لم يضر وإن كثر مع الحاجة فوجهان كما في الضربات المتوالية
الثاني لبس الحرير وجلد الكلب والخنزير جائز عند مفاجأة القتال وليس
جائزا في حالة الاختيار بخلاف الثياب النجسة وفي جلد الشاة الميتة وجهان
يبتنيان على أن تحريم لبس جلد الكلب للتغليظ أو لنجاسة العين
وكذلك في تجليل الخيل بجل من جلد الكلب تردد والظاهر جوازه وفي الاستصباح
بالزيت النجس قولان فأما تسميد الأرض بالزبل فجائز لمسيس الحاجة
= كتاب صلاة العيدين=
وهي سنة مؤكدة على كل ما يلزمه حضور الجمعة والأصل فيه الإجماع والفعل
المتواتر من رسول الله صلى الله  عليه وسلم وقوله تعالى {فصل لربك وانحر}
قيل أراد به صلاة عيد النحر
وذهب الإصطخري إلى أنها من فروض الكفايات وطردوا ذلك في جميع الشعائر
وأقل هذه الصلاة ركعتان كسائر النوافل والتكبيرات الزائدة ليست من
أبعاضها
فلا يتعلق بتركها سجود السهو
ووقتها ما بين طلوع الشمس إلى زوالها
وشروطها كشرط سائر الصلوات وقال في القديم شرطها كشرط الجمعة إلا أن
خطبتها تتأخر ويحوز أداؤها في الجبانة البارزة من خطة البلد
فأما الأكمل فنذكر سوابقه ولواحقه على ترتيب الوجود وله سنن
الأولى إذا غربت الشمس ليلة عيد الفطر يستحب التكبيرات المرسلة إلى أن
يتحرم الإمام بصلاة العيد فالناس يصبحون مكبرين حيث كانوا وفي الطريق
رافعي أصواتهم كذلك كان يفعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ونص في موضع أنهم يكبرون إلى خروج الإمام وقيل إنه قول آخر
والصحيح أن المراد به تحرم الإمام لأنه يتصل به غالبا ونقل نص آخر أنه
يدوم إلى آخر الخطبة
وهل تستحب هذه التكبيرات إدبار الصلوات ليلة العيد وصبيحته فعلى وجهين
ووجه المنع أن يتميز هذا الشعار عن شعار التكبيرات المقيدة في عيد النحر
كما سيأتي
الثانية إحياء ليلتي العيد قال عليه الصلاة والسلام من أحيا ليلتي العيد
لم يمت قلبه يوم تموت القلوب
الثالثة الغسل بعد طلوع الفجر
أما قبله فهل يجزئ فيه وجهان
أحدهما لا كالجمعة والثاني نعم لأن أهل القرى يبكرون ليلا فيعر عليهم
الغسل بعد الخروج فيجعل جميع الليل وقتا
الرابعة التطيب والتزين بالثياب البيض للقاعد والخارج لأنه يوم السرور
وأما العجائز فيخرجن في ثياب البذلة
وقال أبو حنيفة لا يخرجن
ويحرم على الرجال التزين بالحرير والإبريسم المحض
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "fear" or "apprehension" of a harmful event; also used for "knowing" (khāfa bi-maʿnā ʿalima) in some dialects.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal/theological context, khawf denotes a justified apprehension that impedes normal ritual performance, distinct from mere illusion (wahm) or certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for genuine peril; metaphorical (majāz) when the cause is mistaken, as in the case of misperceived camels.
- Root: ع-ي-د (ʿ-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿĪd derives from ʿāda (to return), signifying a recurring festivity; also linked to ʿiyādah (visiting) in some usages.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ʿĪd prayer is a communal celebration of divine favor, recurring annually, with emphasis on its sunnah status versus obligatory Friday prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the festival day; metaphorical for the prayer itself as a "return" to worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text uses "law" (if) and "fa-in" (then if) to structure hypothetical legal scenarios, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis for correct juristic inference.
chapters.translation:
I say: A branch — If one in the state of iḥrām fears missing the standing at ʿArafāt, then he may pray while hastening in his walk in one respect, and abandon the prayer in another respect; but the prayer is incumbent upon him while stationary in yet another respect. The source of this hesitation is whether it falls under the category of seeking something or fearing the loss of something in a realized matter.

The fourth issue: If he sees a dark mass and supposes it to be an enemy he cannot withstand, so he prays the prayer of intense fear (ṣalāt shiddat al-khawf), and it turns out to be grazing camels — then regarding the obligation of making up (qaḍāʾ), there are two well-known opinions (qawlān mashhūrān). In one, consideration is given to the realization of fear; in the second, to the error in the cause. These two opinions apply to every cause that he was ignorant of, such that had he known it, the fear would have ceased — like his ignorance of a fortress near him, or a river barrier between him and his enemy.

Two sub-branches:
The first: If he mounts (an animal) during his prayer due to the onset of fear, and then builds upon his prayer — al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) said it is invalid. But if the fear ceases and he dismounts and prays the remainder of his prayer with full composure, it is valid. Al-Muzanī supposed that the distinction lies in the multiplicity of mounting actions, and he objected that this varies among individuals. It was said the reason is that he began a complete prayer, so he should not complete it in a deficient state — but this is refuted by the case of one who falls ill during his prayer, for he sits for the remainder. Rather, al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) intended the case where he hastens to mount, taking the cautious approach, while it was possible to complete the remainder before mounting. For if fear is assumed to be realized or cut off, there is no difference between dismounting and mounting. Rather, if his action is slight with need, it does not harm; if abundant with need, there are two aspects (wajhān), as in successive strikes (of a weapon).

The second: Wearing silk and the skin of a dog or pig is permissible at the sudden onset of combat, but not permissible in a state of choice — unlike impure garments. Regarding the skin of a dead sheep (maytah), there are two aspects, built upon whether the prohibition of wearing dog skin is for severity (taghlīẓ) or for the impurity of the substance itself. Likewise, there is hesitation in caparisoning horses with a saddlecloth made of dog skin, though the apparent view is its permissibility. Regarding lighting lamps with impure oil, there are two opinions. As for fertilizing land with dung, it is permissible due to pressing need.

= The Book of the Two ʿĪd Prayers =
It is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah) upon everyone for whom attending the Friday prayer is obligatory. The basis for it is consensus (ijmāʿ) and the continuous practice (fiʿl mutawātir) of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and His saying, the Exalted: {«فصل لربك وانحر»} ("So pray to your Lord and sacrifice") — it was said this means the prayer of the ʿĪd of Sacrifice. Al-Iṣṭakhrī held that it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah), and they extended this to all public rites (shaʿāʾir).

The minimum of this prayer is two units (rakʿatān), like other supererogatory prayers, and the additional takbīrs are not integral parts of it, so no prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) attaches to their omission. Its time is from sunrise to its zenith (zawāl). Its conditions are like the conditions of other prayers. In the Old School (al-Qadīm), it was said its condition is like that of Friday, except that its sermon (khuṭbah) is delayed, and it is permissible to perform it in an open field (jabbānah) outside the town's plan.

As for the most complete form, we mention its preliminaries and sequels in the order of existence. It has sunnahs:
The first: When the sun sets on the night of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr, it is recommended to make unrestricted takbīrs (takbīrāt mursalah) until the imam enters the state of iḥrām for the ʿĪd prayer. So people wake up saying takbīr wherever they are, and on the road, raising their voices — thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) do. He stated in one place that they say takbīr until the imam's emergence, and it was said this is another opinion. The correct view is that what is meant is the imam's entering iḥrām, because it is usually connected to it. Another text was transmitted that it continues until the end of the sermon. Whether these takbīrs are recommended after the obligatory prayers on the night of the ʿĪd and its morning — there are two aspects. The aspect of prohibition is that this emblem (shiʿār) should be distinguished from the emblem of restricted takbīrs in ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā, as will come.

The second: Reviving the two ʿĪd nights. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever revives the two ʿĪd nights, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die."

The third: The ritual bath (ghusl) after dawn. As for before it, whether it suffices — there are two aspects. One: no, like Friday. The second: yes, because villagers hasten at night, and it would be burdensome for them to bathe after leaving, so the entire night is made a time.

The fourth: Applying perfume and adorning with white garments, for both the one who stays and the one who goes out, because it is a day of joy. As for elderly women, they go out in plain clothes. Abū Ḥanīfah said they should not go out. It is forbidden for men to adorn themselves with pure silk (ḥarīr) and raw silk (ibrīsam).

chapters.title_en: Section 72 — On the Rulings of Silk, the Two ʿĪd Prayers, and the Takbīrāt of Tashrīq
chapters.arabic_text:
### | وفيه مسائل

الأولى المركب من الإبريسم وغيره فيه طريقان منهم من نظر إلى القلة
والكثرة في الوزن ومنهم من نظر إلى الظهور فأحل الخز وحرم العتابي
الثانية الثوب المطرز والمطرف بالديباج مباح كان لرسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم ثوب كذلك والمحشو بالإبريسم والحرير مباح إذ لا يعد لابسه لابس
حرير فإن كانت البطانة  من حرير لم يجز لأنه لم يحرم بسبب الخيلاء بل لأنه
ترفه في خنوثة لا تليق بشهامة الرجال وأمر الحرير أهون من الذهب إذ المطرف
بغير حاجة جائز والمضبب غير جائز
الثالثة افتراش الحرير محرم على الرجال وفي تحريمه على النساء خلاف تلقيا
من المفاخرة
وفي تحريم إلباس الصبيان الديباج خلاف من حيث إن شهامة الصبي لا تأبي ذلك
الرابعة حيث حرمنا الحرير أبحناه لحاجة القتال ولحاجة المحكة مع السفر
ولو انفردت عن السفر وأمكن التعهد ففيه خلاف ووجه الجواز أن رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم أرخص لحمزة في الحرير لحكة كانت به ولم تخصص السنة
الخامسة إذا اغتسل وتزين وتطيب فليقصد الصحراء ماشيا فهو أولى من الركوب
وليبكر في عيد الأضحى ليتسع وقت الأضحية بعد الصلاة وليستأخر قليلا في
الفطر ليتسع تفرقة الصدقات وليفطر في عيد الفطر قبل الصلاة وليمسك في عيد
النحر حتى يصلي
والصلاة في الصحراء أفضل إلا بمكة فإن اتسع المسجد ببلد آخر فوجهان
أحدهما المسجد أولى كمسجد مكة والثاني لا لأن مكة مخصوصة بالشرف
السادسة ينبغي أن يخرج القوم قبل الإمام ينتظرونه ولا بأس لوصلوا متنفلين
فإذا خرج الإمام تحرم بالصلاة ولم ينتظر أحدا فإذا انتهى إلى المصلى نودي
الصلاة جامعة وتحرم بالصلاة فيقرأ دعاء الاستفتاح أولا ثم يكبر سبعا سوى
تكبيرة الإحرام والهوي ويقول بين كل تكبيرتين سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا
إله إلا الله والله أكبر فإذا فرغ منها
تعوذ وقرأ الفاتحة وسورة ق وفي الثانية يكبر خمسا زائدة كما مضى ثم يقرأ
الفاتحة وسورة اقتربت ويستحب رفع اليدين في هذه التكبيرات
وقال أبو حنيفة التكبيرات الزائدة ثلاثة في كل ركعة
وقال مالك في الأولى ستة وفي الثانية خمسة وهو مذهب ابن عباس
السابعة الخطبة بعد الصلاة وهي كخطبة الجمعة إلا في شيئين
أحدهما أنه يكبر قبل الخطبة الأولى تسع تكبيرات وقبل الثانية سبع تكبيرات
على
مثال الركعتين
الثاني أن الخطيب في الجمعة كما صعد جلس لسماع الأذان وهاهنا يجلس
للاستراحة إذ  لا أذان وقال أبو إسحاق المروزي لا يجلس هاهنا
الثامنة إذا فرغ من الخطبة انصرف إلى بيته من طريق آخر كان رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم يخرج من طريق ويعود من طريق
فقيل كان يحذر من مكائد المنافقين وقيل ليستفتى في الطريقين وقيل كان
يسلك أطول الطريقين في الذهاب لأنه قربة
ثم من شارك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه المعاني تأسى به ومن لم
يشاركه في السبب ففي التأسي به في الحكم وجهان
التاسعة يستحب في عيد النحر رفع الصوت بالتكبير عقيب خمس عشرة مكتوبة
أولها الظهر من يوم العيد وآخرها الصبح من آخر أيام التشريق وهو مذهب ابن
عباس
وفيه قولان آخران
أحدهما أنه يستحب عقيب ثلاث وعشرين صلاة أولها الصبح من يوم عرفة وآخرها
العصر آخر أيام التشريق
الآخر أنه يدخل وقته عقيب صلاة المغرب ليلة النحر ولم يتعرض في هذا النص
للأخير
والقول الثاني في الثلاث مذهب عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما وإحدى الروايتين
عن ابن عمر وابن مسعود ومذهب المزني واختيار ابن سريج
وقيل مذهب الشافعي هو الأول وما عداه حكاية لمذهب الغير

### | ثم اختلفوا في أربع مسائل

الأولى أن إرسال هذه التكبيرات في هذه الأيام هل يستحب من غير صلاة كما
اختلفوا في أن التكبيرات المرسلة ليلتي العيدين هل تستحب عقيب الصلاة
الثانية أنها تستحب عقيب الفرائض وعقيب النوافل قولان
الثالثة لو قضيت صلاة هذه الأيام في غيرها فلا يكبر ولو قضيت فيها كبر
والتكبير مقضي أو مؤدى فيه قولان فإن قلنا مؤدى فلو قضى فيها صلاة غير
هذه
الأيام كبر عقيبها وإن قلنا مقضية فلا
الرابعة إذا كبر الإمام خلف صلاة على خلاف اعتقاد المقتدي فقد تردد ابن
سريج في أنه هل يوافق بسبب القدوة كما يوافق في القنوت من حيث إن توابع
الصلاة من الصلاة
وكيفية هذه التكبيرات أن يقول الله أكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر ثلاثا نسقا
وقال أبو حنيفة مرتين
ثم يقول بعده كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا  وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا لا إله إلا
الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا الله
وحده صدق وعده ونصر
عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (khalasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, sincerity, being free from admixture; the core sense is "to be pure and unmixed."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ikhlāṣ denotes the purification of intention (niyyah) from any motive other than divine proximity — a state of exclusive devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical purity; metaphorical (majāz) for sincerity of heart in acts of worship.
- Root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓahara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become apparent, manifest, victorious; also "back" or "surface."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ẓuhūr as the criterion of perceptible dominance — what is outwardly evident governs the legal determination.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for visibility; metaphorical for evidentiary preponderance in legal reasoning (tarjīḥ bi-l-ẓāhir).
- Root: خ-ن-ث (khanutha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Effeminacy, softness, languidness; the root denotes a departure from masculine vigor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A moral vice opposed to murūʾah (manly virtue) and shahāmah (chivalrous firmness).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical effeminacy; metaphorical for any conduct unbecoming of a man's dignity.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — When multiple rulings are enumerated with "fa-", each clause is syntactically independent yet sequentially linked, requiring the translator to preserve the periodic structure of legal conditionals (sharṭ) and their apodoses (jazāʾ).
chapters.translation:
### | Contained within are several questions

**The First:** Concerning a garment composed of silk (ibrīsam) and other material, there are two approaches (ṭarīqān): among the scholars, one group considers the lesser or greater quantity by weight; another group considers which element is predominant in appearance (ẓuhūr) — thus they deemed permissible the silk-cloth called khazz (a blend of silk and wool) and prohibited the striped silk called ʿattābī.

**The Second:** A garment embroidered or bordered with brocade (dībāj) is permissible — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ possessed such a garment. Likewise, a garment stuffed or padded with silk is permissible, for its wearer is not deemed a wearer of silk. However, if the lining (biṭānah) is of silk, it is not permissible — for the prohibition is not due to pride (khuyalāʾ) alone, but because it is a self-indulgence in effeminacy (khanūthah) unbefitting the manly vigor (shahāmah) of men. The matter of silk is lighter than that of gold, for a garment bordered with silk without need is permissible, whereas one plated with gold is not.

**The Third:** Spreading silk as a floor-covering is prohibited for men; concerning its prohibition for women there is a divergence (khilāf), derived from the consideration of boastful rivalry (mufākharah). Concerning dressing boys in brocade, there is also a divergence, on the ground that a boy's manly vigor does not yet repel such softness.

**The Fourth:** Wherever we have prohibited silk, we permit it for the necessity of combat and for the necessity of itch (ḥakkah) during travel. If the itch occurs apart from travel and regular treatment is possible, there is a divergence. The ground for permissibility is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted a concession to Ḥamzah regarding silk due to an itch afflicting him, and the Sunnah was not restricted to a specific circumstance.

**The Fifth:** When one has bathed, adorned himself, and perfumed himself, let him set out for the open ground (ṣaḥrāʾ) on foot — that is more virtuous than riding. Let him go early on the ʿĪd of Sacrifice (al-Aḍḥā) so that the time for the sacrifice may be ample after the prayer; and let him delay slightly on the ʿĪd of Fast-Breaking (al-Fiṭr) so that the distribution of alms may be ample. Let him break his fast on the ʿĪd of Fiṭr before the prayer, and let him refrain from eating on the ʿĪd of Naḥr until he has prayed.

Prayer in the open ground is more virtuous — except in Mecca. If the mosque of another town is spacious, there are two aspects (wajhān): one, that the mosque is more appropriate, like the mosque of Mecca; the second, that it is not, because Mecca is distinguished by its unique honor.

**The Sixth:** The people should go out before the imam and wait for him. There is no harm if they pray supererogatory prayers. When the imam comes out, he commences the prayer and waits for no one. When he reaches the place of prayer (muṣallā), the call is made: "The prayer is gathering (al-ṣalātu jāmiʿah)." He then commences the prayer, reciting the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ) first, then he makes seven takbīrs besides the takbīr of consecration (takbīrat al-iḥrām) and the takbīr of bowing. Between every two takbīrs he says: "Glory be to God (subḥāna Allāh), praise be to God (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), there is no god but God (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and God is most great (Allāhu akbar)." When he finishes these, he seeks refuge (taʿawwudh) and recites the Fātiḥah and Sūrat Qāf. In the second unit, he makes five additional takbīrs as mentioned before, then recites the Fātiḥah and Sūrat Iqtarabat (al-Qamar). It is recommended to raise the hands during these takbīrs.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: The additional takbīrs are three in each unit. Mālik said: In the first unit six, and in the second five — this being the doctrine of Ibn ʿAbbās.

**The Seventh:** The sermon (khuṭbah) comes after the prayer, and it is like the Friday sermon except in two matters. First: he makes nine takbīrs before the first sermon and seven before the second, following the pattern of the two units. Second: on Friday, when the preacher ascends the pulpit, he sits to hear the call to prayer (adhān); here he sits merely for rest, since there is no adhān. Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī said: He does not sit here.

**The Eighth:** When he finishes the sermon, he returns to his home by another route — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out by one road and return by another. It was said he did so to guard against the plots of the hypocrites; it was said he did so to be consulted on both roads; and it was said he took the longer of the two roads on the outward journey because it is an act of devotion (qurbah). Then, whoever shares with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in these meanings follows his example (taʾassī); and whoever does not share in the cause (sabab), there are two aspects concerning following his example in the ruling.

**The Ninth:** It is recommended on the ʿĪd of Sacrifice to raise the voice with the takbīr immediately after fifteen obligatory prayers — the first being the noon prayer (ẓuhr) of the ʿĪd day and the last being the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ) of the final day of the Tashrīq days. This is the doctrine of Ibn ʿAbbās. There are two other opinions: one, that it is recommended after twenty-three prayers — the first being the dawn prayer of the day of ʿArafah and the last being the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) of the final Tashrīq day; the other, that its time enters after the sunset prayer (maghrib) of the night of Sacrifice — though this text does not address the final limit. The second of the three opinions is the doctrine of ʿUmar and ʿAlī (may God be pleased with them both), one of the two narrations from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd, the doctrine of al-Muzanī, and the choice of Ibn Surayj. It was said that the doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī is the first opinion, and the rest are merely narrations of others' doctrines.

### | Then they differed over four questions

**The First:** Whether the sending forth of these takbīrs during these days is recommended apart from prayer — just as they differed over whether the unconstrained takbīrs of the two ʿĪd nights are recommended after the prayer.

**The Second:** Whether they are recommended after the obligatory prayers and after the supererogatory prayers — two opinions.

**The Third:** If one makes up (qaḍāʾ) a prayer of these days at another time, he does not make the takbīr; but if he makes it up during these days, he does make it. Whether the takbīr itself is "made up" (maqḍiyyah) or "performed in time" (muʾaddāh) — two opinions. If we say it is performed in time, then if one makes up a prayer of other days during these days, he makes the takbīr after it; if we say it is made up, he does not.

**The Fourth:** If the imam makes the takbīr behind a prayer contrary to the belief of the follower, Ibn Surayj hesitated as to whether the follower should concur by virtue of following (qudwah) — just as he concurs in the qunūt — on the ground that the appendages of the prayer are part of the prayer.

The manner of these takbīrs is that one says: "God is most great, God is most great, God is most great" — three times in succession. Abū Ḥanīfah said: twice. Then after it one says: "And praise be to God abundantly (wa-l-ḥamdu li-Allāhi kathīrā), and glory be to God morning and evening (wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā). There is no god but God alone, with no partner (lā ilāha illā Allāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah), sincere to Him in religion (mukhliṣīna lahu al-dīn), even if the disbelievers detest it (wa-law kariha al-kāfirūn). There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and alone vanquished the confederates (lā ilāha illā Allāhu waḥdahu ṣadaqa waʿdahu wa-naṣara ʿabdahu wa-hazama al-aḥzāba waḥdah). There is no god but God, and God is most great (lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-Allāhu akbar)."

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع أربعة

الأول لو ترك تكبيرات الركعة ناسيا وتذكرها بعد القراءة فالمنصوص جديدا
أنه لا يكبر لفوات وقته وقال في القديم يكبر لبقاء القيام
ومن الأصحاب من طرد القول القديم في تدارك دعاء الاستفتاح
الثاني إذا فات صلاة العيدين بزوال الشمس ففي قضائها أربعة أقوال
أحدهما لا يقضي الثاني يقضي ولكن يوم الحادي والثلاثين إن فات يوم
الثلاثين
لأنه يحتمل هذا اليوم الأداء الثالث يقضي طول هذا الشهر الرابع أنه يقضي
أبدا
وقد سبق نظيره في النوافل
الثالث إذا شهدوا على الهلال قبل الزوال أفطرنا وصلينا وإن أنشأوا
الشهادة بعد الغروب يوم الثلاثين لم يصغ إليهم إذ لا فائدة إلا ترك صلاة
العيد وإن أنشأوا بين الزوال
والغروب أفطرنا وبان فوات العيد
فإن رأينا قضاءها فبقية اليوم أولى أو يوم الحادي والثلاثين فيه وجهان
ينظر في أحدهما إلى المبادرة وفي الثاني إلى أن تشبه وقت القضاء
بالأداء وفيه وجه أنا نفطر ولا نحكم بفوات الصلاة فإن الغلط ممكن وهذا
شعار عظيم لا يمكن تفويته فيصلي يوم الحادي والثلاثين بنية الأداء
أما إذا شهدوا قبل الغروب ولكن عدلوا بالليل ففي فوات الصلاة وجهان
أحدهما لا لأن النظر إلى وقت التعديل وقد عدل في غير وقته والثاني أن النظر
إلى وقت الشهادة
الرابع إذا كان العيد يوم الجمعة وحضر أهل القرى ممن يبلغهم النداء
فالقياس أنه لا يجوز لهم الانصراف حتى يصلوا الجمعة
وقال العراقيون الصحيح الجواز ورووا عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم كان يرخص لأهل السواد في مثل هذا اليوم في الانصراف
= كتاب صلاة الخسوف=
وهي سنة في سائر الأوقات لأن لها سببا خلافا لأبي حنيفة
ولما مات إبراهيم ولد النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام كسفت الشمس فقال بعض
الناس إنها  كسفت لموته فخطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال إن الشمس
والقمر لآيتان من آيات الله لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك
فافزعوا إلى ذكر الله والصلاة
ثم أقل هذه الصلاة ركعتان ينوي فيها صلاة الخسوف ثم يقرأ الفاتحة ثم يركع
ثم يعتدل فيقرأ الفاتحة ثم يركع على ترتيب سائر الصلوات وكذلك يفعل في
الثانية وفي كل ركعة قيامان وركوعان فلو تمادى الخسوف جاز أن يزيد ثالثا
ورابعا على أحد الوجهين إذ روى أحمد بن حنبل أن الركوع في كل ركعة ثلاث
فليحمل على صورة التمادي
والقياس المنع إن لم يصح الخبر
وكذا الوجهان في أنه بعد الفراغ هل يستأنف صلاة أخرى عند التمادي وكذا
الوجهان في أنه هل يقتصر على ركوع واحد إن أسرع الانجلاء
فأما الأكمل فهو أن يقرأ في القومة الأولى بعد دعاء الاستفتاح سورة
الفاتحة والبقرة وفي الثانية الفاتحة وآل عمران وفي الثالثة الفاتحة
والنساء وفي الرابعة المائدة أو مقدارها من القرآن وذلك بعد الفاتحة في كل
قومة
فأما الركوع فيسبح في الأول مقدار مائة آية وفي الثاني بقدر ثمانين وفي
الثالث بقدر سبعين وفي الرابع بقدر خمسين
وأما السجدات فلا يطولها ونقل البويطي عنه أنها على قدر الركوع الذي قبله
ولا خلاف أن القعدة بين السجدتين لا تطول
ثم إذا فرغ من الصلاة يستحب أن يخطب خطبتين كما في العيد إلا أنه لا يجهر
في الكسوف بالقرآن لأنه نهاري
ويجهر بالخسوف لأنه بالليل
والجماعة فيها مسنونة غير واجبة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ر-ك (taraka)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To leave, abandon, or omit something; the act of leaving behind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Omission of an obligatory act due to forgetfulness (nisyān), distinct from deliberate abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical leaving; here metaphorical for neglecting a ritual component.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, complete, or render a judgment; to discharge an obligation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Making up a missed act of worship after its appointed time (qaḍāʾ vs. adāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to settle a debt; technical: compensatory performance of a ritual.
- Root: ش-ه-د (shahida)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify, or bear evidence; presence at an event.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal testimony (shahādah) establishing the sighting of the crescent moon.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: juridical attestation.
- Root: خ-س-ف (khasafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To eclipse, swallow up, or cause to sink; the darkening of the moon.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Cosmic sign (āyah) of divine power, distinct from kusūf (solar eclipse) in technical usage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the moon's eclipse; metaphorical: any celestial darkening as a portent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Law (Law + Perfect Verb) — The protasis introduced by law (if) governs a counterfactual or hypothetical condition, with the apodosis in the perfect or imperative, indicating a legal ruling contingent upon a past event.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now, four subsidiary branches [arise from the preceding discussion].

The first: If one abandons the takbīrs of a rakʿah forgetfully and recalls them after the recitation, then the explicitly endorsed ruling (al-manṣūṣ) in the new [school position] (al-jadīd) is that he does not pronounce them, because their time has lapsed. But it was said in the old [school position] (al-qadīm) that he pronounces them, because the standing [posture] remains. And among our companions (al-aṣḥāb) are those who extended the old position to the making up of the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ).

The second: If the prayer of the two festivals (ṣalāt al-ʿīdayn) is missed by the passing of the sun [past its zenith], then concerning its making up (qaḍāʾ) there are four opinions: One is that it is not made up. The second is that it is made up, but on the thirty-first day if the thirtieth was missed, because it is possible that this day [the thirty-first] counts as performance (adāʾ). The third is that it is made up throughout the whole of that month. The fourth is that it is made up forever. And its parallel has already preceded in the discussion of supererogatory prayers (al-nawāfil).

The third: If they testify to the sighting of the crescent [of Shawwāl] before the zenith, then we break the fast and pray [the festival prayer]. But if they initiate the testimony after sunset on the thirtieth [day], we do not listen to them, since there is no benefit except the abandonment of the festival prayer. And if they initiate it between the zenith and sunset, then we break the fast and it becomes evident that the festival [prayer] has been missed. Then if we hold that it is to be made up, [whether] the remainder of that day is more appropriate or the thirty-first day — there are two aspects (wajhān): In one, consideration is given to hastening (al-mubādarah); in the second, to making the time of making up resemble the time of performance. And there is an aspect that we break the fast but do not rule that the prayer has been missed, for error is possible, and this is a great emblem (shiʿār) that cannot be allowed to lapse; so one prays on the thirty-first day with the intention of performance (adāʾ). As for when they testify before sunset but then retract (ʿadalū) at night, then concerning the missing of the prayer there are two aspects: One is that it is not [missed], because consideration is given to the time of retraction, and they retracted outside its proper time. The second is that consideration is given to the time of testimony.

The fourth: If the festival falls on a Friday, and the people of the villages — those whom the call [to Friday prayer] reaches — attend, then the analogical ruling (al-qiyās) is that it is not permissible for them to depart until they pray the Friday [prayer]. But the Iraqis said: The correct [position] is permissibility. And they narrated from Abū Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to grant a concession (yurakhkhiṣ) to the people of the outlying districts (ahl al-sawād) on such a day to depart.

= The Book of the Eclipse Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Khusūf) =

It is a sunnah (supererogatory practice) in all times, because it has a cause — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. And when Ibrāhīm, the son of the Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace, died, the sun eclipsed (kusifat), and some people said that it eclipsed due to his death. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon and said: {«إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ آيَتَانِ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَا يَخْسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلَا لِحَيَاتِهِ فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ ذَلِكَ فَافْزَعُوا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَالصَّلَاةِ»} — "The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they do not eclipse for the death of anyone nor for his life. So when you see that, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and to prayer."

Then the minimum of this prayer is two rakʿahs, in which one intends the eclipse prayer (ṣalāt al-khusūf). Then he recites the Fātiḥah, then bows (rukūʿ), then stands upright and recites the Fātiḥah, then bows, following the order of the rest of the prayers. And likewise he does in the second [rakʿah]. In each rakʿah there are two standings (qiyāmān) and two bowings (rukūʿān). If the eclipse continues (tamāddā), it is permissible to add a third and a fourth [bowing] according to one of the two aspects, since Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated that the bowing in each rakʿah is three; so let it be interpreted upon the case of continuation. And the analogical ruling is prohibition if the report is not authenticated. Likewise, there are two aspects concerning whether, after finishing, one begins another prayer when the eclipse continues. And likewise, there are two aspects concerning whether one limits himself to a single bowing if the eclipse clears quickly.

As for the most complete [form], it is that he recites in the first standing, after the opening supplication, the Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and al-Baqarah; in the second, the Fātiḥah and Āl ʿImrān; in the third, the Fātiḥah and al-Nisāʾ; and in the fourth, al-Māʾidah or its equivalent from the Qurʾān — that being after the Fātiḥah in each standing. As for the bowing, he glorifies in the first to the measure of a hundred verses, in the second to the measure of eighty, in the third to the measure of seventy, and in the fourth to the measure of fifty. As for the prostrations (sajdāt), he does not prolong them; and al-Buwayṭī transmitted from him [al-Shāfiʿī] that they are to the measure of the bowing that precedes them. And there is no disagreement that the sitting between the two prostrations is not prolonged.

Then, when he finishes the prayer, it is recommended (yustaḥabb) that he deliver two sermons (khuṭbatān) as in the festival [prayer], except that he does not recite aloud (lā yajhar) the Qurʾān in the solar eclipse (al-kusūf), because it is daytime. And he recites aloud in the lunar eclipse (al-khusūf), because it is nighttime. And the congregation (al-jamāʿah) in it is sunnah, not obligatory.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع ثلاثة

الأول المسبوق إذا أدرك الركوع الثاني نقل البويطي أنه لا يكون مدركا لأن
الأصل هو الأول وقال صاحب التقريب يصير مدركا للقومة التي قبلها فبقي عليه
قيام واحد وركوع واحد والأول أصح
الثاني تفوت صلاة الكسوف بالانجلاء وبغروب الشمس كاسفة وتفوت صلاة الخسوف
بالانجلاء وبطلوع قرص الشمس ولا تفوت غروب القمر في جنح الليل خاسفا لأن
الليل باق وسلطان القمر في جميعه
وهل تفوت بطلوع الصبح فيه قولان الجديد أنه لا  تفوت لبقاء سلطنة القمر
بدوام الظلمة
الثالث إذا اجتمع عيد وخسوف وخيف الفوات فالعيد أولى وإن اتسع الوقت
فقولان
أحدهما الخسوف أولى لأنه على عرض الفوات بالانجلاء والثاني العيد أولى
لأنه سنة مؤكدة ربما يعوض عنها عائق ولو أنكر منجم وجود الكسوف يوم العيد
لم نرده على قولنا إن الله على كل شيء قدير
ولو اجتمع كسوف وجمعة قدمنا الجمعة إن خفنا فواتها وإلا فقولان كما في
العيد ثم قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه يخطب للجمعة والكسوف خطبة واحدة يتعرض
فيها للكسوف وللجمعة حتى لا يطول الوقت ولا بأس بوقوع الخطبة قبل صلاة
الكسوف لأنها ليست من شرائطها وكذا يفعل عند اجتماع العيد والكسوف
ولو اجتمع جنازة مع هذه الصلوات فهي مقدمة إلا مع الجمعة عند ضيق الوقت
ففيه خلاف والأصح تقديم الجمعة
ووجه تقديم الجنازة أن الجمعة لها بدل
ثم قال الشافعي ولا يبرز بالناس لأنه ربما يفوت بالبروز ولا يصلى لغير
الخسوفين من الآيات كالزلازل وغيرها
= كتاب صلاة الاستسقاء=
وهي سنة عرفت من فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أبو حنيفة بدعة
وسببها أن ينقطع ماء السماء أو العيون فتستحب عنده صلاة الاستسقاء ولو
أخبرنا أن طائفة من المسلمين ابتلوا به فيسن لنا أن نستسقي لهم لأن
المسلمين كنفس واحدة
ثم إن سقوا يوم الخروج فذاك وإن تمادى كررنا ثانيا وثالثا كما يراه
الإمام فإن سقوا
قبل الاستسقاء خرجوا للشكر والموعظة وفي أداء الصلاة للشكر وجهان وكذا في
أدائها للاستزادة في النعمة
ثم أقل هذه الصلاة كأقل صلاة العيد ووقتها وقتها
وأكملها أن يأمر الإمام الناس بالتوبة والخروج من المظالم وأن يستحل
بعضهم بعضا
ويأمرهم بالصوم ثلاثة أيام ثم يخرجون في الرابع في ثياب بذلة وتخشع بخلاف
العيد
ويستحب إخراج الصبيان وفي إخراج البهائم قصدا تردد ولا بأس بخروج أهل
الذمة ويحازون إلى جانب
ومن أصحابنا من قال هي كصلاة العيد إلا أنه يبدل
السورة في إحدى الركعتين فيقرأ {إنا أرسلنا نوحا} لاشتمالها على قوله
تعالى  {يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا}
ثم يخطب الإمام بعد الفراغ خطبتين كما في العيد لكن يبدل التكبيرات
بالاستغفار ثم يلحقه بالدعاء في الخطبة الثانية ويستقبل القبلة فيهما
ويستدبر الناس ثم يحول رداءه تفاؤلا بتحويل الحال وتأسيا برسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم فيقلب الأعلى إلى الأسفل واليمين إلى اليسار والظاهر إلى
الباطن
وكان على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خميصة فتعذر عليه لما حاول قلبها
من الأعلى إلى الأسفل فترك
فرأى الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الجديد الإتيان بما هم به رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم أولى
ويستحب أن يدعو في الخطبة الأولى ويقول اللهم اسقنا غيثا مغيثا هنيئا
مريئا مريعا غدقا مجللا طبقا سحا دائما اللهم اسقنا الغيث ولا تجعلنا من
القانطين اللهم إن بالعباد والبلاد من اللأواء والضنك والجهد ما لا نشكو
إلا إليك اللهم أنبت لنا الزرع وأدر لنا الضرع واسقنا من بركات السماء
اللهم ارفع عنا الجهد والجوع والعري واكشف عنا ما لا يكشفه غيرك اللهم إنا
نستغفرك إنك كنت غفارا فأرسل السماء علينا مدرارا والله أعلم
= كتاب الجنائز =
والنظر فيه يتعلق بآداب المحتضر وبعسل الميت وتزيينه وتكفينه وحمل جنازته
والصلاة عليه ودفنه والتعزية والبكاء عليه
فتجري فيه على ترتيب الوجود اعتيادا

### | القول في المحتضر

من أشرف على الموت فليستقبل به القبلة وهو أن يلقى على قفاه وأخمصاه إلى
القبلة
وقيل إنه يلقى على جنبه الأيمن كما يفعل به في لحده ويستحب أن يلقن كلمتي
الشهادة برفق من غير إضجار وأن تتلى بين يديه سورة يس
وليكن هو في نفسه حسن الظن بالله عز وجل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم لا يموتن أحدكم إلا وهو يحسن الظن بالله
ثم إذا فاضت نفسه تغمض عيناه ويشد لحياه بعصابة كيلا يتشوه خلقه وتلين
مفاصله كيلا يتصلب ويصان عن الثياب المدفئة فإنها يسرع إليه الفساد فيستر
بثوب خفيف ويوضع على بطنه سيف أو مرآة كيلا يربو بطنه ولا يوضع عليه مصحف

### | القول في الغسل

والنظر في  كيفيته وفي الغاسل

### | أما الكيفية

فأقله إمرار الماء على جميع الأعضاء كما في الجنابة
وفي النية وجهان أحدهما لا تجب لتعذرها على المغسول والثاني أنها تجب على
الغاسل وإنما الميت محل الغسل وعلى هذا يبتنى غسل الكافر ومن لفظه البحر
وانغسلت أعضاؤه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ب-ق (sabaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To precede, outstrip, go before; the one preceded (masbūq) is he who arrives late to congregational prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal priority establishing legal precedence; the first unit (rakʿah) is the foundational origin (aṣl) for the latecomer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of overtaking; here used technically for catching a portion of the prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — "If he caught the second bowing (rukūʿ)" sets a hypothetical condition governing the legal ruling that follows.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section comprises three subsidiary branches.

**The First Branch:** Concerning the one preceded (al-masbūq) — if he catches the second bowing (rukūʿ), al-Buwayṭī transmitted that he is not deemed a catcher (mudrik), because the original (al-aṣl) is the first [bowing]. The author of al-Taqrīb said: He becomes a catcher of the standing (qawmah) that preceded it, so there remains upon him one standing and one bowing. The first opinion is the more correct (aṣaḥḥ).

**The Second Branch:** The eclipse prayer of the sun (ṣalāt al-kusūf) is rendered void (tafūt) by the dispelling [of the eclipse] and by the setting of the sun while eclipsed. The eclipse prayer of the moon (ṣalāt al-khusūf) is rendered void by the dispelling [of the eclipse] and by the rising of the sun's disk. It is not rendered void by the setting of the moon while eclipsed in the depths of the night, because the night remains and the dominion (sulṭān) of the moon extends throughout it. Is it rendered void by the advent of dawn? There are two opinions (qawlān): the new opinion (al-jadīd) is that it is not rendered void, due to the persistence of the moon's dominion through the continuance of darkness.

**The Third Branch:** If a festival (ʿīd) and a lunar eclipse coincide, and the loss [of the eclipse prayer] is feared, then the festival takes precedence. If the time is ample, there are two opinions: One of them is that the eclipse prayer takes precedence, because it is exposed to loss by the dispelling [of the eclipse]; the second is that the festival takes precedence, because it is an emphatic Sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah) which perhaps might be compensated for by an obstacle. If an astrologer denied the occurrence of an eclipse on the day of the festival, we would not reject him, upon our saying that God is powerful over all things.

If an eclipse and a Friday [prayer] coincide, we give precedence to the Friday [prayer] if we fear its loss; otherwise, there are two opinions, as in the case of the festival. Then al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said: He delivers for the Friday and the eclipse one single sermon (khuṭbah), in which he touches upon both the eclipse and the Friday, so that the time is not prolonged. There is no harm in the sermon occurring before the eclipse prayer, because it is not among its conditions. Likewise is done when the festival and the eclipse coincide.

If a funeral (janāzah) coincides with these prayers, it is given precedence — except with the Friday [prayer] when time is constrained, for therein is a disagreement, and the more correct (aṣaḥḥ) is to give precedence to the Friday. The rationale for giving precedence to the funeral is that the Friday has a substitute (badal).

Then al-Shāfiʿī said: He does not go out with the people [to the open ground], because perhaps [the prayer] might be lost by going out. Nor is prayer performed for other portents (āyāt) besides the two eclipses, such as earthquakes and other [phenomena].

---

**The Book of the Rain Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Istisqāʾ)**

It is a Sunnah known from the action of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abū Ḥanīfah said it is an innovation (bidʿah). Its cause is the cessation of the water of the sky or of the springs. In his view, the rain prayer is recommended (mustaḥabb). If we are informed that a group of Muslims has been afflicted by this, it is Sunnah for us to pray for rain on their behalf, because the Muslims are as one soul.

Then if they are given rain on the day of going out, that is [sufficient]. If [the drought] continues, we repeat it a second and third time, as the Imām deems fit. If they are given rain before the [prayer for] rain, they go out for thanksgiving and admonition. Regarding the performance of the prayer for thanksgiving, there are two aspects (wajhān); likewise regarding its performance for seeking increase in blessing.

Then the minimum of this prayer is like the minimum of the festival prayer, and its time is its time. Its most complete form is that the Imām commands the people to repent and to relinquish injustices, and that they seek mutual absolution from one another. He commands them to fast three days, then they go out on the fourth day in worn garments and humility, contrary to the festival [attire]. It is recommended to bring out the children. Regarding deliberately bringing out the beasts, there is hesitation (taraddud). There is no harm in the people of the dhimmah going out, and they are segregated to one side.

Among our companions is one who said: It is like the festival prayer, except that the sūrah is changed in one of the two rakʿahs, so he recites {«innā arsalnā nūḥan»} (We sent Noah) due to its inclusion of His saying, the Exalted: {«yursili al-samāʾa ʿalaykum midrāran»} (He will send the sky upon you in torrents).

Then the Imām delivers, after finishing, two sermons as in the festival, except that he replaces the takbīrs with seeking forgiveness (istighfār). Then he appends supplication (duʿāʾ) in the second sermon. He faces the qiblah in both, and turns his back to the people. Then he turns his cloak (ridāʾ) around, as an omen of the transformation of the situation (tafāʾulan bi-taḥwīl al-ḥāl) and in emulation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace — turning the upper to the lower, the right to the left, and the outer to the inner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wearing a striped cloak (khamīṣah), and when he attempted to turn it from upper to lower it became difficult for him, so he left it. Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, held in the new opinion (al-jadīd) that performing what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended is more appropriate.

It is recommended that he supplicate in the first sermon and say: "O God, give us rain — a saving rain, wholesome, nourishing, abundant, covering, overwhelming, pouring, continuous. O God, give us the rain and make us not among the despairing. O God, indeed the servants and the lands are afflicted with distress, hardship, and toil such that we complain to none but You. O God, cause our crops to grow, and make our udders flow, and give us from the blessings of the sky. O God, lift from us toil, hunger, and nakedness, and unveil from us what none but You can unveil. O God, we seek Your forgiveness, for You are ever-Forgiving, so send the sky upon us in torrents." And God knows best.

---

**The Book of Funerals (Janāʾiz)**

The consideration therein pertains to the etiquette of the dying person, the washing of the deceased, his perfuming, his shrouding, the carrying of his bier, the prayer over him, his burial, condolence, and weeping over him. I shall proceed therein according to the customary order of existence.

---

**The Chapter on the Dying Person (al-Muḥtaḍar)**

Whoever is on the verge of death — let him be turned to face the qiblah, which is done by laying him on his back with the soles of his feet toward the qiblah. It is said he is laid on his right side, as is done with him in his grave niche (laḥd). It is recommended that he be prompted (talqīn) with the two words of testimony gently, without annoyance, and that Sūrat Yā Sīn be recited before him. Let him himself have a good opinion of God, the Mighty and Majestic. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Let none of you die except while having a good opinion of God."

Then when his soul departs, his eyes are closed, and his jaw is bound with a band so that his form is not disfigured, and his joints are loosened so that he does not stiffen. He is protected from warming garments, for corruption hastens upon him [through them]; rather, he is covered with a light cloth. A sword or a mirror is placed upon his belly so that his belly does not swell. A muṣḥaf is not placed upon him.

---

**The Chapter on Washing (al-Ghusl)**

The consideration pertains to its modality and to the washer.

**As for the modality:** Its minimum is passing water over all the limbs, as in major ritual impurity (janābah). Regarding the intention (niyyah), there are two aspects: One of them is that it is not obligatory, due to its impossibility for the one washed; the second is that it is obligatory upon the washer, and the deceased is merely the locus of the washing. Upon this is built the washing of the disbeliever, and of one whom the sea cast forth and whose limbs were washed away.

chapters.title_en: Section 75 — On the Complete Washing of the Dead: Preliminary Matters, the Washer, and Adornment
chapters.arabic_text:
### | أما الأكمل فلتقدم عليه ثلاثة أمور

الأول أن ينقل إلى موضع خال على لوح مهيأ لذلك ولا ينزع قميصه بل يغسل
فيه وإن مست الحاجة إلى مس بدنه فتق الغاسل القميص وأدخل يده فيه وإن نزع
القميص جاز ولكن يستر عورته إذ يحرم النظر إليها ويكره النظر إلى جميع بدنه
إلا للحاجة
الثاني أن يحضر ماء باردا كيلا يتسارع إليه الفساد وليكن طاهرا طهورا ولو
استعمل السدر في بعض الغسلات جاز لكن المتغير بالسدر لا يتأدى به الغرض
خلافا لأبي إسحاق المروزي
وينبغي أن يعد موضعا كبيرا للماء وينحيه عن المغتسل بحيث لا يصل إليه
رشاش الماء المستعمل
الثالث أن يبدأ بالاستنجاء فليجلس الميت ويمسح يده على بطنه متحاملا
بقوته لتنتفض الفضلات وعنده تكون المحجرة متقدة فائحة بالطيب ثم يرده إلى
هيئة الاستلقاء ويلف خرقة على يده ويغسل إحدى سوأتيه مبالغا فيه ثم يبدل
الخرقة ويغسل الأخرى وإن كان على بدنه نجاسة أزالها ثم يتعهد أسنانه
ومنخريه بخرقة نظيفة مبلولة ويكون ذلك كالسواك ثم يوضئه ثلاثا مع المضمضة
والاستنشاق فإن كانت أسنانه متراصة فلا يفتحها للمضمضة بل يوصل الماء إلى
أفرة وإن كانت مفتوحة ففي إيصال الماء إلى داخل الفم تردد خيفة من
تسارع الفساد ثم يتعهد شعره بمشط واسع الأسنان احترازا عن النتف ثم يبتدأ
بالغسل
وكيفيته أن يضجعه على جنبه الأيسر ويصب الماء على شقه الأيمن مبتدئا من
رأسه إلى قدمه ثم يضجعه على الشق الأيمن وكذلك يفعل بالشق الأيسر وهي غسلة
واحدة ثم يفعل ذلك ثلاثا ويمر في كل نوبة اليد على بطنه لخروج الفضلات فإن
حصل النقاء بثلاث فذاك وإلا فخمس أو سبع ثم يبالغ في نشفه صيانة للكفن عن
الرطوبة ويستعمل قدرا من  الكافور لدفع الهوام

### | فرعان

أحدهما لو خرجت منه نجاسة بعد الغسل ففيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدهما أنه يعيد
الكل
الثاني أنه يعيد الوضوء دون الغسل الثالث يقتصر على إزالة النجاسة
الثاني لو احترق مسلم وكان في غسله ما يهرئه يممناه ولو كان عليه قروح
وغسله يسرع إليه الفساد غسلناه لأن مصيره إلى البلى

### | النظر الثاني في الغاسل

ويجوز للرجال غسل الرجال وللنساء غسل النساء وعند اختلاف الجنس فلا يجوز
إلا بزوجية أو محرمية ويجوز بملك اليمين للسيد في أمته ومستولداته وهل
ويجوز لهما غسل السيد فوجهان
أحدهما نعم كالزوجة والثاني لا لأنهما صارتا أجنبيتين بالعنق والانتقال
إلى الورثة

### | فرعان

الأول لو ماتت امرأة ولم تجد إلا رجلا أجنبيا أو مات رجل ولم يجد إلا
أجنبية تولى الغسل من حضر مع عض البصر وكذا الخنثى يتولى غسله إما الرجال
وإما النساء استصحابا لحكم الصغر
وقيل يتيمم في هذه الصور وفقد الغاسل كفقد الماء وهو بعيد
الثاني إذا ازدحم جمع يصلحون للغسل على امرأة فالبداية بنساء المحارم ثم
بعدهن بالأجنبيات ثم بالزوج ثم برجال المحارم وترتيب المحارم كترتيبهم في
الصلاة هذه طريقة المراوزة
وذكر العراقيون وجها في تقديم الزوج على نساء المحارم لأنه ينظر إلى ما
لا ينظرون إليه ووجها في تقديم رجال المحارم على الزوج لأن النكاح منقطع
بالموت ولا شك أن المسلم الأجنبي أولى من القريب المشرك
هنا إذا تنافسوا فإن تواكلوا فللمتأخر أن يتعاطى الغسل
قال الشيخ أبو محمد الترتيب بين الرجال والنساء واجب لا يدخله الخيرة أما
التواكل بين الرجال أو بين النساء فغير ممتنع

### | القول في التزيين

وفي قلم أظفار الميت وحلق شعره الذى كان يحلقه ندبا في حال الحياة قولان
أحدهما يستحب لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام افعلوا بموتاكم ما تفعلون
بأحيائكم والثاني لا لأن حكم الموت شامل لأجزائه فلا يفصل منه شئ
أما المحرم فلا يحلق شعره ولا يخمر رأسه إن كان رجلا ووجهه إن كانت امرأة
ولا يقرب طيبا
وفي صيانة المعتدة عن الطيب وجهان ووجه  الفرق أن امتناعها تحرز عن الرجال
أو تفجع على الزوج وقد فات بالموت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-م-ل (K-M-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Completeness, perfection, that which has no deficiency in any of its parts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "most complete" (al-akmal) form of an act is that which fulfills all its conditions and recommended adjuncts, as opposed to the merely sufficient (mujzi').
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of totality; here used technically to denote the fullest ritual performance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with "Law" (Law + māḍī) — expressing hypothetical or counterfactual conditions, governing the permissibility clauses in the text.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the most complete [form of washing], three matters precede it.

The first: that [the deceased] be moved to an empty place, upon a board prepared for that purpose, and his shirt shall not be removed; rather, he is washed therein. If there be need to touch his body, the washer tears the shirt and inserts his hand within it. If he removes the shirt, it is permissible, but he must cover his private parts, for looking upon them is unlawful, and it is disliked to look upon his entire body save for necessity.

The second: that cool water be prepared, lest corruption hasten to him, and it must be pure and purifying. If sidr (lote leaves) be used in some of the washings, it is permissible; however, water altered by sidr does not accomplish the purpose [of purification], contrary to Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī. One should also prepare a spacious place for the water and set it apart from the washing area, such that the spray of the used water does not reach it.

The third: that he begin with the istinjā' (cleansing of the privates). The deceased is seated, and [the washer] passes his hand over his belly with gentle pressure to expel the residues. At that time, the privy area should be heated and fragrant with perfume. Then he returns him to the reclining posture, wraps a cloth around his hand, and washes one of the two private parts with thoroughness. Then he changes the cloth and washes the other. If there be any impurity on his body, he removes it. Then he attends to his teeth and nostrils with a clean, moistened cloth, and this serves as the siwāk. Then he performs the ablution (wuḍū') for him three times, including the rinsing of the mouth (maḍmaḍah) and the snuffing of water into the nose (istinshāq). If his teeth are tightly set, he does not open them for the mouth-rinse; rather, he conveys water to the outer edge. If they are parted, there is hesitation (taraddud) regarding conveying water into the interior of the mouth, out of fear of hastening corruption. Then he attends to his hair with a wide-toothed comb, guarding against plucking. Then he commences the washing.

Its manner: he lays him on his left side and pours water over his right side, beginning from his head to his foot. Then he lays him on his right side and does likewise with his left side — this is one washing. Then he does this three times, passing his hand over his belly in each turn to expel residues. If cleanliness is attained with three, that suffices; otherwise, five or seven. Then he is thorough in drying him, to preserve the shroud from moisture, and he uses a measure of camphor to repel vermin.

### Two Subsidiary Issues

The first: if impurity issues from him after the washing, there are three views (awjuh): one, that he repeats the entire washing; the second, that he repeats the ablution (wuḍū') but not the full washing; the third, that he confines himself to removing the impurity.

The second: if a Muslim is burned [to death], and washing him would cause him to disintegrate, we perform tayammum for him. If he has wounds upon him, and washing would hasten his corruption, we wash him nonetheless, for his end is decay.

### The Second Consideration: Concerning the Washer

It is permissible for men to wash men, and for women to wash women. When the sexes differ, it is not permissible save by marriage or by close kinship (maḥramiyyah). It is permissible by right of ownership (milk al-yamīn) for the master to wash his slave-girl and his umm walad (concubine who bore his child). As to whether it is permissible for them to wash the master, there are two views: one, yes, like the wife; the second, no, for they have become strangers to him by virtue of manumission upon his death and their transfer to the heirs.

### Two Subsidiary Issues

The first: if a woman dies and no one is found save an unrelated man, or a man dies and no unrelated woman is found, then whoever is present undertakes the washing with lowered gaze. Likewise, the hermaphrodite (khunthā) is washed by either men or women, following the ruling of minority [status]. It is said that tayammum is performed in these cases, for the absence of a washer is like the absence of water — but this is remote.

The second: if a group of those qualified to wash a woman crowd together, the beginning is with the women of her maḥram kin, then after them the unrelated women, then the husband, then the maḥram men. The order of the maḥram kin is like their order in the prayer [leadership]. This is the method of the Marwazīs. The Iraqis mention a view preferring the husband over the maḥram women, for he looks upon what they do not look upon, and a view preferring the maḥram men over the husband, for the marriage tie is severed by death. There is no doubt that an unrelated Muslim is more worthy than a polytheist relative.

Here, if they vie with one another and then all decline, it is incumbent upon the last [remaining] to undertake the washing. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: the ordering between men and women is obligatory, and no choice enters into it. As for mutual declination among men or among women, it is not precluded.

### The Discourse on Adornment

Regarding trimming the nails of the deceased and shaving the hair that he used to shave as a recommended practice during life, there are two views. One: it is recommended (mustaḥabb), due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«افعلوا بموتاكم ما تفعلون بأحيائكم»} ("Do with your dead what you do with your living"). The second: no, for the ruling of death encompasses all his parts, and nothing is separated from him. As for the one in iḥrām (pilgrim's consecration), his hair is not shaved, nor is his head covered if he be a man, nor his face if she be a woman, and no perfume is brought near him. Regarding shielding the woman in ʿiddah (waiting period) from perfume, there are two views. The point of distinction is that her abstention is either to guard against men or as mourning for the husband — and that [purpose] has lapsed with death.

chapters.title_en: Section 76 — On Shrouding, Carrying the Bier, and the Funeral Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في التكفين

وأحب الثياب إلى الله البيض ولبكن جنسه القطن أو الكتان أما الحرير فيحرم
على الرجال ويكره للنساء لأجل السرف
وأقل الكفن ثوب واحد ساتر لجميع البدن فلو أوصى بما دون ذلك لم ينفذ لأنه
حق الشرع
فأما الثاني والثالث فهو حق الميت ينفذ وصيته في إسقاطها والصحيح أن
الورثة يلزمهم الثاني والثالث وهل للغرماء المنازعة فيها
فيه وجهان أحدهما نعم لأن تبرئه ذمته أولى من الزيادة على واحد والثاني
لا لأن ذلك من تجمله بعد الموت فهو كعمايتة ودراعته في حال حياته
فأما المرأة إن لم تخلف مالا فهل يجب على زوجها تجهيزها فوجهان
أحدهما لا لأن النكاح قد انتهى الثاني نعم لأن النكاح قد استقر وأوجب
الإرث وهذه آخر حاجاتها في الكسوة فإن لم نوجب على الزوج فتكفين كل فقير من
بيت المال ولكن بثوب واحد أو بثلاثة فيه وجهان الظاهر أنه ثوب واحد
أما الأكمل فهو الثلاث في حق الرجال والزيادة إلى الخمس جائز من غير
استحباب وفي حق النساء مستحب والزيادة على الخمس سرف على الإطلاق
ثم إن كفن في خمس فعمامة وقميص وثلاث لفائف وإن كفن في ثلاث فثلاث لفائف
من غير قميص ولا عمائم كلها سوابغ
وإن كفنت في خمس فإزار وخمار وثلاث لفائف وفي قول تبدل لفافة بقميص وإن
كفنت في ثلاث فثلاث لفائف وإنما التردد في القميص إذا كفنت في خمس
أما كيفية الإدراج في الكفن فأن يفرش اللفافة العليا ويذر عليها الحنوط
ويبسط عليها الثانية ويذر عليها الحنوط ويبسط الثالثة ويزاد في الحنوط
ويوضع الميت عليها ثم يأخذ قدرا صالحا من القطن الحليج ويلف قدرا منه ويدسه
في الأليتين ثم يبسط عليه قدرا عريضا من القطن ويشد الأليتين ويستوثق كيلا
يخرج منه خارج ثم يعمد إلى المنافذ من العين والفم والأنف والأذن ويلصق بكل
موضع قطنه عليها كافور ثم يلف الكفن عليه
ويستحب أن يبخر الكفن  بالعود وهو أولى من المسك وفي كون الحنوط واجبا أو
مستحبا وجهان والصحيح أنه مستحب

### | القول في حمل الجنازة

والأولى أن يحمله ثلاثة ويكون السابق بين العمودين فإن لم يستقل بحمل
