الخشبتين فرجلان من جانبيه وهو بين العمودين فيكونون خمسة
وقال أبو حنيفة الحمل بين العمودين بدعة ومن أراد أن يحمل الجنازة
فليحملها من جميع جوانبها فيحمل على عاتقه الأيمن مقدمة الجنازة ثم يرجع
إلى مقابله من مؤخرتها ثم
يفعل ذلك بالشق الآخر
ثم المشي أمام الجنازة أفضل عندنا
وقال أبو حنيفة خلفها أفضل
وقال أحمد إن كان راكبا فخلفها وإن كان ماشيا فأمامها
والمشي أفضل من الركوب والإسراع بالجنازة أولى قال رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن كان خيرا فإلى خير تقدمونه وإن كان غير ذلك فبعدا لأهل النار

### | القول في الصلاة على الميت

والنظر في أربعة أطراف

### | الأول فيمن يصلى عليه

وهو كل ميت مسلم ليس بشهيد فهذ ثلاثة قيود

### | القيد الأول الميت

وفيه مسألتان الأولى لو صادفنا عضو آدمي واحتمل كون صاحبه حيا لم نصل
عليه وإن قطع بموت صاحبه غسلناه وصلينا عليه وواريناه بخرقة ودفناه وتكون
هذه الصلاة على الميت الغائب
وقال أبو حنيفة لا يصلى عليه إلا إذا وجد النصف الأكبر فإنه لا تجوز
الصلاة على الغائب عنده
الثانية السقط إن خرج واستهل فهو كالكبير وإن لم يظهر عليه التخطيط
فيوارى
في خرقة ولا يغسل ولا يصلى عليه لأنه لم يتحقق حياته
وإن ظهر شكل الآدمي ففيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه كالكبير استدلالا بالشكل
على الروح والثاني لا يغسل ولا يصلى عليه لأنه لم تحقق حياته والثالث أنه
يغسل ولا يصلى عليه والدفن يجب قولا واحدا والكفن لا يجب إكماله إلا إذا
أوجبنا الصلاة وإن اختلج بعد الانفصال قليلا ثم سكن فالخلاف هاهنا مرتب
وأولى بأن يعتقد حياته

### | القيد الثاني

الإسلام فلا يصلى قط على كافر ولا على مبتدع يكفر في بدعته وإن كان
الكافر حربيا فلا يجب دفنه
وأما الذمي فتحرم الصلاة عليه  ولكن دفنه وتكفينه من فروض الكفايات وفاء
بالذمة
وفي كلام الصيدلاني إشارة إلى أنه كالحربي إذ لم يبق له ذمة بعد الموت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-ن (k-f-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wrap, enshroud, cover entirely; the garment in which the dead is wrapped.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The covering of the body's defects in preparation for meeting God; a right of the deceased (ḥaqq al-mayyit) and of sacred law.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical wrapping; metaphorical (majāz) for concealing faults in life.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — "If... then..." constructions (law/fa-) govern legal hypotheticals, requiring protasis-apodosis precision.
chapters.translation:
I say: The most beloved garments to God are white, and its type is cotton or linen. As for silk, it is forbidden (ḥarām) for men and disliked (makrūh) for women due to extravagance (sarf).

The minimum shroud is a single garment covering the entire body. If one bequeaths less than that, it is not executed, for it is a right of the sacred law (ḥaqq al-sharʿ).

As for the second and third [garments], it is the right of the deceased; his bequest to waive them is executed. The correct [position] is that the heirs are obligated [to provide] the second and third. Whether creditors may contest this — there are two views (wajhān): One, yes, because clearing his debt is more incumbent than adding beyond one. Two, no, because this is part of his adornment after death, like his turban and his robe during his life.

As for a woman who leaves no wealth — is her husband obligated to equip her? There are two views: One, no, because the marriage contract has ended. Two, yes, because the marriage has been established (istaqarra) and necessitated inheritance, and this is her final need in clothing. If we do not obligate the husband, then every poor person is shrouded from the public treasury (bayt al-māl) — but with one garment or three? There are two views; the apparent one is a single garment.

As for the most complete (akmal), it is three for men, and increase to five is permissible without recommendation (istihbāb). For women, [five] is recommended (mustaḥabb). Exceeding five is extravagance absolutely.

Then, if shrouded in five: a turban (ʿimāmah), a shirt (qamīṣ), and three wrappers (lafāʾif). If shrouded in three: three wrappers without shirt or turbans — all must be ample (sawābigh). If a woman is shrouded in five: a waist-wrapper (izār), a head-veil (khimār), and three wrappers. In one saying, a wrapper is replaced by a shirt. If shrouded in three: three wrappers. The hesitation concerns the shirt only when shrouded in five.

As for the manner of wrapping in the shroud: one spreads the uppermost wrapper, sprinkles ḥanūṭ (funeral perfume) upon it, spreads the second over it, sprinkles ḥanūṭ, spreads the third, and increases the ḥanūṭ. The deceased is placed upon it. Then one takes a suitable amount of carded cotton, rolls a portion, and tucks it between the buttocks. Then one spreads a wide piece of cotton over him, binds the buttocks firmly so nothing exits from him. Then one attends to the orifices — eyes, mouth, nose, ears — affixing to each place cotton with camphor upon it. Then one wraps the shroud over him.

It is recommended to fumigate the shroud with aloeswood (ʿūd), which is preferable to musk. Whether ḥanūṭ is obligatory or recommended — there are two views; the correct one is that it is recommended.

I say: As for carrying the bier (janāzah), the preferable [method] is that three carry it, with the lead [carrier] between the two poles. If he cannot bear the two planks alone, then two men [carry] from his sides while he is between the poles, making five.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: Carrying between the two poles is an innovation (bidʿah). Whoever wishes to carry the bier should carry it from all its sides: he bears on his right shoulder the front of the bier, then returns to its opposite at the rear, then does likewise on the other side.

Then, walking before the bier is superior (afḍal) in our [school]. Abū Ḥanīfah said: Behind it is superior. Aḥmad said: If riding, then behind it; if walking, then before it. Walking is superior to riding. Hastening with the bier is more appropriate. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«إن كان خيرا فإلى خير تقدمونه وإن كان غير ذلك فبعدا لأهل النار»} — "If it is good, then you advance it toward good; if it is otherwise, then away with the people of the Fire."

I say: As for the prayer over the deceased, the consideration is in four aspects.

The first aspect: On whom is the prayer offered? It is every deceased Muslim who is not a martyr (shahīd). Thus there are three restrictions.

The first restriction: The deceased. In it are two questions. First: If we encounter a human limb and it is possible its owner is alive, we do not pray over it. But if his death is certain, we wash it, pray over it, wrap it in a rag, and bury it. This prayer is [like] the prayer over the absent deceased (ṣalāt al-ghāʾib). Abū Ḥanīfah said: One does not pray over it unless the greater half is found, for prayer over the absent is not permissible in his view.

Second: A miscarried fetus (saqṭ) — if it emerges and cries out, it is like an adult. If no tracing of form (takhtīṭ) appears, it is wrapped in a rag, not washed, and no prayer is offered over it, because its life is not verified. If the human form appears, there are three sayings: One, it is like an adult, inferring the soul from the form. Two, it is not washed nor prayed over, because its life is not verified. Three, it is washed but not prayed over. Burial is obligatory by unanimous saying (qawl wāḥid). The shroud need not be completed unless we deem the prayer obligatory. If it stirred briefly after separation then settled, the disagreement here is ordered, and it is more fitting to deem its life established.

The second restriction: Islam. Prayer is never offered over an unbeliever (kāfir), nor over an innovator (mubtadiʿ) deemed an unbeliever in his innovation. If the unbeliever is a combatant (ḥarbī), his burial is not obligatory. As for a dhimmī, prayer over him is forbidden, but his burial and shrouding are communal obligations (furūḍ al-kifāyāt), fulfilling the covenant (dhimmah). In al-Ṣaydalānī's speech there is an indication that he is like the combatant, since no covenant remains for him after death.

chapters.title_en: Section 77 — On the Martyrs, the Prayer over the Dead, and the Imam's Station
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع إذا اختلط موتى المسلمين بالمشركين نغسلهم ونكفنهم تقصيا عن الواجب ثم عند الصلاة نميز المسلمين عن الكافرين بالنية القيد الثالث الشهادة فلا يغسل شهيد ولا يصلى عليه والشهيد من مات بسبب القتال مع الكفار في وقت قيام القتال فهذه ثلاثة معان فإن كان في قتال أهل البغي أو مات حتف أنفه في قتال الكفار أو مات بعد انقضاء القتال بجراحة مثخنة أصابته في القتال أو قتله الحربي اغتيالا من غير قتال ففي الكل قولان أحدهما يثبت له حكم الشهادة للاشتراك في المعنى والثاني لا لأن لكل وصف من هذه الأوصاف أثرا ولا خلاف أن من أصابه في القتال سلاح مسلم أو وطأته دواب المسلمين فمات فهو شهيد ولا خلاف أن المجروح إذا كان يتوقع حياته فمات بعد انقضاء القتال فليس بشهيد وإنما القولان فيمن يقطع بأنه يموت إذا بقيت فيه حياة مستقرة فأما القتيل ظلما من مسلم أو ذمي أو المبطون أو الغريب إذا مات فهؤلاء يصلى عليهم وإن ورد فيهم لفظ الشهادة والقتيل بالحق قصاصا أو حدا ليس بشهيد ### | فرعان أحدهما تارك الصلاة إذا قتل يصلى عليه قال صاحب التلخيص يطمس قبره ولا يكفن ولا يصلى عليه تحقيرا له وهو بعيد الثاني قاطع الطريق إذا صلب قيل لا يصلى عليه تغليظا والظاهر أنه يغسل ويصلى عليه وإن قلنا إنه يترك مصلوبا حتى يتهرى فالطريق أن نقتله أولا ونغسله ونصلي عليه ونصلبه في كفنه وكأن الهواء قبره وإن قلنا يقتل مصلوبا فينزل بعد القتل ويصلى عليه ويدفن ومن يرى أنه يقتل مصلوبا ويبقى فلا يتمكن من الصلاة فإن قيل فبماذا يفارق الشهيد غيره قلنا في أربعة أمور الأول الغسل فإنه حرام في حقه وإن كان جنبا لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام زملوهم بكلومهم ودمائهم فإنهم يحشرون يوم القيامة وأوداجهم تشخب دما فاللون لون الدم والريح ريح المسك وخرج ابن سريج وجها في الجنب أنه يغسل الثاني الصلاة عليه حرام عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة ومن أصحابنا من قال جائز ولكنه غير واجب الثالث لا يزال دم الشهادة وهل يزال سائر النجاسات فيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها نعم لأن المعفو عنه أثر الشهادة والثاني لا لأن إزالتها يؤدي إلى إزالة أثر الشهادة والثالث أنه إن كان يؤدي إلى الإزالة فلا يزال وإلا فيزال الأمر الرابع التكفين في حقه كهو في حق غيره إلا أن الثياب الملطخة بالدم لا ينزع ولو نزعه الوارث أو أبدله فلا يمنع وأما الدرع والثياب الخشنة فلا شك في نزعها ### | الطرف الثاني فيمن يصلي والنظر في صفة الإمام وموقفه أما الصفة فالأولى بالصلاة القريب ولا يقدم على القرابة إلا الذكورة حتى يقدم صبي مراهق على امرأة والوالي يقدم على القريب في القديم ثم ترتيب الأقارب أن يبدأ بالأب ثم الجد ثم الابن ثم العصبات على ترتيبهم في الولاية ثم في تقديم الأخ من الأب والأم على الأخ من الأب طريقان أحدهما أن فيه قولين كما في النكاح والصحيح التقديم لأن لقرابة النساء مدخلا في الصلاة وكذلك إذا فقدنا العصبات قدمنا ذوي الأرحام والأولى تقديم المعتق عليهم كما في الإرث ### | ### | فرعان أحدهما أن السن والفقه إذا تعارضا في أخوين قالت المراوزة الأفقه أولى كما في سائر الصلوات وقال العراقيون نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه هاهنا يدل على أن السن أولى ونصه في سائر الصلوات يدل على أن الفقه أولى ففي المسألتين قولان بالنقل والتخريج ووجه تقديم السن هاهنا أن المراد الدعاء وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله يستحي أن يرد دعوة ذي الشيبة المسلم الثاني عبد فقيه وحر غير فقيه وأخ رقيق وعم حر ففي المسألتين وجهان ولعل التسوية أولى لتعادل الخصال وعند التسوية لا مرجع إلا إلى القرعة أو التراضي فأما الموقف فليقف الإمام وراء الجنازة عند صدر الميت إن كان رجلا وعند عجيزة المرأة كأنه يحاول سترها عن القوم فلو تقدم على الجنازة ففيه خلاف مرتب على تقدم المقتدي على الإمام وأولى بالجواز لأن الغائب قد يصلى عليه ويكون الميت وراء المصلي وإن كان ذلك بسبب الحاجة فلا بأس بإدخال الجنازة المسجد خلافا لأبي حنيفة ### | فرعان الأول إذا اجتمع الجنائز فيجوز أن يفرد كل واحدة بالصلاة ويجوز أن يصلى على الجمع وفي كيفية الوضع وجهان الأصح أنه يوضع الكل بين يدي الإمام على هذه الصورة الثاني أنه يوضع صفا مادا في يمين الإمام على هذه الصورة الثاني أن قرب الجنازة من الإمام رتبة مطلوبة مستحق بالسبق مرة وبالتقدم في الرتبة أخرى فيوضع الرجل أولا ثم الصبي ثم الخنثى ثم المرأة ولا يقدم بالحرية والرق ولكن بصفات دينية تزيد الرغبة في الصلاة عليه ولو سبقت جنازة امرأة فإذا ألحق رجل نحيت المرأة ولو سبق جنازة صبي لا تنحى بسبب رجل وذكر صاحب التقريب وجها أنه ينحى وعند تساوي الصفات فلا مرجع إلا إلى القرعة أو التراضي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing, cleansing a body with water; ritual purification of the corpse.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical cleansing as a prerequisite for the prayer's validity, distinct from spiritual purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal washing here; metaphorical extension to "washing away" sins is not intended in this juristic context.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify; the martyr (shahīd) as one whose testimony is sealed by death.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The martyr's status as a witness for the faith, with specific legal exemptions (washing, prayer).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "witness" vs. technical legal sense of "martyr" — a shift from testimony to a fixed juristic category.
- Root: ن-ي-ة (n-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intention, purpose, resolve.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The internal act that distinguishes worship (ʿibādah) from mere habit; here, it differentiates Muslim from non-Muslim dead in a mixed burial.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "aim" vs. technical legal "intention" as a pillar of the prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text uses "if... then..." (idhā... fa...) and "except" (illā) to delineate legal rulings, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: A subsidiary branch — If the dead of the Muslims are mixed with the polytheists, we wash them and shroud them, striving to fulfill the obligatory duty. Then, at the time of the prayer, we distinguish the Muslims from the unbelievers by intention (niyyah).

The third restriction: martyrdom (shahādah). Thus, no martyr is washed, nor is the prayer offered over him. The martyr is one who dies due to combat with the unbelievers during the time of active fighting. These are three conditions. If he was in a battle against the people of transgression (ahl al-baghy), or died a natural death during combat with the unbelievers, or died after the cessation of fighting due to a severe wound sustained in battle, or was killed by a combatant through treachery outside of battle — in all these cases there are two opinions. One holds that the ruling of martyrdom is affirmed for him due to the shared meaning; the second holds it is not, because each of these descriptions has its own distinct effect.

There is no disagreement that one struck in battle by a Muslim's weapon, or trampled by the beasts of the Muslims, and who dies, is a martyr. Nor is there disagreement that the wounded person, if his survival was anticipated, who dies after the cessation of fighting, is not a martyr. The two opinions apply only to one of whom it is certain that he will die, while a stable life remains in him.

As for one killed unjustly by a Muslim or a dhimmī, or one who dies of a stomach ailment, or a stranger who dies — these are prayed over, even though the term "martyrdom" is reported concerning them. And one killed by right, whether as retribution (qiṣāṣ) or as a prescribed punishment (ḥadd), is not a martyr.

Two subsidiary branches: First, one who abandons the prayer, if killed, is prayed over. The author of al-Talkhīṣ said: his grave is leveled, he is not shrouded, and no prayer is offered over him, as a humiliation — but this is far-fetched. Second, the highway robber, if crucified: it is said that no prayer is offered over him, as a severity. But the apparent view is that he is washed and prayed over. If we hold that he is left crucified until he decays, then the proper course is that we kill him first, wash him, pray over him, and crucify him in his shroud — as if the air were his grave. And if we hold that he is killed while crucified, then he is lowered after the killing, prayed over, and buried. One who holds that he is killed crucified and left cannot perform the prayer over him.

If it is said: By what does the martyr differ from others? I say: In four matters. First, the washing — it is forbidden in his case, even if he were in a state of major impurity (junub), due to his saying, peace be upon him: {«زَمِّلُوهُمْ بِكُلُومِهِمْ وَدِمَائِهِمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُحْشَرُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَأَوْدَاجُهُمْ تَشْخَبُ دَمًا، فَاللَّوْنُ لَوْنُ الدَّمِ وَالرِّيحُ رِيحُ الْمِسْكِ»} — "Shroud them with their wounds and their blood, for they will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with their jugular veins gushing blood; the color is the color of blood, and the scent is the scent of musk." Ibn Surayj derived a position that the one in major impurity is washed. Second, the prayer over him is forbidden in our view, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah; and among our companions, some said it is permissible but not obligatory. Third, the blood of martyrdom is not removed. As for removing other impurities, there are three aspects: one, yes, because what is excused is the trace of martyrdom; two, no, because removing them leads to removing the trace of martyrdom; three, if it leads to removal, it is not removed, otherwise it is removed. The fourth matter: the shrouding in his case is like that in the case of others, except that the garments stained with blood are not removed. If the heir removes them or replaces them, it is not prevented. As for the armor and coarse garments, there is no doubt about their removal.

The second part: concerning who prays. The consideration is of the imam's description and his station. As for the description: the most entitled to the prayer is the relative. None is given precedence over kinship except masculinity, so that a pubescent boy is given precedence over a woman. And the ruler (wālī) is given precedence over the relative in the old view. Then the order of relatives: one begins with the father, then the grandfather, then the son, then the ʿaṣabāt (agnatic heirs) in their order of inheritance. Then, regarding giving precedence to the full brother over the paternal brother, there are two paths: one holds that there are two opinions, as in marriage; the correct view is precedence, because the kinship of women has a bearing on the prayer. Likewise, when the ʿaṣabāt are absent, we give precedence to the dhawi al-arḥām (uterine kin); and it is preferable to give precedence to the freed slave over them, as in inheritance.

Two subsidiary branches: First, if age and juristic knowledge (fiqh) conflict in two brothers, the Marwazīs said: the more learned is more entitled, as in all other prayers. The Iraqis said: the text of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, here indicates that age is more entitled, while his text in other prayers indicates that fiqh is more entitled. Thus, in both matters there are two opinions, by transmission and by derivation. The rationale for preferring age here is that the purpose is supplication (duʿāʾ), and he, peace be upon him, said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَرُدَّ دَعْوَةَ ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ الْمُسْلِمِ»} — "God is too shy to reject the supplication of an aged Muslim." Second: a learned slave and a free man who is not learned, and a brother who is a slave and a paternal uncle who is free — in both matters there are two aspects. Perhaps equal treatment is preferable, given the equivalence of qualities; and when equal, there is no recourse except to the lot (qurʿah) or mutual consent.

As for the station: the imam stands behind the bier, at the chest of the deceased if it is a man, and at the buttocks of a woman, as if seeking to cover her from the people. If he stands ahead of the bier, there is a dispute, built upon the case of the follower preceding the imam; and it is more likely permissible, because the absent one may be prayed over, with the deceased behind the one praying. If this is due to necessity, there is no harm in bringing the bier into the mosque, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

Two subsidiary branches: First, when multiple biers are gathered, it is permissible to single out each one for the prayer, and it is permissible to pray over them collectively. Regarding the manner of placement, there are two aspects: the sounder is that all are placed before the imam in this form; the second is that they are placed in a row extending to the imam's right, in this form. Second: proximity of the bier to the imam is a sought rank, earned by precedence in time once and by precedence in rank another time. Thus, the man is placed first, then the boy, then the hermaphrodite, then the woman. One is not given precedence by freedom or slavery, but by religious qualities that increase the desire to pray over him. If a woman's bier precedes, and then a man's is brought, the woman is moved aside. If a boy's bier precedes, it is not moved aside due to a man; the author of al-Taqrīb mentioned an aspect that it is moved aside. When qualities are equal, there is no recourse except to the lot or mutual consent.

chapters.title_en: The Third Branch: On the Modality of the Funeral Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الطرف الثالث في كيفية الصلاة

وأقلها تسعة
أركان النية والتكبيرات الأربع والسلام والفاتحة بعد الأولى والصلاة على
الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد الثانية وفي الصلاة على الآل خلاف والدعاء
للميت بعد الثالثة ركن وهو المقصود الأهم وقيل يكفي الدعاء للمؤمنين من غير
ربط بالميت فلو زاد تكبيرة خامسة بطلت الصلاة على أحد الوجهين تشبيها لكل
تكبيرة بركعة
فأما الأكمل فيرفع السيد في التكبيرات عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة وفي دعاء
الاستفتاح والتعوذ ثلاثة أوجه
الأصح أنه لا يستحب الاستفتاح ويتعوذ لأنه من توابع القراءة ولا يجهر
بالقراءة ليلا كان أو نهارا
وقال الصيدلاني يجهر ليلا
وفي استحباب الدعاء للمؤمنين والمؤمنات عند الدعاء للميت تردد لأنه مبني
على التخفيف والأصح الاستحباب ولم يتعرض الشافعي رضي الله عنه لذكر بين
الرابعة
والسلام
وروى البويطي أنه يقول اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده وفي تعدد
السلام خلاف مرتب على سائر الصلوات والاقتصار هاهنا أولى فيسلم بتسليمة
واحدة تلقاء وجهه وقيل يسلم ملتفتا إلى يمينه ويختم ووجهه مائل إلى يساره
فيدير  الوجه في تسليمه واحدة ولا خلاف في أنه لا يسجد في هذه الصلاة لسهو

### | فروع ثلاثة

الأول إن صلى شفعوي خلف من يكبر خمسا إن قلنا إن زيادة التكبير تبطل
الصلاة فهي كالاقتداء بالحنفي وإن قلنا لا تبطل صحت القدوة ولكن في
الموافقة في التكبير الزائد قولان جاريان في اختلاف فعل الإمام والمأموم
وفي القنوت وتكبيرات العيدين أن الأولى المتابعة أم لا
الثاني المسبوق يكبر كما أدرك وإن كان الإمام في القراءة
وقال أبو حنيفة يصبر إلى أن يشتغل الإمام بالتكبيرة التى يستقبلها ثم لا
بأس إن كان هو يقرأ بقية الفاتحة والإمام يصلي على الرسول صلى الله عليه
وسلم لأن هذا هو أول صلاة المسبوق
ولكن يساوق الإمام في التكبيرات فإذا سلم الإمام تدارك البقية ولا يبالي
وإن رفعت الجنازة
الثالث لو تخلف عن الإمام قصدا بتكبيرة بطلت صلاته لأنها كركعة وإذا لم
يوافق فيما بين التكبيرتين لا يبقى للقدوة معنى

### | الطرف الرابع في شرائط الصلاة

وهي كسائر الصلوات وتتميز بأمور
الأول أنه لا يشترط حضور ميت بل يصلى على الغائب خلافا لأبي حنيفة صلى
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على النجاشي وقد مات بالحبشة
وإن كانت الجنازة في البلد ففي صلاة من لم يحضرها خلاف لتيسر الحضور
الثاني لا يشترط ظهور الميت بل تجوز الصلاة عليه بعد الدفن
صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على المسكينة بعد الدفن
نعم لو دفنوا قبل الصلاة خرجوا ولكن تصح صلاتهم وصلاة الطائفة الثانية
صحيحة عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة وليس ذلك تطوعا بل هو كما لو التحقوا
بالجماعة الأولى وإنما التطوع أن يعيد الإنسان صلاة الجنازة وذلك غير مستحب
ثم في مدة جواز الصلاة بعد الدفن خمسة أوجه
أحدها أنه إلى ثلاثة أيام
والثاني إلى شهر
والثالث إلى انمحاق أجزائه
والرابع أن من كان للصلاة أهلا يوم موته يصلى عليه ومن لا فلا
الخامس أنه يجوز أبدا
وعلى هذا فلا تجوز الصلاة على قبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  إذ قال
عليه الصلاة والسلام لعن الله اليهود اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد
الأمر الثالث أن هذه الصلاة فرض على الكفاية ويسقط الفرض بصلاة أربعة من
الرجال صلوا جماعة أو آحادا
وهل يسقط بجنس النساء فيه خلاف
وقيل يكفي شخص واحد وقيل لا بد من ثلاث وقيل لا بد من أربع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-م-ل (K-M-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Completeness, perfection, and the state of being whole without deficiency.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The optimal form (al-akmal) as distinct from the minimal obligatory (al-aqall), marking the gradation between sufficiency and excellence in devotional acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes physical wholeness; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the supererogatory perfection of ritual form.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "لو زاد" governs a protasis whose apodosis ("بطلت") is a legal verdict, requiring the reader to parse the hypothetical as a juridical counterfactual.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third branch concerns the modality of the funeral prayer.

Its minimal form consists of nine [components]: the intention (niyyah), the four takbīrs, the salutation (salām), the Fātiḥah after the first takbīr, and the prayer upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) after the second. Concerning the prayer upon his family (āl), there is a divergence of opinion. The supplication for the deceased after the third takbīr is a pillar (rukn), and it is the most important objective. It is also said that supplicating for the believers in general suffices, without specifically linking it to the deceased. If one adds a fifth takbīr, the prayer is invalidated according to one of the two positions, by analogy to each takbīr being treated as a rakʿah.

As for the most complete form (al-akmal): the master [al-Shāfiʿī] holds that one raises the hands during the takbīrs, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. Concerning the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ) and the seeking of refuge (taʿawwudh), there are three positions. The most sound (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that the opening supplication is not recommended, but one does seek refuge, because it is a corollary of the recitation. One does not recite aloud, whether by night or by day. Al-Ṣaydalānī held that one recites aloud at night. Regarding the recommendation of supplicating for believing men and women during the supplication for the deceased, there is hesitation, because this prayer is founded upon brevity; the most sound position is that it is recommended. Al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) did not address the mention of anything between the fourth takbīr and the salutation.

Al-Buwayṭī narrated that he would say: "O God, do not deprive us of his reward, and do not afflict us after him." Concerning the multiplicity of salutations, there is a divergence built upon [the rules of] other prayers, but restricting [to one] here is more appropriate. Thus one gives a single salutation facing forward. It is also said that one gives the salutation while turning to the right, concluding with the face inclined toward the left, thereby rotating the face in a single salutation. There is no divergence that one does not perform the prostration of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) in this prayer.

### Three Subsidiary Issues

The first: If a Shāfiʿī prays behind one who pronounces five takbīrs — if we hold that the additional takbīr invalidates the prayer, then this is like following a Ḥanafī [imam]; if we hold that it does not invalidate, then the following is valid. However, concerning concurrence in the additional takbīr, there are two positions, parallel to those on the divergence between the imam's and the follower's actions, and on the qunūt and the takbīrs of the two ʿĪds: whether following [the imam] is preferable or not.

The second: The one who is preceded [in part of the prayer] (masbūq) pronounces the takbīr for what he has caught up with, even if the imam is [already] in the recitation. Abū Ḥanīfah said: he should wait until the imam engages in the takbīr that he is about to face; then there is no harm if he [the follower] is reciting the remainder of the Fātiḥah while the imam is praying upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), because this is the beginning of the masbūq's prayer. Rather, he should keep pace with the imam in the takbīrs; when the imam gives the salutation, he makes up the remainder, and he does not mind even if the bier has been lifted.

The third: If one deliberately lags behind the imam by a takbīr, his prayer is invalidated, because it is like a rakʿah. And when one does not concur between the two takbīrs, there remains no meaning to following (iqtidāʾ).

### The Fourth Branch: On the Conditions of the Prayer

These are like the conditions of other prayers, but distinguished by several matters:

The first: The presence of a deceased [body] is not required; rather, one may pray over the absent [dead], contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed over the Negus (al-Najāshī) while he had died in Abyssinia. If the bier is in the town, there is a divergence concerning the prayer of one who did not attend it, because attendance is readily feasible.

The second: The appearance of the deceased is not required; rather, it is permissible to pray over him after burial. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed over the poor woman after her burial. Indeed, if they were buried before the prayer, they are [normally] exhumed, but their prayer is valid, and the prayer of the second group is valid in our school, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. This is not supererogatory (taṭawwuʿ); rather, it is like joining the first congregation. Supererogation is only when a person repeats the funeral prayer [for the same deceased], and that is not recommended. Then, concerning the duration within which prayer after burial is permissible, there are five positions:

One: up to three days.
The second: up to a month.
The third: until the dissolution of his bodily parts.
The fourth: that whoever was worthy of prayer on the day of his death is prayed over, and whoever was not, is not.
The fifth: that it is permissible forever.

On this [last] basis, it is not permissible to pray over the grave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), since he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«لعن الله اليهود اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد»} — "May God curse the Jews who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."

The third matter: This prayer is a communal obligation (farḍ ʿalā al-kifāyah), and the obligation is discharged by the prayer of four men, whether they pray in congregation or individually. Whether it is discharged by women alone is a matter of divergence. It is said that one person suffices; it is said that three are necessary; and it is said that four are necessary.

chapters.title_en: Section 79 — The Discourse on Burial (al-Dafn)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في الدفن

الدفن من فروض الكفايات وأقله حفرة توارى بدن الميت وتحرسه من السباع
وتكتم رائحته
وأكمله قبر على قامة رجل ربع
واللحد أولى من الشق قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشق لغيرنا واللحد
لنا وليكن اللحد في جهة القبلة ثم توضع الجنازة على رأس القبر بحيث يكون
رأس الميت عند مؤخر القبر فيسل الواقف داخل القبر الميت من قبل رأسه ويضعه
في اللحد
وقال أبو حنيفة توضع الجنازة بين القبلة والقبر عرضا ثم ترد قهقرى إلى
القبر
ثم قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه لا يدخل الميت قبره إلا الرجل
فإن كان الميت امرأة فيتولى ذلك زوجها أو محارمها فإن لم يكونوا فعبيدها
فإن لم يكونوا فخصيان فإن لم يكونوا فأرحام فإن لم يكونوا فالأجانب وذلك
لأنهن يضعفن عن مباشرة هذا الأمر
ثم إن كان المدفون صبيا استقل به واحد فإن زاد فليكن عددهم وترا
ثم يضجعون الميت على جنبه الأيمن في اللحد قبالة القبلة بحيث لا ينكب ولا
يستلقي وحسن أن يفضي بوجهه إلى تراب أو لبنة موضوعة تحت رأسه ولا يوضع رأسه
على مخدة ثم ينصب اللين على فتح اللحد ويسد الفرج بما يمنع انهيار التراب
عليه ثم يحثو كل من دنا ثلاث حثيات من التراب ثم يهال التراب عليه بالمساحي
ولا يرفع نعش القبر إلا بمقدار شبر ولا يجصص ولا يطين ولو صب الحصى عليه
فلا بأس ولو وضع حجر على رأس القبر للعلامة فلا بأس
ثم تستطيع القبور عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه أفضل من تسنيمها لكن التسنيم
الآن أفضل مخالفة لشعار الروافض حتى ظن ظانون أن القنوت إن صار شعارا لهم
كان الأولى  تركه هذا بعيد في أبعاض الصلاة وإنما نخالفهم في هيئات مثل
التختم في اليمين وأمثاله
ثم الأفضل أن يمكث المشيع للجنازة إلى أن يواري الميت قال صلى الله عليه
وسلم من صلى على ميت وانصرف فله قيراط من الأجر ومن صلى واتبع الجنازة وشهد
الدفن فله قيراطان

### | فرعان

الأول أنه لا يدفن في قبر واحد ميتان ما أمكن وإن اجتمع موتى في قحط
وموتان جعلنا الرجلين والثلاثة في قبر واحد وقدمنا الأفضل إلى جدار اللحد
فيقدم الأب على الابن والابن على الأم لمكان الذكورة ولأنه الأحسن في هيئة
الوضع ولا يجمع بين الرجال والنساء فإن ظهرت الضرورة جعلنا بينهما حاجزا من
التراب
الثاني القبر محترم فيكره الجلوس والمشي والاتكاء عليه وليخرج الزائر منه
إلا حد كان يقرب منه لو كان حيا ولا يحل نبش القبور إلا إذا انمحق أثر
الميت بطول الزمان أو دفن من غير غسل فالظاهر أنه ينبش القبر ويغسل أو دفن
في أرض مغصوبة وترك المالك إخراجه فإن حق الحي أولى بالمراعاة
ولو دفن قبل الصلاة صلي عليه في القبر
ولو دفن قبل التكفين فوجهان
أظهرهما أنه لا ينبش لأن القبر ستره بخلاف الغسل فإن مقصوده لا يحصل
بالدفن
ولو دفن في كفن مغصوب فثلاثة أوجه
أظهرهما أنه ينبش كالأرض المغصوبة وكما لو ابتلع لؤلؤة فإنه يشق بطنه
لأجل ملك الغير
والثاني أنه في حكم الهالك فيغرم القيمة إن أمكن وإلا فالنبش عند العجز
عن القيمة لا بد منه
والثالث أنه إن تغير الميت وأدى إلى هتك حرمته فلا ينبش وهو الأقيس وإلا
فينبش
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ف-ن (d-f-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To conceal, cover, or bury beneath the earth; the act of interment that hides the object from view.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual burial as a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah) preserving human dignity (karāmah) and fulfilling the command to honor the deceased.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical covering with soil; metaphorical (majāz) — concealing a matter or veiling a fault.
- Root: ل-ح-د (l-ḥ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The niche or side-chamber carved into the grave wall; from laḥada, to incline or slant.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The preferred burial form (al-lahd) symbolizing the deceased's orientation toward the qiblah and the niche's protective function.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the side recess; metaphorical — deviation from uprightness (ilḥād) in religious matters.
- Root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To split or cleave; al-shaqq — the trench grave with a central channel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The alternative burial form permitted for non-Muslims, as per the prophetic tradition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — splitting the earth; metaphorical — discord or division (shiqāq).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing clauses with "in" (if) and "illā" (unless) to delineate legal exceptions, as in the permissibility of exhumation (nabsh) under specified exigencies.
chapters.translation:
I say: Burial (al-dafn) is among the communal obligations (furūḍ al-kifāyāt). Its minimal form is a pit that conceals the deceased's body, guards it from beasts of prey, and suppresses its odor. Its most complete form is a grave of the height of a man, squared (rabʿ). The niche-grave (al-lahd) is preferable to the trench-grave (al-shaqq), for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «الشَّقُّ لِغَيْرِنَا وَاللَّحْدُ لَنَا» ("The trench is for others, and the niche is for us"). The niche should be oriented toward the qiblah. Then the bier (janāzah) is placed at the head of the grave such that the deceased's head is at the grave's rear, and the one standing inside the grave lowers the deceased from the direction of his head and lays him in the niche.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: The bier is placed transversely between the qiblah and the grave, then it is drawn backward (qahqarā) into the grave.

Then al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: None enters the grave with the deceased except a man. If the deceased is a woman, then her husband or her male relatives within the prohibited degrees (maḥārim) undertake this; if none exist, then her male slaves; if none, then eunuchs (khiṣyān); if none, then her kinsmen (arḥām); if none, then unrelated men (ajānib) — this because women are too weak to handle this task directly.

Then, if the buried one is a young boy, a single man suffices for him; if more, let their number be odd (witr). Then they lay the deceased on his right side in the niche, facing the qiblah, such that he is neither tilted face-down (lā yunkab) nor laid flat on his back (lā yastalqī). It is commendable that his face be placed against earth or a brick set beneath his head, and his head should not be rested on a pillow. Then the unfired bricks (al-labin) are set upright over the niche's opening, and the gaps are sealed with what prevents the soil from collapsing upon him. Then every bystander casts three handfuls of earth (ḥathawāt), after which the soil is heaped upon him with shovels (masāḥī). The grave mound is not raised more than a span (shibr), and it is neither plastered (lā yujasṣaṣ) nor coated with clay (lā yuṭayyan). If pebbles are poured over it, there is no harm; if a stone is placed at the grave's head as a marker, there is no harm.

Then, with al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him), leveled graves (tasṭīḥ) are superior to mounded ones (tasnīm), but mounding is now superior — as a divergence from the emblem (shiʿār) of the Rāfiḍah — until some have fancied that if the qunūt (supplication in prayer) became their emblem, it would be better to abandon it. This is far-fetched regarding the parts of the prayer; we only diverge from them in outward forms (hayʾāt), such as wearing the ring on the right hand and the like.

Then it is preferable that the funeral attendant remain until the deceased is interred. He (peace be upon him) said: «مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَى مَيِّتٍ وَانْصَرَفَ فَلَهُ قِيرَاطٌ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ وَمَنْ صَلَّى وَاتَّبَعَ الْجَنَازَةَ وَشَهِدَ الدَّفْنَ فَلَهُ قِيرَاطَانِ» ("Whoever prays over a deceased and departs has one qīrāṭ of reward, and whoever prays, follows the funeral, and witnesses the burial has two qīrāṭs").

### Two Subsidiary Issues (Farʿān)

The First: Two deceased are not buried in a single grave as long as it is possible [to do otherwise]. If deaths accumulate during a famine (qaḥṭ) and many die, we place two or three men in one grave, and we advance the most virtuous toward the niche's wall — the father is advanced over the son, and the son over the mother, on account of masculinity and because it is more fitting in the posture of placement. Men and women are not combined [in one grave]; if necessity arises, we place a barrier of earth between them.

The Second: The grave is inviolable (muḥtaram), so sitting, walking upon, or leaning against it is disliked (makrūh). The visitor should depart from it, except for a need he would have approached were [the deceased] alive. It is not lawful to exhume graves (nabsh) unless the deceased's trace has vanished through the passage of long time, or he was buried without washing (ghusl) — in which case the apparent ruling is that the grave is exhumed and he is washed — or he was buried in usurped land (arḍ maghṣūbah) and the owner demands his property's removal, for the right of the living takes precedence in observance.

If he was buried before the funeral prayer, prayer is offered over him at the grave.

If he was buried before the shrouding (takfīn), there are two views (wajhān). The more apparent of them is that he is not exhumed, because the grave has veiled him — unlike the case of washing, for its purpose is not achieved by burial.

If he was buried in a usurped shroud (kafan maghṣūb), there are three aspects (awjuh). The more apparent of them is that he is exhumed, as in the case of usurped land, and just as if he had swallowed a pearl, his belly would be slit open for the sake of another's property. The second is that it is treated as destroyed (hālik), so its value is paid if possible; otherwise, exhumation upon inability to pay the value is unavoidable. The third is that if the deceased has decomposed and exhumation would lead to violating his sanctity (hatk ḥurmatihi), then he is not exhumed — and this is the more analogically sound (al-aqyas) — otherwise, he is exhumed.

chapters.title_en: Section 80 — On Condolence (Taʿziyah) and Weeping (Bukāʾ), and the Chapter on the Abandoner of Prayer; Commencement of the Book of Alms (Zakāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في التعزية والبكاء

والتعزية سنة قال عليه الصلاة والسلام من عزى مصابا فله مثل أجره
ومقصوده الحمل على الصبر بوعد الأجر والتحذير من الوزر بإفراط الجزع
وتذكير المصاب رجوع الأمر كله إلى الله تعالى
ثم يعزى الكافر بقريبه المسلم والدعاء للميت ويعزى المسلم بقريبه الكافر
ويكون الدعاء للحي فيقول جبر الله مصيبتك وألهمك الصبر ويستحب تهيئة طعام
لأجل أهل الميت ولا يؤثر  التعزية بعد ثلاث لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحل
لامرأة تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن تحد على ميت فوق ثلاث
أما البكاء فجائز من غير ندبة ونياحة وشق جيب وضرب خد فكل ذلك حرام لأنه
يخالف الانقياد لقضاء الله تعالى
بكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بعض أولاده فقال سعد ما هذا فقال
إنها رحمة وإن الله
يرحم من عباده الرحماء
فإن قيل أليس قال إن الميت ليعذب ببكاء أهله عليه هكذا رواه عمر
قلنا قال ابن عمر ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا إنما قال يزاد
الكافر عذابا ببكاء أهله عليه حسبكم قوله تعالى {ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}
وكان الكفار يوصون بالبكاء والنياحة فلذلك زيد في عذابهم
وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها ما كذب عمر ولكنه أخطأ ونسي إنما مر رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم على يهودية ماتت ابنتها وهي تبكي فقال عليه الصلاة
والسلام إنهم يبكون عليها وإنها تعذب في قبرها
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - باب تارك الصلاة - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
تارك الصلاة يقتل قال عليه الصلاة والسلام من ترك صلاة متعمدا فقد كفر
معناه عند الشافعي استوجب عقوبة الكافر وحكم أحمد بكفره وقال أبو حنيفة
بخلى ولا قتل عليه
ثم الصحيح أنه يقتل بصلاة واحدة إذا تركها عمدا وأخرجها عن وقت الضرورة
فلا يقتل بصلاة الظهر إلا إذا غربت الشمس
وفي مهلة الاستتابة ثلاثة أيام خلاف كما في استتابة المرتد
وقد قيل إنه لا يقتل إلا إذا صار الترك عادة له وقيل إذا ترك صلاتين أو
ثلاثة فكل ذلك تحكم
ثم يقتل بالسين ويصلى عليه كما يصلى على المسلمين
وقال صاحب التلخيص لا يرفع نعشه ولا يصلى عليه وهو تحكم لا أصل له والله
أعلم
= كتاب الزكاة =
الأصل فيها من الكتاب قوله تعالى {وآتوا الزكاة}
ومن السنة قوله عليه السلام بني الإسلام على خمس الحديث وقوله مانع
الزكاة في النار
والإجماع منعقد على وجوب الزكاة وهي بالإضافة إلى  متعلقاتها ستة
زكاة النعم والنقدين والتجارة والمعشرات والمعادن والفطرة

### | النوع الأول الزكاة النعم والنظر في وجوبها وآدائها

الطرف الأول في الوجوب وله ثلاثة أركان
من يجب عليه وما يجب فيه وهو السبب والواجب
أما من يجب عليه فلا يشترط فيه عندنا إلا الحرية والإسلام فتجب الزكاة
على الصبي والمجنون ولا تجب على الكافر والرقيق أعني الكافر الأصلي
وأما صفة الواجب وقدره فيتبين ببيان مقادير النصاب
وإنما يطول النظر في الركن الثالث وهو ما يجب فيه وله ستة شرائط أن يكون
نعما نصابا مملوكا متهيئا لكمال التصرف سائمة باقيا حولا

### | الشرط الأول أن يكون نعما

فلا زكاة إلا في الإبل والبقر والغنم ولا زكاة في البغال والحمير والخيل
والرقق
وقال أبو حنيفة في كل فرس أنثى سائمة دينار
ولا زكاة في المتولدة من الظباء والغنم
وقال أبو حنيفة إن كانت الأمهات من الغنم وجب الزكاة

### | الشرط الثاني أن يكون نصابا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ز-ي (ʿ-Z-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To console, to strengthen in patience; derived from ʿazāʾ (consolation), implying the redirection of grief toward endurance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A communal act of moral support (muwāsāh) that aligns the afflicted with divine decree (qaḍāʾ), not mere emotional appeasement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in its sense of binding one to patience; metaphorical (majāz) if taken as mere verbal comfort without spiritual intent.
- Root: ب-ك-ي (B-K-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Shedding tears; distinct from niyāḥah (lamentation with wailing) and nadb (ritualized mourning cries).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Permissible as a natural human response (raḥmah), but forbidden when it becomes a rejection of divine decree (sukhkht).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tearful weeping; metaphorical for excessive grief that manifests in prohibited acts (e.g., tearing garments).
- Root: ج-ب-ر (J-B-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone, to restore; hence, "jabara Allāhu muṣībataka" — may God repair your affliction and compensate you.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine reparation of the believer's state, both in this world and the next, through reward (ajr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of restoration; metaphorical in supplication for divine solace.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In "man ʿazzā muṣāban fa-lahu mithlu ajrihi," the protasis (man ʿazzā) is indefinite-conditional, and the apodosis (fa-lahu) is a nominal sentence carrying the reward, indicating generality and certainty of divine recompense.
chapters.translation:
I say: Condolence (taʿziyah) is a Sunnah. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «Whoever consoles an afflicted person shall have a reward equivalent to his» — meaning, the reward of the afflicted for their patience. Its purpose is to urge endurance through the promise of recompense and to warn against sin through excessive distress (jazaʿ). It also reminds the afflicted that the entire affair returns to God, the Exalted.

Then, one offers condolence to an unbeliever (kāfir) for his Muslim relative, and supplication (duʿāʾ) is made for the deceased. Likewise, one consoles a Muslim for his unbelieving relative, but the supplication is directed to the living, saying: "May God repair your affliction (jabara Allāhu muṣībataka) and inspire you with patience." It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to prepare food for the family of the deceased. Condolence after three days is not preferred, due to his saying, peace be upon him: «It is not lawful for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn (tuḥidd) a deceased person beyond three days.»

As for weeping (bukāʾ), it is permissible without ritual lamentation (nadb), wailing (niyāḥah), tearing the garment (shaqq jayb), or striking the cheek (ḍarb khadd) — for all of these are forbidden, as they oppose submission (inqiyād) to the decree of God, the Exalted.

The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, wept over some of his children. Saʿd said: "What is this?" He replied: «It is mercy (raḥmah), and God shows mercy to the merciful among His servants.»

If it is said: Did he not state, «The deceased is tormented by the weeping of his family over him» — as ʿUmar narrated it? I say: Ibn ʿUmar said, "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, did not say this. He only said: «The unbeliever is increased in torment by the weeping of his family over him.»" Sufficient for you is His saying, the Exalted: {«And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another»} (Q 6:164). The unbelievers used to enjoin weeping and wailing, and thus their torment was increased. ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "ʿUmar did not lie, but he erred and forgot. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, merely passed by a Jewish woman whose daughter had died, and she was weeping. He said, peace be upon him: «They weep over her, and she is being tormented in her grave.»"

— Peace be upon him — Chapter on the Abandoner of Prayer — Peace be upon him —

The abandoner of prayer is to be killed. He said, peace be upon him: «Whoever deliberately abandons prayer has disbelieved (kafara).» Its meaning according to al-Shāfiʿī is that he incurs the punishment of an unbeliever. Aḥmad ruled his outright disbelief (kufr). Abū Ḥanīfah said: He is imprisoned (yukhallā) but not killed.

Then, the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that he is killed for a single prayer if he abandons it deliberately and expels it beyond its necessary time (waqt al-ḍarūrah). Thus, he is not killed for the noon prayer (ẓuhr) unless the sun has set. Regarding the grace period for seeking repentance (istitābah), there is a dispute over three days, as in the case of an apostate (murtadd). It has been said he is not killed unless abandonment becomes habitual; and it has been said he is killed after two or three prayers — all of this is arbitrary ruling (taḥakkum).

Then, he is killed with the sword, and the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah) is offered over him, just as it is offered over Muslims. The author of al-Talkhīṣ said: His bier is not raised, nor is prayer offered over him — but this is an arbitrary ruling with no basis. And God knows best.

= The Book of Alms (Zakāh) =

Its foundation in the Book is His saying, the Exalted: {«And give the alms (zakāh)»} (Q 2:43). From the Sunnah is his saying, peace be upon him: «Islam is built upon five» — the hadith — and his saying: «The withholder of zakāh is in the Fire.» Consensus (ijmāʿ) is established upon the obligation of zakāh. In relation to its objects (mutaʿalliqāt), it is six: zakāh on grazing livestock (naʿam), on the two precious metals (naqdayn), on trade goods (tijārah), on produce of the earth (muʿashsharāt), on minerals (maʿādin), and on the breaking of the fast (fiṭrah).

### | First Type: Zakāh on Grazing Livestock — Consideration of Its Obligation and Payment

The first aspect concerns obligation, which has three pillars: the one upon whom it is obligatory, that upon which it is obligatory (which is the cause, sabab), and the obligatory amount (wājib).

As for the one upon whom it is obligatory, we hold that only freedom (ḥurriyyah) and Islam are required. Thus, zakāh is obligatory upon the minor (ṣabī) and the insane (majnūn), but not upon the unbeliever or the slave — meaning the original unbeliever (kāfir aṣlī).

As for the description of the obligatory amount and its measure, it is clarified by stating the quantities of the niṣāb (threshold). The consideration lengthens only regarding the third pillar — that upon which it is obligatory — which has six conditions: that it be livestock, reaching the niṣāb, owned, prepared for complete disposal, pastured (sāʾimah), and remaining for a full year (ḥawl).

### | First Condition: That It Be Livestock

Thus, zakāh is only on camels, cattle, and sheep. There is no zakāh on mules, donkeys, horses, or slaves. Abū Ḥanīfah said: For every pastured female horse, one dīnār. There is no zakāh on animals born from antelopes and sheep. Abū Ḥanīfah said: If the mothers are from sheep, zakāh is obligatory.

chapters.title_en: Section 81 — On the Zakat Obligations for Camels, Cattle, and Sheep
chapters.arabic_text:
أما الإبل ففي أربع وعشرين من الإبل فما دونها الغنم في كل خمس شاة
فإذا بلغت خمسا وعشرين إلى خمس وثلاثين ففيها بنت مخاض فإن لم يكن فيها
بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر وليس معه شيء
فإذا بلغت ستا وثلاثين إلى خمس وأربعين ففيها بنت لبون
فإذا بلغت ستا وأربعين إلى ستين ففيها حقة
وإذا بلغت إحدى وستين إلى خمس وسبعين ففيها جذعة
فإذا بلغت ستا وسبعين إلى تسعين ففيها بنت لبون
فإذا بلغت إحدى وتسعين إلى مائة وعشرين ففيها حقتان
فإذا زادت على عشرين ومائة ففي كل أربعين بنت لبون وفي كل خمسين حقة
كل ذلك لفظ أبي بكر رضي الله عنه وأرضاه كتبه في كتاب الصدقة لأنس بن
مالك
وبنت المخاض لها سنة وبنت اللبون لها سنتان وللحقة ثلاث وللجذعة أربع
أما البقر فلا شيء فيه حتى تبلغ ثلاثين ففيها تبيع وهو الذي له سنة ثم لا
شيء حتى تبلغ أربعين ففيها مسنة ثم لا شيء حتى تبلغ ستين ففيها تبيعان
ثم استقر الحساب ففي كل ثلاثين تبيع وفي  كل أربعين مسنة وهي التى لها
سنتان
وأما الغنم فقد روى ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب كتاب الصدقة
وفيه في الغنم في كل أربعين شاة إلى عشرين ومائة فإذا
زادت واحدة ففيها شاتان إلى مائتين فإذا زادت واحدة على المائتين ففيها
ثلاث شياه إلى ثلاثمائة فإن كانت الغنم أكثر من ذلك ففي كل مائة شاة
والشاة الواجبة في الغنم هي الجذعة من الضأن أو الثنية من المعز والجذعة
هي التي لها سنة واحدة وقيل ستة أشهر والثنية التى لها سنتان ثم يتصدى
النظر في زكاة الإبل في
ستة مواضع
النظر الأول في إخراج الشاة عن خمس من الإبل وفيه ثلاث مسائل
الأولى أن الواجب من حيث السن جذعة من الضأن أو الثنية من المعز ومن حيث
النوع أعني تعيين الضأن من المعز فيه وجهان أحدهما أنه يعتبر غالب غنم
البلد فإن كان الغالب الضأن أخرج الضأن كما تعتبر زكاة الفطر بغالب القوت
على الأصح خلاف الشاة الواجبة في أربعين فإنه يعتبر بالمخرج منه لأنه من
جنسه
والثاني أنه يخرج ما شاء فإنه ينطلق عليه اسم الشاة ولم يجب إلا شاة كما
يجري في الرقبة المطلقة في الكفاءة ما ينطلق الاسم عليه وكذا الشاة
المذكورة في المناسك
وقيل إنه يعتبر جنس غنم صاحب الإبل وهو بعيد
الثانية لو أخرج جدعا ذكرا أو ثنيا ذكرا فيه وجهان
أحدهما يجزئ اتباعا للاسم والثاني لا تنزيلا للمطلق هاهنا على المفصل في
زكاة الغنم وهي الأنثى وهذا الخلاف جاء في شاة الجبران
الثالثة لو أخرج بعيرا عن العشرين فما دونه يجزئ لأنه يجزئ عن خمس وعشرين
فهو بأن يجزئ عن الأقل أولى ولا بأس وإن كانت قيمته أقل من الشاة
وقال القفال لا يؤخذ ناقص القيمة وهو بعيد لأنه التفات إلى البدل ولم
يوجد هذا بطريق البدلية
وقيل إنه لا يجزئ بعير عن عشرة بل لا بد من حيوانين إما بعير وشاة وإما
بعيران
وهو أيضا بعيد لما ذكرناه من طريق  الأولى
وترددوا في أن البعير المخرج من الخمس هل كله فرض أو الفرض خمسه
النظر الثاني في كيفية العدول عن بنت مخاض عند فقدها إلى ابن لبون وفيه
أربع مسائل
الأولى إن لم يكن في ماله بنت مخاض ولا ابن لبون تخير في الشراء لأنه
مهما اشترى ابن لبون فقد صار موجودا دون بنت مخاض ويلزم أخذه وقال صاحب
التقريب يتعين شراء بنت مخاض لاستوائهما في الفقد كاستوائهما في الوجود
الثانية لو كان في ماله بنت مخاض معيبة فهي كالمعدومة فيؤخذ منه ابن لبون
وإن كانت كريمة فلا يطالب بها قال القفال يلزمه شراء بنت مخاض لأنها موجودة
في ماله وإنما نزل نظرا له فلا يؤخذ ابن لبون وقال غيره يؤخذ لأنها
كالمعدومة إذ لا يجب تسليمها
الثالثة الخنثى من بنات لبون تؤخذ بدلا عن بنت مخاض عند فقده لأنه بين أن
يكون ذكرا أو أنثى وكلاهما مأخوذان وقيل إنه لا يؤخذ بدلا عن بنت مخاض
لتشوه الخلقة بهذا النقصان
الرابعة لو أخرج حقا بدلا عن بنت لبون عند فقدها أخذ جبرا لفوات الأنوثة
بزيادة السن وقياسا على ابن لبون بالنسبة إلى بنت مخاض وقال صاحب التقريب
يحتمل أنه لا يؤخذ لأنه بدل وليس منصوصا عليه
النظر الثالث في الاستقرار فإذا زادت واحدة على مائة وعشرين ففيها ثلاث
بنات
لبون وفي انبساط الواجب على الواحدة وجهان أحدهما القياس أنه ينبسط
والثاني أنه لا ينبسط حتى يكون في كل أربعين بنت لبون وعلى هذا بنى أنه لو
زاد نصف بعير على مائة وعشرين وجب ثلاث بنات لبون وهو بعيد
وأما أبو حنيفة فإنه قال يستأنف الحساب عند ذلك فيجب في كل خمس شاة وقال
ابن خيران يتخير بين مذهب الشافعي ومذهب أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنهما
النظر الرابع في اجتماع بنات اللبون والحقاق فإذا ملك مائتين من الإبل
فهي أربع خمسينيات وخمس أربعينيات فإن لم يوجد في ماله إلا أحد السنين أخذ
وإن فقد فله أن يشتري ما شاء على الصحيح  وإن وجدا جميعا فالواجب إخراج
الأغبط للمساكين لأنهما متساويان في الوجوب والوجود ولا بد من ترجيح فغرض
المساكين أولى ما يرجح به بخلاف الشاتين والدراهم في الجبران فإن لفظ
الخبر دل على أن الخيرة للمعطي فيه
وخرج ابن سريج قولا أنه يتخير هاهنا كما في الجبران ونقل العراقيون قولا
أن الحقة تتعين لأن رغبة الشرع في زيادة السن أكثر منه في زيادة العدد فإنه
لم يزد في العدد إلا بعد انقطاع الأسنان المعتبرة
التفريع على النص إذا أخرج غير الأغبط فأخذ الساعي عمدا لم يقع الموقع
وإن أخذه باجتهاده فوجهان
فإن قلنا يقع الموقع ففي وجوب قدر التفاوت وجهان فإن قلنا يجب فإن لم يجد
به شقصا أخذنا الدراهم فإن وجد فهل يجب شراء شقص فوجهان فإن قلنا يجب
فيشتري من جنس الأغبط أو من جنس المخرج فوجهان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ل-غ (balagha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reach, attain, arrive at a limit or threshold.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic contexts, denotes the attainment of the nisāb (minimum threshold) triggering obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical arrival; metaphorical for reaching a legal limit.
- Root: ج-ز-ء (jaza'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To suffice, be sufficient; a part (juz') replacing a whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for substitution in ritual obligations (ijzā'), where the substitute fulfills the legal purpose.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a portion; metaphorical for legal sufficiency of a substitute.
- Root: ع-د-ل (ʿadala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To turn away, deviate, shift from one thing to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fiqh, the lawful transition to an alternative when the primary is unavailable.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical deviation; metaphorical for juristic substitution.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Constructions (sharṭ wa-jawāb) — The repeated "fa-idhā" (فإذا) clauses establish sequential legal conditions, each with its apodosis, requiring precise temporal and logical parsing.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for camels — upon twenty-four camels or fewer, sheep are due: for every five, one sheep. When they reach twenty-five up to thirty-five, a bint makhāḍ (a female camel entering its second year) is due; if no bint makhāḍ is found among them, then a male ibn labūn (a male camel entering its third year), and nothing else accompanies it. When they reach thirty-six up to forty-five, a bint labūn (a female camel entering its third year) is due. When they reach forty-six up to sixty, a ḥiqqah (a female camel entering its fourth year) is due. When they reach sixty-one up to seventy-five, a jadhaʿah (a female camel entering its fifth year) is due. When they reach seventy-six up to ninety, two bint labūn are due. When they reach ninety-one up to one hundred twenty, two ḥiqqah are due. When they exceed one hundred twenty, then for every forty, a bint labūn, and for every fifty, a ḥiqqah. All of this is the wording of Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him and grant him His good pleasure — which he wrote in the Book of Alms (kitāb al-ṣadaqah) addressed to Anas ibn Mālik. The bint makhāḍ is one year old, the bint labūn is two years old, the ḥiqqah is three, and the jadhaʿah is four.

As for cattle — nothing is due until they reach thirty; then a tabīʿ (a male calf one year old) is due. Then nothing until they reach forty; then a musinnah (a cow entering its third year) is due. Then nothing until they reach sixty; then two tabīʿ are due. Thereafter the reckoning is settled: for every thirty, a tabīʿ, and for every forty, a musinnah — which is the one two years old.

As for sheep — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — wrote the Book of Alms, and in it concerning sheep: for every forty sheep up to one hundred twenty, one sheep; when they increase by one, then two sheep up to two hundred; when they increase by one over two hundred, then three sheep up to three hundred; if the sheep exceed that, then for every hundred, one sheep. The obligatory sheep among flocks is the jadhaʿah of ẓa'n (sheep) or the thaniyyah of maʿz (goats). The jadhaʿah is the one with one full year — and it was said six months — and the thaniyyah is the one with two years.

Then we undertake the examination of the zakat of camels in six loci.

The First Locus: On the extraction of a sheep for five camels, comprising three questions.

The First Question: The obligatory [animal] in terms of age is a jadhaʿah of sheep or a thaniyyah of goats. As for the type — namely, specifying sheep over goats — there are two positions: One is that the predominant sheep of the land are considered; if sheep predominate, then sheep are given, just as the zakat of fiṭr is determined by the predominant staple food, on the soundest view — unlike the sheep obligatory for forty [camels], where the giver's own type is considered because it is of the same kind. The second is that he gives whatever he wishes, for the name "sheep" applies to it, and only a sheep was obligated — just as in the unrestricted slave for expiation (al-raqabah al-muṭlaqah), whatever the name applies to suffices, and likewise the sheep mentioned in the rituals (manāsik). It was also said that the type of the camel-owner's own flock is considered — but this is remote.

The Second Question: If he gives a male jadhaʿ or a male thaniyy, there are two positions: One holds it suffices, following the name; the second holds it does not, treating the unrestricted here as restricted by the detailed ruling in sheep-zakat, which is the female. This dispute also arises regarding the "sheep of compensation" (shāh al-jubrān).

The Third Question: If he gives a camel for twenty or fewer [camels], it suffices — for it suffices for twenty-five, so it is all the more fitting that it suffice for less. There is no harm even if its value is less than the sheep. Al-Qaffāl said: A deficient-value [animal] is not accepted — but this is remote, for it attends to the substitute, and this was not established by way of substitution. It was said that a camel does not suffice for ten; rather, two animals are necessary — either a camel and a sheep, or two camels. This too is remote, for the reason of priority we mentioned. They also deliberated whether the camel given for five is entirely the obligation, or only its fifth.

The Second Locus: On the manner of shifting from bint makhāḍ to ibn labūn when the former is unavailable, comprising four questions.

The First Question: If neither a bint makhāḍ nor an ibn labūn exists in his property, he has the choice in purchasing — for whenever he purchases an ibn labūn, it becomes existent while the bint makhāḍ remains non-existent, and its taking becomes binding. The author of al-Taqrīb said: Purchasing a bint makhāḍ is specifically required, for they are equal in non-existence just as they are equal in existence.

The Second Question: If he possesses a defective bint makhāḍ, it is treated as non-existent, so an ibn labūn is taken from him. But if it is sound, he is not pressed for it. Al-Qaffāl said: He is obliged to purchase a bint makhāḍ, for it exists in his property; it was only waived for his benefit, so an ibn labūn is not taken. Another said: It is taken, for it is as if non-existent, since its delivery is not obligatory.

The Third Question: A hermaphrodite (khunthā) among bint labūn is taken as a substitute for bint makhāḍ when the latter is unavailable — for it is either male or female, and both are taken. It was said it is not taken as a substitute for bint makhāḍ, due to the deformity of its form from this deficiency.

The Fourth Question: If he gives a ḥiqqah as a substitute for bint labūn when the latter is unavailable, it is taken by compulsion, due to the loss of femininity through increased age, by analogy to ibn labūn relative to bint makhāḍ. The author of al-Taqrīb said: It is possible it is not taken, for it is a substitute not stipulated in the text.

The Third Locus: On the settling of the reckoning. When one camel exceeds one hundred twenty, three bint labūn are due. Regarding the spreading of the obligation over the single excess, there are two positions: One, by analogy, is that it spreads; the second is that it does not spread, such that for every forty a bint labūn is due. Upon this latter, it was built that if half a camel exceeds one hundred twenty, three bint labūn become obligatory — but this is remote. As for Abū Ḥanīfah, he said: The reckoning is restarted at that point, so for every five, a sheep is due. Ibn Khayrān said: One chooses between the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the school of Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with them both.

The Fourth Locus: On the conjunction of bint labūn and ḥiqāq. If one owns two hundred camels, these are four fifties and five forties. If only one of the two age-categories exists in his property, it is taken. If both are absent, he may purchase whichever he wishes, on the sound view. If both are present, then the obligation is to give what is more beneficial (aghbaṭ) for the poor — for the two are equal in obligation and existence, and a preference must be made; the interest of the poor is the most worthy basis of preference — unlike the two sheep and dirhams in the jubrān, for the wording of the report indicates that the choice there belongs to the giver. Ibn Surayj derived a position that one chooses here as in the jubrān. The Iraqis transmitted a position that the ḥiqqah is specifically determined, for the Law's desire for increased age is greater than for increased number — for it did not increase the number except after the cessation of the considered ages.

Branches on the Text: If he gives other than the more beneficial, and the collector (sāʿī) takes it deliberately, it does not fulfill the obligation. If he takes it by his own ijtihād, there are two positions. If we say it fulfills, then regarding the obligation of the amount of difference, there are two positions. If we say it is obligatory, then if he finds no share (shiqṣ) to purchase with it, we take the dirhams; if he finds one, is purchasing a share obligatory? Two positions. If we say it is obligatory, does he purchase from the type of the more beneficial or from the type of what was given? Two positions.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ر ع (f-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Branching off from a trunk; offshoot, subdivision, or derivative matter (farʿ) as opposed to the root (aṣl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological method, farʿ denotes a derived ruling or case not explicitly stated in the primary sources, requiring analogical extension (qiyās) from an aṣl.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is botanical branching; here used metaphorically for jurisprudential subdivisions—clearly majāz (metaphorical transfer) from physical to abstract.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The numeral "three" (thalāthah) functions as an explicative appositive to "branches" (furūʿ), specifying its count without altering the grammatical case.

chapters.title_en: Section 83 — On Jabarān (Compensatory Payments) and the Attributes of the Zakatable Asset
chapters.arabic_text:
الأول لو أخرج حقتين وبنتي لبون ونصف ولم يجز للتشقيص فلو ملك أربعمائة
فأخرج أربع حقاق وخمس بنات لبون فالأظهر الجواز
وفيه وجه أنه لا يجوز التفريق في جنس المخرج
الثاني لو جعل الحقاق الأربع أصلا ونزل إلى بنات المخاض وضم ثمانية
جبرانات واتخذ بنات اللبون أصلا ورقي إلى الجذاع وطلب عشر جبرانات لا يجوز
لأنه تخطى في الصورتين سنا واجبا هو أصل في نفسه وتكثير الجبران بغير حاجة
لا يجوز
الثالث لو كان في ماله حقة وأربع بنات لبون فجعل بنات اللبون أصلا وأخذ
جبرانا للحقة جاز ولو جعل الحقة أصلا وأخرج معها ثلاث بنات لبون وثلاث
جبرانات فالمذهب جوازه
وقيل يمتنع لأنه يبقى في ماله بنت لبون وهو مستغن عن الجبران فيه
النظر الخامس في الجبران وجبران كل مرتبة في السن عند فقد السن الواجب
شاتان أو عشرون درهما منصوص عليه وإن رقي بسنين جمع بين جبرانين
ولا مدخل للجبران في زكاة البقر وفيه أربع مسائل
الأولى أن الخيرة إلى المعطى في تعيين الشاة أو الدراهم وفي الانخفاض
لتسليم الجبران أو الارتفاع لأخذ الجبران قيل الخيرة فيه إلى  المالك ومن
أصحابنا من نقل نصا عن الإملاء أن المتبع الأغبط للمساكين كما في اجتماع
الحقاق وبنات اللبون
وهو بعيد لأنه أثبت ترفيها للمالك كيلا يحتاج إلى الشراء فلا يليق به إلا
التخيير
نعم لو كانت إبله مراضا فوجب بنت لبون فأخرج بنت مخاض مع جبران قبل ولو
ارتقى إلى حقة وطلب جبرانا لم يجز لأنه ربما يزيد قيمة الجبران على المريضة
الثانية لو وجب بنت مخاض فنزل إلى فصيل مع جبران لم يجز لأنه ليس ذلك سنا
ولو وجبت جذعة فأخرج ثنية وطلب جبرانا فوجهان أحدهما له ذلك كسائر الأسنان
والثاني لا لأن الثنية ليست من أسنان الزكاة
الثالثة لو كان عليه بنت لبون فلم يجد وفي ماله حقة وجذعة فرقي إلى
الجذعة وطلب جبرانين ففي جوازه وجهان وجه المنع أنه مستغن عن الجبران
الثاني بوجود الحقة
وكذا الخلاف إذا نزل من الحقة إلى بنت المخاض مع وجود بنت اللبون ولو رقي
من بنت لبون إلى الجذعة مع وجود بنت مخاض فوجهان مرتبان وأولى بالجواز لأن
القريب الموجود ليس في جهة الترقي
الرابعة لا يجوز تفريق الجبران الواحد بإخراج شاة وعشرة دراهم ولو رقي
سنين
أو نزل وجمع بين عشرين درهما وشاتين جاز كما في كفاءة يمينين
النظر السادس في صفة المخرج من حيث النقصان والكمال والنقصان خمسة المرض
والعيب والذكورة والصغر ورداءة النوع كالمعز بالنسبة إلى الضأن فإن كان كل
المال كاملا في هذه الصفات لم يؤخذ إلا الكامل وإن كان كل المال ناقصا
فيؤخذ من جنسه إلا في نقصان الذكورة والسن فإن فيها وجهين أحدهما يؤخذ
قياسا على غيره والثاني لا لأن اسم الشاة أو بنت لبون ينطلق على المريضة
والمعيبة والرديئة ولا ينطلق على الذكر والفصيل وقد وجب بلفظ بنت لبون مثلا
ولأنه يؤدي أخذ الذكر والصغير إلى التسوية بين القليل والكثير فيؤخذ من
إحدى وستين واحدة ومن خمس وعشرين واحدة
ويؤخذ من ست وثلاثين ابن لبون ومن خمس وعشرين وهذا محال
وفيه وجه ثالث أنه  حيث يؤدي إلى التسوية فلا يأخذ إلا أنثى وكبيرة وإن
جاوز هذا المقدار وأخذ من الصغار صغيرة أما إذا اختلف المال في هذه الصفات
أما في صفة الذكورة والصغر فلا يأخذ إلا الأكمل فإذا كان في المال أنثى
وكبيرة فلا يأخذ إلا الأنثى والكبيرة لأنه قال في خمس وعشرين بنت مخاض
والغالب أن كل المال لا ينفك عن الصغير والذكر ولما روي أن عمر قال لمصدقه
اعتد عليهم بالسخلة التي يروح بها الراعي على يديه ولا تأخذها ولا تأخذ
الأكولة ولا الربى ولا الماخض ولا فحل الغنم وخذ الجذعة من الضأن والثنية
من المعز فذلك عدل بين غذاء المال
المال وجباره
الأكولة ما اتخذ للأكل والربى التى تربي ولدها والماخض الحامل
وكل ذلك لا يؤخذ نظرا للمالك فإن تبرع به قبل
وأما صفة المرض فإذا انقسم المال إلى صحيح ومريض لم يؤخذ إلا الصحيح نعم
يؤخذ صحيح في أقل الدرجات حتى بالغ بعض أصحابنا وقال لو كان الصحيح واحدة
والواجب شاتان صحيح فأخرجها مع مريضة لم يجز لأن المريضة تزكى المخرج معها
وهي صحيحة وهذا سرف بل يقضى بأنه إذا لم يستبق شيئا من الصحيح جاز ثم يكتفى
بصحيحة بقرب قيمتها من ربع عشر ماله إذا كان المملوك أربعين من الغنم كيلا
يؤدي إلى الإجحاف به
أما صفة العيب فإذا انقسم المال إلى معيب وصحيح فليخرج باعتبار القيمة ما
يكون مساويا ربع عشر ماله في صورة الأربعين وإن كان الكل معيبا وبعضه أردأ
قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه يخرج أجود ما عنده وقال الأصحاب يأخذ الوسط بين
الدرجتين وهو الأصح وأما اختلاف النوع كالمعز والضأن والأرحبية
والمهرية ففيه قولان أحدهما الأخذ بالأغلب لأن تمييز ذلك عسير وإن استويا
فهو كاجتماع الحقاق وبنات اللبون والثاني أنه يأخذ من كل بقسطه حتى لو ملك
عشرة أرحبية وعشرة مجيدية وخمسا مهرية فإنا نأخذ قيمة خمس ببنت مخاض أرحبية
وخمس مجيدية وخمس مهرية ويشترى به صنفا من هذه الأصناف
فخرج من هذا أنه مهما  اختلف المال في الذكورة والأنوثة والصغيرة والكبيرة
لا يأخذ إلا الكبيرة والأنثى وإن اختلف في المرض والعيب والسلامة فيأخذ
بالنسبة من كل واحد وإن اختلف في النوع فقولان هذا بيان النصاب ولا زكاة
على من لم يملك نصابا إلا إذا تم بالخلطة نصابا
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - باب صدقة الخلطاء - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وفيه
خمسة فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone, to restore, to compensate for a deficiency; jabarān denotes that which mends a shortfall.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A compensatory increment supplied to rectify an imbalance in the obligatory category, preserving equity (ʿadl) in the divine ordinance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of "mending" (jabr); metaphorically extended to fiscal substitution where the substitute (badal) stands in for the missing essential.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and disjunctive constructions (sharṭ wa-jazāʾ) governing permissibility; also the rule of taʿlīq (suspension) where rulings hinge on existential states (wujūd/ʿadam).
chapters.translation:
I say: The first [subsidiary]: If one pays two ḥiqqah and two bint labūn and a half — this being impermissible due to fragmentation — then if one owns four hundred [camels] and pays four ḥiqāq and five banāt labūn, the more apparent [position] is permissibility. And there is a face [of the school] that it is impermissible to separate [the payment] across the genus of what is paid out.

The second: If one makes the four ḥiqāq the basis and descends to banāt makhāḍ, annexing eight jabarān, or makes banāt labūn the basis and ascends to jidhāʿ, demanding ten jabarān — this is impermissible, because in both scenarios one has skipped over an obligatory age-category that is itself a root, and multiplying jabarān without need is not permitted.

The third: If one's wealth contains a ḥiqqah and four banāt labūn, and one makes the banāt labūn the basis and takes a jabarān for the ḥiqqah, this is permissible. And if one makes the ḥiqqah the basis and pays out with it three banāt labūn and three jabarān, the [established] school [position] is its permissibility. And it was said [by some] that it is impermissible, because there remains in one's wealth a bint labūn, and one is thereby independent of the jabarān for it.

The fifth consideration concerns the jabarān. The jabarān for each age-category, when the obligatory age is absent, is two sheep or twenty dirhams — this being textually stipulated (manṣūṣ). If one ascends across two age-categories, one combines two jabarān. There is no entry for jabarān in the zakāh of cattle. It contains four subsidiary questions:

The first: The choice (al-khiyarah) in designating the sheep or the dirhams belongs to the giver. As for descending [to a lower age] to deliver a jabarān, or ascending [to a higher age] to take a jabarān, it was said the choice therein belongs to the owner. And among our companions is one who transmitted a text (naṣṣ) from al-Imlāʾ that the criterion is what is more advantageous (aghbaṭ) for the poor — just as in the case of the conjunction of ḥiqāq and banāt labūn. But this is remote, because it establishes a concession (tarfīh) for the owner so that he need not purchase [an animal], and nothing befits this save granting him the choice.

Yes — if one's camels were sick, and a bint labūn became obligatory, and one paid a bint makhāḍ with a jabarān, this is accepted. But if one ascended to a ḥiqqah and demanded a jabarān, it is impermissible, because the value of the jabarān might exceed that of the sick [animal].

The second: If a bint makhāḍ becomes obligatory, and one descends to a faṣīl (weaned young) with a jabarān, this is impermissible, because that is not an age-category [of zakāh]. And if a jadhaʿah becomes obligatory, and one pays a thaniyyah and demands a jabarān, there are two faces: one — he may do so, like other age-categories; the second — no, because the thaniyyah is not among the zakāh age-categories.

The third: If a bint labūn is due upon one, and one finds none, while one's wealth contains a ḥiqqah and a jadhaʿah, and one ascends to the jadhaʿah demanding two jabarān — there are two faces on its permissibility. The face of prohibition [holds] that one is independent of the jabarān by the existence of the ḥiqqah. Likewise the disagreement when one descends from the ḥiqqah to the bint makhāḍ while a bint labūn exists. And if one ascends from a bint labūn to a jadhaʿah while a bint makhāḍ exists, there are two faces, ordered [in strength], and the more deserving of permissibility [is the latter], because the proximate [category] present is not in the direction of the ascent.

The fourth: It is impermissible to split a single jabarān by paying one sheep and ten dirhams. But if one ascends across age-categories or descends, and combines twenty dirhams and two sheep, it is permissible — just as in the case of two expiations (kaffāratayn).

The sixth consideration concerns the attribute of what is paid out, in terms of deficiency and completeness. Deficiency is of five kinds: sickness, defect, maleness, smallness, and inferiority of type — such as goats relative to sheep. If all the wealth is complete in these attributes, nothing is taken save the complete. If all the wealth is deficient, one takes from its own kind — except in the deficiency of maleness and age, for therein are two faces: one — one takes [the male or young] by analogy (qiyāsan) to other [deficiencies]; the second — no, because the name "sheep" or "bint labūn" applies to the sick, the defective, and the inferior, but does not apply to the male or the faṣīl. And the obligation was pronounced by the term "bint labūn," for instance. And because taking the male and the small leads to equating the few and the many: one would take from sixty-one a single [animal], and from twenty-five a single [animal]; and one would take from thirty-six an ibn labūn and from twenty-five a single [animal] — and this is absurd. There is a third face: that wherever it leads to equating [the few and the many], one takes only a female and a large [animal]; but if it exceeds that measure, one takes from the small [animals] a small one.

As for when the wealth differs in these attributes — regarding the attribute of maleness and smallness, one takes only the most complete. So if the wealth contains a female and a large [animal], one takes only the female and the large, because He said: "In twenty-five, a bint makhāḍ," and the dominant [case] is that all wealth is not free of the small and the male. And because it was narrated that ʿUmar said to his collector: "Count for them the young goat (sakhlah) that the shepherd returns upon his hands, but do not take it; and do not take the akūlah, nor the rabā, nor the mākhiḍ, nor the ram of the flock; and take the jadhaʿah from sheep and the thaniyyah from goats — for that is equity between the nourishment of the wealth and its jabarān." The akūlah is what is kept for eating; the rabā is that which rears its young; the mākhiḍ is the pregnant. All of that is not taken, out of consideration for the owner — unless he volunteers it, then it is accepted.

As for the attribute of sickness: if the wealth divides into sound and sick, nothing is taken save the sound. Yes, a sound [animal] is taken at the lowest degree [of soundness], until one of our companions went so far as to say: if the sound [animals] were a single one, and the obligatory [amount] were two sound sheep, and one paid it along with a sick one, it is impermissible — because the sick one would be counted alongside the sound one in discharging the obligation, and this is extravagance (saraf). Rather, it is adjudged that if one has not reserved any of the sound [animals], it is permissible; then one is satisfied with a sound [sheep] whose value approximates one-quarter of one-tenth (rubʿ ʿushr) of one's wealth — when the owned [flock] is forty sheep — so as not to lead to injustice against him.

As for the attribute of defect: if the wealth divides into defective and sound, one pays out, by consideration of value, what equals one-quarter of one-tenth of one's wealth in the case of the forty. If all is defective and some is more inferior, al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: one pays the best of what one has. And the companions said: one takes the middle between the two degrees — and this is the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ).

As for the difference of type — such as goats and sheep, and arḥabiyyah and mahriyyah [camel breeds] — therein are two sayings: one — one takes by the predominant [type], because distinguishing that is difficult; and if they are equal, it is like the conjunction of ḥiqāq and banāt labūn. The second — one takes from each according to its proportion, such that if one owned ten arḥabiyyah, ten mujīdiyyah, and five mahriyyah, we would take the value of five [camels] — a bint makhāḍ arḥabiyyah, five mujīdiyyah, and five mahriyyah — and purchase with it a single type from these types.

It follows from this that whenever the wealth differs in maleness and femaleness, and smallness and largeness, one takes only the large and the female. If it differs in sickness, defect, and soundness, one takes proportionally from each. And if it differs in type, there are two sayings.

This is the exposition of the niṣāb. And there is no zakāh upon one who does not own a niṣāb — except when it is completed to a niṣāb by partnership (khilṭah).

— Peace be upon him — Chapter on the Zakāh of Partners (ṣadaqat al-khulaṭāʾ) — Peace be upon him — It contains five sections:
