### | الطرف الثالث في الاستئجار على 1 الحج والنظر في شرائطه وأحكامه

أما الشرائط فتذكر في الإجارة ونذكر هاهنا أربع شرائط
الأول أن يكون الأجير قادرا على الحج فإن كان مريضا أو كان الطريق مخوفا
أو ضاف الوقت وطالت المسافة لم تنعقد الإجارة ولو جرى في وقت هجوم الأنداء
والثلوج ولكن كان زواله معلوما فالأظهر الصحة وقيل لا يجوز لتعذر النهوض في
الحال ومهما صحت الإجارة وجب على الأجير الخروج مع أول رفقة ولا يجوز
التأخير إلا بعد انتظار الرفقة فلا عذر بعد وجودها
الثاني أن لا يضيف الإجارة الواردة على العين إلى حجة في السنة القابلة
إلا إذا كانت المسافة بحيث لا تقطع في سنة فيجوز له ذلك لإمكان التشاغل
بالسفر في الحال وإن وردت الإجارة على الذمة فله أن يعين أية سنة شاء فإن
أطلق نزل على السنة الأولى
الثالث كون الحج معلوما بأعماله للأجير ولا يحتاج إلى التعريف في العقد
فإنه مشهر في العرف فإنه فرض جهل على الندور من أحدهما لم يصح العقد
وأما تعيين ميقات الإحرام فيه اختلاف نص فقيل قولان أحدهما يشترط لأن غرض
الأجير يتفاوت به والثاني لا لأن غرض المستأجر لا يتفاوت
وقيل بل هو على حالين فإن كان المستأجر له ميتا فلا غرض إلا تبرئة ذمته
فأما الحي فله غرض في تعيين المواقيت فيلزمه ذلك
وقيل إن كان على طريقه ميقات تعين بالعرف وإن كان طريقه يقضي إلى مسلكين
يقضي كل واحد إلى ميقات آخر فلا بد من التعيين
الرابع أن لا  يعقد بصيغة الجعالة فلو قال المعضوب من حج عني فله مائة فحج
عنه إنسان نقل المزني أنه وقع عنه واستحق المائة وخر ج الأصحاب منه تصحيح
صيغة الجعالة في كل ما يقبل الإجارة
وذهب بعض الأصحاب إلى تزييفه فإن ذلك يحتمل من ضرورة الجعالة فعلى هذا
بطلت التسمية وصح الإذن واستحق المأذون أجرة المثل لوقوع الحج عن الإذن
ومهما فسدت الإجارة بفساد العوض بقي الإذن صحيحا ووجب أجرة المثل لوقوع
الحج عن الإذن وقيل إن الإذن يفسد بهذا العموم فإن من قال وكلت كل من أراد
بيع داري لم تصح الوكالة لعدم تعين الوكيل فكذلك هاهنا

### | النظر الثاني في أحكام الإجارة عند اختلاف أحوال الأجير وأحواله سبعة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ج-ر (ajara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Recompense, wage, or hire; the exchange of benefit for a stipulated payment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Contractual hire (ijārah) as a lawful claim upon service or usufruct, distinct from gratuitous permission (idhn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in denoting a stipulated wage; metaphorically extended to divine reward (ajr) in the afterlife.
- Root: ع-ض-ب (ʿaḍaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be incapacitated, especially by chronic illness or physical debility preventing action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The state of one unable to perform an obligation personally, necessitating delegation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bodily incapacity; not metaphorical here, as it grounds legal substitution.
- Root: ج-ع-ل (jaʿala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make, appoint, or stipulate a reward for a specific task.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Juʿālah — a unilateral offer of compensation for a defined result, distinct from ijārah’s bilateral binding.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in reward-for-act; rhetorically contrasts with ijārah in requiring no fixed term or mutual consent at inception.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Dependency (Taʿlīq al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (e.g., "if he is sick") governs the apodosis (contract invalidity), requiring precise parsing of hypotheticals in legal discourse.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third branch concerns hiring for the Hajj, with examination of its conditions and rulings.

As for the conditions, they are mentioned in the chapter on hire (ijārah); here we mention four conditions.

The first: that the hired person be capable of performing the Hajj. If he is sick, or the road is perilous, or the time is constrained and the distance long, the contract does not validly conclude. Even if the contract occurs at a time when rains and snows are imminent, yet their cessation is known [to be certain], the more apparent [view] is validity; and it was said [alternatively]: it is not permissible, due to the impossibility of setting out at present. Whenever the hire contract is valid, the hired person is obligated to depart with the first caravan; delay is not permissible except [while] awaiting the caravan — after its arrival, there is no excuse.

The second: that he not attach a hire contract upon a specific person (al-ʿayn) to a Hajj in the coming year, unless the distance is such that it cannot be traversed within one year — then it is permissible for him [to defer], due to the possibility of occupying himself with travel at present. If the hire contract is upon the liability (al-dhimmah), then he may specify whichever year he wishes; if left unrestricted, it applies to the first year.

The third: that the Hajj be known to the hired person by its rites; there is no need for definition in the contract, for it is well-known in custom. If ignorance of it is rare from either party, the contract is not valid. As for specifying the miqāt (station of iḥrām), there is a divergence of transmitted texts. It was said: two opinions — one: it is required, because the hired person’s purpose varies with it; the second: it is not required, because the employer’s purpose does not vary. And it was said: rather, it is two cases — if the employer is deceased, there is no purpose except clearing his liability; as for the living, he has a purpose in specifying the stations, so it is incumbent upon him. And it was said: if his route has a single miqāt, it is determined by custom; if his route leads to two paths, each leading to a different miqāt, then specification is indispensable.

The fourth: that he not contract by the formula of juʿālah (reward-offer). Thus, if an incapacitated person (maʿḍūb) says: "Whoever performs the Hajj on my behalf shall have one hundred," and a man performs the Hajj for him, al-Muzanī transmitted that it falls on his behalf and he deserves the hundred. The [Shāfiʿī] associates derived from this the validity of the juʿālah formula in everything that admits hire. Some associates held this to be weak, for that [ruling] may arise from the exigency of juʿālah. On this [latter view], the naming [of the reward] is void, but the permission (idhn) remains valid, and the permitted one deserves the equivalent wage (ujrat al-mithl), because the Hajj occurred by permission. Whenever the hire contract is corrupted by corruption of the compensation, the permission remains sound and the equivalent wage is obligatory, since the Hajj occurred by permission. And it was said: the permission is corrupted by this generality — for if one says, "I have deputized anyone who wishes to sell my house," the agency is not valid due to the non-specification of the agent; likewise here.

The second examination concerns the rulings of hire when the hired person’s states differ; his states are seven.

chapters.title_en: Section 113 — On Breach of Contract, Substitution, and Compensation in Hired Pilgrimage (Ḥajj al-Ijārah)
chapters.arabic_text:
الأولى إذا فاته الحج في السنة الأولى بامتناعه عن الخروج انفسخت الإجارة
إن كانت واردة على العين فإن كانت واردة على الذمة قال العراقيون لم ينفسخ
وللمستأجر الخيار كما لو أفلس المشتري بالثمن وقال المراوزة فيه قولان كما
في انقطاع جنس المسلم فيه على قول ينفسخ وعلى قول يثبت الخيار
فإن أثبتنا الخيار وإن كان المستأجر ميتا فلا خيار للورثة لأنه يجب
عليهم صرف الأجرة إلى أجير آخر لتبرئة ذمته والأجير الذى عينه الميت أولى
وفيه احتمال إذ قد يكون للميت فيه مصلحة في إبدال الأجير بمن هو أرغب منه
الثانية إذا خالف في الميقات فأحرم بعمرة عن نفسه ثم أحرم بحج المستأجر
في جوف مكة فيحط شيء من أجرته وفي القدر المحطوط قولان
أحدهما أن يقال حجة من الميقات كم أجرتها وحجة من جوف مكة كم أجرتها
ويعرف نسبة التفاوت فإن كان عشرا فيحط العشر على المسمى
وحقيقة هذا القول ترجع إلى أن الأجرة تقابل الحج المقصود أبدا دون السفر
الذى هو ذريعة فلذلك لم يدخله في الاعتبار
والثاني أنه يعرف التفاوت بين حجة من البلد الذى استؤجر فيها وحجة من جوف
مكة فيكثر التفاوت فيحط عن أجرته وحاصل هذا أن السفر إن كان تقابله الأجرة
فلا يحسب له في هذا القول  لأنه صرفه إلى عمرة نفسه
المسألة بحالها لو عاد إلى الميقات وأنشأ الإحرام بالحج عنه فإن لم نقابل
السفر
بأجرة أصلا استحق تمام الأجرة وإن قابلنا أحبطنا ما قابل المسافة التى
صرفها إلى عمرته فإن حسبنا له السفر استحق تمام الأجرة فإن أحبطنا المسافة
هاهنا لصرفها إلى عمرته فيضبط التفاوت بين أجرة حجة من بلدة نهضتها ومن
الميقات إحرامها وبين حجة أنشئت من الميقات من غير سبق سفر ويحط من المسمى
بنسبته
المسألة بحالها لم يعتمر أصلا لكن أحرم من جوف مكة فما صرف السفر إلى
نفسه لكن لزمه دم الإساءة فهل ينجبر بالدم ما يحط من الأجرة فيه قولان
أحدهما ينجبر فلا يحط شئ والثاني يحط لأن الدم وجب حقا لله تعالى ومقصود
المستأجر لا ينجبر فعلى هذا يعود الخلاف في أن السفر هل يحسب له في توزيع
الأجرة وهاهنا أولى بأن يحسب وإن قلنا إنه ينجبر بالدم فلو كان قيمة الدم
تنقص عما يقتضيه الحط فقدر التفاوت هل يحط فيه وجهان
المسألة بحالها عين له الكوفة ليحرم بها فجاوزها ففي لزوم دم الإساءة
وجهان مأخذهما التردد في أن تعيينه هل يلتحق بتعيين الشرع فإن قلنا يجب
الدم عاد الخلاف في أنه هل يجبر النقصان وإن قلنا لا يجب عاد الخلاف في أن
المسافر هل يحسب له ولا خلاف أنه لو ارتكب محظورا غير مفسد لزمه الدم ولا
حط لأنه أتى بتمام العمل
الثالثة إذا خالف في الجهة بأن استأجره على القران فأفرد فقد زاد خيرا
ولو قرن بإذنه فأصح الوجهين أن دم القران على المستأجر وكأنه قرن بنفسه
والثاني على الأجير لأنه التزم تحصيل الحج والعمرة بطريق القران وتتمة
القران بالدم فليف به ولو استأجره على الإفراد فقرن فالدم على الأجير قطعا
والحج والعمرة واقعان عن المستأجر لأن الشرع جعل القران كالإفراد وهل يحط
شئ من الأجرة
مع جبره بالدم فيه الخلاف السابق
وإن أمره بالقران فتمتع فوجهان أحدهما أنه كالقرآن لأنه إن نقص في إحرام
الحج من  الميقات فقد زاد في العمل والثاني أن زيادته غير محسوبة فإنه غير
مأمور به وعلى هذا فالدم عليه لأنا جعلناه مخالفا وإن جعلناه موافقا
فالوجهان في الدم عائدان
الرابعة إذا جامع الأجير فسد حجه وانفسخت الإجارة إن كانت
وردت على عينه لفوات الوقت ولزمه القضاء لنفسه ورد الأجرة وإن وردت على
ذمته لم تنفسخ وعليه القضاء في السنة الثانية
فإذا قضى فهل يقع عن المستأجر فعلى وجهين أحدهما لا لأن القضاء يقع عمن
انصرف الفاسد إليه فعلى هذا عليه أن يحج عن المستأجر حجة أخرى سوى القضاء
والثاني أنه يقع عنه فإنه لو تمم الأول لوقع عنه وهذا قضاء الأول
الخامسة لو أحرم عن مستأجره ثم صرف إلى نفسه على ظن أنه ينصرف إليه وأتم
الحج فالحج عن المستأجر وفي استحقاقه الأجرة قولان ووجه السقوط أنه قصد أن
يعمل لنفسه وهما جاريان في الصباغ إذا جحد الثوب وصبغه لنفسه في أنه هل
يستحق الأجرة
السادسة إذا مات الأجير في أثناء الحج يقدم على هذا أن من مات في أثناء
حجه فهل لوريثه أن يستأجر من يبني على حجه ويأتي بالبقية فيه قولان
أحدهما نعم لأن الاستنابة في بعضه كالاستنابه في كله والثاني لا إذ يبعد
أداء عبادة واحدة من شخصين
فإن جوزنا فمات قبل الوقوف أحرم الأجير من حيث انتهى إليه المستأجر عنه
ولا ضرر في وقوعه وراء الميقات
وإن مات بعد الوقوف وبعد طلوع الفجر من يوم النحر قال المراوزة يحرم
الأجير وإن لم يكن في أشهر الحج لأن هذا بناء على ما سبق في الأشهر وقال
العراقيون يحرم بعمرة ويأتي ببقية أعمال الحج ولا يأتي بمناسك مني وهو بعيد
وإن مات بين التحللين فقياس المراوزة أن يأتي بإحرام حكمه أن لا يمنع
اللبس والقلم وإن مات بعد التحللين فلا يبقى للإحرام وجه فيتعين الرجوع إلى
إبدال المناسك الواقعة بعد التحللين رجعنا إلى الأجير فإن جوزنا البناء
فالمستأجر متمكن منه فيستحق ورثة الأجير قسطا من الأجرة لأن ما سبق  لم يحبط
وإن قلنا لا يمكن البناء فقد حبط ما سبق ففي استحقاق قسط من الأجرة وجهان
أحدهما لا لأنه لم يحصل له غرض والثاني نعم لأنه أتى بالبعض ولم يقصر في
البعض
فإن قلنا يستحق قسطا ففي التوزيع وجهان أحدهما أنها لا تحسب المسافة بل
يبتدئ التقدير من وقت الإحرام فما يقابله يستحق والثاني تحسب المسافة لأنه
من عمله وعلى هذا يستحق الأكثر لا محالة
وإن مات قبل الإحرام ففي احتساب السفر خلاف مرتب وأولى بأن لا يحسب لأن
الذريعة إذا لم تتصل بالمقصود لا يبقى لها حكم وإن كانت الإجارة واردة على
الذمة فلا تنفسخ بل يبقى الحج دينا في تركه الأجير فيستأجر وارثه من
تركته من يتم على قول تجويز البناء أو من يبتدىء حجا على قول المنع
السابعة لو أحصر الأجير فتحلل فهو كالموت وإن فاته الحج بعد الإحرام فهو
كالإفساد لأنه يجب القضاء ولا يستحق شيئا في مقابلة عمله وذكر العراقيون
وجها أنه يستحق قسطا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-و-ت (f-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Loss, escape, passing of an opportunity or time-window.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Failure to realize an obligatory act within its appointed time; forfeiture of the intended benefit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in time-loss; metaphorical in contractual nullification (infisākh) by loss of the season.
- Root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covenant, protection, liability attached to a person's responsibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A debt or obligation incumbent upon the person (dhimmah), not tied to a specific object.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for personal liability; metaphorical for contractual obligation detached from a designated asset.
- Root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Choice, selection between alternatives.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Option (khiyār) as a legal right to rescind or affirm a contract upon breach or defect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in voluntary election; technical in juristic rescission rights.
- Root: ح-ط-ط (ḥ-ṭ-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lower, deduct, reduce from a quantity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Abatement of a stipulated wage (ujrah) proportional to unfulfilled service.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical lowering; metaphorical for monetary reduction.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, execute, adjudicate, complete a debt or duty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Making up (qaḍāʾ) a missed or invalidated religious obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for judicial decree; technical for compensatory performance of worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Syntax (al-Sharṭ wa al-Taqsīm) — The text repeatedly employs "if... then" (fa-in) and "on one view... on the other" (ʿalā qawl... wa-ʿalā qawl) to structure legal alternatives; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is governed by the protasis, requiring precise tracking of the conditional chain.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first case — if the ḥajj is missed in the first year due to the hired agent's refusal to set out, the hire contract is dissolved if it was contracted upon a specific person (ʿayn). But if it was contracted upon the liability (dhimmah), the Iraqis said it is not dissolved, and the hirer has the option (khiyār), just as when the buyer is declared bankrupt over the price. The Marwazīs held two opinions, as in the case of the interruption of the species of a salam commodity: on one view it is dissolved, and on another the option is affirmed.

If we affirm the option, and the hirer is deceased, then the heirs have no option, because they are obliged to direct the wage to another agent to clear the deceased's liability (barāʾat dhimmah). And the agent whom the deceased had specifically designated is more entitled. Yet there is a possibility [to the contrary], since the deceased may have had an interest in replacing the agent with one more desirable to him.

The second case — if he violated the mīqāt and entered iḥrām for an ʿumrah on his own behalf, then entered iḥrām for the hired ḥajj within Mecca, then something is deducted from his wage. Concerning the amount of the deduction there are two opinions:

One of them is that one says: How much is the wage for a ḥajj from the mīqāt, and how much for a ḥajj from within Mecca? The proportion of the difference is then ascertained — if it is a tenth, then a tenth is deducted from the named wage. The reality of this view reverts to the principle that the wage always corresponds to the intended ḥajj itself, not to the journey (safar) which is merely a means (dhariʿah); therefore the journey is not brought into consideration.

The second is that one ascertains the difference between a ḥajj from the town in which he was hired and a ḥajj from within Mecca, so the difference is greater, and a greater deduction is made from his wage. The upshot of this is that if the journey is what the wage corresponds to, it is not counted for him in this view, because he diverted it to his own ʿumrah.

The case remains the same if he returned to the mīqāt and initiated iḥrām for the ḥajj on behalf of the hirer. If we do not correlate the journey with any wage at all, he deserves the full wage. If we do correlate it, we deduct what corresponds to the distance he diverted to his ʿumrah. If we count the journey for him, he deserves the full wage. If we deduct the distance here because he diverted it to his ʿumrah, then one calibrates the difference between the wage of a ḥajj from a town from which he set out and whose iḥrām is from the mīqāt, and a ḥajj initiated from the mīqāt without prior travel, and deducts from the named [wage] in that proportion.

The case remains the same if he did not perform ʿumrah at all but entered iḥrām from within Mecca — he did not divert the journey to himself, yet the blood [offering] for transgression (dam al-isāʾah) became incumbent upon him. Does the blood [offering] compensate for what is deducted from the wage? There are two opinions:

One of them: it compensates, so nothing is deducted. The second: it is deducted, because the blood [offering] is a right owed to God (ḥaqq Allāh), and the hirer's purpose is not thereby compensated. On this view, the earlier dispute returns as to whether the journey is counted for him in the distribution of the wage — and here it is more appropriate that it be counted. If we say it is compensated by the blood [offering], then if the value of the blood [offering] is less than what the deduction would require, there are two aspects concerning whether the amount of the difference is deducted.

The case remains the same — he designated Kūfah for him to enter iḥrām there, and he passed beyond it. Concerning the obligation of the blood [offering] for transgression there are two aspects, whose basis is the hesitation over whether his designation attaches to the designation of the Sacred Law (taʿyīn al-sharʿ). If we say the blood [offering] is obligatory, the dispute returns as to whether it compensates the deficiency. If we say it is not obligatory, the dispute returns as to whether the journey is counted for him. There is no dispute that if he committed a prohibited act that does not invalidate [the ḥajj], the blood [offering] is obligatory upon him and no deduction is made, because he performed the complete work.

The third case — if he violated the mode (jihat) by being hired for qirān and he performed ifrād, he has added good. If he performed qirān with his permission, then the more correct of the two aspects is that the blood [offering] of qirān is upon the hirer, as if he himself had performed qirān. The second is that it is upon the agent, because he undertook to achieve the ḥajj and ʿumrah by the way of qirān, and the completion of qirān is through the blood [offering], so let him fulfill it. If he was hired for ifrād and performed qirān, the blood [offering] is upon the agent definitively, and the ḥajj and ʿumrah occur on behalf of the hirer, because the Sacred Law made qirān like ifrād. Is anything deducted from the wage, along with its compensation by the blood [offering]? The earlier dispute applies.

If he ordered him to perform qirān and he performed tamattuʿ, there are two aspects: one of them is that it is like qirān, because although he diminished [the iḥrām] of the ḥajj from the mīqāt, he added to the work. The second is that his addition is not counted, because he was not commanded to do it. On this view, the blood [offering] is upon him, for we deem him a violator. If we deem him compliant, the two aspects concerning the blood [offering] return.

The fourth case — if the agent had sexual intercourse [during iḥrām], his ḥajj is invalidated, and the hire contract is dissolved if it was contracted upon his specific person, due to the loss of the time. He is obliged to make up (qaḍāʾ) for himself and to return the wage. If it was contracted upon his liability, it is not dissolved, and he must make up in the second year.

When he makes up, does it occur on behalf of the hirer? There are two aspects: one of them is no, because the make-up occurs on behalf of the one to whom the invalid [ḥajj] was directed. On this view, he must perform another ḥajj for the hirer besides the make-up. The second is that it occurs on his behalf, for if he had completed the first, it would have occurred on his behalf, and this is the make-up of the first.

The fifth case — if he entered iḥrām on behalf of his hirer, then diverted it to himself, thinking that it would revert to him, and completed the ḥajj, then the ḥajj is on behalf of the hirer. Concerning his entitlement to the wage there are two opinions. The basis of its forfeiture is that he intended to work for himself. Both [opinions] apply in the case of the dyer who denied the garment and dyed it for himself — whether he deserves the wage.

The sixth case — if the agent dies during the ḥajj. Prefatory to this: if one dies during his ḥajj, may his heir hire someone to build upon his ḥajj and complete the remainder? There are two opinions:

One of them: yes, because deputization in part is like deputization in whole. The second: no, for it is improbable that a single act of worship be performed by two persons.

If we permit it, and he died before the Standing (wuqūf), the [new] agent enters iḥrām from where the deceased had reached, and there is no harm in its occurring beyond the mīqāt.

If he died after the Standing and after dawn of the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr), the Marwazīs said: the agent enters iḥrām even if it is not in the months of ḥajj, because this builds upon what was said earlier concerning the months. The Iraqis said: he enters iḥrām for an ʿumrah and performs the remaining rites of ḥajj, but does not perform the rites of Minā — and this is far-fetched.

If he died between the two stages of partial release (taḥallulayn), then by the Marwazīs' analogy, he comes with an iḥrām whose legal effect is that it does not prohibit wearing [ordinary clothes] and clipping [nails]. If he died after the two releases, there is no room for iḥrām at all, so one must revert to substitutes for the rites occurring after the two releases.

We return to the agent: if we permit building upon [the deceased's ḥajj], then the hirer is able to achieve [his purpose], so the agent's heirs deserve a portion of the wage, because what preceded is not voided. If we say building is not possible, then what preceded is voided, and concerning entitlement to a portion of the wage there are two aspects: one of them is no, because he did not achieve his purpose; the second is yes, because he performed part and did not fall short in that part.

If we say he deserves a portion, then concerning the distribution there are two aspects: one of them is that the distance is not counted, but the estimation begins from the time of iḥrām, and what corresponds to it is deserved. The second is that the distance is counted, because it is part of his work — and on this view he deserves the greater [portion] necessarily.

If he died before iḥrām, there is an ordered dispute concerning the counting of the journey — and it is more appropriate that it not be counted, because when a means (dhariʿah) does not connect to its intended end, it retains no ruling.

If the hire contract was upon the liability, it is not dissolved; rather, the ḥajj remains a debt in the deceased agent's estate. His heir hires from the estate one who completes [the ḥajj] on the view permitting building, or one who begins a fresh ḥajj on the view prohibiting it.

The seventh case — if the agent was obstructed (iḥṣār) and released himself [from iḥrām], this is like death. If the ḥajj was missed after iḥrām, it is like invalidation (ifsād), because make-up is obligatory and he deserves nothing in return for his work. The Iraqis mentioned one aspect that he deserves a portion.

chapters.title_en: The Second Introduction to Hajj: Examination of the Appointed Times and Places (al-Mawāqīt)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المقدمة الثانية للحج

### | النظر في المواقيت

ويراد بالميقات الزمان والمكان
أما الميقات الزماني للحج فشهر شوال وذو القعدة وتسع من ذي الحجة وفي
ليلة العيد إلى طلوع الفجر وجهان أحدهما الصحة لبقاء وقت الوقوف والثاني لا
يصح ولكن يدوم في حق الوقوف
وقال أبو حنيفة جميع السنة وقت إحرام الحج
أما العمرة فجميع السنة وقتها ولا يكره في وقت كراهية الصلاة ولا في سائر
الأوقات إذا كان متخليا عن النسك
أما الحاج العاكف بمنى فالمعرج على الرمي والمبيت لا تنعقد عمرته في هذا
الوقت لأنه يحرم عليه الاشتغال بعمل العمرة في هذا الوقت لوجوب الرمي
والمبيت

### | فرع

إذا أحرم قبل أشهر الحج انعقد إحرامه ولم يكن حجا ويتحلل بعمل عمرة وهل
تقع عمرته صحيحة حتى يتأدى بها عمرة الإسلام فيه قولان
أحدهما نعم لأنه إذا بطل الحج بقي إحرام مطبق وينصرف إلى العمرة
والثاني أنه لا يقع عمرة بل هو كمن فاته الحج يتحلل بعمل عمرته عن إحرامه
ولا تتأدى  عمرته به وقيل إن صرفه إلى العمرة انصراف إليه

### | أما الميقات المكاني فالحاج أربعة أصناف

الأول الآفاقي المتوجه إلى مكة على قصد النسك عمرة كان أو حجا فعليه أن
يحرم من الميقات وميقات أهل المدينة ذو الحليفة وميقات أهل الشام الجحفة
ولأهل اليمن يلملم ولأهل نجد اليمن ونجد الحجاز قرن ولأهل المشرق ذات عرق
لتعيين عمر رضي الله عنه ذلك واستمر الناس عليه واستحب الشافعي رضي الله
عنه أن يحرم من العتيق قبل ذات عرق لورود خبر مرسل فيه
ثم هذه المواقيت لأهلها ولكل من مر بها من سائر البلاد ويكفيه أن يحرم من
موضع بإزاء ميقاته فإن المقصود مقدار بعده عن مكة والأولى أن يحرم من أول
الميقات وإن أحرم من آخره فلا بأس

### | فروع أربعة

الأول راكب التعاسيف إذا لم ينته إلى ميقات أحرم من حيث يوازي أول
الميقات فهو ميقاته ولو حاذى ميقاتين نسبنا إحرامه إلى أي الميقاتين
أردنا فإن كان أحدهما أبعد من مكة وكان أقرب من موقفه من الآخر نسبنا
إحرامه إليه وإن كان بينهما على سواء فوجهان أحدهما النسبة إلى الأبعد
والثاني إلى الأقرب وتتبين فائدته فيمن جاوز غير محرم ولزمه العود وعسر
الرجوع إلى موقفه بالضلال فإلى أي الميقاتين يرجع ولو رجع إلى موقفه كفاه
بل يكفي كل مجاوز أن يعود إلى مثل تلك المسافة وإن لم يعد إلى ذلك الموقف
بعينه
الثاني الغريب إذا أتى من جانب ولم يمر بميقات ولا حاذاه فيحرم على
مرحلتين من مكة نزولا على قضاء عمر رضي الله عنه في تأقيت ذات عرق لأهل
المشرق والتفاتا إلى حد المذهب في حاضري المسجد الحرام
الثالث مهما جاوز الموضع الذى هو ميقات في حقه فقد أساء فعليه الدم فإن
عاد ولكن بعد دخول مكة لم ينفعه العود وإن قبل دخول مكة وقبل مجاوزة
الميقات من مسافة القصر سقط دم الإساءة وصار متداركا بإحرامه من الميقات
وإن جاوز مسافة القصر فوجهان لأنه إذا بعد انقطع طريق التدارك هذا إذا عاد
وأنشأ الإحرام من الميقات فإن أنشأ الإحرام حيث انتهى وعاد إلى الميقات
محرما ففي
كونه متداركا وجهان فإن جعلناه متداركا فلا يلزمه أن يعود ملبيا خلافا
لأبي حنيفة
الرابع لو أحرم قبل الميقات فهو أفضل قطع به في القديم وقال في الجديد
يكره وهو متأول ومعناه أن يتوقى المخيط والطيب من غير إحرام وإذا قال رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من تمام الحج والعمرة أن يحرم بهما من دويرة أهله
الصنف الثاني من يتوجه إلى مكة لتجارة لا للنسك فهل يلزمه أن يدخل مكة
محرما من الميقات فيه قولان فإن قلنا لا يلزمه فليجاوزه ولا إساءة فإن سنح
له بعد ذلك أن يحرم فميقاته عند ظهور قصد النسك فإن جاوزه فهو كما لو جاوز
الميقات
الصنف الثالث من مسكنه بين الميقات وبين مكة فميقاته مسكنه فلا يجاوزه
الصنف الرابع المقيم بمكة مكيا كان أو آفافيا فميقاته مكة والأفضل أن
يحرم من باب داره أو في المسجد قريبا من البيت فيه اختلاف نص فإن خرج المكي
إلى الحل وأحرم بالحج فهو مسيء يلزمه الدم أو العود
إن أحرم بعد مفارقة العمران وقبل الانتهاء إلى الحل وأحرم بالحج
فوجهان منشؤهما أن الميقات في حقهم هو الحرم أو خطة مكة
أما العمرة فميقاتها كميقات الحج إلا في حق المكي والمستوطن بها فإن
عليهم الخروج إلى أطراف الحل ولو بخطوة في ابتداء الإحرام أو دوامه على رأي
وأفضل أطراف بقاع الحل الجعرانة وهي التي أحرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم بها وبعده التنعيم وهو أقرب إلى الحرم وقد اعتمرت عائشة رضي الله عنها
منه وبعده الحديبية

### | فرع

ولو أحرم من مكة في الحرم ولم يخرج إلى الحل ففي الاعتداد بعمرته قولان
أحدهما نعم لأنه إساءة في الميقات فلا تمنع الاعتداد كالحج
والثاني لا لأن الجمع بين الحل والحرم ركن في الحج فإن عرفة من الحل
فكذلك في العمرة فعلى هذا إن خرج إلى الحل ثم أعاد الطواف والسعي كفاه

- Root: و-ق-ت (wa-qā-ta)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes a fixed measure of time or space; al-waqt is the appointed term, and al-mīqāt is the place or time set as a boundary for ritual entry.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, mīqāt signifies the divinely or prophetically instituted limit (ḥadd) demarcating the valid commencement of iḥrām, both temporally and spatially.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for the fixed boundary; metaphorically (majāz) extended to the act of entering into the sacred state at that boundary.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — Governing the apodosis of hypothetical rulings (e.g., "if he enters iḥrām before the months... then his iḥrām is valid but not as hajj"), with careful parsing of the particle "fa" to mark result clauses.
chapters.translation:
I say: By "appointed time" (mīqāt) is intended both the time and the place.

As for the temporal mīqāt of Hajj, it is the month of Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and the first nine days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Regarding the night of the ʿĪd (i.e., the night preceding the 10th of Dhū al-Ḥijjah) up to the break of dawn, there are two positions (wajhān): one holds its validity due to the remaining time for the Standing at ʿArafāt; the second holds that it is not valid, but the state of iḥrām endures specifically for the purpose of the Standing.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: The entire year is a valid time for the iḥrām of Hajj.

As for ʿUmrah, the entire year is its time; it is not disliked during the times in which prayer is disliked, nor in any other times, provided one is free from an ongoing pilgrimage rite (nusuk).

As for the pilgrim staying continuously at Minā, whose obligation is the stoning (ramy) and the overnight stay (mabīt), his ʿUmrah is not validly contracted at that time, because engaging in the acts of ʿUmrah is forbidden to him at that time due to the obligation of stoning and overnight stay.

### Branch

If one enters iḥrām before the months of Hajj, his iḥrām is validly contracted but does not count as Hajj; he is released from it by performing the acts of ʿUmrah. Whether his ʿUmrah is valid such that it discharges the obligatory ʿUmrah of Islam — there are two opinions (qawlān):

One: Yes, it is valid, because when the Hajj is nullified, there remains an unqualified iḥrām (iḥrām muṭbaq), which is then diverted to ʿUmrah.

The second: It does not count as ʿUmrah; rather, he is like one who has missed the Hajj — he is released from his iḥrām by performing the acts of ʿUmrah, but his obligatory ʿUmrah is not discharged thereby. It was also said that his diverting it to ʿUmrah is itself a valid diversion.

### As for the spatial mīqāt, the pilgrims are of four categories:

The first: The distant pilgrim (āfāqī) heading to Mecca with the intention of a rite (nusuk), whether ʿUmrah or Hajj — he must enter iḥrām from the mīqāt. The mīqāt of the people of Medina is Dhū al-Ḥulayfah; the mīqāt of the people of Syria is al-Juḥfah; for the people of Yemen it is Yalamlam; for the people of Najd of Yemen and Najd of the Hijaz it is Qarn; and for the people of the East it is Dhāt ʿIrq — this being the designation of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him), and the people have continued upon it. Al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) recommended entering iḥrām from al-ʿAtīq before Dhāt ʿIrq, due to a mursal report transmitted concerning it.

Then, these mawāqīt are for their own people and for every passer-by from other lands. It suffices him to enter iḥrām from a spot parallel to his mīqāt, for the intended purpose is the measure of distance from Mecca. The preferable course is to enter iḥrām from the beginning of the mīqāt; if he enters from its end, there is no harm.

### Four Branches

The first: A traveler on a deviating course (rākib al-taʿāsīf) who does not reach a mīqāt — he enters iḥrām from the point parallel to the beginning of his mīqāt; that is his mīqāt. If he parallels two mawāqīt, we attribute his iḥrām to whichever of the two we wish. If one of them is farther from Mecca but closer to his position than the other, we attribute his iḥrām to it. If the two are equidistant, there are two positions: one attributes it to the farther, the second to the nearer. Its benefit becomes evident in the case of one who passes beyond (the mīqāt) without iḥrām, and it becomes incumbent upon him to return, but returning to his exact position is difficult due to being lost — to which of the two mawāqīt does he return? If he returns to his exact position, it suffices him. Indeed, every passer-by is sufficiently served by returning to a distance equivalent to that distance, even if he does not return to that very spot.

The second: A stranger who comes from a direction without passing by a mīqāt nor paralleling one — he enters iḥrām at two stages (marḥalatān) from Mecca, in deference to the ruling of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) in fixing Dhāt ʿIrq for the people of the East, and with regard to the boundary of the school concerning the residents of the Sacred Mosque (ḥāḍirī al-masjid al-ḥarām).

The third: Whenever one passes beyond the spot that is his mīqāt, he has committed an offense (asāʾa); a blood-offering (dam) is incumbent upon him. If he returns, but after entering Mecca, his return does not benefit him. If he returns before entering Mecca and before passing the mīqāt by the distance of qaṣr (i.e., the distance permitting shortening of prayer), the blood-offering for the offense is dropped, and he becomes one who has made up (mutadārik) by his iḥrām from the mīqāt. If he has passed beyond the distance of qaṣr, there are two positions, because when he has gone far, the path of making up is cut off. This applies when he returns and initiates iḥrām from the mīqāt. If he initiates iḥrām where he stopped and then returns to the mīqāt while already in iḥrām, there are two positions on whether he counts as having made up. If we deem him to have made up, he is not obliged to return while pronouncing the talbiyah — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah.

The fourth: If one enters iḥrām before the mīqāt, it is more virtuous — this was definitively stated in the Old School (al-qadīm). In the New School (al-jadīd), he said it is disliked (makrūh), and this is interpreted to mean that one should avoid sewn garments and perfume without formal iḥrām. For the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«مِنْ تَمَامِ الْحَجِّ وَالْعُمْرَةِ أَنْ يُحْرِمَ بِهِمَا مِنْ دُوَيْرَةِ أَهْلِهِ»} — "It is part of the completeness of Hajj and ʿUmrah that one enter iḥrām for them from the dwelling of his family."

The second category: One who heads to Mecca for trade, not for a rite — is he obliged to enter Mecca in iḥrām from the mīqāt? There are two opinions. If we say he is not obliged, let him pass beyond it with no offense. If the intention of a rite then occurs to him, his mīqāt is at the moment the intention of the rite becomes manifest; if he passes beyond it, he is like one who passed beyond the mīqāt.

The third category: One whose dwelling is between the mīqāt and Mecca — his mīqāt is his dwelling; he must not pass beyond it.

The fourth category: One residing in Mecca, whether Meccan or a distant settler — his mīqāt is Mecca. The preferable course is to enter iḥrām from the door of his house or in the mosque near the House — there is a difference in the text (naṣṣ) concerning this. If a Meccan goes out to the ḥill (the area outside the Sacred Precinct) and enters iḥrām for Hajj, he is an offender (musīʾ), and the blood-offering or return is incumbent upon him. If he enters iḥrām for Hajj after departing the built-up area but before reaching the ḥill, there are two positions, whose origin is whether the mīqāt for such persons is the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram) or the boundary of Mecca itself.

As for ʿUmrah, its mīqāt is like the mīqāt of Hajj, except regarding the Meccan and the one settled therein — for them it is incumbent to go out to the edges of the ḥill, even by a single step, at the commencement of iḥrām or its continuation, according to one view. The most virtuous of the edges of the ḥill is al-Jiʿrānah, from which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) entered iḥrām; after it, al-Tanʿīm, which is closest to the Sacred Precinct, and from which ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) performed ʿUmrah; and after it, al-Ḥudaybiyyah.

### Branch

If one enters iḥrām from Mecca within the Sacred Precinct without going out to the ḥill, there are two opinions on whether his ʿUmrah is counted (iʿtidād). One: Yes, it is counted, because it is an offense regarding the mīqāt, which does not prevent counting — as in Hajj. The second: No, because combining the ḥill and the ḥaram is a pillar (rukn) in Hajj — for ʿArafāt is in the ḥill — and so likewise in ʿUmrah. On this basis, if he goes out to the ḥill and then repeats the ṭawāf and the saʿy, it suffices him.

chapters.title_en: The Second Division of the Book on the Objectives (Maqāṣid), Containing Three Chapters — Chapter One on the Modes of Performing the Two Rites (Nusukayn), Having Three Modes
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القسم الثاني من  الكتاب في المقاصد

وفيه ثلاثة أبواب - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في وجوه أداء
النسكين وله ثلاثة أوجه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

### | الأول الإفراد

وهو أن يحرم بالحج من ميقاته أولا فإذا فرغ خرج إلى طرف الحل وأحرم
بالعمرة وكذا لو قدم العمرة في غير أشهر الحج ثم حج من الميقات فهو مفرد

### | الوجه الثاني القران

وهو أن يحرم بهما جميعا فتندرج العمرة تحت الحج ويكون حاله حال الحج
المفرد وكذا لو أحرم بالعمرة ثم أدخل الحج عليه قبل الشروع في أعمال العمرة
فإن خاض في الطواف فأدخل عليه الحج لغا إدخاله لأن أعمال العمرة من أسباب
التحلل فلا يمكن القرآن مع اختلاف الإحرام وفي إدخال العمرة على الحج قولان
أحدهما الجواز كعكسه والثاني لا لأنه لا يتغير حكم الحج بدخول العمرة عليه
بخلاف العمرة فإنها تتغير بزيادة دخول الحج فإن جوزنا ففي وقته أربعة أوجه
أحدها أنه لا يجوز ما لم يستغل بعمل ولو بطواف القدوم
والثاني أنه يجوز ما لم يشتغل بركن ولو بالسعي بعد طواف القدوم
والثالث يجوز ما لم يخرج وقت الوقوف وإن سعى من قبل لأن الحج عرفة
والرابع يجوز وإن فات وقت الوقوف ما لم يشتغل بأسباب التحلل
وعلى هذا لو كان قد سعى فالصحيح أنه لا يلزمه إعادة السعي لأنه إذا صار
قارنا حصل الاندراج وقيل لا يكتفي بالسعي السابق
ثم إذا جعلناه قارنا لم يخرجه إلى نية القران بل يكفيه إحرامه بالنسك
الثاني ويجب على القارن الآفاقي دم كما على المتمتع

### | الوجه الثالث التمتع

والمتمتع هو كل آفاقي زاحم إحرام الحج لنفسه بعمرة في أشهر الحج مع نية
التمتع فيلزمه الدم لأمرين أحدهما ربحه أحد الميقاتين إذا أحرم بالحج من
مكة من غير عود إلى الميقات والثاني زحمة الحج في أشهره بالعمرة

### | وقد اشتملت الرابطة على قيود

الأول الآفاقي فمن كان من حاضري المسجد الحرام فليس عليه دم لأن ميقاته
للحج نفس مكة
وحاضروا المسجد الحرام كل من كان بينه وبين  مكة ما دون مسافة القصر سواء
كان مستوطنا أو مسافرا حتى إن الآفاقي إذا جاوز الميقات غير مريد نسكا فلما
دخل مكة عن له أن يعتمر ثم يحج لم يلزمه الدم وإن عن له ذلك قبل دخول مكة
على أقل من مسافة القصر فأحرم بالعمرة من موضعه ثم حج في تلك السنة ففيه
وجهان أحدهما لا يلزمه كما لو كان وطنه ذلك الموضع والثاني يلزمه لأن اسم
الحاضر لا يتناوله إلا إذا كان في نفس مكة أو كان متسوطنا حواليها

### | فرع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ف-ر-د (afrada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of isolation, singularity, and being alone; al-Ifrād as a technical term denotes performing one rite exclusively without combining another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional law, Ifrād signifies the pilgrim's exclusive intention (niyyah) for Ḥajj alone, unaccompanied by ʿUmrah, reflecting the theological principle of unadulterated worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical solitude; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the legal isolation of one ritual act from another in intention.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (qarana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Joining, coupling, or conjoining two things; al-Qirān in pilgrimage law is the conjunction of Ḥajj and ʿUmrah in a single iḥrām.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, it reflects the subsumption (indirāj) of a lesser act under a greater one, akin to the way general principles encompass particulars.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal joining of physical objects; metaphorical for legal merger where the lesser rite's rulings are absorbed into the greater.
- Root: ت-م-ت-ع (tamattaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enjoyment, benefit, or taking pleasure; al-Tamattuʿ technically is performing ʿUmrah first in the Ḥajj months, then Ḥajj, with a break of iḥrām between.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The term carries a nuance of interim enjoyment — the pilgrim is released from iḥrām and enjoys lawful life before re-entering for Ḥajj.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sensory pleasure; metaphorical for the legal license of temporary release from ritual restrictions.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (law, idhā) and exceptions (illā) to delineate legal boundaries, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine when rulings apply or lapse.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second division of the book concerns the objectives (maqāṣid), and it contains three chapters. Chapter One addresses the modes of performing the two rites (nusukayn), and it has three modes.

**The First Mode: Ifrād (Isolation)**
This is that the pilgrim enters iḥrām for Ḥajj from his mīqāt (appointed station) first; when he finishes, he exits to the edge of the Ḥill (sacred precinct's outer boundary) and enters iḥrām for ʿUmrah. Likewise, if he had earlier performed ʿUmrah outside the months of Ḥajj, then performed Ḥajj from the mīqāt, he is a mufrid (one practicing Ifrād).

**The Second Mode: Qirān (Conjunction)**
This is that he enters iḥrām for both rites simultaneously, whereby the ʿUmrah becomes subsumed (tandarij) under the Ḥajj, and his state becomes that of the mufrid in Ḥajj. Likewise, if he entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah, then brought Ḥajj into it before commencing the acts of ʿUmrah — but if he had plunged into the ṭawāf (circumambulation) and then brought Ḥajj into it, his insertion is void (laghā), because the acts of ʿUmrah are among the causes of release (taḥallul), so Qirān cannot occur with differing iḥrāms. Regarding inserting ʿUmrah into Ḥajj, there are two opinions (qawlān): one permits it, as with its converse; the second forbids it, because the ruling of Ḥajj is not altered by ʿUmrah's entry into it, unlike ʿUmrah, which is altered by the addition of Ḥajj's entry. If we permit it, then concerning its timing there are four aspects (awjuh): 
- First: It is not permissible until he has engaged in some act, even the ṭawāf of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm).
- Second: It is permissible as long as he has not engaged in a pillar (rukn), even the saʿy (running) after the ṭawāf of arrival.
- Third: It is permissible as long as the time of the standing (wuqūf) at ʿArafāt has not lapsed, even if he had performed saʿy earlier, because Ḥajj is ʿArafah.
- Fourth: It is permissible even if the time of wuqūf has lapsed, as long as he has not engaged in the causes of taḥallul.
Upon this, if he had performed saʿy, the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that he is not obliged to repeat the saʿy, because when he becomes a qārin, the subsumption (indirāj) is achieved. Yet it is said that the earlier saʿy does not suffice. Then, when we deem him a qārin, he is not required to renew the intention of Qirān; rather, his iḥrām for the second rite suffices. The qārin who is an āfāqī (one coming from beyond the mīqāt) is obligated to offer a blood sacrifice (dam), just as the mutamattiʿ is.

**The Third Mode: Tamattuʿ (Enjoyment)**
The mutamattiʿ is every āfāqī who crowds the iḥrām of Ḥajj for himself with a ʿUmrah in the months of Ḥajj, with the intention of Tamattuʿ. He is obligated to offer blood for two reasons: first, his profiting from one of the two mīqāts when he enters iḥrām for Ḥajj from Mecca without returning to the mīqāt; second, the crowding of Ḥajj in its months by ʿUmrah.

**The Link (al-Rābiṭah) Comprises Restrictions (quyūd):**
**First Restriction: The Āfāqī.** Whoever is among the residents of the Sacred Mosque (ḥāḍirū al-masjid al-ḥarām) owes no blood, because his mīqāt for Ḥajj is Mecca itself. The residents of the Sacred Mosque are all those whose distance from Mecca is less than the distance permitting the shortening of prayer (masāfat al-qaṣr), whether they are settled inhabitants (mustawṭin) or travelers. Thus, even an āfāqī who passes the mīqāt without intending any rite, then upon entering Mecca it occurs to him to perform ʿUmrah and then Ḥajj — no blood is incumbent upon him. But if this occurred to him before entering Mecca, at a distance less than masāfat al-qaṣr, and he entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah from his location, then performed Ḥajj that same year, there are two aspects (wajhān): one holds that it is not incumbent upon him, just as if that location were his homeland; the second holds that it is incumbent, because the designation "resident" (ḥāḍir) does not apply to him unless he is within Mecca itself or is a settled inhabitant around it.

**A Branch (Farʿ):**

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 116: Conditions of Tamattuʿ and Its Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
لو كان له مسكنان أحدهما خارج عن مسافة القصر فحكمه حكم المسكن الذي أنشأ
الإحرام منه إلا إذا كان سكونه بأحدهما أكثر أو كان أهله بأحدهما فالعبرة
به
القيد الثاني أن يحرم بالعمرة في أشهر الحج فلو تقدمت ثم أحرم بالحج
من جوف مكة كان مفردا لا متمتعا وهل يلزمه دم الإساءة بترك ميقات الحج
فيه وجهان أحدهما لا لأنه لم يجاوز الميقات غير محرم والثاني نعم لأن مكة
ليس ميقات الحج في حق الآفاقي فعلى هذا عليه العود إلى الميقات فإن لم يفعل
لزمه الدم
فأما إذا وقع بعض العمرة في أشهر الحج فإن لم يسبق إلا الإحرام ففي كونه
متمتعا وجهان وإن سبق بعض الأفعال فوجهان مرتبان منشؤهما أن النظر إلى أول
الإحرام أو آخره
وقطع ابن سريج بأنه لو دخل شوال وهو محرم بالعمرة لم يفارق الميقات بعد
فهو متمتع
القيد الثالث أن تقع العمرة والحج في سنة واحدة فلو فرغ من العمرة فأخر
الحج إلى السنة الثانية وأحرم به من مكة فلا دم عليه إذ صارت مكة ميقاتا له
ولو عزم على الإقامة ثم حج في السنة الأولى لم يسقط دم المتمتع فإنه
بالعمرة في الميقات التزم العود إلى الميقات أو الدم
الرابع أن لا يعود إلى الميقات للحج فلو عاد إليه أو إلى مثل مسافته كان
مفردا ولو عاد إلى ميقات قرب من ذلك الميقات ففي سقوط الدم وجهان
ولو أحرم من مكة ثم  عاد إلى الميقات الأول محرما ففي سقوط الدم قولان كما
في دم الإساءة
الخامس وقوع النسكين عن شخص واحد فالأجير إذا اعتمر من الميقات لنفسه وحج
من جوف مكة لمستأجره فليس بمتمتع لأنه لم يزحم حجا واجبا بالشرع بل
بالإجارة وهذا الشرط زاده الخضرى ومن الأصحاب من خالفه وعلى مذهبه يعود
التردد في لزوم دم الإساءة كما في المتمتع إذا أحرم بالعمرة قبل شوال ودم
الإساءة يخالف دم المتمتع في صفه البدل وفي أنه يعصي ملتزمه ويجب عليه
تداركه عند الإمكان
السادس نية التمتع وفيه وجهان أحدهما تعتبر كما في الجمع بين الصلاتين
حتى لو كان عند الإحرام بالعمرة على عزم أن لا يحج في هذه السنة أو على عزم
أن يعود إلى الميقات لم يكن ناويا والثاني لا تعتبر هذه النية كما في
القران
فإن اعتبرنا النية ففي وقته وجهان أحدهما في أول إحرام العمرة
والثاني أنه يتمادى إلى آخر إحرام العمرة كما في الجمع بين الصلاتين
هذه شرائط التمتع فلو جاوز المتمتع مكة في الإحرام بالحج كان مسيئا
ومتمتعا فيلزمه دمان كما يجب دم الإساءة على المكي إذا فارق مكة ولا يكفيه
دم التمتع بل ذلك لزحمة إحرام الحج عن الميقات ودم الإساءة لمفارقة مكة في
إحرام الحج مع أنها ميقاته
فإن قيل فأي الجهات أفضل قلنا الإفراد فإنه يتعدد فيه الميقات والعمل
والقران في آخر الرتب إذ يتحد فيه الميقات والعمل والتمتع يتحد فيه الميقات
ولكن يتعدد العمل فهو بينهما وفيه قول أن التمتع أفضل من الإفراد لاشتماله
على الدم وحكي قول آخر أن القران أفضل من التمتع
ولنذكر الآن موجب القران والتمتع وهذا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - باب ما على
المتمتع والقارن في معناه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
والمتمتع إن كان موسرا فعليه إراقة دم وقت وجوبه الإحرام بالحج وله
إراقته قبل يوم النحر لأنه دم جبران
وقال أبو حنيفة يختص به لأنه دم نسك وقربان وفي جواز إراقته قبل الحج
وبعد العمرة قولان أحدهما نعم  لأنه كفارة مالية فيقدم على أحد سببيه ككفارة
اليمين والثاني لا لأن اسم اليمين متحقق قبل الحنث واسم التمتع إلى الحج لا
يتحقق إلا بعد الحج
فإن جوزنا ذلك ففي جوازه قبل التحلل عن العمرة وجهان ومنشؤه أن السبب
الأول يتم بإحرام العمرة أو بتمامها
أما العاجز فعليه صيام عشرة أيام ثلاثة في الحج وسبعة في الرجوع ويدخل
وقت الثلاث بإحرام الحج ولا يجوز قبله لأنها عبادة بدنية فلا يجوز تقديمها
والأولى أن تقدم على يوم عرفة إذ الصوم مكروه فيه وإن أخر عن النحر فأيام
التشريق لا تقبله كيوم النحر وفي القديم قوله أنه يقبل فإن تأخر عن أيام
التشريق صار قضاء ويلزمه القضاء خلافا لأبي حنيفة وحكى ابن سريج قولا يوافق
مذهب أبي حنيفة
وأما السبعة فأول وقتها بالرجوع إلى الوطن وهل يجوز في الطريق بعد التوجه
إلى الوطن فيه وجهان وللشافعي رضي الله عنه قول أن المراد بالرجوع هو
الرجوع إلى مكة وقول آخر أن المراد بالرجوع الفراغ من الحج وعلى هذا لا
يجوز في أيام التشريق وإن قلنا تقبل الأيام الثلاثة لأنه لم يفرغ بعد من
الحج
والأيام السبعة لا آخر لها فلا تصير قضاء وإن فاتت الأيام الثلاثة حتى
رجع إلى الوطن فعليه عشرة أيام
وهل يجب التفريق بين الثلاثة والسبعة فيه قولان أحدهما نعم كما في الأداء
والثاني لا كما أن قضاء رمضان لا يجب فيه الولاء وإن كان أداؤه متواليا
فإن قلنا يجب فهل يكفي يوم واحد أم يتقدر التفريق بالقدر المتخلل في
الأداء فيه وجهان
فإن قدرنا به فيبتني المقدار المتخلل على معرفة معنى الرجوع وأن أيام
التشريق هل تقبل الصوم
فإن قلنا تقبل والمراد بالرجوع الفراغ فلا يتخلل بينهما فطر فهل يجب
التفريق في القضاء بيوم فوجهان ووجه الإيجاب أن الحال قد افترق في الأداء
بوقع الثلاثة في الحج والسبعة بعدها فلا بد في القضاء أيضا من فرق بالزمان
بدلا عنه
ثم الصحيح أنه إذا صام أحد عشر يوما كفاه واليوم  الرابع لا يقع عن هذه
الجهة ووقع تطوعا وفيه وجه آخر أنه لا بد من الإفطار في اليوم الرابع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dwelling, residence, settled abode; the place where one finds repose and permanence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The established domicile that determines one's legal status regarding distance (masāfat al-qaṣr) and ritual boundaries (mīqāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical habitation; metaphorical (majāz) for legal domicile as the operative criterion in ritual law.
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Visiting, frequenting; the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) as an act of visitation to the Sacred House.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A devotional act combining circumambulation (ṭawāf) and saʿy, distinct from ḥajj in time and obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the ritual; metaphorical for the "flourishing" of a place by visitation.
- Root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enjoyment, taking pleasure; the legal term tamattuʿ denotes combining ʿumrah and ḥajj with a break (taḥallul) between them.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ritual mode where one performs ʿumrah in the months of ḥajj, then disengages (taḥallul) and re-enters iḥrām for ḥajj from Makkah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for enjoyment; metaphorical for the legal concession (rukhṣah) permitting this sequence.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Joining, coupling; qirān as the conjunction of ʿumrah and ḥajj in a single iḥrām.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The mode where both rites are performed with one iḥrām and one set of actions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical joining; metaphorical for the legal unification of two rituals.
- Root: ف-ر-د (f-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Being alone, solitary; ifrād as performing ḥajj alone without ʿumrah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The mode where ḥajj is performed independently, with its own mīqāt and actions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for singleness; metaphorical for the ritual mode of isolation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with "Law" (Law + Perfect Verb) — The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb) with a strict temporal and causal sequence; the particle "law" indicates a hypothetical or counterfactual condition, requiring careful parsing of the main clause's mood and tense.
chapters.translation:
I say: If he possesses two dwellings, one of which lies beyond the distance of shortening (masāfat al-qaṣr), then his ruling follows that of the dwelling from which he initiated the iḥrām — unless his residence in one of them is more frequent, or his family (ahl) is in one of them, in which case the criterion is that one.

The second condition: that he enter iḥrām for ʿumrah during the months of ḥajj (ashhur al-ḥajj). If he performed it earlier, then entered iḥrām for ḥajj from within Makkah, he is a mufrid (one performing ifrād), not a mutamattiʿ. Regarding whether the blood (dam) for transgression (isāʾah) is incumbent upon him for abandoning the mīqāt of ḥajj, there are two views (wajhān): one is no, because he did not pass the mīqāt without being in iḥrām; the second is yes, because Makkah is not the mīqāt for ḥajj for the one coming from afar (āfāqī). On this view, he must return to the mīqāt; if he does not, the blood becomes incumbent.

As for when part of the ʿumrah falls within the months of ḥajj: if only the iḥrām preceded, then regarding his being a mutamattiʿ there are two views. If some of the acts (afʿāl) preceded, then there are two ordered views (wajhān murattabān), whose origin is whether one considers the beginning of the iḥrām or its end.

Ibn Surayj definitively ruled that if he enters Shawwāl while in iḥrām for ʿumrah, not having left the mīqāt yet, he is a mutamattiʿ.

The third condition: that the ʿumrah and ḥajj occur in a single year. If he completes the ʿumrah and delays the ḥajj to the second year, entering iḥrām for it from Makkah, then no blood is upon him, for Makkah has become his mīqāt. If he resolves to stay (iqāmah) and then performs ḥajj in the first year, the blood of tamattuʿ is not dropped, for by performing ʿumrah at the mīqāt he obligated himself to return to the mīqāt or to the blood.

The fourth: that he not return to the mīqāt for the ḥajj. If he returns to it, or to a place of equal distance, he is a mufrid. If he returns to a mīqāt nearer than that mīqāt, then regarding the dropping of the blood there are two views. If he enters iḥrām from Makkah, then returns to the first mīqāt while in iḥrām, there are two positions (qawlān) on the dropping of the blood, as in the case of the blood of transgression (dam al-isāʾah).

The fifth: that both rites be performed for a single person. Thus, if a hired agent (ajīr) performs ʿumrah from the mīqāt for himself and performs ḥajj from within Makkah for his employer (mustaʾjir), he is not a mutamattiʿ, because he did not combine a ḥajj obligatory by sacred law (sharʿ), but rather by contract (ijārah). This condition was added by al-Khuḍarī, and some of the companions (aṣḥāb) opposed him. On his doctrine, the hesitation returns regarding the obligation of the blood of transgression, as in the case of the mutamattiʿ who enters iḥrām for ʿumrah before Shawwāl. The blood of transgression differs from the blood of tamattuʿ in the nature of the substitute (ṣifat al-badal), in that its obligator (multazim) disobeys, and in that he must make it up (tadāruk) when possible.

The sixth: the intention (niyyah) of tamattuʿ. There are two views: one holds it is considered, as in combining two prayers (jamʿ bayn al-ṣalātayn), such that if at the time of iḥrām for ʿumrah he intends not to perform ḥajj that year, or intends to return to the mīqāt, he is not intending tamattuʿ. The second holds this intention is not considered, as in qirān.

If we consider the intention, then regarding its time there are two views: one is at the beginning of the iḥrām of ʿumrah; the second is that it continues until the end of the iḥrām of ʿumrah, as in combining two prayers.

These are the conditions of tamattuʿ. If the mutamattiʿ passes beyond Makkah in his iḥrām for ḥajj, he is a wrongdoer (musīʾ) and a mutamattiʿ, so two bloods are incumbent upon him — just as the blood of transgression is incumbent upon the Meccan (makkiyy) if he departs from Makkah. The blood of tamattuʿ does not suffice him; rather, that is for the crowding of the ḥajj iḥrām away from the mīqāt, and the blood of transgression is for departing Makkah in the ḥajj iḥrām, even though it is his mīqāt.

If it is said: "Which of the modes is superior?" I say: Ifrād, for in it both the mīqāt and the actions are multiplied. Qirān is at the lowest rank, for in it the mīqāt and the actions are unified. Tamattuʿ unifies the mīqāt but multiplies the actions, so it lies between the two. There is a position that tamattuʿ is superior to ifrād, for it includes the blood. Another position is narrated that qirān is superior to tamattuʿ.

Let us now mention what necessitates qirān and tamattuʿ — and this, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the chapter on what is incumbent upon the mutamattiʿ and the qārin in its meaning — may God bless him and grant him peace.

The mutamattiʿ, if he is affluent (mūsir), must shed blood (irāqat dam) at the time of its obligation, which is the iḥrām for ḥajj. He may shed it before the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr), for it is a blood of reparation (dam jibrān).

Abū Ḥanīfah said it is specific to that time, for it is a blood of devotion (dam nusuk) and offering (qurbān). Regarding the permissibility of shedding it before the ḥajj and after the ʿumrah, there are two positions: one is yes, for it is a financial expiation (kaffārah māliyyah), so it may precede one of its two causes, like the expiation of an oath (kaffārat al-yamīn). The second is no, for the name "oath" is realized before the violation (ḥinth), whereas the name "tamattuʿ" is not realized until after the ḥajj.

If we permit that, then regarding its permissibility before the taḥallul from the ʿumrah, there are two views, whose origin is whether the first cause is completed by the iḥrām of ʿumrah or by its completion.

As for the incapable one (ʿājiz), he must fast ten days: three during the ḥajj and seven upon returning (rujūʿ). The time of the three enters with the iḥrām of ḥajj, and it is not permissible before that, for it is a bodily worship (ʿibādah badaniyyah), so it cannot be advanced. It is preferable to advance them before the Day of ʿArafah, for fasting is disliked (makrūh) on that day. If he delays them past the Day of Sacrifice, the Days of Tashrīq do not accept them, like the Day of Sacrifice itself. In the old position (qadīm), it is said they are accepted. If they are delayed past the Days of Tashrīq, they become a make-up (qaḍāʾ), and he must make them up — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. Ibn Surayj narrated a position agreeing with Abū Ḥanīfah's school.

As for the seven, their earliest time is upon returning to the homeland (waṭan). Whether they are permissible on the road after heading toward the homeland, there are two views. For al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, there is a position that "returning" (rujūʿ) means returning to Makkah, and another position that it means completion of the ḥajj. On this latter view, they are not permissible during the Days of Tashrīq, even if we say the three days are accepted, for he has not yet completed the ḥajj.

The seven days have no final limit, so they do not become a make-up. If the three days are missed until he returns to the homeland, then ten days are incumbent upon him.

Is separation (tafrīq) between the three and the seven obligatory? There are two positions: one is yes, as in performance (adāʾ); the second is no, just as the make-up of Ramaḍān does not require consecutiveness (walāʾ), even though its performance is consecutive.

If we say it is obligatory, then is one day sufficient, or is the separation measured by the intervening amount in the performance? There are two views.

If we measure it by that, then the intervening amount depends on understanding the meaning of "returning" and whether the Days of Tashrīq accept fasting.

If we say they accept it and "returning" means completion, then no breaking of the fast (fiṭr) intervenes between them. Then, is separation in the make-up by one day obligatory? There are two views. The view of obligation is that the situation differed in the performance, with the three occurring during the ḥajj and the seven after it, so in the make-up a temporal separation must substitute for it.

Then, the correct view is that if he fasts eleven days, it suffices him, and the fourth day does not count for this purpose but falls as voluntary (taṭawwuʿ). Another view holds that he must break the fast on the fourth day.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرعان

أحدهما إن وجد الهدي بعد الشروع في الصوم لم يلزمه خلافا للمزني
وإن وجد قبله وبعد إحرام الحج ابتنى على أقوال الكفارة في أن الاعتبار
بحالة الأداء أم بحالة الوجوب
الثاني إذا مات المتمتع قبل الفراغ من الحج فهل نتبين أنه لم يحصل
التمتع قولان أحدهما نعم لأن الحج لم يتم وكأنه لم يحج والثاني لا لأنه
بالشروع يحقق التمتع
ولو مات بعد الفراغ من الحج وقبل الرجوع إلى الوطن أخرج الدم من تركته
فإن كان عاجزا ومات برئت الذمة لأنه لم يتمكن في السفر فهو كما إذا دام
السفر والمرض في صوم رمضان إلى الموت وإن مات بعد التمكن في الوطن فحكم هذه
الأيام حكم أيام رمضان حتى يصوم عنه وليه أو يفدي كل يوم بمد
وذكر صاحب التقريب قولين آخرين
أحدهما أنه لا يقاس هذا على رمضان في الفدية وصوم الولي لأنه غير معقول
في نفسه فلم يرد إلا في رمضان
والثاني أنه يرجح إلى الدم إن أمكن لأن صوم رمضان ليس له أصل يرجع إليه
فعلى هذا لو بقي يوم واحد أو يومان فهو كما لو حلق شعرة واحدة أو شعرتين
وسيأتي
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في أعمال الحج - صلى الله عليه وسلم
-

### | ولنقدم عليه جملها

فالآفاقي إذا انتهى إلى الميقات يحرم ويتزيا بزي المحرمين فإذا دخل مكة
لم يعزم على شئ حتى يطوف طواف القدوم وليس هذا الطواف بركن ثم إن شاء يسعى
بعده فيقع السعي ركنا إذ ليس تأخيره عن الوقوف شرطا في كونه ركنا بخلاف
الطواف ثم يصبر إلى اليوم السابع من ذي الحجة فيخطب بهم الإمام ويوصيهم
بالبكور يوم التروية إلى مني وبالنهوض إلى عرفة فيمتدون يوم التروية إلى
مني ويبيتون ليلة عرفة بها وذلك مبيت منزل وعادة لا مبيت نسك ثم يصبحون يوم
عرفة متوجهين إليها فيوافونها قبل الزوال ويشتغلون  بالدعاء ويقبضون منها
عند الغروب إلى مزدلفة ويصلون المغرب مع العشاء ويبيتون بها وهذا المبيت
نسك ثم يصلون الصبح يوم النحر مغلسين ويتوجهون إلى منى وعلى طريقهم المشعر
الحرام فإذا انتهوا إليه وقفوا إلى الإسفار ثم يجاوزونه إلى وادي محسر
فيسرعون فيها عدوا وركضا ثم يوافون منى عند طلوع الشمس ويرمون
ويحلقون ويذبحون ثم يقبضون إلى مكة ويطوفون طواف الركن ويسمى طواف
الإفاضة والزيارة ثم ينطلقون إلى منى للمبيت والرمي في أيام التشريق فإذا
فرغوا عادوا إلى مكة وطافوا طواف الوداع وانصرفوا
وفي الحج أربع خطب يوم السابع من ذي الحجة ويوم عرفة ويوم النحر ويوم
النفر الأول وكل ذلك بعد صلاة الظهر وإفراد إلا يوم عرفة فإنه يخطب خطبتين
بعد الزوال وقبل الظهر
هذه جملها أما التفصيل ففيه اثنا عشر فصلا

### | الفصل الأول في الإحرام

وهو عندنا مجرد النية من غير حاجة إلى تلبية خلافا لأبي حنيفة وحكي قول
قديم مثل مذهبه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ج-د (w-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Finding, encountering, or possessing something after prior absence; also wealth or capacity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Existence or availability of an object at a given moment, contrasted with its non-existence; in legal context, the actual presence of the sacrificial animal (hady).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "finding" as physical attainment; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "capacity" or "means" (wujdah).
- Root: ت-م-ع (t-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enjoyment, gratification, or taking benefit; in pilgrimage context, the mutʿah (tamattuʿ) — performing ʿumrah then hajj with a break.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal status of tamattuʿ as a composite ritual act whose completion depends on finishing both components; its "realization" (taḥqīq) is tied to the full performance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of enjoyment; technical legal sense as a named pilgrimage mode, where the metaphor of "enjoyment" (interim release from iḥrām) becomes a fixed juristic term.
- Root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, defect; but in legal usage, dhimmah — the "covenant" or "liability" of the person, i.e., the moral-legal account.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The abstract entity of obligation residing in the person; "acquittal" (barāʾah) of the dhimmah means the discharge of liability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "blame" vs. metaphorical "protected covenant" — the shift from moral censure to legal responsibility.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To judge, decree, or fulfill; also to complete or finish a duty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, qaḍāʾ — making up a missed obligation after its time, as opposed to adāʾ (performance in time).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "cutting off" or "deciding"; metaphorical extension to "fulfilling a debt" or "compensating a missed act."
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs "if... then" (in... fa-) structures and "except" (khilāfan) to mark legal disagreement; the protasis sets a hypothetical case, the apodosis states the ruling, and the exceptive clause isolates the opposing view.
chapters.translation:
I say: There are two subsidiary branches.

The first: If the sacrificial animal (hady) is found after one has already commenced the fast [of tamattuʿ], it is not incumbent upon him [to switch to the animal] — contrary to al-Muzanī. But if it is found before [commencing the fast] and after the iḥrām of the hajj, then [the ruling] is built upon the divergent opinions concerning expiation (kaffārah) — namely, whether consideration is given to the state of performance (adāʾ) or the state of obligation (wujūb).

The second: If one performing tamattuʿ dies before completing the hajj, are we to ascertain that tamattuʿ was not actually realized? There are two opinions. One: Yes — because the hajj was not completed, and it is as though he never performed the hajj. The second: No — because by commencing [the hajj], tamattuʿ is actualized.

And if he dies after completing the hajj but before returning to his homeland, the blood [offering] is paid from his estate. If he was incapable [of fasting] and then died, his liability (dhimmah) is acquitted — because he was not able [to fast] while traveling, just as when travel and illness persist in the fast of Ramaḍān until death. But if he dies after having the capacity [to fast] in his homeland, then the ruling for these days is the ruling for the days of Ramaḍān — such that his guardian fasts on his behalf, or he feeds [the poor] for each day one mudd [of grain].

The author of al-Taqrīb mentioned two other opinions:
One: This [case] is not analogized to Ramaḍān regarding the redemption (fidyah) and the guardian's fasting — because [the obligation] is not rationally intelligible in itself, and it was only transmitted [as a ruling] for Ramaḍān.
The second: One reverts to the blood [offering] if possible — because the fast of Ramaḍān has no [alternative] origin to which one may return. On this basis, if only one day or two days remain, it is like shaving one hair or two hairs. And this will come later.

— Peace be upon him — The Second Book: On the Rites of the Hajj — Peace be upon him —

Let us preface it with its comprehensive sketch.

Thus, the person from the distant horizons (āfāqī), when he reaches the mīqāt, enters iḥrām and attires himself in the garb of the muḥrimūn. When he enters Mecca, he does not resolve upon anything until he performs the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm). This circumambulation is not a pillar (rukn). Then, if he wishes, he performs the saʿy after it — and in that case the saʿy becomes a pillar, since delaying it until after the standing at ʿArafāt is not a condition for its being a pillar, unlike the circumambulation. Then he waits until the seventh day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, when the imam delivers a sermon to them and instructs them to set out early on the day of Tarwiyah to Minā, and to proceed to ʿArafāt. So they extend [their stay] on the day of Tarwiyah to Minā, and they spend the night of ʿArafah there — and this overnight stay is a matter of lodging and custom, not a ritual overnight stay (mabīt nusuk). Then on the morning of the day of ʿArafah, they set out toward it, arriving before noon, and they occupy themselves with supplication. They depart from it at sunset to Muzdalifah, where they pray the sunset (maghrib) prayer together with the night (ʿishāʾ) prayer, and they spend the night there — and this overnight stay is a ritual act (nusuk). Then they pray the dawn (ṣubḥ) prayer on the day of sacrifice (al-naḥr) in the early darkness, and they proceed to Minā. On their path is al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām; when they reach it, they stand there until the morning light spreads. Then they pass beyond it to the valley of Muḥassir, where they hasten in walking and running. Then they arrive at Minā at sunrise, and they cast the stones (ramy), shave [their heads], and slaughter [the offerings]. Then they depart to Mecca and perform the circumambulation of the pillar — called the circumambulation of ifāḍah and of visitation (ziyārah). Then they return to Minā for the overnight stays and the casting of stones during the days of al-Tashrīq. When they finish, they return to Mecca, perform the circumambulation of farewell (ṭawāf al-wadāʿ), and depart.

In the hajj there are four sermons: on the seventh day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, on the day of ʿArafah, on the day of sacrifice, and on the day of the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal). All of these are after the noon prayer (ẓuhr) and are single [sermons] — except the day of ʿArafah, for on it he delivers two sermons after the sun's decline (zawāl) and before the noon prayer.

This is its comprehensive sketch. As for the detailed exposition, it comprises twelve chapters.

### The First Chapter: On the Iḥrām

It is, in our view, the mere intention (niyyah) without any need for the talbiyah — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. And an old opinion has been related [from our school] resembling his doctrine.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | ثم النية لها ثلاثة أوجه

الأول التفصيل فإذا نوى حجا أو عمرة أو قرانا قضاء كان أو نذرا أو تطوعا
كان كما نوى إلا إذا غير الترتيب بتأخير فرض الإسلام أو تأخير الفرض عن
النفل
ولو أهل بحجتين أو عمرتين معا أو متلاحقا لغا أحدهما ولم تلزمه الزيادة
على الواحد وقال أبو حنيفة ينعقدان ثم ينتقل أحدهما عند الاشتغال بالعمل
إلى الذمة
الوجه الثاني الإطلاق فإذا نوى إحراما مطلقا مهما شاء جعله حجا أو عمرة
أو قرانا ولا يتعين بمجرد الاشتغال بالطواف للعمرة ولا بالوقوف للحج بل لا
بد من نية الصرف خلافا لأبي حنيفة
ولو أحرم مطلقا قبل الأشهر ثم عين للحج بعد الأشهر لم يجز على المذهب
ولو أحرم بالعمرة قبل الأشهر ثم أدخل الحج عليها بعد الأشهر للقران
فوجهان ووجه المنع أن الإحرام للقران كالمتحد فلا ينبغي أن يقدم على الأشهر
الوجه الثالث الإبهام فإذا قال أهللت بإهلال كإهلال زيد صح إذا أهل علي
بإهلال كإهلال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ثم إن  لم يكن زيد محرما انعقد له إحرام مطلق وإن عرف أنه ليس محرما بأن
كان ميتا ففي انعقاد أصل الإحرام وجهان وجه الانعقاد إلغاء الإضافة وإبقاء
الأصل
وقد نص في الأم على أنه لو أحرم عن مستأجرين تعارضا وتساقطا وانعقد عن
الأجير ولو أحرم عن نفسه وعن المستأجر فكذلك إذ بطل التفصيل وبقي أصل
الإحرام
أما إذا كان زيد محرما فله ثلاثة أحوال
إحداها أن يكون إحرامه مفصلا فينزل إحرام المعلق عليه قرانا كان أو
إفرادا
الثانية أن يكون إحرام زيد مطلقا فإحرام المعلق أيضا مطلق وإليه الخيرة
في التعيين ولا يلزمه اتباع زيد فيما يستأنفه من التعيين فأما ما فصله قبل
تعيينه ففي لزومه وجهان ينظر في أحدهما إلى أول الإحرام وكان مطلقا وفي
الثاني إلى الحالة الموجودة عند التعليق وكان مفصلا وكذا إذا كان أحرم أولا
بعمرة ثم أدخل الحج عليه
الثالثة أن يصادف زيدا ميتا بعد الإحرام وتعذر مراجعته فهم كما لو نسي
الرجل ما أحرم به وكان قد أحرم مفصلا وفيه قولان
القديم أن يجتهد ويأخذ بغالب الظن كما في القبلة إن كان له ظن غالب
والجديد الصحيح أنه يلزمه البناء على اليقين وطريقه أن يجعل نفسه قارنا
فإذا فرغ من الحج برئت ذمته من الحج بيقين لأنه إن كان معتمرا أولا فقد
أدخل الحج عليه وتبرأ ذمته عن العمرة أيضا بيقين إلا إذا منعنا إدخال
العمرة على الحج فيحتمل أن يكون إحرامه أولا بالحج
وقال أبو إسحاق إنه يبرأ عن العمرة ويكون هذا عذرا في جواز إدخال العمرة
في الحج كما أن التردد في النية عند نسيان صلاة من الصلوات الخمس عذر في
إجزاء الصلاة فإن قلنا تبرأ عن العمرة لزمه دم القران وإلا فلا يلزمه لأن
القران مشكوك فيه فأما إذا طاف أولا ثم شك فيمنع إدخال الحج لو كان معتمرا
في علم الله فلا يكفيه القران بل طريقه أن يسعي ويحلق ويبتدأ إحراما بالحج
من جوف مكة ويتممه فتبرأ ذمته عن الحج بيقين  لأنه إن كان حاجا فغايته حلق
في غير أوانه وفيه دم وإن كان معتمرا فقد تحلل بالحلق والسعي وأنشأ بعده
حجا فصار متمتعا وفيه دم ولا تبرأ ذمته عن العمرة لاحتمال أن الأول كان حجا
والدم لا بد منه ولكنه لا يدري أهو دم حلق أم دم تمتع وتعيين جهة الكفارات
في النية ليس شرطا فلا يضر التردد نعم لو كان معسرا فبدل الفدية ثلاثة أيام
وبدل التمتع عشرة أيام فإن أتى بالثلاث فهل تبرأ ذمته فيه وجهان
أحدهما نعم لأن الزائد غير مستيقن فلا يوجبه
والثاني لا لأن شغل الذمة بالصوم مستيقن والبراءة بهذا القدر غير مستيقن
ومن أصحابنا من قال الحلق لا نأمره به لاحتمال أنه حاج والحلق في غير
أوانه محرم إلا بأذى من نفس الشعر والأذى هاهنا من النسيان نعم لو بادر
فحلق كان حكمه ما ذكرناه والأظهر أنه يؤمر به لأن هذا الضرر أعظم من أذى
الشعر إذ يؤدى إلى فوات الحج لو لم يفعل ذلك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-و-ي (N-W-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "purpose, resolve, or aim" — the heart's determination toward an act, distinct from mere volition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, niyyah is the discriminating intent that renders an act of worship (ʿibādah) valid and distinguishes its specific type (taʿyīn) from generic devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes inward resolve; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the verbal formula (ṣīghah) of talbiyah as its outward proxy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Dependency (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — the apodosis (jawāb) of "if" clauses (e.g., "if he intended...") is governed by the protasis, requiring careful parsing of nested conditions and exceptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: Then intention (niyyah) has three aspects.

**The First Aspect: Specification (al-Tafṣīl)** — If one intends ḥajj, ʿumrah, or qirān (combined pilgrimage), whether as a make-up (qaḍāʾ), a vow (nadhr), or a supererogatory act (taṭawwuʿ), it is as he intended — except if he alters the order by delaying the obligatory Islam (farḍ al-Islām) or delaying the obligatory (farḍ) after the supererogatory (nafl). If one raises the talbiyah for two ḥajjs or two ʿumrahs simultaneously or consecutively, one of them is void (laghā), and the excess beyond one is not binding upon him. Abū Ḥanīfah said: Both are contracted, then one of them transfers to the liability (dhimmah) upon commencing the rites.

**The Second Aspect: Absoluteness (al-Iṭlāq)** — If one intends an absolute iḥrām, he may make it ḥajj, ʿumrah, or qirān whenever he wishes. It is not determined merely by commencing the circumambulation (ṭawāf) for ʿumrah, nor by standing at ʿArafāt (wuqūf) for ḥajj; rather, an intention of conversion (ṣarf) is indispensable — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah. If one enters iḥrām absolutely before the [pilgrimage] months, then specifies it for ḥajj after the months, it is not permissible according to the [authoritative] school (al-madhhab). If one enters iḥrām for ʿumrah before the months, then inserts ḥajj upon it after the months for qirān, there are two positions (wajhān). The position of prohibition holds that the iḥrām for qirān is as if unified (muttaḥid), so it should not precede the months.

**The Third Aspect: Ambiguity (al-Ibhām)** — If one says: "I raise the talbiyah with an iḥrām like the iḥrām of Zayd," it is valid — just as ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) raised the talbiyah with an iḥrām like the iḥrām of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) {«لَبَّيْكَ بِحَجَّةٍ كَحَجَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ»}. Then, if Zayd was not in iḥrām, an absolute iḥrām is contracted for him. If it is known that he was not in iḥrām — e.g., he was dead — then regarding the contraction of the iḥrām's foundation (aṣl), there are two positions. The position of contraction holds that the annexation (iḍāfah) is nullified while the foundation is preserved. Al-Shāfiʿī has stated in *al-Umm* that if one entered iḥrām on behalf of two employers (mustaʾjirān) whose claims conflicted and were both dropped, it is contracted on behalf of the hired agent (ajīr). Likewise, if one entered iḥrām for himself and for the employer, the specification (tafṣīl) is voided while the foundation of iḥrām remains.

However, if Zayd was in iḥrām, then he has three states:

**First State:** Zayd's iḥrām was specified (mufaṣṣal) — then the iḥrām of the one who suspended [his own upon Zayd's] is likewise rendered as qirān or ifrād (single ḥajj).

**Second State:** Zayd's iḥrām was absolute — then the suspended iḥrām is also absolute, and the choice of specification (taʿyīn) remains with him. He is not bound to follow Zayd in what Zayd subsequently specifies. As for what Zayd specified before his own determination, there are two positions on its binding force: one looks to the beginning of the iḥrām, which was absolute; the second looks to the state existing at the time of suspension, which was specified. The same applies if Zayd first entered iḥrām for ʿumrah, then inserted ḥajj upon it.

**Third State:** Zayd is found dead after his iḥrām, and consulting him is impossible — this is like a man who forgets what he entered iḥrām for, having entered it in a specified manner. There are two rulings (qawlān) on this:

The **old ruling (al-qadīm)**: He must exert his judgment (ijtihād) and act upon the predominant conjecture (ghālib al-ẓann), as in the case of the qiblah, if he has a predominant conjecture.

The **new, correct ruling (al-jadīd al-ṣaḥīḥ)**: He must build upon certainty (yaqīn). His method is to make himself a qārin (one performing qirān). When he completes the ḥajj, his liability (dhimmah) is discharged from ḥajj with certainty — for if he was first a muʿtamir (performer of ʿumrah), he has inserted ḥajj upon it, and his liability is also discharged from ʿumrah with certainty — unless we prohibit inserting ʿumrah upon ḥajj, in which case it is possible that his iḥrām was first for ḥajj. Abū Isḥāq said: He is discharged from ʿumrah, and this [forgetfulness] is a valid excuse (ʿudhr) for permitting the insertion of ʿumrah into ḥajj — just as uncertainty in intention when forgetting one of the five daily prayers is an excuse for the sufficiency of the prayer [performed]. If we say he is discharged from ʿumrah, then the blood [sacrifice] of qirān (dam al-qirān) is obligatory upon him; otherwise, it is not obligatory, because the qirān is doubtful.

As for the case where he first performed ṭawāf, then doubted [his intention]: inserting ḥajj is prevented if he was a muʿtamir in God's knowledge — so qirān does not suffice him. Rather, his method is to perform the saʿy (running between Ṣafā and Marwah), shave [his head], and initiate a new iḥrām for ḥajj from within Mecca, then complete it. His liability is then discharged from ḥajj with certainty — for if he was a ḥājj (pilgrim performing ḥajj), the worst is that he shaved outside its proper time, which entails a blood [sacrifice]; and if he was a muʿtamir, he has exited iḥrām by shaving and saʿy, then initiated ḥajj afterward, becoming a mutamattiʿ (one performing tamattuʿ), which also entails a blood [sacrifice]. His liability is not discharged from ʿumrah, due to the possibility that the first [act] was ḥajj. The blood [sacrifice] is unavoidable, but he does not know whether it is the blood of shaving (dam al-ḥalq) or the blood of tamattuʿ (dam al-tamattuʿ). Specifying the category of expiations (taʿyīn jihāt al-kaffārāt) in intention is not a condition, so the uncertainty does not harm.

Yes, if he was in financial hardship (muʿsir), the substitute for the redemption (fidyah) is three days [of fasting], and the substitute for tamattuʿ is ten days. If he fasts the three, are his liability discharged? There are two positions: One says yes, because the excess is not certain, so it is not obligatory. The second says no, because the liability for fasting is certain, while discharge by this amount is not certain. Among our companions, some said: We do not order him to shave, due to the possibility that he is a ḥājj, and shaving outside its proper time is prohibited unless due to harm from the hair itself — and the harm here arises from forgetfulness. Yes, if he hastened and shaved, his ruling is as we mentioned. The more apparent [position] is that he is ordered to shave, because this harm is greater than the harm of the hair, since it leads to the loss of the ḥajj if he does not do so.
