chapters.arabic_text:
### | الصنف الأول الزوج الزوجة

وللزوج النصف وللزوجة الربع إذ لم يكن للميت ولد وارث ولا ولد ابن وارث
فإن كان فللزوج الربع وللزوجة الثمن
وإن اجتمعت نسوة فلهن الثمن أو الربع يشركن فيه ولا يزيد بزيادة العدد

### | الصنف الثاني الأم والجدة

وللأم الثلث  إلا في أربع مسائل
إحداها زوج وأبوان
والثانية زوجة وأبوان
فلها في المسألتين ثلث ما يبقى بعد نصيب الزوج والزوجة
الثالثة إذا كان للميت ولد وارث أو ولد ابن وارث فإنه يرد الأم من الثلث
إلى السدس
الرابعة إذا كان للميت اثنان من الإخوة أو الأخوات فصاعدا فلها السدس
وأما الجدة فلها السدس أبدا
وإن اشتركت جماعة في درجة اشتركن في السدس وإن كانت واحدة جدة من جهتين
لم يزد نصيبها
والجدة الوارثة هى التى تدلي بوارث وهل كل جدة تدلي بمحض الذكور كأم أب
الأب أو بمحض الإناث كأم أم الأم أو بمحض الإناث إلى محض الذكور كأم أم أب
الأب
فأما إذا أدلت بذكر بين أنثيين فلا ترث لأن الذى تدلي به هو أب أم أو أب
جدة وهو من ذوي الأرحام
وقال مالك رحمه الله كل جدة تدلي بذكر فهي لا ترث إلا أم الأب وأمهاتها
من قبل الأم فأما من تدلي بذكر آخر سوى الأب فلا ترث
وهو قول للشافعي رضي الله عنه والصحيح هو الأول

### | الصنف الثالث الأب والجد

أما الأب فيرث بالفرضية المحضة السدس إن كان الميت ابن أو ابن ابن وتكون
العصوبة للابن
ويرث بالتعصيب المحض إذا لم يكن للميت إلا زوج أو زوجة أو لم يكن وارث
أصلا
ويجمع بين الفرض والتعصيب إن كان للميت بنت أو بنت ابن فله السدس وللبنت
أو بنت الابن نصيبها وما فضل يصرف إلى الأب بالعصوبة
والجد عند عدم الأب يقوم مقام الأب إلا في أربع مسائل
الأولى زوج وأبوان
والثانية زوجة وأبوان
للأم في الصورتين ثلث ما يبقى فإن كان بدله جد فللأم الثلث كاملا
الثالثة الأب يحجب الإخوة والجد لا يحجب إلا الأخ للأم ويقاسم الباقين
الرابعة الأب يحجب أم نفسه والجد أيضا يحجب أم نفسه ولكن لا يحجب أم الأب
لأنها زوجته وهذا أوضح

### | الصنف الرابع الأولاد

فإن تمحض أولاد الصلب فالذكر الواحد يستغرق المال بالعصوبة
وإن كان فيهم ذكور وإناث فالمال بينهم  للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
وإن كان بنت واحدة فلها النصف وإن كانتا اثنتين فصاعدا فلها الثلثان لا
يزيد بزيادة عددهن
وأما أولاد الابن فإن تمحضوا فحكمهم حكم أولاد الصلب إذا تمحضوا
فأما إذا اجتمع البطنان نظر فإن كان في أولاد الصلب ذكر فقد حجب من تحته
واستغرق وإن لم يكن نظر فإن لم يكن إلا بنت واحدة فلها النصف
ثم ينظر في أولاد الابن فإن كان فيهم ذكر فالباقي لهم للذكر مثل حظ
الأنثيين وإن لم يكن ذكر فللواحدة منهم وللعدد السدس تكملة للثلثين فإن
الثلثين فرض البنات وقد بقي منه السدس
أما إذا كان في أولاد الصلب بنتان فلهما الثلثان
ثم ينظر في أولاد الابن فإن كان فيهم ذكر فباقي المال بينهم للذكر مثل حظ
الأنثيين
وإن لم يكن ذكر فيهن ولا أسفل منهن فلا شئ لهن إذ لم يبق من نصيب البنات
شئ فقد استغرق بنات الصلب جميع الثلثين
فإن كان أسفل منهما ابن ابن ابن وإن بعد يعصبها ويكون المال بينهم للذكر
مثل حظ الأنثيين مثاله
بنت وبنت ابن وبنت ابن ابن
لبنت الصلب النصف ولبنت الابن السدس تكملة الثلثين ولا شئ لبنت ابن الابن
إلا أن يكون معها أو أسفل منها ذكر يعصبها
بنتان من الصلب وبنت ابن
لبنتين الثلثان ولا شئ لبنت الابن
بنت وبنت ابن وابن ابن ابن
للبنت من الصلب النصف ولبنت الابن السدس تكملة الثلثين والباقي لابن ابن
الابن ولا يعصبها هاهنا لأنها أخذت تكملة الثلثين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pairing or coupling; a spouse as one of a matched pair in marital union.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The marital bond as a divinely ordained pairing (Quranic {«وَخَلَقَكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا»}), entailing fixed inheritance shares.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the spouse; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to "kinds" (aṣnāf) of heirs.
- Root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Veiling or screening; preventing access.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for exclusion from inheritance (ḥajb), whether partial (nuqṣān) or total (ḥirmān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal veiling of sight; metaphorical for legal barring of an heir.
- Root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wrapping or binding tightly; a nerve or sinew.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ʿaṣabah — agnatic heirs who take the residual estate (taʿṣīb) after fixed shares.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal binding; metaphorical for the heir who "binds" the estate by taking the remainder.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The repeated "if... then" (fa-in kāna... fa-) structures govern the legal outcomes, with the protasis stating the factual condition and the apodosis the resulting share.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first category [of heirs with fixed shares] is the spouse.

The husband takes one-half and the wife one-quarter, provided the deceased has no inheriting child nor inheriting child of a son. If such exists, then the husband takes one-quarter and the wife one-eighth. If multiple wives are gathered, they share the one-eighth or one-quarter jointly, and their portion does not increase with the increase in their number.

The second category is the mother and the grandmother.

The mother takes one-third, except in four cases. The first: a husband and both parents [survive]. The second: a wife and both parents [survive]. In these two cases, she takes one-third of what remains after the share of the husband or wife. The third: if the deceased has an inheriting child or an inheriting child of a son, then the mother is reduced from one-third to one-sixth. The fourth: if the deceased has two or more brothers or sisters, then she takes one-sixth.

As for the grandmother, she takes one-sixth always. If a group shares the same degree [of relation], they share the one-sixth jointly. Even if one [woman] is a grandmother from two lines, her portion does not increase. The inheriting grandmother is the one who traces [her lineage] through an inheritor. [This includes] every grandmother who traces through purely male lines, such as the mother of the father's father; or through purely female lines, such as the mother of the mother's mother; or through purely female lines to purely male lines, such as the mother of the mother of the father's father.

As for one who traces through a male between two females, she does not inherit, because the one through whom she traces is the father of a mother or the father of a grandmother, and he is among the dhawi l-arḥām (distant kindred). Mālik — may God have mercy on him — said: Every grandmother who traces through a male does not inherit, except the mother of the father and her mothers from the mother's side. As for one who traces through a male other than the father, she does not inherit. This is also a view of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — but the correct [view] is the first.

The third category is the father and the grandfather.

As for the father, he inherits by pure fixed share (farḍ) — one-sixth — if the deceased is a son or a son's son, and the residual (ʿaṣabah) goes to the son. He inherits by pure agnation (taʿṣīb) if the deceased has only a husband or a wife, or has no heir at all. He combines the fixed share and agnation if the deceased has a daughter or a son's daughter: he takes one-sixth, the daughter or son's daughter takes her share, and whatever remains is given to the father by agnation.

The grandfather, when the father is absent, stands in the father's place, except in four cases. The first: a husband and both parents. The second: a wife and both parents. In these two scenarios, the mother takes one-third of what remains; but if a grandfather takes the father's place, the mother takes the full one-third. The third: the father excludes the brothers [from inheritance], whereas the grandfather excludes only the uterine brother and shares [the estate] with the remaining [brothers]. The fourth: the father excludes his own mother [from inheritance], and the grandfather also excludes his own mother, but he does not exclude the father's mother, because she is his wife. This is the clearest [of the four].

The fourth category is the children.

If the children of the loins (awlād al-ṣulb) are purely [male], then a single male takes the entire estate by agnation. If among them are males and females, the estate is divided among them: the male takes the share of two females. If there is one daughter, she takes one-half; if there are two or more, they take two-thirds, which does not increase with the increase in their number.

As for the children of the son, if they are purely [male], their ruling is the ruling of the children of the loins when purely [male]. But when the two levels are combined, we examine [the case]. If among the children of the loins there is a male, he excludes those below him and takes the entire [estate]. If there is none, we examine further. If there is only one daughter, she takes one-half. Then we examine the children of the son: if among them there is a male, the remainder goes to them — the male takes the share of two females. If there is no male, then one [daughter of the son] takes one-sixth, and a number [of them] take one-sixth, completing the two-thirds — for two-thirds is the fixed share of the daughters, and one-sixth of it remains.

But if among the children of the loins there are two daughters, they take the two-thirds. Then we examine the children of the son: if among them there is a male, the remainder of the estate is divided among them — the male takes the share of two females. If there is no male among them, nor below them, then they get nothing, for nothing remains of the daughters' share — the daughters of the loins have taken the entire two-thirds.

If below them there is a son of a son's son, however distant, he agnates them (yuʿaṣṣibuhā), and the estate is divided between them — the male takes the share of two females. Its example: a daughter, a son's daughter, and a son's son's daughter. The daughter of the loins takes one-half, the son's daughter takes one-sixth completing the two-thirds, and the son's son's daughter gets nothing — unless there is with her or below her a male who agnates her. [Another example:] two daughters of the loins and a son's daughter: the two daughters take the two-thirds, and the son's daughter gets nothing. [Another example:] a daughter, a son's daughter, and a son's son's son: the daughter of the loins takes one-half, the son's daughter takes one-sixth completing the two-thirds, and the remainder goes to the son's son's son — and he does not agnate her here, because she has taken the completion of the two-thirds.

chapters.title_en: The Fifth Class: Brothers and Sisters
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الصنف الخامس الإخوة والأخوات

أما الإخوة من الأم
فللواحد منهم السدس وللاثنين فصاعدا الثلث لا يزيد حقهم بزيادة العدد
ويتساوى ذكرهم وأنثاهم في قدر الاستحقاق أما الإخوة من الأب والأم
فحكمهم عند الانفراد كحكم أولاد الصلب من غير فرق وأما الأخوة من الأب
فحكمهم أيضا عند الانفراد كحكم الإخوة من الأب والأم من غير فرق إلا في
مسالة المشركة
فإن اجتمع إخوة الأب والأم وإخوة الأب فحكمهم حكم أولاد الصلب وأولاد
الابن إذا اجتمعوا فالأخ من  الأب والأم يسقط أولاد الأب وللأخت الواحدة من
الأب والأم والنصف وللأخت من الأب معها السدس تكملة الثلثين وكذلك إن كن
جمعا فلهن السدس تكملة الثلثين
فإن كان في المسألة أختان من الأب والأم فلهما الثلثان وقد استغرقتا فلا
شئ لأخوات الأب إلا إذا كان في درجتها ذكر يعصبها فيكون الباقي بينهم للذكر
مثل حظ الأنثيين
ولا يعصبها من هو أسفل منها كأولاد الابن وفي هذا تخالف أولاد الابن فإن
بنت الابن يعصبها من هو أسفل منها
فرع ثلاث أخوات متفرقات
للأخت من الأب والأم النصف وللأخت للأب السدس تكملة الثلثين وللأخت للأم
السدس فرضا
ولو كان في المسألة أختان للأب والأم بدل أخت واحدة فلها الثلثان ولا شئ
للأخت للأب إذ لم يبق تكملة الثلثين وللأخت للأم السدس فإن ذلك فرض مستقل
في حقها
فإن قيل وما مسألة المشركة التى فيها يفارق إخوة الأب إخوة الأب والأم
قلنا صورتها زوج وأم وأخوان لأم وأخوان لأم وأب
فللزوج النصف وللأم السدس ولإخوة الأم الثلث فلا يبقى مال
فالإخوة من جهة الأب والأم يشاركون أولاد الأم في نصيبهم ولو كان بدلهم
إخوة للأب لسقطوا
ووقعت المسألة في زمان عمر رضي الله عنه وأرضاه فأسقط إخوة الأب والأم
فقال أخ الأب والأم هب أن أبانا كان حمارا ألسنا من أم واحدة فشرك عمر رضي
الله عنه بينهم وإليه ذهب زيد وعثمان رضي الله عنهما
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يسقطون لأنهم عصبة كأولاد الأب ثم للتشريك
شرطان
أحدهما أن يكونوا أولاد الأب والأم ليقع التشريك بقرابة الأم فإن كانوا
أولاد الأب فلا تشريك
والثاني أن يكون ولد الأم زائدا على واحد فإنه إن كان واحدا فله السدس
ويبقي سدس العصبة فلا حاجة إلى التشريك
هذا حكم الإخوة أما أولادهم
فالإناث منهم لا يرثون والذكور منهم بمنزلتهم إلا في خمس مسائل
الأولى أن ولد إخوة الأم لا يرثون فليسوا بمنزلتهم
والثانية أن اثنين من الإخوة يحجبان الأم من الثلث إلى السدس ولو كان
بدلهم أولادهم لا يحجبون
الثالثة في مسألة الشركة لو كان بدل إخوة الأب والأم أولادهم فلا تشريك
في حقهم
الرابعة الجد لا يحجب الإخوة ويحجب بني الإخوة
الخامسة الأخ يعصب أخته وابن الأخ لا يعصب أخته إذ لا ميراث لأخته أحولا

chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-خ (akh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "one sharing lineage or suckling"; plural forms (ikhwa/ikhwān) denote siblingship in inheritance contexts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In farāʾiḍ (inheritance law), the term distinguishes uterine (li-umm), full (li-ab wa-umm), and consanguine (li-ab) siblings, each with distinct Quranic allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes blood relation; metaphorical extension applies to "sharing" (mushāraka) in the problematic case, where kinship via the mother is treated as a cause for equalization.
- Root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Literally "to veil" or "to screen"; in inheritance, it means to prevent or reduce a share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for exclusion (ḥajb) — either total (ḥirmān) or partial (nuqṣān) — applied to heirs based on proximity and class.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal veiling vs. legal exclusion; here, the grandfather's veiling of siblings' children is a legal metaphor for priority in succession.
- Root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning "to bind" or "to wrap"; in inheritance, ʿaṣabah refers to agnatic heirs who take the residual estate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ʿaṣabah principle — male agnates absorb the remainder after fixed shares (furūḍ), with the male taking double the female's portion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal binding (e.g., a bandage) vs. legal "binding" of inheritance to agnatic males; the consanguine brother's ʿaṣabah is nullified by the full brother's presence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (fa-in, law) and exceptions (illā) to delineate inheritance scenarios, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine shares.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fifth class comprises brothers and sisters.

As for uterine brothers (from the mother alone): each single one receives one-sixth, and two or more receive one-third. Their entitlement does not increase with the increase in their number, and their males and females are equal in the amount of entitlement. As for full brothers (from both father and mother): their ruling when alone is exactly like the ruling of the children of the loins (awlād al-ṣulb), with no difference whatsoever. As for consanguine brothers (from the father alone): their ruling when alone is also exactly like the ruling of full brothers, with no difference except in the case of the "shared" (musharrika) problem.

If full brothers and consanguine brothers are gathered together, their ruling is like the ruling of the children of the loins and the children of the son when they are gathered: the full brother causes the consanguine brothers to fall (i.e., excludes them). For a single full sister, there is one-half; and for a consanguine sister with her, there is one-sixth, completing the two-thirds. Likewise, if they are multiple (i.e., several consanguine sisters), they receive one-sixth, completing the two-thirds.

If in the case there are two full sisters, they receive the two-thirds, and they have exhausted the estate; thus, nothing remains for the consanguine sisters — unless there is a male at their own level (i.e., a consanguine brother) who agnatizes them (yuʿaṣṣibuhā). In that case, the remainder is divided between them, with the male receiving the share of two females.

However, a male who is lower than them (in generation) does not agnatize them, such as the children of the son. In this, they differ from the children of the son, for the daughter of the son is agnatized by one who is lower than her (i.e., the son of the son).

Branch: Three sisters of different categories:
For the full sister, one-half; for the consanguine sister, one-sixth, completing the two-thirds; and for the uterine sister, one-sixth as a fixed share (fard).

If in the case there were two full sisters instead of one, they receive the two-thirds, and nothing remains for the consanguine sister, since no completion of the two-thirds is left; but the uterine sister receives one-sixth, for that is an independent fixed share in her right.

If it is asked: "What is the 'shared' problem (masʾalat al-musharrika) in which consanguine brothers differ from full brothers?" — I say: Its form is: a husband, a mother, two uterine brothers, and two full brothers. The husband receives one-half, the mother one-sixth, and the uterine brothers one-third; thus, no property remains. So the full brothers share with the uterine brothers in their portion. Had consanguine brothers been in their place, they would have fallen (i.e., been excluded).

This case occurred in the time of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him and grant him satisfaction). He excluded the full brothers, and (one of them) said: "O brother of the full brother — suppose our father were a donkey, are we not from one mother?" So ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) made them partners (ashraka) among them. Zayd and ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with them both) also held this view.

Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: They are excluded, because they are agnates (ʿaṣabah), like the children of the father. Then, for the partnership (tashrīk), there are two conditions:
First: They must be full brothers (children of both father and mother), so that the partnership occurs through the mother's kinship. If they are consanguine brothers (children of the father alone), there is no partnership.
Second: The uterine brothers must be more than one. For if there is only one, he receives one-sixth, and one-sixth of the ʿaṣabah remains, so there is no need for partnership.

This is the ruling for brothers. As for their children: the females among them do not inherit, and the males among them are in their position (i.e., take their place) — except in five cases:
First: The children of uterine brothers do not inherit, for they are not in their position.
Second: Two brothers exclude the mother from one-third to one-sixth; but were their children in their place, they would not exclude her.
Third: In the "shared" problem, if the children of full brothers were in their place, there would be no partnership in their right.
Fourth: The grandfather does not exclude brothers, but he excludes the sons of brothers.
Fifth: A brother agnatizes his sister, but a brother's son does not agnatize his sister, since there is no inheritance for his sister at all.

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 284: On 'Aṣabāt (Male Agnatic Heirs) and Ḥajb (Exclusion from Inheritance)
chapters.arabic_text:
الأخوات من جهة الأب والأم أو من جهة الأب مع البنات عصبة أما الأخت من
الأم فتسقط بالبنت
فإن كان في المسألة بنت وأخوات فلها النصف والباقي لهن
ولو كان بنت وأخت لأب وأم وأخت لأب فللبنت النصف والباقي لأخت الأب والأم
وهي عصبة فتسقط أخت الأب
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في العصبات - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
والعصبة الذى يستغرق المال إذا انفرد ويأخذ ما بقي من ذوي الفرائض إذا
كان معه ذو فرض
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
ألحقوا الفرائض بأهلها فما أبقت الفرائض فلأولى عصبة ذكر
والعصبة كل ذكر يدلي إلى الميت بنفسه أو بذكر
والمعتق أيضا والمعتقة من المعصبيات والأخوات أيضا مع بنات الصلب
أو بنات الابن عصبات كما سبق
هذا تفصيلهم أما ترتبيهم
فأولادهم البنون ثم بنوهم ثم الآباء ثم آباؤهم وهم الأجداد من قبل الأب
والإخوة في درجة الجد يقاسمونه إلا إخوة الأم فإنهم يسقطون به ويسقط بنو
الإخوة بالجد وفاقا
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يسقط الإخوة أيضا بالجد
ثم ليعم أن التقدم للأخ من الأب والأم ثم للأخ من الأب ثم ابن الأخ من
الأب والأم ثم ابن الأخ من الأب ثم العم للأب والأم ثم العم للأب ثم بنوهم
على ترتيبهم ثم عم الأب للأب والأم ثم عم الأب للأب ثم بنوهم على ترتيبهم
ثم عم الجد على هذا الترتيب إلى حيث ينتهي
فإن لم يكن واحد من هؤلاء فالمال لمعتق الميت فإن لم يكن فلعصبات المعتق
فإن لم يكن فلمعتق المعتق ثم لعصباته ثم لمعتقه على هذا الترتيب
هذا ترتيبهم وفيه فروع أربعة
الأول ابن الأخ وإن سفل مقدم على العم لأن الجهة هاهنا مقدمة ومختلفة فلا
نظر إلى القرب
وأما بان الأخ للأب يقدم على ابن ابن الأخ للأب والأم إذا سفل للقرب مع
أن جهة الأخوة جنس واحد فإنما يقوم هاهنا بالقوة عند تساوي الدرجة فليتنبه
لهذه الدقيقة
الثاني ابنا عم أحدهما أخ لأم فله بأخوة الأم السدس والباقي بينهما نصفين
ولا ترجح قرابته فتقدمه بخلاف الأخ للأب والأم حيث قدم على الأخ للأب لأن
القرابة ثم متجانسة فامتزجت فأوجبت ترجيحا
والثالث بنت وابنا عم أحدهما أخ لأم النصف للبنت والباقي بينهما بالسوية
وأخوة الأم سقطت بالبنت
وقال ابن الحداد المال كله للذي هو أخ لأم لأنه لا يمكن استعمال قرابته
في التوريث فيستعمل مرجحا وهو ضعيف
الرابع في عصبات المعتق ولا يستحق صاحب فرض بالولاء فلا مدخل لأنثى فيه
إلا إذا كانت معتقة وإنما يستحق بالولاء الذكور كما سبق في العصبات
فإن اجتمع ابن المعتق وأبوه فالمال للابن لأن العصوبة له هاهنا
والأخ للأب والأم يقدم على الأخ للأب وإن لم تؤثر الأمومة هاهنا ولكن
تصلح للترجيح
ومن الأصحاب من طرد قولين كما في التقديم في ولاية النكاح
ولو اجتمع الجد والأخ فقولان
أحدهما الأخ أولى لأن إدلاءه بالنبوة وهي أقوى من العصوبة والولاء يدور
على محض العصوبة
والثاني أنهما يستويان لاستوائهما في القرب والعصوبة
فعلى هذا يقدم الجد على ابن الأخ وعلى الأول يقدم ابن الأخ على الجد لقوة
النبوة
بإن قيل وما طريق مقاسمة الجد والإخوة في الوراثة بالنسب
قلنا مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه إذا لم يكن معهما ذو فرض جعل الجد
كأحد الإخوة ويقسم المال عليه وعلى الإخوة والأخوات للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
ما دام الثلث لا ينقص بالقسمة كما إذا كان معه أخ أو أخوان أو أخ وأخت أو
أخ وأختان أو أربع أخوات
فأما إذا نقص الثلث بأن كانوا أكثر من هذا ويسلم إليه الثلث كاملا وقسم
الباقي على الإخوة للأب والأم
وإن كان معه ذو فرض أعطي صاحب الفرض سهمه فإن لم يبق شئ فرض للجد  السدس
واعتلت المسألة
وإن بقي سدس سلم وإن بقي أقل من السدس اعتلت المسألة وسلم به السدس
وإن كان الباقي أكثر من السدس قسم المال وسلم إلى الجد إما ثلث ما يبقى
بعد سهم ذوي الفروض أو سدس جميع المال أو ما يخصه بالقسمة أيها كان خيرا له
من الأقسام الثلاثة خص به
مسائله مع الجد زوج وأخ
للزوج النصف والباقي بينهما نصفين لأنه خير من السدس وثلث ما يبقى
فلو كانا أخوين استوى القسمة وسدس الجملة وثلث ما يبقى
فلو كانوا ثلاثة استوى السدس وثلث ما يبقى وهما خير من القسمة فله السدس
وهو ثلث ما يبقى
زوج وأم وأخ مع الجد
فللزوج النصف وللأم الثلث لا يبقى إلا سدس فهو للجد وسقط الأخ
ولو كان بدل الأخ أخت فظاهر القياس أنها تسقط أيضا لأنها عصبة مع الجد
كالأخ
والصحيح من مذهب زيد أنه يفرض لها النصف لأن الجد صاحب فرض الآن فهي أيضا
تنقلب إلى فرضها ثم يقسم مجموع حصتهما للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
وأما الأخ فليس له حال فرضية وإسقاط الأخت أيضا نقل عن زيد في رواية
زوج وبنت وأم وإخوة مع الجد
للبنت النصف وللأم السدس وللزوج الربع ويبقى نصف سدس فتعال المسألة حتى
يتم السدس للجد وتسقط الإخوة
هذا كله حكمه مع إخوة الأب والأم وجدهم
فإن كان معه أخوة الأم فهم مسقطون
وإن كان معه إخوة الأب وحدهم فهم عند عدمهم بمنزلتهم أعني بمنزلة إخوة
الأب والأم
فأما إذا اجتمع معه إخوة الأب والأم وإخوة الأب فيجعل الجد كواحد منهم
ويعد إخوة للأم عليه
والحكم ما سبق يعينه ولا يتغير حكم الجد معهم هاهنا وإنما الذى يتجدد أن
إخوة الأب يدخلون أيضا عليه في الحساب وما يخصهم لا يبقى عليهم بل يسترد
منهم أولاد الأب والأم إما على الكمال إن كان فيهم ذكر أو ما يكمل به
النصيب إن تمحض الإناث فيهن أعني إخوة الأب والأم
وعلته أن سقوطهم بإخوة الأب والأم فلا يظهر  فائدته إلا في حقهم أما في حق
الجد فلا يظهر مثاله إذا لم يكن ذو فرض
أخ لأب وأم وأخ لأب مع الجد
فالثلث والقسمة سيان فله الثلث والباقي لأخ الأب والأم ويسقط أخ الأب به
وإن دخل في حساب القسمة
وإن كان بدل الأخ للأب أخت لأب فالقسمة خير إذ يصح المسألة من خمسة ويخص
الجد منها سهمان فيبقى ثلاثة أسهم فتستقر على الأخ من الأب والأم
أخت لأب وأم وأخ لأب مع الجد
فالمسألة من خمسة والقسمة خير للجد فإن له سهمين يبقي ثلاثة واحدة لها
واثنان للأخ من الأب فيسترد منه ما يكمل لها النصف ويبقى الباقي لأخ من
الأب
أختان لأب وأم وأخت لأب مع الجد
فالمسألة من خمسة ويخص الأختين سهمان وهو ناقص عن الثلثين فيسترد ما في
يد الأخت للأب فلا يكمل الثلثين فيقتصر على استرداد ذلك
أما إذا كان في صورة المعادة صاحب فرض فيقدم صاحب الفرض كما سبق في غير
صورة المعادة على ذلك التفصيل ويعتبر بالباقي القسمة أو ثلث ما يبقى أو
السدس فأي ذلك كان خيرا خص الجد به
فإن كان الخير في القسمة روعي في المعادة ما ذكرناه من حرمان أولاد الأب
إن كان في أولاد الأب والأم ذكر واسترداد ما يكمل به نصيب الإناث إن لم يكن
فيهن ذكر
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثالث في الحجب - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
فنعود إلى عد الأصناف المذكورين في الباب الأول ونقول
أما الزوج والزوجة فلا يحجبان بوارث لأنهما يدليان بأنفسهما
وأما الأم فلا تحجب أيضا
والجدة تحجبها الأم فلا ترث مع الأم جدة وأم الأب يحجبها الأب
وذلك القربى من كل جهة من الجدات تحجب البعدى من تلك الجهة
والقربى من جهة الأم تحجب البعدي من جهة الأب
والقربى من جهة الأب هل تحجب البعدى من جهة الأم
فيه قولان أظهرهما أنها لا تحجب بل تشارك لقوة جدودة الأم
وأما الأب فلا يحجبه أحد والجد لا يحجبه إلا الأب
هذا حكم من يدلي من جهة العلو أما من يدلي من جهة السفل
فالابن والبنت لا يحجبان
فأما ابن الابن فلا يحجبه إلا الابن
وبنت الابن يحجبها الابن وابنتان فصاعدا من بنات الصلب وكذا الترتيب فيمن
سفل منهم على اختلاف درجاتهم
وأما المدلون على الأطراف
فالأخ للأب والأم يحجبه ثلاث الأب والابن وابن الابن
وكذا الأخت للأب والأم
وأما الأخ للأب يحجبه هؤلاء الثلاثة والأخ للأب والأم
وأما الأخت للأب يحجبها هؤلاء الأربع واثنتان فصاعدا من الأخوات للأب
والأم
وأما الأخ للأم فيحجبه ستة الأب والجد والابن والبنت وابن الابن وبنت
الابن
وأما العم فيحجبه من يحجب الأخ للأب والأم والأخ للأب كذا بنو الأخوة وقد
نبهنا على ترتيب العصبات من قبل فلا حاجة إلى الإعادة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning denotes binding, wrapping tightly (as a bandage); a paternal male relation who binds the inheritance through his own agnatic tie.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In inheritance law, the ʿaṣabah is the heir who takes the residue after fixed shares (furūḍ) are allotted, or the entirety when sole — a technical legal extension of the root's sense of "encompassing" what remains.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to physical binding; here it is a metaphorical (majāz) transfer to the legal category of residual heirs, since they "bind" the remaining estate.
- Root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To veil, screen, or obstruct from sight.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām and law, ḥajb denotes the legal "veiling" of an heir from inheritance due to a nearer or stronger claimant — a technical theological-legal metaphor of obstruction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical concealment; metaphorical = legal exclusion, as the nearer heir "veils" the remoter one from the estate.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text repeatedly uses conditional clauses (e.g., "if there is no... then...") and exceptions ("except...") to structure legal rulings; Sībawayh's parsing of these governs the precise logical sequencing of inheritance priorities.
chapters.translation:
I say: The sisters [of the deceased] from the father and mother [together], or from the father [alone], are ʿaṣabāt (agnatic residual heirs) alongside daughters. As for the sister from the mother [only], she is excluded (tasquṭ) by the daughter.

If the case involves a daughter and sisters, then the daughter takes half, and the remainder goes to the sisters.

If there is a daughter, a full sister (from father and mother), and a half-sister (from the father), then the daughter takes half, and the remainder goes to the full sister, who is an ʿaṣabah; thus the paternal half-sister is excluded.

— Peace be upon him — Chapter Two: On the ʿAṣabāt — Peace be upon him —

The ʿaṣabah is the one who takes the entire estate when alone, and takes what remains of the fixed-share heirs (ahl al-farāʾiḍ) when a fixed-share heir is present alongside him.

The Prophet — peace be upon him — said: {«ألحقوا الفرائض بأهلها فما أبقت الفرائض فلأولى عصبة ذكر»} ("Give the fixed shares to their due recipients; and whatever the fixed shares leave over, then it belongs to the nearest male ʿaṣabah").

The ʿaṣabah is every male who traces his connection to the deceased either through himself (i.e., directly) or through another male. The manumitter (al-muʿtiq) is also [an ʿaṣabah], and the manumittress (al-muʿtiqah) is among the ʿaṣabāt. Likewise, sisters [become] ʿaṣabāt alongside daughters of the loins (banāt al-ṣulb) or daughters of the son, as previously mentioned.

This is their detailed enumeration. As for their ordering (tartīb): First, their sons (i.e., the deceased's sons), then their sons' sons (grandsons), then the fathers, then their fathers (i.e., grandfathers from the paternal side). The brothers are on the same degree as the grandfather, and they share with him [in the division] — except the maternal brothers, for they are excluded by him (the grandfather). The brothers' sons are also excluded by the grandfather, by agreement [among the scholars].

Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: The brothers [themselves] are also excluded by the grandfather.

Then know that precedence [among the ʿaṣabāt] is as follows: First, the full brother (from father and mother); then the paternal half-brother; then the son of the full brother; then the son of the paternal half-brother; then the full paternal uncle (from father and mother); then the paternal half-uncle (from father); then their sons, in their respective order; then the father's full paternal uncle; then the father's paternal half-uncle; then their sons, in their respective order; then the grandfather's paternal uncle, in this same order, continuing upward until it terminates.

If none of these exists, then the estate goes to the manumitter of the deceased. If not, then to the ʿaṣabāt of the manumitter. If not, then to the manumitter's manumitter, then to his ʿaṣabāt, then to his manumitter, in this order.

This is their ordering. Within it are four subsidiary branches (furūʿ):

**First Branch:** The son of a brother, however low he descends, is given precedence over the paternal uncle, because here the "direction" (al-jihah) is given precedence and is distinct [in kind]; thus proximity [of degree] is not considered.

However, the paternal half-brother's son is given precedence over the son of the full brother's son when the latter descends [further], due to proximity [of degree], even though the direction of brotherhood is a single genus. Thus, strength [of connection] only operates here when the degrees are equal. Let one pay heed to this subtle point (al-daqīqah).

**Second Branch:** Two paternal cousins, one of whom is a maternal brother [of the deceased]: he takes one-sixth by virtue of his maternal brotherhood, and the remainder is divided between them in halves. His [closer] kinship does not give him precedence over the other. This differs from the case of the full brother being preferred over the paternal half-brother, because there the kinship is homogeneous, so it blends and necessitates a preference.

**Third Branch:** A daughter, and two paternal cousins, one of whom is a maternal brother: the daughter takes half, and the remainder is divided between them equally. The maternal brotherhood is dropped by the daughter [i.e., the maternal brother's share as a fixed-share heir is excluded, but he still shares as a cousin]. Ibn al-Ḥaddād said: The entire estate goes to the one who is a maternal brother, because his kinship [as a cousin] cannot be used for inheritance [since the daughter takes half and the other cousin is equally entitled], so it is used as a preponderating factor. But this [view] is weak.

**Fourth Branch:** Concerning the ʿaṣabāt of the manumitter: No fixed-share heir (ṣāḥib farḍ) inherits by virtue of clientage (al-walāʾ). No female has any entry into it, except when she is the manumittress. Only males inherit by clientage, as previously mentioned in the section on ʿaṣabāt.

If the son of the manumitter and the manumitter's father are both present, the estate goes to the son, because the ʿaṣabah [right] belongs to him here. The full brother is preferred over the paternal half-brother [in clientage], even though motherhood has no effect here, but it is suitable for preponderance. Some of our companions extended two opinions [in this matter], just as in the preference in the guardianship of marriage (wilāyat al-nikāḥ).

If the grandfather and the brother are both present [in inheritance], there are two opinions: One is that the brother is more entitled, because his connection (idlāʾ) is through prophethood [i.e., the paternal line of Adam], which is stronger than mere ʿaṣabah; and clientage revolves purely on ʿaṣabah. The second is that they are equal, due to their equality in proximity and in ʿaṣabah. On this second view, the grandfather is preferred over the brother's son; on the first view, the brother's son is preferred over the grandfather, due to the strength of prophethood.

If it is said: What is the method of the grandfather's sharing (muqāsāmah) with the brothers in inheritance by kinship? We say: The school of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — is that when there is no fixed-share heir with them, the grandfather is treated as one of the brothers, and the estate is divided between him and the brothers and sisters, with the male taking the share of two females, as long as the third [of the estate] is not diminished by this division — such as when there is with him one brother, or two brothers, or a brother and a sister, or a brother and two sisters, or four sisters.

But when the third would be diminished — i.e., when they are more numerous than this — then the full third is given to him intact, and the remainder is divided among the full brothers and sisters (from father and mother).

If a fixed-share heir is present with him, the fixed-share heir is given his share. If nothing remains, then the grandfather is assigned one-sixth, and the case becomes ʿāilah (defective, requiring proportional reduction). If a sixth remains, it is given to him intact. If less than a sixth remains, the case becomes ʿāilah, and the sixth is secured for him [by reduction of others]. If the remainder is more than a sixth, then the estate is divided, and the grandfather is given whichever is most beneficial to him of three options: either one-third of what remains after the fixed-share heirs' portions, or one-sixth of the entire estate, or what his share amounts to by division — whichever of the three is best for him, he is allocated that.

**His cases with the grandfather:**

*Case: Husband and brother [with the grandfather]:* The husband takes half, and the remainder is divided between them in halves, because that is better for the grandfather than one-sixth or one-third of what remains.

*Case: Two brothers [with the grandfather]:* The division, the sixth of the total, and the third of what remains are all equal.

*Case: Three brothers [with the grandfather]:* The sixth and the third of what remains are equal, and both are better than division. Thus he takes the sixth, which is the third of what remains.

*Case: Husband, mother, and brother with the grandfather:* The husband takes half, the mother takes one-third, and nothing remains except one-sixth, which goes to the grandfather; the brother is dropped.

If instead of the brother there is a sister, then by apparent analogy (qiyās) she is also dropped, because she is an ʿaṣabah with the grandfather like the brother. But the correct view in the school of Zayd [ibn ʿAlī] is that she is assigned half [as a fixed share], because the grandfather is now a fixed-share heir, so she too converts to her fixed share. Then their combined shares are divided, with the male taking the share of two females.

As for the brother, he has no state of fixed-sharehood. The dropping of the sister [in this case] is also transmitted from Zayd in one narration.

*Case: Husband, daughter, mother, and brothers with the grandfather:* The daughter takes half, the mother takes one-sixth, the husband takes one-quarter, and one-half of a sixth remains. The case becomes ʿāilah so that the sixth is completed for the grandfather, and the brothers are dropped.

All of this is his ruling with full brothers (from father and mother) and their grandfather. If maternal brothers are present with him, they are excluded [by the grandfather]. If paternal half-brothers alone are present with him, then in their absence [of full brothers], they stand in their place — i.e., in the place of full brothers.

But when full brothers and paternal half-brothers are both present with him, the grandfather is treated as one of them, and the maternal brothers are counted against him [i.e., included in the count]. The ruling is as previously indicated; it does not change here. What is new is that the paternal half-brothers also enter into the calculation against him, and what is allocated to them does not remain with them; rather, the full brothers (from father and mother) reclaim it from them — either entirely if there is a male among them, or to complete the share if the full siblings are all females. The reason is that the paternal half-brothers' exclusion [from the grandfather's share] is due to the full brothers, so their benefit appears only in favor of the full brothers, not in favor of the grandfather.

**Example when there is no fixed-share heir:** A full brother and a paternal half-brother with the grandfather: The third and the division are equal [for the grandfather], so he takes the third, and the remainder goes to the full brother; the paternal half-brother is dropped by him, even though he entered into the calculation of division.

If instead of the paternal half-brother there is a paternal half-sister, then division is better [for the grandfather], since the case resolves from five: the grandfather gets two shares, leaving three — which go to the full brother.

*Case: A full sister and a paternal half-brother with the grandfather:* The case is from five, and division is better for the grandfather, for he takes two shares, leaving three — one for her, and two for the paternal half-brother. From him is reclaimed what completes her half, and the rest remains for the paternal half-brother.

*Case: Two full sisters and a paternal half-sister with the grandfather:* The case is from five; the two full sisters get two shares, which is deficient from two-thirds. What is in the hand of the paternal half-sister is reclaimed, but it does not complete the two-thirds, so the reclamation is limited to that amount.

When there is a fixed-share heir in the case of "return" (muʿādah), the fixed-share heir is given precedence, as previously detailed in non-return cases. Then the remainder is considered: whether division, or one-third of what remains, or one-sixth — whichever is best for the grandfather, he is allocated it. If the best is in division, then in the return case one observes what we mentioned: the deprivation of the paternal half-siblings if there is a male among the full siblings, and the reclamation of what completes the share of the females if there is no male among them.

— Peace be upon him — Chapter Three: On Exclusion (al-Ḥajb) — Peace be upon him —

We now return to enumerating the categories mentioned in the first chapter, and we say:

As for the husband and the wife, they are not excluded by any heir, because they connect to the deceased through themselves (i.e., directly, not through another).

As for the mother, she too is not excluded.

The grandmother is excluded by the mother, so no grandmother inherits alongside the mother. The father's mother is excluded by the father.

The nearer [grandmother] from any direction among the grandmothers excludes the remoter one from that same direction. The nearer from the mother's side excludes the remoter from the father's side. As for whether the nearer from the father's side excludes the remoter from the mother's side, there are two opinions; the more apparent of them is that she does not exclude, but rather shares, due to the strength of the maternal grandmotherhood (judūdah al-umm).

As for the father, no one excludes him. The grandfather is excluded only by the father.

This is the ruling for those who connect from the direction of ascent (al-ʿuluw). As for those who connect from the direction of descent (al-sufl):

The son and the daughter are not excluded. As for the son's son, only the son excludes him. The son's daughter is excluded by the son, and by two or more daughters of the loins. Likewise is the ordering for those below them, across their varying degrees.

As for those who connect from the sides (al-aṭrāf):

The full brother (from father and mother) is excluded by three: the father, the son, and the son's son. Likewise the full sister.

As for the paternal half-brother, he is excluded by these three, plus the full brother.

As for the paternal half-sister, she is excluded by these four, plus two or more full sisters.

As for the maternal brother, he is excluded by six: the father, the grandfather, the son, the daughter, the son's son, and the son's daughter.

As for the paternal uncle, he is excluded by whoever excludes the full brother and the paternal half-brother. Likewise the brothers' sons. We have already indicated the ordering of the ʿaṣabāt previously, so there is no need for repetition.

chapters.title_en: Branches on Impediments to Inheritance and the Two Impediments of Religious Difference and Slavery
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع

الأول أن من لا يرث كالقاتل والكافر والرقيق لا يحجب
ويستثنى عن هذا مسألة وهي أبوان وأخوان
فإن الأخوين يسقطان بالأب ويحجبان الأم من الثلث إلى السدس لأن سقوطهما
بالأب لا بالأم فيرجع فائدتهما إلى الأب لا إلى الأم
ومثله جدتان إحداهما أم الأب والأخرى أم الأم ومعها الأب
فلأم الأم السدس ولا يقال ان أم الأب تشارك لولا الأب وإنما سقوطها بالأب
فترجع الفائدة إليه لأن استحقاقها بالفرضية فلا يناسب استحقاق الأب وهو
بالعصوبة
وأما الأخ والأب في تلك الصورة كلاهما يرثان بالعصوبة فأمكن رد الفائدة
إليه
ومن أصحابنا من طرد القياس وقال ليس لأم الأم إلا نصف السدس
الثاني مهما اجتمعت قرابتان من قرابة المجوس على وجه لا يجوز الجمع
بينهما في الإسلام سواء حصل بنكاح المجوس أو بالوطء بالشبهة
فلا يورث بهما عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله بل يورث بأقواهما ويصرف
الأقوى بأمرين
أحدهما أن تكون إحداهما مسقطة للأخرى كبنت هى أخت لأم ترث بالبنوة وتسقط
أخوة الأم
الثاني أن يقل حجاب إحديهما كأخت لأب هى أم الأم فترث
بالجدودة لأنها أثبت إذ لا تسقط إلا بالأم فقط والأخت تسقط بثلاث بالأب
والابن وابن الابن
فإذا تزوج المجوسي بابنته  فأولد بنتا
فمات المجوسي فقد خلف بنتين إحداهما زوجته فلا شيء لها بالزوجية فإنها
فاسدة والأخرى بنت بنت ولا توريث بهما فلهما الثلثان بالبنوة
فلو ماتت العليا بعد موت الواطئ فقد خلفت بنتا هى أخت لأب فلها بالبنوة
النصف
فلو ماتت السفلى أولا فقد خلفت أما هى أخت لأب فلها الثلث بالأمومة ولا
شيء لها بالأخوة
المسألة بحالتها لو وطئ البنت السفلي فأولدها بنتا أخرى
ومات الواطئ فقد خلف ثلاث بنات فلهن الثلثان ولا نظر إلى الزوجة ولا إلى
بنوة البنت
فلو ماتت العليا بعده فقد خلفت بنتا وبنت بنت هما أختان لأب فللبنت
العليا النصف والباقي للسفلى بأخوة الأب فإن الأخت مع البنت عصبة
فلو ماتت الوسطى أولا فقد خلفت أما وبنتا هما أختا أب فللأم السدس وللبنت
النصف وسقط أخوة الأب من الطرفين بالبنوة والأمومة
فلو ماتت السفلى أولا فقد خلفت أما وجدة هما أختا أب فللأم الثلث وللجدة
الباقي بأخوة الأب لأن الجدودة سقطت بالأمومة
فأما إذا وطئ المجوسي أمه فولدت له بنتا
فمات فقد خلف أما وبنتا هى أخت لأم فللأم السدس وللبنت النصف وسقط أخوة
الأم
ولو ماتت البنت فقد خلفت أما هى أم لأب فلها الثلث بالأمومة وتسقط أمومة
الأب
وعلى هذا الترتيب جميع المسائل والله أعلم
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الرابع في موانع الميراث - صلى الله عليه
وسلم -
وهي ستة

### | الأول اختلاف الدين

فلا يرث كافر من مسلم ولا مسلم من كافر لقوله عليه السلام
لا يتوارث أهل ملتين شتى
ويرث اليهود من النصارى المجوس لأن جميع الملل في البطلان كالملة الواحدة
وفي هذا المعنى قال الله تعالى {لكم دينكم ولي دين}

### | فرعان

أحدهما الذمي هل يرث من الحربي فيه قولان
أحدهما نعم لاتحاد الدين
والثاني لا لأن حكمنا لا يجري على أهل الحرب والتوريث حكم شرعي
وأما المعاهد فهو في حكم الذمي لأمانه
وقال ابن سريج قياس قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه في حكم الحربي لأنه لم
يستوطئ دارنا والصحيح  الأول
الثاني المرتد لا يرث ولا يرثه لا قريبة الكافر ولا قريبة المسلم ولا
قربة المرتد بل ماله فيء
ولا فرق بين ما اكتسب بعد الردة وبين ما اكتسبه قبله
والزنديق حكمه حكم المرتد
هذا إذا قتل أو مات فإن عاد إلى الإسلام استقر ملكه

### | المانع الثاني الرقيق

وهو لا يرث ولا يورث سواء كان قنا أو أم ولد أو مكاتبا لأنه لا يملك ومن
يراه أهلا للملك على قول فهو ملك بإذن السيد لا قرار له ولا مدخل للإذن في
الميراث
فرع من نصفه حر ونصفه رقيق لا يرث
وإذا مات فهل ترثه أقاربه
قال في القديم لا يرث كما لا يورث
وقال في الجديد يورث لأنه تحقق الملك والقريب أولى الناس به
فإن قلنا لا يورث فماله للسيد أو لبيت المال أو أيهما أولى به فيه خلاف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Literally "to veil, screen, or obstruct from sight"; in inheritance law, the technical sense of preventing a heir from receiving a share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine veiling (ḥijāb) as a metaphysical barrier; here applied jurisprudentially to denote exclusion from succession due to a nearer or stronger claimant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) in inheritance contexts—actual exclusion from a fixed share—not metaphorically.
- Root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bind or wrap tightly; the ʿaṣabah are the agnatic heirs who "bind" the estate through male-line kinship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In divine law, the ʿaṣabah represent the principle of residual succession by proximity through the paternal line, reflecting the patriarchal order of tribal solidarity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in inheritance—those who take the residue (taʿṣīb) after fixed shares are allocated.
- Root: ر-ق-ق (r-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Thinness or softness; riqq (slavery) as a legal state of diminished capacity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The slave lacks full legal personality (dhimmah); ownership is incomplete, hence no inheritance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal legal incapacity, not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text uses "illā" (except) and "law" (if) to structure hypothetical cases, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to render the legal consequences accurately.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first branch is that whoever does not inherit—such as the killer, the disbeliever, and the slave—does not act as a ḥājib (excluder). An exception to this is a case: two parents and two brothers. For the two brothers are dropped by the father, and they exclude the mother from a third to a sixth, because their exclusion is due to the father, not the mother. Thus their benefit reverts to the father, not to the mother. Similarly, two grandmothers—one being the mother of the father and the other the mother of the mother—with the father present: the mother of the mother receives a sixth, and it is not said that the mother of the father shares, for were it not for the father, she would be excluded; rather, her exclusion is by the father, so the benefit reverts to him, because her entitlement is by fixed share (fard), which does not suit the father's entitlement, which is by agnacy (taʿṣīb). As for the brother and the father in that scenario, both inherit by agnacy, so it is possible for the benefit to revert to him. Among our companions (Shāfiʿīs) is one who extended the analogy (qiyās) and said: the mother of the mother receives only half of a sixth.

The second branch: Whenever two kinships from the kinship of the Magians (Majūs) converge in a manner that does not permit combining both in Islam—whether arising from Magian marriage or from intercourse under doubtful circumstances (waṭʾ al-shubhah)—then inheritance is not given through both according to us, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him. Rather, inheritance is given through the stronger of the two, and the stronger is determined by two matters: First, that one of them excludes the other, such as a daughter who is a maternal sister—she inherits by daughterhood and drops the maternal sisterhood. Second, that the exclusion (ḥijāb) of one of them is lesser, such as a paternal sister who is the mother of the mother—she inherits by grandmotherhood because it is more established, since she is not excluded except by the mother alone, whereas the sister is excluded by three: the father, the son, and the son's son.

Thus, if a Magian marries his daughter and she bears him a daughter, then the Magian dies, he has left behind two daughters: one is his wife—she gets nothing by marriage, for it is invalid—and the other is a daughter of a daughter, and there is no inheritance through either of these two relations; so they receive two-thirds by daughterhood. If the upper one dies after the death of the fornicator, she leaves behind a daughter who is a paternal sister—she receives half by daughterhood. If the lower one dies first, she leaves behind a mother who is a paternal sister—she receives a third by motherhood, and nothing by sisterhood.

The same case in its state: if he had intercourse with the lower daughter and she bore him another daughter, and the fornicator dies, he leaves behind three daughters—they receive two-thirds, with no regard to the wife nor to the daughterhood of the daughter. If the upper one dies after him, she leaves behind a daughter and a daughter of a daughter, both being paternal sisters—the upper daughter receives half, and the remainder goes to the lower one by paternal sisterhood, for the sister with the daughter is an ʿaṣabah. If the middle one dies first, she leaves behind a mother and a daughter, both being paternal sisters of the father—the mother receives a sixth, the daughter half, and the paternal sisterhood from both sides is dropped by daughterhood and motherhood. If the lower one dies first, she leaves behind a mother and a grandmother, both being paternal sisters of the father—the mother receives a third, and the grandmother receives the remainder by paternal sisterhood, because grandmotherhood is dropped by motherhood.

As for when a Magian has intercourse with his mother, and she bears him a daughter, then he dies: he leaves behind a mother and a daughter who is a maternal sister—the mother receives a sixth, the daughter half, and the maternal sisterhood is dropped. If the daughter dies, she leaves behind a mother who is a paternal mother—she receives a third by motherhood, and the paternal motherhood is dropped. Upon this ordering are all the cases, and God knows best.

May peace and blessings be upon him. The fourth chapter on the impediments to inheritance—may peace and blessings be upon him—and they are six.

The first: Difference of religion. A disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, nor a Muslim from a disbeliever, due to his saying, peace be upon him: «لا يتوارث أهل ملتين شتى» (People of two different religions do not inherit from one another). Jews inherit from Christians and Magians, because all creeds, in their falsity, are like a single creed. In this meaning, God Most High said: {لكم دينكم ولي دين} ("To you your religion, and to me my religion").

Two sub-branches: First, does a dhimmī (protected non-Muslim) inherit from a ḥarbī (enemy combatant)? There are two opinions: one is yes, due to unity of religion; the second is no, because our legal authority does not apply to the people of war, and inheritance is a legal ruling. As for the muʿāhad (one with a truce), he is in the status of a dhimmī due to his security (amān). Ibn Surayj said: the implication of al-Shāfiʿī's statement, may God be pleased with him, is that he is in the status of a ḥarbī, because he has not settled in our abode. The correct view is the first.

Second: The apostate (murtadd) does not inherit, nor is he inherited from—neither by his disbelieving relative, nor his Muslim relative, nor his apostate relative. Rather, his wealth is fayʾ (booty for the public treasury). There is no difference between what he acquired after apostasy and what he acquired before it. The zindīq (heretic) has the same ruling as the apostate. This applies if he is killed or dies; if he returns to Islam, his ownership is confirmed.

The second impediment: Slavery (riqq). The slave does not inherit nor is he inherited from—whether he is a qinn (full slave), umm walad (mother of a child), or mukātab (one contracted for manumission)—because he does not own. And whoever considers him eligible for ownership, on one opinion, his ownership is by the master's permission with no permanence, and permission has no entry into inheritance.

A sub-branch: One who is half free and half slave does not inherit. If he dies, do his relatives inherit from him? In the Old Doctrine (al-qadīm), he said: they do not inherit, just as he is not inherited from. In the New Doctrine (al-jadīd), he said: he is inherited from, because ownership is realized, and the relative is the person most entitled to him. If we say he is not inherited from, then his wealth goes to the master or to the public treasury—or which of the two is more entitled to it—there is a disagreement therein.

chapters.title_en: The Third Impediment: Homicide
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المانع الثالث القتل

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
ليس للقاتل من الميراث شئ
والقتل قسمان مضمون وغير مضمون
أما المضمون فيوجب الحرمان سواء ضمن بالدية أو الكفارة أو القصاص
وسواء كان عمدا أو خطأ بسبب كحفر البئر أو بمباشرة من مكلف أو مجنون أو
صبي
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يحرم الصبي ولا من قتل بحفر البئر
فأما الذى ليس بمضمون كالقتل المستحق حدا لله تعالى
فالإمام إذا قتل حدا ففي حرمانه ثلاثة أقوال
حدها المنع لعموم الحديث
والثاني أنه لا يحرم لأن المفهوم السابق من اللفظ قتل بغير حق ولأن
الإمام كالنائب والقاتل هو الله عز وجل
والثالث أنه إن ثبت بإقراره فلا حرمان إذ لا تهمة وإن ثبت ببينة فربما
يتطرق تهمته إلى القاضي فيه
أما المستحق الذى يجوز تركه كالقتل قصاصا ودفع الصائل وقتل العادل الباغي
فيه خلاف مرتب وأولى بالحرمان لأنه مختار فيه وقد قتل لنفسه
والمكره محروم لأنه آثم وإن قلنا إن الضمان على المكره وفيه وجه على هذا
القول

### | المانع الرابع استبهام تاريخ الموت

فإذا مات جماعة من الأقارب تحت هدم أو غرق أو  في سفر واستبهم المتقدم
والمتأخر فيقدر في حق كل واحد منهم كأنه لم يخلف الآخرين فلا يتوارثون
ويوزع مال كل واحد منهم على من هو حي من جملة الأقارب إذ ليس التقدم بأولى
من التأخر
وكذلك إذا علمنا أنهم تلاحقوا في الموت ولكن لم نطلع على الترتيب وكذلك
لو اطلعنا ولكن نسيناه
وفي هذه الصورة الأخيرة احتمال وقد ذكرنا في مثل هذه الصورة في النكاحين
والجمعتين خلافا لأن إعادة الجمعة وفسخ النكاح له وجه وهاهنا لا حيلة فيه
ولا معنى للتوقف أبدا

### | المانع الخامس اللعان

فإنه يقطع ميراث الولد وكان في هذا ليس مانعا بل هو دافع للنسب إلا أنه
يقتصر أثره على الأب ومن يدلي به
أما الأم فالولد يرثها وهي ترث الولد ولها من ماله الثلث
وقال ابن مسعود أمه عصبة فلها الجميع
ولو نفى توأمين فهل يرث أحدهما الآخر بالعصوبة
المذهب أنه لا يرث لأنه لا يدلي إلا بقرابة الأمومة أما الأبوة فقد انتفت
فهو أخ لأم فقط
وقال مالك رحمه الله هو عصبة والأبوة انتفت في حق الأب بحجة ضرورية وهو
وجه لأصحابنا بعيد
وإذا ولدت المرأة من الزنا فهي ترثه والولد يرثها والتوأمان يتوارثان
بأخوة الأم
ومن ينسب إلى الزنا فلا أبوة له ولا ميراث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To kill, slay; the act of taking life, whether intentional or accidental; encompasses both direct causation (mubāsharah) and indirect causation (sabab).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, homicide is categorized by liability (ḍamān) — that which entails worldly recompense (diyah, qiṣāṣ) or expiation (kaffārah) — versus that which is exempt, such as lawful execution (ḥadd) or defensive killing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes actual killing; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to causation, e.g., digging a well that causes death, where the agent is termed "killer" by legal attribution.
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, deprive, render unlawful; core sense of prohibition and exclusion from a right or share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In inheritance law, ḥirmān signifies the legal deprivation of a statutory share (farīḍah) due to an impediment (māniʿ) — here, the moral-legal culpability of the killer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: prohibition of an act; metaphorical: denial of a right, as in "deprived of inheritance" — a transferred application from act to entitlement.
- Root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To curse, expel, distance; in legal context, the mutual imprecation (liʿān) between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The oath of condemnation that severs lineage (nafas) — a declarative act, not a punitive impediment, operating specifically against the father's claim.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cursing; metaphorical: legal severance of paternity, where the effect is "repulsion" (dafʿ) of lineage rather than "prevention" (manʿ) of an existing right.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muqaddar) — In "إذا مات جماعة... واستبهم المتقدم والمتأخر," the conditional particle governs a hypothetical scenario where the apodosis (taqdīr: "as if each left no other") is a legal fiction, requiring the interpreter to supply the unstated condition of ignorance of temporal priority.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third impediment is homicide.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: {«ليس للقاتل من الميراث شئ»} — "The killer has no share of inheritance."

Homicide is of two kinds: that which entails liability (maḍmūn) and that which entails no liability (ghayr maḍmūn).

As for that which entails liability, it necessitates deprivation (ḥirmān) — whether the liability is discharged by blood-money (diyah), expiation (kaffārah), or retaliation (qiṣāṣ). And it is equal whether the killing was intentional or erroneous, whether caused by indirect means such as digging a well, or by direct act (mubāsharah) of a legally responsible person (mukallaf), a madman, or a child.

Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) said: A child is not deprived, nor is one who kills by digging a well.

As for that which entails no liability — such as a killing that is legally warranted as a prescribed punishment (ḥadd) for God's right — if the Imām executes someone as a ḥadd penalty, there are three opinions concerning his deprivation:

The first is that he is deprived, due to the generality of the hadith.

The second is that he is not deprived, because the prior understanding from the wording [of the hadith] is killing without right, and because the Imām is like a deputy — the true killer is God, Exalted and Majestic.

The third is that if the [adultery] was established by his own confession, then there is no deprivation, since there is no suspicion [of self-interest]; but if it was established by testimony, then suspicion might attach to the judge in it.

As for the legally warranted killing that may be omitted — such as killing in retaliation (qiṣāṣ), repelling an aggressor (dafʿ al-ṣāʾil), and killing a rebellious transgressor (al-bāghī) by the just party — there is a graded disagreement [among the scholars], and it is more deserving of deprivation, because the killer had a choice in it and killed for his own sake.

The one compelled (mukrah) is deprived, because he is sinful — even if we hold that the liability (ḍamān) falls upon the compeller. And there is a face [of the school] on this [latter] saying.

---

The Fourth Impediment: Obscurity of the Time of Death

If a group of relatives die together under a collapsed structure, by drowning, or on a journey, and it is obscure which preceded and which followed, then each one is deemed, with respect to the other, as if he had not left the other behind — so they do not inherit from one another. The wealth of each one is distributed among those who are alive from the totality of the relatives, since precedence is no more likely than subsequence.

Likewise, if we know that they died in succession but we have not ascertained the order — and likewise if we had ascertained it but then forgot it.

In this last scenario there is a possibility [of a different ruling]. We have mentioned, in similar scenarios, in the cases of two marriages and two Friday prayers, a disagreement — because repeating the Friday prayer and annulling the marriage have a [valid] face [of permissibility]. But here there is no stratagem, and there is no meaning to suspending [judgment] ever.

---

The Fifth Impediment: Liʿān (Mutual Imprecation)

It severs the inheritance of the child. Yet in this [case] it is not an impediment [in the strict sense] but rather a repulsion (dāfiʿ) of lineage — except that its effect is confined to the father and those who trace [inheritance] through him.

As for the mother, the child inherits from her and she inherits from the child, and she receives from his wealth one-third.

Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) said: The mother is an ʿaṣabah (residuary heir), so she receives the entirety.

If he repudiated twins [by liʿān], does one of them inherit from the other by residuary right (ʿaṣabah)? The [established] school holds that he does not inherit, because he traces [kinship] only through maternal relation — for paternity has been negated, so he is merely a uterine brother.

Mālik (may God have mercy on him) said: He is an ʿaṣabah, and paternity is negated only with respect to the father by a necessary proof — and this is a remote face [of the school] among our companions.

If a woman gives birth from fornication (zinā), she inherits from him and the child inherits from her, and the twins inherit from one another by uterine brotherhood. And whoever is attributed to fornication has no paternity and no inheritance.

chapters.title_en: The Sixth Impediment: Doubt Concerning Entitlement (al-Shakk fī al-Istiḥqāq)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المانع السادس الشك في الاستحقاق

وسببه أربعة أمور
الأول التردد في الوجود
وذلك في المفقود والأسير الذى انقطع خبره فلا يرث عنه أحد ما لم تقم بينة
على موته أو لم تمض مدة يقضي الحاكم في مثلها بأن ذلك الشخص لا يحيا أكثر
من ذلك وتعتبر المدة من وقت ولادة المفقود لا من وقت غيبته
فإذا قضى بموته ورثه أقاربه الموجودون وقت الحكم لا وقت الغيبة
فأما ميراثه من الحاضرين فيجب التوقف في نصيبه إذا مات له قريب فإن حكم
القاضي بموته بعد ذلك فيقدر كأنه لم يكن موجودا عند موت قريبه ويصرف
الموقوف إلى الورثة الموجودين من حال موت قريب المفقود
وأما الحاضرون فإن كان المفقود ممن يتصور حجب  الحاضر به فلا يصرف إليهم
شئ وإن تصور أن يحجب عن البعض فيتوقف في قدر الاحتمال ولا يصرف إليهم إلا
المستقين ونأخذ بأسوأ الأحوال في حق كل واحد
فإن كان النقصان في تقدير الحياة قدرناها وإن كان في تقدير الموت قدرنا
الموت حتى إذا خلفت المرأة زوجا وأختين لأب حاضرتين وأخا لأب مفقودا فإن
كان
الأخ ميتا فللزوج النصف وللأختين الثلثان والمسألة تعول إلى سبعة من ستة
وإن كان حيا فللزوج نصف غير عائل والربع للأختين فلا يصرف إلى الزوج إلا
ثلاثة أسباع المال وهو النصف العائل ويقدر موت المفقود في حقه لأنه أسوأ
الأحوال وللأختين الربع على تقدير الحياة فإنه الأسوأ والباقي موقوف إلى
البيان
ومن أصحابنا من قال تقدر الحياة في حق كل واحد منهم في الحال فإن ظهر
نقيضه غيرنا الحكم
ومنهم من قال نأخذ بالموت لأن استحقاق هؤلاء مستيقن فإن ظهر نقيضه غيرنا
الحكم
وهذان وجهان متقابلان إذ يقابل الأخير قول الأول إن الأصل بقاء الحياة
فالصحيح التوقف عند الإشكال
السبب الثاني الشك في النسب
حيث يحتاج إلى القائف فحكمه في مدة الإشكال حكم المفقود فنأخذ بأسوأ
الأحوال في حق الجميع
السبب الثالث الشك بسبب الحمل
فإن الحمل يرث بشرطين
أحدهما أن ينفصل حيا فلو انفصل ميتا ولو بجناية جان كان كما لو
انعدم من أصله
والثاني أن يكون موجودا عند الموت وهو أن يؤتى به لأقل من ستة أشهر من
وقت الموت فإن كان لأكثر من أربع سنين فلا يرث وإن كان بين المدتين ورث لأن
النسب يثبت والإرث يتبع النسب
ولو انفصل الجنين وصرخ ثم مات ورث
وكذا إذا فتح الطرف وامتص الثدي وأمارات الحياة ظاهرة
ولو تحرك فإن كان من قبيل اختلاج وتقلص عصب وعضلة فلا أثر له وإن كان
اختياريا كقبض الأصابع وبسطها فهو دليل الحياة وإن تردد بين الجهتين فقولان
أحدهما لا يرث لعدم اليقين
والثاني يرث اعتمادا على غالب الظن بالعلامة
ولو برز نصف الجنين وصرخ ثم مات وانفصل ففيه  وجهان محتملان
هذا إذا انفصل فأما قبل الانفصال فهو وقت الإشكال فيقدر أضر الأحوال على
بقية الورثة وأقصى الممكن تقديرا أربعة من الأولاد في البطن والأنوثة
والذكورة محتملة فنقدر ما هو الأضر بكل حال مثاله
مات رجل وخلف امرأة حاملا وأخا
لا شئ للأخ في الحال لاحتمال أن الحمل ذكر فيحجب
ولو خلف أبوين وامرأة حاملا
أعطي كل واحد من الأبوين السدس عائلا من سبعة وعشرين لاحتمال أن يكون
الحمل بنتين فتقول المسألة من أربع وعشرين إلى سبعة وعشرين يكون للأم أربعة
وللأب
أربعة وللمرأة ثلاثة ولكل واحد من البنتين ثمانية فهذا أضر التقديرات
فنقدره في الحال
فإن قيل وهل يتسلط الحاضرون على ما سلم إليهم
قلنا قال القفال لا إذ لا تصح القسمة عن الحمل إلا بالقاضي وليس للقاضي
التصرف في مال الأجنة بخلاف الغائبين
والصحيح أنهم يتسلطون وأنه يجب على القاضي أن ينوب في القسمة كيلا تتعطل
الحقوق
فإن قيل فلو ادعت المرأة الحمل فربما تكون معاندة فكيف ينتظر بقولها أربع
سنين
قلنا إن ظهر مخايل الحمل أو كانت قريبة العهد بوطء يحتمل العلوق فلا بد
من التوقف
وإن لم يظهر مثل هذه العلامات فالمسألة محتملة والأولى الاعتماد عليها
فإنها أعلم بالعلامات الخفية وهي مؤتمنة في رحمها

### | السبب الرابع الخنوثة

والخنثى مشكل الذكورة والأنوثة
وقال بعض أهل العلم لا يرث لأنه ليس بذكر ولا أنثى وليس في الكتاب إلا
ميراث الذكور والإناث
وقيل أيضا يأخذ نصف نصيب الذكر ونصف نصيب الأنثى
وإنما مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه إما ذكر وإما أنثى وهو مشكل فيأخذ
في الحال بأضر التقديرات إلى البيان كما في الحمل والمفقود

### | مسائله

إذا مات وخلف أخا لأب وولدا خنثى
فلا شئ للأخ لاحتمال أنه ابن للخنثى النصف في الحال لأنه أضر أحواله
ولو كانا ولدين خنثيين فلهما الثلثان في الحال لأنه الأضر والباقي موقوف
بينهما وبين الأخ إلى البيان والاصطلاح منهم على شئ
ولو كانوا ثلاثة خناثى يدفع إلى كل واحد خمس المال في  الحال لاحتمال أنه
أنثى وصاحباه ذكران ويوقف بين الخناثى ما بين ثلاثة أخماس إلى تمام الثلثين
لاحق فيه للأخ ويوقف الثلث الباقي بينهم وبين الأخ
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الخامس في حساب الفرائض - صلى الله عليه
وسلم -
وفيه فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be pierced or penetrated," hence "doubt" as that which penetrates certainty and renders it porous.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential theology, shakk denotes the absence of preponderant probability (rajāḥah) — a state where neither existence nor non-existence of a legal cause can be affirmed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to piercing a spear; metaphorical (majāz) usage denotes the penetration of uncertainty into a previously settled ruling.
- Root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To be true, established, obligatory" — the root denotes fixed reality that cannot be overturned.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istiḥqāq is the fixed entitlement that the Lawgiver attaches to a cause (sabab) once its conditions are verified.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah (literal truth) vs. majāz — here, entitlement is literal when the cause is certain, and suspended when doubt intervenes.
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To measure, determine, estimate" — the act of assigning a precise quantum.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqdīr in inheritance law is the juristic estimation of the most prejudicial scenario (aḍarr al-ḥālāt) to protect the rights of the absent or unknown.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used metaphorically for "judicial estimation" — not literal measurement but legal construction of a hypothetical state.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction with Taqdīr (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb bi-al-Taqdīr) — When a legal consequence depends on a hypothetical state (e.g., "as if he were dead"), the apodosis is governed by the estimated condition, not the actual unknown. This governs the entire section's method of suspending shares (tawaqquf) until clarification (bayān).
chapters.translation:
### | The Sixth Impediment: Doubt Concerning Entitlement

Its causes are four matters.

**The First: Uncertainty Regarding Existence**

This applies to the missing person (al-mafqūd) and the captive whose news has been cut off. No one inherits from him unless evidence (bayyinah) is established of his death, or unless a period elapses such that the judge rules that a person of his kind does not survive beyond that duration. The period is reckoned from the time of the missing person's birth, not from the time of his disappearance.

When the judge rules his death, his relatives who are present at the time of the ruling inherit from him — not those present at the time of his disappearance.

As for his inheritance from those present [among his kin]: if a relative of his dies [while he is missing], one must suspend (tawaqquf) his share. If the judge subsequently rules his death, then he is estimated as if he had not existed at the death of his relative, and the suspended [share] is diverted to the heirs present from the moment of the missing person's relative's death.

As for those present: if the missing person is of the kind who could conceivably block (ḥajb) the present heir, then nothing is paid to them. If he could conceivably block only some of them, then suspension applies to the extent of the probability, and only the certain portion (al-mustayqan) is paid to them. We adopt the worst scenario (aswaʾ al-ḥālāt) with respect to each individual.

Thus, if the deficiency lies in estimating life, we estimate life; if it lies in estimating death, we estimate death. For example: if a woman leaves a husband, two full sisters present, and a full brother missing — if the brother were dead, the husband takes half, the two sisters take two-thirds, and the case ʿawls (increases) from six to seven. If he were alive, the husband takes a non-ʿāʾil half, and the sisters take a quarter. So the husband is paid only three-sevenths of the estate — that being the ʿāʾil half — and we estimate the missing brother's death with respect to him, because that is the worst scenario. The sisters receive the quarter on the estimation of life, for that is the worst for them. The remainder is suspended until clarification.

Among our companions (aṣḥāb) there are those who say: estimate life with respect to each of them in the present; if the contrary becomes manifest, we alter the ruling. And among them are those who say: we adopt death, because the entitlement of these [present heirs] is certain (mustayqan); if the contrary appears, we alter the ruling. These two are opposing positions — for the latter is countered by the former's principle that the original presumption is the continuation of life (baqāʾ al-ḥayāh). The correct position is suspension when the matter is problematic (ishkāl).

**The Second Cause: Doubt Concerning Lineage (al-Nasab)**

This applies where recourse to the physiognomist (al-qāʾif) is needed. Its ruling during the period of uncertainty is the ruling of the missing person: we adopt the worst scenario with respect to all.

**The Third Cause: Doubt Due to Pregnancy (al-Ḥaml)**

The fetus inherits under two conditions:

First: that it emerges alive. If it emerges dead — even due to a criminal act (jināyah) — it is as if it had never existed at all.

Second: that it existed at the time of death — meaning it is delivered at less than six months from the time of death. If it is delivered after more than four years, it does not inherit. If between the two periods, it inherits, because lineage is established and inheritance follows lineage.

If the fetus emerges, cries out, then dies, it inherits. Likewise if it opens its eye, suckles the breast, and the signs of life are apparent. If it merely moves — if the movement is of the kind of twitching (ikhtilāj) or contraction of nerve and muscle, it has no effect. If it is voluntary — like clenching and unclenching the fingers — it is evidence of life. If it is ambiguous between the two kinds, there are two positions (qawlān): one, it does not inherit for lack of certainty; the second, it inherits, relying on the preponderant conjecture (ghālib al-ẓann) based on the sign.

If half of the fetus emerges, cries out, then dies and is [fully] delivered, there are two plausible positions (wajhān muḥtamilān).

This [ruling] applies after delivery. As for before delivery, that is the period of uncertainty: we estimate the most harmful state (aḍarr al-ḥālāt) upon the remaining heirs. The maximum possible estimation is four offspring in the womb, with femininity and masculinity both possible — so we estimate what is most harmful in every case. Example: a man dies leaving a pregnant wife and a [paternal] brother. The brother receives nothing in the present, because it is possible the fetus is male and blocks him.

If he leaves two parents and a pregnant wife: each of the parents is given the sixth, with ʿawl from twenty-four to twenty-seven, because it is possible the fetus is two daughters. The case is [constructed] from twenty-four to twenty-seven: the mother gets four, the father four, the wife three, and each of the two daughters eight. This is the most harmful estimation, so we estimate it in the present.

If it is said: "Are those present empowered over what has been paid to them?" We say: al-Qaffāl said no — for division (qismah) concerning a fetus is not valid except through the judge, and the judge has no authority to dispose of the property of fetuses, unlike absent persons. The correct position is that they are empowered, and the judge must undertake the division on their behalf, so that rights are not rendered void.

If it is said: "If the woman claims pregnancy, she might be obstinate — how can we wait four years on her word?" We say: if signs of pregnancy appear, or she is recently close to intercourse that could plausibly have conceived, then suspension is obligatory. If no such signs appear, the matter is probable, and the preferred course is to rely on her — for she is most knowledgeable of hidden signs, and she is entrusted (muʾtamanah) concerning her womb.

### | The Fourth Cause: Hermaphroditism (al-Khunūthah)

The hermaphrodite (al-khunthā) is one whose masculinity and femininity are problematic (mushkil).

Some scholars said: he does not inherit, for he is neither male nor female, and the Book contains only the inheritance of males and females. It was also said: he takes half the male's share and half the female's share.

But the madhhab of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — is that he is either male or female, but it is problematic [which]. So in the present he takes the most harmful of the two estimations, until clarification — just as in the case of the fetus and the missing person.

### | Its Subsidiary Cases (Masāʾiluhu)

If a man dies leaving a paternal brother and one hermaphrodite child: the brother gets nothing, because it is possible the hermaphrodite is a son. The hermaphrodite takes half in the present, for that is the most harmful of his states.

If there are two hermaphrodite children: they take two-thirds in the present, for that is the most harmful, and the remainder is suspended between them and the brother until clarification and their agreement upon something.

If there are three hermaphrodites: each is paid one-fifth of the estate in the present, because it is possible he is female while his two companions are male. Suspended among the hermaphrodites is [the amount] between three-fifths and the completion of two-thirds — in which the brother has no share — and the remaining third is suspended between them and the brother.

— Peace be upon him — The Fifth Chapter: On the Computation of Inheritary Shares (Ḥisāb al-Farāʾiḍ) — Peace be upon him —

It contains sections.
