- Root: ك-ف-ن (k-f-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wrapping, enshrouding; the garment in which the dead is wrapped.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Material provision for the deceased’s burial; ownership transfer (tamlīk) vs. mere usufruct (manfaʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical shroud; metaphorical: provision of dignity for the deceased.
- Root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Command, injunction; bequest (waṣiyyah) as a posthumous directive.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal disposition of property effective after death; requires capacity and valid recipient.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: verbal command; juristic: transfer of ownership (tamlīk) contingent on death.
- Root: ح-ر-ب (ḥ-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: War, combat; ḥarbī = one belonging to the abode of war (dār al-ḥarb).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hostile status affecting legal capacity for inheritance and bequest.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: warfare; juristic: enemy alien with no pact (ʿahd) or amnesty (amān).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (law qāla) governs the apodosis (fa-huwa bāṭil), requiring precise parsing of hypothetical legal utterances.
chapters.translation:
I say: There are two subsidiary questions.

The first: If a man says, “Take this garment and shroud your deceased relative with it,” al-Qaffāl held that the heir may replace it with another, based on the principle that the shroud belongs to the owner [of the garment], and the attribution to the deceased is a transfer of ownership (tamlīk) to him. This is more remote than what he mentioned regarding the beast of burden, and that too is remote. Rather, the correct view here is that this constitutes a loan (ʿāriyah) with respect to the deceased.

The second: If a man says, “I have endowed (waqaftu) upon the mosque” or “I have bequeathed (awṣaytu) to the mosque,” and then says, “I intended to transfer ownership to the mosque,” this is invalid (bāṭil). But if he says, “I intended to direct it to its maintenance and benefit (maṣlaḥah),” it is valid. If he leaves it unqualified (muṭlaq), Shaykh Abū ʿAlī said it is invalid, because the mosque cannot own property, like the beast. However, this is remote regarding the mosque, because custom (ʿurf) interprets the unqualified expression as directing the usufruct to its maintenance.

As for the ḥarbī (enemy combatant), a bequest to him is valid, just as a sale from him and a gift to him are valid. Likewise, the apostate (murtadd) and the dhimmī.

The author of al-Talkhīṣ transmitted from the text (naṣṣ) of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — the invalidity of a bequest to the ḥarbī, and he justified it by the severance of alliance (inqiṭāʿ al-muwālāh). This is weak, for there is no meaning to requiring alliance in bequest, even if it is considered in inheritance.

If a Muslim or a dhimmī bequeaths to the weapons of the people of war, or to a church (bīʿah), or to a synagogue (kanīsah), it is corrupt (fāsid), because that is disobedience (maʿṣiyah). This differs from a bequest to a specific ḥarbī, for a gift from him is not disobedience.

As for the killer [of the testator], there are three opinions regarding the bequest to him:

The first: Prohibition (manʿ), by analogy with inheritance — for since he disobeyed by seeking the cause [of death], he is punished by the opposite of his intent, and its fruit is cut off from him; and the bequest is likewise a fruit of death.

The second: Validity (ṣiḥḥah), because the cause is the transfer of ownership (tamlīk), not death itself, and it is his own choice. Thus it resembles the case of the umm walad (slave-mother) who kills her master, or the creditor who kills his debtor — for she is freed, since her freedom is by her choice of istīlād (bearing her master’s child).

The third: If he bequeathed first and then killed, the bequest is cut off, because he hastened [the death]. But if [the testator] died [naturally] and then he bequeathed to him, it is permissible.

As for the mudabbar (slave whose freedom is deferred to master’s death) who kills his master: If we say that tadbīr is a bequest, then it follows the [three] opinions. If we say it is a suspension (taʿlīq) of freeing half of him, then likening him to the umm walad is more appropriate.

If we say the bequest to the killer is invalid, is it executed by the heirs’ ratification (ijāzah)? There is a dispute, as in the ratification of a bequest to an heir.

If one bequeaths to the slave of the killer, it is as if he bequeathed to the slave of the heir. If he bequeaths to a slave who is himself the killer, it is valid, because the locus of ownership is other than him.

As for the fetus (ḥaml), a bequest to it is valid under two conditions:

The first: That it emerges alive — for if it emerges dead, even due to another’s aggression, it does not deserve [the bequest], since we grant it the status of the living only because of the expectation of its coming to life.

The second: That it exists at the time of the bequest — namely, that it emerges within less than six months from the time of the bequest. If it emerges after more than four years, it does not deserve it. If the period is between these two, there is consideration: If the woman has a husband who has intercourse with her, it does not deserve it, because the supervention [of pregnancy] is apparent. If she has no husband, there are two aspects. The aspect of deserving is that estimating intercourse by doubtful circumstances (shubhah) is remote, and fornication (zinā) we do not estimate, thinking well of the Muslim.

If one explicitly bequeaths to a fetus that will come into existence [in the future], the apparent view is prohibition, because there is no object of entitlement at present. The Iraqis decisively held this, unlike the bequest to an existing fetus. Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī said it is permissible, like the bequest to an expected fetus. This is supported by the permissibility of endowment (waqf) upon the child’s child.

As for the heir, a bequest to him is invalid, due to his saying — peace be upon him: {«لَا وَصِيَّةَ لِوَارِثٍ»} (“No bequest to an heir”). We mean this when the rest of the heirs reject it. If they ratify it, and we hold that the heirs’ ratification is execution (tanfīdh) and not an initiating gift (ibtidāʾ ʿaṭiyyah), then there are two opinions on the validity of this bequest by ratification — and likewise the bequest to the killer. One: No, due to the absolute prohibition. The second: It is executed, and the prohibition is interpreted as applying to [cases] contrary to the heirs’ intent. Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that he — peace be upon him — said: {«لَا تَجُوزُ لِوَارِثٍ وَصِيَّةٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ الْوَرَثَةُ»} (“A bequest to an heir is not permissible unless the heirs so wish”).

chapters.title_en: Six Subsidiary Branches and the Third Pillar: The Bequeathed Object
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع ستة

الأول إذا أوصى لكل واحد بمقدار حصته فهو لغو لا فائدة لا
فأما إذا خصصه بعين على مقدار حصته ففي الحاجة إلى الإجازة وجهان
أحدهما لا إذ لا وصية بزيادة مال
والثاني وهو الأصح أنه يحتاج لأن في أعيان الأموال أغراضا
وكذلك لو أوصى بأن  تباع داره من إنسان تنفذ عندنا وصيته خلافا لأبي حنيفة
رحمه الله
الثاني إذا وقف على كل واحد قدر حصته
فإن قلنا الوصية للوارث أصلا باطل ولا يتأثر بالإجازة فأصل الوقف باطل
وإن قلنا ينفذ بالإجازة فله أن يرد بقدر الزائد على الثلث وليس له إبطال
الثلث فإنه لم يخصص بعض الورثة به
ومن وقف عليه لا يمكنه أن يرد نصيب نفسه فيقول خصصني فإن التخصيص يستدعي
تعددا
ويظهر فهم هذا إذا كان الوارث واحدا فليقس عليه العدد أيضا
الثالث إذا أوصى بالثلث لأجنبي ووارث فرد ما للوارث فللأجنبي سدس المال
لأنه أوصى لهما على صيغة التشريك
بخلاف ما إذا أوصى للوارث بالثلث ثم أوصى للأجنبي بالثلث فإنه إن رد ما
للوارث سلم الثلث للأجنبي
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يسلم الثلث للأجنبي في الصورتين
الرابع أوصى للأجنبي بالثلث ولكل واحد من ابنيه بالثلث فرد ما لابنه
سلم الثلث للأجنبي إذ لا مدخل لإجازة الورثة في قدر الثلث
وعن القفال وجه أنه يسلم للأجنبي ثلث الثلث لأن ثلثه شائع في الأثلاث وهو
مزيف
الخامس لو أوصى للأجنبي بالثلث ولبعض الورثة بالكل وأجبزت الوصايا
فللأجنبي الثلث كاملا لا يزاحمه الوارث والثلثان للوارث الموصى به هكذا حكي
عن ابن سريج
ولا يبعد أن يقال إن الوارث يزاحم في الثلث بكونه موصى له لا بكونه
وارثا كما لو أوصى لأجنبي بالكل ولأجنبي آخر بالثلث إذ لا يسلم الثلث
لصاحب الثلث بل يزاحمه فيه
السادس أوصى لأجنبي بالنصف ولأحد ابنيه بالنصف وأجيز الكل
سئل القفال عنه ببخارى فأجاب بأن الأجنبي يفوز بالنصف والابن بالنصف فنقل
له عن ابن سريج أن للأجنبي النصف وللابن الموصى له ربعا وسدسا يبقى نصف سدس
للابن الذى ليس بموصى له قال القفال فتأملت حتى خرجت وجهه بالبناء على
الوجهين في مسألة وهي أنه لو أوصى لأحد ابنيه بالنصف وأجيز شاطر في النصف
الثاني لأنه التركة
ولو أوصى له بالثلثين فهل يشاطر في الثلث الباقي وجهان
أحدهما نعم كالصورة الأولى  لأن ما أخذ بالوصية كأنه لم يكن والتركة هو
الباقي فكان كما لو أوصى بالثلثين لأجنبي وأجيز
والثاني لا لأن المفهوم من الوصية له بالثلثين التخصيص له بالسدس الزائد
على النصف الذى هو قدر حقه فكأنه قال لا تنازعوه في ثلثي الدار ليكون له
النصف بالإرث والباقي بالوصية
فعلى هذا يستقيم مذهب ابن سريج فإن الأجنبي الموصى له بالنصف سلم له
الثلث من رأس المال من غير حاجة إلى إجازة
بقي الثلثان التوريث يقتضي للابن الموصى له الثلث وقد أوصى له بالنصف
فخصص بمزيد فانقطع حقه عن السدس الباقي وبقي السدس خالصا للابن الذى لم
يوص له
إلا أن الأجنبي بعد يطلب سدسا وقد أجازاه فيكون نصيب الابن الذى لم يوص
له في ذلك إجازة نصف السدس فيأخذ منه نصف سدسه من هذا السدس ويبقى له نصف
سدس ويأخذ النصف الآخر من نصيب الابن الموصى له فيكمل له النصف وينقص نصيب
الموصى له بنصف سدس
وإن فرعنا على أنه يشاطر الموصى له في الباقي فالباقي سدس مشترك بين
الابنين وقد أجازاه للأجنبي فيصح منه جواب القفال

### | الركن الثالث في الموصى به

ولا يشترط فيه أن يكون مالا فيصح الوصية بالزبل والكلب والخمر المحرمة
ولا كونه معلوما فيصح الوصية بالمجهول
ولا كونه مقدورا على تسليمه فيصح الوصية بالآبق والمغصوب والحمل وهو
مجهول وغير مقدور عليه
ولا كونه معينا فتصح الوصية بأحد العبدين والأظهر أنه لا يصح الوصية لأحد
الشخصين فلا يحتمل ذلك في الموصى له وإن احتمل في الموصى به وقد ذكرناه
نظيره في الوقف
نعم يشترط أربعة أمور
الأول أن يكون موجودا فإن كان مفقودا كالمنافع جازت الوصية لأنها
كالموجود شرعا في المعاوضة
وفي الوصية بالحمل الذى سيوجد وجهان مشهوران
أحدهما المنع إذ لا متعلق للوصية فكان كالوصية للحمل الذى سيكون فإنه
ممنوع على الأظهر
والثاني الجواز كما في المنافع
وفي الثمار الذى ستحدث طريقان
منهم من ألحق بالمنافع لتكرر وجودها في العادة
ومنهم من ألحقها بالحمل الثاني أن يكون  مخصوصا بالموصي
فلو أوصى بمال الغير فسد وإن ملكه بعد ذلك لبطلان الإضافة في الحال
الثالث أن يكون منتفعا به
فلا تجوز الوصية بالكلب الذى لا ينتفع به ولا بالخمر المستحقة الإراقة
التى اتخذت للخمرية
وتصح الوصية بالجرو إذ مصيره إلى الانتفاع
وفي هبة الكلب وجهان
أحدهما الجواز كالوصية وكأن المحرم أخذ ثمنه لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
الكلب خبيث وخبيث ثمنه
والثاني المنع لأن الوصية في حكم خلافه يضاهى الإرث بخلاف الهبة
نعم يجرى الإرث في حد القذف والقصاص دون الوصية لأنه لا ينتفع الموصى له

chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ص-ص (kha-ṣād-ṣād)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To single out, to distinguish, to allocate exclusively to a particular one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Designation (takhṣīṣ) as a legal act of specifying a beneficiary or object, distinct from general inclusion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in legal stipulation; metaphorically, any act of preference that implies multiplicity of parties.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Coordination (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis (in) governs the apodosis (fa-), requiring careful parsing of legal consequences from hypothetical premises.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first branch: If one bequeaths to each [heir] an amount equal to his [inheritance] share, it is nugatory (laghw), having no benefit.

But if he designates (khaṣṣaṣa) a specific chattel to him to the extent of his share, then there are two views (wajhān) concerning the need for ratification (ijāzah):
One: No need, for there is no bequest of excess wealth.
The second — and it is the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) — that he does need [ratification], because in the specific chattels of wealth there are particular purposes (aghrāḍ).

Likewise, if he bequeaths that his house be sold to a certain person, his bequest is executed in our [school], contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him.

The second branch: If he makes an endowment (waqf) upon each one to the extent of his share:
If we say that the bequest to an heir is void in principle (aṣlan) and is not affected by ratification, then the foundation of the endowment is void.
But if we say it is executed by ratification, then he may reject (yarudda) to the extent of the excess over the third, and he may not annul the third — for he did not designate some heirs over others with it.
And the one upon whom the endowment is made cannot reject his own portion, saying, "He designated me" — for designation (takhṣīṣ) requires multiplicity.
The understanding of this becomes apparent when the heir is one; then analogize the number to it as well.

The third branch: If he bequeaths the third to a stranger (ajnabī) and to an heir, rejecting what is for the heir — then the stranger receives a sixth of the estate, because he bequeathed to both of them in the form of partnership (ṣīghat al-tashrīk).
Contrary to the case where he bequeaths the third to the heir, then bequeaths the third to the stranger — for if [the heir] rejects what is for the heir, the third is secured for the stranger.
Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: The third is secured for the stranger in both cases.

The fourth branch: He bequeaths the third to a stranger and to each of his two sons the third; [the son] rejects what is for his son — the third is secured for the stranger, for the ratification of the heirs has no entry into the extent of the third.
From al-Qaffāl there is a view that a third of the third is secured for the stranger, because his third is diffused (shāʾiʿ) among the thirds — and this is weak (muzayyaf).

The fifth branch: If he bequeaths the third to a stranger and to some heir the whole, and the bequests are ratified — then the stranger receives the full third, the heir not competing with him therein, and the two-thirds go to the heir bequeathed to. Thus it is related from Ibn Surayj.
And it is not far-fetched to say that the heir competes in the third by virtue of being a legatee, not by virtue of being an heir — just as if he bequeathed the whole to a stranger and the third to another stranger, for the third is not secured to its owner but he competes with him therein.

The sixth branch: He bequeaths the half to a stranger and the half to one of his two sons, and the whole is ratified.
Al-Qaffāl was asked about it in Bukhārā and answered that the stranger wins the half and the son the half. Then it was transmitted to him from Ibn Surayj that the stranger gets the half, and the son bequeathed to gets a quarter and a sixth, leaving half a sixth for the son who was not bequeathed to. Al-Qaffāl said: I pondered until I extracted its rationale by building upon the two views in a certain question — namely, that if he bequeaths the half to one of his two sons and it is ratified, he shares (yushāṭiru) in the second half, because it is the estate.
And if he bequeaths to him the two-thirds, does he share in the remaining third? Two views:
One: Yes, like the first case — because what he takes by bequest is as if it were not, and the estate is what remains; so it is as if he bequeathed the two-thirds to a stranger and it was ratified.
The second: No — because the understood meaning of bequeathing the two-thirds to him is his designation (takhṣīṣ) with the extra sixth beyond the half, which is the extent of his right. It is as if he said: "Do not contest him over two-thirds of the house," so that he has the half by inheritance and the remainder by bequest.
Upon this, the doctrine of Ibn Surayj becomes sound — for the stranger bequeathed the half: the third is secured to him from the capital (raʾs al-māl) without need for ratification.
There remains the two-thirds: inheritance requires for the son bequeathed to the third, and he was bequeathed the half, so he is designated with an increase; thus his right is cut off from the remaining sixth, and the sixth remains pure for the son who was not bequeathed to.
Except that the stranger then seeks a sixth, and both have ratified it — so the portion of the son not bequeathed to in that [sixth] is ratification of half the sixth. He takes from it half his sixth, and there remains for him half a sixth; and the other half is taken from the portion of the son bequeathed to, completing the [stranger's] half, while the portion of the bequeathed-to son is diminished by half a sixth.
And if we branch upon [the view] that he shares with the bequeathed-to [son] in the remainder — then the remainder is a sixth shared between the two sons, and they have ratified it for the stranger; thus al-Qaffāl's answer is sound.

### The Third Pillar: The Bequeathed Object

It is not required therein that it be wealth (māl), so the bequest of dung, a dog, and prohibited wine is valid.
Nor that it be known (maʿlūm), so the bequest of an unknown thing is valid.
Nor that it be within capacity to deliver, so the bequest of a runaway slave, a usurped object, and a fetus — which is unknown and not within capacity — is valid.
Nor that it be specified (muʿayyan), so the bequest of one of two slaves is valid. But the more apparent (al-aẓhar) is that the bequest to one of two persons is not valid — for that is not tolerated in the legatee, though it is tolerated in the bequeathed object; we have mentioned its analogue in the endowment.

Yes, four matters are required:
The first: That it exist. If it is non-existent (mafqūd), like usufructs (manāfiʿ), the bequest is permissible — because it is, legally, like the existent in commutative contracts (muʿāwaḍah).
Concerning the bequest of a fetus that will come into being, there are two well-known views:
One: Prohibition — for there is no object for the bequest, so it is like the bequest to a fetus that will be, which is prohibited on the more apparent view.
The second: Permissibility, as in usufructs.
Concerning fruits that will come into being, there are two paths:
Among them, one who likens them to usufructs due to their recurrent existence by custom.
And among them, one who likens them to the fetus.

The second: That it be specifically owned by the testator (makhṣūṣan bi-l-mūṣī). If he bequeaths the property of another, it is void — even if he owns it afterward — because the attribution (iḍāfah) is nullified at the moment [of the bequest].

The third: That it be of benefit (muntafaʿan bihi). Thus the bequest of a dog from which no benefit is derived is not permissible, nor of wine deserving to be poured out that was made for wine-ness.
But the bequest of a puppy is valid, for its end is benefit.
Concerning the gift (hibah) of a dog, there are two views:
One: Permissibility, like the bequest — as if what is prohibited is taking its price, due to his saying — peace be upon him: {«الكلب خبيث وخبيث ثمنه»} "The dog is impure, and impure is its price."
The second: Prohibition — because the bequest, in its ruling, resembles inheritance (irth), unlike the gift.
Yes, inheritance applies in the limits of slander (qadhf) and retaliation (qiṣāṣ), but not the bequest — because the legatee derives no benefit from it.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع

الأول من لا كلب له إذا أوصى بكلب لا يصح لأنا نحتاج إلى شرائه وهو غير
ممكن
وإن كان له كلاب ففي كيفية خروجه من الثلث خلاف
قال الشيخ أبو علي إن ملك شيئا آخر ولو دانقا يصح الوصية لأنه خير من كل
الكلاب إذ لا قيمة للكلب
وقال العراقيون لا ينفذ إلا في ثلث الكلاب وكأنه كل ماله إذ لا يمكن
نسبته
إلى سائر الأموال
ثم إذا لم يكن له إلا كلاب وأوصى بالكلب فثلاثة أوجه
أحدها أنه ينظر إلى العدد فإن ملك ثلاثة كلاب نفذت وصيته بواحدة
ومنهم من قدر قيمة الكلب
ومنه من قدر الثلث بتقدير المنفعة فإنه منتفع به
وإذا كان له خمر وكلب وطبل لهو فأوصى بواحد فلا يمكن إلا تقدير القيمة إذ
لا مناسبة في العدد والمنفعة
الثاني إذا أوصى بطبل لهو وكان يصلح للحرب بأدنى تغيير مع بقاء اسم الطبل
صحت الوصية
ولو كان لا ينتفع به إلا برضاضه لا يصح لأنه لا يقصد منه الرضاض إلا إذا
كان من ذهب أو عود أو شئ نفيس فيصح لأنه المقصود
ولو قال أوصيت برضاض هذا الطبل صح وتقديره أنه له بعد الكسر
والوصية تقبل التعليق بخلاف البيع

### | الشرط الرابع أن لا يكون الموصى به زائدا على الثلث لقصة سعد

فإن زاد على الثلث ولم يكن له وارث فالوصية بالزيادة باطلة خلافا لأبي
حنيفة رحمه الله  لأن الزيادة للمسلمين ولا مجيز له
نعم لو رأى القاضي مصلحة في تلك الجهة جاز له تقريرها فيها
وإن كان له وارث ففي بطلان الوصية من أصلها قولان كما في أصل الوصية
للوارث
فإن قلنا إنها باطلة فالإجازة إن فرضت فهي ابتداء عطية تفتقر إلى القبض
والقبول
وهل ينفذ بلفظ الإجازة فيه وجهان
أحدهما لا لأنه ينبني على تقرير ما سبق ولا ثبات لما سبق
والثاني أنه يصح ومعناه تقرير مقصود ما سبق بإثبات مثله
وعلى هذا إذا كان الوصية عتقا كان الولاء للوارث
وإن قلنا إنها صحيحة فالإجازة يتقيد والولاء للمورث
وكل تبرع منجز في مرض الموت فهو أيضا محسوب من الثلث
وكذا إذا وهب في الصحة ولكن أقبض في المرض
وهذا يستدعي بيان ثلاثة أمور الأول مرض الموت
وهو كل مرض مخوف يستعد الإنسان بسببه لما بعد الموت كالطاعون والقولنج
وذات الجنب والرعاف الدائم والإسهال المتواتر وقيام الدم والسل في انتهائه
والفالج الحادث في ابتدائه والحمى المطبقة لأن هذه الأمراض يظهر معها خوف
الموت
أما السل في ابتدائه والفالج في انتهائه والجرب ووجع الضرس والصداع
اليسير وحمى يوم ويومين فكل ذلك ليس بمخوف
فإذا هجم المرض المخوف حجرنا عليه في التصرف فيما يزيد على الثلث وتوقفنا
في تبرعاته
فإن زال نفذناه وتبينا صحته
وإن كان غير مخوف كوجع الضرس وآخر الفالج فالتصرف نافذ
وإن مات عند ذلك فجأة أو بسب آخر لا بذلك السبب فلا يمتنع به التبرعات
المنجزة
فأما حمى يوم ويومين وإسهال يوم ويومين فهو إذا دام صار مخوفا وابتداؤه
مشكل فلا يحجر عليه فإن دام ومات تبينا فساد التصرف إذ بان أن الأول كان
مخوفا
وما أشكل من ذلك يتعرف من طبيبين مسلمين لا من أهل الذمة
فأما إذا كان في الصف وقد التحم الفريقان أو كان في البحر وقد تموج أو في
أسر كفار عادتهم قتل الأسارى أو قدم للقتل في قطع الطريق أو الرجم للزنا أو
ظهر الطاعون في بلد ولكن بعد لم  يظهر في بدنه شئ ففي تبرعه في هذه الأحوال
قولان
أحدهما أنه كالمريض المخوف لأنه سبب ظاهر في الاستعداد لما بعد الموت
والثاني أنه كالصحيح إذ لا يمس بدنه شئ ولا ضبط لما قبل تغير البدن
للأسباب
أما إذا قدم للقصاص فالمنصوص أنه لا تعتبر عطيته من الثلث ما لم يخرج
وقال أبو إسحاق المروزي هو كالأسير وقع في يد قوم عادتهم القتل
وفهم من فرق بأن المسلم الغالب عليه الرحمة والعفو في القصاص
وأما الحامل فليس بمخوف قبل أن يضربها الطلق فإن ضربها الطلق فهو مخوف
ومنهم من قال لا لأن السلامة منه أكثر الأمر الثاني حد التبرع
وهو إزالة الملك عن مال مجانا من غير وجوب
فالعتق والصدقات تبرع
والزكاة والكفارة الواجبة والحج الواجب ليس بتبرع فما أوصى به لها فهو من
رأس المال
وكذا قضاء الديون لأن ذلك يستند إلى وجوب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ص-ي (waṣā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To connect, join, or entrust; a bequest (waṣiyyah) as a covenant of conveyance posthumously.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A legal dispensation (tasarruf) effective after death, contingent upon the testator's intent and the third-limit constraint.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in property transfer; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to mere permission, as in "bequeathing" a benefit.
- Root: ث-ل-ث (thulth)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: One-third; a fractional share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legally fixed maximum for voluntary dispositions (tabarruʿāt) in terminal illness, rooted in the ḥadīth of Saʿd.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal numerical fraction; metaphorically, the boundary of permissible generosity beyond heirs' claims.
- Root: خ-و-ف (khawf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fear, apprehension of harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The criterion for terminal illness (marad al-mawt)—a subjective state of dread regarding death, objectively assessed by physicians.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in bodily symptoms; metaphorical in external perils (battle, sea, captivity) that induce the same legal status.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The permissibility of taʿlīq (suspension) in bequests versus its prohibition in sales, parsed as a conditional nexus where the bequest's validity hinges on a future event (death), unlike sales which require immediate execution.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now I shall expound the branches (furūʿ) arising from the preceding principles.

**The First Branch:** Concerning one who owns no dog—if he bequeaths a dog, the bequest is invalid, because we would need to purchase it [to fulfill the bequest], and that is impossible [since the testator did not own it].

If he owns dogs, then there is a divergence of opinion regarding how the bequest exits from the third (al-thulth).

Shaykh Abū ʿAlī said: If he owns something else, even a single dāniq (a small coin), the bequest is valid, because that [other property] is better than all the dogs, since a dog has no legal value (qīmah).

The Iraqis said: It does not execute except within the third of the dogs, as if the dogs were his entire wealth, since it is impossible to attribute [the bequest's value] to other properties.

Then, if he owns nothing but dogs and bequeaths one dog, there are three aspects (awjuh):
- One: That one looks to the number—if he owns three dogs, his bequest of one executes.
- Among them is one who estimated the dog's value.
- Among them is one who estimated the third by estimating the utility (manfaʿah), for the dog is useful [for hunting, guarding, etc.].

If he owns wine, a dog, and a drum of frivolity (ṭabl lahw), and he bequeaths one of them, then estimation is only possible by value, since there is no proportionality in number or utility.

**The Second Branch:** If he bequeaths a drum of frivolity, and it could be adapted for warfare with the slightest alteration while retaining the name "drum," the bequest is valid.

If it could not be used except for its broken fragments (ruḍāḍ), the bequest is invalid, because the fragments are not the intended object—unless it is made of gold, aloeswood, or something precious, in which case the bequest is valid, because the fragments are the intended purpose.

If he says, "I bequeath the fragments of this drum," it is valid, and its estimation is that it belongs to him after the breaking. And a bequest accepts suspension (taʿlīq), unlike a sale.

**The Fourth Condition:** That the bequeathed object not exceed the third, due to the story of Saʿd.

If it exceeds the third and he has no heir, then the bequest of the excess is void, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him), because the excess belongs to the Muslims [as public treasury], and there is no one to ratify it (mujīz).

Yes, if the judge sees a public interest (maṣlaḥah) in that particular direction [of the bequest], he may permit its allocation there.

If he has an heir, then there are two opinions (qawlān) on whether the bequest is void from its very origin, just as in the case of a bequest to an heir.

If we say it is void, then ratification (ijāzah), if assumed, constitutes a new gift (ʿaṭiyyah) that requires delivery (qabḍ) and acceptance (qabūl).

Does it execute by the mere utterance of ratification? There are two aspects:
- One: No, because it is built upon confirming what preceded, and there is no subsistence for what preceded.
- The second: Yes, it is valid, and its meaning is the confirmation of the intended purpose of what preceded by establishing its equivalent.

Upon this [second view], if the bequest was manumission (ʿitq), the clientage (walāʾ) belongs to the heir.

If we say it is valid [from the origin], then ratification is restricted [to the excess], and the clientage belongs to the testator [i.e., his estate].

Every gratuitous disposition (tabarruʿ) executed (munajjaz) during terminal illness is also counted from the third.

Likewise, if one gifts in health but delivers possession during illness, [it is counted from the third].

This necessitates the exposition of three matters:

**The First Matter: Terminal Illness (marad al-mawt).**
It is every illness that inspires fear (mukhīf), due to which a person prepares for what comes after death—such as plague (ṭāʿūn), colic (qawlanj), pleurisy (dhāt al-janb), persistent nosebleed (ruʿāf dāʾim), recurrent diarrhea (ishāl mutawātir), the rising of blood [hemorrhage], consumption (sill) at its final stage, sudden paralysis (fālij) at its onset, and continuous fever (ḥummā muṭbiqah)—because with these illnesses, the fear of death becomes manifest.

As for consumption at its onset, paralysis at its end, scabies (jarb), toothache (wajaʿ al-ḍirs), mild headache (ṣudāʿ yasīr), and a fever of one or two days—all of these are not fear-inspiring.

When a fear-inspiring illness strikes, we place him under legal interdiction (ḥajarnā ʿalayhi) regarding dispositions exceeding the third, and we suspend (tawaqqafnā) his gratuitous acts.

If the illness ceases, we execute them and it becomes evident they were valid.

If it is not fear-inspiring—like toothache or the final stage of paralysis—then his disposition is executed.

If he dies suddenly from that [non-fear-inspiring cause] or from another cause, not from that [fear-inspiring] cause, then his executed gratuitous acts are not impeded.

As for a fever of one or two days, or diarrhea of one or two days—if it persists, it becomes fear-inspiring, but its onset is ambiguous (mushkil), so he is not placed under interdiction. If it persists and he dies, then the corruption of his disposition becomes evident, because it is clear that the initial [state] was fear-inspiring.

What is ambiguous in this is ascertained by two Muslim physicians, not from the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimmah).

As for one who is in battle with the two ranks locked in combat, or at sea with waves surging, or in the captivity of disbelievers whose custom is to kill prisoners, or brought forth for execution on the highway (qaṭʿ al-ṭarīq), or for stoning due to adultery (rajm li-l-zinā), or plague has appeared in his city but nothing has yet manifested in his body—regarding his gratuitous disposition in these situations, there are two opinions:
- One: He is like the fear-inspiring patient, because it is a manifest cause for preparing for what comes after death.
- The second: He is like the healthy person, since nothing touches his body, and there is no control over what precedes bodily change due to these causes.

As for one brought forth for retribution (qiṣāṣ), the text (manṣūṣ) states that his gift is not counted from the third unless he is released. Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī said: He is like a captive fallen into the hands of a people whose custom is killing. And it is understood from the distinction that the Muslim [executioner] is predominantly characterized by mercy and pardon in retribution.

As for a pregnant woman, she is not fear-inspiring before labor pains strike her. If labor pains strike her, then she is fear-inspiring. Among them is one who said: No, because safety from it is more prevalent.

**The Second Matter: The Limit of Gratuitous Disposition (ḥadd al-tabarruʿ).**
It is the removal of ownership from wealth gratuitously, without any obligation (wujūb).

Thus, manumission and charities (ṣadaqāt) are gratuitous.

The obligatory alms (zakāh), obligatory expiation (kaffārah), and obligatory pilgrimage (ḥajj) are not gratuitous. Whatever one bequeaths for these is from the capital (raʾs al-māl).

Likewise, the settlement of debts, because these are grounded in obligation.

chapters.title_en: Two Subsidiary Issues and the Manner of Accounting from the Third
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرعان

أحدهما إذا باع بثمن المثل نفذ وإن كان من الوارث
وكذلك إذا قضى دين بعض الغرماء لم يكن للباقي المنع
وخالف أبو حنيفة رحمه الله فيه وفي البيع من الوارث
أما إذا كان في البيع محاباة فقدر المحاباة حكمه حكم التبرعات
وكذلك إذا نكح امرأة بأكثر من مهر المثل فالزيادة تبرع محسوب من الثلث
الثاني إذا نكحت المرأة بأقل من مهر المثل لم يحسب من الثلث لأنها لم
تنزل إلا عن البضع والبضع ليس بمال لو أجر عبيده ودوابه مع المحاباة فهو
تبرع لأنه مال
ولو أجر نفسه وحابى فيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه تبرع كمنافع العبيد فإن منفعته مال
والثاني لا لأنه لا يعد مالا يطمع فيه الوارث فيشبه بضع المرأة من هذا
الوجه وكان ذلك يعد امتناعا عن الاكتساب لا تفويتا الأمر الثالث في كيفية
الاحتساب من الثلث
ووجهه أنه إن كانت التبرعات كلها منجزة في المرض فيقدم الأول فالأول
فإن كان الأول هبة والثاني عتقا قدمت الهبة لأنه استوفى الثلث بها فسقط
العتق بعده
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله إنهما يتساويان إذ لهذا  قوة العتق ولذاك قوة
التقدم
أما إذا كانت متساوية فإن كان الكل هبة ومحاباة فتوزع عليهم الثلث على
نسبة أقدارها
وإن كان الكل عتقا أقرع بين العبيد ولم يوزع حذارا من التشقيص بخلاف
الهبة ولما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرع بين ستة أعبد أعنقهم مريض
وجزاهم ثلاثة أجزاء فأرق أربعا وأعتق اثنين
وإن اجتمع الهبة والعتق في حالة واحدة بقول وكيل أو بإضافة الكل إلى ما
بعد الموت ففي تقديم العتق قولان
أحدهما لا للتساوي في وقت الاستحقاق
والثاني نعم لأن العتق يزحم ملك الغير بالسراية
وفي إلحاق الكتابة بالعتق في استحقاق تقديمها على المحاباة خلاف
أما إذا أضيف الكل إلى ما بعد الموت فلا ينظر إلى ما تقدم في بعض الوصايا
لأن وقت اللزوم واحد في الكل وإنما يبقى النظر في تقديم العتق على غيره
ولو أوصى بعتق عبد وعلق عتق آخر على الموت فلا تقديم لأحدهما بحال

### | فروع

الأول إذا كان له عبدان غانم وسالم فقال لغانم إن أعتقتك فسالم حر ثم
أعتق غانما والثلث لا يفي إلا بأحدهما يعتق غانم ولا يقرع بينهما إذ ربما
تخرج القرعة على سالم فيؤدي إلى أن يعتق دون عتق عانم ويكون ذلك تحصيلا
للمسبب دون السبب وهو محال
أما إذا كان له سوى غانم عبدان فعلق عتقهما بعتق غانم ووفى الثلث بغانم
وبأحدهما عتق غانم وأقرع بينهما فمن خرجت قرعته عتق
الثاني إذا ملك جارية حاملا ومجموع ماله ثلثمائة والولد من الجملة مائة
والأم خمسون
فقال إن أعتقت نصف الحمل فالأم حرة ثم أعتق نصف الحمل عتق
خمسون وبقي لنا خمسون إلى تمام الثلث مردد بين النصف الآخر من الولد
بالسراية أو الأم بالتعليق فيقرع بينهما فإن خرجت على الولد عتق كله ورق
الأم
وإن خرج على الأم لا يمكن إعتاق كلها إذا يبقى بعض الولد رقيقا مع عتق كل
الأم والولد في حكم عضو من أعضائها لا يقبل عتقه الانفصال عن عتقها فيعتق
بقدر خمسين منها على نسبة  واحدة ويحكم بعتق نصف الأم وهو خمس وعشرون ليقتضي
ذلك عتق نصف الولد وهو خمسون
ولكن يخص النصف الحر منه النصف فيبقى للنصف الرقيق النصف وهو قدر خمس
وعشرين فيعتق إذا من الأم نصفها ومن الولد ثلاثة أرباعه نصف بالمباشرة وربع
بسراية عتق الأم
الثالث إذا أوصى بعبد لإنسان وهو ثلث ماله وثلثا ماله غائب فلا نسلم
العبد إذ المال ربما يتلف فيكون العبد كل المال
وهل يسلم ثلث العبد ليتسلط عليه فيه وجهان
أحدهما نعم لأنه أقل أحواله
والثاني لا فإن حق الشرع أن لا يتسلط الموصى له على شئ إلا ويتسلط الوارث
على مثليه وهاهنا ليس يمكن تسليط الوارث على الثلثين من العبد فإنه ربما
يسلم للموصى له
فإن استبهم خبر المال الغائب وتواطئا على إشاعة الوصية في جميع المال حتى
يصير العبد مثلثا بينهم لم يكن لهما ذلك لأنه نقل الوصية من عين إلى غيره
وقال مالك يجوز ذلك للمصلحة
ولو أعتق عبدا وهو ثلث ماله أو دبره وثلثا ماله غائب ففي تنفيذ العتق في
ثلث العبد الخلاف الذى ذكرناه بعينه في الوصية
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ب-و (ḥ-b-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to give freely, to favor, to prefer" — the root denotes preferential giving without compensation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, muḥābāh (محاباة) is a contractual favoritism — selling below market value or transacting with concession — which jurisprudentially is treated as a gratuitous transfer (tabarruʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "showing affection/favor"; in legal discourse it is a metaphorical extension (majāz) to any transactional concession that creates a gratuitous component.
- Root: ق-ر-ع (q-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "lot, casting lots, drawing" — from the sense of striking/pecking (as a bird pecks seed), hence selection by chance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In inheritance and manumission law, qurʿah (قرعة) is the procedural device for allocating limited shares among competing claimants when equal priority exists.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the physical act of casting lots; metaphorically extended to judicial determination by lottery.
- Root: س-ر-ي (s-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to travel by night, to move, to spread" — hence sarāyah (سراية) as the "spreading" of an effect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the legal principle that manumission of a part of a slave spreads to the whole (sarāyat al-ʿitq), and similarly that freeing a mother affects her unborn child.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = nocturnal journey; metaphorical = the transitive propagation of a legal effect from one object to another.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Constructions (الشّرط والجزاء) — The text repeatedly uses conditional sentences (e.g., "if he sold...", "if he married...") where the protasis establishes a hypothetical legal scenario and the apodosis states the ruling. Also, the rule of ʿAṭf (coordination) with wa (و) to join parallel legal cases, requiring careful parsing of whether the conjunction coordinates rulings or conditions.
chapters.translation:
### | Two Subsidiary Issues

**The First:** If he sold at the fair price (thaman al-mithl), it is effective even if [the buyer] was the heir. Likewise, if he paid the debt of some of the creditors, the rest have no right to prevent [it]. Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — dissented in this and in the sale to the heir.

But if there was favoritism (muḥābāh) in the sale, then the amount of the favoritism has the ruling of gratuitous transfers (tabarruʿāt). Likewise, if he married a woman for more than the fair dower (mahr al-mithl), the excess is a gratuity counted from the third [of the estate].

**The Second:** If a woman married for less than the fair dower, it is not counted from the third, because she has only relinquished her vulva (buḍʿ), and the vulva is not property. If he leased his slaves and his beasts with favoritism, it is a gratuity, because it is property.

But if he leased his own person (nafsahu) with favoritism, there are two views:
- **The First:** It is a gratuity, like the usufructs of slaves, for his usufruct is property.
- **The Second:** No — because it is not counted as property that the heir would covet, so it resembles the vulva of a woman in this respect. And this was counted as a refusal to earn (imtināʿ ʿan al-iktisāb), not as a forfeiture (tafwīt).

**The Third Matter: The Manner of Accounting from the Third**

Its principle is: if all the gratuitous transfers were executed (munajjazah) during the illness [of death], then the first is given precedence, then the next. So if the first was a gift (hibah) and the second a manumission (ʿitq), the gift is given precedence, because the third was fulfilled by it, and the manumission after it falls away.

Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: They are equal, for this one has the force of manumission and that one has the force of precedence.

But if they are equal [in time], then:
- If all are gifts and favoritisms, the third is distributed among them proportionally to their amounts.
- If all are manumissions, lots are cast among the slaves and it is not distributed proportionally — out of caution against fractional division (tashqīṣ) — unlike the case of gifts. This is due to what was narrated: that the Prophet ﷺ cast lots among six slaves whom a sick man had manumitted, and divided them into three parts, keeping four in slavery and freeing two.

If gift and manumission coincide in a single moment — by the word of an agent (wakīl) or by attaching both to after death — then regarding giving precedence to manumission there are two views:
- **The First:** No — because of the equality in the time of entitlement.
- **The Second:** Yes — because manumission presses against the property of another through its spreading effect (sarāyah).

Regarding attaching kitābah (contract of manumission) to manumission in deserving precedence over favoritism, there is a difference [of opinion].

But if all is attached to after death, then no consideration is given to what preceded in some of the bequests, because the time of binding (luzūm) is one for all. The only remaining consideration is giving precedence to manumission over others.

If he bequeathed the manumission of a slave and attached the manumission of another to death, there is no precedence for either in any case.

### | Subsidiary Branches

**The First:** If he had two slaves, Ghānim and Sālim, and said to Ghānim: "If I free you, then Sālim is free," then he freed Ghānim, and the third suffices only for one of them — Ghānim is freed, and no lot is cast between them. For perhaps the lot would fall on Sālim, leading to his being freed without Ghānim being freed, and that would be an attainment of the consequent (musabbab) without the antecedent (sabab), which is impossible.

But if he had, besides Ghānim, two slaves, and attached their freedom to the freedom of Ghānim, and the third suffices for Ghānim and one of them — then Ghānim is freed, and lots are cast between the two; whoever's lot comes out is freed.

**The Second:** If he owned a pregnant slave-girl, and his total wealth was three hundred, the child being one hundred of the total and the mother fifty. Then he said: "If I free half of the pregnancy, then the mother is free." Then he freed half of the pregnancy. Fifty is freed, and there remains for us fifty to complete the third, suspended (muraddad) between the other half of the child — by the spreading effect (sarāyah) — or the mother — by the conditional attachment (taʿlīq). So lots are cast between them. If it falls on the child, the whole child is freed and the mother remains enslaved.

If it falls on the mother, it is not possible to free all of her, for some of the child would remain enslaved while the whole mother is free — and the child is in the ruling of a limb of her limbs, whose freedom cannot be separated from her freedom. So she is freed to the extent of fifty of her, on a single proportion, and it is ruled that half of the mother is freed — which is twenty-five — so that this necessitates the freedom of half of the child — which is fifty. But the free half of the child is allocated to its half, so there remains for the enslaved half its half — which is the amount of twenty-five. Thus there is freed from the mother half of her, and from the child three-quarters of him: half by direct action (mubāsharah) and a quarter by the spreading of the mother's freedom (sarāyat ʿitq al-umm).

**The Third:** If he bequeathed a slave to a person, and it is a third of his wealth, while two-thirds of his wealth is absent (ghāʾib), we do not hand over the slave — for the wealth might perish, making the slave the entirety of the wealth.

And is a third of the slave handed over so that [the legatee] may have power over it? There are two views:
- **The First:** Yes — because it is the least of its possible states.
- **The Second:** No — for the right of the Law is that the legatee should not have power over anything unless the heir has power over twice its like. And here it is not possible to give the heir power over two-thirds of the slave, for perhaps it will be handed over to the legatee.

If the news of the absent wealth becomes obscure, and they mutually agree to spread the bequest over all the wealth until the slave becomes divided into thirds among them — that is not permissible for them, because it transfers the bequest from one specific object (ʿayn) to another. Mālik said: That is permissible for the sake of public interest (maṣlaḥah).

If he freed a slave — it being a third of his wealth — or made him mudabbar (freed upon death), while two-thirds of his wealth is absent, then regarding the execution of the manumission in a third of the slave, there is the very same difference [of opinion] that we mentioned in the case of the bequest.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الركن الرابع الصيغة

وهو الإيجاب والقبول
أما الإيجاب فقوله أوصيت له أو أعطوه أو جعلت هذا له أو ملكته بعد الموت
ولو قال عينت هذا له فكناية والوصية تنعقد بها عند النية فإنه إذا قبل
التعليق بالإغرار فبأن يقبل الكناية أولى
ولو قال وهبت هذا منه ونوى الوصية ففي كونه كناية وجهان ووجه المنع أنه
صريح في اقتضاء ملك ناجز
ولو قال هذا لفلان ثم قال أردت الوصية لم يقبل لأنه صيغة إقرار إلا أن
يقول هذا من مالي لفلان
أما القبول فلا بد منه ولكن بعد الموت فلا أثر لقبوله ورده قبل موت
الموصى
وإن مات الموصى له قبل القبول قام وارثه مقامه لأنه حق التملك فهو بالإرث
أولى من الشفعة
وإن قبل الموصى له ثم رده قبل القبض ففي نفوذ رده وجهان
أحدهما لا إذ تم ملكه بالقبول بعد الموت
والثاني نعم  لأنه ملك بغير عوض فيتطرق الرد إليه
هذا إذا أوصى لمعينين أما إذا أوصى للفقراء أو لجهة عامة لزم بالموت إذ
لا يتصور شرط القبول فيه
ثم اختلف قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه في وقت حصول الملك على ثلاثة أقوال
الأول أنه يحصل بالموت لأنه أضاف إلى الموت
والثاني بالقبول إذ يبعد أن يدخل الشئ في ملكه قهرا
والثالث وهو الأصح أنه موقوف فإن قبل تبين حصوله بالموت وإن رد تبين أنه
لم يحصل من أصله
فإن فرعنا على أنه يحصل بالقبول فهو قبل القبول ملك الوارث أو ملك الميت
فيه وجهان
ومنشأ التردد أن في إضافته إلى كل واحد منهما نوع استحالة إذ لا ملك لميت
ولا ميراث إلا بعد الوصية

### | ويتفرع على الأقوال مسائل خمسة

الأولى إذا حدثت زيادة قبل القبول فهي للموصى له على كل قول إن قبل
الوصية إلا إذا

### | فرع

نا على أن الملك يحصل بالقبول ففيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه له نظرا إلى القرار
والثاني لا إذ حدث قبل قبوله وملكه
وعلى هذا إن قلنا إن الملك للميت فتقضى منه الديون وإن قلنا للوارث فلا
إذ الصحيح أن وثيقة الدين لا يتعدى إلى الزيادة كوثيقة الرهن
أما إذا رد فالزيادة من التركة بكل حال إلا إذا فرعنا على أن الملك يحصل
بالموت ففيه وجهان أحدهما أنه يتبع الأصل في الرد
والثاني أنه يبقى على ملك الموصى له لأنه حصل على ملكه فهو كزيادة المبيع
الثانية النفقة والمؤن وزكاة الفطر بين الموت والقبول على الموصى له إن
قبل عل كل قول وعلى الوارث إن رد على كل قول
ولا يعود الوجه المذكور في الزيادات وإن كان يحتمل أن يقال الغرم في
مقابلة الغنم ولكن إدخال شئ في الملك قهرا أهون من إلزام مؤنة قهرا
فرع
مهما توقف في القبول والرد مع الحاجة إلى النفقة كلف النفقة قهرا فإن
أراد الخلاص فليرد
وإن لم يكن إلى النفقة حاجة ولكن أراد الوارث أن يستقر الأمر معه فيطالب
بالقبول  أو الرد
فإن توقف حكم عليه بالرد لأجل المصلحة فيقال إما أن تقبل أو نحكم عليك
بالرد إن توقفت
الثالثة إذا كان الموصى به زوجة الموصى له
فإن قبل انفسخ النكاح
وإن رأينا الوقف كان بطريق التبين من وقت الموت
وإن رد لم ينفسخ إلا إذا فرعنا على أنه يملك بالموت فيفسخ وإن كان الملك
ضعيفا لأن ملك اليمين يضاد ملك النكاح
وإن كانت زوجة الوارث
فإن قبل الموصى له لم ينفسخ نكاحه إلا إذا فرعنا على أنه يملك بالقبول
وأنه قبل القبول للوارث ففيه وجهان
ووجه بقاء النكاح ضعف الملك مع أن الاختيار إلى غيره بخلاف الموصى له فإن
الاختيار إليه
وإن رد فينفسخ النكاح وهل يستند إلى حالة الموت فيه خلاف منشؤه ضعف ذلك
الملك
ولو كان الموصى به قريبا للموصى له أو الوارث قرابة يعتق بالملك فتخريجه
على الأقوال كتخريج انفساخ نكاح الزوجة
الرابعة إذا أوصى بأمة لزوجها الحر وولدت قبل القبول بعد الموت قال
الشافعي رضي الله عنه عتق الأولاد ولم تكن أمهم أم ولد له
هذا نقل المزني وهو خطأ إذ لا وجه للفرق بين الأم والولد على كل قول
أثبتنا الملك أو نفينا أو توقفنا
نعم قال بعد ذلك ولو مات الموصى له فقبل الوارث عتق الأولاد وهو صحيح
يخرج على قولنا يحصل الملك بالموت للموصى له وعلى قول الوقف أيضا
الخامسة أوصى له بولده فمات فقبل وارثه
فعتقه يبنى على أن الملك بماذا يحصل
فإن قلنا بالموت أو قلنا بالوقف تبين العتق على الموصى له قبل موته
وإن قلنا بالقبول ففي قبول الوارث وجهان
أحدهما أنه يترتب على قبوله كقبول المورث
والثاني أنا نسنده إلى ألطف حين قبل موت الموصى له
فعلى هذا هو تركة يقضى منه الديون ونتبين عتقه
وإن قلنا يترتب على القبول فلا يعتق لأن الميت لا يعتق القريب عليه بحال
إذ ملكه وإن قدر لا قرار له
نعم هل تقضى الديون مما قبله الوارث فيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه لا  يقضى إذ لم يملكه الميت وإنما ورث هذا حق التمليك ابتداء
وذكر هذا الوجه في الصيد المتعلق بشبكة نصبها قبل موته ولكنه أبعد فيه
والوجه الثاني أنه يقضى منه الديون وكأنا نقدر حصول الملك للميت مختطفا
ثم نقدر انتقاله إلى الوارث تلقيا منه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ي-غ (ṣ-y-gh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to form, fashion, or cast" (as a metalworker shapes molten ore); hence a verbal formula is that which "casts" the legal meaning into a determinate utterance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, al-ṣīghah denotes the articulated expression that constitutes a binding performative (inshāʾ), as opposed to mere informative speech (ikhbār).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical molding; metaphorical extension (majāz) applies to speech that "molds" legal reality — the utterance itself becomes the efficient cause of obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAmal fī al-Jumal (Operative Force in Sentences) — The grammatical form of a performative (e.g., "I have bequeathed") carries its own operative effect without requiring a separate copula, just as the verb governs its object directly.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth pillar is the formula (al-ṣīghah), which comprises the offer (ījāb) and the acceptance (qabūl).

As for the offer, it is his statement: "I have bequeathed to him," or "Give it to him," or "I have made this for him," or "I have made him its owner after death." If he says, "I have designated this for him," it is a metonymy (kināyah), and the bequest is validly concluded by it when accompanied by intention (niyyah) — for if the bequest is valid when suspended upon a condition of deception (ighrār), then accepting it via metonymy is even more fitting.

If he says, "I have gifted this to him" and intends thereby a bequest, there are two views (wajhān) as to whether it constitutes a metonymy. The view prohibiting it holds that this wording is explicit (ṣarīḥ) in requiring an immediate transfer of ownership (tamlīk nājiz).

If he says, "This belongs to so-and-so," then claims, "I intended a bequest," it is not accepted, because it is a formula of acknowledgment (iqrār) — unless he says, "This, from my wealth, is for so-and-so."

As for acceptance, it is indispensable — but only after death. Thus, his acceptance or rejection before the testator's death has no effect.

If the legatee dies before acceptance, his heir stands in his place, because it is a right of acquisition (ḥaqq al-tamalluk), and it takes precedence over pre-emption (shufʿah) by way of inheritance.

If the legatee accepts, then rejects before taking possession (qabḍ), there are two views on the validity of his rejection:
One: It is not valid, for his ownership was completed by acceptance after death.
Two: It is valid, because he owns it without exchange (ʿiwad), so rejection may apply to it.

This applies when he bequeaths to specified individuals. But if he bequeaths to the poor or to a general public purpose (jihah ʿāmmah), the bequest becomes binding upon death, since the condition of acceptance is inconceivable therein.

Then the statements of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — differ regarding the time of ownership's acquisition, yielding three opinions:
First: It is acquired upon death, because the testator annexed the bequest to death.
Second: It is acquired upon acceptance, for it is unlikely that a thing enters one's ownership coercively (qahran).
Third — and this is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ): It is suspended (mawqūf). If he accepts, it becomes evident that ownership occurred at death; if he rejects, it becomes evident that it never occurred at all.

If we build upon the view that ownership is acquired upon acceptance, then before acceptance it is either the heir's property or the deceased's property — two views. The source of hesitation is that annexing it to either entails a kind of impossibility: for the deceased has no ownership, and there is no inheritance except after the bequest.

---

Five subsidiary questions branch from these opinions:

**First:** If an increase (ziyādah) occurs before acceptance, it belongs to the legatee on every opinion — if he accepts the bequest — except when we build upon the view that ownership is acquired upon acceptance; then there are two views:
One: It is his, in consideration of the final settlement (qarār).
Two: It is not his, for it arose before his acceptance and ownership.

Upon this [second view], if we say the ownership belongs to the deceased, debts are settled from it; but if we say it belongs to the heir, they are not — for the correct principle is that the lien of debt (wathīqat al-dayn) does not extend to the increase, just as the lien of pledge (wathīqat al-rahn) does not.

But if he rejects, the increase belongs to the estate (tarikah) in all cases — except when we build upon the view that ownership is acquired upon death; then there are two views:
One: It follows the principal in the rejection.
Two: It remains in the legatee's ownership, because it arose upon his property, like the increase of a sold item.

**Second:** Maintenance (nafaqah), expenses (muʾan), and the alms of breaking the fast (zakāt al-fiṭr) between death and acceptance fall upon the legatee if he accepts — on every opinion — and upon the heir if he rejects — on every opinion. The aforementioned view regarding increases does not recur here, although one might say: "The loss is in exchange for the gain (al-ghurm bi-muqābil al-ghunm)." But coercively admitting a thing into ownership is lighter than coercively imposing a maintenance burden.

*Branch:* Whenever he delays acceptance or rejection while there is need for maintenance, he is compelled to pay maintenance coercively. If he wishes to be released, let him reject. If there is no need for maintenance, but the heir wishes to settle the matter, he may demand acceptance or rejection. If he delays, judgment is passed against him for rejection for the sake of public interest (maṣlaḥah) — it is said: "Either accept, or we rule your rejection if you delay."

**Third:** If the bequeathed item is the legatee's wife:
If he accepts, the marriage is dissolved (infasakha al-nikāḥ).
If we adopt the view of suspension, this dissolution is by way of retroactive clarification (tabayyun) from the time of death.
If he rejects, the marriage is not dissolved — except when we build upon the view that he owns upon death; then it is dissolved, even if the ownership is weak, because the ownership of the right hand (milk al-yamīn) contradicts the ownership of marriage (milk al-nikāḥ).

If the bequeathed item is the heir's wife:
If the legatee accepts, her marriage is not dissolved — except when we build upon the view that he owns upon acceptance, and that before acceptance the property belongs to the heir; then there are two views. The view upholding the marriage's continuance rests on the weakness of the ownership, combined with the fact that the choice belongs to another — unlike the legatee's case, where the choice is his own.
If he rejects, the marriage is dissolved. Whether this dissolution is retroactive to the moment of death is a point of disagreement, whose source is the weakness of that ownership.

If the bequeathed item is a relative of the legatee or the heir — a relative whose emancipation is effected by ownership — its derivation from the three opinions is like the derivation of the wife's marriage dissolution.

**Fourth:** If he bequeaths a slave-girl (ummah) to her free husband, and she gives birth before acceptance after death, al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: The offspring are emancipated, but their mother does not become an umm walad for him. This is al-Muzanī's transmission, and it is an error — for there is no ground for distinguishing between the mother and the offspring on any opinion, whether we affirm ownership, negate it, or suspend it. However, he said afterward: "If the legatee dies and his heir accepts, the offspring are emancipated" — and this is correct, derived from our view that ownership is acquired by the legatee upon death, and also upon the view of suspension.

**Fifth:** He bequeaths his own child to someone, then the legatee dies and his heir accepts. The child's emancipation is built upon how ownership is acquired:
If we say upon death, or say upon suspension, the emancipation is clarified as having occurred for the legatee before his death.
If we say upon acceptance, then there are two views regarding the heir's acceptance:
One: It is consequent upon his acceptance, like the acceptance of the testator [i.e., the original legatee].
Two: We attribute it to the more subtle [consideration] — that it occurred before the legatee's death. Upon this view, it is an estate (tarikah) from which debts are settled, and his emancipation is clarified.
If we say it is consequent upon acceptance, then he is not emancipated — for the deceased cannot emancipate a relative upon himself in any case, since his ownership, even if posited, has no settlement (qarār).

However, whether debts are settled from what the heir accepted — two views:
One: They are not settled, for the deceased never owned it; rather, the heir inherited this right of acquisition (ḥaqq al-tamalluk) anew. This view was mentioned regarding game caught in a net set before his death — but it was deemed far-fetched therein.
Two: Debts are settled from it, as if we posit that ownership accrued to the deceased momentarily (mukhtatafan), then posit its transfer to the heir, receiving it from him.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | التفريع

إذا قلنا يعتق الولد بقبول الوارث فلا يرث لأن القابل إن كان أخا يصير
محجوبا به فيسقط حقه عن القبول فيمتنع العتق فيؤدي توريثه إلى منع توريثه
فهو دور فقهي
وإن كان له ابن آخر فشركته تمنع كمال حقه في القبول لا يبقى له إلا قبول
النصف
ومن نصفه حر لا يرث ولا يمكن أن يقبل نصيب نفسه لأن صحة قبوله موقوف على
توريثه وتوريثه موقوف على صحة قبوله فيتمانعان
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في أحكام الوصية الصحيحة - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - والنظر في أقسام

### | القسم الأول في الأحكام اللفظية

وفيه فصلان

### | الفصل الأول فيما يتعلق بالموصى به

والكلام في أطراف

### | الطرف الأول في الحمل

والوصية بالحمل صحيحة بشرط أن يكون موجودا حالة الوصية
ويعرف تاريخ ذلك في الحيوانات من أهل الخبرة فإنها مختلفة
فإن انفصل حمل الجارية ميتا بجناية جان صرف الأرش إلى الموصى له ولم
يتبين فساد الوصية بخلاف ما إذا أوصى لحمل فانفصل ميتا بجنابة جان لا يصرف
إلى ورثته لأن كونه مالكا يستدعي حياة مستقرة وكونه مملوكا لا يستدعي إلا
التقوم وقد يقوم بالأرش
ولو أوصى بجارية دون حملها جاز
ولو أطلق الوصية ففي اندراج الحمل تحت مطلق اللفظ تردد
فإن قلنا يندرج لم تبطل الوصية فيه بانفصاله قبل موت الموصي لأنه زيادة
في الموصى به

### | الطرف الثاني

إذا أوصى بطبل من طبوله وله طبل لهو وحرب
نزل على طبل الحرب تصحيحا له
وإذا أوصى بعود من عيدانه وعنده عود اللهو وعود القوس وعود البناء فوجهان
أحدهما أنه فاسد لأنه لا يفهم منه إلا عود اللهو
والثاني أنه يعطى عود البناء أو القوس لأنه يسمى عودا فيتكلف تصحيحه كما
في  الطبل
أما إذا لم يكن عنده إلا عود القوس أو البناء أعطي ذلك لأنه متعين

### | الثالث إذا أوصى بقوس

حمل على القوس الذي يرمي منه النبل والنشاب دون قوس الندف والجلاهق وهو
قوس البندق
ويدخل تحته الحسبان فإنه يرمى منه الناوك وهو نشاب
وهل يعطى الوتر مع القوس فيه وجهان
فإن قال أعطوه قوسا من قسي ولم يكن عنده إلا قوس ندف أعطى لأنه تعين
وإن كان عنده قوس ندف وحلاهق أعطى الجلاهق لأنه أسبق إلى الفهم

### | الطرف الرابع إذا قال أعطوه شاة

جاز أن يدفع إليه الكبير والصغير والظأن والمعز لأن الاسم شامل
وقال الصيدلاني لا يعطى السخلة وقال أراد الشافعي رضي الله عنه
بالصغير الجذعة
والمنصوص أنه لا يعطى الكبش
ومنهم من قال يعطى لأن الشاة اسم جنس كالإنسان والتاء فيه ليس للتأنيث
وأصله الشاهة وتصغيره شويهة
ولو قال أعطوه بقرة لم يعط ثورا
ولو قال أعطوه جملا لم يعط ناقة
ولو قال أعطوه بعيرا فالمنصوص أنه لا يعطى ناقة
ومن أصحابنا من قال يعطى لأن البعير كالإنسان للرجال والنساء
ولو قال أعطوه رأسا من الإبل أو الغنم أو البقر جاز الذكر والأنثى
فإن قال أعطوه كلبا أو حمارا لم يعط الكلبة والحمارة فإن الأنثى مميزة
فيهما بالتاء
ولو قال أعطوه دابة فالمنصوص أنه يعطى من الخيل أو البغال أو الحمير ولا
يعطى من الإبل قطعا
قال بعض الأصحاب أطلق الشافعي رضي الله عنه ذلك على لغة مغر وفي غيره لا
يفهم منه إلا الفرس
ومنهم من قال الوضع الأصلي أولى بالمراعاة من العرف الخاص المخصص
ولو قال أعطوه دابة ليقاتل عليه لم يعط إلا الفرس
فإن قال ليحمل عليه لم يعط إلا بغلا أو حمارا
ولو قال لينتفع بنسله لم يعط إلا فرسا أو حمارا

- Root: د-و-ر (d-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cyclic motion, revolving; a circle (dā'irah) — denotes logical circularity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Circular reasoning (dawr) as an invalid epistemic dependency in legal causation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical rotation; metaphorically, a vicious circle in juristic inference.
- Root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To accept, receive, face toward; acceptance (qabūl) as a contractual act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Acceptance as the volitional ratification of a legal disposition (ījāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "taking with the hand"; metaphorical for legal acceptance.
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To carry, bear; pregnancy (ḥaml) — a fetus carried in the womb.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The embryo as a potential legal subject, contingent on live birth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal carrying of a burden; metaphorical for bearing responsibility or a fetus.
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return; a reed, stick, or branch (ʿūd) — wood used for various purposes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Material substance (jawhar) as opposed to accidents; here, a physical object of bequest.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal wood; metaphorical for a lute (ʿūd al-lahw) or bow (ʿūd al-qaws) by contextual extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Operator) — When a noun is qualified by a genitive construct (iḍāfah), the omitted operator is estimated contextually, affecting legal interpretation of general vs. specific terms.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now for the subsidiary rulings (tafrīʿ).

If we hold that the child is emancipated upon the heir's acceptance, then he does not inherit. For if the acceptor is a brother, he becomes excluded (maḥjūb) by the child, so his right to accept falls away, and thus emancipation is prevented. Consequently, granting him inheritance leads to preventing his inheritance — this is a juristic circularity (dawr fiqhī).

If the deceased has another son, then the child's partnership (shirkah) prevents the acceptor from having full right of acceptance; he retains only the acceptance of half. And one who is half-free does not inherit, nor can he accept his own portion, because the validity of his acceptance is contingent upon his inheriting, while his inheriting is contingent upon the validity of his acceptance — so the two mutually preclude each other.

— Peace be upon him — Chapter Two: On the Rulings of a Valid Bequest — Peace be upon him — And the consideration is in its divisions.

### Division One: On Verbal Rulings

This contains two sections.

### Section One: On What Pertains to the Bequeathed Object

The discussion covers several aspects.

### Aspect One: On the Fetus (al-ḥaml)

A bequest to a fetus is valid, provided that it exists at the time of the bequest. The determination of its existence at that time, in the case of animals, is established by experts, for their gestation periods differ.

If the fetus of a slave-girl is delivered dead due to an injury inflicted by an aggressor, the compensation (arsh) is paid to the legatee, and the invalidity of the bequest is not established — unlike the case where one bequeaths to a fetus and it is delivered dead due to an aggressor's injury; then the compensation is not paid to its heirs, because its being a possessor (mālik) requires a settled life, whereas its being possessed (mamlūk) requires only that it have value (taqawwum), and it may acquire value through the compensation.

If one bequeaths a slave-girl without her fetus, this is permissible. If one makes an absolute bequest, there is hesitation (taraddud) as to whether the fetus is included under the absolute wording. If we say it is included, the bequest in it is not invalidated by its being delivered before the testator's death, because that is an increase in the bequeathed object.

### Aspect Two

If one bequeaths "a drum (ṭabl) from his drums," and he has both a drum of amusement and a war drum, it is construed as the war drum, to validate the bequest.

If one bequeaths "a wood (ʿūd) from his woods," and he possesses a lute (ʿūd al-lahw), a bow wood (ʿūd al-qaws), and a building timber (ʿūd al-bināʾ), there are two opinions (wajhān):
One: It is invalid, because nothing is understood from it except the lute.
Second: He is given the building timber or the bow wood, because it is called "wood" (ʿūd), so one strives to validate it, as in the case of the drum.

However, if he possesses only a bow wood or a building timber, he is given that, because it is determined (mutʿayyin).

### Aspect Three: If one bequeaths a bow (qaws)

It is construed as the bow from which arrows (nabl) and crossbow bolts (nashshāb) are shot, not the bow of cotton-carding (nadf) nor the pellet bow (jalāhiq) — which is the bow for hazelnuts. Included under it is the crossbow (ḥasbān), for the nāwak (a type of arrow) is shot from it, and it is a kind of nashshāb.

Is the bowstring (watr) given along with the bow? There are two opinions.

If he says, "Give him a bow from my bows," and he possesses only a cotton-carding bow, he is given it, because it is determined. If he possesses both a cotton-carding bow and a pellet bow, he is given the pellet bow, because it is more readily understood (asbaq ilā al-fahm).

### Aspect Four: If he says, "Give him a sheep (shāh)"

It is permissible to give him a large or small one, a ewe (ḍaʾn) or a goat (maʿz), because the name is inclusive. Al-Ṣaydalānī said: "A lamb (sakhlah) is not given," and he claimed that al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — meant by "small" a yearling (jadhaʿah). The textually stipulated ruling (manṣūṣ) is that a ram (kabsh) is not given. Some say it is given, because "sheep" (shāh) is a generic noun (ism jins) like "human" (insān), and the tāʾ in it is not for feminine gender; its origin is shāhah, and its diminutive is shuwaihah.

If he says, "Give him a cow (baqarah)," a bull (thawr) is not given. If he says, "Give him a camel (jamal)," a she-camel (nāqah) is not given. If he says, "Give him a camel (baʿīr)," the textually stipulated ruling is that a she-camel is not given. Some of our companions say it is given, because "camel" (baʿīr) is like "human," applying to males and females.

If he says, "Give him a head (raʾs) of camels, sheep, or cattle," both male and female are permissible.

If he says, "Give him a dog (kalb) or a donkey (ḥimār)," a bitch (kalbah) and a she-donkey (ḥimārah) are not given, because the female in these two is distinguished by the tāʾ.

If he says, "Give him a beast (dābbah)," the textually stipulated ruling is that he is given from horses, mules, or donkeys, but not from camels, definitively. Some companions said: "Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — stated this according to the dialect of Muzar; in other dialects, nothing is understood from it except a horse." Some say: "The original lexical usage (al-waḍʿ al-aṣlī) is more deserving of consideration than the specific customary usage (al-ʿurf al-khāṣṣ) that restricts it."

If he says, "Give him a beast to fight upon," only a horse is given. If he says, "to carry upon," only a mule or donkey is given. If he says, "to benefit from its offspring," only a horse or donkey is given.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الخامس في العبد

فإن قال أعطوه رأسا من رقيقي جاز أن يعطى السليم والمعيب والصغير والكبير
والذكر والأنثى والخنثى
وإن لم يكن عند موته إلا رقيق واحد تعين ذلك الواحد
فإن مات  أرقاؤه او قتلوه قبل موته انفسخت الوصية
وإن قتلوا بعد موته يخير الوارث في صرف قيمة واحد إليه لأن حقه المتأكد
أو ملكه متعلق به بعد موته فينتقل إلى القيمة
فلو قتل كلهم إلا واحدا لم يتعين ذلك الواحد بل يخير الوارث بين تسليمه
وتسليم قيمة واحد
وفيه وجه أنه يتعين ذلك الواحد حذرا من العدول إلى القيمة مع الإمكان
وإن قال أعتقوه عني عبدا جاز المعيب والسليم
وفيه وجه أنه ينزل على ما يجزئ في الكفارة لأن الشرع عادة في العتق لا في
الهبة والوصية فينزل على عرف الشرع
فإن أوصى أن يعتق عنه رقاب فأقله ثلاثة إن وفى الثلث به فإن لم يف إلا
باثنين اقتصر عليه
فإن وفى باثنين وبعض الثالث فوجهان
أحدهما الاقتصار على اثنين لأن البعض ليس رقبة
والثاني أنه يشتري الفضل لأنه أقرب إلى مقصود الموصي
وعلى هذا لو وجدنا نفيسين أو خسيسين وشقصا فأيهما أولى فيه وجهان
أحدهما النفيس أولى لقوله عليه السلام
لما سئل عن أفضل الرقاب فقال أكثرها ثمنا وأنفسها عند أهلها
والثاني الزيادة في عدد الرقبة أولى لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أعتق
رقبة أعتق الله بكل عضو منه عضوا منه من النار
ولو قال أعتقوا عبدا من عبيدي وله خنثى حكم بكونه رجلا ففي إعتاقه وجهان
ووجه المنع أن اسم البعد مطلقا لا ينصرف إليه
ولو قال أعتقوا أحد رقيقي وفيهم خنثى مشكل
روى الربيع فيمن أوصى بكتابة أحد رقيقه أنه لا يجوز الخنثى المكشل
وروى المزني أنه يجوز
واختلف الأصحاب والأولى ما قاله المزني

### | الفصل الثاني فيما يتعلق بالموصى له

وله أطراف

### | الطرف الأول إذا قال أعطوا حمل فلانة كذا فأتت بولدين

صرف إليهما بالسوية وإن كان أحدهما ذكرا والآخر أنثى
ولو خرج أحدهما حيا والآخر ميتا فالكل للحي
وفيه وجه آخر أن له النصف ونصف الميت يعود إلى الورثة وهو ضعيف
ولو قال إن كان حملها غلاما فأعطوه كذا فولدت غلامين لم يستحقا شيئا فإن
الصيغة  للتوحيد في النكرة
وكذا إن جاءت بغلام وجارية
ولو قال إن كان في بطنها غلام فأعطوه كذا فجاءت بغلام وجارية أعطي الغلام
وإن جاءت بغلامين فأيهما يعطى فيه ثلاث أقوال
أحدها أنه يصرف الوارث إلى أيهما شاء وله خيار التعيين فإن رأيه يصلح
للترجيح
والثاني يوزع عليهما لتساويهما
والثالث أنه موقوف بينهما إلى أن يبلغا ويصطلحا
ولو قال أوصيت لأحد هذين الشخصين ففي صحتها خلاف ذكرنا نظيره في الوقف
فإن صح ومات قبل التعيين خرج على الأوجه الثلاثة

### | الطرف الثاني إذا أوصى لجيرانه

صرف إلى أربعين دارا من كل جانب لما روى أبو هريرة أنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم قال
حق الجوار أربعون دارا هكذا وهكذا وهكذا وأشار يمينا وشمالا وقداما وخلفا
ولو أوصى لقراء القرآن صرف إلى من يحفظ جميع القرآن
وهل يصرف إلى من يقرأ ولا يحفظ عن ظهر القلب فيه وجهان
أحدهما نعم للعموم
والثاني لا إذ العرف يخصص بالحفاظ
ولو أوصى للعلماء صرف إلى العلماء بعلوم الشرع دون الأطباء والمنجمين
والمعبرين والأدباء لأن العرف يخصص
ولا يصرف إلى من يسمع الأحاديث فقط ولا علم له بطرق الحديث
ولو أوصى للأيتام لم يدخل فيه من له أب ولا بالغ لقوله صلى الله عليه
وسلم
لا يتم بعد البلوغ وفي الغني وجهان
وإن أوصى للأرامل دخل فيه من لا زوج لها من النساء وهل يدخل فيه من لا
زوجة له من الرجال فيه وجهان
أحدهما لا للعرف
والثاني نعم للوضع إذ قد يسمى الرجل أرمل
قال الشاعر ... كل الأرامل قد قضت حاجته ... فمن لحاجة هذا الأرمل الذكر
...
وهل يدخل الغني فيه وجهان كما في اليتيم
ولو أوصى للشيوخ أعطي من جاوز الأربعين
وإن أوصى للفتيان والشبان أعطي من جاوز البلوغ إلى الثلاثين
وإن أوصى للصبيان والغلمان صرف إلى من لم يبلغ اتباعا للعرف في هذه
الألفاظ
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ق-ب (raqaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The neck; by extension, a slave or captive held in bondage, as ownership was conceptualized as control over the neck.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, it denotes the human being as a whole in the context of manumission (ʿitq), where freeing the "neck" (raqaba) is a comprehensive act of liberation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the physical neck; metaphorical (majāz) transfer to the entire slave as a unit of property, common in juristic usage.
- Root: خ-ن-ث (khunutha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, pliancy; a person with ambiguous genitalia (khunthā), neither clearly male nor female.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A legal status of ambiguity (ishkāl) affecting inheritance, manumission, and ritual obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical ambiguity; metaphorical for legal indeterminacy in classification.
- Root: ج-و-ر (jāwara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Proximity, adjacency; a neighbor (jār) is one whose dwelling is contiguous.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic tradition, neighborliness (jīwār) is a covenant of mutual rights, extending to forty houses per direction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for spatial nearness; metaphorical for social obligation of protection and kindness.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — In phrases like "If he said: 'Give them...'", the protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb), and the legal effect hinges on the precise wording of the testator's utterance, requiring strict grammatical parsing of indefinite nouns (nakirah) and their scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fifth issue concerns the slave [as an object of bequest].

If the testator says: "Give them a head from my slaves," it is permissible to give the healthy, the defective, the young, the old, the male, the female, and the hermaphrodite (khunthā). If at the time of his death he possesses only one slave, that single one is specifically designated [by necessity].

If his slaves die before his death, or they kill him before his death, the bequest is annulled. But if they kill him after his death, the heir is given the choice to pay the value of one slave [to the legatee], because the legatee's confirmed right (ḥaqq muʾakkad) or his ownership is attached to the slave after the testator's death, and thus it transfers to the [monetary] value.

If all the slaves are killed except one, that one does not become specifically designated; rather, the heir chooses between surrendering him or surrendering the value of one slave. There is another opinion (wajh) that the single one is indeed designated, in order to avoid resorting to value while the [actual slave] is still possible.

If he says: "Free a slave on my behalf," it is permissible to free the defective and the healthy. There is an opinion that it is restricted to what suffices for an expiatory manumission (kafārah), because the legal custom (ʿurf al-sharʿ) in manumission—not in gift or bequest—governs, so it is interpreted according to the custom of the Law.

If he bequeaths that necks (riqāb) be freed on his behalf, the minimum is three, provided the third of the estate suffices for them. If it suffices only for two, then one limits [the bequest] to two. If it suffices for two and part of a third, there are two opinions (wajhān): One is to limit to two, because a part is not a "neck." The second is to purchase the remainder [with the surplus], because it is closer to the testator's intent.

Upon this [principle], if we find two precious slaves or two cheap ones and a fractional share (shiqṣ), which is preferable? There are two opinions: One is that the precious one is preferable, due to his saying, peace be upon him, when asked about the best necks (riqāb): "The most expensive of them and the most precious to their owners." The second is that increasing the number of necks is preferable, due to his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever frees a neck, Allah frees a limb of his from the Fire for every limb [of the slave]."

If he says: "Free a slave from among my slaves," and he has a hermaphrodite, and it is ruled that he is a man, then regarding his manumission there are two opinions. The basis for prohibition is that the absolute noun (ism al-ʿabd) does not apply to him [in common usage].

If he says: "Free one of my two slaves," and among them is an ambiguous hermaphrodite (khunthā mushkil), al-Rabīʿ reported—regarding one who bequeaths the kitābah (contractual manumission) of one of his two slaves—that the ambiguous hermaphrodite is not permissible. Al-Muzanī reported that it is permissible. The companions differed, and the preferable [view] is what al-Muzanī said.

### The Second Chapter: Matters Pertaining to the Legatee

This chapter has several branches (aṭrāf).

### The First Branch: If he says, "Give the child of so-and-so such-and-such," and she gives birth to two children

It is distributed between them equally, even if one is male and the other female. If one emerges alive and the other dead, the entirety goes to the living one. There is another opinion that he gets half, and the half of the dead one reverts to the heirs—but this is weak.

If he says: "If her child is a boy, give him such-and-such," and she gives birth to two boys, they deserve nothing, because the formulation [uses the singular] for the indefinite noun (nakirah) indicating unity. Likewise, if she brings a boy and a girl [they get nothing].

If he says: "If there is a boy in her womb, give him such-and-such," and she brings a boy and a girl, the boy is given [the bequest]. If she brings two boys, which one is given? There are three opinions (aqwāl): One is that the heir directs it to whichever he wishes, having the option of specification, for his judgment is suitable for preponderance. The second is that it is divided between them due to their equality. The third is that it is suspended between them until they reach maturity and reach a mutual settlement.

If he says: "I bequeath to one of these two persons," there is a dispute over its validity, which we mentioned analogously in the chapter on endowment (waqf). If it is valid and he dies before specification, it proceeds according to the three opinions [above].

### The Second Branch: If he bequeaths to his neighbors

It is distributed to forty houses from each side, due to what Abū Hurayrah reported that he, peace be upon him, said: "The right of neighborliness is forty houses—thus, thus, and thus"—and he gestured right, left, front, and back.

If he bequeaths to the reciters of the Qurʾān, it is given to those who memorize the entire Qurʾān. Is it given to one who reads but does not memorize by heart? There are two opinions: One, yes, due to the generality [of the term]; the second, no, because custom (ʿurf) restricts it to memorizers.

If he bequeaths to the scholars (ʿulamāʾ), it is given to scholars of the religious sciences, not to physicians, astrologers, dream-interpreters, or literary men, because custom restricts [the term]. Nor is it given to one who merely hears hadiths without knowledge of the chains of transmission (ṭuruq al-ḥadīth).

If he bequeaths to orphans (aytām), one who has a father is not included, nor an adult, due to his saying, peace be upon him: "There is no orphanhood after puberty." Regarding the wealthy [orphan], there are two opinions.

If he bequeaths to widows (arāmil), included are women who have no husband. Are men who have no wife included? There are two opinions: One, no, due to custom; the second, yes, due to linguistic usage (waḍʿ), for a man may be called "armal." The poet said: "All the widows have fulfilled their need... so who [will attend] to the need of this male widow?" Does the wealthy [widow] enter? There are two opinions, as with the orphan.

If he bequeaths to the elders (shuyūkh), one who has passed forty is given. If he bequeaths to the youths (fityān) and young men (shubbān), one who has passed puberty up to thirty is given. If he bequeaths to the boys (ṣibyān) and lads (ghilmān), it is given to those who have not reached puberty, following custom in these expressions.
