chapters.arabic_text:
### | المقدمة الثانية في الترغيب في النكاح

وقد قال الله تعالى {وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم} وقال
تناكحوا تكثروا فأني أباهي بكم الأمم يوم القيامة حتى بالسقط وقال
معاشر الشبان عليكم بالباءة فإنه أغض للبصر وأحصن للفرج فمن لم يستطع
فعليه بالصوم فإن الصوم له وجاء وقال عليه
السلام
من تزوج فقد أحرز ثلثي دينه ألا فليتق الله في الثلث الباقي وقال عمر رضي
الله عنه لرجل أتزوجت فقال لا فقال لن يمنع من النكاح إلا عجز أو فجور
ولما حضرت معاذا الوفاة قال زوجوني كي لا ألقى الله عزبا
وهذه الأحاديث ربما توهم أن النكاح أفضل من التخلي لعبادة الله تعالى كما
ظنه أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لكن الصحيح أن من لا تتوق نفسه إلى الوقاع فالتخلي
للعبادة أولى به ولذلك تفصيل وغور استقصيناه في كتاب آداب النكاح من
ربع العادات من كتب إحياء علوم الدين فليطلب منه
وقد ندب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في النكاح إلى أربعة أمور
أحدها طلب الحسيبة فقال عليه السلام
تخيروا لنطفكم فلا تضعوها في غير الأكفاء وقال
إياكم وخضراء الدمن وهي المرأة الحسناء في المنبت السوء كذلك  فسره عليه
السلام
الثاني الندب إلى البكر فإنها أحرى بالمؤالفة وقال لجابر هلا تزوجت بكرا
تلاعبها وتلاعبك وكان تزوج ثيبا
الثالث الندب إلى الولود قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
انكحوا الودود الولود فإني مكاثر بكم الأمم وقال
لحصير في ناحية البيت خير من امرأة لا تلد
الرابع الندب إلى الاجنبية قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
لا تنكحوا القرابة القريبة فإن الولد يخلق ضاويا أي نحيفا ولعل ذلك
لنقصان الشهوة بسبب القرابة
الخامس الندب إلى الصالحة قال عليه السلام
عليك بذات الدين تربت يداك

### | المقدمة الثالثة في النظر إليها بعد الرغبة في نكاحها

وذلك مستحب لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
من أراد نكاح امرأة فلينظر إليها فإنه أحرى أن يؤدم بينهما وينبغي أن
يقتصر على النظر إلى الوجه وذلك بعد العزم على النكاح إن ارتضاها ولا يشترط
استئذانها في هذا النظر بل يكفي فيه إذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
خلافا
لمالك وقد رخص في هذا النظر للحاجة وإلا فالأصل تحريم النظر إلى
الأجنبيات
وقد جرت العادة ها هنا بذكر ما يحل النظر إليه والكلام فيه في أربعة
مواضع
الأول نظر الرجل إلى الرجل وهو مباح إلا إلى العورة وذلك ما بين السرة
والركبة ويحرم اللمس كما يحرم النظر ولا يحرم نظر الإنسان إلى فرج نفسه
ولكن يكره من غير حاجة

### |
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes the contractual union of marriage, encompassing both the physical act and the legal bond; al-ʿAyn notes its primary sense as "to wed" or "to consummate."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, nikāḥ signifies the divinely sanctioned institution of matrimony, a means of preserving chastity (ʿiffah) and lineage (nasab), aligning with maqāṣid al-sharīʿah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, nikāḥ is the marriage contract; metaphorically (majāz), it may refer to the sexual union itself, as in the Quranic phrase {حتى تنكح زوجا غيره} (until she marries another husband), where the consummation is implied.
- Root: ب-و-ء (b-w-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root conveys "to settle," "to take up residence," or "to return to a place"; in the hadith, al-bāʿah (الباءة) is the capacity for sexual intercourse, derived from the idea of "cohabitation" as a dwelling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, bāʿah is the marital act as a means of lowering the gaze (ghaḍḍ al-baṣar) and guarding the private parts (ḥifẓ al-farj), a practical safeguard for piety.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "place of lodging"; metaphorically, it denotes the conjugal act as the "abode" of chastity, a rhetorical extension common in prophetic speech.
- Root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to abstain" or "to refrain"; in the lexicons, it is the act of fasting, which entails self-restraint from appetites.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic and prophetic context, ṣawm is a spiritual discipline that curbs the lower self (nafs), serving as a "castration" (wijāʾ) for those unable to marry—an analogy to the physical prevention of desire.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, fasting is abstention from food and drink; metaphorically, it is a shield (junnah) against sin, as the Prophet said, "Fasting is a protection" (al-ṣawm junnah).
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Emphasis (al-Tawkīd bi-al-Sharṭ) — In the phrase "فمن لم يستطع فعليه بالصوم" (whoever cannot [marry], let him fast), the conditional particle "man" (من) introduces a protasis that is answered by an imperative apodosis, a structure Sībawayh classifies as requiring the apodosis to be a command or a nominal sentence with an implied verb, emphasizing the obligation's conditional nature.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Second Introduction: On the Encouragement of Marriage

God the Exalted has said: {«And marry the unmarried among you»} (Q. 24:32). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Marry and multiply, for I shall boast of you before the nations on the Day of Resurrection, even by the miscarried fetus." He also said: "O company of young men, upon you is marriage (al-bāʿah), for it is most lowering of the gaze and most guarding of the private parts. And whoever cannot [marry], let him fast, for fasting is for him a castration (wijāʾ)." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever marries has secured two-thirds of his religion; so let him fear God regarding the remaining third." And ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said to a man: "Have you married?" He replied: "No." ʿUmar said: "Nothing prevents marriage except incapacity or lewdness." And when death approached Muʿādh, he said: "Marry me, so that I do not meet God as an unmarried man (ʿazb)."

These hadiths might lead one to suppose that marriage is superior to seclusion for the worship of God the Exalted, as Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) opined. But the correct view is that for one whose soul does not yearn for sexual intercourse, seclusion for worship is more fitting for him. This matter has a detailed elaboration and depth which we have fully investigated in the Book of the Etiquettes of Marriage (Kitāb Ādāb al-Nikāḥ) from the Quarter of Customs (Rubʿ al-ʿĀdāt) of the books of the Revival of the Religious Sciences (Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn); let it be sought from there.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) recommended four matters in marriage:

The first: Seeking a noble lineage (al-ḥasībah). He (peace be upon him) said: "Choose [carefully] for your sperm, and do not place it in other than suitable equals (al-akfāʾ)." And he said: "Beware of the green one upon a dung-heap (khaḍrāʾ al-diman)—that is, the beautiful woman of evil origin." Thus he (peace be upon him) interpreted it.

The second: The recommendation of a virgin (al-bikr), for she is more likely to foster affection (al-muʾālafah). He said to Jābir: "Why did you not marry a virgin, so that you might sport with her and she with you?"—for Jābir had married a widow (thayyib).

The third: The recommendation of a woman who is loving and fertile (al-wadūd al-walūd). He (peace be upon him) said: "Marry the loving and fertile, for I shall boast of your numbers before the nations." And he said: "A mat in the corner of the house is better than a woman who does not bear children."

The fourth: The recommendation of a woman from outside the close kin (al-ajnabiyyah). He (peace be upon him) said: "Do not marry close relatives, for the child is born weak (ḍāwiyan)—that is, thin." Perhaps this is due to the diminution of desire because of kinship.

The fifth: The recommendation of a righteous woman (al-ṣāliḥah). He (peace be upon him) said: "Upon you is the one possessed of religion; may your hands be dust-covered (taribat yadāk)."

I say: The Third Introduction: On Looking at Her After Desiring Her Marriage

This is recommended (mustaḥabb) due to his saying (peace be upon him): "Whoever intends to marry a woman, let him look at her, for that is more likely to foster harmony (iʾdām) between them." One should limit oneself to looking at the face, and this [is permissible] after resolving upon marriage if one is pleased with her. Her permission is not a condition for this looking; rather, the permission of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) suffices for it—contrary to Mālik. And this looking has been permitted for the sake of need; otherwise, the original principle is the prohibition of looking at unrelated women (ajnabiyyāt).

The custom here is to mention what is permissible to look at, and the discussion thereof falls into four topics:

The first: A man's looking at another man. This is permissible except at the ʿawrah—that which is between the navel and the knee. Touching is prohibited just as looking is prohibited. It is not prohibited for a man to look at his own private part, but it is disliked (makrūh) without need.

chapters.title_en: Two Subsidiary Points on the Gaze and Its Rulings
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرعان أحدهما أنه يحرم النظر إلى المرد بالشهوة ويحل بغير شهوه عند الأمن من الفتنة وعند خوف الفتنة وجهان أحدهما التحريم لأنهم في معنى المرأة والثاني الحل لما روي أن قوما وفدوا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيهم غلام حسن فأجلسه وراءه وقال ألا أخاف على نفسي ما أصاب أخي داود ولم يأمره بالاحتجاب عن الناس بخلاف النساء ولم يزل الصبيان بين الناس مكشوفين فالوجه الإباحة إلا في حق من أحس في نفسه بالفتنة فعند ذلك يحرم عليه بينه وبين الله تعالى إعادة النظر الثاني أن يكره للرجلين الاضطجاع في ثوب واحد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يفضي الرجل إلى الرجل في ثوب واحد ولا تفضي المرأة إلى المرأة في ثوب واحد الموضع الثاني نظر المرأة إلى المرأة وهو مباح إلا فيما بين السرة والركبة وقيل إنه كالنظر إلى المحارم وسيأتي والصحيح أن الذمية كالمسلمة وقيل إنه لا يحل للمسلمة التكشف للذمية الموضع الثالث نظر الرجل إلى المرأة فإن كانت منكوحة أو مملوكة حل النظر إلى جميع بدنها وفي النظر إلى فرجها فيه تردد وحمل الأصحاب النهي على أنه أراد به كراهية والكراهية في باطن الفرج أشد وإن كانت محرما نظر إلى ما يبدو في حالة المهنة كالوجه والأطراف ولا ينظر إلى العورة وفيما بين ذلك وجهان وقيل إن الثدي قد يلتحق بالوجه لأنه قد يبدو كثيرا فأمره أخف وإن كانت أجنبية حرم النظر إليها مطلقا ومنهم من جوز النظر إلى الوجه حيث تؤمن الفتنة وهذا يؤدي إلى التسوية بين النساء والمرد وهو بعيد لأن الشهوة وخوف الفتنة أمر باطن فالضبط بالأنوثة التي هي من الأسباب الظاهرة أقرب إلى المصلحة وكذلك لا يجوز للمخنث والعنين والشيخ الهم النظر حسما للباب ونظرا إلى الفحولة الظاهرة دون الشهوة الباطنة نعم يجوز للممسوح عند الأكثرين لأن الجب سبب ظاهر في قطع غائلة الفحولة وعليه يحمل قوله تعالى {غير أولي الإربة من الرجال} وكذلك الطفولة سبب ظاهر فلا يجب الاحتجاب عنهم نعم تستر العورة عن الذي ظهر فيه داعية الحكاية فإذا قارب البلوغ وظهر مبادئ الشهوة وجب الاحتجاب وقال القفال ثبت الحل فلا يرتفع إلا بسبب ظاهر وهو البلوغ ولا يستثنى عن هذه القاعدة إلا نظر الغلام إلى سيدته فإنه مباح لقوله تعالى {أو ما ملكت أيمانهن} ولعل السبب فيه الحاجة وقد قيل بتحريم ذلك لما فيه من الخطر ولكن ذلك يحوج إلى تعسف في تأويل الآية ومن المستثنيات النظر إلى الإماء حتى روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه قال لجارية متقنعة أتتشبهين بالحرائر يا لكعاء ولعل السبب فيه أن الرقيقة تحتاج إلى التردد في المهمات ومنهم من قال إنها كالحرة لا ينظر إليها إلا لحاجة الشراء وهو القياس ### | فرعان أحدهما ما أبين من المرأة يجوز النظر إليه إن لم يتميز بصورته عما للرجال كالقلامة وما ينتف من الشعر والجلدة المتكشطة وإن تميز كالعضو المبان والعقيصة فلا يحل النظر إليه الثاني الصبية لا يحل النظر إلى فرجها وفي النظر إلى وجهها وجهان أحدهما الجواز لأنها خرجت عن مظنة الشهوة بسبب ظاهر والثاني التحريم نظرا إلى جنس الأنوثة وعلى الجملة أمرها أهون من أمر العجوز فإنها محل للوطء والشهوات لا تنضبط الموضع الرابع نظر المرأة إلى الرجل أما نظرها إلى زوجها فكنظره إليها ونظرها إلى الأجانب فيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه كنظر الرجل إليها والثاني أنه كنظره إلى المحارم والثالث وهو الأصح أنها تنظر إلى ما وراء العورة وتحترز عند خوف الفتنة كما يحترز الرجل من النظر إلى الأمرد إذ لو استوى النظران لأمر الرجال أيضا بالتنقب كما أمر النساء هذا كله في النظر بغير حاجة فإن مست الحاجة لتحمل شهادة أو رغبة نكاح جاز النظر إلى الوجه ولا يحل النظر إلى العورة إلا لحاجة مؤكدة كمعالجة مرض شديد يخاف عليه فوت العضو أو طول الضنى ولتكن الحاجة في السوأتين آكد وهو أن تكون بحيث لا يعد التكشف لأجله هتكا للمروءة وتعذر فيه في العادة فإن ستر العورة من المروءات الواجبة ولم يجوز الإصطخري النظر إلى الفرج لتحمل شهادة الزنا وخالف فيه الأصحاب وما ذكره غير بعيد لأن ستر العورة وستر الفواحش كلاهما مقصودان فيختص تحمل الشهادة بما إذا وقع البصر عليه وفاقا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The physical act of sight; directing the eye toward an object; also used for deliberation and waiting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the intentional, purposeful glance (al-naẓar al-murād) that carries moral weight, as opposed to an accidental or involuntary glance (al-lamḥah al-khāṭifah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for ocular vision; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual consideration (taʾammul). Here, the ruling hinges on the literal sense, but the underlying cause (ʿillah) is the arousal of desire (shahwah).
- Root: ف-ت-ن (fa-ta-na)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trial, tribulation; the act of burning or smelting to purify gold—hence, a test that reveals one's inner state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Quranic lexicon, it is the divinely ordained trial that exposes the heart's inclination toward sin; here, it is the fear of succumbing to illicit desire.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used metaphorically for the inner turmoil that leads to transgression; the "fear of fitnah" is a subjective state, not an objective fact.
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿa-wa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The defect or blemish; the part of the body that must be concealed; the eye that has lost its sight.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The pudenda or intimate parts (sawʾatān) that are legally and morally obligatory to cover; the term extends to anything whose exposure invites corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the bodily parts; metaphorical for any vulnerability that must be guarded.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Taʿlīq (Conditional Suspension) — When a ruling is predicated on a subjective condition (e.g., "fear of fitnah"), the jurist must anchor it to an objective, observable cause (sabab ẓāhir) to render it enforceable, as seen in the distinction between the beardless youth (amrad) and the eunuch (mamsūḥ).
chapters.translation:
I say: This section contains two subsidiary points.

**The First Subsidiary Point:** It is unlawful (yaḥrumu) to gaze upon a beardless youth (al-murd) with lustful desire (shahwah), and it is lawful (yaḥillu) to gaze upon him without lust when one is secure from temptation (fitnah). When one fears temptation, there are two positions (wajhān): The first is that it is unlawful, for they are in the same category as women. The second is that it is lawful, due to what has been narrated—that a group of people came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and among them was a handsome young man. The Prophet seated him behind him and said: "I do not fear for myself what befell my brother David." He did not command him to veil himself from the people, unlike women. And young boys have always remained uncovered among the people. Thus, the preponderant position (al-wajh) is permissibility, except for one who senses within himself the stirring of temptation—for then it becomes unlawful for him, between him and Allah the Exalted, to repeat the glance.

**The Second Subsidiary Point:** It is disliked (yukrahu) for two men to lie together under a single garment. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«لَا يُفْضِي الرَّجُلُ إِلَى الرَّجُلِ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَلَا تُفْضِي الْمَرْأَةُ إِلَى الْمَرْأَةِ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ»} — "Let not a man touch a man's skin under a single garment, nor let a woman touch a woman's skin under a single garment."

**The Second Locus: The Woman's Gaze upon Another Woman.** This is permissible (mubāḥ), except regarding what lies between the navel and the knee. It has been said that it is like the gaze upon one's unmarriageable kin (maḥārim), and this will be discussed later. The correct position (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that a non-Muslim woman (dhimmīyah) is like a Muslim woman in this regard. It has been said that it is not lawful for a Muslim woman to uncover herself before a non-Muslim woman.

**The Third Locus: The Man's Gaze upon a Woman.** If she is his wife (mankūḥah) or his slave-girl (mamlūkah), it is lawful to gaze upon her entire body. Regarding gazing upon her private parts (farj), there is hesitation (taraddud); the companions (al-aṣḥāb) interpreted the prohibition as indicating dislike (karāhah), and the dislike is more severe regarding the inner part of the private part (bāṭin al-farj).

If she is an unmarriageable kin (maḥram), he may gaze upon what is ordinarily visible during the course of work (hihnah)—such as the face and the extremities (al-aṭrāf)—but he may not gaze upon the private parts (ʿawrah). Regarding what lies between these two categories, there are two positions. It has been said that the breast may be annexed to the face, for it is often exposed, so its matter is lighter.

If she is a foreign woman (ajnabīyah), gazing upon her is unlawful absolutely (ḥarama al-naẓar ilayhā muṭlaqan). Among the scholars, some permitted gazing upon the face where one is secure from temptation. But this leads to equating women with beardless youths—which is far-fetched, for lust and the fear of temptation are internal matters. Anchoring the ruling to femininity (unūthah), which is an external cause (sabab ẓāhir), is closer to the public interest (maṣlaḥah). Likewise, it is not permissible for the effeminate man (mukhannath), the impotent man (ʿanīn), and the decrepit old man (shaykh al-hamm) to gaze [upon women], in order to close the door (saddan lil-bāb) and with regard to the apparent masculinity (fuḥūlah ẓāhirah) rather than the inner lust. Yes, it is permissible for the eunuch (mamsūḥ) according to the majority (al-aktharīn), for castration (jabb) is an apparent cause that severs the threat of masculinity. Upon this is carried the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«غَيْرِ أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ»} — "Those men who have no need of women" (Quran 24:31). Likewise, childhood (ṭufūlah) is an apparent cause, so it is not obligatory to veil from them. Yes, the private parts must be covered from a child in whom the stirring of desire has appeared. When he approaches puberty and the beginnings of lust manifest, veiling becomes obligatory.

Al-Qaffāl said: "Permissibility is established, so it is not lifted except by an apparent cause—namely, puberty." No exception is made from this rule except the gaze of a young male slave (ghulām) upon his mistress (sayyidah), for it is permissible due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ»} — "Or what their right hands possess" (Quran 24:31). Perhaps the reason (sabab) for this is necessity (ḥājah). It has been said that this is unlawful due to the danger involved, but that would necessitate a strained interpretation (taʿassuf) of the verse.

Among the exceptions is gazing upon slave-women (imāʾ). It is narrated that ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to a slave-girl who had veiled herself: "Do you imitate free women, O you foolish girl?" Perhaps the reason is that the slave-woman needs to move about for important errands. Among the scholars, some said she is like a free woman—she is not to be gazed upon except for the need of purchase, and this is the analogical position (al-qiyās).

**Two Subsidiary Points:**

**The First:** What is severed from a woman—it is permissible to gaze upon it if it is not distinguished by its form as belonging to men, such as a nail clipping, plucked hair, or a scraped piece of skin. If it is distinguished—such as a severed limb or a braided lock of hair—then it is not lawful to gaze upon it.

**The Second:** It is not lawful to gaze upon the private part of a young girl (ṣabīyah). Regarding gazing upon her face, there are two positions: The first is permissibility, for she has exited the locus of lust due to an apparent cause. The second is prohibition, with regard to the genus of femininity. In sum, her matter is lighter than that of an old woman (ʿajūz), for the latter is a locus of intercourse and lusts that cannot be regulated.

**The Fourth Locus: The Woman's Gaze upon a Man.** As for her gaze upon her husband, it is like his gaze upon her. As for her gaze upon foreign men (ajānib), there are three positions: The first is that it is like the man's gaze upon her. The second is that it is like his gaze upon his unmarriageable kin. The third—and this is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ)—is that she may gaze upon what is beyond the private parts, and she must be cautious when fearing temptation, just as a man is cautious in gazing upon a beardless youth. For if the two gazes were equivalent, then men would also be commanded to veil their faces, just as women are commanded.

All of this pertains to gazing without need. If need arises—such as bearing testimony (taḥammul al-shahādah) or desiring marriage (raghbah fī nikāḥ)—then gazing upon the face is permissible. It is not lawful to gaze upon the private parts except for a pressing need, such as treating a severe illness where one fears the loss of a limb or prolonged suffering. The need regarding the two private parts (sawʾatān) is even more stringent—it must be such that uncovering for its sake is not deemed a violation of manliness (hātik al-murūʾah), and it is ordinarily unattainable otherwise. For covering the private parts is among the obligatory virtues (murūʾāt wājibah).

Al-Iṣṭakhrī did not permit gazing upon the private part for the purpose of bearing testimony to adultery (shahādat al-zinā), and the companions differed with him on this. What he mentioned is not far-fetched, for both covering the private parts and concealing indecencies (satr al-fawāḥish) are intended objectives. Thus, bearing testimony is specifically restricted to when the gaze falls upon it accidentally, by agreement.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | المقدمة الرابعة في الخطبة وآدابها

وينبغي أن يقدم النظر عليها إذ في الرد بعد الخطبة إيحاش والتصريح بخطبة
المعتدة حرام والتعريض جائز في عدة الوفاة وحرام في عدة الرجعية وفي عدة
البائنة وجهان
وسبب التحريم أنها مستوحشة بالطلاق فربما كذبت في انقضاء العدة مسارعة
إلى مكافأة الزوج
والتعريض هو أن يقول رب راغب فيك وإذا حللت فآذنيني كما قال رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا تجوز  الخطبة على خطبة الغير بعد الإجابة وتجوز
قبل الإجابة وهل يكون السكوت كالإجابة فيه قولان وقد روي أنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم قال لفاطمة بنت قيس إذا حللت فآذنيني فلما حلت قال انكحي أسامة فقالت
خطبني أبو جهم ومعاوية قال أما معاوية فصعلوك لا مال له وأما أبو جهم فلا
يضع عصاه عن عاتقة أي يداوم الضرب وقيل يدوام السفر وذلك يدل على جواز ذكر
الغائب بما يكرهه إذا كان فيه مصلحة لغيره ولذلك قال عليه السلام
اذكروا الفاسق بما فيه كي يحذره الناس

### | المقدمة الخامسة في الخطبة

ويستحب ذلك عند الخطبة وعند إنشاء العقد وسواء يخطب العاقدان أو غيرهما
فهو حسن وإن قال الولي الحمد لله والصلاة على رسول الله زوجتك فلانه فقال
الزوج الحمد لله والصلاة على رسول الله قبلت صح النكاح وكان أحسن وتخلل هذه
الكلمة اليسيرة وهي متعلقة بغرض العقد لا يقطع الجواب عن الخطاب وفيه وجه
بعيد أنه يقطع
هذا هو الكلام في قسم المقدمات جرينا فيه على ترتيب الوجود إذ البداية
بالرغبة ثم بالنظر ثم بالخطبة ثم بالخطبة فنشرع في شرح العقد

### | القسم الثاني من الكتاب في الأركان والشرائط

وهي أربعة الصيغة والمحل والشاهد والولي
الأول الصيغة وهي الإيجاب والقبول الدالان على جزم الرضا دلالة صريحة
قاطعة وفيه مسائل ستة
الأولى أن الصريح هو كلمة الإنكاح والتزويج فلا يقوم لفظ آخر مقامهما لأن
النكاح يشتمل على أحكام غريبة لا يحيط بجميعها لفظ من حيث اللغة فيتعين
اللفظ المحيط بها شرعا ولذلك لا نزيد أيضا في صرائح الطلاق على ما ورد في
القرآن
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ينعقد النكاح بلفظ الهبة والبيع والتمليك وكل
ما يفيد معنى التمليك

chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ ط ب (Kha-Ṭā-Bā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address, to deliver an oration, to seek in marriage — the act of requesting a woman's hand with explicit or allusive speech.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The formal request of marriage (khiṭbah) as a pre-contractual declaration of intent, distinct from the contract itself (ʿaqd), carrying moral and legal weight in the Shariah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — direct verbal proposal; metaphorical (majāz) — allusive speech (taʿrīḍ) that hints at intent without explicit commitment.
- Root: ع ق د (ʿAyn-Qāf-Dāl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tie, to bind, to knot — the firm fastening of a covenant.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The marriage contract (ʿaqd al-nikāḥ) as a binding legal tie requiring explicit offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl) that decisively indicate consent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical tying of a knot; metaphorical — the legal binding of two parties through mutual agreement.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Continuity (al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sharṭ) — In the phrase "If you become lawful, then inform me" (fa-ādhinīnī), the imperative is syntactically dependent on the conditional clause, indicating a deferred permission contingent upon the expiration of the waiting period (ʿiddah).
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth preliminary discourse concerns the marriage proposal (khiṭbah) and its etiquette.

It is fitting that one should give consideration to it beforehand, for rejection after a proposal causes estrangement (īḥāsh). And the explicit proposal (taṣrīḥ) to a woman undergoing the waiting period (muʿtaddah) is forbidden (ḥarām), while allusive speech (taʿrīḍ) is permissible in the waiting period of death (ʿiddat al-wafāh) but forbidden in the waiting period of a revocable divorce (ʿiddat al-rajʿiyyah). Concerning the waiting period of an irrevocable divorce (ʿiddat al-bāʾinah), there are two opinions (wajhān).

The cause of this prohibition is that she is distressed by the divorce (mustawḥishah), and perhaps she might lie about the completion of her waiting period out of haste to reciprocate the husband's action.

Allusive speech (taʿrīḍ) is that one says: "Perhaps there is one desirous of you, and when you become lawful, then inform me" — just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said. And it is not permissible to propose over the proposal of another (al-khiṭbah ʿalā khiṭbat al-ghayr) after acceptance, but it is permissible before acceptance. And whether silence is equivalent to acceptance — therein are two opinions (qawlān).

It has been narrated that he (peace be upon him) said to Fāṭimah bint Qays: "When you become lawful, then inform me." When she became lawful, he said: "Marry Usāmah." She said: "Abū Jahm and Muʿāwiyah proposed to me." He said: "As for Muʿāwiyah, he is a penniless pauper (ṣaʿlūk) with no wealth; and as for Abū Jahm, he does not lay down his staff from his shoulder" — meaning he continually beats [his wives], and it was said: he continually travels. This indicates the permissibility of mentioning an absent person with what he dislikes when therein lies a benefit for others. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: "Mention the wicked person with what is in him, so that people may beware of him."

I say: The fifth preliminary discourse concerns the sermon (khuṭbah).

It is recommended (mustaḥabb) at the time of the proposal and at the time of concluding the contract. Whether the two contracting parties deliver the sermon or others do so, it is commendable. If the guardian (walī) says: "Praise be to Allah, and blessings upon the Messenger of Allah — I give you in marriage so-and-so," and the husband says: "Praise be to Allah, and blessings upon the Messenger of Allah — I accept," the marriage is valid (ṣaḥḥa al-nikāḥ) and it is more excellent. This brief utterance, which pertains to the purpose of the contract, does not sever the response from the address. And there is a remote opinion (wajh baʿīd) that it does sever.

This concludes the discourse on the section of preliminaries. We have proceeded therein according to the order of existence, for the beginning is with desire (raghbah), then with consideration (naẓar), then with the proposal (khiṭbah), then with the sermon (khuṭbah). We now commence the explanation of the contract.

I say: The second section of the book concerns the pillars (arkān) and conditions (sharāʾiṭ).

They are four: the formula (ṣīghah), the subject matter (maḥall), the witnesses (shāhid), and the guardian (walī).

The first is the formula (ṣīghah), which is the offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl) that indicate decisiveness of consent (jazm al-riḍā) with explicit, conclusive indication (dalālah ṣarīḥah qāṭiʿah). Therein are six questions.

The first: The explicit term (ṣarīḥ) is the word "marriage" (inkāḥ) and "wedlock" (tazwīj). No other word stands in their place, for marriage comprises peculiar rulings (aḥkām gharībah) that no single word encompasses linguistically. Thus, the word that encompasses them is specified by the Sacred Law (sharʿan). For this reason, we do not add to the explicit terms of divorce (ṣarāʾiḥ al-ṭalāq) beyond what is mentioned in the Quran.

Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The marriage contract is concluded with the word "gift" (hibah), "sale" (bayʿ), "transfer of ownership" (tamlīk), and every word that conveys the meaning of transfer of ownership.

chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع الصحيح أن ترجمتها بالفارسية وسائر اللغات يقوم مقامها لأنها في معناها وقيل يقوم مقامها عند العجز فقط وقيل لا يجوز ذلك أيضا وعلى العاجز أن يستنيب القادر الثانية لا ينعقد النكاح بالكنايات مع النية لأنها تتعلق بتفهيم الشاهد ولا مطلع له على النية ويصح بها الإبراء والفسخ والطلاق وما يستقل به الإنسان وأما البيع وما ليفتقر إلى القبول ففيه وجهان مأخذهما أن القائل هل يكون كالشاهد حتى لا يكفي تفهيمه بقرينة الحال فرع إذا قال زوجتكها فينبغي أن يقول الزوج قبلت نكاحها أو قبلت هذا النكاح فلو اقتصر على قوله قبلت ففيه وجهان مأخذهما أن قوله قبلت ليس صريحا لنفسه ما لم ينضم فيه الإيجاب السابق الثالثة نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه على أن النكاح ينعقد بالاستيجاب والإيجاب وهو قوله زوجنيها وقول الولي وزجتكها ونص في البيع على قولين وقطع الأصحاب بأن ذلك يكفي في الخلع والعتق على المال والصلح عن دم العمد لأن العوض غير مقصود فيها وإنما لا ينعقد البيع على قول لأنه قد يقول بعني على سبيل استبانة الرغبة من غير بت الرضا في الحال لأنه قد يقع بعته بخلاف النكاح ومن الأصحاب من طرد القولين في النكاح ومنهم من طرد القولين في الخلع والصلح وغير هذا وهو غريب لكنه منقاس جدا الرابعة النكاح لا يقبل حقيقة التعليق مثل أن يقول إذا جاء رأس الشهر فقد زوجتك ولا يحتمل أيضا لفظه مثل أن يقول إن كان قد ولد لي بنت فقد زوجتكها ثم بان أنه كان قد ولدت فلا يصح النكاح بصيغة التعليق وكذلك لو قال إن انقضت عدتها فقد زوجتك وكان قد انقضت وفيه وجه أنه يصح مأخوذ من الوجهين فيما إذا قال إن كان أبي مات فقد بعت منك ماله الخامسة نكاح الشغار باطل للنهي الوارد فيه وصورته الكاملة أن يقول زوجتك ابتني على أن نزوجني ابنتك أو أختك على أن يكون بضع كل واحد منهما صداق الأخرى ومهما انعقد لك نكاح ابنتي انعقد لي نكاح ابنتك وهذا يشتمل على ثلاثة أمور تعليق وشرط عقد واشتراك في البضع بجعله صداقا وقد قال القفال إنما يبطل العقد بالتعليق وهو المراد بالشغار مأخوذا من قولهم شغر الكلب برجله أي لا ترفع رجل ابنتي ما لم أرفع رجل ابنتك وكان ذلك من عادة العرب لأنفتها من التزويج فقال لو اقتصر على شرط التزويج في العقد وعلى إصداق البضع صح العقد لأن النكاح لا يفسد بالشرائط الفاسدة وجماهير الأصحاب عللوا بالاشتراك في البضع بجعله صداقا وقالوا يشبه ذلك ما لو نكحت الحرة عبدا على أن تكون رقبته صداقا لها فإن ذلك يبطله ومنهم من قال لو قال زوجتك ابنتي على أن تزوجني ابنتك واقتصر عليه بطل أيضا لما فيه من الخلو عن المهر وأخذ الشغار من قولهم شغر البلد إذا خلا من الوالي وما ذكره القفال أقيس وما ذكره الجماهير إلى الخبر أقرب وأما الإبطال بمجرد اشتراط العقد والخلو عن المهر فبعيد السادسة تأقيت النكاح باطل وهو أن يقول زوجتك شهرا وذلك هو نكاح المتعة سمي بها لأن مقصوده مجرد التمتع ### | الركن الثاني المحل وهي المنكوحة وشرطها أن تكون خلية من الموانع وهي قريب من عشرين ألا تكون منكوحة الغير أو في عدة الغير أو مرتدة أو مجوسية أو زنديقة لا تنسب إلى ملة أو كتابية دانت بدينهم بعد التبديل أو بعد المبعث وليست مع ذلك من بني إسرائيل أو تكون رقيقة والناكح حر واجد طول حرة أو غير خائف من العنت أو مملوكة للناكح بعضها أو كلها أو كانت من المحارم إما من نسب أو رضاع أو مصاهرة أو تكون خامسة بأن يكون تحته أربع أو يكون تحت الزوج أختها أو عمتها أو خالتها فيكون بالنكاح جامعا بينهما أو يكون الناكح قد طلقها ثلاثا ولم يطأها بعده زوج أخر أو يكون الناكح قد لاعن عنها أو تكون محرمة بحج أو عمرة أو تكون ثيبا صغيرة أو يتيمة أو كانت من أزواج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك لا يوجد في هذا الزمان فهذه مجامع الموانع وسيأتي شرحها في القسم الثالث من الكتاب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-أ (k-f-') — *Note: This root is not among the prohibited list; however, to comply with the instruction against repeating previously used roots, I shall instead anchor on the root ق-و-م (q-w-m) for "stands in place of" (qāma maqāmahā).*
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ق-و-م denotes "to stand upright, to be established, to take the place of something" — the core sense of substitution and standing in the stead of another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, qiyām (standing in place) implies functional equivalence in fulfilling the maqṣūd (intended purpose) of an act, not mere formal identity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) standing is physical; here it is metaphorical (majāz) — the translation "stands in the place of" the Arabic formula in conveying the same legal meaning.
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿAqd is "to tie, to bind firmly" — the knotting of a covenant or contract.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, ʿaqd denotes the binding legal nexus between offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl) producing obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The "tying" is metaphorical for the mutual commitment of two parties; the literal knot is physical.
- Root: ش-غ-ر (sh-gh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Shighār derives from shaghara al-kalb (the dog raising its leg to urinate) and shaghara al-balad (the town being empty of its governor).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal terminology, it denotes a marriage conditioned upon another marriage, with each woman's dower being the other's sexual access (buḍʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is metaphorical — the "emptiness" of the marriage from a proper dower, or the "raising of the leg" as a pre-Islamic Arab custom of refusing marriage until reciprocal terms were met.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Conditional Suspension) — In Arabic syntax, a conditional particle (in, idhā) suspends the apodosis upon the protasis; in legal formulation, this maps to the invalidity of suspending a marriage contract upon a future or unknown condition, unlike in sales where the rule is disputed.
chapters.translation:
I say: The correct position is that translating the marriage formula into Persian and other languages stands in its place, because it conveys the same meaning. And it was said: it stands in its place only in cases of incapacity. And it was said: that is not permissible at all. And the one who is incapable must appoint a capable proxy.

The second [subsidiary issue]: The marriage contract is not concluded by allusive expressions (kināyāt) even with intention, because they pertain to conveying [the meaning] to the witness, and he has no access to the intention. But by them are valid: acquittal (ibrāʾ), dissolution (faskh), divorce (ṭalāq), and whatever a person undertakes independently. As for sale and what requires acceptance, there are two positions therein, whose basis is whether the speaker is like a witness such that conveying [the meaning] to him by contextual indication (qarīnat al-ḥāl) is not sufficient.

A subsidiary issue: If he says "I have married her to you" (zawwajtukahā), the husband should say "I accept her marriage" (qabiltu nikāḥahā) or "I accept this marriage" (qabiltu hādhā al-nikāḥ). If he confines himself to saying "I accept" (qabiltu), there are two positions therein, whose basis is that his saying "I accept" is not explicit by itself unless the preceding offer is conjoined to it.

The third [subsidiary issue]: Al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — explicitly ruled that marriage is concluded by the formula of asking for marriage (istījāb) and granting it (ījāb), namely his saying "marry her to me" (zawwijnīhā) and the guardian's saying "I have married her to you" (zawwajtukahā). And he explicitly ruled in sale two positions. And the associates (al-aṣḥāb) definitively ruled that this suffices in khulʿ (divorce by ransom), manumission for a consideration, and settlement (ṣulḥ) regarding the blood of intentional homicide, because the consideration is not the intended object therein. Sale is not concluded — according to one position — because he might say "sell to me" by way of ascertaining desire without definitively resolving satisfaction at the moment, for he might [merely] be saying "I will buy it" — unlike marriage. And among the associates are those who extended the two positions to marriage, and among them are those who extended the two positions to khulʿ and settlement and other than that. And this is odd, but it is highly analogically consistent.

The fourth [subsidiary issue]: Marriage does not admit true suspension (taʿlīq), such as his saying "when the beginning of the month comes, I have married her to you." Nor does it admit a [retroactive] conditional formulation, such as his saying "if a daughter has been born to me, I have married her to you," and then it becomes apparent that a daughter had been born — the marriage is not valid by the conditional formula. Likewise, if he said "if her waiting period has expired, I have married her to you," and it had expired. And there is a position that it is valid, derived from the two positions in the case where he says "if my father has died, I have sold you his property."

The fifth [subsidiary issue]: The marriage of shighār is void due to the prohibition reported concerning it. Its complete form is that he says: "I marry my daughter to you on condition that you marry your daughter or sister to me, on condition that the sexual access (buḍʿ) of each one of them is the dower of the other." And whenever the marriage of my daughter is concluded for you, the marriage of your daughter is concluded for me. This comprises three matters: suspension (taʿlīq), a condition in the contract, and sharing in sexual access by making it a dower. Al-Qaffāl said: "The contract is only invalidated by the suspension, and that is what is meant by shighār," derived from their saying "the dog raised its leg" (shaghara al-kalb bi-rijlihi), i.e., "I will not raise the leg of my daughter unless you raise the leg of your daughter." And that was from the custom of the Arabs, due to their pride concerning marriage. He said: "If one confined himself to the condition of marriage in the contract and to making sexual access the dower, the contract would be valid, because marriage is not corrupted by corrupt conditions." And the majority of the associates (jumhūr al-aṣḥāb) explained [the invalidity] by the sharing in sexual access by making it a dower, and they said: this resembles the case where a free woman marries a slave on condition that his person (raqabah) be her dower — for that invalidates it. And among them are those who said: if he said "I marry my daughter to you on condition that you marry your daughter to me" and confined himself to that, it is also void, due to what it contains of being devoid of a dower. And the taking of shighār from their saying "the town was empty" (shaghara al-balad) when it is devoid of its governor. What al-Qaffāl mentioned is more analogically sound (aqyas), and what the majority mentioned is closer to the report (khabar). As for invalidation merely by the condition of the contract and the absence of a dower, that is remote.

The sixth [subsidiary issue]: Fixing a time limit for marriage is void, namely his saying "I marry her to you for a month." That is the marriage of mutʿah (temporary pleasure marriage). It was named thus because its sole purpose is mere enjoyment (tamattuʿ).

### | The Second Pillar: The Subject (al-Maḥall)

It is the woman being married. Its condition is that she be free of impediments (mawāniʿ), which number nearly twenty: that she not be the wife of another, nor in the waiting period (ʿiddah) of another, nor an apostate (murtaddah), nor a Magian (majūsiyyah), nor a zindīqah who does not ascribe to a religion, nor a Scriptural woman (kitābiyyah) who follows their religion after the alteration [of scripture] or after the mission [of the Prophet] — and she is not, with that, from the Children of Israel — nor a slave woman while the free man who marries her is able to afford a free woman, or does not fear falling into fornication (ʿanat); nor [a slave] partially or wholly owned by the one marrying her; nor one of the prohibited relatives (maḥārim), whether by lineage (nasab), fosterage (riḍāʿ), or affinity (muṣāharah); nor a fifth wife, such that he has four [already] under him; nor that the husband has her sister, paternal aunt, or maternal aunt [already married to him], such that by this marriage he would be combining between them; nor that the one marrying has divorced her three times and no other husband has had intercourse with her afterward; nor that the one marrying has pronounced liʿān (mutual imprecation) against her; nor that she be in a state of iḥrām for Hajj or ʿUmrah; nor that she be a minor who has been previously married (thayyib) or an orphan; nor that she be one of the wives of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and that is not found in this age. These are the comprehensive categories of impediments, and their detailed explanation will come in the third section of the book.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الركن الثالث الشهود

وهو شرط ولكن تساهلنا بتسميته ركنا ولا ينعقد النكاح إلا بحضور عدلين ولا
ينعقد بحضور رجل وامرأتين خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقال داود لا حاجة
إلى الشهادة وقال مالك يكفي الإعلان وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
لا نكاح إلا
بولي وشاهدي عدل فنقول لا بد من حضور من هو أهل للشهادة فلا يكفي حضور
الصبي والذمي والرقيق والأصم والفاسق وفي حضور الأعمى خلاف
لأنه أهل لبعض الشهادات
ولو حضر ابن الزوجين أو أبو الزوجين ففيه أربعة أوجه
أحدها الانعقاد لأنه أهل على الجملة
والثاني لا لأنه ليس أهلا في هذا النكاح
والثالث أنه إن حضر ابن الزوج وابن الزوجة لم يكتف لأنه لا يتصور الإثبات
وإن حضر ابنان لأحدهما جاز لأنه يمكن الإثبات على والدها
والرابع أنهما إن كانا ابنيها صح وإن كانا ابني الزوج لم يصح لأن الحاجة
إلى الإثبات عليها عند الجحود لا على الزوج فيقبل عليها قول ابنيها
وتجري هذه الزوجه في عدوي الزوجين
ولو حضر من حاله في الفسق مستور على الزوجين جميعا صح العقد على الأصح
وذكر المحاملي فيه خلافا ويعضده أن مستور الحرية لا يكفي حضوره على الأظهر
لكن الحرية مكشوفة في الغالب والفسق خفي وفي المنع من المستور حرج وتضييق
فإن صححنا فبان بينه عادلة فسقهما حالة العقد ففي تبين بطلان العقد قولان
كالقولين في نقض القضاء المبني على قولهما
ولا التفات إلى قولهما كنا فاسقين ولو قال الزوج كنت أعرف فسقه حالة
العقد وأنكرت المرأة قال الصيدلاني ينزل منزلة الطلاق حتى يتشطر المهر قبل
الدخول وبعده يجب جميع المهر وتعود إليه بطلقتين إن نكحها ونص الشافعي رضي
الله عنه على أن الحر إذا نكح أمة ثم قال كنت واجدا طول الحرة بانت منه
بطلقة
أما تشطير المهر فمعقول لأنه فراق حصل بجهته لا بزعم المرأة وأما جعله
طلاقا ولم يجر عقد فليس يتبين لي وجهه إلا أن يجعل طلاقا في حق المرأة
المنكرة خاصة أو يجعل في حق الزوج طلاقا في الظاهر لجريان الشهادة على ظاهر
النكاح لا بينه وبين الله تعالى
فرع تردد الشيخ أبو محمد في أن المعلن بالفسق إذا تاب في  مجلس العقد هل
يلتحق بالمستور وكان عادته استتابة الحاضرين ووجهه أنه يمكن أن يكون صادقا
في توبته
ولا خلاف في أنه لا يشترط الإشهاد على رضاء المرأة

### | الركن الرابع العاقدان

وهو الزوج والولي لأن المرأة مسلوبة العبارة عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه في
عقد النكاح فلا تصح عبارتها بالنيابة ولا بالوكالة ولا بالاستقلال لا في
التزويج ولا في القبول ويصح إقرارها بالنكاح على الجديد لأن شرط الولي إنما
ورد في الإنشاء قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا نكاح إلا بولي إلا
أنها لو أقرت وكذبها الولي قال القفال لا تقبل لأنها أقرت على الولي
بالتزويج ومنهم من قال تقبل لأنها مقرة على نفسها بالرق
ثم إن اعتبرنا تصديق الولي فكان غائبا سلمناها في الحال إلى الزوج
بإقرارها للضرورة
إذ يعسر ملازمة الولي حضرا وسفرا لكن لو رجع وكذب فالظاهر أنه يحال
بينهما لزوال الضرورة
وصيغة الإقرار أن تقول زوجني الولي منه فلو أقرت بالزوجيه ولم تضف إلى
الولي ففيه خلاف مبني على أن دعوى النكاح مطلقا من غير التقييد بالشرط هل
تسمع
فأما إقرار الولي المجبر فنافذ إن أقر في حالة القدرة على الإجبار وأما
أبو حنيفة رحمه الله فقد قضى بأنها تزوج نفسها
لكن الولي يفسخ العقد إن وضعت نفسها تحت غير كفؤ وقال مالك تزوج الدنية
نفسها دون الشريفة
وعندنا أن الوطء في النكاح بغير ولي يوجب المهر للشبهة ولا يوجب الحد
وقال الصيرفي يجب الحد وقال بعض الأصحاب ينقض قضاء الحنفي بصحة نكاح بلا
ولي لمخالفته الحديث الظاهر وتفاصيل أحكام الولاية يستوفيه بابان باب في
الولي باب في المولي عليه
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في الأولياء وفيه فصول - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, witnessing, giving testimony; the root denotes being present at an event and bearing witness to it with one's senses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, shahādah is the act of establishing a right before a judge through truthful testimony; it is a form of bearing witness to a contractual reality (ʿaqd) that requires moral probity (ʿadālah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical presence (ḥuḍūr); metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the legal act of testifying to an occurrence, even if the witness was not physically present at the inception.
- Root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Nearness, guardianship, authority; the walī is the one who stands in proximity to another to manage their affairs.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Walāyah in marriage is a divinely-ordained guardianship over the woman's consent, since she is deemed deficient in independent contractual expression (ʿibārah) in the marriage contract.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: proximity in place or kinship; metaphorical: legal authority and custodianship over another's contractual capacity.
- Root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Straightness, equity, moral probity; the ʿadl is one whose testimony is accepted due to uprightness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAdālah is the moral and religious uprightness that renders one's testimony legally probative (muʿtabar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical straightness; metaphorical: moral rectitude in religious observance and social conduct.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Ellipsis (al-Sharṭ bi-Ḥadhf al-Jawāb) — In the Prophetic statement «لا نكاح إلا بولي وشاهدي عدل», the negative particle lā with illā functions as a restrictive conditional, where the implied apodosis is "the marriage is not valid" (lā yaṣiḥḥu), governing the entire legal ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third pillar is the witnesses (al-shuhūd). It is actually a condition (sharṭ), but we have been lenient in calling it a pillar. The marriage contract is not concluded except in the presence of two upright witnesses (ʿadlayn), and it is not concluded in the presence of one man and two women, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him). Dāwūd said: There is no need for testimony. Mālik said: Public announcement (iʿlān) suffices. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«لا نكاح إلا بولي وشاهدي عدل»} — "There is no marriage except with a guardian and two upright witnesses."

We say: The presence of one who is qualified for testimony is indispensable. Thus, the presence of a minor, a dhimmī, a slave, a deaf person, or a sinner (fāsiq) is not sufficient. Regarding the presence of a blind person, there is a difference of opinion, because he is qualified for some types of testimony.

If the son of the two spouses, or the father of the two spouses, is present [as a witness], there are four aspects (awjuh):
First: The contract is concluded, because he is qualified in general.
Second: It is not concluded, because he is not qualified in this particular marriage.
Third: If the son of the husband and the son of the wife are present, it is not sufficient, because establishing [the marriage] is inconceivable [against the father]; but if two sons of one of them are present, it is permissible, because establishing [the marriage] against her father is possible.
Fourth: If they are her two sons, it is valid; if they are the husband's two sons, it is not valid, because the need is to establish [the marriage] against her at the time of denial, not against the husband. Thus, the testimony of her two sons is accepted against her.

This same discussion applies to the two enemies of the spouses (ʿadaway al-zawjayn).

If one whose state of sinfulness (fisq) is concealed (mustūr) from both spouses is present, the contract is valid according to the most correct opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ). Al-Maḥāmilī mentioned a difference of opinion regarding this. It is supported [by the view of invalidity] that the presence of one whose freedom is concealed is not sufficient according to the most apparent opinion (al-aẓhar). However, freedom is generally manifest, while sinfulness is hidden, and in prohibiting the concealed sinner there is hardship (ḥaraj) and constriction.

If we deem the contract valid, and then it becomes evident that both witnesses were sinners at the time of the contract, there are two opinions (qawlān) regarding the nullification of the contract, like the two opinions regarding the reversal of a judicial ruling (naqḍ al-qaḍāʾ) based on their testimony.

No attention is paid to their statement, "We were sinners." If the husband says, "I knew of their sinfulness at the time of the contract," and the woman denies this, al-Ṣaydalānī said: It is treated as a divorce (ṭalāq), such that half the dowry (mahr) is due before consummation, and after consummation the full dowry is due, and she returns to him with two divorces if he marries her. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) explicitly stated that if a free man marries a slave woman, then says, "I was able to afford a free woman," she is separated from him by one divorce.

As for the halving of the dowry, it is intelligible, because it is a separation (furqah) that occurred due to his own action, not due to the woman's claim. As for making it a divorce, while no contract was executed [by him], I do not see the basis for this, except that it is made a divorce with respect to the denying woman specifically, or it is made a divorce with respect to the husband in the external sense (fī al-ẓāhir), because testimony runs on the external appearance of the marriage, not between him and Allah Almighty.

Branch (farʿ): Shaykh Abū Muḥammad hesitated regarding whether one who openly commits sin (al-muʿlin bi-al-fisq), if he repents during the session of the contract, is treated as one whose sin is concealed (mustūr). His practice was to require repentance from those present. The basis for [treating him as mustūr] is that he might be truthful in his repentance.

There is no disagreement that witnessing the woman's consent is not a condition.

### The Fourth Pillar: The Two Contracting Parties

It is the husband and the guardian (al-walī), because the woman is stripped of contractual expression (maslūbat al-ʿibārah) according to al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) in the marriage contract. Thus, her expression is not valid by proxy (niyābah), nor by agency (wakālah), nor independently — neither in giving herself in marriage (tazwīj) nor in acceptance (qabūl). However, her acknowledgment (iqrār) of the marriage is valid according to the new opinion (al-jadīd), because the condition of the guardian was only stipulated for the origination (inshāʾ) of the contract. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«لا نكاح إلا بولي»} — "There is no marriage except with a guardian."

Yet if she acknowledges [the marriage] and the guardian denies it, al-Qaffāl said: It is not accepted, because she is acknowledging against the guardian that he gave her in marriage. Some said: It is accepted, because she is acknowledging against herself regarding the marriage bond (riqq).

Then, if we consider the guardian's confirmation [necessary], and he is absent, we hand her over to the husband immediately based on her acknowledgment, out of necessity (ḍarūrah), since it is difficult for the guardian to remain with her constantly, whether present or traveling. But if he returns and denies, the apparent ruling is that they are separated, because the necessity has ceased.

The formula of acknowledgment is that she says: "The guardian married me to him." If she acknowledges the marriage (zawjiyyah) without attributing it to the guardian, there is a difference of opinion, built upon whether a claim of marriage in absolute terms, without restriction to the condition, is heard [in court].

As for the acknowledgment of the guardian who has the power of compulsion (al-walī al-mujbir), it is effective if he acknowledges while able to compel. As for Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him), he ruled that she marries herself, but the guardian may annul the contract if she places herself under someone who is not her equal (kufʾ). Mālik said: The lowly woman (al-daniyyah) marries herself, but not the noble woman (al-sharīfah).

In our school, intercourse in a marriage without a guardian necessitates the dowry due to ambiguity (shubhah), but does not necessitate the ḥadd punishment. Al-Ṣayrafī said: It necessitates the ḥadd. Some of our companions said: The ruling of a Ḥanafī judge regarding the validity of a marriage without a guardian is overturned, because it contradicts the apparent hadith. The details of the rulings on guardianship are covered in two chapters: a chapter on the guardian (al-walī) and a chapter on the one under guardianship (al-muwallā ʿalayh).

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الأول في أسباب الولاية

وهي أربعة
الأبوة والجدودة في معناها
والعصوبة بالنسب
والولاء
والسلطنة أما الأب والجد أب الأب فلهما منصب الإجبار في حالة البكارة ولو
بعد البلوغ وفي البنين في الصغر دون الكبر وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه
البكر البالغة لا تجبر على النكاح والثيب الصغيرة يجوز أجبارها عنده
ونظر الشافعي رضي الله عنه إلى الثيابة والبكارة لقوله عليه السلام الثيب
أحق بنفسها من وليها والبكر تستأمر في نفسها وإذنها صماتها
ومعنى إجبارها أن الأب لو زوجها من كفؤ وهي ساخطة نفذ ولو التمست التزويج
من الولي وجبت الإجابة وإن كانت مجبرة كالصبي الذي يلتمس الطعام
ولو عينت كفؤا وعين الولي كفؤا فمنهم من قال يجب رعاية حقها في الأعيان
وإنما حظ الولي في الكفاءة فقط ومنهم من قال تعيين الولي أولى
ومهما ثابت ولو بالزنا لم تجبر ولو انفتق جلد العذرة بوثبة أو طفرة
فالأظهر أنها بكر لأن واطئها مبتكر
ولم ير أبو حنيفة للزنا أثرا في إزالة حكم البكارة
فأما العصبات من جهة النسب كالإخوة والأعمام وأولادهم فليس لهم الإجبار
بحال وإنما لهم تزويج البكر والثيب بعد البلوغ برضاهها وهل لهم الاكتفاء
بصمت البكر وجهان
أحدهما نعم لظاهر الحديث
والثاني لا لأن السكوت مردد ومعنى الحديث حث المجبر على مراجعتها من غير
تكليف نطق
وأما الولي المعتق فولايته كولاية العصبات وأما السلطان فولي في أربعة
مواضع عند عدم الولي وغيبته وعضله وإذا أراد الولي أن يزوج من نفسه وليس
للسلطان ولاية الإجبار خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
وليس للوصي ولاية التزويج وإن فوض إليه الموصي إذ ليس له قرابة تدعوه إلى
الشفقة والنظر ولا حظ له في الكفاءة

### | الفصل الثاني في ترتيب الأولياء من القرابة والولاء والسلطنه

وجهة القرابة مقدمة على الولاء والولاء مقدم على السلطنة والازدحام يفرض
في النسب والولاء
أما النسب فالأب ثم الجد ولهما ولاية الإجبار ثم ترتيب باقي العصبات
كترتيبهم في الميراث إلا في ثلاث مسائل
إحداها أن الابن عصبة في الميراث ولا يزوج بحكم النبوة خلافا لأبي حنيفة
رحمه الله نعم إن كان قاضيا أو عصبة أو ابن عم أو معتقا زوج بهذه الأسباب
فالبنوة لا تمنع ولا تفيد
الثانية الجد في الميراث يقاسم الإخوة وهاهنا يقدم الجد لأنه على عمود
النسب
وشفقته أكمل
الثالثة أن الأخ من الأب والأم مقدم على الأخ من الأب في الميراث وكذلك
في الصلاة على الجنازة وفي الولاية قولان لأن جهة الأمومة لا مدخل لها في
الولاية فيجوز أن لا توجب ترجيحا واختار المزني التقديم في التزويج أيضا
ويجري القولان في العم من الأب والأم والعم من الأب وابنيهما ولا يجري في
ابني عم أحدهما أخ لأم لأن أخوة الأم هاهنا لا تفيد عصوبة في الميراث وكذلك
إذا كان لها ابنا ابن عم أحدهما ابنها أو ابنا معتق أحدهما منها فلا ترجيح
ونص ابن الحداد على أن ابنها من المعتق مقدم على سائر البنين وهو بعيد
أما ترتيب الولاء فالمتعق أولى فإن لم يكن فعصباته فإن لم يكونوا فمعتق
المعتق ثم عصباته وترتيب عصبات المعتق كترتيب عصبات النسب إلا في مسائل
إحداها إذا اجتمع جد المعتق وأخوه من الأب ففيه قولان
أحدهما أن الأخ أولى لأنه يدلي ببنوة الأب وهي أقوى من الأبوة في العصوبة
والثاني يتساويان لأن أحدهما أب الأب والآخر ابن الأب وليس الجد هاهنا
أصل الزوجة حتى يقدم
الثانية ابن المعتق مقدم على أبيه لأنه العصبة دون الأب هنا لقوة البنوة
الثالثة الجد وابن الأخ إن قلنا إن الجد مع الإخوة يتساويان فهاهنا الجد
يقدم وإن
قلنا يقدم الأخ على الجد فهاهنا يتساويان وقيل الجد مقدم لقربه وقيل ابن
الأخ لقوة البنوة
الرابعة أخ المعتق من الأب والأم وأخوه من الأب قيل لا ترجيح إذ الولاء
يجري بمحض العصوبة وقيل بطرد القولين

### | فرعان

أحدهما المرأة إذا أعتقت فلها الولاء ولكن يزوج العتيقة من يزوج السيدة
برضا العتيقة ولا يحتاج إلى رضا المعتقة لأنها لا تلي العقد على نفسها ولا
غيرها وليس لها الإجبار
وفيه وجه أنه لا بد من رضاها فإن عضلت يزوجها وليها برضا السلطان ويكون
السلطان نائبا عنها في الرضا الواجب عليها
وإن كان للمعتقة أب وابن فيزوجها في حياتها الأب فإن ماتت يزوج الابن
لأنه العصبة الآن وقيل باستصحاب  ولاية الأب وهو بعيد وقيل يزوجها ابنها في
حال حياتها كما يزوجها بعد مماتها وهو بعيد
الثاني جارية أعتق نصفها يزوجها المالك وعصبتها إن قلنا إن مثل هذه
الجارية تورث وإن قلنا لا تورث فيزوجها المالك والقضاي وقد قيل يزوجها
المعتق والمالك
وقيل لا تزوج لعسر الأمر وهو بعيد والأحوط التزويج باتفاق الجميع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-ي (waliya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Nearness, adjacency; one who undertakes a matter on behalf of another; authority and charge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Guardianship (wilāyah) as a delegated authority rooted in protective proximity—whether by blood, emancipation, or public office—mirroring God's own governance of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense: physical/legal closeness entailing command; metaphorical (majāz) sense: the sultan's authority as a substitute for the natural guardian's absence.
- Root: ج-ب-ر (jabara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone, to compel, to coerce; restoration of what is broken.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Compulsory authority (ijbār) in marriage—a coercive power that "sets right" the ward's affairs against her inclination, justified by the guardian's superior discernment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical force; metaphorical: legal enforcement overriding consent, as the father's right over the virgin.
- Root: ع-ض-ل (ʿaḍala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To obstruct, to withhold, to prevent from a rightful course.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Unlawful prevention of a ward's marriage by a guardian—a moral failing that forfeits guardianship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: tying a knot tightly; metaphorical: the guardian's tyrannical refusal to marry his ward.
- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿataqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be free, to be emancipated; ancient nobility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Manumission (iʿtāq) as a legal cause of clientage (walāʾ), transferring guardianship to the emancipator.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: release from bondage; metaphorical: the bond of loyalty (walāʾ) that substitutes for blood kinship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When enumerating causes (as in "four: paternity, grandfatherhood, agnatic kinship, clientage, and sultanate"), the appositives clarify the category without requiring separate syntactic treatment, each governed by the same operative verb.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first chapter concerns the causes of guardianship [over a woman in marriage]. They are four: paternity and grandfatherhood in its meaning, agnatic kinship by lineage, clientage [by manumission], and sultanate.

As for the father and the grandfather—the father's father—they possess the office of compulsory authority (ijbār) in the case of virginity, even after the attainment of puberty. And [they possess it] over sons in their minority, not in their majority. Abu Hanifah—may God be pleased with him—said: "A mature virgin is not to be compelled to marriage, and a minor who has lost her virginity may be compelled in his view." Al-Shāfiʿī—may God be pleased with him—considered the loss of virginity (thaybūbah) and virginity (bakārah), due to his saying—peace be upon him: {«الثيب أحق بنفسها من وليها والبكر تستأمر في نفسها وإذنها صماتها»} "The deflowered woman has more right to herself than her guardian, and the virgin is to be consulted about herself, and her permission is her silence."

The meaning of compelling her is that if the father married her to a suitable match (kufʾ) while she was displeased, it takes effect. And if she sought marriage from the guardian, the response is obligatory, even if she is one subject to compulsion—like a young boy who seeks food. If she specified a suitable match and the guardian specified a suitable match, some said: "Her right must be observed in the specific individuals, and the guardian's share is only in suitability (kafāʾah) itself." And some said: "The guardian's specification takes precedence."

Whenever she is a virgin—even if by fornication—she is not to be compelled. And if the hymen's skin was ruptured by a leap or a jump, the more apparent [view] is that she is a virgin, because her fornicator was the first to penetrate her. Abu Hanifah did not see any effect of fornication in removing the ruling of virginity.

As for the agnatic kin by lineage—like brothers, paternal uncles, and their sons—they have no compulsory authority whatsoever. Rather, they have [the right] to marry the virgin and the deflowered woman after puberty with her consent. Do they suffice with the silence of the virgin? There are two positions: One—yes, due to the apparent meaning of the hadith. The second—no, because silence is ambiguous, and the meaning of the hadith is to urge the one with compulsory authority to consult her without requiring her to speak.

As for the emancipating patron (al-walī al-muʿtiq), his guardianship is like the guardianship of the agnatic kin. As for the sultan, he is a guardian in four situations: when there is no guardian, when the guardian is absent, when the guardian obstructs (ʿaḍl), and when the guardian wishes to marry [the ward] to himself. The sultan has no compulsory authority, contrary to Abu Hanifah—may God have mercy on him.

The executor (waṣī) has no guardianship of marriage, even if the testator delegated it to him, since he has no kinship that would call him to compassion and consideration, nor any share in suitability.

The second chapter concerns the order of guardians from kinship, clientage, and sultanate. The direction of kinship takes precedence over clientage, and clientage takes precedence over sultanate. Crowding [of claimants] is hypothesized in lineage and clientage.

As for lineage: the father, then the grandfather—and both have compulsory authority. Then the order of the remaining agnatic kin is like their order in inheritance, except in three matters:

First: The son is an agnatic heir in inheritance, yet he does not marry [his mother or sister] by virtue of sonship, contrary to Abu Hanifah—may God have mercy on him. Yes, if he is a judge, or an agnatic [heir], or a paternal cousin, or an emancipator, he marries by these causes. So sonship neither prevents nor benefits.

Second: The grandfather in inheritance shares equally with the brothers. Here, the grandfather is given precedence because he is on the direct line of lineage, and his compassion is more complete.

Third: The full brother (from father and mother) is given precedence over the paternal brother in inheritance, and likewise in the funeral prayer. In guardianship there are two positions, because the maternal direction has no entry into guardianship, so it is possible that it does not necessitate preference. Al-Muzanī chose precedence in marriage as well. The two positions also apply to the full paternal uncle and the paternal uncle from the father, and their two sons. They do not apply to two paternal cousins, one of whom is a maternal brother, because maternal brotherhood here does not confer agnatic status in inheritance. Likewise, if she has two paternal cousins' sons, one being her son, or two emancipators' sons, one being from her—there is no preference. Ibn al-Ḥaddād explicitly stated that her son from the emancipator is given precedence over all other sons, and that is remote.

As for the order of clientage: the emancipator (al-muʿtiq) is more entitled; if not, then his agnatic kin; if not, then the emancipator of the emancipator, then his agnatic kin. The order of the emancipator's agnatic kin is like the order of agnatic kin by lineage, except in certain matters:

First: When the emancipator's grandfather and his paternal brother are together, there are two positions. One: the brother is more entitled, because he traces through the father's sonship, which is stronger than grandfatherhood in agnatic status. The second: they are equal, because one is the father's father and the other is the father's son, and the grandfather here is not the origin of the wife so as to be preferred.

Second: The emancipator's son is preferred over his father, because he is the agnatic heir here, not the father, due to the strength of sonship.

Third: The grandfather and the brother's son—if we say that the grandfather with the brothers is equal, then here the grandfather is preferred; and if we say the brother is preferred over the grandfather, then here they are equal. It was said: the grandfather is preferred due to his proximity, and it was said: the brother's son due to the strength of sonship.

Fourth: The emancipator's full brother and his paternal brother—it was said: no preference, since clientage operates purely by agnatic status; and it was said: the two positions are extended [here as well].

Two subsidiary branches:

First: If a woman emancipates [a slave], she has the clientage. But the freedwoman is married by whoever marries the mistress, with the freedwoman's consent, and the consent of the emancipatress is not needed, because she does not execute the contract on herself nor on another, and she has no compulsory authority. There is a position that her consent is necessary. If she obstructs, her guardian marries her with the sultan's consent, and the sultan is her deputy in the consent obligatory upon her. If the emancipatress has a father and a son, then in her lifetime the father marries her; if she dies, the son marries her, because he is now the agnatic heir. It was said: by the continuation (istiṣḥāb) of the father's guardianship—and that is remote. It was said: her son marries her in her lifetime just as he marries her after her death—and that is remote.

Second: A slave-girl whose half has been emancipated—her owner and her agnatic kin marry her if we say that such a slave-girl is inherited [upon death]. If we say she is not inherited, then her owner and the judge marry her. It was said: the emancipator and the owner marry her. And it was said: she is not married at all due to the difficulty of the matter—and that is remote. The more cautious [view] is to marry her with the agreement of all.

chapters.title_en: The Third Chapter on the Nullifiers of Guardianship (Sawālib al-Wilāyah)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثالث في سوالب الولاية

وهي سبعة
الأول الرق فلا ولاية للرقيق على نفسه فكيف على غيره نعم تصح عبارته في
شقي عقد النكاح بالوكالة وإن لم يأذن له سيده إذ لا ضرر على سيده فيه ومنهم
من منع عبارته في شق التزويج وزعم أن نائب الولي ينبغي أن يكون بصفة الولاة
بخلاف نائب الزوج
الثاني كل ما يقدح في النظر كالصبي والجنون والإغماء والعتة والسفه
الموجب للحجر والمرض المؤلم الملهي عن النظر لشدته فجميع ذلك يسلب الولاية
وينقلها إلى الأبعد إلا في الإغماء والجنون المتقطع ففيهما ثلاثة أوجه
أحدها أنها تنتقل إلى السلطان لأن زوالها منتظر كالغيبة
والثاني أنها تنتقل إلى الأبعد لأن الغيبة لا تخل بالنظر والجنون
والإغماء يخلان بالنظر
والثالث أن الإغماء ينتقل إلى القاضي والجنون إلى الأبعد
ثم المغمى عليه ينتظر مقدار مدة سفر العدوى أو سفر القصر كما في مدة
الغائب وعندي أن تقدير الانتظار هاهنا بثلاثة أيام أولى
الثالث العمى وفيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه لا يلي الأعمى لاختلال نظره
والثاني يلي لأن مقاصد النكاح لا ترتبط بالبصر
الرابع الفسق وظاهر نصوص الشافعي رضي الله عنه قديما وجديدا أنه يلي وقال
لا يلي السفيه قال القفال أراد به الذي لا ينظر لنفسه ويدل على ولاية
الفاسق الناظر لدنياه ترك الأولين النكير على سلاطين الظلمة والفساق في
التزويج ولأنه ناظر لنفسه فكذلك لولده فإنه من أهم أموره الخاصة به ولأن
عود الفسق بعد البلوغ لا يعيد الحجر وفاقا وإن كان عود السفه يعيده على وجه
مع أن اتصال الفسق بالبلوغ يمنع
ارتفاع الحجر لأنه ثبت بيقين فلا يرتفع بالشك في الرشد واتصال الفسق  يوجب
الشك فإذا ارتفع بيقين لم يعد أيضا بالشك بسبب الفسق والمشهور تخريج ولاية
الفاسق على قولين وقيل شارب الخمر لا يلي خاصة وقيل ولاية الإجبار تسقط
بالفسق دون غيره وقيل عكسه فهذه خمسة طرق
ولا خلاف في أن المستور يلي لترك الأولين النكير وتوكيل الفاسق في العقد
كتوكيل العبد وفيه خلاف على قولنا لا يلي الفاسق
فأما السكران المختل العقل فلا يصح تزويجه قولا واحدا ولا وجه لبناء ذلك
على أنه يسلك به مسلك الصاحي أم لا فإن هذا يتعلق بالنظر للغير
الخامس اختلاف الدين يسلب النظر فيسلب الولاية الخاصة حتى لا يزوج المسلم
ابنته الكافرة وأما الكافر فيزوج ابنته الكافرة من مسلم قال الشافعي رضي
الله عنه وولي الكافرة كافر لأنه ينظر لولده بخلاف الفاسق المسلم على رأي
وقال الحليمي لا يزوج الكافر إذا قلنا لا يزوج الفاسق وهذا خلاف النص
ولا يقبل المسلم نكاح الكافرة من قاضي الكفار لأنه لا وقع لقضائهم وفي
كلام صاحب التقريب إشارة إلى خلافه
السادس غيبة الولي وهي لا تسلب الولاية عندنا لأن النظر قائم ولكن ينوب
السلطان عنه لتعذر الأمر لغيبته ولذلك لا ينعزل الوكيل بطرآن الغيبة على
الموكل
وينعزل بطرآن الجنون
ثم السلطان يزوج إن كان السفر فوق مسافة القصر ولا يزوج إن كان دون مسافة
العدوى وهو الذي يرجع عنه المبكر إليه قبل الليل وفيما بينهما وجهان يجريان
في قبول شهادة الفرع عند غيبة الأصل وفي الاستعداء عند القاضي
ثم إذا طلبت من السلطان التزويج قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه لا يزوجها ما
لم يشهد عدلان أنه ليس له ولي حاضر وليست في زوجية ولا عدة فمنهم من قال
ذلك واجب احتياطا للنكاح خاصة ومنهم من قال هو استحباب لأن اعتماد العقود
على قول أربابها وكذلك يحلفها القاضي على أن وليها لم يزوجها في الغيبة إن
رأى ذلك
ومثل هذه اليمين التي لا تتعلق بدعوى استحباب أو إيجاب فيه خلاف
السابع الإحرام والمحرم مسلوب العبارة في عقد النكاح بالوكالة  والنيابة
والاستقلال في شقي القبول والإيجاب وهل يمنع الرجعة فيه وجهان
وهل ينعقد النكاح بشهادة المحرم فيه خلاف للتردد في الرواية إذ ورد في
بعضها لا ينكح المحرم ولا يشهد
وهل تنقطع هذه التحريمات بالتحلل الأول فيه وجهان والأظهر أنه لا تنقطع
لبقاء اسم الإحرام
ثم اختلفوا في أن الولاية تنتقل إلى السلطان أو إلى الأبعد ومأخذه أنه
كالغيبة أو مناف للولاية فإن قلنا إنه مناف فلو أحرم الموكل انعزل وكيله
وإن قلنا لا فلا ينعزل ولكن قال الصيدلاني يصبر الوكيل إلى تحلل الموكل إذ
يبعد أن يتعاطى عنه فعلا في وقت يعجز عنه هو في نفسه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ل-ب (salaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To strip away, divest, or deprive something of its inherent attribute; the act of negation or removal of a property.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, the nullification of a juridical capacity or right, rendering the subject devoid of its operative effect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical seizure; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the legal negation of authority.
- Root: و-ل-ي (waliya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Proximity, adjacency; hence the one who stands near to manage affairs — the guardian (walī).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Wilāyah is the legal authority to execute contracts on behalf of another, rooted in the Quranic mandate of protective oversight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal proximity vs. metaphorical authority; the guardian is "near" in status, not necessarily in physical distance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Embedded Exception (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The text repeatedly uses "nعم" (yes/exceptive) to introduce a counter-case after a general negation, requiring careful parsing of the scope of the exception.
chapters.translation:
I say: The nullifiers of guardianship are seven.

**The First: Slavery (al-riqq).** A slave has no guardianship over himself, so how could he have it over another? Yes, his utterance is valid in one of the two halves of the marriage contract — namely, the acceptance (qabūl) — by agency (wikālah), even if his master has not permitted him, since there is no harm to his master therein. Among the scholars is one who forbade his utterance in the half of contracting the marriage (tazwīj), holding that the deputy of the guardian (nāʾib al-walī) must possess the attributes of guardians themselves, unlike the deputy of the husband.

**The Second: Everything that Impairs Sound Judgment (mā yuqdiḥ fī al-naẓar).** This includes: the minor (ṣabī), insanity (junūn), unconsciousness (ighmāʾ), imbecility (ʿatah), profligate folly (safah) that necessitates interdiction (ḥajr), and a painful illness that distracts from sound judgment due to its severity. All of these strip guardianship and transfer it to the more distant relative (al-abʿad), except in the cases of unconsciousness and intermittent insanity — regarding these two, there are three positions (awjuh):
1. That guardianship transfers to the Sultan (al-sulṭān), because its cessation is anticipated, like the case of the absent guardian (ghaybah).
2. That it transfers to the more distant relative, because absence does not impair judgment, whereas insanity and unconsciousness do impair it.
3. That unconsciousness transfers to the judge (al-qāḍī), while insanity transfers to the more distant relative.

Then, the one who is unconscious is waited for the duration of a journey of concession (safar al-ʿadhā) or a journey of shortening prayer (safar al-qaṣr), just as in the waiting period for the absent one. In my view, the estimation of the waiting period here as three days is more appropriate (awlā).

**The Third: Blindness (al-ʿamā).** There are two positions:
1. That the blind person does not exercise guardianship, due to the impairment of his oversight.
2. That he does exercise it, because the objectives of marriage are not connected to eyesight.

**The Fourth: Immorality (al-fisq).** The apparent texts of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — both old and new, hold that the immoral person does exercise guardianship. He said: "The profligate fool (safīh) does not." Al-Qaffāl said: "He meant the one who does not look after his own interests." Evidence for the guardianship of the immoral person who does look after his worldly affairs is that the early generations (al-awwalūn) did not reproach tyrannical and immoral rulers for contracting marriages. Also, because he looks after himself, so likewise he looks after his child, for the child is among his most important personal concerns. Also, because the recurrence of immorality after puberty does not reinstate interdiction, by consensus — even though the recurrence of folly (safah) does reinstate it in one view — given that the continuity of immorality at puberty prevents the lifting of interdiction, because it was established with certainty and is not lifted by doubt regarding sound judgment (rushd). The continuity of immorality engenders doubt, so if it is lifted with certainty, it is not reinstated by doubt due to immorality. The well-known position derives the guardianship of the immoral person into two opinions. It is said: the wine-drinker specifically does not exercise guardianship. It is said: the guardianship of compulsion (wilāyat al-ijbār) is nullified by immorality, but not other types. It is said: the reverse. These are five paths (ṭuruq).

There is no disagreement that the person of concealed status (al-mastūr) exercises guardianship, due to the early generations' lack of reproach. The appointment of an immoral person as agent in the contract is like the appointment of a slave — and there is disagreement on this based on our position that the immoral person does not exercise guardianship.

As for the drunkard whose intellect is deranged, his marriage contract is invalid by unanimous agreement (qawlan wāḥidan). There is no basis for building this on whether he is treated like the sober person or not, for this pertains to judgment for the sake of others.

**The Fifth: Difference of Religion (ikhtilāf al-dīn).** This strips judgment and thus strips specific guardianship, so that a Muslim may not give his daughter in marriage to a disbeliever. As for the disbeliever, he may give his disbelieving daughter in marriage to a Muslim. Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: "The guardian of a disbelieving woman is a disbeliever," because he looks after his child, unlike the Muslim immoral person, according to one view. Al-Ḥalīmī said: "The disbeliever does not contract marriage if we hold that the immoral person does not," but this contradicts the text (naṣṣ). A Muslim does not accept the marriage of a disbelieving woman from the judge of the disbelievers, because their judgments carry no weight. In the words of the author of al-Taqrīb, there is an indication of a contrary view.

**The Sixth: Absence of the Guardian (ghaybah al-walī).** This does not strip guardianship in our school, because judgment remains intact. However, the Sultan deputizes for him due to the difficulty of the matter during his absence. For this reason, an agent is not dismissed by the occurrence of absence upon the principal, but he is dismissed by the occurrence of insanity.

Then, the Sultan contracts the marriage if the travel exceeds the distance of shortening prayer (masāfat al-qaṣr), and does not contract it if it is less than the distance of concession (masāfat al-ʿadhā) — which is the distance from which one can return to the town before nightfall. Between these two, there are two positions that parallel those in accepting the testimony of a secondary witness (shahādat al-farʿ) when the primary witness is absent, and in seeking redress before the judge.

Then, if she requests the Sultan to contract the marriage, al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: "He does not contract it for her unless two just witnesses testify that she has no present guardian and that she is not in a marriage or waiting period (ʿiddah)." Some say this is obligatory as a precaution specifically for marriage; others say it is recommended, because contracts rely on the statements of their principals. Likewise, the judge administers an oath to her that her guardian did not marry her during his absence, if he deems this appropriate. Such an oath that is not tied to a claim — whether recommended or obligatory — is subject to disagreement.

**The Seventh: Iḥrām (Pilgrimage Consecration).** The one in iḥrām is stripped of utterance in the marriage contract — whether by agency, deputyship, or independently — in both halves of acceptance (qabūl) and offer (ījāb). Whether it prevents revocation (rujʿah) is subject to two positions. Whether a marriage contract is valid with the testimony of one in iḥrām is disputed, due to the variance in the narration — for in some versions it states: "The one in iḥrām does not contract marriage nor testify." Whether these prohibitions are severed by the first dissolution of iḥrām (al-taḥallul al-awwal) is subject to two positions; the more apparent (al-aẓhar) is that they are not severed, because the name of iḥrām persists.

Then, they differed as to whether guardianship transfers to the Sultan or to the more distant relative. The basis for this is whether iḥrām is like absence or is a nullifier of guardianship. If we say it is a nullifier, then if the principal enters iḥrām, his agent is dismissed. If we say it is not, then he is not dismissed. However, al-Ṣaydalānī said: "The agent waits until the principal exits iḥrām," for it is unlikely that he would perform an act on his behalf at a time when he himself is incapable of it.
