chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

إذا ولدت من الزنا لم يحل لها نكاح ولدها والمخلوقة من ماء الزنا لا يحرم
نكاحها على الزاني لأنها تنفصل عن الأم وهي إنسان وبعض منها وتنفصل عن
الفحل وهو نطفة فعلة تحريمه النسب الشرعي وقد انتفى ولو كان بعضا حقيقيا
منه لما انعقد ولد الحر رقيقا في منكوحة رقيقة كما لا تلد الحرة رقيقا  من
زوج رقيق
أما المنفية باللعان فهل تحرم على النافي فيه وجهان وجه التحريم أنها
عرضة اللحوق بسبب الفراش إن كذب نفسه
المانع الثاني الرضاع قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحرم من الرضاع
ما يحرم من النسب فتحرم منه الأم والبنت والأخ والأخت وبناتهما والعمة
والخالة
وأمك كل امرأة أرضعتك أو أرضعت من أرضعتك أو أرضعت من يرجع نسبك إليه من
جهة أبيك أو أمك وكذلك كل امرأة يرجع نسب المرضعة إليها
وكل امرأة يرجع نسبها إلى هذه المرضعة من قبل أبيها أو أمها فهي أختك
وكذلك كل
امرأة أرضعتها أمك بلبان أبيك فهي أختك من الأب والأم وإن أرضعتها أمك
بلبان غير أبيك فهي أختك من الأم وإن أرضعتها أجنيبة بلبان أبيك فهي أختك
من الأب وكذلك قياس العمات وسيأتي في كتاب الرضاع شرحه
فرع لو اختلطت أخته من الرضاع بأهل بلد أو قرية لا ينحصرون في العادة فله
أن ينكح من شاء كما لو غصب شاة في بلدة فلا يحرم عليه اللحم
ولو اختلطت بعشر أو عشرين أو عدد محصور على الجملة فيلزمه اجتناب الكل
لأن يقين التحريم عارض يقيت الحل في عدد وقيل يجوز الهجوم وهو بعيد
المانع الثالث المصاهرة والمحرمات بالمصاهرة أربع
أم الزوجة وجداتها من الرضاع والنسب
وبنتها وحفدتها من الرضاع والنسب
وزوجة الابن والحفدة
وزوجة الأب والجد
ويحرم الجميع بمجرد النكاح إلا بنت الزوجة فلا تحرم إلا بالدخول قال الله
تعالى {وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن}
والوطء الحلال بملك اليمين والوطء بالشبهة يحرم الأربع كالوطء في النكاح
بخلاف الزنا فإنه لا يحرم خلافا لأبي حنيفة إذ الشبهة كالحقيقة في جلب
المحرمات كالعدة والمهر والنسب وسقوط الحد لكن يرجع في وجوب المهر إلى
الاشتباه عليها فقط وينظر في ثبوت النسب والعدة إلى الاشتباه عليه وقيل في
المصاهرة إنه تكفي الشبهة من أحد الجانبين وقيل لا بد من الاشتباه على
الرجل لأنه قرينة النسب في كتاب الله تعالى وقيل لا  بد فيه من الاشتباه
عليهما جميعا
والصحيح أن مجرد الملامسة لا يقوم مقام الوطء في تحريم المصاهرة كانت
بالشبهة أو في النكاح وفيه قول آخر أنه يلتحق به وقيل يطرد ذلك القول في
النظر بالشبهة أيضا

### | الجنس الثاني ما يتعلق بتعبد عددي ولا تتأبد به الحرمة

وهي ثلاث

### | المانع الأول نكاح الأخت في عدة الأخت

قال الله تعالى {وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف} فقيل أراد ما سلف
قبل التحريم فلا يرد وقيل ما سلف في الجاهلية
ثم ألحق به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جميع المحارم فقال لا تنكح
المرأة على عمتها ولا على خالتها والضابط أن كل شخصين بينهما قرابة أو رضاع
لو كان أحدهما ذكرا والأخرى أنثى حرم النكاح بينهما فلا يجوز الجمع بينهما
واحترزنا بالقرابة والرضاع عن الجمع بين المرأة وأم زوجها أو ابنة زوجها
فإن ذلك جائز وإن كان النكاح يحرم بينهما لو كان أحدهما ذكرا
ثم ألحق الفقهاء ملك اليمين بالنكاح حتى قالوا لو اشترى أمة ووطئها حرمت
عليه أختها وخالتها وعمتها فإن ملك الجميع فما لم يحرم الموطوءة على نفسه
ببيع أو عتق أو تزويج أو كتابة فلا يحل له وطء الباقيات ولا تقوم العوارض
المحرمة مقام البيع كالحيض والعدة بالشبهة والردة والإحرام وفي الرهن
والبيع بشرط الخيار خلاف وتحل الأخت بالطلاق البائن ولا تحل بالطلاق الرجعي
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا تحل أيضا بالبائن وكذا الخلاف في نكاح الخامسة
فرع لو وطئ أمة ثم نكح أختها الحرة صح النكاح وحرمت الأمة وليس كما لو
نكحها ثم نكح عليها أختها فإن الطارئ لا يصح لأن ملك اليمين ضعيف في
مقصود الوطء فلا يدفع النكاح المقصود بل يدفع به حله
ولو اشترى الرجل منكوحته صح الشراء وانفسخ النكاح لأن ملك اليمين أقوى في
نفسه

### | المانع الثاني

الزيادة على الأربع ممتنع على الحر والثالثة في حق العبد كالخامسة في حق
الحر فلا يزيد العبد على اثنتين وقال مالك ينكح العبد أربعة
فرع لو نكح خمسا في عقد فالعقد باطل فيهن ولو كان فيهن أختان بطل فيهما
وفي الباقيات قولا تفريق الصفقة وكذا لو جمع بين معتدة وخلية من العدة ففي
الخلية القولان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ن-ي (zanā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is illicit sexual intercourse (al-zinā), distinct from lawful union (nikāḥ) and from doubtful intercourse (waṭʾ al-shubhah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, zinā generates no lineage (nasab) and no consequential marital prohibitions, as it is an act of pure transgression severed from the divinely ordained institution of family.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the physical act; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "prohibition" is rejected here — the act is a cause only of moral corruption, not of legal kinship.
- Root: ر-ض-ع (raḍaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Suckling (riḍāʿ) — the ingestion of milk by an infant from a woman, establishing a fictive kinship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, riḍāʿ is a legal cause (sabab) that replicates the prohibitions of blood lineage (nasab), as affirmed by the prophetic hadith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical act of nursing; metaphorical — the legal extension of kinship ties, treated as ḥaqīqah sharʿiyyah (legal reality).
- Root: ص-ه-ر (ṣihr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Affinal relationship (muṣāharah) — kinship through marriage, distinct from blood (nasab) and milk (raḍāʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divinely instituted bond arising from valid marriage or lawful intercourse, creating permanent prohibitions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the marital tie; metaphorical — the legal consequences of that tie, such as prohibition of the spouse's ascendants and descendants.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — In the verse {«وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ»}, the restrictive clause "who are in your care" is a condition (sharṭ) that is not legally operative for the prohibition, but the exception "unless you have consummated" (istithnāʾ) is operative, requiring precise parsing of the conditional structure.
chapters.translation:
### | Branch

If a woman gives birth to a child from fornication (zinā), it is not permissible for her to marry her own child; but a female created from the sperm of fornication is not prohibited for the fornicator to marry, because she separates from the mother as a human being and a part of her, and separates from the male as mere sperm. The cause of prohibition is legitimate lineage (al-nasab al-sharʿī), and that has been negated. Had she been a true part of him, the child of a free man would not be conceived as a slave in the womb of a slave wife, just as a free woman does not give birth to a slave from a slave husband.

As for the woman repudiated by mutual imprecation (al-mulaʿʿanah), whether she is prohibited for the one who repudiates — there are two views. The view of prohibition holds that she is susceptible to reattachment of lineage due to the marriage bed (al-firāsh) if he retracts his accusation.

The second impediment: fosterage (al-riḍāʿ). The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: {«يَحْرُمُ مِنَ الرَّضَاعِ مَا يَحْرُمُ مِنَ النَّسَبِ»} — "What is prohibited by fosterage is what is prohibited by lineage." Thus prohibited for him are: the mother, the daughter, the sister, the brother's daughter, the sister's daughter, the paternal aunt, and the maternal aunt.

Your mother [by fosterage] is every woman who suckled you, or who suckled the one who suckled you, or who suckled one whose lineage traces back to you through your father or your mother. Likewise, every woman to whom the lineage of the wet-nurse traces back [is your mother]. And every woman whose lineage traces back to this wet-nurse through her father or her mother is your sister. Likewise, every woman whom your mother suckled with the milk of your father is your sister from both father and mother. If your mother suckled her with the milk of someone other than your father, she is your sister from the mother only. If a stranger suckled her with the milk of your father, she is your sister from the father only. Similarly, by analogy, [apply this to] the paternal and maternal aunts. The detailed explanation will come in the Book of Fosterage.

Branch: If his foster-sister is mixed among the people of a city or village who are not, by custom, limited in number, he may marry whomever he wishes — just as if a sheep were wrongfully seized in a town, the meat is not prohibited for him. But if she is mixed among ten, or twenty, or any limited number, then he must avoid all of them, because the certainty of prohibition confronts the certainty of permissibility within a limited count. It was said that he may proceed [to marry any of them], but this is far-fetched.

The third impediment: affinity (al-muṣāharah). Those prohibited by affinity are four:
1. The wife's mother and her grandmothers, whether by fosterage or lineage.
2. The wife's daughter and her granddaughters, whether by fosterage or lineage.
3. The son's wife and the grandson's wife.
4. The father's wife and the grandfather's wife.

All of these become prohibited merely by the marriage contract, except the wife's daughter, who is not prohibited except by consummation. Allah the Exalted said: {«وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ مِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ اللَّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ»} — "And your step-daughters who are in your care from your wives with whom you have consummated."

Lawful intercourse by right of ownership (milk al-yamīn) and intercourse under doubtful circumstances (al-waṭʾ bi-l-shubhah) prohibit the four [categories] just as intercourse in marriage does. This is contrary to fornication (zinā), which does not prohibit — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah — for the doubtful [intercourse] is like the real [intercourse] in bringing about prohibitions, just as it brings about the waiting period (al-ʿiddah), the dowry (al-mahr), lineage (al-nasab), and the dropping of the penal sanction (ḥadd). However, regarding the obligation of the dowry, one refers to the doubt on her side only; and regarding the establishment of lineage and the waiting period, one looks to the doubt on his side. It was said regarding affinity that doubt on one side suffices; and it was said that doubt on the man's side is necessary, because he is the one whose lineage is the indicator in the Book of Allah the Exalted; and it was said that doubt on both sides is required.

The correct view is that mere touching (al-mulāmasah) does not stand in the place of intercourse in prohibiting affinity, whether it occurred under doubt or in marriage. There is another view that it is annexed to it. And it was said that this view is extended to looking with desire under doubtful circumstances as well.

### | The Second Genus: What Pertains to a Numerical Act of Worship and Whose Prohibition Is Not Perpetual

These are three [impediments].

### | The First Impediment: Marrying a Sister during the Waiting Period of Her Sister

Allah the Exalted said: {«وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ»} — "And that you combine between two sisters, except what has already passed." It was said that "what has passed" means before the prohibition, so it is not considered; and it was said it means what passed in the pre-Islamic era (al-Jāhilīyyah).

Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, annexed to this all [other] close relatives, saying: "Do not marry a woman over her paternal aunt, nor over her maternal aunt." The controlling principle is: any two persons between whom there is kinship or fosterage such that, were one male and the other female, marriage between them would be prohibited — then combining them [in marriage to one man] is not permissible. We restricted [the principle] to kinship and fosterage to exclude combining a woman with her husband's mother or her husband's daughter, for that is permissible, even though marriage between them would be prohibited were one of them male.

Then the jurists annexed right of ownership (milk al-yamīn) to marriage, so that they said: if a man buys a slave-girl and has intercourse with her, her sister, her maternal aunt, and her paternal aunt become prohibited for him. If he owns all of them, then as long as he has not made the one with whom he had intercourse unlawful for himself by sale, manumission, marriage, or kitābah (contract of manumission), it is not lawful for him to have intercourse with the rest. And the incidental impediments that prohibit [intercourse] do not stand in the place of sale — such as menstruation, the waiting period due to doubtful intercourse, apostasy, and the state of iḥrām. Regarding pledging as security and sale with the option of revocation, there is a difference of opinion. The sister becomes lawful by irrevocable divorce (al-ṭalāq al-bāʾin), but not by revocable divorce (al-ṭalāq al-rajʿī). Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, said she does not become lawful even by irrevocable divorce. Likewise, there is a difference of opinion regarding marrying a fifth [wife].

Branch: If a man has intercourse with a slave-girl, then marries her free sister, the marriage is valid and the slave-girl becomes prohibited [for him]. This is not like the case where he marries her and then marries her sister over her, for the latter, being subsequent, is not valid — because right of ownership is weak in the purpose of intercourse, so it does not repel the marriage, which is the primary purpose; rather, it is repelled by it. But if a man buys his own married wife [as a slave], the purchase is valid and the marriage is dissolved, because right of ownership is stronger in itself.

### | The Second Impediment

Exceeding four [wives] is prohibited for the free man, and the third [wife] in the case of the slave is like the fifth in the case of the free man. Thus the slave may not exceed two. Mālik said: the slave may marry four.

Branch: If he marries five women in a single contract, the contract is void with respect to all of them. If among them were two sisters, it is void with respect to them; and regarding the rest, there are the two views on the division of the transaction (tafrīq al-ṣafqah). Likewise, if he combines a woman in her waiting period with one free from the waiting period, the two views apply to the latter.

chapters.title_en: The Third Impediment: Completion of the Number of Divorces
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المانع الثالث استيفاء عدد الطلاق

فلا تحل المطلقة ثلاثا حتى تنكح زوجا غيره ويطأ في نكاح صحيح ثم يطلقها
وتنقضي عدتها ولا يحصل بالوطء في ملك اليمين والمذهب أنه لا يحصل بالوطء في
نكاح فاسد ويحصل بوطء الصبي ونزولها على الزوج وهو نائم وبالاستدخال خال من
غير انتشار وفيه وجه بعيد ويحصل بمجرد تغييب الحشفة أو مقدار الحشفة من
مقطوع الحشفة ومنهم من قال لا بد من تغييب الجميع إذا زالت الحشفة
ومن لطائف الحيل للفرار من الغيظ أن يشتري عبدا صغيرا ويزوجها منه ثم
يستدخل زبيبة الصغير ولو مع حائل من ثوب ثم يبيع العبد منها حتى ينفسخ
النكاح فيحصل التحليل إلا إذا قلنا لا يجوز إجبار الصغير
فإن قيل فما معنى قوله عليه السلام لعن الله المحلل والمحلل له
قلنا قيل أراد به طالب الحل من نكاح المتعة وهو المؤقت رسما وسمي محللا
وإن لم يحلل له لأنه يعتقده ويطلب الحل منه وأما طالب الحل من طريقه فلا
يستوجب اللعن وقيل إنما لعن مع حصول التحليل لأن التماس ذلك هتك للمروءة
والملتمس هو المحلل له وإعارة النفس في الوطء لعرض الغير أيضا رذيلة فإنه
إنما يطؤها ليعرضها لوطء الغير وهو قلة حمية ولذلك قال عليه السلام ذلك هو
التيس المستعار
وإنما يكون ذلك مستعارا إذا سبق منه التماس من المطلق ومن عرض الوطء
الغير من هي منكوحته أو من كانت منكوحته أو ستكون منكوحته فهو مزموم جدا
فلا يبعد أن يلعن ولا يقتضي هذا اللعن بطلان العقد لأنه سماه مع ذلك محللا
إلا أنه إذا شرط الطلاق في نفس العقد فإنه يفسد على وجه كالتأقيت ولا يفسد
على وجه لأنه شرط فاسد كما لو شرط أن لا يتسرى عليها ولا يسافر بها وكسائر
الشرائط المفسدة للمهر
وأما  التأقيت فإنه وضع للعقد قاصرا على مدة ولا يمكن الاقتصار ولا
التسرية
أما إذا قال بشرط أن لا تحل لك فينبغي أن يفسد لأنه يجعل اللفظ متناقضا
ولو قال بشرط أن لا تطأها ففيه وجهان
وهذه الشروط إذا لم تقارن العقد لا تضر وفيه وجه بعيد أن المقدم كالمقارن
أخذا من مهر السر والعلانية كما سيأتي وعلى هذا لا يصح التحليل بالالتماس
إلا إذا زوج مطلقا ثم التمس الطلاق بعد العقد

### | الجنس الثالث من الموانع الرق والملك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To untie, unbind, dissolve; the opposite of ʿaqd (binding knot); also denotes permissibility after prohibition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for rendering lawful (taḥlīl) what was previously unlawful—here, the re-permission of a thrice-divorced woman to her first husband through an intervening marriage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = untying a physical knot; metaphorical (majāz) = dissolving a marital contract. The term "muḥallil" (one who makes lawful) shifts between literal and figurative senses depending on intent.
- Root: و-ط-ء (w-ṭ-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tread, step upon; in juristic usage, sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, the physical act that consummates marriage and triggers ʿiddah (waiting period).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the physical act; never metaphorical in this legal context.
- Root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To penetrate, pass through; interstice or gap between things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In this passage, istikhlāl (استدخال) = full penetration of the glans; also the root for "khillah" (friendship) but here purely physical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical penetration; the derived term "khilāl" (toothpick) shows the root's core sense of passing between.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with Implied Apodosis (al-sharṭ bi-jawāb maḥdhūf) — When the protasis (e.g., "if he says...") is followed by an elliptical apodosis, the missing main clause is inferred from context, as in "فإن قيل" (if it is said) where the response "we say" (قلنا) is the implied completion.
chapters.translation:
### | The Third Impediment: Completion of the Number of Divorces

A woman divorced three times does not become lawful [to her first husband] until she marries another husband, and he has intercourse with her in a valid marriage, then divorces her, and her waiting period (ʿiddah) expires. Intercourse with her does not occur through ownership of a slave-woman (milk al-yamīn). The established doctrine (al-madhhab) is that it does not occur through intercourse in an invalid marriage (nikāḥ fāsid). It does occur through the intercourse of a minor boy, and through her lowering herself upon a sleeping husband, and through full insertion (istikhlāl) without erection—though there is a remote opinion [against this]. It also occurs through the mere disappearance of the glans (ḥashafah), or the equivalent amount of the glans in the case of one whose glans has been amputated. Some say that when the glans is removed, full insertion of the entire member is required.

Among the subtle stratagems (ḥiyal) for escaping rage is that a man purchases a young slave boy, marries the woman to him, then inserts the boy's "raisin" (zabībah—i.e., his small organ) even with a cloth barrier, then sells the slave to her so that the marriage is dissolved—thus taḥlīl is achieved—unless we hold that compelling a minor [to divorce] is impermissible.

If it is said: What then is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: «لعن الله المحلل والمحلل له» (May Allah curse the one who makes lawful and the one for whom it is made lawful)?

We say: It is said that he meant thereby the seeker of lawfulness through temporary marriage (nikāḥ al-mutʿah)—that which is time-limited by stipulation. He is called "muḥallil" even though he does not actually make her lawful, because he believes it and seeks lawfulness through it. As for the one who seeks lawfulness through its proper path, he does not incur the curse. And it is said that the curse applies only when taḥlīl is achieved, because seeking that is a violation of manly virtue (murūʾah), and the seeker is the one for whom it is made lawful. Lending one's self for intercourse for the sake of another's access is also a vice—for he only has intercourse with her to present her for another's intercourse, which is a lack of protective jealousy (ghayrah). Therefore he said, peace be upon him: "That one is the borrowed stud-buck (al-tays al-mustaʿār)."

This [borrowing] only applies when there was prior solicitation from the divorcer. One who offers his wife—whether she is currently his wife, was his wife, or will be his wife—for another's intercourse is severely blameworthy. Thus it is not far-fetched that he is cursed. However, this curse does not entail the nullity of the contract, for he nonetheless called him "muḥallil." But if divorce is stipulated within the very contract itself, it corrupts [the marriage] in one respect—like time-limiting (taʾqīt)—and does not corrupt in another respect, because it is a corrupt condition (sharṭ fāsid), just as if he stipulated that he will not take a concubine over her or will not travel with her, and like other conditions that corrupt the dower (mahr).

As for time-limiting (taʾqīt), it places the contract as deficient for a specified duration, and neither restriction nor extension is possible.

If he says: "On condition that she not become lawful to you"—this should corrupt [the contract], because it renders the utterance self-contradictory. If he says: "On condition that you do not have intercourse with her"—there are two opinions.

These conditions, if they do not accompany the contract itself, cause no harm. There is a remote opinion that the prior [stipulation] is like the concurrent [stipulation], derived from the case of the secret and public dower (mahr al-sirr wa al-ʿalāniyyah), as will come later. On this basis, taḥlīl is not valid through solicitation unless one marries [her] absolutely, then solicits the divorce after the contract.

### | The Third Category of Impediments: Slavery and Ownership

chapters.title_en: On the Impediment of Slavery (al-Riqq) to Marriage and Its Conditions
chapters.arabic_text:
أما الرق فمانع على الجملة عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه في بعض الأحوال فلا
يجوز للحر المسلم أن ينكح الأمة إلا بخمسة شرائط
ثلاثة فيه وهو فقد الحرة تحته وفقد طول الحرة وخوف العنت
واثنان في الأمة وهي أن تكون مسلمة ومملوكة لمسلم
الشرط الأول ألا يكون تحته حرة فإن كانت تحته رتقاء أو هرمة أو غائبة أو
كتابية لم يجز أيضا نكاح الأمة بل يجب عليه طلاقها بخلاف ما إذا وجد مالا
ولكنه
غائب فإنه كالفاقد للطول
الشرط الثاني فقد طول الحرة فمن ليس تحته حرة ولكنه قادر عليها لم يجز له
نكاح الأمة لقوله تعالى {ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات} الآية
ويجوز للمفلس نكاح الأمة وإن وجد حرة ترضى بمهر مؤجل جاز لأن الأجل سيحل
وهو معسر وكذلك إذا كان له مال غائب وهو يخاف العنت في الحال قبل القدرة
على المال وكذلك إذا رضيت الحرة بدون مهر المثل وملك ذلك القدر لأنه لا
يلزمه تحمل المنة وفيه وجه آخر اختاره الصيدلاني أنه لا يجوز له نكاح الأمة
لأن المنة بالمهر مستحقر في النكاح بخلاف المنة في بيع الماء والثوب الساتر
للعورة في الصلاة
ولو وجد مالا ولم يجد حرة ينكحها جاز له نكاح الأمة ولو لم يجد إلا حرة
تغاليه في المهر مغالاة يعد احتمال ذلك سرفا بالإضافة إلى مقاصد النكاح فله
نكاح الأمة وإن كان ذلك قدرا قريبا لم يرخص بسببه
وكذلك الولي إذا نقص من  مهر المثل قدرا يحتمل ذلك لأغراض النكاح فلا
ينبغي أن يثبت الإعراض للمرأة بل إذا أفرط في النقصان فإن مقاصد النكاح
تغطي على هذه المحقرات وكذلك لو لم يجد إلا حرة غائبة غيبة قريبة يحتمل
مثلها في مقاصد النكاح لم ينكح الأمة وإن كانت بعيدا نكح الأمة
ولو لم يجد إلا حرة كتابية جاز له نكاح الأمة على أحسن الوجهين لأن الحذر
من مخالطة المشركات مهم ويشهد له ظاهر قوله {المحصنات المؤمنات}
الشرط الثالث خوف العنت وإنما يتم ذلك بغلبة الشهوة وضعف عصام التقوى ولا
يشترط في الخوف غلبة وقوع الزنا بل توقع وقوعه كما أن الطريق المخوف هو
الذي يتوقع فيه الهلاك وإن لم يغلب والأمن هو أن لا يتوقع وإن كان ذلك
ممكنا على الندور
ومن ضعفت شهوته وقوي تقواه فهو آمن ومن غلب عليه شهوته ولكنه راسخ التقوى
فإن كان يفضي به الصبر إلى مرض فلينكح الأمة وإلا فالصبر أحسن من إرقاق
الولد ولا يبعد أن يترخص ولا يكلف المشقة في مصابرة الشهوة
ومن قدر على التسري فالظاهر أنه لا ينكح الأمة لأنه لا يخاف العنت وفيه
وجه أنه ينكح لأن ملك اليمين لا يقصد به التحصن
الشرط الرابع في الأمة وهي أن تكون مسلمة فلا يحل عند الشافعي رضي الله
عنه للمسلم نكاح الأمة الكتابية بحال لقوله تعالى {من فتياتكم المؤمنات}
وكأن الأصل في المشركات والإماء التحريم وهذا مستثنى مع التقييد
الشرط الخامس أن تكون مملوكة لمسلم حتى لا يرق ولد المسلم لكافر وفي هذا
الشرط خلاف ولعل الظاهر أنه لا يشترط لأنه إن رق لكافر فيباع عليه في الحال
واختتام الشرائط بأمرين
أحدهما أن العبد لا تعتبر فيه الشرائط كلها إلا الشرط الرابع والخامس بل
الأمة في حقه كالحرة حتى يجوز له الجمع بين الأمتين ولا يجوز للحر الجمع
بين أمتين بحال وهذا لأن المحذور من نكاح الإماء إرقاق الولد والعبد رقيق
ليس عليه النظر لولده الموجود فلا يؤمر بالنظر لولده المفقود
والمكاتب ومن نصفه  رقيق في هذا كالعبد كما أن من نصفها رقيق كالأمة حتى
تفتقر إلى الشرائط في نكاح الحر إياها نعم يحتمل تردد في أن من قدر على
مثلثها هل يجوز له نكاح أمة كاملة الرق لأن إرقاق بعض الولد أهون من إرقاق
جميعه
وأما الحر الكتابي فهو كالمسلم في شرائط النكاح إلا في نكاح الأمة
الكتابية إذ نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه على أن الكافر يزوج أمته وذلك يدل على
أن تزويجها ممكن ويتجه ذلك من حيث إن الكفر ليس نقصا في حق الكافر ولكن هذا
ينقضه نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن العبد المسلم لا ينكح الأمة الكتابية
والرق ليس نقصا بالإضافة إليه لما اعتورها نقصان في حقه فمن الأصحاب من جعل
المسألتين على قولين ويرجع الخلاف إلى أن الأمة الكتابية هل هي محرمة في
عينها كالوثنيات أو هي محرمة لاجتماع النقصين
الأمر الثاني أن شرط فقد الحرة وطولها وخوف العنت يعتبر في ابتداء النكاح
دون دوامه فلو نكح حره على أمة يجوز وقال المزني ينقطع نكاحها بوجدان طول
الحرة والقدرة عليها فضلا عن وجودها ولم يطرد ذلك في زوال خوف العنت
وأما إسلام المالك إن شرطناه فلا شك في أنه لا يعتبر في الدوام
فرع لو جمع بين حرة وأمة في عقد واحد بطل نكاح الأمة وفي نكاح الحرة قولا
تفريق الصفقة الأصح وهو نص القديم صحة نكاح الحرة لأن النكاح لا يفسد بفساد
المهر فكيف يفسد بفساد القرينة المباينة له
ولو جمع بينهما من يحل له نكاح الأمة مع القدرة على الحرة وهي أن تكون
هذه الحرة رضيت بدون مهر المثل وقلنا لا يلزمه تقلد المنة فلا يصح هاهنا
نكاح الأمة لأن الأمة لا تضام الحرة فلا يصح إلا إذا سبق نكاحها وها هنا لم
يسبق وأما نكاح الحرة فطريقان
أحدهما طرد القولين
والاخر القطع بالفساد كما لو جمع بين أختين فإنه الآن قادر عليهما جميعا
وهذا بعيد لأن إحدى الأختين ليست أولى بالدفع وهاهنا الأمة أولى بالدفع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ق-ق (riqq)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is thinness and softness; applied to slavery as a legal state of diminished capacity and subjugation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudence, riqq denotes a legal deficiency (nuqṣān) that restricts the slave's eligibility and rights, particularly in marriage contracts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here as a legal impediment (māniʿ), not metaphorically; it is a concrete juridical category.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text uses layered conditional constructions (e.g., "if... then...") to delineate legal rulings, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for slavery (al-riqq), it is an impediment in general terms according to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) in certain situations. Thus, it is not permissible for a free Muslim man to marry a slave woman (amah) except under five conditions: three pertain to him — namely, the absence of a free woman under his authority (as wife), the lack of means to marry a free woman, and the fear of committing fornication (al-ʿanat); and two pertain to the slave woman — namely, that she be Muslim and owned by a Muslim.

The first condition is that he must not have a free woman under his authority. If he has a free wife who is barren (ratqāʾ), or decrepit (harmaʾ), or absent (ghāʾibah), or a Scriptuary (kitābiyyah), it is still not permissible for him to marry a slave woman; rather, he must divorce her. This differs from the case where he possesses wealth but it is absent — for he is then like one lacking the means (ka-l-fāqid li-l-ṭawl).

The second condition is the lack of means to marry a free woman. Whoever has no free wife but is able to marry one — it is not permissible for him to marry a slave woman, due to God's saying: {«And whoever among you cannot afford [the means] to marry free believing women»} — the verse. It is permissible for an insolvent man (al-muf lis) to marry a slave woman. If he finds a free woman who consents to a deferred dowry (mahr muʾajjal), it is permissible [for him to marry the slave woman], because the deferred term will eventually mature while he is currently in straitened circumstances. Likewise, if he has wealth that is absent and he fears fornication in the present moment before gaining access to that wealth. Similarly, if a free woman consents to less than the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl) and he possesses that amount, it is permissible — because he is not obliged to bear the burden of a favor (al-minnah). There is another view, chosen by al-Ṣaydalānī, that it is not permissible for him to marry a slave woman, because the favor of the dowry is deemed negligible in marriage, unlike the favor in selling water or a garment that covers the nakedness in prayer.

If he finds wealth but does not find a free woman to marry, it is permissible for him to marry a slave woman. If he finds only a free woman who demands an exorbitant dowry — an exorbitance such that bearing it would be considered wasteful (sarf) relative to the purposes of marriage — then he may marry a slave woman. But if that amount is close [to the norm], no concession is granted on its account.

Likewise, if the guardian (walī) reduces the equivalent dowry by an amount that is tolerable for the purposes of marriage, then no aversion (iʿrāḍ) should be established for the woman. But if he is excessive in the reduction, then the purposes of marriage override these trivialities. Similarly, if he finds only a free woman who is absent — an absence that is short and tolerable in the purposes of marriage — he should not marry a slave woman; but if the absence is long, he may marry a slave woman.

If he finds only a free Scriptuary woman, it is permissible for him to marry a slave woman according to the better of the two views, because the caution against mixing with polytheist women is significant. This is supported by the apparent meaning of His saying: {«...free believing women»}.

The third condition is the fear of fornication (khawf al-ʿanat). This is only fulfilled by the predominance of lust and the weakness of the restraint of piety (ʿiṣām al-taqwā). It is not required in this fear that the occurrence of fornication be predominant; rather, the anticipation of its occurrence suffices — just as a fearful road is one where destruction is anticipated, even if not predominant. And safety (al-amn) is that one does not anticipate it, even if it is possible on rare occasions.

Whoever's lust is weak and whose piety is strong is safe. Whoever's lust overcomes him but whose piety is firmly rooted — if patience would lead him to illness, let him marry a slave woman; otherwise, patience is better than enslaving one's offspring. It is not far-fetched that he may avail himself of the concession and not be burdened with hardship in resisting lust.

Whoever is able to take a concubine (tasarrī), the apparent view is that he should not marry a slave woman, because he does not fear fornication. There is a view that he may marry, because the possession of the right hand (milk al-yamīn) is not intended for the purpose of chastity (taḥaṣṣun).

The fourth condition pertains to the slave woman: that she be Muslim. It is not permissible, according to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him), for a Muslim to marry a Scriptuary slave woman under any circumstances, due to His saying: {«...from among your believing slave girls»}. It is as if the original ruling regarding polytheist women and slave women is prohibition, and this [permission] is an exception with restriction.

The fifth condition is that she be owned by a Muslim, so that the child of a Muslim is not enslaved to a disbeliever. There is disagreement regarding this condition. Perhaps the apparent view is that it is not required, because if the child is enslaved to a disbeliever, he would be sold away from him immediately.

The conclusion of the conditions concerns two matters:

The first: For a slave man (ʿabd), not all conditions are considered — only the fourth and fifth. Rather, a slave woman is like a free woman in his regard, such that it is permissible for him to combine two slave women [in marriage], whereas it is not permissible for a free man to combine two slave women under any circumstances. This is because the harm in marrying slave women is the enslavement of offspring, and a slave is himself enslaved — he is not charged with regard to his existing offspring, so he is not commanded to consider his future offspring.

The mukātab (slave under contract of manumission) and one who is half-free are like a slave in this matter, just as a woman who is half-free is like a slave woman — such that she requires the conditions when a free man marries her. Indeed, there is room for hesitation regarding whether one who can afford to marry a half-free woman may marry a fully enslaved woman, because the enslavement of part of one's offspring is lighter than the enslavement of all of it.

As for a free Scriptuary man, he is like a Muslim regarding the conditions of marriage, except in marrying a Scriptuary slave woman — for al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) explicitly stated that a disbeliever may marry off his slave woman, which indicates that marrying her is possible. This is reasoned from the fact that disbelief is not a deficiency in the disbeliever's own regard. However, this is refuted by al-Shāfiʿī's explicit statement that a Muslim slave man may not marry a Scriptuary slave woman — and slavery is not a deficiency relative to him. Since two deficiencies have converged in her regard, some companions treated the two cases as two positions (qawlān). The disagreement reduces to whether a Scriptuary slave woman is prohibited in her very essence, like idolatrous women, or whether she is prohibited due to the conjunction of the two deficiencies.

The second matter: The conditions of the absence of a free wife, the lack of means, and the fear of fornication are considered at the inception of the marriage, not its continuation. Thus, if a free man marries a slave woman permissibly, and then al-Muzanī said: "Her marriage is terminated upon his finding the means to a free woman and his ability to marry her" — let alone her actual presence. But this was not extended to the cessation of the fear of fornication.

As for the Islam of the owner — if we stipulate it — there is no doubt that it is not considered in the continuation.

A branch: If one combines a free woman and a slave woman in a single contract, the marriage to the slave woman is void. Regarding the marriage to the free woman, there are the two positions on the division of the transaction (tafrīq al-ṣafqah). The more correct view — and it is the text of the Old [School] (al-Qadīm) — is the validity of the marriage to the free woman, because marriage is not invalidated by the invalidity of the dowry; how then would it be invalidated by the invalidity of a separate concomitant?

If one combines them — where it is permissible for him to marry a slave woman despite his ability to marry a free woman, namely, when this free woman consents to less than the equivalent dowry and we hold that he is not obliged to bear the burden of a favor — then the marriage to the slave woman is not valid here, because a slave woman cannot be joined with a free woman [in a single contract]. It is only valid if her marriage precedes [the free woman's], and here it did not precede. As for the marriage to the free woman, there are two paths: one is to extend the two positions; the other is to decisively rule its invalidity — as in the case of combining two sisters, for he is now able to marry both. But this is far-fetched, because neither of the two sisters is more deserving of being repelled, whereas here the slave woman is more deserving of being repelled.

chapters.title_en: The Second Impediment: Ownership (al-Milk) and the Fourth Category of Impediments: Disbelief (al-Kufr)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المانع الثاني الملك

وهو وراء الرق فإن من يحل له نكاح الأمة لا يحل له أن ينكح أمة نفسه وإن
قلنا إن القدرة على التسري لا تمنع نكاح الأمة بل لو اشترى زوجته أو ورثها
انفسخ النكاح
وكذلك لا تنكح الحرة عبد نفسها ولو اشترت زوجها العبد أو ورثته انفسخ
النكاح

### | الجنس الرابع من الموانع

الكفر وفيه ثلاثة فصول

### | الفصل الأول في أصناف الكفار

وهي ثلاثة
الصنف الأول أهل الكتاب وهم اليهود والنصارى وكفرهم أخف فتحل مناكحتهم
وذبائحهم وحكمهم في حقوق النكاح كالمسلمات إلا في الميراث إذ لا إرث مع
اختلاف الدين ولا كراهية في نكاحهن فإن الاستفراش إهانة والكافرة جديرة
بذلك
وقال مالك يكره نكاحهن نعم الحربية الكتابية يكره نكاحها فإن صحبة الكفار
في ديارهم توجب الافتتان وربما تسبى الحربية وهي حامل بولد مسلم والكراهية
تثبت بأقل من هذا
الصنف الثاني عبدة الأوثان والمعطلة والدهرية ومن لا يقر بالجزية فلا يحل
نكاحهم وذبائحهم وتدخل فيهم المرتدة
الصنف الثالث المجوس ويسلك بهم مسلك أهل الكتاب في التقرير بالجزية دون
المناكحة والذبيحة وحكي في مناكحتهم قول بعيد للشافعي رضي الله عنه ولا وجه
له وقيل كان لهم كتاب فأسري به
ثم حق الكتابية في القسم والنفقة وسائر الحقوق كالمسلمة وللمسلم منعها من
الخروج إلى الكنائس كما له منع المسلمة من المساجد وله أن أن يلزمها الغسل
من الحيض حتى تحل له
وهل يلزمها الغسل من الجنابة لأجل العيافة فيه قولان وكذلك في إلزام
الاستحداد الذي يكسر
الشهوة تركه وكذلك في المنع من تناول الخنزير والمستقذرات وأكل الثوم وكل
ذلك في المسلمة أيضا

### | الفصل الثاني في أقسام أهل الكتاب

فنقول من آمن أول آبائه قبل التحريف أو بعده ولكن علم المحرف ولم يؤمن به
وكانت من نسب بني إسرائيل فقد اجتمع لهما الشرفان فيصح نكاحها قطعا وإن لم
تكن من بني إسرائيل ففي جواز نكاحها قولان وإن كان أول آبائها آمن بعد
التحريف ففي جواز نكاحها أيضا قولان وإن شككنا في ذلك  فقولان مرتبان وأولى
بالجواز
ولا خلاف في أن من آمن أول آبائه بعد المبعث أو شككنا في ذلك لم تحل
مناكحته
وإذا آمن أول آباء اليهودية بعد نزول عيسى عليه السلام فهل يكون كما بعد
المبعث فيه وجهان والأقيس ألا يعتبر نسب بني إسرائيل ولا يقدم إيمان الآباء
على التحريف
وأما الصابئون والسامرة وهم من طوائف اليهود والنصارى وبينهم خلاف في
الاعتقاد نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه في موضع على جواز مناكحتهم ونص في موضع
على خلافه واتفق جماهير الأصحاب على أن المسألة ليست على قولين ولكن ظن
الشافعي رضي الله عنه مرة أنهم يخالفون القوم فيما يوجب التكفير فتلتحق
بالزنادقة وظن مرة أنهم يخالفون فيما يوجب البدعة ونكاح المبتدعة صحيح
وأطلق الشيخ أبو علي طرد القولين

### | الفصل الثالث في تبديل الدين

وله صور
إحداها أن يتنصر يهودي أو يتهود نصراني ففيه ثلاثة أقوال
أحدها أنه يقرر عليه لأنهما دينان متساويان الآن
والثاني أنه لا يقنع منه إلا بالإسلام ولو عاد إلى تنصره لم يكفه لأنه
أبطل تلك العصمة فلا يستحدثه بعد المبعث عصمة
والثالث أنه لا يقنع منه إلا بالإسلام أو بالعود إلى التنصر فإن أصر
وقلنا لا يقر عليه فيلتحق بمأمنه أو يقتل قتل المرتد فيه قولان
الصورة الثانية أن يتنصر وثني فلا يقر عليه أصلا لأنه لم يكن معصوما
ويريد استحداث عصمة بدين باطل وإن توثن النصراني فلا يقر أصلا ولكن في قول
لا يقنع إلا بالإسلام وفي قول يقنع بالإسلام أو بالعود إلى التنصر وفي قول
يقنع وإن عاد إلى التهود
الصورة الثالثة أن يرتد مسلم والعياذ بالله فالأديان في حقه سواء ولا
يقنع منه إلا بالسيف أو الإسلام
ويمتنع نكاح المرتد والمرتدة وإن طرأ على دوام النكاح تنجزت الفرقه قبل
المسيس وإن جرى بعد المسيس توقف على انقضاء العدة عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه
فإن عاد إلى
الإسلام استمر العقد وإلا تبين بطلان النكاح بنفس الردة وكذلك لو ارتدا
معا فهو كما لو ارتد أحدهما  وكذلك لو أسلم أحد الزوجين المجوسيين أو
الوثنيين أو أسلمت الكتابية تحت كافر تنجزت الفرقة قبل المسيس وتوقف على
العدة بعد المسيس ولو أسلما معا استمر النكاح
فرع متولد من يهودي ومجوسي ففي حل مناكحته قولان
أحدهما التحريم تغليبا لجانب الحرمة
والثاني النظر إلى جانب الأب اعتبارا للنسب
ثم قال القفال هذا في الصغير فإن بلغ وتمجس فله ذلك وهو مجوسي ويحتمل أن
يقال إذا كان أبوه يهوديا لم يمكن من التمجس بعد البلوغ وجعل كاليهودي يمجس
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - هذا باب نكاح المشركات - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وهذا أوان ذكره لانشعاب مسائله عن الموانع السابقة وفيه فصول

### | الفصل الأول في حكم أنكحة الكفار في الصحة والفساد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Possession, dominion, ownership — the legal capacity of exclusive control over a thing or person.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ownership as a juridical construct that creates a barrier (māniʿ) to contractual validity, distinct from mere physical power (qudra).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal ownership (ḥaqīqah) of a slave versus metaphorical extension (majāz) in marital rights — the impediment is real, not figurative.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, concealing — theological disbelief as veiling of truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kufr as rejection of prophetic truth, graded by severity (akhaff = lighter for Ahl al-Kitāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal disbelief (kufr) versus legal classification (takfīr) — the distinction between what necessitates excommunication versus mere innovation (bidʿah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — the legal consequences (fasād, infisākh) are governed by temporal markers (qabla al-masīs / baʿdahu), requiring precise parsing of the protasis-apodosis structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second impediment is ownership (al-milk). It lies beyond the scope of slavery (al-riqq), for he to whom it is lawful to marry a slave-girl (al-amah) is not lawful for him to marry his own slave-girl — even if we hold that the capacity for taking a concubine (al-tasarrī) does not prevent marrying a slave-girl. Rather, if he purchases his wife [who is a slave] or inherits her, the marriage is dissolved (infasakha al-nikāḥ). Likewise, a free woman may not marry her own male slave; if she purchases her slave-husband or inherits him, the marriage is dissolved.

### The Fourth Category of Impediments: Disbelief (al-Kufr)
It comprises three chapters.

### Chapter One: On the Categories of Disbelievers
They are three categories.

**The First Category:** The People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitāb) — they are the Jews and the Christians. Their disbelief is the lightest (akhaff), so marrying them and [eating] their slaughtered meat (dhabāʾiḥ) is lawful. Their ruling in the rights of marriage is like that of Muslim women, except in inheritance — for there is no inheritance with differing religion. And there is no dislike (karāhah) in marrying them, for taking to bed (al-istifrāsh) is a form of humiliation, and the disbelieving woman is worthy of that. Mālik said: It is disliked to marry them. Yes, the scriptuary woman of the warring territory (al-ḥarbiyyah al-kitābiyyah) — her marriage is disliked, for companionship with disbelievers in their lands necessitates temptation (iftitān). Perhaps a ḥarbiyyah woman is captured while pregnant with a Muslim child — and dislike is established by less than this.

**The Second Category:** The idol-worshippers (ʿabadat al-awthān), the deniers of the Creator (al-muʿaṭṭilah), the materialists (al-dahriyyah), and those who do not acknowledge the poll-tax (al-jizyah). Their marriage and slaughtered meat are not lawful. The apostate woman (al-murtaddah) is included among them.

**The Third Category:** The Magians (al-Majūs). They are treated in the manner of the People of the Book regarding the imposition of the poll-tax, but not regarding marriage or slaughtered meat. A remote opinion (qawl baʿīd) has been reported from al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — regarding their marriage, but it has no basis. It was said that they had a scripture, but it was taken up [to heaven] (usriya bihi).

Then the scriptuary woman's right to division of nights (al-qasm), maintenance (al-nafaqah), and all other rights is like that of a Muslim woman. The Muslim husband may prevent her from going out to the churches, just as he may prevent a Muslim woman from [going to] the mosques. He may oblige her to perform the major ablution (al-ghusl) from menstruation so that she becomes lawful to him. Whether he may oblige her to perform the major ablution from sexual defilement (al-janābah) for the sake of aversion (al-ʿiyāfah) — there are two opinions (qawlān). Likewise regarding obliging her to remove pubic hair (al-istihdād) which breaks desire — its abandonment [is also disputed]. Likewise regarding preventing her from consuming pork, filth (al-mustaqdharāt), and eating garlic — all of this applies also to the Muslim woman.

### Chapter Two: On the Divisions of the People of the Book
We say: Whose first forefather believed before the corruption (taḥrīf) or after it, but he knew of the corruption and did not believe in it, and she was of the lineage of the Children of Israel (Banī Isrāʾīl) — then both honors (al-sharafān) have been combined for her, so her marriage is valid definitively. If she was not of the Children of Israel, then there are two opinions (qawlān) on the permissibility of her marriage. If her first forefather believed after the corruption, then there are also two opinions on the permissibility of her marriage. If we are doubtful about that, then there are two ordered opinions (qawlān murattabān), and the more appropriate is permissibility.

There is no disagreement that whose first forefather believed after the mission (al-mabʿath) [of the Prophet], or we are doubtful about that — his marriage is not lawful.

If the first forefather of a Jewish woman believed after the descent of Jesus — peace be upon him — is it like [believing] after the mission? There are two aspects (wajhān). The more analogically sound (al-aqyas) is that the lineage of the Children of Israel is not considered, nor is the faith of the forefathers before the corruption given precedence.

As for the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) and the Samaritans (al-Sāmirah) — they are sects of the Jews and Christians, with differences among them in belief. Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — stated in one place the permissibility of marrying them, and stated in another place the contrary. The majority of the companions (jamāhīr al-aṣḥāb) agreed that the issue is not [truly] two opinions, but rather al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — conjectured once that they differ from the [main] communities in what necessitates excommunication (takfīr), so they are annexed to the heretics (al-zanādiqah); and he conjectured another time that they differ in what necessitates innovation (bidʿah), and the marriage of an innovator (mubtadiʿah) is valid. Shaykh Abū ʿAlī [al-Ṭabarī] explicitly extended the two opinions [as genuine].

### Chapter Three: On Changing Religion (Tabdīl al-Dīn)
It has several forms.

**The First Form:** A Jew becomes a Christian, or a Christian becomes a Jew. There are three opinions (aqwāl):
1. One is that he is confirmed upon it, because the two religions are now equal.
2. The second is that nothing less than Islam is accepted from him; even if he returns to his Christianity, it does not suffice him — because he has nullified that [former] inviolability (ʿiṣmah), and he cannot newly acquire inviolability after the mission.
3. The third is that nothing less than Islam is accepted from him, or his return to Christianity. If he persists, and we say he is not confirmed upon it — then he is either sent to his place of safety (maʾmanihi) or killed as an apostate (qatl al-murtadd) — two opinions.

**The Second Form:** An idol-worshipper becomes a Christian. He is not confirmed upon it at all, because he was not inviolable [before], and he seeks to newly acquire inviolability through a false religion. If a Christian becomes an idol-worshipper, he is not confirmed upon it at all. But in one opinion, nothing less than Islam is accepted; in another opinion, Islam or return to Christianity is accepted; in another opinion, he is accepted even if he returns to Judaism.

**The Third Form:** A Muslim apostatizes — God forbid (wa al-ʿiyādhu billāh). The religions are equal in his regard, and nothing less than the sword or Islam is accepted from him.

The marriage of an apostate man (al-murtadd) and an apostate woman (al-murtaddah) is prevented. If apostasy occurs during the continuance of an existing marriage, the separation (al-furqah) is effected immediately before consummation (qabla al-masīs). If it occurs after consummation, it is suspended upon the completion of the waiting period (al-ʿiddah) according to al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him. If he returns to Islam, the contract continues; otherwise, it becomes evident that the marriage was void from the very act of apostasy (binafs al-riddah). Likewise, if both apostatize together, it is as if one of them apostatized. Likewise, if one of the two Magian or idol-worshipping spouses embraces Islam, or a scriptuary woman embraces Islam while under a disbelieving husband — the separation is effected immediately before consummation, and suspended upon the waiting period after consummation. If both embrace Islam together, the marriage continues.

**A Branch (Farʿ):** A child born of a Jewish father and a Magian mother — regarding the lawfulness of marrying him, there are two opinions:
1. One is prohibition, giving preponderance to the side of unlawfulness (taghlīban li-jānib al-ḥurmah).
2. The second is looking to the side of the father, considering lineage (iʿtibāran lil-nasab).

Then al-Qaffāl said: This applies to the minor. If he reaches maturity and becomes a Magian, he may do so, and he is a Magian. It is possible to say: If his father was Jewish, he is not permitted to become a Magian after maturity, and he is treated like a Jew who becomes a Magian — may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the chapter on marrying polytheistic women — may God bless him and grant him peace. And this is the time to mention it, for its issues branch out from the preceding impediments. It contains chapters.

### Chapter One: On the Ruling of the Marriages of Disbelievers Regarding Validity and Corruption
