أجرة الصنعة من نقد البلد
المسألة الرابعة لو أصدق الذمي زوجته خمرا فقبضت ثم أسلما فانقلب خلا
فطلقها ففيه وجهان
أحدهما وهو قول ابن حداد أنه يرجع بنصف الخل
والثاني أنه لا يرجع لأن هذا مالية جديدة ومالية الخمر قبلها لا تعتبر في
الإسلام فكيف يرجع فيها وهو لا يرجع في زيادة منفصلة
التفريع إن قلنا يرجع فلو أتلفت الخل ثم طلقها قال الخضري يرجع بمثل بنصف
الخل لأنه من ذوات الأمثال
وقال ابن الحداد لايرجع بشيئ لأنه في التلف ينظر إلى قيمة يوم الإصداق أو
القبض ولم يكن  خلا ذلك اليوم حتى يجب مثله ولا هو موجود في الحال حتى يرد
عينه
ولو أصدقها جلد ميتة فدبغته فمنع الرجوع هاهنا أولى إذ حصلت المالية
باختيارها
فإن قلنا يرجع فقول ابن الحداد في أنه لا يرجع عند التلف هاهنا أظهر لأنه
لا مثل له فتتعين قيمته يوم القبض ولا قيمة له إذ ذاك
المسألة الخامسة لو أصدقها دينا ثم سلم فطلق فليس لها منعه من عين ما سلم
وإن لم
يكن متعينا في العقد لأنه أقرب إلى حقه لا محالة وقيل إن لها الإبدال فإن
العقد لم يرد عليه بعينه
المسألة السادسة لو أصدقها تعليم القرآن فلم يتفق حتى طلقها فقد عسر
التعليم وبقي في ذمته الشطر وتعسر تعيين شطر القرآن إذ سوره تختلف في العسر
واليسر وكذلك خياطة نصف الثوب تعسر إذا أصدقها الخياطة فلها نصف مهر المثل
على قول ضمان العقد وعلى القول الثاني نصف أجرة الخياطة أو التعليم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-م-ح (s-m-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be lenient, to concede, to be generous in yielding" — the root conveys easing a burden by voluntary relinquishment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, musāmahah denotes a unilateral or bilateral relaxation of a strict right, distinct from ibrah (release) which is absolute, and from muwāfaqah (mutual accord) which is a reciprocal pact.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "to make wide/spacious" (as in a broad path); metaphorically (majāz), it is "to widen the scope of another's option by removing one's own insistence."
- Root: و-ف-ق (w-f-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to agree, to be harmonious, to fit together" — from it derives tawfīq (divine accord) and muwāfaqah (mutual consent).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Muwāfaqah in contractual contexts implies a bilateral meeting of wills that creates mutual obligations, unlike musāmahah which is a one-sided concession.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to find the right way" (as in hitting a mark); metaphorical sense is "two parties aligning their intentions on a shared course of action."
- Root: ع-س-ر (ʿ-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "difficulty, hardship, straitness" — the opposite of yusr (ease).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic reasoning, ʿusr is the operative cause (ʿillah) for invoking concessionary rulings (rukhṣah) and for overriding strict contractual terms.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "narrowness" (as in a constricted path); metaphorical sense is "a situation that presses upon one's capacity to fulfill an obligation."
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Suspended Judgment (al-Sharṭ al-Muʿallaq) — When a legal consequence is made contingent upon a future condition (e.g., "if he fulfills the promise"), the ruling remains suspended (mawqūf) until the condition is realized; if the condition fails, the original state is re-established retroactively.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for mutual concession (musāmahah), it has several forms.

The first: The husband says, "I return to half of the trees, but I will not water them, and the choice is yours — if you wish, water them, and if you wish, leave off watering." She is not obliged to respond [by watering], because she is harmed by leaving off watering while his trees benefit from her watering. Likewise, her concession in this manner does not necessitate the obligation of response.

The second: The husband says, "I take half of the trees and I will water them myself," or the woman says, "Return to the half, and I undertake the watering." Then there are two views (wajhān) regarding the obligation to grant the request (ījāb al-isʿāf):
One of them: Yes, it is obligatory, because the hardship (al-ʿusr) is repelled by the concession and the undertaking.
The second: No, it is not obligatory, because it is a promise (waʿd) whose fulfillment is not binding, and because the woman might fear for her fruits due to his entering the orchard, or he might fear for the trees due to her entering it.

If we say he is to be granted [the request], then if he returns [to the half] and leaves off watering, we determine that ownership did not transfer to him in the half, because it was suspended (mawqūf) upon fulfillment of the promise. And if we say he is not to be granted, then she receives the value (al-qīmah). Then if he fulfills the promise, there is hesitation (taraddud) regarding returning the value and reverting to the specific property (al-ʿayn). The apparent [view] is that he does not return it, since it is far-fetched to negate a ruling after it has been established.

The third: That she hastens to cut her fruits, and this cuts off the hardship. If she gifts half of the fruits to him such that the whole becomes shared, then there are two views on the obligation of response. The view of prevention (manʿ) is based on what it contains of obligation (minnah). The view of obligation is based on necessity (ḍarūrah). This necessity does not apply to cultivated land (al-arḍ al-mazrūʿah), for land does not benefit from watering. So if he returns to half of the land, she must water for the sake of her own crops. This hardship also applies in the case where he gave her as dowry a slave-girl (jāriyah) who then gave birth, and he divorced her while the child is still nursing — for if he returns to half of the slave-girl, the child is harmed by the cutting off of nursing. If he says, "I am content that she remain a wet-nurse until weaning," then this is a form of concession, and there are two views on the obligation of response.

As for mutual agreement (muwāfaqah), it has two forms:

The first: That one of them undertakes the watering with the consent of the other. This is a mutual promise (tawāʿud) from them. If they fulfill it, then that is that; otherwise, it becomes clear that ownership was not obtained in the half-share.

The second: That they mutually agree that the husband takes half of the palm-trees, and neither of them undertakes watering, but rather the watering is left off, or whoever wishes waters as a volunteer. If one of them regrets and says, "I want to water," he is not permitted to do so — unlike the case where he undertook watering and then regretted, because that [undertaking] is a relinquishment of a right and an undertaking of harm, so it is binding. As for undertaking watering, it is a promise that is not binding before delivery (taslīm).

The second question: If he gave her as dowry a pregnant slave-girl, and she gave birth, then he divorced her — he returns to half of the child if we say that the child is offset by a portion of the price. And it was said: No, he does not return, because most of the value was obtained through separation (infiṣāl) in her ownership, and this increase occurred in her possession and belongs to her, and the value of the fetus cannot be distinguished from the separated [child], since the fetus has no value. And if we say that no portion of the price is offset by it, then we surrender the child to her.

The third question: If he gave her as dowry jewelry (ḥuliyy), and she broke it and remade it into another craft, this is an increase in one respect and a decrease in another. She has the choice. If she remade that same craft [as originally], does she have the right to refuse surrendering half? There are two views:
One of them: No, just as if it were fat and then became thin, then returned to fat.
The second: She has the right to refuse — and this is the choice of Ibn al-Ḥaddād — because it is an increase that occurred by her own choice.

The ramification (tafrīʿ): If we say he returns with half the value, the correct [view] is that he returns with half the value including the craft. And it was said: He returns to the equivalent of half a bar (tibr) of the jewelry, weight for weight, and then the woman pays half the wage of the craft in the currency of the land.

The fourth question: If a dhimmī gave his wife wine (khamr) as dowry, and she took possession, then both embraced Islam, and it turned into vinegar (khall), then he divorced her — there are two views:
One of them — and it is the saying of Ibn Ḥaddād — that he returns with half of the vinegar.
The second: That he does not return, because this is a new property-value (māliyyah jadīdah), and the property-value of the wine before [Islam] is not considered in Islam. So how can he return to it, when he does not return to a detached increase (ziyādah munfaṣilah)?

The ramification: If we say he returns, then if she destroyed the vinegar and then he divorced her, al-Khaḍirī said: He returns with the equivalent (mithl) of half of the vinegar, because it is among things with equivalents (dhawāt al-amthāl). Ibn al-Ḥaddād said: He does not return with anything, because in destruction, one looks to the value on the day of the dowry contract or the day of possession, and it was not vinegar on that day such that its equivalent would be obligatory; nor is it existent at present such that its specific entity would be returned.

And if he gave her as dowry the skin of a dead animal (jild maytah), and she tanned it (dabaghat-hu), then preventing the return here is more appropriate (awlā), since the property-value was obtained by her own choice. If we say he returns, then the saying of Ibn al-Ḥaddād that he does not return upon destruction is more manifest (aẓhar) here, because it has no equivalent, so its value on the day of possession is determined — and it had no value at that time.

The fifth question: If he gave her as dowry a debt (dayn), then he paid it (sallama), then divorced her — she does not have the right to prevent him from the specific entity of what was paid, even if it was not specified (mutʿayyan) in the contract, because it is closer to his right, without doubt. And it was said: She has the right to substitute (ibdāl), because the contract did not apply to it as a specific entity.

The sixth question: If he gave her as dowry the teaching of the Qurʾān (taʿlīm al-Qurʾān), and it did not happen until he divorced her — the teaching has become difficult (taʿassara), and half remains in his liability (dhimmah), and specifying half of the Qurʾān is difficult, since its sūrahs differ in ease and difficulty. Likewise, sewing half of a garment becomes difficult if he gave her sewing as dowry. So she receives half of the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl) on the view of contractual liability (ḍamān al-ʿaqd); and on the second view, half of the wage of sewing or teaching.

chapters.title_en: Two Governing Principles and the Third Chapter on Acts Preventing Reclamation
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قاعدتان ينعطف حكمهما على المسائل

الأولى أنا حيث أثبتنا الخيار من الجانبين فلا نحكم بالملك قبل الاختبار
وإن فرعنا على الأصح في أن الصداق يتشطر بنفس الطلاق ولكن ننتظر ما يجري من
اختيار أو توافق ولا يكون هذا الخيار على الفور بل هو كخيار الرجوع في
الهبة وإذا ثبت لها الخيار لم يسقط بالتأخير بل للزوج المطالبة بحقه إما
القيمة وإما العين فإن أبت حبس القاضي عين الصداق عنهما وامتنع تصرفها كما
في الرهن
وإذا ثبت الخيار لها في صورة الزيادة المتصلة وأصرت على المنع باع القاضي
من نصف الصداق ما بقي بنصف القيمة دون تقدير الزيادة فإن كان لا يشتري
النصف بأكثر من نصف القيمة فلا فائدة في البيع فالصحيح أنه يسلم إليه ولكن
لا يملكه ما لم يقض له القاضي به لأنه يدرك بالاجتهاد وفي نص الشافعي رضي
الله عنه على هذا غلط من غلط حيث اعتبر القضاء في أصل التشطير
والثانية إذا مست الحاجة إلى القيمة فأي قيمة تعتبر
ينظر إن تلف في يدها بعد  الطلاق وقلنا إنه مضمون عليها فيعتبر يوم التلف
أما إذا تلف من قبل أو امتنع الرد إليه لعيب أو زيادة فالواجب عليها أقل
قيمة من يوم الإصداق إلى الإقباض لأنه إن نقص قبل الإقباض فهو من ضمان
الزوج فلا يحسب عليها وإن كان يحتمل أن يقال إن كان المانع هو الزيادة
والعين قائمة تعتبر حالة التقويم لكن قدرت الزيادة كالمفوت للرجوع

### | الفصل الثالث في التصرفات المانعة من الرجوع

وفيه مسائل
إحداها إذا زال ملكها بجهة لازمة من بيع أو هبة أو عتق امتنع الرجوع
وتقرر القيمة
وإن تعلق به حق لازم من غير زوال ملك كرهن أو إجارة فليس له الفسخ وله
طلب القيمة في الحال فإن قال أنتظر الفكاك للرجوع فلها إجباره على قبول
القيمة خيفة من غرر الضمان إن قلنا إن الصداق بعد الطلاق مضمون في يدها
وإن قلنا لا ضمان أو أبرأها من الضمان حيث نصحح الإبراء عن ضمان ما لم
يجب فهل تلزمها الإجابة فيه وجهان ومنشؤهما أن هذا وعد وربما يبدو له
المطالبة بالقيمة وتخلو يدها في ذلك الوقت عن النقد وإن قلنا لا يلزمها
الإجابة فلو لم تتفق المطالبة حتى انفك فهل له الآن التعلق بالعين فيه
وجهان
أحدهما نعم لأنه لا مانع
والثاني لا إذ المانع نقل حقه إلى القيمة فلا ينقض بعده
الثانية لو أصدقها عبدا فدبرته ثم طلقها نقل المزني أنه تتعين القيمة
فاختلف
الأصحاب على ثلاث طرق
منهم من قطع بأنه غلط لأن التدبير لا يمنع إزالة الملك اختيارا فكيف يمنع
الرجوع قهرا ومنهم من قرر النص وقال التدبير قربة مقصودة فلا يتقاعد عن
زيادة متصلة مقصودة لا تؤثر في زيادة القيمة فإنها تمنع الرجوع قهرا ومنهم
من قال المسألة على قولين ينبنيان على أن التدبير وصية أو تعليق
فإن قلنا تعليق فيمتنع الرجوع لأن إبطال التعليق بالتصريح به ممتنع وهذا
البناء ضعيف فإن التعليق لا يمنع البيع فكيف يمنع التشطير
ثم اختلف المقررون للنص في أن صريح تعليق العتق  هل يكون كالتدبير وأن
الوصية بالعتق للعبد هل تكون كالتدبير وأن التدبير هل يمنع الرجوع في الهبه
ورجوع البائع في العوض المتسرد عن رد المعوض بالعيب والأظهر أنه لا يمنع
الثالثة إذا أصدقها صيدا والزوج محرم عند الطلاق فإن قلنا إنه يحتاج إلى
الاختيار فهو كشراء المحرم للصيد وفيه خلاف وإن قلنا ينقلب إليه فهاهنا
وجهان
أحدهما أنه ينقلب إليه لأنه ملك قهري فهو كالإرث
والثاني أنه كالشراء لأن الطلاق إلى اختياره
فإن قلنا لا ينقلب فيرجع إلى نصف القيمة وإن كان المانع من جهته وإن قلنا
ينقلب فكيف يجب إرسال نصف الصيد أو كيف يمسك ونصفه لمحرم وفيه خلاف يبنى
على أن المقدم عند التزاحم حق الله تعالى أو حق الآدمي أم يتساويان فإن
قدمنا حق الله وجب على الزوج الإرسال وغرم قيمة نصيبها وإن قلنا حق الآدمي
بقي ملكا للمحرم للضرورة وإن قلنا يتساويان فإليهما الخيرة فإن أرسله الرجل
برضاها غرم لها وإلا بقي مشتركا
الرابعة إذا زال ملكها بغيب أو هبة لازمة ثم عاد فهل يمتنع الرجوع فيه
قولان مأخذهما أن الزائل العائد كالذي لم يزل أو كالذي لم يعد وإن كان
الطارئ هو الرهن والإجارة فإذا زال لم يمتنع الرجوع
وترددوا في الكتابة والتدبير والصحيح أنهما بعد الانقطاع لا يمنعان
الرجوع عند الطلاق
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is selection, choice, or the better of two things; in legal context, it denotes an elective right (khiyār) granted to a party.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential theology, khiyār reflects the moral agency of the contracting party, balancing divine command with human discretion in transactional justice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to actual choosing; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the legal power to affirm or rescind a contract.
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes standing, value, or subsistence; in legal terms, it yields qīmah (monetary value) and taqwīm (valuation).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Valuation is tied to equitable compensation (miṯl) in cases where the specific object (ʿayn) is lost or inaccessible, ensuring no unjust enrichment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal meaning is "standing upright"; metaphorical usage in law refers to assessing a substitute value when the original is unattainable.
- Root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is return, reversion, or revocation; in marriage law, it denotes the husband's right to take back the wife during ʿiddah (waiting period).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, rujūʿ signifies the restoration of a prior state, often involving the reclamation of property or rights after a temporary transfer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is physical return; metaphorical usage in jurisprudence refers to legal reclamation, such as revoking a gift (hibah) or reclaiming a dower (ṣadāq).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text frequently uses conditional clauses (e.g., "if she refuses," "if the impediment is from his side") to structure legal rulings, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine the operative legal outcome.
chapters.translation:
I say: Two principles whose ruling applies to the various issues [follow].

The first principle: Wherever we have established the option (khiyār) for both parties, we do not rule on ownership before the exercise of choice. Even if we build upon the more correct view that the dower (ṣadāq) is split by the very act of divorce, we still await what occurs—either a choice or mutual agreement. This option is not immediate; rather, it is like the option of revocation in a gift (hibah). When the option is established for her, it is not forfeited by delay. Rather, the husband may demand his right—either the value (qīmah) or the specific object (ʿayn). If she refuses, the judge (qāḍī) detains the dower's specific object from both of them, and her disposition of it is prevented, as in the case of a pledge (rahn).

When the option is established for her in the case of a connected increase (ziyādah muttaṣilah), and she persists in refusal, the judge sells from half of the dower what remains at half of its value, without assessing the increase. If the half cannot be sold for more than half the value, then there is no benefit in the sale. The correct view is that it is surrendered to him, but he does not own it until the judge rules in his favor, because it is attainable through juristic reasoning (ijtihād). In the text of al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) on this point, one who erred has erred, for he considered the judge's ruling necessary in the very principle of splitting (tashṭīr).

The second principle: When the need arises for the value (qīmah), which value is to be considered? We look: if the object perishes in her possession after the divorce, and we hold that it is guaranteed (maḍmūn) upon her, then the day of perishing is considered. However, if it perished beforehand, or her return of it is prevented due to a defect or an increase, then what is obligatory upon her is the least value from the day of the dower's contract (īṣdāq) to the day of delivery (iqbāḍ). This is because if it decreased before delivery, that decrease is from the husband's guarantee, so it is not counted against her. Although it might be said that if the impediment is the increase and the specific object remains extant, the valuation at the time of appraisal is considered, but the increase is treated as something that defeats the right of reclamation.

### Chapter Three: On Acts That Prevent Reclamation

This chapter contains several issues.

The first issue: If her ownership is removed by a binding cause—such as sale, gift, or manumission—reclamation is prevented, and the value is established. If a binding right attaches to it without removal of ownership—such as a pledge (rahn) or lease (ijārah)—then he has no right to rescind, but he may demand the value immediately. If he says, "I will wait for the release (fakāk) in order to reclaim," she may compel him to accept the value, out of fear of the risk of guarantee (gharar al-ḍamān), if we hold that the dower after divorce is guaranteed in her possession. If we hold there is no guarantee, or she has released him from the guarantee—where we deem valid the release from a guarantee for what has not yet become obligatory—then are two views on whether she must respond [to his demand]. The source of these two views is that this is a promise, and perhaps he may later demand the value, and her hand may be empty of cash at that time. If we hold that she is not obliged to respond, and the demand does not coincide until the release occurs, then does he now have the right to attach to the specific object? There are two views: One is yes, because there is no impediment. The second is no, because the impediment—his transfer of his right to the value—cannot be rescinded afterward.

The second issue: If he gave her as dower a slave, and she made him a mudabbar (one whose manumission is deferred upon the master's death), then he divorced her. Al-Muzanī transmitted that the value becomes obligatory. The companions differed on three paths: Among them are those who definitively held it an error, because tadbīr does not prevent the removal of ownership voluntarily, so how could it prevent reclamation by force? Among them are those who affirmed the text and said: Tadhīr is an intended act of devotion (qurbah), so it does not fall short of an intended connected increase that does not affect the increase in value—for such an increase prevents reclamation by force. Among them are those who said the issue rests on two views, built upon whether tadbīr is a bequest (waṣiyyah) or a conditional suspension (taʿlīq). If we say it is a suspension, then reclamation is prevented, because nullifying a suspension by explicit statement is impossible. But this construction is weak, for a suspension does not prevent sale, so how could it prevent splitting (tashṭīr)?

Then those who affirmed the text differed on whether an explicit conditional suspension of manumission is like tadbīr, whether a bequest of manumission for the slave is like tadbīr, and whether tadbīr prevents reclamation in a gift (hibah) and the seller's reclamation of the consideration returned due to the rejection of the sold object for a defect. The more apparent view is that it does not prevent.

The third issue: If he gave her as dower a hunted animal (ṣayd), and the husband is in a state of iḥrām at the time of divorce, then if we say he needs to exercise choice, it is like a muḥrim purchasing a hunted animal, and there is a difference of opinion on it. If we say it reverts to him, then there are two views here: One is that it reverts to him, because it is compulsory ownership, like inheritance. The second is that it is like purchase, because divorce is subject to his choice. If we say it does not revert, then he returns to half the value, even if the impediment is from his side. If we say it reverts, then how must half of the hunted animal be released, or how can he retain it while half belongs to a muḥrim? There is a difference of opinion built upon whether, when rights conflict, the right of God (ḥaqq Allāh) takes precedence, or the right of a human being (ḥaqq al-ādamī), or whether they are equal. If we give precedence to God's right, the husband must release it and pay the value of her share. If we say the human right prevails, it remains the property of the muḥrim out of necessity. If we say they are equal, then the choice is theirs: if the man releases it with her consent, he pays her; otherwise, it remains shared.

The fourth issue: If her ownership is removed by a gift or a binding gift, then it returns—does reclamation become prevented? There are two views, whose source is whether that which has gone and returned is like that which never went, or like that which never returned. If the intervening cause is a pledge or lease, then when it ceases, reclamation is not prevented. They hesitated regarding kitābah (contract of manumission) and tadbīr, and the correct view is that after their termination, they do not prevent reclamation at the time of divorce.

chapters.title_en: Section 366: On the Wife Gifting the Dowry to Her Husband, Then His Divorcing Her
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الرابع فيما لو وهبت الصداق من زوجها ثم طلقها

ونقدم عليه مقدمتين
إحداهما أن الله تعالى قال {فنصف ما فرضتم إلا أن يعفون أو يعفو الذي
بيده عقدة النكاح}
أما عفوهن فمعلوم أنه يوجب سقوط حقهن عن النصف الباقي إذا كان الصداق في
الذمة
أما الذي بيده عقدة النكاح فقد اختلفوا فيه
فمذهب ابن عباس وهو القول القديم أن المراد به الولي دون الزوج لأنه ذكر
الأزواج
بصيغة المخاطبة فقال {فنصف ما فرضتم} وهذا بصيغة المغايبة ولأنه عطف على
عفوها فليحمل على من يوجب عفوه سلامة الصداق له
ومذهب علي وابن جريج وابن المسيب رضي الله عنهم أن المراد به الزوج وهو
الجديد لأنه ذكر عفوها الموجب لخلوص الجميع له ثم ذكر عفوه الموجب لخلوص
الجميع لها وهذا يؤيد قول الحاجة إلى الاختيار ولأنه قال {أقرب للتقوى}
وعفو الولي لا يوصف بذلك

### | التفريع

إن منعنا عفو الولي وهو القياس فلا كلام وإن أثبتنا عفوه فهو مقيد بخمس
شرائط
أن يكون الولي مجبرا كالأب والجد
وأن لا تكون مالكة أمر نفسها
وأن يكون قبل المسيس فأما ما بعده تعطيل لحقها
وأن يكون بعد الطلاق لا قبله فإن كان معه بأن اختلعها بالمهر ففيه تردد
والأظهر أنه كالمتأخر
وأن يكون الصداق دينا إذ لفظ العفو إنما يستعمل فيه لا في العين وقال
الشيخ أبو محمد العين في معنى الدين في حكم القياس والمصلحة لأنه جوز رخصة
لتخليصها إذا مست الحاجة إليه ثم اختلف الأصحاب في ثلاث مسائل
إحداها أنه هل يعفو مهر الصغيرة المجنونة فقيل نعم للعموم وقيل لا لأن
الغرض تخليصها لتنكح غيره وهذه لا يرغب فيها
الثانية البكر البالغ قيل يعفو عن مهرها للعموم وقيل لا لأنها مالكة أمر
نفسها وعلى هذا ينبني أن الولي هل يستقل بقبض صداقها وكأن من جوز ذلك سحب
ولايته على عوض البضع لتعلقه بالبضع
الثالثة البكر الصغيرة إذا زوجت وثابت في صلب النكاح بوطء شبهة فالظاهر
أنه ليس للولي العفو لأن عقدة النكاح ليست بيده الآن
المقدمة الثانية في ألفاظ العفو إذا كان الصداق دينا يسقط بلفظ العفو
والإبراء ولا يحتاج إلى القبول على الصحيح ولو قالت وهبت فهل يفتقر إلى
القبول فيه وجهان وإن كان عينا لم يسقط بلفظ الإبراء وإن قبل وفي لفظ العفو
تردد والأشهر أنه كلفظ الإبراء وقال القاضي يكفي ذلك في الصداق خاصة لعموم
الآية
رجعنا إلى المقصود فنقول في رجوع الصداق إلى الزوج قبل الطلاق خمس صور
إحداها أن يكون بمعاوضة فإذا طلق رجع إلى القيمة سواء كان محاباة أو بثمن
المثل
الثانية أن يرجع بهبة وهل يمنع الرجوع بالقيمة عليها فيه قولان
الثالثة أن يكون دينا ورجع بالإبراء فطريقان
منهم من قطع بأنه لا يرجع بالقيمة
ومنهم من قال قولان
الرابعة أن يكون بهبة الدين وفيه قولان مرتبان وأولى بالرجوع
الخامسة أن يكون بهبة الدين المقبوض وفيه قولان مرتبان وأولى بأن يرجع

### | توجيه أصل القولين

من قال لا يرجع جعل هبة الصداق كتعجيل رده إليه قبل الطلاق ومن قال يرجع
أنكر أن تكون الهبة تعجيلا إذ لو صرح بالتعجيل لم يصح بل الهبة سبب مستأنف
لا يغير حكم الطلاق وترتيب الإبراء على الهبة سببه أن الإبراء يضاهي
الإسقاط من وجه ولكن لا يشترط فيه القبول في ظاهر المذهب ويجري القولان في
الفسوخ وكل جهة تقتضي الرجوع إلى عوض حتى لو باع عبدا بجارية فوهب منه
العبد ثم أراد رد الجارية بالعيب لم يجز له طلب قيمة العبد على هذا القول
ويمتنع بسببه رد الجارية عند بعضهم لعروه عن الفائدة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes effacement, obliteration, and pardoning—the act of erasing a claim or obligation entirely.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, ʿafw signifies the voluntary relinquishment of a right (isqāṭ al-ḥaqq), particularly the remission of a debt or obligation owed to the remitter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to debts and obligations in the dhimmah (liability); metaphorical (majāz) extension to specific chattels (al-ʿayn) is contested, as the root's core sense of "erasure" fits abstract liabilities, not physical objects.
- Root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes bestowal and gratuitous giving without expectation of compensation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hibah in juristic discourse is a unilateral gift contract, distinct from ṣadaqah (charity) in lacking a spiritual reward motive, and from ʿafw in requiring acceptance (qabūl) for completion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is a transfer of ownership (tamlīk) in exchange for nothing; metaphorical usage may extend to remission of debts, but this is a secondary derivation requiring contextual justification.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Nasaq (Coordination of Sequence) — When a clause is coordinated with a preceding one via wa, the coordinated element shares the grammatical case and, crucially, the semantic scope of the antecedent, unless a separate governing context (qarīnah) intervenes. This rule underpins the dispute over whether "the one in whose hand is the marriage knot" (alladhī bi-yadihi ʿuqdat al-nikāḥ) refers to the husband (coordinated with the wives' pardon) or the guardian (distinguished by the shift from second-person to third-person address).
chapters.translation:
I say: We preface this section with two introductory matters.

The first: God Most High has said {«...then half of what you have fixed [as dowry], unless they [the wives] pardon, or the one in whose hand is the marriage knot pardons»}. As for their pardon, it is known that it necessitates the fall of their right to the remaining half when the dowry is a debt in the liability (dhimmah). As for the one in whose hand is the marriage knot, there is disagreement concerning him. The doctrine of Ibn ʿAbbās—and this is the old opinion (al-qawl al-qadīm)—is that what is meant is the guardian, not the husband, because the verse mentions the husbands in the second-person address, saying {«...then half of what you have fixed»}, whereas this [latter clause] is in the third-person form, and because it is coordinated with her pardon, so it should be carried upon the one whose pardon entails the soundness of the dowry for him [i.e., the guardian's pardon secures the dowry for the husband]. The doctrine of ʿAlī, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn al-Musayyib—may God be pleased with them—is that what is meant is the husband, and this is the new opinion (al-jadīd), because He mentioned her pardon, which necessitates the entirety [of the dowry] being reserved for him, then mentioned his pardon, which necessitates the entirety being reserved for her. And this supports the need for choice [between the two pardons]. And because He said {«...that is nearer to piety»}—and the guardian's pardon is not described by that.

### | Ramification

If we disallow the guardian's pardon—and this is the analogical position (al-qiyās)—then there is no further discussion. But if we affirm it, it is restricted by five conditions: that the guardian be one with coercive authority (mujbir), such as the father and grandfather; that she not be the owner of her own affair; that it be before consummation (masīs)—for after that, it is a nullification of her right; that it be after the divorce, not before—for if it were simultaneous with it, as when he divorced her in exchange for the dowry (khulʿ), there is hesitation, and the more apparent view is that it is like the delayed [pardon]; and that the dowry be a debt, for the expression "pardon" (ʿafw) is only used for that, not for specific chattel (al-ʿayn). Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: specific chattel is in the meaning of debt in the ruling of analogy and public interest (maṣlaḥah), because the concession was permitted for her release when need arises for it.

Then the companions (aṣḥāb) differed on three subsidiary questions. The first: whether the guardian may pardon the dowry of a minor or insane girl. It was said yes, for the generality [of the verse]; and it was said no, because the purpose is her release so that she may marry another, and such a one is not desired [in marriage]. The second: concerning a mature virgin—it was said he may pardon her dowry, for the generality; and it was said no, because she is the owner of her own affair. Upon this is built the question of whether the guardian is independent in receiving her dowry—and it is as though the one who permitted that extended his guardianship over the compensation for the vulva (badal al-buḍʿ) due to its connection to the vulva. The third: concerning a minor virgin who is married and then confirmed within the marriage bond through intercourse under a semblance of right (waṭʾ shubhah)—the apparent view is that the guardian has no right to pardon, because the marriage knot is not in his hand at that moment.

The second introductory matter concerns the expressions of pardon. When the dowry is a debt, it falls by the expression "pardon" (ʿafw) and "acquittance" (ibrāʾ), and acceptance is not required on the correct view. If she said "I have gifted" (wahaba), then is acceptance required? There are two positions. If it is specific chattel, it does not fall by the expression of acquittance even if accepted; and concerning the expression "pardon," there is hesitation, with the more famous view being that it is like the expression of acquittance. Al-Qāḍī said: that suffices for the dowry specifically, due to the generality of the verse.

We return to the main purpose and say: concerning the return of the dowry to the husband before divorce, there are five forms. The first: that it be by way of exchange (muʿāwaḍah)—then if he divorces, he returns to the value, whether it was a favorable deal or at the fair price. The second: that it return by way of gift (hibah)—and whether the return of the value is prevented upon her: there are two positions. The third: that it be a debt and returns by acquittance—there are two paths: some definitively hold that he does not return to the value; others say there are two positions. The fourth: that it be by gifting a debt—there are two positions, ordered, and the return is more appropriate. The fifth: that it be by gifting a debt already received—there are two positions, ordered, and the return is even more appropriate.

### | Directing the Basis of the Two Positions

The one who says he does not return treats the gifting of the dowry as an acceleration of its return to him before the divorce. The one who says he returns denies that the gift is an acceleration, for if he had explicitly stated acceleration, it would not be valid—rather, the gift is an independent cause (sabab mustaʾnaf) that does not alter the ruling of divorce. The ordering of acquittance upon the gift is because acquittance resembles an annulment (isqāṭ) in one respect, but acceptance is not stipulated in it on the apparent doctrine. The two positions apply to rescissions (fusūkh) and every ground that entails return to a compensation—such that if a man sold a slave for a slave-girl, then the slave was gifted back to him, and he then wished to return the slave-girl for a defect, he may not demand the value of the slave on this position; and by reason of it, the return of the slave-girl is prevented according to some, due to its being devoid of benefit.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرعان

أحدهما لو وهبت من الزوج نصف الصداق ثم طلقها فإن قلنا الهبة لا تمنع
الرجوع فله الرجوع بالنصف وفي كيفيته ثلاثة أقوال
أحدها أنه يرجع إلى النصف الباقي ليخلص له الكل وانحصر هبتها في نصيبها
وهو المستيقن وهذا يعرف بقول الحصر
والثاني أنه يرجع إلى نصف الباقي وربع قيمة الجملة إذ لا بد من الإشاعة
فإن الحصر تحكم
والثالث أن الإشاعة حق ولكن تؤدي إلى تبعيض حق الزوج فله الخيار إن شاء
طلب قيمة النصف وإن شاء رجع إلى نصف الباقي وربع قيمة الجملة
وتجري الأقوال فيما لو أصدقها أربعين من الغنم فأخرجت واحدة للزكاة ثم
طلقها ففي قول يرجع إلى عشرين من الباقي وتنحصر زكاتها في نصيبها وفي قول
يرجع إلى نصف الباقي وبقية القيمة
وفي قول يتخير بين ذلك وبين قيمة العشرين وكذلك تجري فيما لو وهبت النصف
من الأجنبي
أما إذا فرعنا على أن الهبة تمنع الرجوع فإن قلنا بالحصر
فمنهم من حصر الهبة في جانبها وأثبت للزوج الرجوع بالنصف الباقي ليخلص له
الكل
ومنهم من حصر الهبة في جانبه وجعل الموهوب كأنه المعجل فلا يبقى  له حق في
التشطير فكأنه عجل ما يستحق من النصف بالطلاق قبل المسيس
وإذ قلنا بالإشاعة رجع إلى النصف الباقي وهو ربع الجملة ولا يجري قول
الخيار لأنا
على هذا القول نعني على قول منع الرجوع جعلناها معجلة للربع فيضاف الربع
الباقي إليه
الفرع الثاني إذا اختلعت المرأة قبل المسيس بعين الصداق فينبغي أن تقول
اختلعت بالنصف الذي يبقى لي فإن قالت اختلعت بالنصف مطلقا فعلى قول الحصر
ينحصر في نصفها ويصير كما لو صرحت بما يبقى لها وعلى قول الشيوع يفسد نصف
العوض وفي الباقي قولا تفريق الصفقة فإن جوزنا تفريق الصفقة سلم للزوج من
الصداق ثلاثة أرباعه نصف بحكم التشطير وربع بحكم الخلع ويرجع إلى قيمة
الربع الباقي أو إلى نصف مهر المثل لأن ربع الصداق هو نصف عوض الخلع وفيه
القولان المذكوران في فساد الصداق

### | الفصل الخامس في المتعة

وقد قال الله تعالى {ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره} فهي
واجبة عندنا وعند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقال مالك إنها مستحبة
والنظر في محل وجوبها وقدرها أما المحل فالنظر في المطلقات وأنواع الفراق
أما المطلقات فثلاثه ثلاثة أقسام
إحداها المطلقة المفوضة وهي تستحق المتعة مهما طلقت قبل الفرض والمسيس إذ
ليس لها نصف مهر وفيها ورد القرآن
الثانية مطلقة استحقت شطر المهر قبل المسيس فلا تستحق المتعة لأنهما
كالمتعاقبين في نص القرآن
الثالثة وهي التي استقر مهرها بالمسيس ففيها قولان
أحدهما لا تستحق إذ سلم لها جميع المهر
والثاني تستحق لأن جميع المهر في مقابلة البضع فكأنها لم تستحق للإبتذال
شيئا
وأما أنواع الفراق ففي معنى الطلاق فراق العان لأنه يتعلق بمجرد لعانه
وكذا ردته وكل فراق مشطر للمهر فيوجب المتعة إذا لم يشطر
وأما ما يستند إليها كفسخها بعيبه أو فسخه بعيبها فلا يوجب المتعة
ونقل المزني في فسخها بجبه أنه يثبت المتعة واتفقوا على تغليطه
وأما الخلع فقد ترددوا فيه من حيث إنه مشطر ولكنه يتعلق برضاها وجانبها
وأما ما لا يتعلق بالجانبين كالانفساخ  برضاع محرم فيوجب المتعة لأنها
تأذت بالفراق وإن لم يؤذها الزوج وكأن المتعة جبر لأذى الفراق إذا لم يجبر
بالمهر
وأما المتوفى عنها زوجها فلا خلاف في أنها لا متعة لها لأنها متفجعة لا
مستوحشة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ه-ب (wahaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bestow gratuitously; a gift (hibah) entails transfer of ownership without exchange.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, hibah contrasts with ʿiwad (compensation); its effect on prior rights (rujūʿ) is a matter of legal construction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for outright transfer; metaphorical (majāz) when used for relinquishing a claim, as in the wife's waiver of dower.
- Root: ش-ي-ع (shāʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To spread, be common; ishāʿah means undivided co-ownership in every particle.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, ishāʿah denotes a share permeating the whole corpus, unlike ḥaṣr (segregation).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical diffusion; technical in jurisprudence for fractional entitlement without specification.
- Root: م-ت-ع (mataʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enjoyment, provision; mutʿah is a consolatory gift to a divorced woman.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quranic term {«ومتعوهن»} (al-Baqarah 2:236) — a mandated compensation for emotional harm of separation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tangible benefit; metaphorical for the juristic obligation of solace.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with faʾ (الفاء في جواب الشرط) — the protasis (law wahabat) governs the apodosis (fa-lahu al-rujūʿ), requiring the latter to be a new sentence, not a mere continuation.
chapters.translation:
### | Two Subsidiary Issues

**First Subsidiary Issue:** If a wife gifts to her husband half of the dower (ṣadāq), then he divorces her — if we hold that the gift does not prevent revocation (rujūʿ), then he has the right to reclaim the half. Regarding the modality of this reclamation, there are three opinions:

**One:** He returns to the remaining half so that the whole becomes exclusively his, and her gift is confined (inḥaṣarat) to her own share — this being the certain outcome. This is known as the doctrine of segregation (ḥaṣr).

**Second:** He returns to half of the remaining [dower] plus a quarter of the total value, because undivided co-ownership (ishāʿah) is unavoidable — for segregation is an arbitrary ruling (taḥakkum).

**Third:** Undivided co-ownership is the correct principle, but it leads to fragmentation of the husband's right. Thus he has the option: if he wishes, he demands the value of the half; if he wishes, he returns to half of the remaining plus a quarter of the total value.

These opinions also apply in the case where he dowered her with forty sheep, and she set aside one for zakāh, then he divorced her. On one opinion, he returns to twenty of the remaining, and her zakāh is confined to her share. On another opinion, he returns to half of the remaining plus the rest of the value. On a third opinion, he chooses between that and the value of the twenty. The same applies if she gifted the half to a stranger (ajnabī).

However, if we proceed on the basis that the gift prevents revocation — then if we adopt segregation, some scholars confine the gift to her side and affirm for the husband the right to reclaim the remaining half so that the whole becomes his. Others confine the gift to his side, treating the gifted portion as if it were an advance payment (muʿajjal) — thus he retains no right to halving (tashṭīr), as if he had advanced what he deserves of the half by divorce before consummation (qabla al-masīs).

And if we adopt undivided co-ownership, he returns to the remaining half, which is a quarter of the total. The opinion of option (khiyār) does not apply here, because on this view — namely, the view that the gift prevents revocation — we treat her as having advanced the quarter, so the remaining quarter is added to it.

**Second Subsidiary Issue:** If a woman obtains a khulʿ (divorce by redemption) before consummation using the very dower (ʿayn al-ṣadāq), she ought to say: "I have obtained khulʿ for the half that remains for me." If she says "I have obtained khulʿ for the half" absolutely, then on the doctrine of segregation, it is confined to her half, and it becomes as if she had explicitly stated what remains for her. On the doctrine of co-ownership (shuyūʿ), half of the consideration is corrupted (fasada), and regarding the remainder, the two opinions on division of the contract (tafrīq al-ṣafqah) apply. If we permit division of the contract, then the husband secures from the dower three-quarters: half by virtue of halving (tashṭīr) and a quarter by virtue of the khulʿ. He then returns to the value of the remaining quarter, or to half of the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl) — because the quarter of the dower is half of the khulʿ consideration, and regarding it, the two aforementioned opinions on corruption of the dower apply.

### | Fifth Chapter: On the Consolatory Gift (Mutʿah)

God Almighty has said: {«ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره»} (al-Baqarah 2:236) — "And provide for them — the wealthy according to his means and the constrained according to his means." It is obligatory (wājibah) in our view and in the view of Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him). Mālik said it is recommended (mustaḥabbah).

The inquiry concerns the locus of its obligation and its measure. As for the locus, the inquiry concerns divorced women and the types of separation.

As for divorced women, they are of three categories:

**First:** The woman divorced before dower fixation (tafwīḍ) — she deserves the consolatory gift whenever she is divorced before fixation and consummation, for she has no half-dower. Concerning her, the Quranic verse was revealed.

**Second:** A woman who deserved half the dower before consummation — she does not deserve the consolatory gift, for the two [dower and mutʿah] are like two successive alternatives in the text of the Quran.

**Third:** She whose dower was confirmed by consummation — regarding her, there are two opinions:

**One:** She does not deserve it, for the entire dower was delivered to her.

**Second:** She does deserve it, because the entire dower is in exchange for sexual intimacy (buḍʿ) — as if she deserved nothing for the mere act of exposure (ibtidhāl).

As for the types of separation: In the meaning of divorce is the separation of the imprecating husband (mulaʿʿin), because it attaches to his mere imprecation (liʿān). Likewise his apostasy (riddah). Every separation that halves the dower (mushaṭṭir) necessitates the consolatory gift when it does not halve [the dower].

As for what is attributable to her — like her annulment due to his defect, or his annulment due to her defect — it does not necessitate the consolatory gift. Al-Muzanī transmitted regarding her annulment due to leprosy (juthām) that the consolatory gift is established, but they agreed on his error (taghlīṭ).

As for khulʿ, they hesitated over it — because it halves [the dower], yet it attaches to her consent and her side.

As for what does not attach to either side — like dissolution due to foster-relationship (riḍāʿ muḥarrim) — it necessitates the consolatory gift, because she is harmed by the separation even if the husband did not harm her. It is as if the consolatory gift is compensation for the harm of separation when that harm is not compensated by the dower.

As for the woman whose husband has died — there is no disagreement that she has no consolatory gift, because she is bereaved (mutafajjiʿah), not estranged (mustawḥishah).

chapters.title_en: Second Consideration: The Quantum of the Consolatory Gift (Mutʿah) and Its Determination
chapters.arabic_text:
### | النظر الثاني في قدرها وفيه وجهان

أحدهما أن أقل ما يتمول به يعني فلا تقدير فيه
والثاني أنه يجتهد فيه القاضي فما يراه لائقا بالحال يقدره وقيل ينظر
القاضي الى حاله في اليسار والإعسار وقيل بل إلى حالها ومنصبها
والصحيح أنه ينظر إليهما جميعا وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه يفرض القاضي
لها مقنعتا أو خاتما أو ثوبا والأصل أنه لا ضابط فيه إلا الاجتهاد كما في
التعزيزان فإنها على قدر الجنايات وعلى
قدر أخلاق الجناة في الغرامة والسلامة
ثم لا يزاد في المتعة على نصف المهر كما لا يزاد التعزير على الحد ثم إن
لم يكن في النكاح مهر فمرد المتعة إلى نصف مهر المثل فلتنقص عنه
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الخامس في النزاع في الصداق - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -
وفيه مسائل خمس
الأولى إذا تنازعا في مقدار الصداق أو جنسه أوصفته كما وصفانه في البيع
تحالفا وإن كان بعد الموت جرى التحالف مع الوارث لكن الوارث النافي يحلف
على نفي العلم والمثبت يحلف على البت وكذلك يجري التحالف بعد ارتفاع النكاح
لأن الصداق مستقل بنفسه وفائدة التحالف فيه انفساخ الصداق والرجوع على مهر
المثل إلى الأقوال كلها لأن منشأ التحالف الجهل بمقدار الصداق فلا يمكن
الرجوع إلى القيمة
وقال ابن خيران إذا كان ما تدعيه المرأة أقل من مهر المثل فلا ترجع إلى
مهر المثل بل يكفيها ما تدعيه وهو بعيد لأن رجوعها إلى المهر بجهة الفسخ
يخالف جهة الدعوة
ولو ادعت المرأة التسمية وأنكر الزوج أصل التسمية تحالفا وإنما يفيد ذلك
إذا ادعت زيادة على مهر المثل وفيه وجه أن القول قوله لأن الأصل عدم
التسمية وهو ضعيف لأن حاصل النزاع يرجع إلى أن الثابت مهر المثل أو أكثر
الثانية لو اعترف  الزوج بالنكاح وأنكر أصل المهر أو سكت عنه قال القاضي
لها مهر المثل ولكن نحلفها لأن الظاهر معها وزاد فقال لو قال هذا الصبي
ابني من فلانة فلها مهر المثل إن حلفت لأن الظاهر أن الولد يكون من وطء
محترم فإن استدخال الماء بعيد وما ذكره فيه نظر لأن هذا يدل على أصل المهر
فأما مقداره فلا يدل عليه فإن إنكاره أصل المهر أبلغ من إنكاره بعض المهر
وذلك يوجب التحالف نعم ما ذكره يستمد من مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله حيث قال
لو تنازعا وكان ما تدعيه المرأة مقدار مهر المثل فالقول قولها ولا تحالف
ونحن لا ننظر إلى ذلك
الثالثة لو تنازع الزوج وولي الصبية في مقدار المهر هل يتحالفان فيه
وجهان ووجه تحليف الولي أنه مقبول الإقرار فيه فلا يبعد أن يحلف وحيث لا
يقبل إقراره فلا يحلف
ويجري هذا الخلاف في الوصي والقيم والوكيل فيما يتعلق بإنشائهم أما إذا
ادعى الولي على إنسان أنه أتلف مال طفل فنكل المدعي عليه فالظاهر أنه لا
ترد اليمين على الولي لأنه لا يتعلق بإنشائه ولكن لا يقضى بنكوله عليه
ويتوقف إلى بلوغ الصبي حتى يحلف وعن هذا قال بعضهم لا تعرض اليمين عليه بل
يتوقف في أصل الخصومة لأنه لا يعجز عن النكول ومن أصحابنا من قال ترد
اليمين على الولي هاهنا أيضا فلو نكل هل يقضى على الطفل بنكوله أم له أن
يحلف بعد البلوغ فيه وجهان
الرابعة لو ادعت ألفين في عقدين أحدهما يوم الخميس والآخر يوم الجمعة
وأقامت البينة استقحت وحمل على تخلل الطلاق فإن ادعى الرجل أن الطلاق قبل
المسيس ليسقط النصف وما أقامت بينة على المسيس قلنا له النكاح مثبت للكل
وعليك بيان المسقط
الخامسة لو كان في ملك الرجل أبوها وأمها فأصدقها أحدهما على التعيين لكن
تنازعا فقالت المرأة أصدقتني الأم وقال الزوج أصدقتك الأب تحالفا وفيه وجه
أنهما لا يتحالفان لأن الصداق عقد مستقل بنفسه ولم يتفقا على صداق واحد فهو
كما  لو قال بعتني الجارية بدينار فقال بل بعتك العبد بدرهم فإنهما لا
يتحالفان وهذا ضعيف لأن الصداق له حكم الأعواض
ثم لو تحالفا رجعت إلى مهر المثل ورقت الأم وعتق الأب على الزوج بإقراره
ولا يرجع إليها بقيمته لأنها منكرة وولاؤه موقوف إذ لا مدعي له
ولو حلف الزوج ونكلت المرأة رقت الأم وحكم بأن الصداق هو الأب وعتق ولا
ولاء لها لإنكارها
أما إذا قال الزوج أصدقتك الأب ونصف الأم وقالت بل أصدقتهما جميعا فإذا
تحالفا رجعت إلى مهر المثل وعتق الأب لأنه متفق عليه وعليها قيمته وعتق نصف
الأم والباقي يعتق بالسراية إن كانت موسرة
وقد تم كتاب الصداق ونردفه بباب في الوليمة والنثر على ترتيب الشافعي رضي
الله عنه وفيه فصول ثلاثة

### | الوليمة والنثر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "measure," "extent," or "capacity" — the inherent limit or quantity of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, taqdīr denotes the judicial determination of a specific amount where no textual (naṣṣ) limit exists, aligning with juristic discretion (ijtihād).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) here for quantifying a financial obligation; metaphorically (majāz) it would imply divine decree, which is not intended in this juristic discourse.
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of effort to the utmost; striving.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ijtihād as the qualified jurist's maximal effort to derive a ruling or, as here, to assess a discretionary amount.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "effort" applied technically to judicial reasoning; no metaphorical extension in this passage.
- Root: ع-ض-و (ʿ-ḍ-w) — for taʿzīr (discretionary punishment)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes "member/limb" but in legal usage taʿzīr derives from ʿazr (prevention/reproof).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taʿzīr is a chastisement less than the prescribed ḥadd, left to the judge's discretion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "deterrence/reproof" — here used technically for discretionary corporal punishment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with "In" (الشّرط بـ "إن") — The phrase "فإن لم يكن في النكاح مهر" employs a conditional construction where the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), requiring careful parsing of the legal consequence (reduction of mutʿah below half the dower-equivalent).
chapters.translation:
I say: The second consideration concerns its quantum, and therein are two aspects.

The first is that the minimum that can be considered property (mutamawwal) suffices — meaning there is no fixed estimation for it. The second is that the judge exercises ijtihād therein, and whatever he deems fitting to the circumstance, he determines. And it was said: the judge looks to the husband's state of affluence or straitened means. And it was said: rather, he looks to her state and her social standing. The correct position is that he looks to both of them together. Al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — said: the judge assesses for her a face-veil (miqnaʿah), a ring, or a garment. The foundational principle is that there is no fixed criterion therein except ijtihād, just as in discretionary punishments (taʿzīrāt), for they are proportionate to the gravity of the offenses and to the moral characters of the offenders — in respect of the fine and the exemption.

Then, the consolatory gift (mutʿah) is not increased beyond half the dower (mahr), just as taʿzīr is not increased beyond the ḥadd. Then, if there was no dower in the marriage, the mutʿah is referred back to half the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl), so it must be less than that.

— Peace be upon him — The Fifth Chapter: On Disputes Concerning the Dower (Ṣidāq) — Peace be upon him —

And therein are five questions.

The first: If the spouses dispute over the amount of the dower, or its type, or its attribute — just as they would describe it in a sale — they both take oaths (taḥāluf). And if this occurs after death, the mutual oath-taking proceeds with the heir; however, the denying heir swears upon negation of knowledge, while the affirming one swears with certainty (al-batt). Likewise, mutual oath-taking proceeds after the dissolution of the marriage, because the dower is an independent obligation in itself. The benefit of mutual oath-taking therein is the rescission of the dower and the recourse to the equivalent dower — according to all the opinions — because the origin of mutual oath-taking is ignorance of the dower's amount, so recourse to the market value is not possible.

Ibn Khayrān said: If what the woman claims is less than the equivalent dower, she does not revert to the equivalent dower; rather, what she claims suffices her. But this is far-fetched, because her recourse to the dower is by way of rescission, which differs from the way of her claim.

And if the woman claims the specification (tasmiyah) and the husband denies the specification entirely, they take mutual oaths. This is only beneficial if she claims an increase over the equivalent dower. And therein is an aspect that the husband's word is accepted, because the default is the absence of specification — but this is weak, because the crux of the dispute reverts to whether what is established is the equivalent dower or more.

The second: If the husband acknowledges the marriage but denies the dower entirely, or remains silent about it, al-Qāḍī said: she is entitled to the equivalent dower, but we administer the oath to her, because the apparent evidence (al-ẓāhir) supports her. He added: And he said: If he said, "This boy is my son from so-and-so," then she is entitled to the equivalent dower if she swears, because the apparent evidence is that the child results from lawful intercourse, for the introduction of water [without intercourse] is far-fetched. But what he mentioned is subject to scrutiny, because this indicates the existence of the dower in principle; as for its amount, it does not indicate it. For his denial of the dower entirely is more emphatic than his denial of part of it, and that necessitates mutual oath-taking. Indeed, what he mentioned derives from the school of Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah have mercy on him — who said: If they dispute and what the woman claims equals the amount of the equivalent dower, then her word is accepted and there is no mutual oath-taking. But we do not regard that.

The third: If the husband and the guardian of the minor girl dispute over the amount of the dower — do they take mutual oaths therein? There are two aspects. The aspect of administering the oath to the guardian is that his acknowledgment is accepted therein, so it is not improbable that he be sworn. And where his acknowledgment is not accepted, he is not sworn.

This disagreement applies to the executor (waṣī), the trustee (qayyim), and the agent (wakīl) regarding matters pertaining to their own contractual acts. As for when the guardian claims against a person that he destroyed a child's property, and the defendant declines to take the oath (nukūl), the apparent position is that the oath is not returned to the guardian, because it does not pertain to his contractual act; but judgment is not rendered against the defendant based on his nukūl. Rather, the matter is suspended until the child reaches majority so that he may swear. And regarding this, some said: the oath is not presented to him at all; rather, the entire litigation is suspended, because he is not incapable of nukūl. And among our companions is one who said: the oath is returned to the guardian here as well. Then, if he declines, is judgment rendered against the child based on his nukūl, or may the child swear after reaching majority? Therein are two aspects.

The fourth: If she claims two thousand [dirhams] in two contracts — one on Thursday and the other on Friday — and she produces evidence, she is entitled to the full amount, and it is construed that a divorce intervened between them. If the man claims that the divorce occurred before consummation so as to drop half, and she produces no evidence of consummation, we say to him: marriage establishes the entirety, and upon you is the burden of demonstrating what drops it.

The fifth: If the woman's father and mother were both in the man's possession (milk), and he gave one of them to her as dower by specification, but they disputed — the woman saying, "You gave me the mother as dower," and the husband saying, "I gave you the father as dower" — they take mutual oaths. And therein is an aspect that they do not take mutual oaths, because the dower is an independent contract in itself, and they have not agreed upon a single dower — just as if he said, "You sold me the slave-girl for a dinar," and he replied, "Rather, I sold you the slave for a dirham," for they do not take mutual oaths. But this is weak, because the dower has the ruling of counter-values (aʿwāḍ).

Then, if they take mutual oaths, she reverts to the equivalent dower, the mother becomes a slave, and the father is freed by virtue of the husband's acknowledgment — and he does not revert upon her for his value, because she denies it. And his clientage (walāʾ) is suspended, for he has no claimant.

And if the husband swears and the woman declines (nukūl), the mother becomes a slave, and it is adjudged that the dower was the father, and he is freed — and she has no clientage over him due to her denial.

As for when the husband says, "I gave you the father and half the mother as dower," and she says, "Rather, you gave me both of them entirely" — then, if they take mutual oaths, she reverts to the equivalent dower, the father is freed because he is agreed upon, and she owes his value; and half the mother is freed, and the remainder is freed by way of the right of emancipation by proximity (sirāyah) if she is solvent.

And the Book of the Dower is completed. We follow it with a chapter on the wedding feast (walīmah) and the scattering of gifts (nathr), according to the arrangement of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him. And therein are three sections.

### | The Wedding Feast and the Scattering of Gifts

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الأول في وجوبها ووجوب الإجابة

فنقول الوليمة عبارة في اللغة عن مأدبة سببها سرور من ختان أو قدوم أو
إملاك لكنا نريد به مأدبة العرس فإن الأمر فيه مؤكد كان رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم لا يترك الوليمة في حضر ولا سفر وأولم على صفية بسويق وتمر في
السفر وقال لعبد الرحمن
ابن عوف أولم ولو بشاة
وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه في سائر الدعوات من تركها لم يبن لي أنه عاص
كما تبين لي في وليمة العرس فاختلف الأصحاب فمنهم من قال فيه قولان ومنهم
من قطع بأنه لا تجب وحمل الأمر على الاستحباب وحمل كلام الشافعي رضي الله
عنه على ترك الإجابة إلى الوليمة ومنهم من قطع بأن الإجابة أيضا لا تجب
وحمل قوله عليه
الصلاة والسلام من لم يجب الداعي فقد عصى أبا القاسم على أنه عصى في
سيرته والاقتداء بمحاسن أخلاقه إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أهدي إلي ذراع
لقبلت ولو دعيت إلى قراع لأجبت ثم إن قلنا تجب الإجابة فيسقط الوجوب بأعذار
الأول أن يكون في الدعوة شيئ من المنكرات فإن كان يهاب ويرتفع ذلك بحضوره
فليحضر وإلا فليمتنع فإن حضر ورأى ذلك ولم  يقدر على التغيير فليخرج إذ
الإقامة في مشاهدة المنكرات حرام
الثاني أن يكون في البيت المدعو إليه صورة مصورة للحيوانان أو على الستور
والسقوف فإن ذلك حرام ولا بأس بصور الأشجار وأما صورة الحيوانات فلا يعفى
عنها إلا على الفرش وما تحت الأقدام لا المنصوبة على صور الأصنام والوسادة
الكبيرة في الصدر في حكم المنصوب وقد روت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنه صلى الله
عليه وسلم رأى في داره سترة عليها صور فكان يدنو منها وينصرف فعل ذلك مرارا
ثم قال حطيها واتخذي منها نمارق ولا يجوز لبس الثياب وعليها صور الحيوان لا
للرجال ولا للنساء وأما نسج تلك الثياب فجوزه الشيخ أبو محمد لأنه ينتفع به
في الفرش إلا أن الظاهر تحريم ذلك لعموم الحديث حيث قال يحشر المصورون يوم
القيامة ويقال لهم انفخوا الروح فيما خلقتم وما هم بنافخين ولا يخفف عنهم
العذاب نعم لا يبعد أن يقال ما اتخذوه يجوز أن
يوطء بالأقدام وقد قال عليه الصلاة والسلام لا تدخل الملائكة بيتا فيه
صورة والظاهر أن الدخول مكروه ومنهم من حرم ذلك
الثالث لو أحضر أكواما من الأراذل والسفلة وكانت مجالستهم تزري بمنصبه
ومروءته فالظاهر أنه لا تجب الإجابة
الرابع أن الصوم ليس بعذر بل يحضر فإن صام عن فرض أمسك وإن كان عن نفل
أفطر إلا إذا علم أنه لا يعز على الداعي إمساكه فعند ذلك يمسك أيضا
وحيث تجب الإجابة فإنما تجب إذا قصده الداعي فإن قال لغلامه ادع من شئت
فلا تجب على من دعاه الغلام الإجابة
ولو دعا جماعة ولم يقصد الآحاد سقط الوجوب بحضور جماعة كرد السلام

### | الفصل الثاني في الضيافة

وفيه مسائل
الأولى أنه لا يعين طعاما في الضيافة بل الخيرة إلى المضيف لكن في
الوليمة ينبغي أن ب 180 يتخذ يتأخذ ما يليق بمنصبه وحاله
الثانية أنه لا يفتقر إلى تصريح بالإباحة بعد إحضار الطعام وقيل لا بد من
لفظ كقوله كلوا أو الصلاة
الثالثة الضيف يأكل ملك الغير بطريق  الإباحة وله الرجوع وقيل إنه يملك
لكن اختلفوا في وقته منهم من قال عند رفع اللقمة وقيل عند الوضع في الفم
وقيل عند المضغ وقيل عند الازدراد نتبين أنه يملك مع الازدراد وقيل لا يملك
أصلا وإنما هذه الترددات في وقت امتناع الرجوع عن الإباحة والقياس أنه لا
يملك ولا يمتنع الرجوع إلا بالفوات
الرابعة زلت الصوفية حرام إلا إذا علم يقينا بقرينة الحال رضا المالك فإن
تردد فيه فالظاهر التحريم

### | الفصل الثالث في نثر السكر والجوز

وفيه مسائل
إحداها أن النثر والالتقاط كلاهما مباحان لما روى جابر بن عبد الله أن
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم حضر إملاكا فقال أين أطباقكم فأتي
بأطباق عليها جوز ولوز وتمر فنثرت قال جابر فقبضنا أيدينا فقال عليه الصلاة
والسلام ما لكم لا تأخذون فقالوا لأنك نهيتنا عن النهبى فقال إنما نهيتكم
عن نهبي العساكر خذوا على اسم الله تعالى فجاذبنا وجاذبناه قال الشافعي رضي
الله عنه
ترك ذلك أحب إلي وإنما فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للرخصة وبيانها
فلا نقول إنه مكروه ولكن ربما يؤثر الناثر بعض الناس دون بعض فتركه أولى
الثانية ما وقع في الأرض فالحاضرون فيه سواء ويملكه من يبتدره ومن تثبت
يده على شيء منه فلا يسلب بل هو كالصيد
الثالثة لو وقع في حجر إنسان وقد بسطه لذلك ملكه فإن سقط منه فهل لغيره
أخذه فيحتمل أن يقال له ذلك وقرار أمره موقوف على استقراره في يده
أما إذا لم يبسطه لذلك فلغيره أخذه كما إذا عشش الطائر في داره ثم طار
أما إذا وقع الصيد في الشبكة ثم أفلت فالظاهر أن ملكه لا يزول وفي وجه أنه
في العرف لا يعد مستقرا
= كتاب القسم والنشوز = وفيه مقدمة وستة فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-م (walama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to prepare food for a gathering," specifically tied to a festive occasion; the walīmah is a feast (ma'dubah) whose cause is joy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic-theological usage, it denotes the wedding feast, whose command is emphatically stressed in the Sunnah, distinguishing it from mere hospitality (ḍiyāfah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the feast itself; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to any celebratory meal, but the technical legal sense is restricted to marriage.
- Root: أ-ج-ب (ajaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To respond, answer, comply" — carrying the sense of a required reply to a call.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, it denotes obligatory compliance (wujūb al-imtithāl) with a summons, particularly when the caller is the Prophet ﷺ or a host in a wedding context.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is verbal response; the metaphorical sense is the act of attending, which is the intended meaning in the hadith.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Ellipsis (al-sharṭ bi-ḥadhf al-jawāb) — In "If we say the response is obligatory, then it is waived by excuses," the protasis governs the apodosis, and the legal ruling is suspended on the condition, requiring precise parsing of the exception clauses that follow.
chapters.translation:
I say: The walīmah (wedding feast) is, in language, an expression for a meal (ma'dubah) whose cause is joy — whether from circumcision, arrival, or betrothal. But we intend by it specifically the wedding feast, for the command concerning it is emphatically stressed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never abandoned the walīmah whether present or traveling. He gave a walīmah for Ṣafiyyah with sawīq (barley porridge) and dates while traveling, and he said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: "Give a walīmah, even if with a single sheep."

Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning other invitations: "If one abandons them, it has not become clear to me that he is disobedient, as it has become clear to me regarding the wedding feast." The companions (of al-Shāfiʿī) then differed: some said there are two opinions (on this matter); others definitively held that it is not obligatory, interpreting the command as indicating recommendation (istiḥbāb) and interpreting al-Shāfiʿī's words as referring to abandoning the response to the wedding feast; and others definitively held that the response itself is also not obligatory, interpreting his saying ﷺ — "Whoever does not respond to the caller has disobeyed Abā al-Qāsim" — as disobedience in his sunnah (way) and in emulating the excellences of his character, since he ﷺ said: "If a foreleg were gifted to me, I would accept it; and if I were invited to a foreleg, I would respond."

Then, if we say the response is obligatory, it is waived by excuses:
First: That there be in the invitation something objectionable (munkar). If the host is feared and the objectionable thing would be removed by one's presence, then let him attend; otherwise, let him abstain. If he attends and sees it and cannot change it, let him leave, for remaining in the presence of objectionable things is unlawful (ḥarām).
Second: That in the house to which one is invited there be a picture of an animal — whether on curtains or ceilings. For that is unlawful. There is no harm in pictures of trees. As for pictures of animals, they are not excused except on carpets and what is underfoot — not those erected like idols. A large cushion at the chest is in the ruling of the erected. ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated that he ﷺ saw in his house a curtain with pictures on it, and he would approach it and then turn away — doing so repeatedly — then said: "Cut it up and make of it cushions." It is not permissible to wear garments with animal pictures on them, neither for men nor for women. As for weaving such garments, Shaykh Abū Muḥammad permitted it because one benefits from them as carpets; however, the apparent position is that this is unlawful due to the generality of the hadith where he ﷺ said: "The image-makers will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them: 'Blow the spirit into what you have created' — and they will not be able to blow." And their punishment will not be lightened. Indeed, it is not far-fetched to say that what they have made may be trodden underfoot, for he ﷺ said: "Angels do not enter a house in which there is a picture." The apparent position is that entering (such a house) is disliked (makrūh), though some have declared it unlawful.
Third: If the host gathers crowds of rabble and lowlifes, and sitting with them demeans one's standing and manliness (murūʾah), then the apparent position is that the response is not obligatory.
Fourth: Fasting is not an excuse; rather, one attends. If one is fasting an obligatory fast, he refrains (from eating); if it is a supererogatory fast, he breaks it — except when he knows that the host would not be offended by his refraining, in which case he refrains as well.

Wherever the response is obligatory, it is only obligatory if the host intends the specific person. If he says to his servant: "Invite whomever you wish," then the response is not obligatory upon the one the servant invites. And if he invites a group without intending specific individuals, the obligation is waived by the presence of the group — like the reply to the greeting (radd al-salām).

ENGLISH_TITLE: The Second Chapter on Hospitality (al-Ḍiyāfah)

QUAD_ANCHORS:
- Root: ض-ي-ف (ḍāfa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to incline, lean toward, or lodge with someone"; the guest (ḍayf) is one who inclines to a host for provision.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal usage, it denotes the host's voluntary provision of food to a guest, distinct from the obligatory walīmah; its ruling is recommendation, not obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical lodging; metaphorical sense is the entitlement to eat from the host's property by way of permissibility (ibāḥah), not ownership.
- Root: أ-ك-ل (akala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To eat, consume" — the act of ingesting food.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic discourse, it concerns the legal status of consuming another's property — whether it transfers ownership or merely grants permissive use.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal act of eating is contrasted with the metaphorical "eating" of unlawful gain; here, the focus is on the precise moment of acquisition.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Genitive of Specification (al-iḍāfah) — In "the guest eats the property of another," the construct phrase (milk al-ghayr) requires parsing the possessor as the legal owner, while the permissibility (ibāḥah) is a separate predicate, clarifying that no ownership transfer occurs by mere permission.

### | أما المقدمة

فهي أن الحق في النكاح مشترك بين الزوجين وإن كان بينهما تفاوت قال الله
تعالى {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف} إذ لهن النفقة والكسوه والمهر والقسم
كما لهم عليهن الاستعداد  للاستمتاع والتمكين والطاعة ولزوم قعر البيت حتى
يمنعها عن زيارة الوالدين وتشييع جنائزهما وعيادتهما وإن كان الأولى أن
يرخص في ذلك كيلا يؤدي إلى الوحشة وقطيعة الرحم
ولكن ليس للمنفردة في النكاح مطالبة الزوج بالمبيت عندها ولا بالوقاع
اكتفاء بدواعي الطبع والأولى بالزوج أن لا يخليهن عن الإيناس والوقاع
تحصينا لهن عن الفجور وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا بد وأن يبيت عندها في كل
أربع ليال ليلة
واحدة لأنه أقصى ما يمكن في حقه أربع نساء وذلك غير سديد بل لو كان له
أربع نسوة فأعرض عن جميعهن لم يكن لهن مطالبته نعم إذا بات عند واحدة لزمه
مثله في حق الباقيات
ولا قسم بين المستولدات والإماء ولا بينهن وبين المنكوحات بل له أن يفعل
فيهن ما شاء وإن كان الأولى الإنصاف بينهن وترك الإيذاء لكن وجوب القسم من
خاصية النكاح هذه هي المقدمة

### | أما الفصل الأول فيمن يستحق القسم ويستحق عليه

فنقول المريضة والرتقاء والحائض والنفساء والمحرمة والتي آلى عنها زوجها
أو ظاهرا وجميع أصناف النساء ممن بهن عذر شرعي أو طبعي يثبت لهن استحقاق
القسم لأن هذه الأشياء تمنع الوطء ومقصود القسم السكن والأنس والحذر من
التخصيص المؤذي
أما الناشزة فلا تستحق حتى لو كان يدعوهن إلى منزله فامتنعت واحدة في
نوبتها سقط حقها إذ يجب عليهن الإجابة إلا إذا كان يساكن واحدة ويدعوا
الأخرى فامتنعت فيحتمل ألا تجعل ناشزة حتى يجب عليه أن يأتيهن أو يدعوا
جميعهن إذ مساكنة واحدة تخصيص موحش ويحتمل أن يترخص في هذا القدر من
التخصيص
أما المسافرة بغير إذنه فناشزة وإن سافرت في غرضه بإذنه فحقها قائم
وتستحق القضاء وإن كان في غرضها فقولان والجديد الصحيح
أنها لا تستحق القضاء لأنها مشغولة بغرض نفسها
أما من يستحق عليه فهو كل زوج حتى المجنون قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه على
الولي أن يطوف به على ويحتمل أن يقال لا يجب على الولي ذلك إذ العاقل لو
امتنع عن الكل جاز ذلك وكذا  المجنون ولكن العاقل يكتفي بدعايته الباعثة
والمجنون
بخلافه فلا يبعد أن يجب على الولي ذلك
فإن قلنا يجب فعليه مراعاة البيتوتة وإن قلنا لا يجب على الولي ذلك فلو
حمله إلى واحدة ليلة يلزمه مثل ذلك لغيره ويحتمل أن يقال التخصيص إنما يثقل
من الزوج وهذا من الولي فلا يعظم ضرره
وأما السفيه فلا شك في وجوب القسم عليه لأنه مكلف
فرع لو كان يجن ويفيق وأمكن الضبط فلا يجوز تخصيص واحدة بالإفاقة وإن لم
يمكن فأفاق في نوبة واحدة ففي كلام الشافعي رضي الله عنه ما يدل على أنه
يقضي للأخرى يوم الجنون لنقصان حقها

- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, distribution into shares; the act of partitioning something among rightful claimants.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In marital jurisprudence, the equitable apportionment of the husband's nights among co-wives, rooted in the divine command of fairness (ʿadl) and the Prophetic practice of equal treatment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical division of property; here it is a metaphorical (majāz) extension to temporal allocation of the husband's presence, indicating a legally constructed right rather than a natural one.
- Root: ن-ش-ز (n-sh-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Rising, elevation; a woman's rising against her husband in defiance, i.e., disobedience (nushūz).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal disobedience by a wife against her husband's legitimate authority, suspending her claim to maintenance and division of nights.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The root's physical sense of "rising up" is transferred metaphorically to moral insubordination — a woman "rising" against her husband's station.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs repeated conditional clauses (law, idhā) and exceptions (illā) to delineate legal rulings precisely, requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine when rights are established, suspended, or forfeited.
chapters.translation:
### | As for the Introduction

Know that the right in marriage is shared between the two spouses, even though there is disparity between them. Allah the Exalted said: {«And they (women) have rights similar to those (of men) over them in kindness»} (Quran 2:228). For they have the right to maintenance, clothing, dower, and division of nights, just as they owe him readiness for enjoyment, submission, obedience, and remaining within the confines of the home — to the extent that he may prevent her from visiting her parents, attending their funeral processions, and visiting them in illness, although the preferable course is to grant permission in such matters, lest it lead to estrangement and severance of kinship ties.

However, a woman who is alone in marriage (i.e., without co-wives) has no right to demand that her husband spend the night with her, nor to demand intercourse, relying upon the natural inclinations (of desire). Yet it is preferable for the husband not to deprive them of companionship and intercourse, as a safeguard for them against unchastity. Abu Hanifah — may Allah have mercy on him — said: He must spend the night with her at least one night out of every four nights, because that is the maximum possible in his case with four wives. But this is not sound. Rather, if a man had four wives and he turned away from all of them, they would have no right to demand (his presence). However, if he spent the night with one, then he is obligated to do the like for the remaining ones.

And there is no division (qasm) among slave-concubines (mustawladdāt) nor among female slaves, nor between them and free married wives. Rather, he may do with them as he wishes, although the preferable course is to be equitable among them and to refrain from causing harm. But the obligation of division is a specific characteristic of marriage (nikāḥ). This is the introduction.

### | As for the First Chapter: On Who Is Entitled to Division and Upon Whom It Is Obligatory

We say: The sick woman, the woman with an imperforate vagina (ratqāʾ), the menstruating woman, the woman in post-natal bleeding (nufasāʾ), the woman in a state of iḥrām (pilgrimage consecration), the woman against whom her husband has sworn an oath of abstention (īlāʾ), or against whom he has pronounced ẓihār (injurious comparison to a female relative) — and all categories of women who have a legal or natural impediment — their entitlement to division is established. For these matters prevent intercourse, and the purpose of division is dwelling together, companionship, and protection against hurtful preferential treatment (takhṣīṣ).

As for the defiantly disobedient woman (nāshiz), she is not entitled (to division). Thus, if he were to summon them to his residence and one of them refused during her turn, her right is forfeited, for they are obligated to respond. Except if he were cohabiting with one (in her residence) and summoned the other, and she refused — then there are two possible views: it may be held that she is not deemed defiantly disobedient, since he is obligated to go to them or summon them all together, for cohabiting with one is a hurtful preferential treatment; and it may be held that he is granted latitude in this measure of preferential treatment.

As for the woman who travels without his permission, she is defiantly disobedient. But if she traveled for his purpose with his permission, her right remains established and she is entitled to make up (the missed night). If she traveled for her own purpose, there are two opinions (qawlān); the new and sound opinion (al-jadīd al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that she is not entitled to make it up, because she is occupied with her own affair.

As for the one upon whom division is obligatory — it is every husband, even the insane man. Al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — said: The guardian (walī) must circulate him (among his wives). And it may be said that this is not obligatory upon the guardian, for if a sane man refrained from all (of them), that would be permissible, and likewise the insane man. But the sane man is satisfied by his innate drives that impel him (toward his wives), whereas the insane man is not like that. Thus it is not far-fetched that this should be obligatory upon the guardian.

If we say it is obligatory (upon the guardian), then he must observe the overnight stay (baytūtah). But if we say it is not obligatory upon the guardian, then if he carried him to one (wife) for a night, he would be obligated to do the like for the others. And it may be said that preferential treatment is only burdensome when it comes from the husband himself, whereas this comes from the guardian, so its harm is not magnified.

As for the foolish spendthrift (safīh), there is no doubt that division is obligatory upon him, for he is legally accountable (mukallaf).

**Branch (farʿ):** If a man suffers from intermittent insanity and lucidity, and it is possible to regulate (his cycles), then it is not permissible to single out one wife with the periods of lucidity. But if it is not possible (to regulate), and he becomes lucid during one wife's turn, then in al-Shāfiʿī's words — may Allah be pleased with him — there is an indication that he must make up (the missed night) to the other wife for the day of insanity, due to the deficiency in her right.
