chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في التماسها طلاقا مقيدا بعدد

وفيه أربع مسائل
إحداها أن تقول طلقني ثلاثا بألف فطلقها طلقة واحدة استحق ثلث الألف كما
ذكرناه على قياس الجعالة بخلاف جانبه
فإن لم يبق له عليها إلا طلقة فقالت طلقني ثلاثا بألف فطلق طلقة واحدة
قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه استحق جميع الألف لأن مرادها البينونة الكبرى وقد
حصلت بكمالها
وقال المزني رحمه الله يستحق ثلث الألف اتباعا للحساب وقال أبو إسحاق
المروزي إن علمت أنه لم يبق إلا واحدة استحق الجميع وإن لم تعلم استحق
الثلث ولا تفريع بعد هذا  على مذهبه
أما إذا بقيت له طلقتان فطلق واحدة استحق الثلث عند الشافعي رضي
الله عنه والمزني جميعا لأن الشافعي رضي الله عنه أيضا يتبع الحساب إلا
إذا حصلت البينونة الكبرى وإن طلقها اثنتين استحق الجميع عند الشافعي رضي
الله عنه والثلثين عند المزني
فلو قالت طلقني عشرا بألف استحق بالواحدة العشر وبالثنتين الخمس بالاتفاق
وأما بالثلاث استحق الجميع عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه وقياس المزني إنه
يستحق ثلاثة أعشار المال وقيل تخريجا على قياسه إنه إنما يوزع على العدد
الشرعي ويوافق الشافعي رضي الله عنه في استحقاق الجيمع بالثلاث في هذه
الصورة
الثانية إذ قالت طلقني ثلاثا بألف فقال أنت طالق واحدة بألف وثنتين مجانا
قال جماعة من أئمة المذهب تقع الواحدة بثلث الأف والزيادة لا تلزمها
والثنتان بعدها لا تقعان لأنها صارت بائنة بالأولى وهذا لا وجه له بل ينبغي
أن لا تقع الأولى لأنه ما رضي بوقوعها إلا بألف وهي ما التزمت على واحدة
إلا لثلاث نعم تقع الطلقتان مجانا وهما رجعيتان
أما إذا عكس فقال أنت طالق واحدة مجانا واثنتين بثلثي الاف وقعت واحدة
رجعية وتخرج الثنتان على مخالعه الرجعية إن جوزنا نفذنا أيضا بثلثي الأف
وإن منعنا وقعت طلقتان أيضا إذا قبلت لأن الرجعية يلحقها الطلاق وبالجملة
إذا خالع الرجعية على قولنا لا تصح مخالعتها كان كمخالعة السفيهة حتى يقع
طلاق بلا عوض
الثالثة إذ قالت طلقني واحدة بألف فقال أنت طالق ثلاثا قال الشافعي رضي
الله عنه طلقت ثلاثا واستحق الألف لأنه أجابها وزاد وإليه سار أبو يوسف
ومحمد وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يستحق شيئا لأنها لم تلتمس البينونة
الكبرى وسلم أنها لو قالت طلقني ثلاثا بألف فطلق واحدة إنه استحق ثلث الأف
وإن خالف
أما إذا عاد الزوج ذكر المال فقال أنت طالق ثلاثا بألف فأكثر الأصحاب على
أنه لا فرق بين أن يعيد أو لا يعيد وحكى الفوراني وجها عن القفال إنه إذا
أعاد فقد قابل كل طلقة بثلث الألف  فلا يلزمها إلا ثلث الألف ووقع الثلاث
أما إذا لم يعد ذكر المال أمكن أن يقال التمست واحدة فأجابها إلى بينونة
أغلظ منه فيرجع إلى زيادة صفة أما هاهنا فيظهر التوزيع ولكن يلزم على قياس
القفال أن لا يقع إلا واحدة لأنه قابل طلقتين بثلثي الألف وهي ما قبلت وقد
قيل بهذا أيضا ويلزم ألا تقع الأولى أيضا لأنها التمست بألف فأجاب بثلث
الألف
فهو كقوله بعني بألف فقال بعت بخمسمائة فإنه لا يكون جوابا وقد قيل بهذا
أيضا وقد قيل في البيع أيضا إنه يصح ويقول أيضا إذا قالت طلقني واحدة بألف
فقال طلقت واحدة بخمسمائة إنه يستحق تمام الألف لأن تقدير العوض إليها لا
إليه
وعلى الجملة مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله في صورة إعادة المال أوجه
الرابعة إذ قالت طلقني نصف طلقة بألف أو طلق نصفي أو يدي بألف فأجابها
نفذ الطلاق وفسد العوض لفساد صيغة المقابلة فيرجع إلى مهر المثل وفيه وجه
منقاس أنه يثبت المسمى لأنه خصص العوض بما لا يختص به ولكن كمله الشرع فلا
يبعد أن ينزل منزلة المقابلة بالكامل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط ل ق (ṭ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To release, untie, or set free; in legal terms, the dissolution of the marriage bond (al-ṭalāq) as an act of releasing the wife from the marital tie.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological-legal nuance of ṭalāq as a definitive severance (ḥall al-rabṭ) with degrees of severity—minor (baʿīnūnā al-ṣughrā) and major (baʿīnūnā al-kubrā)—affecting the right of return (rujʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical release; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to legal divorce as a contractual act, where the verbal formula (ṣīghah) carries binding force.
- Root: ج ع ل (j-ʿ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make, appoint, or stipulate a reward; in jurisprudence, the basis of the reward-for-service contract (juʿālah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological nuance of juʿālah as a conditional obligation (iltizām) tied to a specified outcome, analogous to divine recompense for acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes creation or assignment; metaphorical usage in legal contexts refers to a unilateral promise of compensation (ʿiwaḍ) for a defined act.
- Root: ع و ض (ʿ-w-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To compensate, exchange, or give in return; the core notion of quid pro quo in transactions.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological-legal sense of ʿiwaḍ as a countervalue in contracts, requiring mutual consent (tarāḍī) and proportionality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes substitution; metaphorical usage in divorce law refers to the financial consideration (māl) exchanged for the wife’s release (khulʿ).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Dependency (Taʿlīq al-Sharṭ bi al-Jazāʾ) — The legal effect of a conditional utterance (e.g., "If you divorce me three times for a thousand") depends on the precise syntactic linkage between the condition (sharṭ) and the response (jazāʾ), where the number specified governs the apportionment of the countervalue.
chapters.translation:
I say: This chapter contains four legal questions (masāʾil).

**The First Question:** If she says, "Divorce me three times for a thousand [dirhams]," and he divorces her once, he is entitled to one-third of the thousand, as we have mentioned, by analogy to the reward-for-service contract (juʿālah)—unlike the case on his side [where he might claim more].

But if he has only one divorce remaining over her, and she says, "Divorce me three times for a thousand," and he divorces her once, Imam al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) ruled that he is entitled to the entire thousand, because her intent was the major irrevocable separation (al-baynūnah al-kubrā), and that has been fully achieved.

Al-Muzanī (may God have mercy on him) ruled that he is entitled to one-third of the thousand, following the arithmetic [apportionment]. Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī ruled: If she knew that only one [divorce] remained, he is entitled to the entirety; if she did not know, he is entitled to one-third. There is no further subdivision (tafrīʿ) after this on his doctrine.

However, if he has two divorces remaining and he divorces her once, he is entitled to one-third according to both al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) and al-Muzanī, because al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) also follows the arithmetic—except when the major irrevocable separation is achieved. If he divorces her twice, he is entitled to the entirety according to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him), and to two-thirds according to al-Muzanī.

If she says, "Divorce me ten times for a thousand," he is entitled to one-tenth for one divorce and one-fifth for two, by consensus. As for three, he is entitled to the entirety according to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him); and by al-Muzanī’s analogy, he would be entitled to three-tenths of the wealth. It was also said, as a derivation (takhrij) on his analogy, that the distribution is only over the legally recognized number [i.e., three], and he agrees with al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) in entitlement to the entirety upon three in this scenario.

**The Second Question:** If she says, "Divorce me three times for a thousand," and he says, "You are divorced once for a thousand, and twice for free," a group of the imams of the school ruled that the one divorce occurs for one-third of the thousand, and the excess is not binding upon her; the two [subsequent] divorces do not occur, because she became irrevocably separated (bāʾin) by the first. But this has no basis. Rather, the first should not occur, because he was not satisfied with its occurrence except for a thousand, and she did not commit to one [divorce] except for three. Yes, the two divorces occur for free, and they are revocable (rajʿiyyatān).

But if he reverses and says, "You are divorced once for free, and twice for two-thirds of the thousand," one revocable divorce occurs, and the two [subsequent divorces] are derived from the case of a revocable divorcee (mukhālaʿah al-rajʿiyyah): If we permit [her khulʿ], they also occur for two-thirds of the thousand; if we prohibit it, two divorces also occur if she accepts, because the revocable divorcee is subject to further divorce. In sum, if a revocable divorcee seeks khulʿ—and on our view her khulʿ is invalid—it is like the khulʿ of a foolish woman (safīhah), such that divorce occurs without compensation.

**The Third Question:** If she says, "Divorce me once for a thousand," and he says, "You are divorced three times," al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) ruled that she is divorced three times and he is entitled to the thousand, because he responded to her and added [more]. Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad [al-Shaybānī] concurred with this. Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) ruled that he is entitled to nothing, because she did not seek the major irrevocable separation. He conceded that if she said, "Divorce me three times for a thousand," and he divorced her once, he is entitled to one-third of the thousand, even though he contravened [her request].

But if the husband repeats the mention of the wealth and says, "You are divorced three times for a thousand," most of the companions (al-aṣḥāb) hold that there is no difference between repeating and not repeating. Al-Fūrānī reported a view (wajh) from al-Qaffāl that if he repeats, he has matched each divorce with one-third of the thousand, so only one-third of the thousand is binding upon her, and the three [divorces] occur. But if he does not repeat the mention of the wealth, it could be said that she sought one [divorce], and he responded with a severance more severe than it, so it reverts to an increase in attribute (ṣifah). Here, however, the distribution is apparent. But on al-Qaffāl’s analogy, it would follow that only one occurs, because he matched two divorces with two-thirds of the thousand, which she did not accept. This view has also been stated. And it would also follow that the first does not occur, because she sought [a divorce] for a thousand, and he responded with one-third of the thousand—like his saying, "Sell to me for a thousand," and he says, "I sold for five hundred," which is not a valid response. This view has also been stated. And in sale, it was also said that it is valid. He also says: If she says, "Divorce me once for a thousand," and he says, "I divorced you once for five hundred," he is entitled to the full thousand, because the estimation of the countervalue (taqdīr al-ʿiwaḍ) is hers, not his.

In sum, the doctrine of Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) in the scenario of repeating the wealth has multiple aspects (awjuh).

**The Fourth Question:** If she says, "Divorce me half a divorce for a thousand," or "Divorce my half," or "my hand, for a thousand," and he responds to her, the divorce takes effect, but the countervalue is corrupted (fasada al-ʿiwaḍ) due to the corruption of the form of the exchange (ṣīghat al-muqābalah), so it reverts to the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl). There is a derived view (wajh munqās) that the named [amount] is established, because he specified the countervalue with what is not specific to it, but the Law (al-sharʿ) completes it—so it is not unlikely that it is treated as a full exchange.

chapters.title_en: Section 383: The Third Chapter on Her Requesting a Divorce Suspended upon a Time
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثالث في استدعائها طلاقا معلقا بزمان

وفيه صور
الأولى أن تقول طلقني غدا ولك ألف فإن طلق بعد غد نفذ رجعيا ولا مال له
لأنه خالف وإن طلق في الغد وقعت البينونة وفسد العوض لأنه لا يحتمل التعليق
فيرجع إلى مهر المثل
ولو طلق في الحال أو قبل الغد فقد أجاب وزاد إذ عجل فيثبت مهر المثل
وفي كل حال لا يستحق المال قبل الطلاق
الثانية أن تقول خذ مني ألف وأنت مخير في تطليقي من اليوم إلى شهر فلك
الألف متى لم تؤخر عن الشهر فمهما طلقها في الشهر على قصد الإجابة استحق
مهر المثل كالصورة الأولى وهذا بخلاف قولها متى ما طلقتني فلك ألف فإن متى
ما وإن كان ظاهرا في التأخير فلا يستحق العوض إلا بطلاق في المجلس لأن
قرينة العوض قابل عموم اللفظ فخصصه بالمجلس أما هاهنا فرفعت  الاحتمال
بالتصريح والتخيير في الشهر ومن الأصحاب من نقل الجواب من كل مسألة إلى
أختها وسوى بينهما
الثالثة إذ قال أنت طالق غدا على ألف فقالت قبلت فإذا جاء الغد وقع
الطلاق بائنا وفيما يلزمها وجهان
إحدهما مهر المثل لأن المعاوضة لا تقبل التعليق وهذا تعليق معاوضة
والثاني أنه يصح ويجب المسمى لأن مقابلة المعلق بالمال كمقابلة المنجز
والمعاوضة إنما صحت بوجود شقي الإيجاب والقبول في الحال من غير تعليق فإذا
صح قوله إذا أعطيتني ألفا فأنت طالق من غير قبول منها فبأن يصح هذا
التعليق مع قبولها في الحال أولى وفيه وجه ضعيف أن الطلاق لا يقع أصلا لأنه
علق بالعوض ولا سبيل إلى إثبات العوض بالتعليق ولا إلى إيقاع الطلاق وقد
علقه بالعوض
ثم إذا أوقعنا الطلاق عند مجيء الغد وجب العوض بعد نفوذ الطلاق ولا يجب
بمجرد قبولها في الحال وليس لها الرجوع بعد القبول لأنه قد تم شقا العقد
بالقبول

### | الفصل الرابع في سؤال الأجنبي واختلاعه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط ل ق (ṭ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To release, unbind, or set free; in legal usage, the dissolution of the marriage tie.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The absolute release from a binding covenant; in Kalām, it contrasts with taqyīd (restriction) — here, the suspension of an act upon a temporal condition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical release; metaphorical (majāz) for legal divorce, where the "binding" is the marital contract.
- Root: ع و ض (ʿ-w-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To compensate, exchange, or give in return; a substitute (ʿiwaḍ) for a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In transactional theology, the counter-value in a commutative contract (muʿāwaḍah); here, the monetary consideration for divorce.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for barter; metaphorical for any quid pro quo, including the wife's payment for her release (khulʿ).
- Root: خ ي ر (kh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To choose, select, or have the option; the act of deliberation between alternatives.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The faculty of free choice (ikhtiyār) as a condition for valid legal agency; here, the wife's grant of a temporal window for the husband's decision.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for choosing; metaphorical for legal option (takhyīr) in contracts, where the choice itself is the operative act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīm al-Ẓarf wa Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm (Fronting the Adverbial and Suspending the Ruling) — When a temporal adverb (ẓarf) like "tomorrow" (ghadan) is fronted in a conditional construction, it governs the entire apodosis, making the ruling contingent upon the arrival of that time, unless a contextual indicator (qarīnah) restricts its scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third chapter concerns her requesting a divorce suspended upon a time.

This contains several cases.

The first case: She says, "Divorce me tomorrow, and you shall have one thousand." If he divorces her after tomorrow, it takes effect as a revocable divorce (rajʿī), and he has no claim to the money, because he contravened [the specified time]. But if he divorces her on the morrow itself, the irrevocable separation (baynūnah) occurs, and the counter-value is void, because it does not admit of suspension. Thus, he reverts to the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl).

And if he divorces her immediately, or before the morrow, then he has responded [to her request] and added [to it] by hastening [the divorce]; so the equivalent dower is established. And in every case, he does not deserve the money before the divorce [actually occurs].

The second case: She says, "Take from me one thousand, and you are given the choice (mukhayyar) to divorce me from today up to a month; you shall have the thousand provided you do not delay beyond the month." So whenever he divorces her within the month with the intention of responding [to her offer], he deserves the equivalent dower, just as in the first case. This differs from her saying, "Whenever you divorce me, you shall have one thousand," for although "whenever" (matā mā) is apparently [indicative] of delay, he does not deserve the counter-value except by a divorce [issued] in the same session (majlis), because the contextual indicator of the counter-value qualifies the generality of the expression and restricts it to the session. But here, she has removed the possibility [of ambiguity] by explicit statement and by granting the choice within the month. Among our companions (al-aṣḥāb) are those who transfer the ruling from each case to its sister and equate the two.

The third case: When he says, "You are divorced tomorrow for one thousand," and she says, "I accept," then when the morrow arrives, the divorce occurs as an irrevocable separation (bāʾin). Regarding what is incumbent upon her, there are two views:

One: The equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl), because a commutative exchange (muʿāwaḍah) does not admit of suspension, and this is a suspended exchange.

The second: It is valid, and the named sum (al-musammā) is obligatory, because making the suspended [divorce] the counterpart of money is like making the immediate [divorce] the counterpart of money. The exchange is only valid by the existence of both parts — the offer (ījāb) and the acceptance (qabūl) — in the present moment, without suspension. For if his saying, "If you give me one thousand, you are divorced," is valid without her acceptance, then it is all the more fitting that this suspension be valid with her acceptance in the present moment. There is a weak view that the divorce does not occur at all, because he suspended it upon the counter-value, and there is no way to establish the counter-value by suspension, nor to effect the divorce, since he has suspended it upon the counter-value.

Then, when we effect the divorce upon the arrival of the morrow, the counter-value becomes obligatory after the divorce takes effect, and it is not obligatory merely by her acceptance in the present moment. Nor does she have the right to retract after the acceptance, because both parts of the contract have been completed by the acceptance.

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 384: The Khulʿ of a Third Party, Its Variants, and Disputes Arising Therein
chapters.arabic_text:
واعلم أن اختلاع الأجنبي كاختلاع المرأة في جميع صيغ الالتزام وأحكامه
لأن الطلاق مما يستقل به الزوج وإنما يحتاج إلى قبولها لالتزام المال
وللأجنبي أن يلتزم المال على سبيل الافتداء ولكن الأجنبي إن كان وكيلا من
جهتها فله أن يعقد لها ولنفسه وينظر إلى لفظه ونيته ومطلقه يقع من جهة
الوكالة ولكن إن لم يصرح بالفسادة تعلقت به العهدة وطولب بالعوض كالوكيل في
الشراء
وإن قال الأجنبي اختلعت بوكالتها ثم بأن أنه لم يكن وكيلا تبين أن الطلاق
لم يقع لأن الخطاب كأنه معها ولم يجر قبولها ولا قبول نائبها
فرع أبوها إذا كان هو المختلع فهو كالأجنبي وإن كانت طفلة فاختلعها بمال
نفسه فهو كالأجنبي وإن اختلعها بمالها فله أحوال
الأولى أن يكون اختلعت على سبيل الولاية بمالها أو بهذا العبد من مالها
لم يقع الطلاق بل هو كالوكيل الكاذب
الثانية أن يكون اختلعت على سبيل الاستقلال لكن بهذا العبد من مالها فهو
كالاختلاع بالمال المغصوب وقد سبق
الثالثة  أن يكون اختلعت بهذا العبد الذي هو من مالها ولم يتعرض لما يزيد
على هذا من نيابة أو استقلال وقع الطلاق رجعيا كاختلاع السفيهة وكأنه أهل
للقبول
ومحجور عليه في مالها كالسفيهة محجور عليها في مال نفسها وهذا في غموض
المختلع بالمغصوب لو أضاف المال إلى المالك وقع الطلاق بائنا
وقيل الفساد في العوض فخرج القاضي وجها هاهنا إنه كالمغصوب وخرج في
المغصوب هاهنا وجها إن الطلاق يقع رجعيا
الرابع أن يكون اختلعت بهذا العبد ولم يذكر إنه من مالها فإن الزوج جاهلا
به فهو كما لو خرج العوض مستحقا وإن كان عالما فوجهان
أحدهما أن يصير المعلوم كالمذكور لفظا فيقع الطلاق على المشهور رجعيا
والثاني أن يكون كما لو كان جاهلا نظرا إلى مجرد اللفظ
الخامسة أن يختلعها بالبراءة عن الصداق فإن جوزنا له العفو عن صدقها في
الاختلاع صح الخلع كما لو اختلعت بنفسها وإن منعنا بذلك وهو الصحيح ففيه
ثلاثة أوجه
أحدهما وهو ظاهر النص أن الطلاق يقع رجعيا كالسفيهة
والثاني أنه كالوكيل الكاذب حتى لا يقع الطلاق لأن إضافته إلى الصداق وهو
أب يشعر بأنه كالنائب أما إضافته إلى العبد فهو المغصوب أشبه
والثالث أن يقع الطلاق بائنا ويجب مهر المثل كالعبد المغصوب
السادسة أن يقول خلعها وإن ضامن براءتك فالقياس أنه يقع الطلاق رجعيا ولا
يلزمه شيء لأن ضمان عين البراءة محال فيلفوا الحال ويصح القبول وإن قال
طلقها وإن طولبت بالصداق فأنا ضامن براءتك فتحصل البينونة ويجب مهر المثل
لفساد صيغة الالتزام
وضابط النظر في هذه المسائل أن الخلع إنما يختل إما بسبب في نفس القبول
فيوجب نفي أقبل الطلاق أو لخلل في نفس الالتزام فيوجب نفي البينونة لا نفي
الطلاق أو لخلل في الملتزم إلا في الالتزام كالخمر المقصود فيوجب نفي
المسمى لا نفي البينونة ويكون التردد في أصل الطلاق للتردد في صحة القبول
والتردد في البينونة للتردد في صحة أصل الالتزام والتردد في المسمى للتردد
في صحة الملتزم والله تعالى أعلم بالصواب
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في النزاع في الخلع - صلى الله عليه
وسلم -
وهو أنواع
الأول أن يقع في أصل عوض أو جنسه أو قدره
فإن وقع في الأصل فالقول قولها إن أنكرت العوض وإن خلفت وقعت البينونة
مؤاخذة للرجل بقوله إني خالعت على عوض
وإن تنازعا في الجنس فقال خالعتك بدراهم وقالت بل بفلوس تحالفا والرجوع
إلى مهر المثل كما في الصداق وكذلك في المقدار وإن توافقا على جريان الخلع
بألف درهم ولكن قال الزوج أردنا به الدراهم وقالت بل أردنا الفلوس فهذا
يستدعي مقدمة وهي أنه لو كانت النقود مختلفة ولا غالب فيها فقال بعت بألف
درهم وقال اشتريت بألف درهم ولم يتعرضا للجنس ولكن توافقا على إرادة نوع
واحد لم يصح البيع ولم يحتمل هذه الجهالة فيه والمشهور الظاهر في الخلع أنه
يحتمل ذلك ويكفل فيه النية أو العلم بالعوض وإن كان شرطا لثبوت المسمى ولكن
يحتمل فيه ما لم يحتمل في البيع ولذلك حصل الملك بمجرد الإعطاء من غير لفظ
وهذا ليس يخلو عن أشكال
ثم لا خلاف إنه لو قال خالعتك على ألف وقبلت وتوافقا على إرادة نوع واحد
لم يحتمل هذا لأن اللفظ صريح في الاحتمال والترديد بين الأنواع وإنما
المذكور مجرد العدد وهو عرضي لا ينبئ عن ماهية جنسية ولا نوعية بخلاف ما
إذا ذكر الدراهم فإنه لم يبق إلا التفصيل بالصفات فلا يبعد تخصيص عمومه
بالنية وفي كلام القاضي دلالة على أن عموم الألف كعموم الدراهم مع أنه
قطع بأنه لو قال ألف شيء لم تؤثر النية لأن لفظ الشيء آكد في حقيقة
الاحتمال والنية لا تغيره وقال الشيخ أبو محمد النية في الدراهم أيضا إنما
تؤثر إذا توافقا قبل العقد على ما يقصد أن به فإن لم يسبق التواطؤ فلا يؤثر
توافق النية وكأنه يلتفت على معنى مسألة السر والعلانية ولا يخفى أن يعتبر
هذا بالنية أقرب من إرادة الألف بالألفين فإن ذلك تغيير صريح فنعود إلى
النزاع وله صور
الأولى أن يقول الزوج أردنا الدراهم جميعا وقالت بل أردنا الفلوس جميعا
فهذا نزاع في الجنس فيتحالفان وفيه وجه بعيد أن التحالف لا يجري لأنه نزاع
في النية وإنما اختلاف في الجنس يتولد منع تبعا وهو ضعيف
الثاني أن يتوافقا على جانب جانب الزوج وإرادته الدراهم قالت المرأة أردت
الفلوس فالقول قولها وإذا حلفت انتفى عنها العوض ووقعت البينونة مؤاخذة له
بقوله
الثالثة أن يتوافقا على جانبها وإرادتها الفلوس وإرادته ولكن قال الزوج
أردت الدراهم فلا فرق لاختلاف الجواب فحكم هذا إن البينونة واقعة لأننا
ننتظر إلى الملفوظ وقد قال خالعتك على ألف فقالت قبلت فلا مطلع على النية
ويلزم من هذا أنهما لو توافقا أيضا على اختلاف القصد وقعت البينونة لظاهر
اللفظ ولو تصور إطلاع كل واحد منهما على باطن صاحبه حتى تتحقق المخالفة في
النية فينبغي أن لا يقع الطلاق باطنا ثم قال القاضي للزوج مهر المثل لأن
البينونة وقعت ظاهرا ولغا أثر النية فبقي اللفظ مجهولا وكأن النية عنده
إنما تؤثر إذا توافقا في واتفقا عليه فإذ لم يتفقا لغت النية ونظر إلى مجرد
اللفظ وهو بعيد لأن موجب قول الزوج لأن لا بينونة ولا عوض فالحكم عليه
بالبنيونة له وجه أما الحكم له بالعوض وهو لا يدعيه فبعيد
الرابعة توفقا على أنه أراد الدراهم فقالت أردت الدراهم أيضا وحصلت
الفرقة وقال بل أردت الفلوس وقال ولا فرقة فالقول قولها في نيتها فإذا حلفت
حصلت الفرقة وعند القاضي له مهر المثل وإن كان هو منكرا للفرقة وهو بعيد
الخامسة أن يقول أردت الدراهم وما ادعى عليها شيء وقالت أردت الفلوس وما
ادعت عليه شيء فالفرقة أيضا حاصلة وقال القاضي يتحالفان وهذا لا وجه له
لأنه ليس يدعي عليها مالا معينا فكيف يحلف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ع (kh-l-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pull off, strip away, or divest — as one removes a garment; hence the contractual divestiture of marital tie for a compensation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The dissolution of the marriage bond by the wife's ransoming herself (iftidāʾ), transferring the right of divorce from the husband to a compensatory transaction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of stripping; metaphorical (majāz) in juristic usage for the divorce-with-compensation contract, where the "stripping" is of the marital bond.
- Root: ض-م-ن (ḍ-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guarantee, undertake, or assume liability for a debt or obligation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The assumption of a financial obligation (iltizām al-māl) as a valid contractual act, distinct from the unilateral power of divorce.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — to contain or include; metaphorical — to stand surety for a claim, as in ḍamān al-ʿuhdah (liability for the compensation).
- Root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be near, to govern, to take charge of; hence walī (guardian) and wilāyah (guardianship).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal authority to act on behalf of another, particularly a father over a minor daughter in financial and marital matters.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — proximity; metaphorical — legal guardianship and agency (wikālah), where the guardian stands in the place of the principal.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Element) — When the agent's capacity (e.g., as wakīl or walī) is unstated or disputed, the syntactic construction is parsed according to the apparent (ẓāhir) wording, while the intended (niyyah) meaning may alter the ruling; the sentence's grammatical subject (the divorcing party) is determined by the explicit or implicit agency.
chapters.translation:
Know that the khulʿ (divestiture) by a third party (ajnabī) is like the khulʿ by the wife herself in all the formulae of obligation (ṣiyagh al-iltizām) and their rulings — for divorce (ṭalāq) is a matter the husband alone is competent to effect, and he only needs her acceptance (qabūl) for the obligation of the wealth (iltizām al-māl). And a third party may obligate the wealth by way of ransoming (iftidāʾ). However, if the third party is an agent (wakīl) on her behalf, then he may contract for her and for himself, and regard is given to his wording (lafẓ) and his intention (niyyah); and his unqualified (muṭlaq) utterance falls on the side of agency (wikālah). But if he does not explicitly state the annulment (fasādah), the liability (ʿuhdah) attaches to him, and he is pursued for the compensation (ʿiwaḍ) — like the agent in purchase (al-wakīl fī al-shirāʾ).

And if the third party says, "I effected khulʿ by her agency," then it becomes clear that he was not an agent — it is thereby known that the divorce did not occur, because the address (khiṭāb) was as if directed to her, and neither her acceptance nor the acceptance of her deputy (nāʾib) took place.

Branch: Her father — if he is the one effecting khulʿ — he is like a third party. And if she is a minor (ṭiflah), and he effects khulʿ with his own wealth, he is like a third party. But if he effects khulʿ with her wealth, then he has several states:

The first: That he effects khulʿ on the basis of guardianship (wilāyah) with her wealth, or with this slave from her wealth — the divorce does not occur; rather, he is like the false agent (al-wakīl al-kādhib).

The second: That he effects khulʿ on the basis of independence (istiqlāl), but with this slave from her wealth — this is like khulʿ with usurped wealth (al-māl al-maghṣūb), which has already been discussed.

The third: That he effects khulʿ with this slave which is from her wealth, and he does not address anything beyond this — neither agency nor independence — the divorce occurs as a revocable divorce (rajʿī), like the khulʿ of the foolish woman (al-safīhah); and it is as though he is qualified for acceptance (ahl li-l-qabūl). And he is interdicted (maḥjūr ʿalayh) regarding her wealth, just as the foolish woman is interdicted regarding her own wealth. And this is in the obscurity (ghumūḍ) of the one effecting khulʿ with the usurped [wealth]: if he attributed the wealth to its owner, the divorce would occur as an irrevocable divorce (bāʾin). And it was said [that] the corruption (fasād) is in the compensation (ʿiwaḍ); so al-Qāḍī derived a face (wajh) here that it is like the usurped [wealth], and he derived in the usurped [wealth] here a face that the divorce occurs as revocable.

The fourth: That he effects khulʿ with this slave, and he does not mention that it is from her wealth — and the husband is ignorant of it — then it is as if the compensation turned out to be legally claimed (mustaḥaqq). But if he [the husband] was aware, then there are two faces: One of them — that the known (al-maʿlūm) becomes like the mentioned (al-madhkūr) verbally, so the divorce occurs, on the well-known [view], as revocable. And the second — that it is as if he were ignorant, considering only the bare wording (mujarrad al-lafẓ).

The fifth: That he effects khulʿ with her by the acquittal (barāʾah) from the dower (ṣadāq). If we permit him to waive her dower in khulʿ, then the khulʿ is valid, just as if she had effected khulʿ herself. But if we forbid that — and this is the correct [view] — then there are three faces: One of them, which is the apparent [import] of the text (ẓāhir al-naṣṣ), is that the divorce occurs as revocable, like [the case of] the foolish woman. The second — that he is like the false agent, so that the divorce does not occur, because his attribution (iḍāfah) of [the khulʿ] to the dower, while he is a father, suggests that he is a deputy (nāʾib); whereas his attribution to the slave — which is the usurped [wealth] — is more akin [to independence]. The third — that the divorce occurs as irrevocable, and the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl) is obligatory, like [the case of] the usurped slave.

The sixth: That he says, "I effect khulʿ of her, and I guarantee your acquittal (ḍāmin barāʾatik)" — then the analogical [ruling] (qiyās) is that the divorce occurs as revocable, and nothing is incumbent upon him, because the guarantee of the very acquittal (ḍamān ʿayn al-barāʾah) is impossible (muḥāl); so the [guarantee] is nullified (yalghū), and the acceptance is valid. But if he says, "I divorce her, and if you are pursued for the dower, I guarantee your acquittal" — then irrevocability (baynūnah) is achieved, and the equivalent dower is obligatory, due to the corruption of the formula of obligation (fasād ṣīghat al-iltizām).

And the governing principle (ḍābiṭ) of consideration in these matters is that khulʿ is only vitiated either: (1) due to a defect in the acceptance itself (sabab fī nafs al-qabūl), which necessitates the negation of the occurrence of divorce; or (2) due to a defect in the obligation itself (khalal fī nafs al-iltizām), which necessitates the negation of irrevocability (baynūnah) but not the negation of divorce; or (3) due to a defect in the obligated thing (al-multazam) — i.e., in the obligation [itself], like the intended wine (al-khamr al-maqṣūd) — which necessitates the negation of the named compensation (al-musammā) but not the negation of irrevocability. And the hesitation (taraddud) regarding the very divorce is due to hesitation regarding the validity of the acceptance; and the hesitation regarding irrevocability is due to hesitation regarding the validity of the very obligation; and the hesitation regarding the named compensation is due to hesitation regarding the validity of the obligated thing. And God Most High knows best what is correct.

— Peace be upon him — The First Chapter: On Disputes in Khulʿ — Peace be upon him —

And it is of several types:

The first: That the dispute occurs regarding the very substance of the compensation (aṣl al-ʿiwaḍ), or its genus (jins), or its amount (qadr).

If the dispute is regarding the substance — then the statement (al-qawl) is hers if she denies the compensation; and if she takes an oath (ḥalafat), irrevocability (baynūnah) occurs, holding the man to his statement, "I effected khulʿ upon a compensation."

And if they dispute regarding the genus — he says, "I effected khulʿ with dirhams," and she says, "Rather, with fils" — then they both take oaths (taḥāluf), and recourse is to the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl), as in the case of the dower (ṣadāq). And likewise regarding the amount. And if they agree upon the occurrence of khulʿ with one thousand dirhams, but the husband says, "We intended by it dirhams," and she says, "Rather, we intended fils" — this requires a preliminary [point] (muqaddimah), namely: that if the currencies (nuqūd) were different with no predominant one, and he said, "I sold for one thousand dirhams," and she said, "I bought for one thousand dirhams," and they did not address the genus, but agreed upon intending one specific type — the sale would not be valid, and this ignorance (jahālah) would not be tolerated in it. But the well-known and apparent [view] in khulʿ is that it tolerates that, and intention (niyyah) or knowledge of the compensation suffices therein — even if it is a condition for the establishment of the named [compensation] — yet it tolerates what is not tolerated in sale. And for this reason, ownership (milk) is achieved by mere giving (iʿṭāʾ) without a verbal formula (lafẓ). And this is not free from difficulty (ishkāl).

Then there is no disagreement that if he said, "I effected khulʿ with you for one thousand," and she accepted, and they agreed upon intending one specific type — this is not tolerated, because the wording is explicit in its probability (iḥtimāl) and hesitation (tardīd) between the types; for what is mentioned is merely the number (ʿadad), which is accidental (ʿaraḍī) and does not indicate a generic or specific quiddity (māhiyyah jinsiyyah wa lā nawʿiyyah) — unlike when dirhams are mentioned, for then nothing remains except specification by attributes (tafṣīl bi-l-ṣifāt), so it is not far-fetched that its generality (ʿumūm) be particularized by intention. And in the speech of al-Qāḍī there is an indication that the generality of "one thousand" is like the generality of "dirhams," even though he decisively held that if he said, "one thousand things" (alf shayʾ), intention would have no effect, because the word "thing" (shayʾ) is more emphatic in the reality of probability, and intention does not change it. And Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: Intention in "dirhams" also only has effect if they had agreed before the contract (qabl al-ʿaqd) upon what he intends by it; but if no prior collusion (tawāṭuʾ) preceded, then the agreement of intention has no effect. And it is as though this turns upon the meaning of the question of the secret and the public (al-sirr wa al-ʿalāniyyah). And it is not hidden that considering this by intention is closer than intending "one thousand" as "two thousand," for that is an explicit alteration (taghyīr ṣarīḥ). So we return to the dispute, and it has several forms:

The first: That the husband says, "We both intended dirhams," and she says, "Rather, we both intended fils" — this is a dispute regarding the genus, so they both take oaths. And there is a remote face (wajh baʿīd) that mutual oath-taking (taḥāluf) does not apply, because it is a dispute regarding intention, and the difference in genus is generated from it only as a consequence (tabaʿan) — and this is weak.

The second: That they agree on his side — his intention being dirhams — and the woman says, "I intended fils" — then the statement is hers; and when she takes the oath, the compensation is negated from her, and irrevocability occurs, holding him to his statement.

The third: That they agree on her side — her intention being fils — and his intention [also being fils], but the husband says, "I intended dirhams" — then there is no difference in the answer [i.e., the ruling is the same]. For the ruling of this is that irrevocability occurs, because we look to the uttered [wording] (al-malfūẓ), and he said, "I effected khulʿ with you for one thousand," and she said, "I accepted" — so there is no access to the intention (lā muṭṭalaʿ ʿalā al-niyyah). And it follows from this that if they also agreed upon the divergence of intent (ikhtilāf al-qaṣd), irrevocability would occur due to the apparent [import] of the wording — even if one could imagine each of them having access to the inner [mind] of the other, such that the divergence in intention is verified — then the divorce should not occur inwardly (bāṭinan). Then al-Qāḍī said: The husband is entitled to the equivalent dower, because irrevocability occurred outwardly (ẓāhir), and the effect of intention was nullified (laghā athar al-niyyah), so the wording remained unknown (majhūl). And it is as though, in his view, intention only has effect when they agree and concur upon it; but when they do not concur, intention is nullified, and regard is given to the bare wording. And this is remote — because the implication of the husband's statement is that there is neither irrevocability nor compensation; so ruling against him with irrevocability has a basis, but ruling for him with the compensation, which he does not claim, is remote.

The fourth: That they agree that he intended dirhams, and she says, "I also intended dirhams," and separation (furqah) occurred; then he says, "Rather, I intended fils," and says, "There is no separation" — then the statement is hers regarding her intention; and when she takes the oath, separation is established. And in al-Qāḍī's view, he is entitled to the equivalent dower, even though he denies the separation — and this is remote.

The fifth: That he says, "I intended dirhams," and he claims nothing against her; and she says, "I intended fils," and she claims nothing against him — then separation is also established. And al-Qāḍī said: They both take oaths. And this has no basis, because he does not claim against her a specific wealth (māl muʿayyan) — so how would he take an oath?

chapters.title_en: The Second Type: Disagreement Over the Countervalue (al-ʿIwaḍ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | النوع الثاني الاختلاف في العوض

فإذا قالت سألتك ثلاث طلقات بألف فأجبتني فقال بل طلقة بألف فأجبتك فقد
اتفقا على الألف وتنازعا في مقدرا المعوض فيتحالفان والرجوع إلى مهر المثل
فأما عدد الطلاق فلا يعتبر  فيه إلا قوله فلا نزيد على واحدة فإن قيل فإذا
كان القول قوله في عدد الطلاق والألف متفق عليه فأي معنى للتحالف ولا فائدة
له إلا إبدال الألف المتفق عليه بمهر المثل
قلنا مقتضى التحالف إبطال العوضين لكن الطلاق لا يقبل الإبطال فجرينا على
قياس التحالف في تطرق الفسخ إلى ما يتطرق إليه خاصة

### | النوع الثالث النزاع في المستحق عليه

فإذا ادعى عليها الاختلاع فقالت إنما اختلعني أجنبي فالقول قولها في
انكار الاختلاع ولا رجوع له على الأجنبي لاعترافه بأنه لم يختلع
أما إذا قالت أضفت الاختلاع إلى أجنبي وكنت سفيرة له ففيه وجهان
أحدهما أنهما يتحالفان لاتفاقهما على أصل الالتزام واختلافهما في صفة
الإضافة
والثاني أن القول قولها لأنها أنكرت أصل الالتزام
= كتاب الطلاق = والنظر في شطرين
أحدهما في عموم أحكامه
والثاني في التعليقات خاصة أما الشطر الأول ففيه ستة أبواب
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في معنى السنة والبدعة - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - وفيه فصلان

### | الفصل الأول في مواقع السنة والبدعة

وقد اتفق العلماء على انقسام الطلاق إلى سني وبدعي فالبدعي هو الطلاق
المحرم إيقاعه وإن كان نافذا والسني ما لا تحريم فيه
والبدعي هو الطلاق الواقع بعد المسيس في الحيض دون سؤالها والواقع في طهر
جامعها فيه ولم يتبين حملها فهذان أصلان
أما الأول وهو الحيض فيحرم في الطلاق بعد المسيس ولا بدعة في طلاق غير
الممسوسة أصلا وأما الممسوسة فيحرم طلاقها في الحيض بغير سؤالها لما روي أن
ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما طلق امرأة في الحيض فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم لعمر رضي الله عنه مره فليراجعها حتى تطهر ثم تحيض ثم تطهر ثم إن شاء
طلقها وإن شاء أمسكها فتلك العدة
التي أمر الله تعالى أن تطلق لها النساء وأراد به قوله تعالى {فطلقوهن
لعدتهن} أي لقبل عدتهن حتى يشرعن عقيب الطلاق في العدة المحسوبة فإن بقيت
الحيض لا تحسب فتطول العدة ثم أمر صلى الله عليه وسلم زوجة ثابت بالافتداء
ولم يستفصل أهي حائض أم لا فدل على أن الخلع مستثنى ولا تحريم فيه
فمنهم من فهم ذلك لكونها راضية فكأنه جوز تطويل العدة برضاها وقال لا
حرمة في الطلاق بسؤالها وإن لم يكن بمال ويحرم اختلاع الأجنبي لعدم رضاها
ومنهم من جعل ذلك من خاصبة الابتداء لأنه لا يبذل إلا لضرورة فجوز اختلاع
الأجنبي وحرم الطلاق وإن كان بسؤالها ويشهد بذلك جواز الطلاق للمؤلي إذا
طولب به لأن ذلك
واجب بنوع ضرورة فاتفقوا على جواز الخلع وطلاق المؤلي وترددوا في اختلاع
الأجنبي والطلاق برضاها
وأما قوله إن دخلت الدار فأنت طالق فلا بدعة فيه وإن جرى في الحيض لكن
ينظر إن اتفق الدخول في الحيض نفذ الطلاق بدعيا وفائدته أنه يؤمر بالرجعة
على سبيل الاستحباب وإذا رجع فهل يجوز أن يطلقها في الطهر الأول بعده فيه
وجهان
أحدهما نعم إذ لا معنى للمنع في الطهر وقد ورد في بعض الروايات مرة
فليراجعها حتى تطهر
والثاني أنه يصبر على الطهر الثاني لأن ذلك يؤدي إلى أن تكون الرجعة لأجل
الطلاق وذلك لا يليق بمحاسن الشرع ويشهد لذالك حديث ابن عمر
وعلى هذا ترددوا في أنه هل يستحب أن يجامعها حتى يظهر مقصود الرجعة
أما إذا طلقها طلاقا غير بدعي ثم راجعها فله أن يطلقها في الحال إذ لا
بدعة حتى تستدرك
وأما الجمع بين الثلاث فلا بدعة فيه خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله نعم
الأولى أن
يفرق كيلا يلحقه ندم
فرع إذ قال أنت طالق مع آخر جزء من الحيض فهذا طلاق يصادف الحيض ولكن
يستعقب العدة فمنهم من نظر إلى المعنى وقال هو سني ومنهم من نظر إلى المظنة
وهو الحيض فقال هو بدعي وكذا الخلاف فيما إذا قال أنت طالق مع آخر جزء من
الطهر ولعل النظر إلى المظنة أولى
الأصل الثاني في بدعة الطلاق في طهر جامعها فيه وهو بدعة إلا إن يكون
عالما بكونها حاملا فيحل الطلاق لأن المحذور لحوق الندم بسبب الجهل بالولد
واستدخالها ماء  الزوج في معنى الوطء لأنه يتوقع منه الولد والإتيان في
غير المأتى فيه تردد فإنه وإن لم يتوقع منه الولد فالعدة تجب به وترددوا
فيما لو وطئها في الحيض ثم طهرت أنه هل يحرم طلاقها لأن بقية الحيض قد تدل
على عدم الولد دلالة دون دلالة ابتداء الحيض
والظاهر أنه لا بدعة في خلاعها أيضا كما في حالة الحيض ومنهم من قال
السبب
هاهنا حذار الولد ورضاها لا يؤثر والمحذور ثم طول العدة فلا يبعد أن يؤثر
رضاها في حقها
وقد خرج من هذا أن خمسا من النسوة لا بدعة في طلاقهن ولا سنة
غير الممسوسة
والحامل بيقين
والآيسة والصغيرة إذ لاحيض لهما ولا ولد
والمختلعة

### | الفصل الثاني في إضافة الطلاق إلى السنة والبدعة تنجيزا وتعليقا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ض (ʿ-w-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "compensation," "substitute," or "equivalent given in exchange"; al-ʿiwaḍ denotes the quid pro quo in a contractual exchange.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, al-ʿiwaḍ is the material countervalue in commutative transactions (muʿāwaḍāt), distinct from the act itself (al-ʿaqd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to a tangible equivalent; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to legal constructs where the countervalue is replaced by a standard (mithl).
- Root: خ-ل-ع (kh-l-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "pulling off" or "stripping away," as in removing a garment; technically, khulʿ is the wife's redemption from marriage by payment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām and fiqh, khulʿ is a dissolution (faskh) of the marriage tie through mutual consent with compensation, distinct from repudiation (ṭalāq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical removal; metaphorical sense is the legal severance of the marital bond.
- Root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root means "likeness" or "similarity"; mahr al-mithl is the "equivalent dower" determined by parity with women of similar status.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, al-mithl is the standard of equivalence used when the specified amount is invalidated or disputed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes resemblance; metaphorical usage in law denotes a normative benchmark.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taḥāluf (Mutual Oaths) — When two parties dispute over the quantum of a contractual obligation and neither can prove their claim, each takes an oath, and the contract is rescinded or the disputed term is replaced by a standard (mithl). This applies to the countervalue but not to acts that cannot be annulled (e.g., ṭalāq).
chapters.translation:
I say: The second type concerns disagreement over the countervalue (al-ʿiwaḍ). If she says, "I asked you for three divorces for one thousand [dirhams], and you agreed," and he says, "Rather, [I gave] one divorce for one thousand, and I agreed to that," then they have agreed upon the thousand but disputed the quantity of the counter-compensated [act]. Thus, they take mutual oaths (yataḥālafān), and recourse is made to the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl). As for the number of divorces, only his statement is considered, so we do not exceed one. If it is said: When his statement prevails regarding the number of divorces, and the thousand is agreed upon, what meaning is there in mutual oaths? There is no benefit except replacing the agreed-upon thousand with the equivalent dower. We reply: The requirement of mutual oaths is the nullification of both countervalues, but divorce (ṭalāq) does not admit nullification. So we proceed according to the analogy of mutual oaths in extending rescission (faskh) only to what admits it.

The third type concerns dispute over the one upon whom the obligation rests. If she claims that he divorced her by khulʿ (redemption), and he says, "Rather, a stranger (ajnabī) effected khulʿ with me," then her statement prevails in denying the khulʿ, and he has no recourse against the stranger, because he admits that he did not effect khulʿ. However, if she says, "I attributed the khulʿ to a stranger, and I was his agent (safīrah)," then there are two views (wajhān): One is that they take mutual oaths, because they agree on the underlying obligation (aṣl al-iltizām) but differ on the attribute of attribution (ṣifat al-iḍāfah). The second is that her statement prevails, because she denies the underlying obligation itself.

= The Book of Divorce (Kitāb al-Ṭalāq) = And the consideration is in two parts: one on its general rulings, and the second on conditional suspensions (taʿlīqāt) specifically. As for the first part, it contains six chapters.

Chapter One: On the Meaning of Sunnah and Innovation (Bidʿah) — and it contains two sections.

Section One: On the Loci of Sunnah and Innovation. The scholars have agreed upon the division of divorce into sunnī (conforming to the Sunnah) and bidʿī (innovative). The bidʿī is the divorce whose occurrence is prohibited (muḥarram), though it is effective (nāfidh); the sunnī is that which has no prohibition in it. The bidʿī is the divorce occurring after consummation (masīs) during menstruation (ḥayḍ) without her asking for it, and that occurring in a state of purity (ṭuhr) in which he had intercourse with her and her pregnancy has not become evident. These are two foundational principles (aṣlān).

As for the first — menstruation — divorce after consummation is prohibited, and there is no innovation in divorcing a non-consummated woman at all. As for the consummated woman, divorcing her during menstruation without her request is prohibited, due to what was narrated that Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) divorced his wife during menstruation, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "Command him to take her back (murhu fa-l-yurājiʿhā) until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure; then if he wishes, he may divorce her, and if he wishes, he may retain her. That is the waiting period (ʿiddah) which Allah the Exalted has commanded that women be divorced for." He intended His saying, the Exalted: {فطلقوهن لعدتهن} ("Divorce them for their ʿiddah"), i.e., before their ʿiddah, so that they commence, immediately after the divorce, the countable ʿiddah. For if the menstruation remains, it is not counted, and the ʿiddah is prolonged. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded the wife of Thābit to ransom herself (iftidāʾ) and did not inquire whether she was menstruating or not. This indicates that khulʿ is excepted and has no prohibition in it. Some understood this because she is consenting (rāḍiyah), as if he permitted the prolongation of the ʿiddah with her consent, and said there is no prohibition in divorce at her request, even if not for wealth; but the khulʿ of a stranger is prohibited due to her lack of consent. Others made this a specific characteristic of the initiation (ibtidāʾ), because [khulʿ] is not offered except out of necessity (ḍarūrah); thus they permitted the khulʿ of a stranger and prohibited divorce even if at her request. This is supported by the permissibility of divorce for the one who has sworn abstinence (al-mūlī) when he is demanded [to fulfill or divorce], because that is obligatory by a kind of necessity. So they agreed on the permissibility of khulʿ and the divorce of the mūlī, but they differed over the khulʿ of a stranger and divorce with her consent.

As for his saying, "If you enter the house, you are divorced," there is no innovation in it, even if it occurs during menstruation. However, consideration is given: if the entry occurs during menstruation, the divorce takes effect as bidʿī, and its benefit is that he is commanded to take her back (rujʿah) by way of recommendation (istihbāb). If he takes her back, is it permissible for him to divorce her in the first subsequent purity? There are two views: One is yes, for there is no meaning to prohibition in purity, and it has been reported in some narrations: "Then let him take her back until she becomes pure." The second is that he waits for the second purity, because that would lead to the return (rujʿah) being for the sake of divorce, which does not befit the beauties of the Law (maḥāsin al-sharʿ). The ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar supports this. And upon this, they differed over whether it is recommended that he have intercourse with her so that the purpose of the return becomes manifest. As for when he divorces her with a non-bidʿī divorce and then takes her back, he may divorce her immediately, for there is no innovation until she is overtaken [by menstruation].

As for combining three [divorces] at once, there is no innovation in it, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him). Yes, it is preferable to separate them, lest regret (nadam) overtake him.

Branch (farʿ): If he says, "You are divorced with the last part of menstruation," this is a divorce that coincides with menstruation but is followed by the ʿiddah. Some considered the meaning (maʿnā) and said it is sunnī; others considered the indicant (maẓinnah), which is menstruation, and said it is bidʿī. Likewise, the disagreement applies if he says, "You are divorced with the last part of purity." Perhaps considering the indicant is more appropriate (awlā).

The second foundational principle concerns the innovation of divorce in a state of purity in which he had intercourse with her; it is bidʿī, except if he knows with certainty that she is pregnant, then divorce is lawful, because the harm (maḥdhūr) is the onset of regret due to ignorance of the child. And the introduction of the husband's fluid (māʾ al-zawj) is in the meaning of intercourse (waṭʾ), because offspring is expected from it. As for intercourse in other than the [usual] place (ītān fī ghayr al-maʾtā), there is hesitation (taraddud): for although offspring is not expected from it, the ʿiddah is obligatory by it. They also hesitated over the case where he had intercourse with her during menstruation and then she became pure — whether her divorce is prohibited, because the remainder of menstruation may indicate the absence of offspring with an indication weaker than that of the beginning of menstruation. And the apparent view is that there is no innovation in her khulʿ as well, just as in the case of menstruation. Some said: The cause (sabab) here is the fear of offspring, and her consent has no effect; whereas the harm there is the prolongation of the ʿiddah, so it is not unlikely that her consent has an effect regarding her own right.

From this it emerges that five types of women have no innovation in their divorce and no Sunnah [specific to it]: the non-consummated woman, the certainly pregnant woman, the menopausal woman (āʾisah), the minor (ṣaghīrah) — for neither has menstruation nor offspring — and the woman divorced by khulʿ (mukhtalaʿah).

Section Two: On Attributing Divorce to Sunnah and Innovation, Both Immediately (tanjīzan) and Conditionally (taʿlīqan).
