chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be free, to become liberated from bondage"; also denotes "oldness" or "ancientness" (as in ʿatīq, "ancient"), and "excellence" or "nobility" (as in ʿitq al-ṭayr, "the soaring of a bird").
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential and theological usage, al-ʿitq denotes the legal removal of the bond of slavery (riqq) from a human being, thereby restoring full legal capacity (ahliyyah) and personal autonomy. It is a form of moral purification and a means of expiation (kaffārah) in many rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the physical/legal act of freeing a slave; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "freedom from" something—e.g., freedom from blame, defect, or obligation—as in "ʿatīq" for a person free from fault.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Predication (al-ḫabar al-ismī) — The phrase "الخصلة الأولى العتق" is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) where "الخصلة الأولى" is the subject (mubtadaʾ) and "العتق" is the predicate (khabar). The predicate is a single noun, not a clause, indicating a direct, unqualified identification of the first attribute with manumission.
chapters.translation: I say: The first attribute [of the one who is qualified to act as a witness or judge, or in the context of legal qualifications] is manumission (al-ʿitq) — that is, the person must be free, not a slave.

chapters.title_en: Section 417: Conditions for Valid Manumission in Expiation (Kaffārah)
chapters.arabic_text:
ولا يجزىء في الكفارات إلا رقبة مسلمة سليمة كاملة الرق تعتق بنية جازمة
عتقا خاليا عن شوب العوض فهذه خمسة شروط فلنفصلها
الشرط الأول الإسلام والمسلم كل من ولده مسلم أو مسلمة أو أسلم أحد أبويه
في صغره أو التقط في دار الإسلام أو سباه مسلم في صغره وليس معه أبواه أو
نطق بكلمتي الشهادة بعد البلوغ فلو نطق وهو صبي مميز ففيه قولان ولو نطق
مرها فهو مسلم إلا أن يكون ذميا فلا يحكم بإسلامه على أحد القولين وفيه
مسألتان
إحداهما أنه لو نطق بكلمتي الشهادة فالصحيح أنه إسلام وإن لم يصرح
بالبراءة عن سائر الملل ومنهم من شرط ذلك نعم لو اقتصر على قوله لا إله إلا
الله وكان ذلك على وفق ملته لا يحكم بإسلامه وإن كان على خلافه كالثنوي
والنصراني القائل بالتثليث فمنهم من حكم بإسلامه ثم قال يطالب بالشهادة
الثانية فإن أبى جعل مرتدا ومنهم من لم يحكم بإسلامه ما لم يأت بكلمتي
الشهادة
المسألة الثانية لو أقر بصلاة أو ركن من أركان الإسلام يخالف ملته هل
يجعل به  مسلما فيه وجهان وضابطه عند من يجعله مسلما أن كل ما يكفر المسلم
بإنكاره فيصير الكافر بالإقرار به مسلما لأن التصديق والتكذيب لا يتجزأ
ولعلنا قد استقصينا هذه الأحكام في كتاب اللقيط فلا نعيده
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يشترط الإيمان في رقبة كفارة الظهار فإن
الوارد في القرآن رقبة مطلقة ولكن عندنا يحمل المطلق على المقيد
الشرط الثاني السلامة من العيوب وعليه تنزل الرقبة المطلقة في القرآن ثم
قال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله الأقطع يجزىء والأصم والأبكم لا يجزىء وجعل الضابط
فيه زوال جنس من المنفعة لأن العيب المعتبر في البياعات لا يعتبر فاعتبر
كمال أجناس الأعضاء والمنافع والشافعي رضي الله عنه اعتبر ما يؤثر في العمل
أثرا بينا إذ غرض الإعتاق أن يستقل ويسعى لنفسه
والزمن لا يجزىء في العتق ويجزىء الأصم والأعور إذ يقدر على العمل والكسب
وكذلك الأقرع والأعرج والعنين والخصي والأقطع لا يجزىء وقطع الإبهام أو
المسبحة أو الوسطى مانع وقطع الخنصر أو البنصر لا يمنع وقطعهما جميعا مانع
إن كان من يد واحدة ومن يدين لا يؤثر وقطع أنملة لا يؤثر إلا من الإبهام
وفقد أصابع الرجل لا يؤثر
والمجنون لا يجزىء إذا كان جنونه مطبقا والمريض الذي لا يرجى زواله لا
يجزىء فإن زال على الندور فهل يتبين إجزاؤه فيه خلاف والذي يرجى زواله
يجزىء فإن مات فهل نتيقن أنه لم يقع موقعه فيه خلاف وإن كان يجن ويفيق
فيجزىء إن كان أيام الإفاقة أكثر وإلا ففيه تردد والهرم العاجز لا يجزىء
والصغير وهو ابن يوم يجزىء لأن مصيره إلى الكبر والظاهر أن الجنين لا يجزىء
وفيه وجه
وأما الأخرس فالقياس أنه يجزىء وقد اختلف فيه نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه
ومنهم من قال قولان وأجراهما في الأصم الأصلخ ومنهم من قطع بالجواز وحمل
النص على الذي لا يفهم الإشارة
الشرط الثالث كمال الرق فلا يجزىء عتق المستولدة لأنه يمتنع بيعها ولا
عتق المكاتب كتابة صحيحة لنقصان الرق ولوقوع العتق عن جهة  الكتابة بدليل
استتباع الإكساب والأولاد والمكاتب كتابة فاسدة يبتنى على العلتين إن عللنا
بنقصان الرق نفذ وإن عللنا بالاستتباع وقلنا إنه يستتبع لم ينفذ
ولو اشترى عبدا بشرط العتق وأعتقه عن الكفارة ففيه تفصيل ذكرناه في البيع
أما عتق العبد المرهون والجاني إن نفذناه فهو يجزىء عن الكفارة لأنه يفك
الرهن بخلاف الكتابة
فروع
الأول العبد الغائب الذي تتواصل أخباره يجزىء إعتاقه والمنقطع الخبر نص
على أنه لا يجزىء ونص أنه يخرج عنه زكاة الفطر فقيل هو ميل إلى الإحتياط
في المسألتين وقيل فيهما قولان لأن الأصل بقاؤه والأصل اشتغال الذمة
الثاني العبد المغصوب في يد متغلب يجزىء إعتاقه وفيه وجه أنه لا يجزىء
لأنه لا يستفيد استقلالا كاملا كالأطقع وهو أميل
الثالث إذا اشترى قريبه بنية الكفارة لم يجزئه لأن عتقه يستحق من جهة
القرابة وقال الأودني إذا اشتراه الخيار وأعتقه عن كفارته جاز
الرابع إذا أعتق نصفين من عبد في دفعتين أجزأه ولو أعتق نصفي عبدين ففيه
وجهان
أحدهما يجزىء لأن الأشقاص تجمع أشخاصا في الزكاة كذلك هذا
والثاني لا لأن المقصود إفادة الإستقلال فلا تحصل بالتجزئة نعم لو ملك
عبدين وعليه كفارتان فقال أعتقهما عن كفارتي نصف كل واحد
منهما عن كفارة فقد حكي عن نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه يجزىء فمنهم من
قال عتق العبدان عن الكفارتين ولا معنى لتجزئته وإضافته
الخامس إذا ملك المعسر نصف عبد فأعتق نصفه عن كفارته ثم اشترى النصف
الثاني وأعتق جاز لأنه كمل الخلاص وإن كان موسرا ففي كيفية نفوذ العتق
ثلاثة أقوال
فإن فرعنا على تنجز العتق نظر فإن وجه العتق على جملة العبد وقال أعتقك
عن الكفارة نفذ وأجزأ وقال القفال لا ينصرف النصف الثاني إليها لأنه عتق
بتسرية الشرع لا بإعتاقه إلا أنا نقول حصل بتسببه فصار كما لو قال إن دخلت
الدار فأنت حر عن كفارتي فدخل العبد عتق وأجزأه إن وجه على النصف لم ينصرف
النصف الباقي إلى الكفارة وهل يجزىء ذلك النصف يبتنى  على عتق الأشقاص
وإن فرعنا على أن العتق يتوقف على أداء القيمة فنوى عند اللفظ صرف النصف
وعند الأداء صرف النصف الثاني جاز وإن نوى الكل عند اللفظ ففيه وجهان
أحدهما الجواز لأنه السبب المعتق عند الأداء
والثاني أنه لا بد عند العتق من النية
وقال الشيخ أبو حامد يجب أن ينوي الكل عند اللفظ ولا يعتد بالنية عند
الأداء
الشرط الرابع أن يكون خاليا عن العوض فلو أعتق على أن يرد العبد إليه
دينارا لم يقع عن الكفارة ولو قال لغيره أعتق عبدك عن كفارتك ولك ألف علي
فأعتق نفذ لا عن الكفارة وهل يستحق الألف فيه وجهان جاريان في الإلتماس من
غير ذكر الكفارة
أحدهما لا لأن العتق وقع منه فكيف يستحق العوض
والثاني يستحق كما لو قال أعتق مستولدتك ولك علي ألف وكأن الخلاف يرجع
إلى أن الفداء هل يجوز مع إمكان هذا الشراء
وعند هذا جرت العادة بذكر النظر في التماس العتق وفيه مسائل
الأولى إذا قال أعتق مستولدتك ولك علي ألف نفذ ولزم الألف وهو افتداء
ومقابلة للمال بإسقاط الملك كما في اختلاع الأجنبي
ولو قال أعتق مستولدتك عني على ألف فقال أعتقت عنك عتقت ولغا قوله عنك
والظاهر أنه لا يستحق العوض لأنه رضي به بشرط الوقوع عنه ولم يقع وفيه وجه
أنه يستحق ويلغي قوله عني كما لو قال طلق زوجتك عني فإنه يحمل على أنه أراد
طلقها لأجلي فيستحق الزوج العوض
واعلم أن حكم الشافعي رضي الله عنه بنفوذ العتق في المستولدة مع قوله
أعتقت عنك يدل على أنه إذا وصف العتق أو الطلاق بوصف محال يلغي الوصف دون
الأصل
الثانية إذا قال أعتق عبدك عني فقال أعتقت وقع عن المستدعي ثم إن ذكر
عوضا استحقه وإن لم يذكر فهل يستحق فيه وجهان
أحدهما لا يستحق بل يحمل على الهبة
والثاني أنه يستحق كما لو قال اقض ديني فإنه يرجع على رأي ولكن هذا
التوجيه إنما يستقيم إذا قال أعتق عن كفارتي  فإنه أداء حق مستحق
ولو صرح وقال أعتقه عني مجانا فقال أعتقت نفذ ولا عوض وقال أبو حنيفة
رحمه الله لا ينفذ لأن الملك لا يحصل في الهبة دون القبض ولكن قال بعض
الأصحاب إعتاقه تسليط تام أقوى من الإقباض وبنوا عليه أنه لو وهب ثم قال
للمتهب أعتقه عن نفسك فأعتق نفذ عتقه من غير قبض
أما إذا أطلق وقال أعتق عبدك ولم يقل عني أو عنك فأعتق فعلى ماذا ينزل
فيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه عن المستدعي بقرينة الإستدعاء
والثاني أنه كقوله أعتق عن نفسك حتى يخرج النظر في العوض على ما ذكرناه
الثالثة إذا قال إذا جاء الغد فعبدي حر عنك بألف فقال قبلت فهذا كتعليق
الخلع وقد ذكرناه ولو قال أعتق عبدك عني غدا بألف فصبر حتى جاء الغد وقال
أعتقت قال صاحب التقريب ها هنا يستحق المسمى لأنه ليس تعليقا وفيه نظر أيضا
ذكرناه في الخلع ولو قال أعتقه عني على خمر أو مغصوب فهو كالخلع على
المغصوب ويحتمل ها هنا الفساد في العوض وإن كان الملك
يحصل للمستدعي لأنه ملك ضمني فلا تعتبر شروطه وينظر إلى صورة الإعتاق
ولذلك لم يشترط القبض في الإعتاق مجانا
فإن قيل العتق يحصل متصلا بآخر قوله أعتقت فالملك كيف يحصل قبله فيكون قد
حصل قبل اللفظ أو كيف يحصل بعده فيكون متأخرا عن العتق أو معه فيكون مع
العتق والكل محال قلنا ذكر فيه خمسة أوجه
أحدها أنا نتبين حصوله بعد الإلتماس وقبل الإجابة
والثاني أنه يتبين حصوله عند الشروع في اللفظ وهما بعيدان لأنه تقديم
المسبب على السبب
والثالث أنه يحصل الملك مع آخر أجزاء اللفظ والعتق مرتبا عليه
والرابع أنه يحصل مرتبا على اللفظ والعتق يتأخر لحظة
والخامس وهو اختيار أبي إسحاق رحمه الله أن الملك والعتق يترتب
على اللفظ معا واستبعد ذلك منه ونسب إلى الجمع بين المتضادين ولعله يعني
أنه جرى سبب الملك والعتق في حالة واحدة فيندفع الملك في وقت جريان سببه
ويكون ذلك  في معنى الإنقطاع ولهذا غور ذكرناه من قبل
وبالجملة فقد اختلفوا في أن كل حكم يترتب على لفظ فيكون مع آخر جزء من
اللفظ أو متأخرا مترتبا عليه ترتب الضد على زوال الضد والأصح أنه مع آخر
جزء من اللفظ لأن المعلول ينبغي أن يكون مع العلة كما ذكرناه
الشرط الخامس النية ولا بد منها لأن الكفارة فيها مشابه العبادات نعم
تصح من الذمي والمرتد إذا قلنا لا يزول ملكه أو يستثنى قدر الكفارة عن
ملكه الزائل كما نستثني قدر الدين ولا تصح النية منهما ولكن يستقل بمشابه
الغرامات فإن فيها شبه الغرامات أما صوم الكفارة فلا يصح منهما لأنه عبادة
محضة كالزكاة فلذلك لا يتصور من كافر
فرع لا يشترط تعيين النية في الكفارات عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
فلو كان عليه الكفارات فيكفيه أن ينوي الإعتاق عن الكفارة لأن تعيين
النية عندنا يجب قصدا إلى التقرب بالصفات المقصودة في العبادات المختلفة
المراتب ومرتبة الظهر تغاير مرتبة الصبح وكذلك صوم رمضان يغاير صوم النذر
ولا تفاوت في الكفارات كما لا تفاوت في زكاة أعيان الأموال فالأموال أسباب
الزكاة والجنايات أسباب الكفارات وهي متفاوتة وقد طردوا هذا في العتق
الملتزم بالنذر مع
الكفارة وإن كان النذر قربة والكفارة سببها جريمة ولكن لم يلتفت إلى هذا
نعم إذا أعتق في الكفارة وأخطأ لم يجزئه فإذا كان عليه كفارة قتل فنوى
الظهار لم يقع عن القتل وقد صرفه عنه وعليه الإعادة وهو كتعيين الإمامة في
القدوة ولا تشترط ولكن لو أخطأ فسدت القدوة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be free" or "to become free" from bondage; the root denotes liberation from servitude, whether physical or metaphorical.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, ʿitq (manumission) is a legal act of freeing a slave, which in the context of kaffārah (expiation) serves as a means of spiritual purification and reparation for a transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it refers to the physical act of freeing a slave; metaphorically, it can denote liberation from sin or blame, but in jurisprudential context, it is strictly literal (ḥaqīqah).
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root signifies "to cover" or "to conceal"; in legal terms, kaffārah is an act that "covers" or "expiates" a sin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kaffārah is a divinely ordained compensatory act, such as freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor, to atone for specific violations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally as a legal term for expiation; metaphorical usage is absent in juristic discourse.
- Root: ر-ق-ب-ة (r-q-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Literally means "neck"; in legal terminology, it denotes a slave (as a whole person), emphasizing the entirety of the individual.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and legal contexts, it refers to a slave who is to be freed, with conditions of soundness and completeness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for a slave; no metaphorical extension in this context.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition (Sharṭ) and Qualified (Manʿūt) — The sentence structure "لا يجزىء إلا رقبة مسلمة سليمة" employs an exception (istithnāʾ) with "إلا", which restricts the general rule, requiring precise parsing to identify the excluded and included elements.
chapters.translation:
I say: In expiations (kaffārāt), nothing suffices except a Muslim slave, sound, complete in servitude, freed with a firm intention, and manumission free from any taint of compensation. These are five conditions; let us detail them.

**The First Condition: Islam (al-Islām)**
A Muslim is anyone born to a Muslim father or mother, or one whose parent embraced Islam during his minority, or a foundling (laqīṭ) picked up in the Abode of Islam (Dār al-Islām), or a captive taken by a Muslim during his minority without his parents, or one who utters the two testimonies of faith (shahādatayn) after reaching puberty. If a discerning child (ṣabī mumayyiz) utters them, there are two opinions (qawlān). If one utters them under duress, he is a Muslim, except if he is a dhimmī (protected non-Muslim), in which case his Islam is not judged valid according to one of the two opinions. There are two sub-issues here:

**First Sub-Issue:** If he utters the two testimonies, the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that he becomes a Muslim, even if he does not explicitly disavow other religions. Some scholars stipulated that disavowal. However, if he limits himself to saying "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh) and this conforms to his own creed, he is not judged a Muslim. If it contradicts his creed—such as a dualist (thanawī) or a Christian who professes the Trinity—some scholars judge him a Muslim, then say he is demanded to utter the second testimony; if he refuses, he is deemed an apostate (murtadd). Others do not judge him a Muslim until he utters both testimonies.

**Second Sub-Issue:** If he acknowledges a prayer (ṣalāh) or a pillar of Islam that contradicts his creed, is he thereby deemed a Muslim? There are two faces (wajhān). The controlling principle (ḍābiṭ) for those who deem him a Muslim is that whatever makes a Muslim an unbeliever by denying it, a non-Muslim becomes a Muslim by affirming it, because affirmation (taṣdīq) and denial (takdhīb) are indivisible. Perhaps we have exhaustively covered these rulings in the Book of the Foundling (Kitāb al-Laqīṭ), so we shall not repeat them.

Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Faith (īmān) is not a condition for the slave in the expiation of ẓihār (injurious comparison), for the Quranic text mentions an absolute slave (raqabah muṭlaqah). But in our view, the absolute is restricted by the qualified (al-muṭlaq yuḥmal ʿalā al-muqayyad).

**The Second Condition: Soundness from Defects (al-Salāmah min al-ʿUyūb)**
Upon this, the absolute slave in the Quran is interpreted. Then Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The amputee (aqṭaʿ) suffices, but the deaf (aṣamm) and the mute (abkam) do not. He made the controlling principle the loss of a category of benefit (jins min al-manfaʿah), because defects considered in sales are not considered here; rather, the completeness of the categories of limbs and benefits is considered. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) considered what affects work with a clear effect, for the purpose of manumission is that the slave becomes independent and strives for himself.

The chronically ill (zamin) does not suffice in manumission, but the deaf and the one-eyed (aʿwar) suffice, as they are capable of work and earning. Likewise, the bald (aqraʿ), the lame (aʿraj), the impotent (ʿanīn), and the eunuch (khaṣī) suffice. The amputee does not suffice. The cutting off of the thumb, index finger, or middle finger is a preventive defect; the cutting off of the little finger or ring finger is not preventive. The cutting off of both (little and ring fingers) from one hand is preventive, but from both hands it has no effect. The cutting off of a phalanx (anmulah) has no effect, except from the thumb. The loss of toes has no effect.

The insane (majnūn) does not suffice if his insanity is continuous (muṭbiq). The sick person whose recovery is not hoped for does not suffice; if recovery occurs rarely, there is a dispute (khilāf) as to whether his sufficiency becomes evident. The one whose recovery is hoped for suffices; if he dies, there is a dispute as to whether we are certain that it did not take effect. If he alternates between insanity and lucidity, he suffices if the days of lucidity are more numerous; otherwise, there is hesitation (taraddud). The decrepit elderly person (harim) who is incapable does not suffice. The young child, even a day old, suffices, because his end is to grow up. The apparent view is that a fetus does not suffice, though there is a face (wajh) [that it does].

As for the mute (akhras), the analogy (qiyās) is that he suffices. There is a difference of opinion regarding the text (naṣṣ) of al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him). Some say there are two opinions (qawlān), applying them to the profoundly deaf (aṣamm aṣlakh). Others definitively rule permissibility and interpret the text as referring to one who does not understand gestures (ishārah).

**The Third Condition: Completeness of Servitude (Kamāl al-Riqq)**
The manumission of a umm walad (slave mother of a master's child) does not suffice, because her sale is prohibited. Nor does the manumission of a mukātib (slave under a contract of manumission) with a valid kitābah (manumission contract) suffice, due to the deficiency of servitude and because the manumission occurs by virtue of the kitābah, as evidenced by the inclusion of earnings and offspring. For a mukātib with an invalid kitābah, the ruling is built upon the two causes (ʿillatayn): if we reason by the deficiency of servitude, it takes effect; if we reason by inclusion (istitbāʿ) and say it includes, it does not take effect.

If one buys a slave with the condition of manumission and frees him for the expiation, there is a detailed ruling we mentioned in the Book of Sales. As for the manumission of a pledged slave (al-ʿabd al-marhūn) or a criminal slave (al-jānī), if we deem it effective, it suffices for the expiation, because it releases the pledge (fakk al-rahn), unlike the kitābah.

**Branches (Furūʿ)**

**First:** A distant slave whose news continues to arrive suffices for manumission. For one whose news is cut off (munqaṭiʿ al-khabar), the text states it does not suffice, and the text states that zakāt al-fiṭr is paid on his behalf. It is said this is an inclination toward caution (iḥtiyāṭ) in both matters. It is also said there are two opinions in both, because the principle is his continued existence and the principle is the liability of the debt.

**Second:** A usurped slave (al-ʿabd al-maghṣūb) in the hands of a tyrant suffices for manumission. There is a face that it does not suffice, because he does not gain complete independence, like the amputee. This latter is more inclined (amīl).

**Third:** If one buys his relative with the intention of expiation, it does not suffice, because his manumission is obligatory by virtue of kinship. Al-Awdanī said: If a free man (al-khiyār) buys him and frees him for his expiation, it is permissible.

**Fourth:** If one frees two halves of a slave in two separate acts, it suffices. If one frees halves of two different slaves, there are two faces:
- One: It suffices, because fractions are combined into persons in zakāh; likewise here.
- Two: It does not suffice, because the goal is to grant independence, which is not achieved by fractioning. However, if one owns two slaves and owes two expiations, and says: "I free both for my expiation, half of each for one expiation," it is reported from the text of al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) that it suffices. Some say the freeing of both slaves is for the two expiations, and there is no meaning to fractioning and assigning.

**Fifth:** If an insolvent (muʿsir) owns half of a slave and frees his half for his expiation, then buys the other half and frees it, it is permissible, because the liberation is completed. If he is wealthy (mūsir), there are three opinions (aqwāl) regarding the modality of the manumission's effectiveness:
- If we base it on the immediate effectiveness of manumission (tanajjuz al-ʿitq), then if he directed the manumission at the whole slave and said: "I free you for the expiation," it takes effect and suffices. Al-Qaffāl said: The second half does not apply to it, because it is freed by the legal extension (tasriyah al-sharʿ), not by his manumission. But we say it occurred by his causation, so it is as if he said: "If you enter the house, you are free for my expiation," and the slave entered, he is freed and it suffices. If he directed it at the half, the remaining half does not apply to the expiation. Whether that half suffices is built upon the manumission of fractions.
- If we base it on the manumission being suspended upon payment of the value (qīmah), then if he intended at the utterance to apply the half, and at payment to apply the second half, it is permissible. If he intended the whole at the utterance, there are two faces:
  - One: Permissibility, because it is the cause that frees at payment.
  - Two: Intention is required at the time of manumission.
- Shaykh Abū Ḥāmid said: He must intend the whole at the utterance, and intention at payment is not counted.

**The Fourth Condition: Freedom from Compensation (al-Khalāṣ ʿan al-ʿAwaḍ)**
If he frees a slave on condition that the slave returns a dinar to him, it does not count for the expiation. If he says to another: "Free your slave for your expiation, and I owe you a thousand," and he frees him, it takes effect but not for the expiation. Whether he deserves the thousand has two faces, parallel to those in requesting manumission without mentioning the expiation:
- One: No, because the manumission was from him, so how can he deserve compensation?
- Two: Yes, as if he said: "Free your umm walad, and I owe you a thousand." The dispute seems to revert to whether ransom (fidāʾ) is permissible when this purchase is possible.

At this point, it is customary to mention the examination of requesting manumission (iltimās al-ʿitq). It contains several issues:

**First:** If he says: "Free your umm walad, and I owe you a thousand," it takes effect and the thousand is obligatory. This is a ransom (iftidāʾ) and a exchange of wealth for the relinquishment of ownership, as in the khulʿ (divorce by compensation) by a third party. If he says: "Free your umm walad on my behalf for a thousand," and he says: "I freed her on your behalf," she is freed, and his words "on your behalf" are void (laghw). The apparent view is that he does not deserve the compensation, because he consented to it conditionally upon its occurrence on his behalf, and it did not occur. There is a face that he deserves it, and his words "on my behalf" are void, as if he said: "Divorce your wife on my behalf," for it is interpreted as meaning "divorce her for my sake," and the husband deserves the compensation.

Know that al-Shāfiʿī's (may Allah be pleased with him) ruling of the effectiveness of manumission in the umm walad with his saying "I freed her on your behalf" indicates that when manumission or divorce is described with an impossible description, the description is void, not the original act.

**Second:** If he says: "Free your slave on my behalf," and he says: "I freed him," it occurs on behalf of the requester (al-mustadʿī). Then if he mentions compensation, he deserves it. If he does not mention it, does he deserve it? Two faces:
- One: He does not deserve it; rather, it is interpreted as a gift (hibah).
- Two: He deserves it, as if he said: "Pay my debt," for he can reclaim it on one view. But this justification is only sound if he said: "Free him for my expiation," for it is the performance of an obligatory right.
If he explicitly says: "Free him on my behalf gratuitously (majjānan)," and he says: "I freed him," it takes effect with no compensation. Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It does not take effect, because ownership is not established in a gift without possession (qabḍ). But some companions said: His manumission is a complete empowerment (taslīṭ tāmm), stronger than handing over (iqbāḍ). They built upon this that if one gifts a slave, then says to the recipient: "Free him on your own behalf," and he frees him, his manumission takes effect without possession.

As for when he says absolutely: "Free your slave," without saying "on my behalf" or "on your behalf," and he frees him, upon what is it interpreted? Two faces:
- One: It is on behalf of the requester, by the indication of the request (qarīnat al-istidʿāʾ).
- Two: It is like his saying "Free him on your own behalf," so the examination of compensation proceeds as we mentioned.

**Third:** If he says: "When tomorrow comes, my slave is free on your behalf for a thousand," and he says: "I accept," this is like a suspended khulʿ, which we have mentioned. If he says: "Free your slave on my behalf tomorrow for a thousand," and he waits until tomorrow comes and says: "I freed him," the author of al-Taqrīb said: Here he deserves the named amount, because it is not a suspension. There is also a consideration (naẓar) here, which we mentioned in khulʿ. If he says: "Free him on my behalf for wine or a usurped item," it is like khulʿ for a usurped item. It is possible here that the compensation is corrupt (fasād), even though ownership is established for the requester, because it is a derivative ownership (milk ḍimnī), so its conditions are not considered; rather, one looks at the form of manumission. For this reason, possession was not required in gratuitous manumission.

If it is said: Manumission occurs connected to the last part of his utterance "I freed him," so how can ownership occur before it—thus it would occur before the utterance—or how can it occur after it—thus it would be delayed from the manumission—or with it—thus it would be simultaneous with the manumission—and all are impossible? We say: Five faces are mentioned regarding this:
- **One:** We ascertain its occurrence after the request and before the response.
- **Two:** We ascertain its occurrence at the commencement of the utterance. Both are far-fetched, because it is the precedence of the effect over the cause.
- **Three:** Ownership occurs with the last part of the utterance, with manumission ordered upon it.
- **Four:** Ownership occurs ordered upon the utterance, and manumission is delayed for a moment.
- **Five:** This is the choice of Abū Isḥāq (may Allah have mercy on him): that ownership and manumission are both ordered upon the utterance simultaneously. This was deemed far-fetched from him and attributed to combining two contradictories. Perhaps he meant that the causes of ownership and manumission run in a single state, so ownership is repelled at the time its cause runs, and this is in the sense of interruption (inqiṭāʿ). This is why we mentioned this consideration before.

In sum, they differed over whether every ruling ordered upon an utterance occurs with the last part of the utterance or is delayed, ordered upon it like the ordering of a contrary upon the removal of its contrary. The more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that it occurs with the last part of the utterance, because the effect should be simultaneous with the cause, as we mentioned.

**The Fifth Condition: Intention (al-Niyyah)**
It is indispensable, because the expiation has a resemblance to acts of worship (ʿibādāt). However, it is valid from a dhimmī and an apostate (murtadd) if we say his ownership does not lapse, or we exempt the amount of the expiation from his lapsed ownership, just as we exempt the amount of debt. But intention from them is not valid; rather, it stands alone in its resemblance to indemnities (gharāmāt), for it contains a resemblance to indemnities. As for the fast of expiation, it is not valid from them, because it is a pure act of worship, like zakāh; therefore, it is not conceivable from a disbeliever.

**Branch:** Specification of intention (taʿyīn al-niyyah) is not required in expiations in our view, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him). If one owes multiple expiations, it suffices for him to intend manumission for the expiation, because in our view, specification of intention is required only for the purpose of drawing near through the intended qualities in acts of worship of different ranks. The rank of ẓuhr differs from the rank of ṣubḥ, and likewise the fast of Ramaḍān differs from the fast of a vow (nadhr). There is no difference among expiations, just as there is no difference among the zakāh of specific wealth categories. Wealth is the cause of zakāh, and offenses are the causes of expiations, and they are differentiated. They extended this to manumission obligated by a vow along with the expiation, even though the vow is an act of devotion and the expiation's cause is an offense; but this was not heeded. However, if he frees for an expiation and errs, it does not suffice. If he owes an expiation for killing (qatl) and intends ẓihār, it does not count for the killing; he has diverted it from it, and he must repeat. This is like specifying the imam in following (iqtidāʾ): it is not required, but if one errs, the following is invalidated.

chapters.title_en: The Second Attribute: Fasting (al-Ṣiyām)
chapters.arabic_text: ### | الخصلة الثانية الصيام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "abstention" (imsāk) — from the root denoting cessation and restraint, whether from food, speech, or movement; al-ʿAyn notes it applies to any act of withholding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law (sharʿ), ṣiyām is the specific abstention from appetitive acts (shahawāt) and other specified nullifiers during daylight hours, with the intention (niyyah) of drawing near to God — a technical narrowing of the linguistic sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is general abstention; the juristic sense is a metaphorical (majāz) specialization, since the term is transferred from its broad root to a defined ritual act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naʿt-ʿAṭf (Attributive Coordination) — The phrase "الخصلة الثانية" (the second attribute) functions as a definite noun phrase with an ordinal adjective, governing the following genitive construct; the section heading operates as a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) with an implied predicate, establishing a new topic in the structured legal compendium.
chapters.translation: I say: The second attribute [of the pillars of Islam] is fasting (al-ṣiyām).

chapters.title_en: Section 419: On the Substitutes for Manumission in Expiation and the Rulings of Fasting
chapters.arabic_text:
وفيه نظران
الأول فيما يجوز العدول إليه ولا يعتبر عندنا عجز محقق عن الإعتاق بل
يكفي أن يعسر ذلك عليه لغرض معتبر معتد به والذي لا يملك شيئا لا يخفى أمره
أما إن ملك عبدا أو مسكنا أو مالا ففيه نظر فنقول إن كان زمنا وهو محتاج
إلى العبد لخدمته أو كان منصبه يقتضي أن يخدم ولا يباشر الأعمال بنفسه
فيجوز له الصوم عندنا خلافا  لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
وإن كان عبده نفيسا يمكن إبداله بعبدين يلزمه ذلك إلا إذا كان قد ألف
العبد وارتضاه من زمان فإنه يعسر عليه الإبدال فلا يلزمه وفيه وجه أنه
يلزمه ذلك ولا يعتبر الإلف
أما المسكن فلا يباع إلا إذا كان فضلا عن مقدار حاجته لاتساع خطته وأمكنه
بيع بعضه فإن كان بيتا نفيسا وأمكن إبداله بمثليه فهو كالعبد النفيس
المألوف لأن الجلاء عن المسكن أيضا شديد ففيه وجهان
أما المال إذا ملكه زائدا عن المسكن واللباس والأثاث المحتاج إليه فيصرف
إلى العتق إلا إذا كان رأس ماله أو ضيعة لو باعها لصار مسكينا يحل له سهم
المساكين فالإنتقال إلى حال المسكنة أشد من الإنتقال من دار أو عبد فقياس
قول الأصحاب أنه لا يكلف ذلك ويكاد يخالف هذا قوله تعالى {فمن لم يجد
فصيام} ولكن توسع الأصحاب في هذا لأن صوم شهرين يكاد يكون أشق من إعتاق عبد
وليس بينهما كبير تفاوت وليس كذلك زكاة الفطر فإنه يصرف إليه كل ما فضل عن
قوت اليوم لأنه أصل وتركه إبطال لا إبدال
أما إذا كان له مال غائب فلا يجوز له الصوم لأن الكفارة على التراخي
ويمكن أداؤها عنه بعد موته بخلاف قضاء الصلاة فإنه تجوز بالتيمم مع توقع
الماء في ثاني الحال لأن الموت متوقع في كل حال فإن قيل فيعتبر إعساره عند
الوجوب أو الأداء قلنا فيه ثلاثة أقوال
أحدها أنه يعتبر حالة الوجوب تغليبا لمشابه العقوبات فعلى هذا لو كان
معسرا ثم أيسر وأعتق جاز بطريق الأولى وذكر صاحب التقريب وجها أنه لا يجوز
لأن هذا الترتيب بعيد وإلا فالصوم أشق وهو بعيد إذ المعسر لو تكلف الإعتاق
فلا ينبغي أن يمنع نعم ذكر وجهان في العبد إذا أعتق قبل الصوم وأيسر أنه هل
يعتق لأنه لم يكن أهلا لوجوب العتق في الإبتداء وهذا منقدح
القول الثاني أنه يعتبر حالة الأداء تشبيها بالعبادات إذ يعتبر في القعود
في الصلاة وفي التيمم حالة الأداء وهذا مذهب  أبي حنيفة رحمه الله
وعلى هذا لو شرع في الصوم ثم أيسر لا يقطع عليه لأنه إذا شرع في البدل
فقد استقر الأمر كالمتيمم إذا وجد الماء بعد الشروع في الصلاة وقال أبو
حنيفة رحمه الله والمزني لا مبالاة بالشروع بل يستقر الأمر بالفراغ لأن
وزان الشروع في الصوم الشروع في التيمم دون الصلاة وعندهما تنتقض الصلاة
برؤية الماء
ومن اصحابنا من وافق المزني ها هنا فعلى هذا القول نقول الواجب الصوم
بشرط أن يستمر الإعسار إلى الفراغ
القول الثالث أنه يعتبر أغلظ الحالتين فإذا أيسر عند الأداء أو عند
الوجوب لزم العتق احتياطا وعلى هذا لو كان معسرا في الطرفين وتخلل اليسار
لم يؤثر فكأن ما اقتضاه حالة الوجوب لا يغيره إلا حالة الأداء
وأما العبد فمعسر وكفارته بالصوم وأما الإطعام والعتق فيبنى على أنه هل
يملك بالتمليك والعتق أولى بأن يمتنع عليه والصحيح أنه لا يملك بالتمليك
ثم إن العبد لا يصوم إلا بإذن السيد إلا إذا حلف وحنث بإذنه فإن حلف
بإذنه وحنث بغير إذنه لم يصم وإن حلف بغير إذنه وحنث بإذنه فوجهان وإنما
يعتبر إذنه لأن حق السيد على الفور والصوم على التراخي بخلاف شهر رمضان
وأما من نصفه حر ونصفه عبد فهو كالأحرار في الكفارة وكالعبيد في الجمعة
والشهادة والولاية وصدقة فطره تتوزع على الرق والحرية
النظر الثاني في حكم الصوم
وفيه مسائل
إحداها أنه يجب عليه تبييت النية ولا يجب تعيين جهة الكفارة نعم ينوي صوم
الكفارة وهل ينوي التتابع فيه وجهان فإن قلنا ينوي يكفيه ذلك في الليلة
الأولى أو يجددها كل ليلة فيه وجهان وإذا مات لم يصم
عنه وليه على الصحيح
الثانية يصوم شهرين بالأهلة فإن ابتدأ في أثناء شهر صام الشهر الثاني
بالهلال وكمل الشهر الأول ثلاثين من الشهر الثالث خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه
الله
الثالثة لا بد من التتابع في كفارة الظهار والوقاع والقتل فلو أفسد اليوم
الأخير أو نسي النية فيه وجب استئناف الكل وهل يفسد ما  مضى أو ينقلب نفلا
فيه وفي نظائره قولان
أما إذا وطىء المظاهر ليلا لم يفسد تتابعه ولكنه يعصي إذ التتابع قائم
والتقديم على الوطء قد فات وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يستأنف
الرابعة الحيض لا يقطع التتابع والمرض الذي يبيح مثله الإفطار فيه قولان
مشهوران
أحدهما أنه لا يقطع التتابع لأنه لا يزيد وصف التتابع على وصف شهر رمضان
والثاني أنه يقطع لأن تدارك التتابع ها هنا ممكن بخلاف وصف رمضان
وفي السفر قولان مرتبان وأولى بأن يقطع لأنه منوط بالإختيار ولو قيل إنه
لا يقطع على بعد فلا يبعد أن يجزىء فيما إذا نسي النية ولا قائل به لأنه
مقصر بالنسيان ولذلك يلزمه الإمساك دون الحائض والمسافر إذا زال عذرهما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-س-ر (ʿ-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Difficulty, straitness, hardship; the opposite of ease (yusr). A "muʿsir" is one constrained by poverty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, it denotes a genuine incapacity that alters obligation, distinct from mere preference.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in financial contexts (paucity of means); metaphorical when applied to psychological or social burden (e.g., attachment to property).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Embedded Exception (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "إلا إذا" introduces a restrictive condition that suspends the general ruling, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: In this matter there are two points of investigation.

The first concerns what it is permissible to deviate to [i.e., fasting instead of manumission]. With us [the Shafiʿites], a verified incapacity for manumission is not required; rather, it suffices that manumission be difficult for him due to a considered and weighty purpose. As for one who owns nothing, his case is obvious.

However, if he owns a slave, a dwelling, or wealth, then there is investigation. We say: If he is chronically ill (zamin) and needs the slave for his service, or if his station requires that he be served and not perform tasks himself, then fasting is permissible for him — contrary to Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him).

If his slave is precious and can be exchanged for two slaves, then he is obligated to do so — unless he has become attached to the slave and has been pleased with him for a long time, for then exchange would be difficult for him, and it is not incumbent upon him. There is a face (wajh) that it is incumbent upon him and that attachment is not considered.

As for the dwelling, it is not sold unless it exceeds his need due to the vastness of his plot, and he can sell part of it. If it is a precious house and can be exchanged for two like it, then it is like the precious, beloved slave — because relocation from a dwelling is also severe. Thus there are two faces.

As for wealth: if he owns it in excess of the dwelling, clothing, and furnishings he needs, it is directed toward manumission — unless it is his capital (raʾs māl) or an estate (ḍayʿah) such that if he sold it, he would become a pauper eligible for the share of the poor. For transitioning to the state of pauperism is more severe than transitioning from a house or a slave. Thus, by the analogy of the companions' doctrine, he is not burdened with that. This nearly contradicts the saying of Allah the Exalted: {فمن لم يجد فصيام} "And whoever does not find [a slave], then a fast..." — but the companions expanded [the concession] here because fasting two months is nearly more arduous than manumitting a slave, and there is no great disparity between them. This is not so with the alms of breaking the fast (zakāt al-fiṭr), for everything exceeding one day's sustenance is directed to it, because it is a foundational obligation; abandoning it is nullification, not substitution.

If he has wealth that is absent (ghāʾib), he may not fast, because the expiation is deferred (ʿalā al-tarākhī) and can be discharged on his behalf after his death — unlike the make-up of prayer, which permits tayammum even while hoping for water in the immediate future, because death is anticipated in every state.

If it is said: Is his incapacity considered at the time of obligation or at the time of performance? We say: There are three sayings.

One: It is considered at the time of obligation, giving preponderance to the resemblance of punishments. On this basis, if he was incapacitated, then became wealthy and manumitted, it is valid a fortiori. The author of al-Taqrīb mentioned a face that it is not valid, because this sequence is remote — otherwise fasting would be more arduous, which is remote, for if the incapacitated one burdens himself with manumission, he should not be prevented. Yes, two faces are mentioned regarding the slave: if he manumitted before fasting and then became wealthy, is it valid? Because he was not qualified for the obligation of manumission at the outset. This is plausible.

The second saying: It is considered at the time of performance, by analogy to acts of worship — for sitting in prayer and tayammum are considered at the time of performance. This is the doctrine of Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him). On this basis, if he began fasting and then became wealthy, he is not interrupted, because once he has begun the substitute, the matter is settled — like the one performing tayammum who finds water after beginning the prayer. Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) and al-Muzanī said: Beginning is of no consequence; rather, the matter is settled upon completion, because the analogue of beginning the fast is beginning the tayammum, not the prayer — and in their view, the prayer is invalidated by seeing water. Some of our companions agreed with al-Muzanī here. On this saying, we say: The obligatory act is fasting, conditioned upon the continuance of incapacity until completion.

The third saying: The more stringent of the two states is considered. If he becomes wealthy at performance or at obligation, manumission becomes incumbent as a precaution. On this basis, if he was incapacitated at both ends but wealth intervened in between, it has no effect — as if what the state of obligation required is not altered except by the state of performance.

As for the slave: he is incapacitated, and his expiation is by fasting. As for feeding and manumission, they are built upon whether he owns property through gift (tamlīk) — and manumission is more apt to be prevented from him. The correct view is that he does not own through gift.

Then, the slave does not fast except with the master's permission — unless he swore an oath and broke it with his permission. If he swore with permission and broke without permission, he does not fast. If he swore without permission and broke with permission, there are two faces. Permission is only considered because the master's right is immediate (ʿalā al-fawr), while fasting is deferred — unlike Ramadan.

As for one who is half-free and half-slave: he is like the free in expiation, and like slaves in Friday prayer, testimony, and guardianship. His alms of breaking the fast are apportioned between slavery and freedom.

The second point of investigation concerns the rulings of the fast itself.

In it are several issues:

First: He must intend during the night (tabyīt al-niyyah), but he need not specify the type of expiation. Rather, he intends "the fast of expiation." Whether he must intend consecutiveness (tadbīj) — there are two faces. If we say he must intend it, does it suffice in the first night, or must he renew it every night? There are two faces. If he dies, his guardian does not fast on his behalf — this is the correct view.

Second: He fasts two months by the lunar months. If he begins mid-month, he fasts the second month by the crescent, and completes the first month to thirty days from the third month — contrary to Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him).

Third: Consecutiveness is required in the expiation of ẓihār, intercourse [in Ramadan], and killing. If he invalidates the last day or forgets the intention therein, he must restart the entire [period]. Whether what passed is invalidated or converted to supererogatory — there are two sayings on this and its analogues.

As for the one who commits ẓihār and then has intercourse at night: it does not break his consecutiveness, but he sins — because consecutiveness remains, though the precedence of intercourse [before the expiation] has been lost. Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: He must restart.

Fourth: Menstruation does not break consecutiveness. As for illness that permits breaking the fast — there are two well-known sayings:
One: It does not break consecutiveness, because the attribute of consecutiveness does not exceed the attribute of Ramadan.
The second: It breaks it, because repairing consecutiveness here is possible, unlike the attribute of Ramadan.

Regarding travel, there are two ordered sayings — and it is more apt to break consecutiveness, because it is tied to choice. If it were said it does not break it, that is remote. It is not far that it suffices in the case of forgetting the intention — but no one holds this, because he is negligent in forgetting, and therefore he must refrain [from eating] — unlike the menstruating woman and the traveler when their excuses cease.

chapters.title_en: Section 420 — The Third Characteristic: Feeding (al-Iṭʿām); and the Book of Mutual Cursing (al-Liʿān)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو أرادت الحائض أن تفطر ثم بعد الطهر تستأنف شهرين ففيه إحباط لوصف
الفرضية من الصوم السابق فهذا فيه احتمال والأظهر جوازه لأنه على التراخي
وما مضى لا يفسد وكانت الفرضية موقوفة على الفراغ

### | الخصلة الثالثة الإطعام

ويعدل إليه العاجز عن الصوم بالهرم والمرض الذي يدوم شهرين وليس توقع
الصحة بعده كتوقع رجوع المال الغائب بعد شهرين لأن من له مال غائب يسمى
واجدا وهذا يسمى عاجزا في الحال وفي انتقال المسافر إلى الإطعام تردد
وأما الشبق المفرط فالظاهر أنه لا يرخص في العدول إلى الإطعام وهو القياس
وفيه وجه يستند إلى حديث الأعرابي وقد ذكرنا إشكاله في الصوم
والنظر بعد هذا في قدر المخرج وجنسه والمخرج إليه والإخراج
أما جنس المخرج فهو كزكاة الفطر وأما قدره فستون مدا
وأما المخرج إليه فالمسكين الذي يجوز صرف الزكاة إليه ولا يجوز عندنا أن
يصرف إلى مسكين واحد ستين مدا في ستين يوما خلافا لأبي حنيفة
رحمه الله فلا بد من رعاية عدد المساكين لظاهر الآية وأما الإخراج فهو
التمليك والتسليط التام فلا يكفي التغدية والتعشية بتقديم التمر إلى
المساكين
= كتاب اللعان=
واللعان عبارة عن أيمان يذكر اللعن فيها من نسب زوجته إلى الزنا فيدرأ
الحد والنسب عن نفسه بمجرد  يمينه وذلك رخصة لمسيس الحاجة إلى صيانة الأنساب
وعسر إقامة البينة على زنا المرأة
وردت أولا في عويمر بن مالك العجلاني قذف زوجته بشريك بن السحماء
فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
لتأتين بأربعة شهداء أو لأجلدن ظهرك فاغتم وقال أرجو أن ينزل الله قرآنا
يبرىء ظهري فنزل قوله تعالى {والذين يرمون أزواجهم} الآية
ونظر الكتاب في قسمين القذف واللعان

### | القسم الأول في القذف

وفيه بابان - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول فيما يكون قذفا من كافة
الخلق وفي موجبه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وفيه فصلان

### | الفصل الأول في ألفاظ القذف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط ع م (ṭ-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to feed" or "to provide sustenance"; al-ṭaʿām is food, and al-iṭʿām is the act of giving food.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential context, al-iṭʿām as expiation (kaffārah) or substitute for fasting denotes a transfer of nutritive ownership, not mere presentation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is actual feeding; metaphorical (majāz) would be any form of provision, but here the literal act of ownership-transfer is intended.
- Root: ل ع ن (l-ʿ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "to curse" or "to banish from mercy"; al-liʿān is the mutual cursing between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Quranic context, al-liʿān is a solemn oath-ritual (mubāhalah) invoking divine curse to establish truth in accusations of adultery.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is the invocation of curse; metaphorical usage extends to the entire legal procedure of mutual imprecation.
- Root: ق ذ ف (q-dh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to throw" or "to hurl"; technically, it is the false accusation of fornication (qadhf).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, qadhf is a specific ḥadd offense requiring proof or prescribed punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical throwing; metaphorical is the verbal casting of accusation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Suspended Judgment (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In "لو أرادت الحائض أن تفطر" (If a menstruating woman intended to break her fast), the protasis (sharṭ) is followed by an apodosis (jawāb) that is grammatically suspended, indicating a hypothetical legal scenario requiring juristic deliberation.
chapters.translation:
I say: A branch — If a menstruating woman intended to break her fast and then, after purification, to resume two months [of fasting], then in this there is a nullification of the attribute of obligatory status (al-farḍiyyah) from the preceding fast. So this [matter] contains a probability, and the more apparent [opinion] is its permissibility, because [the obligation] is on deferment (al-tarākhī), and what has passed is not corrupted, and the obligatory status was suspended upon completion.

The Third Characteristic: Feeding (al-Iṭʿām)
And recourse is made to it by the one incapable of fasting due to decrepitude (al-haram) or an illness that endures for two months, and after which recovery is not anticipated — like the anticipation of the return of absent wealth after two months. For whoever has absent wealth is called "possessor" (wājid), whereas this one is called "incapable" (ʿājiz) in the present moment. And regarding the transition of the traveler to feeding, there is hesitation (taraddud). As for excessive sexual urge (al-shabaq al-mufriṭ), the apparent [opinion] is that concession is not granted to deviate to feeding, and that is the analogical ruling (al-qiyās). Yet there is a [counter-]view relying upon the ḥadīth of the Bedouin (al-Aʿrābī), and we have already mentioned its difficulty in [the chapter on] fasting.

The consideration after this concerns: the quantity of the expiatory payment (al-mukhrij), its kind (jins), the recipient (al-mukhraj ilayh), and the act of payment (al-ikhrāj). As for the kind of the payment, it is like the Zakāh of Fast-Breaking (Zakāt al-Fiṭr). As for its quantity, it is sixty mudds (mudd). As for the recipient, it is the poor person (miskīn) to whom it is permissible to direct the Zakāh. And it is not permissible in our [school] to direct sixty mudds to a single poor person over sixty days — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him. Thus, it is necessary to observe the number of the poor, due to the apparent [meaning] of the verse. As for the act of payment, it is the complete transfer of ownership (al-tamlīk) and full empowerment (al-taslīṭ), so mere feeding of lunch and dinner by presenting dates to the poor is not sufficient.

= The Book of Mutual Cursing (al-Liʿān) =
And al-liʿān consists of oaths in which cursing is mentioned, [taken] by one who attributes his wife to adultery (zinā), whereby he repels the ḥadd [punishment] and the [impugning of] lineage from himself by virtue of his mere oath. And that is a concession (rukhṣah) due to the pressing need for the preservation of lineages and the difficulty of establishing proof (bayyinah) of the woman's adultery. It was first [revealed] regarding ʿUwaymir ibn Mālik al-ʿAjlānī, who accused his wife of [adultery with] Sharīk ibn al-Saḥmāʾ. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "You must bring four witnesses, or I shall flog your back." So he was distressed and said: "I hope that God will reveal a Qurʾān that will absolve my back." Then God revealed His saying: {«And those who accuse their wives»} — the verse.

And the consideration of the book is in two divisions: the accusation (al-qadhf) and the mutual cursing (al-liʿān).

The First Division: On the Accusation (al-Qadhf)
And in it are two chapters — peace and blessings be upon him. The first chapter concerns what constitutes an accusation from all of creation, and concerning its obligatory consequence — peace and blessings be upon him. And in it are two sections.

The First Section: On the Wording of Accusation (alfāẓ al-qadhf)

chapters.title_en: Section 421: The Three Categories of Accusatory Speech — Explicit (Ṣarīḥ), Allusive (Kināyah), and Indirect (Taʿrīḍ)
chapters.arabic_text:
وفيه ثلاثة أقسام صريح وكناية وتعريض
أما الصريح فهو كقوله يا زاني أو زنيت أو زنى فرجك وكذلك ذكر النيك
وإيلاج الفرج مع الوصف بالتحريم فهذا لا يقبل فيها تأويل
أما الكناية فكقوله للنبطي يا عربي أو للعربي با نبطي فإن أراد الزنا فهو
قذف وإلا فلا ثم إذا أنكر إراد الزنا توجهت اليمين عليه وإنما يتم القذف
باعترافه بالنية إذ به يحصل الإيذاء التام ويجب الحد بينه وبين الله تعالى
إذا نوى
وإن أنكر النية كاذبا فهل يلزمه إظهار النية فيه نظر من حيث إن فيه إيذاء
فيبعد إيجابه وستر ذلك لكف الأذى أولى إلا أن يرهق إليه باليمين فلا يباح
له اليمين الغموس فيلزمه الإعتراف وقد قال الأصحاب يجب عليه الإظهار بكل
حال كما لو قال في خفية فيلزمه الإظهار وقد ذهب بعض العلماء إلى أنه لا قذف
بالكناية لأن الإيذاء لا يتم به
وأما التعريض فكقوله يا ابن الحلال وكقوله أما أنا فلست بزان فهذا ليس
بقذف وإن نوى لأن اللفظ ليس يشعر به ولقد جاء رجل من فزارة إلى رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال إن امرأتي ولدت غلاما أسود معرضا بزناها فلم يجعله
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاذفا ولكن قال
هل لك إبل فقال نعم قال
ما ألوانها قال حمر قال
فهل فيها أسود قال نعم قال
فلم ذلك قال لعل عرقا  نزع فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
لعل عرقا نزع وقال مالك رحمه الله التعريض قذف والحديث حجة عليه
ويتم النظر في الألفاظ برسم مسائل
إحداها إذا قال لامرأة زنيت بك فهذا إقرار بالزنا وقذف للمرأة فعليه حدان
وكان يحتمل أن لا يجعل قاذفا لاحتمال أن يفسر بأنها كانت مستكرهة ولم تكن
مختارة ولكن جعل قاذفا اعتمادا على ما يقتضيه الظاهر
ولو قال لامرأته أنت زانية فقالت زنيت بك فراجعناها فإن أرادت الزنا قبل
النكاح سقط حد القذف عن الزوج ووجب عليها حدان حد الزنا وحد القذف للزوج
فإن رجعت سقط عنها حد الزنا ولا يسقط حد القذف إذ الرجوع لا يسقط حق الآدمي
إنما يسقط حدود الله تعالى ولو قالت أردت نفي الزنا كما يقول القائل سرقت
فيقول المخاطب سرقت سرقت معك فيقبل قولها مع اليمين ويكون لها طلب حد القذف
من الزوج لأن ذلك معتاد في الجواب وقد اختلف أصحابنا فيما لو قال لي عليك
دينار فقال زنه أنه هل يكون إقرارا
الثانية لو قال يا زانية فقالت أنت أزنى مني فهو قاذف وليست هي مقرة ولا
قاذفة للزوج لأنها لم تنسب لنفسها زنا حتى يكون هو زانيا بكونه أزنى منها
ولا نقول إن الترجيح يوجب المشاركة في الأصل فإن عادة المشاتمة لا تنزل على
وضع اللسان نعم لو قال فلان زان وأنت أزنى منه فهو قذف للشخصين جميعا ولو
قال أنت أزنى من فلان فليس بقذف
وكذا لو قال أنت أزنى من الناس أو أزنى الناس ولو قال في الناس زناة وأنت
أزنى منهم كان قذفا ولا نقول إنه يعلم أن في الناس زناة وإن لم يذكر بل
ينظر إلى لفظه ولو قال أنت أزنى من فلان وكان قد ثبت زنا فلان بالبينة وكان
القائل جاهلا لم يكن قذفا وإن كان عالما كان قذفا
ولو قالت أردت أنك زان ولست أنا زانية فهي قاذفة فلكل واحد على صاحبه حد
ولا يتقاصان لأن المقاصة في العقوبات مع تفاوت  موقعها في النفوس لا وجه له
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يتقاصان
الثالثة إذا قال للرجل يا زانية أو للمرأة يا زاني فهو قاذف عندنا خلافا
لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله في الصورة الأولى والسبب فيه أن الإشارة تقدم على
النحو والتذكير والتأنيث ولا خلاف أنه لو قال للرجل زنيت وللمرأة زنيت أنه
قاذف ولو قال زنأت في
الجبل وقال أردت الترقي فيه فليس بقاذف ولو قال زنيت في الجبل وقال أردت
الترقي فهل يقبل وجهان ووجه القبول أن حذف الهمزة قد يغلب على اللسان
وقرينة ذكر الجبل تشهد له ونص الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه لو قال يا زانية في
الجبل أنه قذف وقيل يفرق بين البصير في العربية والجاهل فلا يقبل حذف
الهمزة من البصير
الرابعة إذا قال زنى فرجك فهو قذف ولو قال زنى عينك أو يدك أو رجلك ففيه
وجهان وظاهر ما نقله المزني رحمه الله أنه قذف وهو فاسد إذ قال صلى الله
عليه وسلم
العينان تزنيان واليد تزنيان
ومن جعله قاذقا قال ذكر صريح الزنا وأضافه إلى البعض ومن ضرورة الإضافة
إلى البعض الإضافة إلى الكل ولو خرج ذلك عن كونه صريحا لكان قوله يا زاني
غير صريح إذ له أن يفسر فيقول أردت بالزاني العين
الخامسة إذا قال لولده لست مني أو لست ولدي ثم قال أردت أنك لست تشبهني
خلقا وخلقا لم يكن قاذفا نص عليه ونص أن الأجنبي إذا قال لست ولد فلان أن
ذلك لا يقبل منه ويكون قاذفا فمنهم من قال قولان بالنقل والتخريج وإليه ميل
المزني رحمه الله
أحدهما أنه يقبل منه لعرو اللفظ عن ذكر الزنا واحتمال ما قاله
والثاني أن ذلك لا يفهم منه في العادة
ومنهم من فرق بأن الأب يحتمل منه ذلك في معرض التأديب دون الأجنبي
والأقيس أنه كناية في الموضعين جميعا إذ ربما ينسبه إلى الوطء بالشبهة أو
ينكر ولادته على فراشه ثم إذا فسر بشيء من ذلك فلا يخفى كيفية فصل الخصومة
في نفي الولد ولحوقه
السادسة إذا قال للولد المنفي باللعان لست من الملاعن فإن أراد به النفي
الشرعي
فليس بقاذف وإن كان أراد تصديق الملاعن في نسبة الولد إلى الزنا فهو قاذف
ولو قال لقرشي لست من قريش فإن قال أردت أن واحدة من أمهاته في الجاهلية
زنت فليس بقاذف لأنها غير معينة ومن قال واحد من أهل البلد زنى أو الناس
زناة فلا يكون قاذفا ما لم يعين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ر-ح (Ṣ-R-Ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Clarity, explicitness, and the removal of ambiguity; the core sense is "to be clear and manifest."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, it denotes a statement whose apparent meaning is definitive and admits no alternative interpretation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for unambiguous speech, as opposed to kināyah, which is metaphorical (majāz) in its indirection.
- Root: ك-ن-ي (K-N-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To conceal or allude; the root conveys the idea of speaking indirectly, veiling the intended meaning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A euphemistic or allusive expression that requires intention (niyyah) to complete its legal effect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical usage where the literal sense is not intended; the rhetorical force depends on context.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-R-Ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To present, expose, or hint obliquely; the root implies turning something aside from its direct course.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A subtle insinuation that does not explicitly state the accusation but implies it through contrast or suggestion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The most indirect form of majāz, where the utterance itself does not linguistically indicate the intended meaning.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Grammatical Indication (Dalālah al-Iʿrāb) — The syntactic structure and case endings determine the default interpretation, but pragmatic context (qarīnah) can override literal parsing in legal judgments.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section comprises three categories: explicit (ṣarīḥ), allusive (kināyah), and indirect (taʿrīḍ).

As for the explicit (ṣarīḥ), it is like one's saying: "O fornicator!" or "You have fornicated!" or "Your private part has fornicated!" — and likewise the mention of sexual intercourse (al-nīk) and the insertion of the private part with the description of its prohibition. Such [utterances] admit no interpretation [that would deflect the accusation].

As for the allusive (kināyah), it is like one's saying to a Nabatean: "O Arab!" or to an Arab: "O Nabatean!" If he intended thereby [to accuse of] fornication (zinā), then it is a slanderous accusation (qadhf); otherwise, it is not. Then, if he denies [the intention], the oath (yamīn) is directed upon him. The slanderous accusation is only completed by his confession of the intention, for through it complete harm (īdhāʾ) is achieved. The prescribed punishment (ḥadd) becomes obligatory between him and God most high if he intended [the accusation].

And if he denies the intention falsely, is he obliged to disclose the intention? There is a consideration (naẓar) therein: since it involves harm, its imposition is unlikely, and concealing it to repel harm is more appropriate — unless he is compelled to it by the oath, for the perjurious oath (yamīn ghamūs) is not permitted to him, so he must confess. The companions (al-aṣḥāb) have said: He must disclose it in every case, just as if he had said it in secret, he would be obliged to disclose it. Some scholars have held that there is no slanderous accusation (qadhf) through allusive speech (kināyah), because complete harm is not achieved through it.

As for the indirect (taʿrīḍ), it is like one's saying: "O son of the lawful!" or one's saying: "As for me, I am not a fornicator." This is not a slanderous accusation, even if he intended [it], because the utterance does not indicate it. Indeed, a man from Fazārah came to the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — and said: "My wife has given birth to a black boy," indirectly accusing her of fornication. The Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — did not deem him a slanderer (qādhi f), but said: "Do you have camels?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What are their colors?" He said: "Red." He said: "Is there a black one among them?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How is that?" He said: "Perhaps a vein has pulled it." The Prophet — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Perhaps a vein has pulled it." Mālik — may God have mercy on him — said: The indirect (taʿrīḍ) is a slanderous accusation, and the hadith is an argument against him.

The examination of the utterances is completed by drawing up certain cases (masāʾil):

The first case: If a man says to a woman: "I have fornicated with you," this is an admission of fornication and a slanderous accusation against the woman. Thus, two prescribed punishments (ḥaddān) are incumbent upon him. It could have been possible not to deem him a slanderer, due to the possibility that he might interpret it as [meaning] she was coerced and not consenting. But he is deemed a slanderer, relying on what the apparent [meaning] requires.

And if a man says to his wife: "You are a fornicatress," and she says: "You have fornicated with me," and we refer her [to interpretation]: If she intended fornication before the marriage, the punishment of slander (ḥadd al-qadhf) is dropped from the husband, and two punishments are incumbent upon her: the punishment of fornication and the punishment of slander against the husband. If she retracts, the punishment of fornication is dropped from her, but the punishment of slander is not dropped, for retraction does not drop the right of an individual (ḥaqq ādamī); it only drops the rights of God most high. And if she says: "I intended to deny fornication," just as when one says: "I stole," and the addressee says: "I stole, I stole with you," then her statement is accepted with her oath, and she has the right to demand the punishment of slander from the husband, because that is customary in responses. Our companions have differed regarding the case where one says: "I owe you a dinar," and he says: "Weigh it" — whether that constitutes an admission.

The second case: If she says: "O fornicatress!" and she says: "You are more of a fornicator than me," he is a slanderer, and she is neither admitting [fornication] nor slandering the husband, because she has not attributed fornication to herself such that he would be a fornicator by virtue of being more of a fornicator than her. We do not say that the comparative (tafḍīl) necessitates participation in the root [quality], for the custom of vituperation (mushātamah) does not descend upon the grammatical construction. Yes, if he said: "So-and-so is a fornicator, and you are more of a fornicator than him," it is a slanderous accusation against both persons. And if he said: "You are more of a fornicator than so-and-so," it is not a slanderous accusation.

Likewise, if he said: "You are more of a fornicator than the people" or "the most fornicating of the people." And if he said: "Among the people are fornicators, and you are more of a fornicator than them," it is a slanderous accusation. We do not say that it is known that among the people are fornicators even if he did not mention [them]; rather, one looks to his utterance. And if he said: "You are more of a fornicator than so-and-so," and so-and-so's fornication had been established by evidence (bayyinah), and the speaker was ignorant [of that], it is not a slanderous accusation; but if he was knowledgeable, it is a slanderous accusation.

And if she says: "I intended that you are a fornicator, and I am not a fornicatress," then she is a slanderer. Thus, each one has a prescribed punishment against the other, and they do not cancel each other out (taqāṣ), because cancellation in punishments, given the differing impact on souls, has no basis. Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: They cancel each other out.

The third case: If a man says to a man: "O fornicatress!" or to a woman: "O fornicator!" he is a slanderer in our view, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — in the first case. The reason for it is that the referent (ishārah) takes precedence over the grammatical form (al-naḥw) and the masculine/feminine distinction. There is no disagreement that if he said to a man: "You have fornicated," and to a woman: "You have fornicated," he is a slanderer. And if he said: "I ascended (zanaʾtu) the mountain," and he said: "I intended ascent," he is not a slanderer. And if he said: "I fornicated (zanaytu) in the mountain," and he said: "I intended ascent," is it accepted? There are two views. The basis for acceptance is that the elision of the hamzah may dominate the tongue, and the contextual indication (qarīnah) of mentioning the mountain testifies for him. Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — explicitly stated that if he said: "O fornicatress in the mountain," it is a slanderous accusation. And it is said: One distinguishes between the expert in Arabic (al-baṣīr) and the ignorant one, so the elision of the hamzah is not accepted from the expert.

The fourth case: If he said: "Your private part has fornicated," it is a slanderous accusation. And if he said: "Your eye has fornicated," or "your hand," or "your foot," there are two views. The apparent [position] transmitted by al-Muzanī — may God have mercy on him — is that it is a slanderous accusation, and it is unsound (fāsid), for he — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The two eyes fornicate, and the two hands fornicate." And whoever deems him a slanderer says: He mentioned explicit fornication and attributed it to a part, and from the necessity of attributing it to a part is the attribution to the whole. And if that were to exit from being explicit, then his saying "O fornicator" would not be explicit, since he could interpret it and say: "I intended by 'fornicator' the eye."

The fifth case: If a man says to his child: "You are not from me," or "You are not my child," then he says: "I intended that you do not resemble me in form (khalq) and character (khuluq)," he is not a slanderer — this is explicitly stated [by al-Shāfiʿī]. And he explicitly stated that if a stranger (ajnabī) says: "You are not the child of so-and-so," that is not accepted from him, and he is a slanderer. Among them are those who said: There are two opinions, by transmission (naql) and by derivation (takhrij), and al-Muzanī — may God have mercy on him — inclined toward [one of them]: One is that it is accepted from him, due to the utterance being devoid of mentioning fornication and the possibility of what he said. The second is that it is not understood from him customarily. And among them are those who distinguished: The father may be understood [to say] this in the context of discipline (taʾdīb), unlike the stranger. And the more analogically sound (al-aqyas) is that it is allusive (kināyah) in both cases, for perhaps he attributes him to intercourse by doubtful [contract] (waṭʾ al-shubhah) or denies his birth upon his bed. Then, if he interprets it by any of that, the manner of settling the dispute regarding the denial of lineage and its affirmation is not obscure.

The sixth case: If he says to the child disowned by mutual imprecation (al-mulāʿan): "You are not from the one who imprecated (al-mulāʿin)," if he intended thereby the legal disavowal (al-nafy al-sharʿī), he is not a slanderer. But if he intended to affirm the imprecator's attribution of the child to fornication, he is a slanderer. And if he says to a Qurayshī: "You are not from Quraysh," and he says: "I intended that one of his maternal ancestors in the pre-Islamic era (al-jāhiliyyah) fornicated," he is not a slanderer, because she is not specified. And whoever says: "One of the people of the town fornicated," or "The people are fornicators," is not a slanderer as long as he does not specify.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في موجب القذف

والقذف يوجب التعزير إلا إذا صادف محصنا فيوجب الحد ثمانين جلدة
وخصال الإحصان التكليف والإسلام والحرية والعفة عن الزنا الموجب للحد فإن
من ثبت منه الزنا فكيف يصان عرضه مع أن القاذف صادق نعم يعزر وأما الوطء
الحرام الذي لا يوجب الحد لقيام ملك أو شبهة ملك فهل يبطل الإحصان فيه خلاف
وله درجات فإذا وطىء مملكوته المحرمة برضاع أو نسب ففيه وجهان وفي الجارية
المشتركة أو جارية الإبن وجهان مرتبان وأولى بأن لا يبطل الإحصان وفي مذهب
الشافعي رضي الله عنه إذا وطىء في النكاح بلا ولي وجهان مرتبان وأولى بأن
لا يبطل وفي الوطء بالشبهة وظن الزوجية وجهان مرتبان وأولى بأن لا يبطل
ووجه إبطاله أن ذلك يدل على قلة التحفظ ولو كان قد جرى صورة الفاحشة في
الصبي فوجهان مرتبان على الوطء بالشبهة وأولى بأن لا يبطل
أما الوطء في الحيض والصوم والإحرام فلا يبطل وفيه وجه بعيد أنه يبطل أما
مقدمات الوقاع من اللمس والقبلة فلا تسقط الإحصان

### | فروع

الأول لو زنى المقذوف بعد القذف وقبل الحد نص أن الحد يسقط ونص في
الردة أنه لا يسقط وعلل ذلك بأن الزنا لا يقع هجوما بل يتقدمه في الغالب
مراودات تقدح في المروءة وهذا ضعيف لأن المراودات السابقة لا تبطل الإحصان
ولا يمكن أن يقال الزنا لا يقع هجوما فإنه لا بد وأن يكون له أول والردة
أيضا لا تخلو عن تقدم ترددات بل السبب أن من ثبت زناه في الحال يبعد أن
يجلد ظهر غيره لصيانة عرضه وهو قد هتك عرضه بخلاف المرتد إذا عاد فإن العرض
قائم وقد كان الإسلام موجودا عند القذف وقال المزني رحمه الله لا يسقط
بطرآن الزنا كما لا يسقط بطرآن الردة وقيل هو قول قديم للشافعي رضي الله
عنه
الثاني من زنى مرة في عمره ثم عاد وحسنت حاله قال القاضي لا حد على قاذفه
لبطلان إحصانه فإن اسم الزاني لا يسقط عنه وهذا بعيد فيما إذا صرح بقذفه
بزنا جديد ولكن كأن العرض إذا انخرم بالزنا فلا يزايله الخلل بالعفة بعده
الثالث لو أقام القاذف بينة على زنا المقذوف سقط عنه الحد ويكفيه لذلك
شاهدان ولو عجز فطلب يمين المقذوف على أنه ما زنى ففيه قولان
أحدهما لا يجب لأن ظاهره الإحصان ولا عهد باليمين على نفي الكبائر
والثاني نعم لأنه لو أقر به لسقط عنه الحد فليحلف أو لينكل حتى يحلف
القاذف
الرابع لو مات المقذوف قبل استيفاء حد القذف ثبت الحد والتعزير لوارثه
لأن الغالب عندنا في حد القذف حق الآدميين وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا
يورث
واعترف بأنه لو قذف ميتا فلوارثه طلب الحد ابتداء
ولو قذف مورثه فمات المورث سقط الحد لأنه صار شريكا في استحقاق الحد على
نفسه ثم فيمن يرث ثلاثة أوجه
أحدها أنه يوزع على فرائض الله تعالى
والثاني أنه يختص بالنسب إذ لا مدخل للزوج في حماية العرض ودفع العار
والثالث أنه يختص بالعصبات من النسب الذين لهم ولاية التزويج لدفع العار
وعلى هذا لا يستحق الإبن ومنهم من قال يستحق لأنه أقوى العصبات في الميراث
ولو عفا أحد الورثة سقط الكل على وجه لأنه لا يتجزأ ولم يسقط على وجه
لأنه يستحيل أن يبطل حق الباقين من غير بدل بخلاف القصاص الذي له بدل
والثالث أنه يوزع
فيسقط نصيبه
الخامس إذا قذف المجنون بزنا قبل الجنون فالحد يجب ونصبر إلى إفاقته وليس
للولي الإستيفاء لأنه متعلق بتشفي الغيظ فلو مات ثبت لوارثه
ولو قذف مملوك  فحق طلب التعزير له لا لسيده لأنه من خواص حقوقه بل لو
قذفه سيده استحق العبد تعزيره على المذهب الظاهر ومنهم من قال يقال له لا
تعد فإن عاد يعزر كما يعزر لو زاد في استخدامه على الحد الواجب
ولو مات العبد بعد استحقاق التعزير على أجنبي فهو يستوفيه السيد فيه
وجهان ووجهه أنه أولى الناس به إلا أنه لا قرابة
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في قذف الأزواج خاصة - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -
وفيه فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ذ-ف (q-dh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To throw, cast, or hurl from a distance; in juristic usage, to cast an accusation of illicit sexual intercourse (zinā) against a chaste person.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of projecting a grave slander that assaults the protected honor (ʿirḍ) of a person, entailing a fixed legal penalty (ḥadd) when the accused is muḥṣan (chaste and free).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of physical casting; metaphorical (majāz) in the legal sense of verbal defamation, which is the operative usage here.
- Root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fortification, protection, inaccessibility; a fortress (ḥiṣn) that guards against attack.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The state of moral and legal inviolability (iḥṣān) that renders the accused's honor worthy of penal protection, contingent on specified conditions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a fortified place; metaphorical — the fortified chastity of a free, adult, Muslim who has not committed punishable zinā.
- Root: ع-ف-ف (ʿ-f-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abstention from what is unlawful; purity and continence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The positive moral quality of refraining from illicit sexual acts, which is a constitutive element of iḥṣān.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — refraining from filth; metaphorical — the sustained state of sexual purity that the law presumes unless proven otherwise.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "except if it coincides with a muḥṣan" (إلا إذا صادف محصنا) establishes a conditional exception that shifts the ruling from discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) to the fixed penalty (ḥadd), requiring precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Qadhf (false accusation of unchastity) necessitates discretionary punishment (taʿzīr), except when it coincides with a muḥṣan (chaste person), in which case it necessitates the fixed penalty (ḥadd) of eighty lashes. The characteristics of iḥṣān (chastity that triggers the ḥadd) are: legal responsibility (taklīf), Islam, freedom, and chastity (ʿiffah) from zinā that necessitates the ḥadd. For if a person has been established to have committed zinā, how could his honor be protected, given that the accuser is truthful? Rather, he is given taʿzīr. As for unlawful intercourse (waṭʾ ḥarām) that does not necessitate the ḥadd due to the existence of ownership (milk) or a semblance of ownership (shubhat milk), there is a disagreement (khilāf) as to whether it nullifies iḥṣān. This has degrees: if one has intercourse with his female slave who is unlawful to him due to fosterage (riḍāʿ) or lineage (nasab), there are two views (wajhān). Regarding a jointly-owned slave-girl or the son's slave-girl, there are two ranked views, and it is more appropriate that iḥṣān is not nullified. In the school of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — if one has intercourse in a marriage without a guardian (walī), there are two ranked views, and it is more appropriate that it does not nullify. Regarding intercourse under a semblance of ownership (shubhah) and the presumption of marriage (ẓann al-zawjiyyah), there are two ranked views, and it is more appropriate that it does not nullify. The basis for nullification is that such an act indicates a lack of self-restraint. If the form of lewdness (ṣūrat al-fāḥishah) had occurred with a minor boy, there are two ranked views based on the case of intercourse under shubhah, and it is more appropriate that it does not nullify. As for intercourse during menstruation (ḥayḍ), fasting (ṣawm), or pilgrimage consecration (iḥrām), it does not nullify iḥṣān, though there is a remote view that it does. As for the preliminaries of intercourse — touching (lams) and kissing (qublah) — they do not nullify iḥṣān.

### Branches (Furūʿ)

**First:** If the accused person commits zinā after the accusation (qadhf) but before the execution of the ḥadd, it is explicitly stated (naṣṣ) that the ḥadd is dropped. It is also explicitly stated regarding apostasy (riddah) that it does not drop. This was rationalized by saying that zinā does not occur impulsively but is generally preceded by solicitations (murāwaḍāt) that impugn one's probity (murūʾah). This is weak, because prior solicitations do not nullify iḥṣān, and one cannot say that zinā does not occur impulsively, for it necessarily has a beginning. Apostasy likewise is not free of preceding hesitations. Rather, the reason is that a person whose zinā is established at the present moment is unlikely to have another's back lashed for the protection of his honor when he has already violated his own honor — unlike the apostate who returns, for his honor remains intact, and Islam was present at the time of the accusation. Al-Muzanī — may Allah have mercy on him — said: It does not drop by the supervention of zinā, just as it does not drop by the supervention of apostasy. It is said this is an old opinion (qawl qadīm) of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him.

**Second:** If a person committed zinā once in his life, then repented and his condition improved, al-Qāḍī said: There is no ḥadd upon his accuser, due to the nullification of his iḥṣān, for the name "zānī" (fornicator) is not removed from him. This is remote (baʿīd) in the case where the accuser explicitly accuses him of new zinā. Rather, it is as if once honor is breached by zinā, the defect does not depart from it by subsequent chastity.

**Third:** If the accuser produces evidence (bayyinah) of the accused's zinā, the ḥadd is dropped from him, and two witnesses suffice for that. If he fails and requests the accused's oath that he did not commit zinā, there are two opinions (qawlān): One — it is not obligatory, because the apparent state is iḥṣān, and there is no precedent for oaths regarding the negation of major sins (kabāʾir). The second — yes, it is obligatory, because if he had confessed to it, the ḥadd would have dropped from the accuser; so let him swear, or else decline (nukūl) so that the accuser swears.

**Fourth:** If the accused dies before the execution of the ḥadd for qadhf, the ḥadd and the taʿzīr are established for his heir, because in our school the dominant view is that the ḥadd for qadhf is a right of human beings (ḥaqq ādamī). Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah have mercy on him — said: It is not inherited. He conceded that if one accuses a dead person, his heir has the right to demand the ḥadd ab initio. If one accuses his own testator (mūrith) and the testator dies, the ḥadd drops, because the accuser has become a partner in claiming the ḥadd against himself. Then, regarding who inherits, there are three views (awjuh): One — it is distributed according to the fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) of Allah the Exalted. The second — it is restricted to the lineage (nasab), since the spouse has no role in protecting honor and repelling disgrace. The third — it is restricted to the ʿaṣabāt (agnatic heirs) from the lineage who have the authority of marriage (wilāyat al-tazwīj) for repelling disgrace. On this basis, the son does not inherit it, though some said he does, because he is the strongest of the ʿaṣabāt in inheritance. If one of the heirs pardons, the whole drops according to one view, because it is indivisible; and it does not drop according to another view, because it is impossible to nullify the right of the remaining heirs without compensation, unlike qiṣāṣ (retaliation), which has a substitute. The third view: it is distributed, and his share drops.

**Fifth:** If a madman (majnūn) is accused of zinā committed before his madness, the ḥadd is obligatory, and we wait until his recovery. The guardian (walī) does not have the right to execute it, because it is connected to the gratification of anger (tashaffī al-ghayẓ). If he dies, it is established for his heir. If a slave (mamlūk) is accused, the right to demand taʿzīr belongs to him, not to his master, because it is among his specific personal rights. Indeed, if his master accuses him, the slave deserves taʿzīr against the master according to the apparent school (al-madhhab al-ẓāhir). Some said: It is said to the master, "Do not repeat," and if he repeats, he is given taʿzīr, just as he would be given taʿzīr if he exceeded the prescribed limit in employing him. If the slave dies after establishing his right to taʿzīr against a stranger, there are two views on whether the master executes it: one view is that he does, because he is the person most entitled to him, except that there is no kinship (qarābah).

— Peace be upon him — The Second Book on Accusation of Unchastity Specifically Regarding Spouses — Peace be upon him —

And it contains chapters.
