### | الفصل الأول فيما يبيح القذف واللعان أو يوجبه

واعلم أن قذف الزوج في إيجاب الحد والتعزير كقذف الأجانب ولكن يفارق
الأجانب في ثلاثة أمور
أحدها في أنه قد يباح له القذف ويجب عليه لضرورة نفي النسب
والثاني أن العقوبة التي تتوجه عليه من حد وتعزير تندفع باللعان
والثالث أن المرأة تتعرض لحد الزنا بلعانه إلا إذا دفعت عن نفسها باللعان
لقوله تعالى {ويدرأ عنها العذاب أن تشهد} الآية
وإنما يباح له القذف إذا استيقن أنها زنت أو غلبت على ظنه ذلك ولكن إذا
لم يكن ولد فالأولى أن يطلقها ولا يقذف ولا يلاعن ولكن لو فعل لم يأثم وهذا
فيه غموض ولكن كأن القذف واللعان كالإنتقام منها حيث لطخت فراشه
ثم تحصل الغلبة على الظن بقول عدل حكى مشاهدته الزنا وتحصل مهما
استفاض بين الناس أن فلانا يزني بها إذا رأى مع ذلك مخيلة بأن رآها معه
في خلوة فإن تجرد أحد المعنيين لم يحل له ذلك لأن الخلوة مرة لا تدل على
الزنا نعم لو رآها معه تحت شعار على نعت مكروه حل له القذف وإن كان لا تحل
الشهادة بهذا القدر وإن رآها في الخلوة مرارا متكررة فهذا قريب من المرة
الواحدة إذا انضمت إليه الشيوع فإن مستند أهل الإستفاضة هو مشاهدة ذلك
مرارا
أما نفي الولد باللعان فإنما يجوز بينه وبين الله تعالى إذا تيقن أن
الولد ليس منه بأن لم يكن وطئها أو كان يعزل قطعا أو أتت بولد  قبل ستة أشهر
من وقت الوطء وقال مالك رحمه الله لا مبالاة بالعزل وليس له اللعان إذا
اعترف بالوطء وأمكن إحالة الولد عليه
أما إذا استبرأها بحيضة بعد الوطء ثم أتت بولد فهذا هل يبيح النفي فيه
ثلاثة أوجه
أحدها نعم لأن ذلك أمارة شرعية على النفي ولذلك يندفع النسب عن التابع
والثاني أنه إن ظهر مع ذلك أمارة الزنا جاز وإلا فلا يجوز لأن الحيض ليس
بقاطع والحامل قد تحيض
والثالث أنه يجوز ولكن حيث يجوز النفي يجب لأن السكوت عن إلحاق الباطل
حرام إذ النسب يتعلق بأحكام كثيرة ولكن هاهنا وإن جاز فلا يجب
وقال الإمام لا يبعد أن لا يوجب اللعان لأنه إفضاح وقدح في المروءة فنقول
إنما يحرم الإستلحاق كاذبا أما إذا ألحق الفراش به وهو ساكت فلا يبعد أن لا
يحرم السكوت وهذا غير منقدح في صورة اليقين لأن أمر النسب عظيم فلا يقضي
عليه بالرسوم والمروءات
ولا خلاف في أنه لا يحل النفي بمجرد مشابهة الولد لغيره في الخلق والخلق
ولمخالفته للولد في الحسن والقبح نعم لو كان الأب في غاية البياض والولد في
غاية السواد أو العكس ذكر العراقيون وجهين وهذا ينقدح إن كان مع ذلك تظهر
مخيلة الزنا فأما مجرد ذلك فلا فلعل عرقا قد نزع وأبو حنيفة رحمه الله حيث
يلحق ولد المشرقي بالمغربي فلا شك في أنه يبيح القذف ويحرمه عند إمكان
العلوق بالوطء ونحن لا نلحق النسب إلا بعد ستة أشهر من وقت إمكان الوطء
فرع إذا أتت بولد لمدة الإمكان ولكن الزوج رآها تزني واحتمل أن يكون من
الزنا فلو قذف ولاعن انتفى في الظاهر بدليل قصة العجلاني ولكن لا يباح له
ذلك مع تعارض الإحتمال ثم قال الأصحاب ليس له القذف واللعان إن ترك نفي
النسب وقد صرحوا بجواز
القذف إذا لم يكن ولد لمجرد الإنتقام من الزنا فهذا محتمل وغاية تعليله
أنه إذا كان ثم ولد لم يجز نفيه فنسبتها إلى الزنا بغير الولد وتطلق
الألسنة  في نسبه فلا يقاوم هذا الغرض غرض التشفي فليقتصر على طلاقها إن
أراد نظرا لولده والذي لحقه

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ذ-ف (Q-Dh-F)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To throw, cast, or hurl; specifically casting an accusation of illicit sexual intercourse (zinā) against a chaste person.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal accusation of fornication entailing the ḥadd penalty (fixed corporal punishment) for false accusation; a verbal act with juridical consequences.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of 'throwing' words; metaphorical (majāz) in the legal technical sense of 'defamation of chastity'.
- Root: ل-ع-ن (L-ʿ-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To curse, banish, or drive away from mercy; in legal context, the mutual oath-taking procedure between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic ordinance of mutual imprecation (liʿān) as a substitute for penal proof when a husband accuses his wife of adultery without witnesses.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal 'cursing'; metaphorical for the entire legal ritual of oath-swearing that repels punishment.
- Root: ن-ف-ي (N-F-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To negate, deny, or disavow; specifically repudiation of paternity (nafy al-nasab).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal disavowal of lineage through liʿān, severing the child's genealogical attachment to the father.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal 'negation'; metaphorical for the juridical act of repudiating a child's lineage.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna (إنما) — Restrictive construction (qasr) where the predicate is confined to the subject, indicating exclusive permissibility under specified conditions.
chapters.translation:
Know that a husband's accusation of fornication (qadhf) against his wife, regarding the obligation of the ḥadd penalty and discretionary punishment (taʿzīr), is like his accusation against strangers (ajānib). However, it differs from the case of strangers in three matters:

**First:** It may become permissible for him to accuse her, and even obligatory upon him, due to the necessity of repudiating the child's lineage (nafy al-nasab).

**Second:** The punishment that would be directed against him—whether ḥadd or taʿzīr—is repelled by the mutual imprecation (liʿān).

**Third:** The woman becomes exposed to the ḥadd penalty for fornication by his imprecation, unless she repels it from herself by her own imprecation, due to the saying of the Exalted: {«And it shall avert the punishment from her if she bears witness...»} (Q. 24:8) to the end of the verse.

His accusation is only permissible when he is certain that she has committed fornication, or when overwhelming presumption (ghalabat al-ẓann) prevails upon him of that. However, if there is no child [involved], then it is more proper (al-awlā) that he divorce her and neither accuse her nor imprecate. But if he does so, he does not sin. This matter contains some obscurity (ghumūḍ), yet it is as though the accusation and imprecation are a form of vengeance against her, since she has sullied his bed (farāsh).

Then overwhelming presumption is established by the statement of a just person (ʿadl) who reports having witnessed the fornication. It is also established when the matter becomes widely circulated among people (istifāḍah) that so-and-so fornicates with her, provided that he also observes some indication (makhīlah) alongside it—such as seeing her alone with him in seclusion (khalwah). If either of the two elements is isolated [without the other], it is not lawful for him [to accuse], because a single seclusion does not indicate fornication. Yes—if he saw her with him beneath a single covering (shiʿār) in a reprehensible manner, then his accusation becomes lawful, even though bearing witness to that extent is not lawful. And if he saw her in seclusion repeatedly and frequently, this is close to the single instance when public circulation (shuyūʿ) is joined to it, for the basis of those who rely on widespread report is the observation of such [occurrences] repeatedly.

As for repudiating the child through liʿān, it is only permissible between him and God the Exalted when he is certain that the child is not from him—such as when he never had intercourse with her, or he practiced coitus interruptus (ʿazl) definitively, or she brought a child before six months from the time of intercourse. Imam Mālik (may God have mercy on him) said: No consideration is given to coitus interruptus, and he has no right to liʿān if he acknowledges intercourse and it is possible to attribute the child to him.

As for when he observes her purity by one menstrual period (istibrāʾ bi-ḥayḍah) after intercourse, then she brings a child—does this permit repudiation? There are three positions (awjuh):

**One:** Yes, because that [menstrual period] is a legal indication (amārah sharʿiyyah) of repudiation, and for this reason lineage is repelled from the follower (tābiʿ) [i.e., the child of a slave-woman].

**Second:** If an indication of fornication also appears alongside it, then it is permissible; otherwise it is not, because menstruation is not decisive (qāṭiʿ), and a pregnant woman may menstruate.

**Third:** It is permissible, but wherever repudiation is permissible, it is obligatory—because remaining silent about affirming what is false (ilḥāq al-bāṭil) is forbidden, since lineage is connected to many legal rulings. However, here, although it is permissible, it is not obligatory.

The Imām [al-Ghazālī] said: It is not far-fetched that it does not obligate liʿān, because it is an exposure (ifḍāḥ) and an attack upon manliness (murūʾah). We say: What is forbidden is only to affirm [the child] falsely (istilḥāq kādhiban). But as for when he attributes the bed to himself while remaining silent, it is not far-fetched that silence is not forbidden. Yet this [reasoning] does not hold in the case of certainty, because the matter of lineage is grave, and one does not adjudicate it by customs and manly virtues.

There is no disagreement that repudiation is not lawful merely by the child's resemblance to someone else in creation (khalq) or character (khuluq), nor by the child's differing from him in beauty or ugliness. Yes—if the father is extremely white and the child is extremely black, or the reverse, the Iraqis mentioned two positions (wajhayn). This [repudiation] holds if, alongside that, an indication of fornication appears. But mere [resemblance] alone [is insufficient], for perhaps a root [of ancestry] has been extracted (ʿirq nazaʿa). Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him), who attributes the child of an Easterner to a Westerner—there is no doubt that he permits accusation and forbids it when conception is possible through intercourse. We do not attribute lineage except after six months from the time intercourse was possible.

**Branch (farʿ):** If she brings a child within the period of possibility, but the husband saw her committing fornication and it is possible that [the child] is from the fornication—if he accuses and imprecates, the lineage is repudiated in appearance (fī al-ẓāhir), as evidenced by the story of al-ʿUjlānī. But it is not permissible for him to do so given the conflict of probabilities. Then the companions (aṣḥāb) said: He has no right to accusation and liʿān if he abandons repudiating the lineage. Yet they explicitly stated the permissibility of accusation when there is no child, merely for vengeance against the fornication. This is plausible, and the ultimate justification for it is that when there is a child, he may not repudiate him; so attributing her to fornication without [repudiating] the child would set tongues loose regarding his lineage. This purpose does not outweigh the purpose of vindictive satisfaction (tashaffī). So let him confine himself to divorcing her if he seeks what is best for his child and for what attaches to him.

### The Second Chapter on the Pillars (Arkān) of Liʿān and Its Procedures

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 424: The Rulings of Mutual Imprecation (Liʿān)
chapters.arabic_text:
وللعان سبب وهو القذف وثمرة وأهل أعني الملاعن فهذه ثلاثة أركان سوى
ألفاظه
الركن الأول الثمرة وثمرته أربعة نفي النسب أو قطع النكاح أو دفع عقوبة
القذف أو دفع عار الكذب في القذف
أما نفي النسب في النكاح إن تجرد جاز اللعان لأجله وإن لم تكن عقوبة
بعفوها مثلا وكذلك إن لم يكن قطع نكاح بأن كان قد أبانها ولو تجرد غرض
الدفع للعقوبة ولم يكن ولد ولا قطع نكاح جاز اللعان كما لو قذفها وأبانها
ولم يكن ولد ولا فرق بين أن تكون العقوبة حدا أو تعزيرا بأن تكون الزوجة
أمة أو ذمية أو غير محصنة على الجملة وفيه وجه بعيد أن اللعان لدفع التعزير
غير جائز وهو ضعيف فإن عقوبة محذورة وقد تنتهي إلى قريب من الحد وهذا إذا
كان التعزير لتكذيبه فيكون له غرض في تصديق نفسه وفي دفع العقوبة فيجتمع
الغرضان
فإن كان تعزير تأديب لا تعزير تكذيب مثل أن ينسبها إلى زنا قد قامت
البينة عليه من قبل أو اعترفت به فيؤدب لإيذائه بتجديد ذكر الفاحشة عليها
وقد نقل المزني رحمه الله ها هنا أنها إن طلبت ذلك غزر ولم يلتعن
ونقل الربيع رحمه الله عزر إن لم يلتعن فمنهم من قطع بأنه يلاعن وغلط
المزني رحمه الله ومنهم من قطع بأنه لا يلاعن وغلط الربيع ومنهم من قال
قولان والأصح أنه لا يلتعن لأن اللعان حجة تصديق فكيف يقام على ما ثبت صدقه
وإنما اندفاع العقوبة تابع لظهور صدقه باللعان وهذا معترف به فلا يزيده
اللعان وضوحا
فرعان
أحدهما أن طلب العقوبة إليها لا إلى السلطان فإن عفت فهل يلاعن إذا لم
يكن غرض آخر من نسب يدفع فيه وجهان
أحدهما نعم لأن دفع عار الكذب مقصود أيضا وإفضاحها أيضا للإنتقام منها
مقصود باللعان المؤبد للحرمة فله إقامة الحجة وإنما يندفع  هذا باعترافها لا
بعفوها
والثاني أنه لا يلاعن لأن هذا غرض ضعيف واللعان حجة ضرورة فلا بد من غرض
مهم كدفع النسب أو العقوبة أما قطع النكاح فممكن بالطلاق
أما إذا سكتت عن الطلب فوجهان مرتبان وأولى بجواز اللعان لأن غرضه الطلب
وهذا الخلاف يرجع إلى أن طلب العقوبة هل هو شرط اللعان إذا لم يكن ثمة غرض
من دفع نسب وقطع نكاح وإن كانت مجنونة فوجهان مرتبان على العفو وأولى
بالجواز
الثاني لو قال زنى بك ممسوح أو قال للرتقاء زينب فهو كلام محال وليس فيه
إلا التعزير للإيداء ولا سبيل إلى اللعان إذ كيف يمكن من أن يحلف على ما
يعلم أنه كاذب فيه وذكر العراقيون فيه وجهين كما في تعزير التأديب وهو بعيد
الركن الثاني الملاعن وشرطه أهلية اليمين مع الزوجية
أما أهلية اليمين فنعني به أنه لا يشترط أهلية الشهادة فيصح لعان العبد
والذمي والمحدود في القذف خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
ثم الذمي لا يجبر على اللعان إلا إذا رضي بحكمنا فإن طلبت المرأة اللعان
وامتنع الزوج فهل يجبر فيه قولان يجريان في كل خصومة تجري بين أهل الذمة إن
رضي بحكمنا أحد الخصمين أما إذا لاعن وامتنعت ولم ترض بحكمنا لم نجبرها على
اللعان ولا على الحد فإن الحد حق الله تعالى لا حق الزوج فلا غرض للزوج في
لعانها وهكذا
لو قذف المسلم زوجته الذمية فامتنعت فلا نجبرها وإنما عليها حد الزنا وهو
حق الله تعالى لا حق الزروج نعم المسلمة إذا امتنعت من اللعان ولم يطلب
الزوج لعانها عرضناها لحد الزنا حتى تلاعن إن شاءت الدفع ومن أصحابنا من
أجرى القولين في إجبار المرأة الذمية وهو بعيد
الشرط الثاني الزوجية فلو قذف الأجنبي فلا يلاعن والنظر في نكاح ضعيف
بالطلاق أو الردة وفي النكاح الفاسد
أما الرجعية فيلاعن عنها ولا يتوقف على الرجعة بخلاف الإيلاء والظهار لأن
مقصود اللعان نفي النسب والتحريم المؤبد ودفع الحد وكل ذلك لا ينافيه حال
الرجعة
أما  إذا ارتد بعد المسيس فقذف أو كان قذفه بزنا قبل الردة فإن لاعن في
الردة ثم عاد إلى الإسلام صح لعانه كما صح لعان الذمي فإن أصر تبين فساد
لعانه وعند ذلك هل يقضي بوجوب الحد مع جريان لعان فاسد فيه وجهان سنذكر
مأخذهما
أما إذا نكح نكاحا فاسدا أو وطىء بالشبهة ثم قذف فإن كان ثم نسب تعرض
للحوق وأراد نفيه فيلاعن ويندفع الحد لأن اللعان عندنا يستقل بمقصود نفي
النسب خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
وإن لم يكن ثم نسب فهو كالأجنبي لا يلاعن وعليه الحد
فإن ظن صحة النكاح فلاعن عند القاضي ثم بان فساده فهل تندفع العقوبة فيه
وجهان كما في المرتد المصر
أحدهما لا لأن اللعان فاسد
والثاني نعم لأن الحد يندفع بالشبهة وهذه حجة قامت على ظن الصحة في مجلس
القاضي
ثم مهما جرى اللعان في النكاح الفاسد ففي تعلق الحرمة المؤبدة به خلاف
مأخذه أنه لم يفد تحريما فكأن التأبيد تابع للحرمة وقد كانت هي محرمة وكذلك
في لعانها
خلاف يرجع حاصله إلى أنها هل تتعرض للحد بسبب لعانه فمنهم من قال نعم
لقيام حجة صحيحة على زناها ومنهم من قال لا لأن إيجاب الحد عليها بعيد عن
القياس فيختص بمقصود الإنتقام من تلطيخ الفراش فلا يجري إلا في نكاح صحيح
أما إذا قذف في نكاح صحيح ثم أبانها فله أن يلاعن لدرء النسب إن كان أو
لدفع العقوبة لأنه جرى القذف حيث كان معذورا فكان يجوز له اللعان فلا يتغير
بما يطرأ بعد ذلك
أما إذا قذفها في النكاح بزنا قبل النكاح فإن لم يكن نسب ينفيه باللعان
لم يلاعن وإن كان فوجهان ووجه المنع أنه قصر إذ ذكر التاريخ فكان ينبغي أن
يقتصر على القذف واللعان
أما إذا قذف بعد البينونة فإن كان ثم ولد فله اللعان وإلا فلا لأنه قذف
أجنبية وفيه وجه أنه إن أضاف الزنا إلى حالة النكاح لاعن وهذا لا وجه له
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ع-ن (la-ʿa-na)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to curse, to drive away from mercy," and in juristic convention it denotes the mutual oaths of condemnation between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qurʾānic context {«وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ»} (Q. 24:6), it signifies the solemn invocation of divine curse as a legal proof (ḥujjah) substituting for testimony.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the act of cursing; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the entire legal procedure of mutual imprecation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Structure (al-Sharṭ wa-l-Jawāb) — The text frequently employs conditional constructions (e.g., "if... then...") requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve the legal conditionality.
chapters.translation:
I say: The mutual imprecation (liʿān) has a cause, which is the accusation of fornication (qadhf); a fruit (thamrah); and a person, namely the one who performs the imprecation (mulāʿin). These constitute three pillars (arkān) apart from its verbal formulas.

**The First Pillar: The Fruit (al-Thamrah)**
Its fruits are four: negation of lineage (nafy al-nasab), severance of marriage (qaṭʿ al-nikāḥ), repelling the punishment for qadhf, or repelling the disgrace of falsehood in the accusation.

As for negating lineage within marriage: if it stands alone, the liʿān is permissible for its sake, even if there is no punishment — for example, due to the wife's pardon. Likewise, it is permissible even if there is no severance of marriage, such as when he had already divorced her irrevocably (bāʾin). And if the sole purpose were repelling punishment, with no child and no severance of marriage, the liʿān is still permissible — as when he accuses her and divorces her irrevocably with no child. There is no difference whether the punishment be a fixed legal penalty (ḥadd) or a discretionary punishment (taʿzīr), such as when the wife is a slave-girl, a dhimmī, or non-muḥṣanah in general. There is a remote opinion (wajh baʿīd) that liʿān for repelling taʿzīr is impermissible, but this is weak — for it is a punishment to be feared, and it may escalate to something close to the ḥadd. This applies when the taʿzīr is for his false accusation (takdhīb), so that he has an interest in affirming his own truthfulness and in repelling the punishment — thus the two interests combine.

But if the taʿzīr is disciplinary (taʿdīb), not for accusation — such as when he attributes to her a fornication for which evidence had previously been established or which she had confessed — then he is disciplined for harming her by renewing mention of the obscenity against her. Al-Muzanī (may Allah have mercy on him) transmitted here that if she requests it, he is disciplined and does not perform liʿān. Al-Rabīʿ (may Allah have mercy on him) transmitted that he is disciplined if he does not perform liʿān. Among our companions, some definitively held that he does perform liʿān, declaring al-Muzanī mistaken; others definitively held that he does not, declaring al-Rabīʿ mistaken; and others held two opinions (qawlān). The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that he does not perform liʿān — because the liʿān is a proof of verification (ḥujjat taṣdīq); how then could it be established regarding something whose truthfulness is already confirmed? The repelling of punishment is merely consequent upon the manifestation of his truthfulness through liʿān, but here he is already acknowledged as truthful, so the liʿān adds no clarity.

**Two Subsidiary Issues (Farʿān)**

**First:** The request for punishment belongs to her, not to the ruler (sulṭān). If she pardons, does he perform liʿān when there is no other purpose of negating lineage to be repelled? There are two opinions:
- One: Yes — because repelling the disgrace of falsehood is also intended, and exposing her for vengeance is likewise intended through the liʿān which perpetually prohibits her. Thus he may establish the proof; this disgrace is repelled by her confession, not by her pardon.
- The second: He does not perform liʿān — because this is a weak purpose, and the liʿān is a proof of necessity; it requires a significant purpose such as repelling lineage or punishment. As for severing marriage, that is achievable through divorce.

But if she remains silent about requesting, there are two opinions arranged hierarchically, with the permissibility of liʿān being more apt — because his purpose is the request. This disagreement reduces to whether requesting punishment is a condition for liʿān when there is no purpose of repelling lineage or severing marriage. If she is insane, there are two opinions arranged on the pardon case, with permissibility being more apt.

**Second:** If he says, "A eunuch (mamsūḥ) fornicated with you," or says to a woman with vaginal occlusion (ratqāʾ), "Zaynab fornicated with you," this is impossible speech (kalām muḥāl). There is nothing in it except taʿzīr for harm, and no path to liʿān — for how can one swear to what he knows is false? The Iraqis mentioned two opinions here, as in the case of disciplinary taʿzīr, but this is remote.

**The Second Pillar: The One Who Performs Liʿān (al-Mulāʿin)**
Its condition is competence for oath-taking (ahliyyat al-yamīn) along with marital status (zawjiyyah).

As for competence for oath-taking, I mean that competence for testimony (ahliyyat al-shahādah) is not required. Thus the liʿān of a slave, a dhimmī, and one previously punished for qadhf is valid — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him).

Then, the dhimmī is not compelled to perform liʿān unless he accepts our jurisdiction (ḥukm). If the woman requests liʿān and the husband refuses, is he compelled? There are two opinions (qawlān) that apply to every dispute between dhimmīs when one of the two litigants accepts our jurisdiction. But if he performs liʿān and she refuses without accepting our jurisdiction, we do not compel her to liʿān nor to the ḥadd — for the ḥadd is a right of Allah (may He be exalted), not a right of the husband, so the husband has no interest in her liʿān. Likewise, if a Muslim accuses his dhimmī wife and she refuses, we do not compel her; rather, upon her is the ḥadd for fornication, being a right of Allah, not a right of the husband. Yes — if a Muslim woman refuses liʿān and the husband does not request her liʿān, we expose her to the ḥadd for fornication until she performs liʿān if she wishes to repel it. Some of our companions extended the two opinions to compelling the dhimmī woman, but this is remote.

**The Second Condition: Marital Status (al-Zawjiyyah)**
If a stranger (ajnabī) accuses, there is no liʿān. Consideration is given to a weak marriage — through divorce or apostasy (riddah) — and to a defective marriage (nikāḥ fāsid).

As for the revocably divorced wife (rajʿiyyah): liʿān is performed regarding her and is not contingent upon returning to her (rajʿah) — unlike ʿīlāʾ and ẓihār — because the purpose of liʿān is negating lineage, perpetual prohibition, and repelling the ḥadd, none of which is incompatible with the state of rajʿah.

If he apostatizes after consummation (masīs) and then accuses, or his accusation was of fornication before apostasy: if he performs liʿān during apostasy and then returns to Islam, his liʿān is valid — just as the liʿān of a dhimmī is valid. But if he persists in apostasy, the invalidity of his liʿān becomes evident. At that point, is the ḥadd decreed as obligatory despite the occurrence of a defective liʿān? There are two opinions whose bases we shall mention.

If he contracts a defective marriage or has intercourse under ambiguity (shubhah) and then accuses: if there is lineage that could attach and he wishes to negate it, he performs liʿān and the ḥadd is repelled — because for us, the liʿān independently achieves the purpose of negating lineage, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him). If there is no lineage, he is like a stranger — no liʿān, and upon him is the ḥadd.

If he believed the marriage valid, performed liʿān before the judge, and then its invalidity became evident — is the punishment repelled? There are two opinions, as in the case of the apostate who persists:
- One: No — because the liʿān is defective.
- The second: Yes — because the ḥadd is repelled by ambiguity (shubhah), and this is a proof established upon the belief of validity in the judge's assembly.

Then, whenever liʿān occurs in a defective marriage, there is disagreement regarding the attachment of perpetual prohibition (ḥurmat muʾabbadah) to it. Its basis is that it did not effect prohibition, so perpetuity is consequent upon prohibition — and she was already prohibited. Likewise regarding her liʿān, there is a disagreement whose summary reduces to whether she becomes exposed to the ḥadd due to his liʿān. Some said yes — because a valid proof of her fornication has been established. Others said no — because imposing the ḥadd upon her is remote from analogy (qiyās); it is confined to the purpose of vengeance against the defilement of the marriage bed, so it applies only in a valid marriage.

If he accuses within a valid marriage and then divorces her irrevocably, he may perform liʿān to repel lineage, if any, or to repel punishment — because the accusation occurred while he was excused, so liʿān was permissible for him; it does not change due to what occurs afterward.

If he accuses her within marriage of fornication before the marriage: if there is no lineage to negate through liʿān, he does not perform it. If there is, there are two opinions. The basis of prohibition is that he was deficient when he mentioned the date — he should have confined himself to the accusation and the liʿān.

If he accuses after irrevocable separation (baynūnah): if there is a child, he may perform liʿān; otherwise not — because he has accused a stranger. There is an opinion that if he attributes the fornication to the state of marriage, he performs liʿān — but this has no basis.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع

الأول إذا قذفها فلاعن  ثم أبانها ثم قذفها فلا لعان لأنه قذف بعد
البينونة وأما الحد فينظر فإن قذفها بذلك الزنا الذي لاعن عنه فلا حد ولكن
يلزمه التعزير للإيذاء ولو قذفها بزنية أخرى فقولان
أحدهما وجوب الحد كما إذا لم يتقدم لعان
والثاني لا لأنه سقطت حصانتها في حقه بحجة اللعان
ومن أصحابنا من قطع بالوجوب وقال اللعان حجة ضرورة وهو حجة قاصرة كيف وقد
عارضه لعانها فتساقطا فلا وجه لإسقاط الحصانة نعم إذا حدت ولم تلاعن ففيه
وجهان مشهوران
أما إذا قذفها بزنا منسوب إلى ما قبل اللعان سوى الزنا الذي لاعن عنه فقد
صادف حالة الحصانة فالظاهر أنه يحد وفيه وجه أن انخرام الحصانة ينعطف حكمه
على ما سبق فلا يحد في الحال وهي غير محصنة في حقه
أما إذا كان القذف من أجنبي فهو أولى بالتزام الحد لأن تسرية حكم اللعان
إلى غير الزوجين أبعد
الثاني إذا قذف أجنبية ثم نكحها ثم قذفها ففي تعدد الحد مع اتحاد المقذوف
قولان فإن قلنا يتعدد فإن لم يلاعن استوفى الحدان وإن لاعن استوفى أحدهما
وإن قلنا الحد متحد فيستوفى حد واحد وإن لاعن فإن الحد الأول لا يؤثر فيه
اللعان وإنما يندرج تحت الحد الثاني إذا استوفى
الثالث المذهب الصحيح أن النسب في ملك اليمين لا ينفى باللعان لأن اللعان
ورد في النكاح فلو اشترى زوجته الرقيقة فأتت بولد لزمان لا يحتمل أن يكون
من ملك اليمين فله النفي باللعان كما بعد البينونة بالطلاق وإن احتمل أن
يكون من النكاح وملك اليمين جميعا لم يلاعن لأن الفراش الأخير يقطع الفراش
الأول وينسخه ولذلك إذا نكحت زوجا آخر وأتت بولد لزمان يحتمل العلوق من
الأول والثاني ألحق بالثاني قطعا حتى فرع ابن
الحداد على هذا وقال لو ادعى المشتري الإستبراء بعد الوطء لم يلحقه الولد
بملك اليمين للإستبراء ولا بملك النكاح لانقطاع ذلك الفراش بفراش ملك يمين
وطابقه عليه جماهير الأصحاب وفيه وجه أنه يلحقه وأن ملك اليمين لا يقطع حكم
فراش النكاح  من كل وجه
الركن الثالث القذف المسلط على اللعان نسبتها إلى الوطء الحرام كالزنا
ولو نسبها إلى زنا هي مستكرهة فيه والواطىء زان فوجهان
أحدهما أنه يجري اللعان لنفي النسب
والثاني لا لأن القذف مخصوص في كتاب الله تعالى بالرمي الذي يحتاج فيه
إلى الشهادة وهو الزنا لأن اللعان انتقام منها وإفضاح والمستكرهة لا تستحق
ذلك
ولو نسبها إلى وطء شبهة تشتمل الشهبة الجانبين فوجهان مرتبان وأولى بان
لا يجري وقطع العراقيون بأنه لا يجري لأن الولد يمكن أن يلتحق بالواطىء
بالشبهة فيدور بينهما ويعرض على القائف فلعله يلحقه به وإنما اللعان لنفي
ولد لا يكون له نسب وهذا إنما يتجه إذا اعترف الواطىء بالشبهة بالوطء فإن
لم يعترف فلا بد من تجويز اللعان لأجل النسب
أما إذا قال ليس الولد مني ولم يضف إلى جهة ففيه تردد لأنه دائر بين
المستكرهة وبين الشبهة وبين الزنا
ولا يشترط في القذف أن يقول رأيتها تزني ولا أن يدعي الاستبراء خلافا
لمالك رحمة الله عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ذ-ف (Q-DH-F)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To throw, cast, or hurl; in juristic usage, to accuse of illicit intercourse (qadhf) — a verbal assault entailing a fixed penalty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of casting an accusation of zinā (fornication/adultery) against a chaste person; a legal act triggering either ḥadd or liʿān.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical throwing; metaphorical (majāz) — hurling an accusation, as in {«وَرَمَوْا الْمُحْصَنَاتِ»} (Q. 24:4), where "ramy" (casting) is the Quranic term for qadhf.
- Root: ل-ع-ن (L-ʿ-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To curse, banish, or expel from mercy; in legal terms, the mutual imprecation between spouses under oath.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A solemn oath procedure (muʿāranah) wherein each spouse invokes God's curse upon themselves if lying; it severs the marital bond and negates lineage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — cursing; metaphorical — the legal ritual of mutual oath-taking that substitutes for penal proof.
- Root: ح-ص-ن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fortification, protection; a chaste person (muḥṣan) is one protected by marriage, freedom, or virtue.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal status of chastity (iḥṣān) that renders one eligible for the ḥadd penalty against false accusation; its loss (inḥirām al-ḥiṣānah) nullifies the ḥadd.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a fortified place; metaphorical — the inviolable honor of a chaste person.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (idhā... fa...) and exceptions (illā, ammā) to delineate legal outcomes; the particle "fa" marks the apodosis, and "ammā" introduces contrastive cases, requiring precise parsing to preserve the juristic distinctions.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first branch — If a man accuses his wife of fornication, then performs liʿān, then divorces her irrevocably (bāʾinah), then accuses her again, no liʿān is required, because the accusation occurred after final separation (baynūnah). As for the ḥadd penalty, we examine the matter: if he accused her of the same act of zinā for which he had already performed liʿān, then no ḥadd is imposed, but he is liable to discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) for the harm caused. If he accused her of a different act of zinā, there are two opinions (qawlān): One holds that the ḥadd is obligatory, just as if no liʿān had preceded. The second holds that it is not obligatory, because her chastity (ḥiṣānah) has been nullified in his regard by virtue of the liʿān evidence. Among our companions (aṣḥāb) there are those who definitively affirmed the obligation, saying: "Liʿān is an evidence of necessity, and it is a deficient evidence. How can it be otherwise, when her own liʿān countered his, so they mutually annulled each other? There is thus no basis for nullifying chastity." However, if she was subjected to the ḥadd penalty and did not perform liʿān, then there are two well-known aspects (wajhān).

As for the case where he accused her of zinā attributed to a time before the liʿān, other than the specific act for which he performed liʿān — this accusation encountered her in a state of chastity, so the apparent ruling is that he is subject to the ḥadd. There is also an aspect that the nullification of chastity (inḥirām al-ḥiṣānah) retroactively applies its ruling to what preceded, so he is not penalized in the present, since she is not chaste in his regard.

As for the case where the accusation comes from a stranger (ajnabī), he is even more deserving of the ḥadd penalty, because extending the ruling of liʿān to non-spouses is more remote.

The second branch — If a man accused a foreign woman (ajnabiyyah), then married her, then accused her again, there are two opinions regarding whether the ḥadd is multiplied while the accused person is one. If we say it is multiplied, then: if he did not perform liʿān, both penalties are exacted; if he performed liʿān, only one of them is exacted. If we say the ḥadd is singular, then only one penalty is exacted; and if he performed liʿān, the first ḥadd is not affected by the liʿān — rather, it is subsumed under the second ḥadd when it is exacted.

The third branch — The correct doctrine (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that lineage (nasab) in the case of a slave-woman (milk al-yamīn) is not negated by liʿān, because liʿān was legislated specifically for marriage (nikāḥ). Thus, if a man purchased his own wife who was a slave-girl, and she gave birth to a child at a time that cannot possibly be attributed to his ownership of her (milk al-yamīn), then he may negate the lineage through liʿān, just as after final separation by divorce. But if the time could possibly be attributed to both the marriage and the ownership, he does not perform liʿān, because the later bed (al-firāsh al-ākhir) severs the earlier bed and abrogates it. For this reason, if a woman married another husband and gave birth at a time that could possibly be from conception by either the first or the second, the child is definitively attributed to the second. Indeed, Ibn al-Ḥaddād derived a subsidiary ruling from this, saying: "If the purchaser claims istibrāʾ (the waiting period to ensure the womb is empty) after intercourse, the child is not attributed to him through milk al-yamīn because of the istibrāʾ, nor through the marriage, because that bed was severed by the bed of milk al-yamīn." The majority of our companions concurred with him. There is an aspect that the child is attributed to him, and that milk al-yamīn does not sever the ruling of the marriage bed in every respect.

The third pillar — The qadhf that authorizes liʿān is the attribution of the act to unlawful intercourse, such as zinā. If he attributed it to zinā in which she was coerced (mustakrahah), while the one who had intercourse with her was a fornicator, there are two aspects: One holds that liʿān proceeds to negate the lineage. The second holds that it does not, because qadhf in the Book of God Almighty is specifically restricted to the accusation that requires testimony — namely, zinā — because liʿān is a punishment against her and a public disgrace, and the coerced woman does not deserve that.

If he attributed it to intercourse under doubtful circumstances (shubhah) involving doubt on both sides, there are two ordered aspects, and it is even more appropriate that liʿān does not proceed. The Iraqis definitively ruled that it does not proceed, because the child could potentially be attributed to the one who had intercourse under doubt, so the child's lineage oscillates between the two, and the matter is referred to the physiognomist (qāʾif) — perhaps he will attribute it to him. Liʿān is only for negating a child who has no lineage at all. This reasoning holds only if the one who had intercourse admits to the doubtful intercourse; if he does not admit, then liʿān must be permitted for the sake of the lineage.

As for the case where he said, "This child is not from me," without attributing it to any specific cause — there is hesitation (taraddud), because the matter oscillates between coercion, doubtful intercourse, and zinā.

It is not a condition for qadhf that he say, "I saw her committing zinā," nor that he claim istibrāʾ — contrary to Mālik, may God have mercy on him.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثالث في فروع متفرقة

وهي خمسة
الأول إذا قذفها بأجنبي تعرض لحد الأجنبي فإن لاعن سقط عنه الحد عند
الشافعي رضي الله عنه لأنه أقام حجة على عين تلك الزنية فصدق من وجه والحد
يسقط بالشبهة وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله أثر اللعان مقصور على الزوجين فلا
يتعدى إلى الأجنبي
وهذا إذا ذكره في اللعان فإن لم يذكره في اللعان فقولان
أحدهما السقوط للشبهة ولقصة العجلاني فإنه لم يذكر شريك بن السحماء في
اللعان وذكره في القذف
والثاني يجب وهو القياس لأنه لم يقم عليه حجة
وأما ابن السحماء فلعله لم يطلب ونشأ من هذا نظر وهو أنه عليه السلام لم
ينبه ابن السحماء على ثبوت حد القذف له فذكر صاحب التقريب وجهين في أن من
قذف عند القاضي فهل على القاضي أن ينبه المقذوف
أحدهما لا لقصة شريك بن السحماء
والثاني نعم لقصة العسيف إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
واغد يا أنيس على امرأة  هذا فإن اعترفت فارجمها إذ لم يكن الغرض إقرارها
للرجم بل إنكارها ليثبت حد القذف
الثاني إذا قذف نسوة بكلمة واحدة ففي تعدد الحد قولان فإن قذف امرأته
وأجنبية بكلمة واحدة فقولان مرتبان وأولى بالتعدد لانقسام حكمهما في اللعان
ولو قال لزوجته يا زانية بنت الزانية فقد قذفها وأمها بكلمتين فعليه حدان
وهل يقدم حد المقذوف أولا فيه وجهان
أحدهما نعم كما لو قتل شخصين
والثاني لا كما لو أتلف مال شخصين
فإن قلنا يقدم ففي مسألتنا المقدم البنت فيقدم الحد أو اللعان وقيل إن
الأم ها هنا تقدم لأن حق البنت يعرض للسقوط باللعان دون الأم ثم مهما
حددناه بواحد
أمهلناه حتى يبرأ جلده ولا نوالي بين الحدود ولو قذف أربع نسوة بكلمة
واحدة وقلنا يتحد الحد ففي تعدد اللعان وجهان ينظر في أحدهما إلى اتحاد
الصيغة والملاعن وفي الثاني إلى تعدد النسوة مع أن هذه حجة تبعد عن التداخل
فإن قلنا يتحد اللعان فذلك ينفع إذا توافقن في الطلب أو قلنا لا يشترط
طلبهن اللعان فإن طلبت واحدة وقلنا يشترط طلبها فلا بد من اللعان عنه ثم
يستأنف لعانا للباقيات وحيث قلنا يتعدد فلو رضين بلعان واحد فلا أثر لرضاهن
وكذلك لو رضي جماعة من المدعين بيمين واحدة لم يؤثر ذلك في تغيير وصف الحجج
أما إذا قذف امرأة واحدة مرتين بزنيتين ففي تعدد الحد واللعان أيضا خلاف
لاتحاد المقذوف وتعدد الصيغة
الثالث إذا ادعت عليه القذف فأنكر فأقامت البينة فأراد اللعان فإن كان قد
أنكر بالسكوت أو قال أردت بالإنكار أنه لم يكن قذفا بل كان حقا فله اللعان
وإن لم يؤول إنكاره فوجهان
أحدهما لا لأنه أنكر القذف ولا لعان إلا بقذف لينشيء قذفا إن أراد
ويستفيد به درء حد القذف الذي ثبت بالبينة أيضا
والثاني أنه يلاعن وإنكاره يحمل على المعتاد في الخصومات كما لو ادعى
عليه ملك فقال اشتريته من زيد وكان يملكه فانتزع من يده بالبينة فرجع على
زيد بالثمن ولا يؤخذ بإقراره  له بالملك
أما إذا قال ما قذفتك وما زنيت فلا يلاعن إلا إذا أنشأ قذفا بالزنا يحتمل
أن يكون قد
طرأ بعد شهادته لها بالبراءة فإن لم يحتمل فلا يلاعن وأطلق القاضي القول
بجواز اللعان
الرابع إذا امتنع الزوج عن اللعان او الزوجة فعرضناهما للحد فرجعا إلى
اللعان مكناهما من ذلك وليس هذا كاليمين لا يجوز الرجوع إليها بعد النكول
بل يلحق اللعان بالبينة في هذا المعنى ولو قال بعد أن حد ألاعن قال الأصحاب
لم يمكن لأنه لا فائدة قال القفال إن كان ثم ولد يمكن منه وإلا فلا
الخامس إذا قال زنيت وأنت مجنونة او أمة أو مشركة وعهد لها تلك الحال فلا
يجب إلا التعزير وكان كما لو أضاف إلى الصغر وإن لم يعهد ولم يقم الزوج
عليه بينة سقطت الإضافة وعليه الحد وفيه وجه أنه لا حد لأنه إذا انتفى تلك
الحال انتفى المضاف إليه
ولو قال زنيت مستكرهة ففي وجوب التعزير خلاف لأن ذلك يعيرها وإن لم
يسنبها إلى معصية ثم الصحيح أنه يلاعن لدفع التعزير كما يلاعن لدفع الحد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ذ-ف (q-dh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cast or hurl (a stone, word, or accusation); the core sense is forceful projection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the specific act of false accusation of unlawful intercourse (qadhf), carrying a fixed penalty (ḥadd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical casting; metaphorical (majāz) for verbal accusation, here fixed as a technical legal term.
- Root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To curse, banish, or repel; in legal context, the mutual imprecation (liʿān) between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The oath-swearing procedure that substitutes for the ḥadd penalty, establishing perjury as a ground for divine curse.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal cursing; metaphorical for the legal ritual of mutual oath-taking that separates spouses.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Similarity, ambiguity, or confusion between two things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, the legal doubt (shubhah) that averts fixed penalties (ḥudūd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal resemblance; metaphorical for juridical uncertainty that mitigates punishment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The particle "in" (if) governs protasis-apodosis structures, while "illā" (except) restricts the scope of the preceding negative, crucial for parsing legal conditions and exceptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third chapter concerns miscellaneous branches, and they are five.

**The First Branch:** If a man accuses his wife of fornication with a specific outsider (ajnabī), he exposes himself to the ḥadd penalty of the outsider. If he then performs the liʿān, the ḥadd penalty is dropped from him according to al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him), because he has established a proof (ḥujjah) upon that very act of fornication, and thus he is believed from one aspect, and the ḥadd penalty is dropped by virtue of legal doubt (shubhah). Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The effect of the liʿān is confined to the two spouses and does not extend to the outsider.

This applies when he mentions the outsider in the liʿān. If he does not mention him in the liʿān, there are two opinions (qawlān): One is that the penalty drops due to the legal doubt and due to the story of al-ʿAjlānī, for he did not mention Sharīk ibn al-Saḥmāʾ in the liʿān but mentioned him in the accusation (qadhf). The second is that the penalty is obligatory, and this is the analogical ruling (qiyās), because he has not established a proof against him.

As for Ibn al-Saḥmāʾ, perhaps he did not demand [his right]. From this arose a consideration: The Prophet (peace be upon him) did not alert Ibn al-Saḥmāʾ to the establishment of the ḥadd penalty of qadhf in his favor. Thus, the author of al-Taqrīb mentioned two aspects (wajhayn) regarding one who accuses another before a judge: Is the judge obligated to alert the accused party [of his right to demand the penalty]? One aspect: No, due to the story of Sharīk ibn al-Saḥmāʾ. The second: Yes, due to the story of al-ʿAsīf, when he (peace be upon him) said: {«واغد يا أنيس على امرأة هذا فإن اعترفت فارجمها»} — "Go early, O Unays, to the wife of this man, and if she confesses, then stone her." For the purpose was not her confession leading to stoning, but rather her denial, so that the ḥadd penalty of qadhf might be established.

**The Second Branch:** If a man accuses multiple women with a single word, there are two opinions regarding the multiplicity of the ḥadd penalty. If he accuses his wife and an outsider woman with a single word, there are two opinions, arranged hierarchically, and multiplicity is more appropriate due to the division of their rulings in the liʿān.

If he says to his wife: "O fornicatress, daughter of a fornicatress," he has accused her and her mother with two words, and two ḥadd penalties are due upon him. Is the penalty of the accused one presented first, or not? There are two aspects (wajhān): One is yes, just as if he killed two persons. The second is no, just as if he destroyed the property of two persons. If we say the first is presented, then in our case the presented one is the daughter — is the ḥadd penalty or the liʿān presented? It was said that the mother here is presented, because the right of the daughter is susceptible to dropping by the liʿān, unlike the mother. Then, whenever we impose a ḥadd penalty upon him for one, we grant him respite until his skin heals, and we do not administer the penalties consecutively.

If he accuses four women with a single word, and we say the ḥadd penalty is single, then regarding the multiplicity of the liʿān there are two aspects: In one, consideration is given to the unity of the utterance (ṣīghah) and the one who performs the liʿān; in the second, consideration is given to the multiplicity of the women, even though this proof (ḥujjah) is far from overlapping (tadākhul). If we say the liʿān is single, that benefits when they agree in their demand, or if we say their demand for the liʿān is not a condition. If one of them demands it, and we say her demand is a condition, then the liʿān must be performed for her, and then a new liʿān is initiated for the rest. Wherever we say it is multiple, if they consent to a single liʿān, their consent has no effect. Likewise, if a group of claimants consent to a single oath, that does not affect the alteration of the description of the proofs.

As for when he accuses a single woman twice with two acts of fornication, there is also disagreement regarding the multiplicity of the ḥadd penalty and the liʿān, due to the unity of the accused and the multiplicity of the utterance.

**The Third Branch:** If she claims qadhf against him, and he denies it, and she then establishes evidence (bayyinah), and he wishes to perform the liʿān — if he denied by silence, or said: "By my denial I meant that it was not a qadhf but rather true," then he may perform the liʿān. If he does not interpret his denial [in this way], there are two aspects: One is that he may not, because he denied the qadhf, and there is no liʿān except by a qadhf, so let him initiate a qadhf if he wishes, and thereby derive the benefit of averting the ḥadd penalty of qadhf that was established by the evidence. The second is that he may perform the liʿān, and his denial is interpreted according to the customary manner in litigation, just as if someone claimed ownership against him and he said: "I bought it from Zayd who owned it," and it was then wrested from his hand by evidence, he may then recourse against Zayd for the price, and he is not bound by his admission of Zayd's ownership.

As for when he says: "I did not accuse you, and you did not fornicate," he may not perform the liʿān unless he initiates a qadhf of fornication that could plausibly have occurred after her testimony of innocence. If it is not plausible, he may not perform the liʿān. Al-Qāḍī gave an unqualified ruling permitting the liʿān.

**The Fourth Branch:** If the husband refrains from the liʿān, or the wife does, and we present them for the ḥadd penalty, and then they return to the liʿān, we enable them to do so. This is not like the oath (yamīn), to which return is not permitted after refusal (nukūl). Rather, the liʿān is likened to the evidence (bayyinah) in this regard. If he says after being penalized: "I will perform the liʿān," the companions (al-aṣḥāb) said: He is not enabled, because there is no benefit. Al-Qaffāl said: If there is a child, he may be enabled; otherwise, no.

**The Fifth Branch:** If he says: "You fornicated while you were insane, or a slave-woman, or a polytheist," and that state was known of her, then only discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) is obligatory, just as if he attributed it to her minority. If that state was not known, and the husband does not establish evidence for it, the attribution is dropped and the ḥadd penalty is due upon him. There is an aspect that no ḥadd penalty is due, because when that state is negated, the attributed [qualifier] is negated.

If he says: "You fornicated under coercion," there is disagreement regarding the obligation of taʿzīr, because that defames her, even though he does not attribute to her a sin. Then the correct view is that he performs the liʿān to avert the taʿzīr, just as he performs the liʿān to avert the ḥadd penalty.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الركن الرابع في صيغة اللعان

والنظر في أصله وتغليظاته وسننه
النظر الأول في أصل كلماته وهو أن يقول الزوج أربع مرات أشهد بالله إني
لمن الصادقين فيما رميتها به من الزنا وإن الولد من الزنا وليس مني إن كان
ثم ولد ويقول في الخامسة لعنة الله علي إن كنت من الكاذبين فيما رميتها به
وتقابله المرأة فتشهد أربع مرات بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين فيما رماها به من
الزنا وتقول في الخامسة غضب الله علي إن كان من الصادقين فيما رماني به
ويجب على الزوج إعادة نفي الولد في كل شهادة فإن تركها مرة لم تحسب
ولا يجب على المرأة إعادة أمر الولد إذ لا يتعلق إثباته بلعانها ولا تقوم
عندنا معظم الكلمات مقام الكل خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
والصحيح أنه يتعين لفظ الشهادة فلا يجوز إبدالها بالحلف وأنه يتعين لفظ
اللعن والغضب من الجانبين  ويجب رعاية الترتيب بتأخير اللعن والغضب وتجب
الموالاة بين
الكلمات وكل ذلك ميل إلى التعبد لخروج الأمر عن القياس وفيه وجه أنه يجوز
إبدال الشهادة بالقسم وإبدال اللعن بالغضب وكذا عكسه وأن الترتيب والموالاة
لا تشترط وكل ذلك تشوف إلى اتباع المعنى

### | فروع ثلاثة

الأول يصح عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه لعان الأخرس وقذفه خلافا لأبي حنيفة
رحمه الله مع أن الأصح أنه لا تقبل شهادته ولكن يغلب مشابه اليمين في
اللعان ولكن لا يمكن فهم اللعن والغضب منه وهو تعبد لفظي فالطريق أن يكلف
الكتبة مع الإشارة إن قدر أو يقول له ناطق لعنة الله عليك إن كان كذا فيقول
نعم
أما إذا اعتقل لسانه بعد القذف وقال أهل الصناعة إنه سينطلق لسانه على
قرب أمهلناه كذلك قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه ومن الأصحاب من قال لا مزيد في
مهلته على ثلاثة أيام إذ تأخير حد القذف إضرار بالمقذوف
ومهما لاعن بالإشارة ثم انطلق لسانه فقال لم أرد قذفا ولا لعانا لم يقبل
الثاني الأعجمي العاجز عن العربية يلقن معنى اللعن والغضب بلسانه كما في
كلمة التكبير والنكاح
ثم القاضي ينصب ترجمانا ولا بد من العدد لأنه في حكم شهادة وهل يكتفي
باثنين أم لا بد من أربع لما فيه من إثبات زناها فيه خلاف
الثالث لو مات الزوج في أثناء كلمات اللعان لم ينقطع النكاح ولحق النسب
ولم تقم الورثة مقامه في اللعان أصلا
وإن ماتت المرأة في خلال لعانه استكمل الزوج إن كان ثم ولد فإن لم يكن
فلا حاجة إلى لعانه إن قلنا إن الزوج يرث حد القذف ويتضمن سقوط بعضه سقوط
الكل

### | النظر الثاني في التغليطات

وهي بالزمان والمكان والجمع
أما الزمان فبأن يؤخر إلى بعد العصر فإنه وقت شريف وإن لم يكن طلب حثيث
فإلى العصر من يوم الجمعة
أما المكان فبأن يلاعن في أشرف المواضع فإن لاعن وهو بمكة فبين الركن
والمقام وبالمدينة فبين المنبر والقبر وبالقدس عند الصخرة وفي سائر البلاد
في  مقصورة الجامع ويلاعن الذمي في أفضل موضع عندهم من بيعة وكنيسة سوى بيوت
الأصنام فلا يأتيها أصلا وفي بيوت النيران للمجوس خلاف والظاهر أن الزنديق
يغلظ عليه بهذه الجهات ليناله شؤمه وإن لم يعتقده والحائض تلاعن على باب
المسجد واعترض المزني رحمه الله وقال جوز للمشركة اللعان في المسجد وربما
تكون حائضا
واختلفوا في المشرك الجنب فمنهم من قال لا يؤاخذون بتفصيل شرعنا في
الأحكام وإن كانوا يؤاخذون عند الله تعالى
أما الجمع فلا بد من حضور جماعة لقوله تعالى {وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من
المؤمنين} ولا ينبغي أن ينقصوا عن عدد شهادة الزنا
والتغليظ بالمكان مستحب أو مستحق فيه قولان وفي التغليظ بالزمان والجمع
طريقان منهم من قطع بالإستحباب ومنهم من قال قولان
أما جريان ذلك في مجلس الحكم فشرط قطعا فلو تلاعنا في البيت لم يصح إلا
عند المحكم على قول جواز التحكيم في العقوبات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ع-ن (la-ʿa-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to curse, to drive away from mercy," and in the context of liʿān, it denotes the formal invocation of divine malediction upon oneself if one is lying.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic and legal context, it is the solemn oath of condemnation exchanged between spouses, tied to the divine decree in {«وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ»} (Q. 24:6), establishing a ritual of mutual accusation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally (ḥaqīqah) it is "cursing"; metaphorically (majāz) in jurisprudence, it is the entire legal procedure of imprecation, where the utterance substitutes for penal proof.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To testify, to bear witness, to be present; the root implies ocular or declarative attestation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) as a legal act of truth-assertion, here elevated to a quasi-oath in liʿān, distinct from ordinary witnessing due to its repetitive and ritualized form.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): In liʿān, "shahādah" is used literally as "testifying," but its function is metaphorical—it operates as an oath (yamīn) rather than evidentiary testimony, since it is not subject to cross-examination.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Conditional Suspension) — The conditional particle "in" (if) governs the apodosis, as in "إن كان ثم ولد" (if there is a child), requiring the protasis to precede the legal effect, and the repetition of the negation "ليس مني" (he is not from me) to be syntactically bound to each testimony for validity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth pillar concerns the formulary of mutual imprecation (ṣīghat al-liʿān). The inquiry into it covers its foundational words, its aggravations (taghlīẓāt), and its customary practices (sunan).

**The First Inquiry: The Foundational Utterances**

Know that the foundational words are that the husband says four times: "I testify by God that I am indeed among the truthful in what I have accused her of regarding adultery, and that the child is from adultery and is not from me—if there is a child." Then he says in the fifth [utterance]: "May the curse of God be upon me if I am among the liars in what I have accused her of." The woman then responds to him, testifying four times by God that he is indeed among the liars in what he accused her of regarding adultery, and she says in the fifth: "May the wrath of God be upon me if he is among the truthful in what he accused me of."

It is obligatory upon the husband to repeat the negation of the child's lineage in every testimony; if he omits it once, that [testimony] is not counted. It is not obligatory upon the woman to repeat the matter of the child, since the affirmation of the child's lineage is not tied to her imprecation. In our school, the majority of the words do not stand in place of the whole, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him).

The correct position is that the specific wording of "testimony" (shahādah) is mandated, and it is not permissible to substitute it with a mere oath (ḥalif). Likewise, the specific wording of "curse" (laʿn) and "wrath" (ghaḍab) is mandated from both sides. Observing the order is obligatory, by delaying the curse and wrath [to the fifth utterance], and continuity (muwālāh) between the words is obligatory. All of this leans toward devotional adherence (taʿabbud), because the matter departs from analogical reasoning (qiyās). There is another view that it is permissible to substitute "testimony" with "oath" and "curse" with "wrath," and likewise the reverse, and that order and continuity are not stipulated—all of this leaning toward following the underlying meaning (maʿnā).

**Three Subsidiary Branches**

**The First:** According to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him), the imprecation of the mute person and his accusation [of adultery] are valid, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him). This is despite the fact that the more correct view is that his testimony is not accepted; however, the resemblance to an oath (yamīn) predominates in liʿān. But since the understanding of "curse" and "wrath" cannot be grasped from him—and this is a verbal devotional act—the method is to require him to write with a gesture, if he is able, or a speaking person says to him: "The curse of God be upon you if it is such," and he replies "Yes."

As for when his tongue is seized after the accusation, and the experts in the craft say his tongue will be released shortly, we grant him a delay—likewise said al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him). Some of our companions said: his delay should not exceed three days, since postponing the ḥadd punishment for false accusation (qadhf) harms the accused woman.

Whenever he performs liʿān by gesture, then his tongue is released and he says, "I did not intend an accusation nor an imprecation," it is not accepted from him.

**The Second:** The non-Arab who is incapable of Arabic is taught the meaning of "curse" and "wrath" in his own tongue, just as in the word of the takbīr and marriage contract. Then the judge appoints a translator. The number [of witnesses] is indispensable because it is in the category of testimony (shahādah). Is it sufficient to have two, or must there be four, given that it involves affirming her adultery? There is a difference of opinion on this.

**The Third:** If the husband dies during the utterances of the liʿān, the marriage is not severed, the lineage is attributed [to him], and the heirs do not stand in his place in the liʿān at all. If the wife dies during his liʿān, the husband completes it if there is a child; if there is no child, then there is no need for his liʿān—if we hold that the husband inherits the ḥadd of qadhf, and that the dropping of part of it entails the dropping of the whole.

**The Second Inquiry: The Aggravations (Taghlīẓāt)**

These are by time, place, and congregation.

As for **time**: it is to delay until after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr), for it is a noble time; if there is no urgent request, then until the ʿaṣr of Friday.

As for **place**: he performs liʿān in the most honorable locations. If he performs it while in Mecca, then between the Corner (al-Rukn) and the Station of Abraham (al-Maqām); in Medina, between the pulpit (minbar) and the grave [of the Prophet]; in Jerusalem, at the Rock (al-Ṣakhrah); and in all other lands, in the enclosed prayer area (maqṣūrah) of the congregational mosque. A dhimmī performs liʿān in the most virtuous place according to them, whether a synagogue or church, except for houses of idols—he does not enter them at all. Regarding fire-temples for the Magians, there is a difference of opinion. The apparent view is that a zindīq (heretic) is aggravated upon by these means so that its ill-omen afflicts him, even if he does not believe in it. A menstruating woman performs liʿān at the door of the mosque. Al-Muzanī (may God have mercy on him) objected, saying: "You have permitted a polytheist woman to perform liʿān in the mosque, and she might be menstruating."

They differed concerning a polytheist in a state of major ritual impurity (junub): some said they are not held accountable for the details of our sacred law in worldly rulings, even if they are held accountable before God Almighty.

As for **congregation**: the presence of a group is indispensable, due to His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَائِفَةٌ مِّنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ»} (And let a group of the believers witness their punishment—Q. 24:2). They should not be fewer than the number required for the testimony of adultery (i.e., four).

Regarding aggravation by place, there are two opinions: is it recommended (mustaḥabb) or obligatory (mustaḥaqq)? Regarding aggravation by time and congregation, there are two paths: some definitively state it is recommended, and others say there are two opinions.

As for the occurrence of all this in the court of judgment (majlis al-ḥukm), it is a condition without doubt. If they perform liʿān in a house, it is not valid—except before an arbitrator (muḥakkam), according to the view permitting arbitration in penal matters.

### | النظر الثالث في السنن

وهي ثلاثة
الأول أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لاعن بين العجلاني وزوجته على
المنبر فقيل كان العجلاني على المنبر ولعله الأليق للشهرة
وقيل كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على المنبر فعلى هذا يسن للقاضي صعود
المنبر
الثاني أن يهدد كل واحد من الزوجين ويخوفهما بالله فلعلهما يتصادقان
فيقول للرجل ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
أيما رجل جحد ولده وهو ينظر إليه احتجب الله عنه وفضحه على رءوس الأولين
والآخرين ويروي للمرأة قوله عليه السلام
أيما امرأة أدخلت على قوم من ليس منهم فليست من الله في شيء ولن يدخلها
الله جنته وحديث
المعراج أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بنسوة معلقات بثديهن فقال لجبريل عليه
السلام من هؤلاء فقال جبريل عليه السلام هن اللاتي ألحقن بأزواجهن من ليس
منهم يأكل حرائبهم وينظر إلى عوراتهم
الثالث أن يأتي الرجل عند الخامسة رجل من ورائه فيضع يده على فيه ويقول
صاحب المجلس للملاعن اتق الله فإنها موجبة والمرأة تأتيها امرأة من ورائها
ويقال لها كذلك والله  أعلم
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثالث في جوامع أحكام اللعان وحكم الولد
خاصة - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
أما أحكام اللعان فخمسة وقوع التفرقة وتأبد الحرمة وسقوط حد القذف
وانتفاء النسب ووجوب حد الزنا عليها وجملة ذلك تتعلق بلعان الزوج ولا يتعلق
بلعانها إلا سقوط الحد عنها وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله الفرقة تتعلق
بلعانهما وقضاء القاضي وقال مالك رحمه الله تتعلق بلعانهما
ولا يجب الحد عليها بلعانه عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله ولا تتأبد الحرمة
عنده بل يحل له نكاحها مهما كذب نفسه أو خرج عن أهلية الشهادة بأن يخرس أو
يحد في
القذف نعم اختلف أصحابنا في أن هذه الحرمة هل تشتمل ملك اليمين وهل تتعلق
باللعان في النكاح الفاسد وبعد البينونة
أما حكم الولد وانتفائه ولحوقه ففيه ثلاثة فصول

### | الفصل الأول فيمن يلحقه النسب

وهو كل من يمكن أن يولد له والنظر في الصبي والمجبوب والخصي
أما الصبي فإمكان العلوق منه بعد كمال السنة العاشرة فيلحقه ولد أتت به
زوجته لستة أشهر بعد السنة العاشرة وقيل يمكن العلوق في أثناء العاشرة
ويلحقه الولد بعد العاشرة
ومهما أتت به قبل الإمكان لم يفتقر إلى اللعان إذ لا يلحقه ومهما لحقه
فقال ألاعن وأنا بالغ يمكن منه فلو قال أنا صبي وألاعن لم يمكن ولو قال
كذبت وأنا بالغ فألاعن قبل منه لأن الصبي لا يعرف بلوغه إلا بقوله
أما المجبوب الذكر الباقي الأنثيين فالولد يلحقه لبقاء أوعية المني فيحمل
انزلاق المني ويحتمل استدخال مائه
أما المنزوع الأنثيين الباقي ذكره فقطع المحققون بلحوق الولد لبقاء
اللآلة وقال الفوراني يرجع فيه إلى الأطباء
وأما الممسوح ذكره وأنثياه ففيه وجهان أظهرهما أنه لا يلحقه الولد إذ
التجربة تدل على استحالة الإعلاق منه
وحيث قضينا بأنه لا إمكان فلا حاجة إلى اللعان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ع-ن (la-ʿa-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to curse, to drive away from mercy," and in juristic context, the mutual imprecation between spouses (liʿān) invoking divine curse upon the liar.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, it denotes the formal oath-ritual of mutual anathema, distinct from mere testimony, as a judicial means to resolve accusations of adultery without witnesses.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the act of cursing; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to the entire legal procedure of mutual imprecation, where the curse stands as a substitute for penal evidence.
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes relation, lineage, or attribution; in genealogy, it signifies the legal affiliation of a child to a father.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, it concerns the establishment or negation of paternity (nasab), a status affecting inheritance, guardianship, and marital prohibitions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is kinship by blood; metaphorical usage extends to legal attribution, such as the child's affiliation through a valid marriage contract.
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to forbid, to make sacred or prohibited"; in this context, it denotes the perpetual prohibition of marital relations.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, it signifies a divine injunction rendering an act unlawful; here, it marks the permanent severance of marital permissibility.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is the state of being forbidden; metaphorical usage applies to the enduring legal consequence of liʿān, where the prohibition persists even after retraction.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if he retracts" or "if he becomes mute") and exceptions (e.g., "except by his own statement") to delineate legal outcomes, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine juristic applicability.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third consideration concerns the sunnahs [of liʿān], and they are three.

The first: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conducted the mutual imprecation between al-ʿAjlānī and his wife upon the minbar. It was said that al-ʿAjlānī was upon the minbar, and perhaps this is more fitting for public notoriety. And it was said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was upon the minbar; upon this view, it is a sunnah for the judge to ascend the minbar.

The second: That the judge threatens each of the two spouses and frightens them with God, so that perhaps they may both speak truthfully. He says to the man what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Any man who denies his child while he looks upon him, God will veil Himself from him and disgrace him before the first and the last." And it is narrated for the woman his saying, peace be upon him: "Any woman who brings into a people one who is not of them, she has nothing to do with God, and God will never admit her into His Paradise." And the hadith of the Night Journey (al-miʿrāj): that he, peace be upon him, passed by women suspended by their breasts, and he said to Gabriel, peace be upon him, "Who are these?" Gabriel, peace be upon him, said, "These are the women who attached to their husbands those who were not of them, consuming their inheritances (ḥarāʾib) and looking upon their private parts."

The third: That when the man reaches the fifth [oath], a man comes from behind him and places his hand over his mouth, and the master of the session says to the one performing liʿān: "Fear God, for it is a cause of obligation." And the woman is approached by a woman from behind her, and the same is said to her. And God knows best.

— May God bless him and grant him peace — The Third Chapter: On the Comprehensive Rulings of Liʿān and the Ruling of the Child Specifically.

As for the rulings of liʿān, they are five: the occurrence of separation, the perpetuity of prohibition, the dropping of the hadd punishment for qadhf (false accusation of adultery), the negation of lineage, and the obligation of the hadd punishment for adultery upon her. The totality of that is attached to the husband's liʿān, and nothing is attached to her liʿān except the dropping of the hadd punishment from her. Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: The separation is attached to both of their liʿān and to the judge's ruling. And Mālik, may God have mercy on him, said: It is attached to both of their liʿān. And the hadd punishment is not obligatory upon her by his liʿān according to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, nor does the prohibition become perpetual in his view; rather, it becomes lawful for him to marry her whenever he retracts his accusation against himself, or he exits from the qualification of testimony—such as by becoming mute or being flogged for qadhf. Yes, our companions differed as to whether this prohibition encompasses the possession of the right hand (milk al-yamīn), and whether it attaches to liʿān in a corrupt marriage (nikāḥ fāsid) and after the final separation (baynūnah).

As for the ruling of the child—its negation and its attachment—there are three chapters concerning it.

### | The First Chapter: On Whom the Lineage Attaches

It attaches to anyone from whom birth is possible. The consideration concerns the young boy, the one whose male organ is severed but testicles remain (majbūb), and the eunuch (khaṣī).

As for the young boy: the possibility of impregnation from him [is established] after the completion of the tenth year. Thus, a child brought by his wife six months after the tenth year attaches to him. And it was said: impregnation is possible during the tenth year, and the child attaches to him after the tenth year. Whenever she brings a child before the possibility [of impregnation], there is no need for liʿān, since it does not attach to him. And whenever it attaches to him, and he says, "I will perform liʿān, and I am an adult capable of it," it is possible. But if he says, "I am a young boy, and I will perform liʿān," it is not possible. And if he says, "I have accused her falsely, and I am an adult," then he performs liʿān, it is accepted from him, because the young boy's adulthood is not known except by his own statement.

As for the one whose male organ is severed but whose testicles remain: the child attaches to him, because the vessels of semen remain, so the emission of semen is possible, and the retention of his fluid is conceivable.

As for the one whose testicles are removed but whose male organ remains: the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) have definitively ruled the attachment of the child, due to the remaining organ. Al-Fūrānī said: The matter is referred to physicians.

As for the one whose male organ and testicles are both crushed (mamsūḥ): there are two positions. The more apparent of them is that the child does not attach to him, since experience indicates the impossibility of impregnation from him. And wherever we have ruled that there is no possibility, there is no need for liʿān.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في أحوال الولد

وله ثلاثة أحوال
الحالة الأولى أن يكون حملا وهل يجوز نفيه باللعان قبل الإنفصال فيه
قولان
أحدهما لا لأن الحمل لا يتيقن فلعله ريح ينفش
والثاني نعم لأنه يظن ظنا غالبا وفي التأخير خطر موت الزوج ولحوق النسب
وهذا بعد البينونة أما في صلب النكاح فالصحيح أنه يلاعن لأن العجلاني لاعن
عن الحمل ولأن اللعان دون الولد لمجرد قطع النكاح جائز وقيل بطرد القولين
ولا وجه له وقد بنى الأصحاب القولين على أن الحمل هل يعرف بقينا وهو ضعيف
بل الصحيح أنه لا يعرف يقينا ولكن الأحكام منها ما يثبت بالنظر ومنها ما لا
يثبت ومنها ما يتردد فيه فلأجل ذلك اختلف قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه في بعض
المسائل لا لتردده في أن الحمل لا يتيقن
الحالة الثانية أن يكونا توأمين من بطن واحد فلا يتبعض نفيهما فإن اقتصر
على نفي أحدهما لم ينتف مع لحوق الثاني ولو نفاهما واستلحق أحدهما لحقه
الثاني ولو نفى الحمل فأتت بتوأمين انتفيا ولو أتت بواحد في النكاح فلاعن
فأتت بثان لأكثر من ستة أشهر لحقه الثاني دون الأول لأنه من بطن أخرى
ويحتمل العلوق بعد انفصال الأول وقبل اللعان ولو نفى الحمل فأتت بولد ثم
أتت بآخر لأكثر من ستة أشهر انتفى من غير لعان لأنه لا يحتمل العلوق به في
صلب النكاح
فرعان
أحدهما أنه مهما أراد أن ينفي أولادا عدة يكفيه لعان واحد ولا يحتاج كل
واحد إلى لعان
الثاني أن التوأمين المنفيين باللعان أخوان من الأم وهل يتوارثان بأخوة
الأب فيه وجهان
أحدهما لا لأن اللعان أبطل الأبوة
والثاني نعم لأن اللعان أثره قاصر عن الملاعن
الحالة الثالثة أن يموت الولد فله أن يلاعن لأن الموت لا يقطع النسب وقال
أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ليس له ذلك إلا إذا كان للولد ولد حي
ثم عندنا مهما استلحقه بعد اللعان لحقه فلو نفاه فلما مات استلحقه ليحوز
ميراثه لحقه وورث مع التهمة لأن الأصل هو النسب ويلحق بمجرد قوله والميراث
تابع وكذلك لو نفاه بعد الموت فلما قسم ميراثه عاد واستلحقه فالظاهر أنه
يلحقه ويسترد نصيبه من الميراث نظرا إلى ثبوت النسب وفيه وجه أنه  إذا سقط
الميراث لم يرجع إليه

### | الفصل الثالث فيما يسقط حق النفي

والصحيح أنه على الفور لأنه في حكم ضرار يدفع بعد معرفته فلا وجه للتأخير
وفيه قول آخر لا بأس به أنه يمهل ريثما يتروى فإن الأمر فيه خطر ولعله
يتقدر بثلاثة أيام وحكي قول ثالث أنه لا يسقط إلا بالاستلحاق وهذا بعيد
والتفريع على أنه على الفور فعلى هذا لا يعذر إلا إذا لم تحصل له حقيقة
المعرفة فلو صبر حتى ينفصل الحمل جاز لأنه لا يتيقن فربما يكون ريحا فينفش
فلو قال عرفت الحمل ولكن قلت ربما تجهض فهل يبطل حقه فيه وجهان
ولو أخبره فاجر بالولادة فقال لم أصدقه جاز وإن أخبره عدلان فلا وإن
أخبره عدل واحد فوجهان لقبول روايته ورد شهادته ولو قال كنت لا أدري أن لي
حق النفي فيعذر إن لم يكن من جملة الفقهاء

### | فرع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ع-ن (la-ʿa-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to curse, to drive away, to remove from mercy"; in legal context, it denotes the mutual imprecation between spouses (liʿān) to sever lineage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, it signifies the declaration of divine curse upon the liar, used as a judicial oath to establish or negate paternity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the act of cursing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the legal procedure of imprecation that severs marital ties and lineage.
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to carry, to bear"; refers to the fetus in the womb.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, it denotes the pregnancy as a state of uncertainty regarding existence and lineage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is physical carrying; metaphorical usage applies to the legal presumption of paternity during gestation.
- Root: ن-ف-ي (n-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to deny, to negate, to repel"; in legal context, it means the husband's repudiation of paternity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): It signifies the act of disavowal that contradicts the default presumption of lineage (al-nasab).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is negation; metaphorical usage is the legal act of disowning a child through liʿān.
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to attribute, to relate"; refers to lineage or kinship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, it denotes the established filiation that carries inheritance and guardianship rights.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is genealogical relation; metaphorical usage is the legal presumption of paternity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if he limits to denying one") and exceptions ("except if the child has a living offspring") to delineate legal outcomes, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: The child has three conditions.

The first condition is that it be a pregnancy. Whether it is permissible to deny it through liʿān before separation [from the womb] — there are two opinions. One of them is no, because pregnancy is not certain; perhaps it is wind that disperses. The second is yes, because it is presumed with a prevailing presumption, and in delay there is the danger of the husband's death and the attachment of lineage. This [permissibility] is after separation [from the marriage bond]. As for during the continuance of the marriage, the correct [opinion] is that he may perform liʿān, because al-ʿAjlānī performed liʿān regarding the pregnancy, and because liʿān without [denying] the child merely to sever the marriage is permissible. It was said: the two opinions are extended [to this case], but there is no basis for that. The companions (al-aṣḥāb) built the two opinions on whether pregnancy is known with certainty — and that is weak. Rather, the correct [view] is that it is not known with certainty, but among the legal rulings, some are established by consideration, some are not established, and some are subject to hesitation. For that reason, the statements of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — differed in some issues, not due to his hesitation that pregnancy is not certain.

The second condition is that they be twins from one womb. Their denial cannot be partial. If he limits himself to denying one of them, it is not denied while the second remains attached [to him]. If he denies both and then acknowledges one, the second is attached to him. If he denies the pregnancy and she gives birth to twins, both are denied. If she gives birth to one during the marriage, and he performs liʿān, then she gives birth to a second after more than six months, the second is attached to him without the first, because it is from another womb. It is possible that conception occurred after the separation of the first and before the liʿān. If he denies the pregnancy and she gives birth to a child, then she gives birth to another after more than six months, it is denied without liʿān, because it is not possible that conception occurred with it during the continuance of the marriage.

Two subsidiary branches:
The first: Whenever he wishes to deny multiple children, a single liʿān suffices for him, and each one does not require a separate liʿān.
The second: The twins denied through liʿān are brothers through the mother. Whether they inherit from each other through paternal brotherhood — there are two aspects. One of them is no, because liʿān nullified paternity. The second is yes, because the effect of liʿān is limited to the one who performed liʿān.

The third condition is that the child dies. He may perform liʿān, because death does not sever lineage. Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: He does not have that [right] except if the child has a living offspring.

Then, in our [school], whenever he acknowledges the child after liʿān, it is attached to him. If he denied him, then when he died he acknowledged him to obtain his inheritance, it is attached to him, and he inherits despite the accusation, because the foundational principle is lineage, and it is attached merely by his statement, and inheritance is subsidiary. Likewise, if he denied him after death, then when his inheritance was distributed, he returned and acknowledged him — the apparent [view] is that he is attached to him and reclaims his share of the inheritance, considering the establishment of lineage. There is an aspect that if the inheritance has lapsed, it does not return to him.

### The Third Chapter: On What Nullifies the Right of Denial

The correct [view] is that it is immediate, because it is in the category of harm (ḍirār) that is repelled after knowing it, so there is no basis for delay. There is another opinion — no harm in it — that he is granted respite until he deliberates, for the matter involves danger, and perhaps it is estimated at three days. A third opinion was narrated: it is not nullified except by acknowledgment. This is far-fetched. The subsidiary rulings are based on it being immediate. On this basis, he is excused only if true knowledge has not been attained by him. If he waited until the pregnancy separated, it is permissible, because he is not certain; perhaps it is wind that disperses. If he said: "I knew of the pregnancy, but I said: perhaps she will miscarry" — whether his right is nullified — there are two aspects. If a sinful person informed him of the birth, and he said: "I did not believe him," it is permissible. If two upright witnesses informed him, then no. If a single upright witness informed him, there are two aspects, due to the acceptance of his narration and the rejection of his testimony. If he said: "I did not know that I had the right of denial," he is excused if he is not among the jurists.

### A Subsidiary Branch
