chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 440: Paternity, Fosterage, and Its Pillars
chapters.arabic_text: نا على المذهب فأنكرت فالقول قوله فكأنا نقول لم يقر إقرارا ملحقا وإن كانت هي المؤتمنة في رحمها ولو ادعت أمية الولد فلها تحليفه ثم فيه وجهان أحدهما يحلف أنها حاضت بعد الوطء وما وطئها بعد الحيض والثاني أنه يضيف إلى ذلك أن الولد ليس مني حتى ينتفي ولو أتت بعد الوطء لأكثر من أربع سنين فمقتضى قولنا إنها صارت فراشا أنه يلحقه فإن قلنا إنه ينتفي بدعوى الإستبراء فهذا أظهر وإن قلنا لا ينتفي فهذا فيه تردد وعلى الجملة هذا بالنفي أولى من الإستبراء ويقرب من هذا أنها لو أتت بولد ثم أتت بولد آخر لأكثر من ستة أشهر من الولد الأول فإنه ولد بعد الإستبراء بالولد الأول فمنهم من قال يلحق إذ صارت فراشا ومنهم من قال لا إذ ليس يثبت لها عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه حكم المستفرشة وعلى هذا يلتفت أن المستفرشة إذا طلقها زوجها هل تعود فراشا بمجرد الطلاق حتى يجب الإستبراء بعتقها قبل الوطء فإن قلنا تعود فراشا لحقه الولد من غير إقرار جديد بالوطء لكن الأصح أنها لا تعود فراشا فرع إذا اشترى زوجته وأتت بولد لزمان يحتمل أن يكون في النكاح وفي ملك اليمين فيلحقه الولد إذ الأمة لا تنحط عن البائنة ولكن لا تصير أم ولد له إذا لم يعترف بوطء في الملك وفيه وجه أنها تصير أم ولد له لأنها ولدت منه في ملكه وهو بعيد نعم لو أقر بالوطء واحتمل أن يكون من النكاح وملك اليمين فيحتمل ترددا في أمية الولد ووجه إثباته أن يقال ملك اليمين مع الإقرار بالوطء يثبت فراشا ناسخا لفراش النكاح فيحال الولد على الناسخ ويمكن أن يقال ملك اليمين لا يقوى على نسخ فراش النكاح ويبتني عليه تردد في أن زوج الأمة إذا طلقها قبل المسيس وأقر السيد بوطئها وأتت بولد لزمان يحتمل أن يكون منهما فيحتمل أن يلحق بالسيد لأن فراشه ناسخ ويحتمل أن يعرض على القائف = كتاب الرضاع = والأصل فيه قوله تعالى {وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة} وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب وفي الكتاب أربعة أبواب - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في أركان الرضاع وشرائطه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أما الأركان فثلاثة المرضع واللبن والمرتضع أما المرضع فهو كل امرأة حية تحتمل الولادة فاحترزنا بالمرأة عن البهيمة والرجل فلو ارتضع صغيران من بهيمة فلا أخوة بينهما لأن الأخوة تتبع الأمومة وقال عطاء تثبت الأخوة ولو در لبن من ثدي الرجل فلا أثر له وفيه وجه أنه كلبن المرأة والصبية بنت ثمان إن در لبنها فلا حكم له بل هو كلبن الرجل وفي لبن البكر وجهان أحدهما يحرم لأنها في محل الولادة وإن لم تلد قطعا والثاني أنها كالرجل إذ اللبن فرع للولد ولا ولد أما لو أجهضت جنينا فلبنها مؤثر وإذا در لبن لصبية بنت سنين وقلنا يعتبر لبن البكر اعتبر ذلك لاحتمال البلوغ ثم لا يحكم ببلوغها بمجرد اللبن ولكن كما يلحق الولد بابن تسع سنين ولا يحكم ببلوغه وأما المرأة الميتة إذا بقي في ضرعها لبن فلا يؤثر لبنها لأنها جثة منفكة عن الحل والحرمة كالبهيمة نعم لو حلب في حياتها وارتضع بعد الموت كان محرما على المذاهب وفيه وجه أنه لا يحرم لأن الميت لا يحتمل ابتداء الأمومة الركن الثاني اللبن والمعتبر عندنا وصول عينه إلى الجوف وإن لم يبق اسمه حتى لو اتخذ منه جبن أو أقط أو مخض منه زبد فأكله الصبي حرم فلم يتبع الشافعي رضي الله عنه اسم اللبن وإن اتبع اسم الإرضاع وعول على الخبر فيه ولو اختلط بمائع وهو غالب حرم وإن كان مغلوبا بحيث لا يظهر له لون وطعم فإن اختلط بما دون القلتين وشرب الصبي جميعه ففيه قولان أحدهما أنه لا يحرم لأنه قد انمحق والثاني نعم لأن العين باق فيه وقد وصل إلى الجوف فعلى هذا لو شرب بعضه فوجهان أحدهما يحرم لانه مثبت في الجميع والثاني لا فلعله في الباقي والوجه القطع بأنه يعتبر يقين الإثبات فإن شك فالأصل عدم التحريم أما إذا اختلط بقلتين فالترتيب على العكس وهو أنه إن شرب بعضه لم يحرم وإن شرب كله فقولان مرتبان على ما دون القلتين وأولى بأن لا يؤثر ثم لم نعتبر القلتين في سائر المائعات بل في الماء خاصة واعتباره بعيد وقال الشيخ أبو حامد المغلوب يعني به الذي لا يؤثر في التغذية لا الذي لا يؤثر في اللون الركن الثالث المحل وهو جوف الصبي الحي فلا يؤثر الإيصال إلى جوف الميت ولا إلى جوف الكبير ونعني بالجوف المعدة ومحل التغذية لأن الرضاع ما انبت اللحم وأنشر العظم فلو وصل إلى جوف لا يغذي كالمثانة والإحليل فحيث لا يفطر لا يؤثر وحيث يحصل الإفطار ففي تحريم الرضاع قولان وفي السعوط طريقان منهم من طرد القولين ومنهم من قطع بالحصول لأن الدماغ له مجرى إلى المعدة فينتهي إليها بخلاف الحقنة أما الشرط فهو اثنان الأول الوقت فلا أثر للرضاع بعد الحولين عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا رضاع إلا في الحولين ولقوله تعالى {حولين كاملين لمن أراد أن يتم الرضاعة} ولا حكم لما بعد التمام وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ثلاثون شهرا وقال ابن أبي ليلى ثلاث سنين وقالا داود أبدا وبه قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها واستدلت بأن سهلة بنت سهيل قالت كنا نرى سالما ولدا وكان يدخل علينا فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أرضعيه خمس رضعات ففعلت وكان كبيرا وأبى سائر الصحابة ذلك وقالوا كان ذلك رخصة لسالم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to settle, establish, or affirm" — in legal context, an acknowledgment (iqrār) that fixes a right or status.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, iqrār is a declarative act that brings latent obligations or lineages into binding actuality; it is a speech-act that constitutes, not merely reports.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical settling; metaphorical (majāz) usage in law denotes the binding establishment of a claim through utterance.
- Root: ر-ض-ع (r-ḍ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes sucking or drawing milk from a breast; the act of nursing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic register, it signifies the physical nourishment that creates a fictive kinship (ummahātukum allātī arḍaʿnakum), transferring maternal and fraternal prohibitions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical act of milk ingestion; metaphorical — the legal consequence of kinship prohibition (ḥurma) attached to that act.
- Root: ف-ر-ش (f-r-sh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root means to spread out; in law, farāsh denotes the marital bed or valid sexual union that establishes paternity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, farāsh is the licit domain of cohabitation; it is the presumptive basis for attributing offspring to the husband or master.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the bed itself; metaphorical — the legal presumption of paternity arising from an ongoing valid union.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text repeatedly uses "law" (if) and "fa-" (then) to structure legal hypotheticals, where the protasis sets a factual condition and the apodosis states the juridical consequence; also the use of "wa-in" (even if) for concessive conditions, requiring careful parsing of nested clauses.
chapters.translation:
I say: If she is the one entrusted with her womb, and she claims the child is not from him, then he is to be made to take an oath. There are two aspects (wajhān) in this matter.

One of them: He swears that she menstruated after the intercourse, and that he did not have intercourse with her after that menstruation.

The second: He adds to that an oath that the child is not from his semen, so that paternity is negated.

If she gives birth after intercourse at a period exceeding four years, then the implication of our doctrine — that she has become a bed (farāsh) — is that the child is attributed to him. If we say that paternity is negated by the claim of seeking istibrāʾ (declaring the womb free), then this is the more apparent (aẓhar) view. And if we say it is not negated, then there is hesitation (taraddud) in this. In sum, this case is more deserving of negation than the case of istibrāʾ.

Close to this is the case where she gives birth to a child, then gives birth to another child more than six months after the first child. For this second child is born after istibrāʾ by means of the first child. Among the scholars, some said it is attributed to him, since she has become a bed (farāsh). Others said it is not, since — in the view of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him — she does not acquire the status of a woman whose bed is contested (mustafrashah). Upon this depends the question: If a mustafrashah is divorced by her husband, does she return to being a bed (farāsh) merely by the divorce, such that istibrāʾ becomes obligatory by her manumission before intercourse? If we say she returns to being a bed, then the child is attributed to him without a new acknowledgment (iqrār) of intercourse. But the more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that she does not return to being a bed.

A Branch (farʿ):

If a man purchases his own wife, and she gives birth to a child at a time that could plausibly be from the marriage or from the right-hand ownership (milk al-yamīn), then the child is attributed to him — for a slave-woman does not fall below the status of a divorced woman (bāʾinah). However, she does not become an umm walad (mother of a child) for him if he does not acknowledge intercourse during the ownership. There is an aspect (wajh) that she does become an umm walad, because she gave birth to him from him while in his ownership — but this is remote (baʿīd).

Yes, if he acknowledges intercourse, and the child could plausibly be from the marriage or from the right-hand ownership, then there is a plausible hesitation (taraddud) regarding her status as umm walad. The aspect affirming it is to say: Right-hand ownership, combined with the acknowledgment of intercourse, establishes a bed (farāsh) that abrogates (nāsikh) the bed of marriage; thus the child is referred to the abrogating bed. And it can be said: Right-hand ownership does not have the strength to abrogate the bed of marriage. Upon this is built the hesitation in the case where a man divorces his slave-wife before consummation, and the master acknowledges intercourse with her, and she gives birth at a time that could plausibly be from either of them. It is plausible that the child is attributed to the master, because his bed is abrogating (nāsikh); and it is plausible that the child is referred to the physiognomist (qāʾif).

= The Book of Fosterage (al-Riḍāʿ) =

The foundational basis for this is the saying of God, the Exalted: {«And your mothers who nursed you, and your sisters from fosterage»} (Q 4:23). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "What is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by fosterage."

In this book there are four chapters.

— Peace be upon him — Chapter One: On the Pillars (arkān) of Fosterage and Its Conditions — Peace be upon him —

As for the pillars, they are three: the nursing woman (murḍiʿ), the milk (laban), and the nursling (murtadiʿ).

As for the nursing woman: She is every living woman who is capable of childbearing. By "woman" we exclude the beast and the man. Thus, if two infants suckle from a beast, there is no brotherhood between them, because brotherhood follows motherhood. ʿAṭāʾ said: Brotherhood is established. And if milk flows from the breast of a man, it has no effect. There is an aspect (wajh) that it is like the milk of a woman. As for a young girl of eight years, if her milk flows, it has no legal effect — it is like the milk of a man. Regarding the milk of a virgin, there are two aspects:

One of them: It is prohibitive, because she is in the locus of childbirth, even if she has never given birth definitively.

The second: She is like a man, since milk is a branch of childbirth, and she has no child.

But if she miscarries a fetus, then her milk is effective. And if milk flows from a young girl of several years, and we hold that the milk of a virgin is considered, then it is considered due to the possibility of puberty. However, her puberty is not adjudged merely by the milk — just as a child is attributed to a boy of nine years without adjudging his puberty.

As for a dead woman: If milk remains in her breast, her milk has no effect, because she is a corpse detached from the states of licit and illicit (ḥill wa ḥurma), like a beast. Yes, if the milk was milked during her lifetime and suckled after her death, it is prohibitive according to the established doctrines (al-madhāhib). There is an aspect (wajh) that it is not prohibitive, because the dead cannot initiate motherhood.

The second pillar: The milk (laban). What is considered valid in our view is the arrival of its substance (ʿayn) into the stomach, even if its name no longer remains. Thus, even if cheese (jubn), dried curd (aqiṭ), or butter (zubd) is made from it, and the child eats it, it is prohibitive. For al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, did not follow the name of milk, though he followed the name of nursing (irḍāʿ), and relied upon the report (khabar) in this.

If it is mixed with a liquid and it is the dominant component, it is prohibitive. But if it is the dominated component, such that no color or taste of it appears, then: if it is mixed with less than two qullas (approximately 500 liters) and the child drinks all of it, there are two opinions (qawlān):

One of them: It is not prohibitive, because it has been obliterated (inmaḥaqa).

The second: Yes, it is prohibitive, because the substance remains in it and has reached the stomach. Upon this, if he drinks only part of it, there are two aspects:

One of them: It is prohibitive, because it is established in the whole.

The second: No, for perhaps it is in the remainder. The decisive view (al-qaṭʿ) is that certainty of establishment is required; if there is doubt, then the default principle is non-prohibition.

As for when it is mixed with two qullas, the order is reversed: if he drinks part of it, it is not prohibitive; if he drinks all of it, there are two opinions, arranged analogously to the case of less than two qullas — and it is even more fitting that it has no effect.

Then, we do not consider the measure of two qullas for other liquids, but only for water specifically. And considering it is remote (baʿīd). Shaykh Abū Ḥāmid said: "The dominated (al-maghlūb) means that which does not affect nutrition, not that which does not affect color."

The third pillar: The locus (maḥall), which is the stomach of a living infant. Thus, delivery into the stomach of a dead person has no effect, nor into the stomach of an adult. By "stomach" we mean the stomach (miʿdah) and the locus of nutrition, because fosterage is what grows flesh and strengthens bone. If it reaches a cavity that does not nourish — like the bladder (mathānah) or the urethra (iḥlīl) — then wherever it does not break the fast, it has no effect. And wherever it does break the fast, there are two opinions regarding the prohibition of fosterage. Regarding snuffing (saʿūṭ) into the nose, there are two paths (ṭarīqān): among the scholars, some extended the two opinions; others decisively affirmed the prohibition, because the brain has a passage to the stomach, so it reaches it — unlike the enema (ḥuqnah).

As for the conditions, they are two:

The first: The time (waqt). There is no effect of fosterage after two years (al-ḥawlayn) according to al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, due to his saying, peace be upon him: "There is no fosterage except within two years," and due to the saying of God, the Exalted: {«Two complete years, for whoever desires to complete the nursing»} (Q 2:233). And there is no legal effect for what comes after completion. Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: Thirty months. Ibn Abī Laylā said: Three years. Dāwūd said: Forever — and this was also the view of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her. She argued by the report that Sahlah bint Suhayl said: "We used to regard Sālim as a son, and he would enter upon us." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Nurse him five times." She did so, and he was an adult. The rest of the Companions rejected this and said: That was a concession (rukhṣah) specific to Sālim.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو شككنا في وقوع الرضاع في الحولين فيقرب من تقابل الأصلين إذ الأصل
بقاء الحولين والأصل عدم التحريم والأظهر أنه لا يحرم فإنه الأصل كالماسح
إذا شك في انقضاء مدة المسح قلنا الأصل وجوب الغسل لا بقاء المدة
الشرط الثاني العدد فلا يحرم إلا خمس رضعات لقول عائشة رضي الله عنها
أنزلت عشر رضعات محرمات فنسخن بخمس رضعات وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يحرم
برضعة وقال أبو ثور وابن أبي ليلى يحصل بثلاث رضعات
ثم النظر في أمرين
أحدهما في التعدد وإنما يتعدد بتخلل فصل بين الرضعتين ويتبع فيه العرف
كموجب اليمين ولا ينقطع التواصل بأن يلفظ الصبي الثدي ويلهو لحظة ولا بأن
يتحول من ثدي إلى ثدي لأن ذلك إتمام رضعة واحدة وإنما ينقطع بالإضراب ساعة
والعرف هو المحكم وعند الشك الأصل نفي التحريم
أما إذا حلبت اللبن دفعة واحدة وشربه الصبي في خمس رضعات فقولان الأصح
حصول العدد نظرا إلى تقطع الوصول والثاني أنه ينظر إلى اتحاد الحصول
والإنفصال
وإن حلب خمس دفعات وتناوله الصبي من إناء واحد دفعة واحدة فهو رضعة فإن
تناوله بدفعات فطريقان
منهم من قطع بالعدد لتعدد الطرفين
ومنهم من قال اللبن في حكم المتحد لما اختلط
الأمر الثاني أن يتعدد المرضع ويتحد الفحل كالرجل له خمسة مستولدات أو
أربع نسوة ومستولدة أرضعن بلبانه صغيرة كل واحدة مرة لا تحصل الأمومة وهل
تحصل الأبوة للفحل فيه وجهان مشهوران
أحدهما أنه لا تحصل لأن الأمومة أصل والأبوة تبع
والثاني  تحصل لأن الأبوة أيضا أصل وقد حصل العدد في حقه
ولو كان بدلهن خمس بنات فوجهان مرتبان وأولى بأن لا تحصل لأن اللبن ليس
منه حتى نقول كأنه المرضع وهن كالظروف للبنه لأن البنات كبنت واحدة من وجه
والأخوات كالبنات وإذا ثبتت الحرمة مع ابنتيه انجرت إليه
ولو كن مختلفات كأم وأخت وبنت وجدة وزوجة فالظاهر أنه لا يحرم لأن هذا
المجموع لا يحصل منه قرابة واحدة يعبر عنها بعبارة وقيل يحرم إذ لو استتمت
كل واحدة خمسا لحرمت
فرع يعتبر تخلل فصل بين رضعات الزوجات فلو أرضعن دفعة واحدة على التواصل
فوجهان
أحدهما أنه يتعدد لتعدد المرضع
والثاني أنه يتحد كتعدد الثدي من واحدة لأن الصبي ارتضع دفعة واحدة فعلى
هذا لو عادت واحدة وأرضعت أربعا حرم عليها لأنها كملت الخمس وفيه وجه أنه
لا يحرم لأن الرضعة الأولى لم تحسب رضعة تامة ولو حسبت لحصل التحريم
بالمجموع وهذا ضعيف
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني فيمن يحرم بالرضاع - صلى الله عليه
وسلم -
ويحرم بالرضاع أصول وفروع والأصول ثلاثة
المرضعة وهي الأم وزوجها وهو الأب
والمرتضع وهو الولد ومنهم تنتشر الحرمة إلى الأطراف حتى يحرم من الرضاع
ما يحرم من النسب
بيانه أنه إذا حرم على المرتضع المرضعة حرم عليها أمهاتها نسبا ورضاعا
فإنهن جدات وحرم عليه أخواتها نسبا ورضاعا فإنهن خالات ولم تحرم عليه بنات
أخواتها وإخوتها فإنهن بنات الخالات والأخوال وحرمت بناتها عليه نسبا
ورضاعا فإنهن أخوات المرتضع وحرمت أولاد بنات المرضعة قربن أو بعدن من
النسب والرضاع فإنه خالهن وكما حرمت المرضعة على المرتضع حرمت على أولاده
من النسب والرضاع فإنهم حوافدها ولم تحرم على أب المرتضع فلو تزوج بها أبوه
فكأنه تزوج بأم الابن ولا منع منه ولو تزوج أخوه بها فلا منع وكأنه تزوج
بأم الأخ وهو جائز وإنما لا يجوز في النسب لأنها زوجة الأب وذلك حرام بحكم
المصاهرة
وهذا القياس بعينه جار بين المرتضع والفحل فإذا كان هو للمرتضع أبا فأبوه
جد  وأخوه عم وابنه أخ وعلى هذا القياس
والأصل في الفحل أن عائشة رضي الله عنها احتجبت من أفلح فقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم
ليلج عليك فإنه عمك وكانت قد ارتضعت من زوجة أخيه ولا يخالف الرضاع النسب
إلا في أم الأخ من الرضاع وأم الإبن من الرضاع فإنهما لا يحرمان من الرضاع
وإنما يحرمان من النسب للمصاهرة والزوجية

### | فصل في مسائل تتعلق بالفحل خاصة

فنقول إنما تثبت الحرمة من الفحل إذا أرضعت بلبانه ونسب اللبن ينسب الولد
إليه وكل ولد منفي عنه فاللبن الحاصل بسببه منفي عنه كولد الزنا والولد
المنفي باللعان
وأما لبن المولود من وطء الشبهة فالصحيح أنه منسوب إليه كالولد وقد نقل
فيه قول ووجهه أن النسب يثبت للضرورة ولا ضرورة في الرضاع وكذا طردوا هذا
القول في الصهر

### | فرعان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ض-ع (raḍaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Suckling, the act of an infant drawing milk from the breast; the milk itself is termed *laban*.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, fosterage establishes a fictive kinship (qarābah) that mirrors consanguinity (nasab) in prohibiting marriage, based on Quranic verse {«وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ»} (Q. 4:23).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical suckling; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the legal effect of creating kinship prohibitions.
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥarama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, to make sacred; the root conveys both prohibition and sanctity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, *taḥrīm* is a divine command that renders an act unlawful; here, it denotes the legal prohibition of marriage due to foster relationships.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for legal prohibition, distinct from *karāhah* (dislike) or *taḥrīm* in ritual contexts.
- Root: ع-د-د (ʿadad)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Number, counting; the act of enumerating discrete units.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudence, the required number of sucklings (five) is a legal condition (sharṭ) for establishing foster-kinship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for numerical count; metaphorical when applied to the legal effect of repeated acts.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with *law* (لو) — [The particle *law* introduces a hypothetical condition, often followed by a past-tense verb, indicating a counterfactual or doubtful scenario; the apodosis is introduced by *la-* or a nominal sentence, as in "لو شككنا" (if we were to doubt)].
chapters.translation:
### | Branch

If we doubt whether the suckling occurred within the two years [of infancy], then this approaches the conflict of two foundational principles (aṣl): for the foundational principle is the continuation of the two-year period, and the foundational principle is the absence of prohibition. The more apparent (aẓhar) ruling is that it does not effect prohibition, for this is the foundational principle—just as in the case of one who wipes over his leather socks (al-māsiḥ): if he doubts whether the period of wiping has expired, we say the foundational principle is the obligation of washing the feet, not the continuation of the wiping period.

The second condition is the number. Prohibition is not established except by five sucklings, due to the saying of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her: "Ten sucklings were revealed as prohibitive, then they were abrogated by five sucklings." Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: prohibition is established by a single suckling. Abū Thawr and Ibn Abī Laylā said: it is established by three sucklings.

Then the consideration is in two matters:

The first is multiplicity. Multiplicity is only achieved by the interposition of a separation (faṣl) between two sucklings, and custom (ʿurf) is followed therein—like the requirements of an oath. The continuity is not broken by the infant releasing the breast and playing for a moment, nor by shifting from one breast to another, for that is the completion of a single suckling. Rather, it is only broken by desisting for a while, and custom is the arbiter. When there is doubt, the foundational principle is the negation of prohibition.

As for when milk is expressed in a single flow and the infant drinks it in five separate intakes, there are two opinions. The more correct (aṣaḥḥ) is that the number is achieved, considering the interruption of the intake. The second is that one looks to the unity of the expression and the separation.

If milk is expressed in five separate flows and the infant consumes it from a single vessel in one intake, it is one suckling. If he consumes it in separate intakes, then there are two paths (ṭarīqān):
- Among them, some definitively ruled the number is achieved due to the multiplicity of both ends.
- Among them, some said the milk is treated as a single entity because it was mixed.

The second matter: that the wet nurses are multiple but the male progenitor (al-faḥl) is one—like a man who has five slave-concubines (mustawlidāt) or four wives and a slave-concubine who suckled a young girl with his milk, each one once. Motherhood is not established. Is paternity for the male progenitor established? There are two well-known faces (wajhān):
- One: it is not established, because motherhood is the root and paternity is subsidiary.
- The second: it is established, because paternity is also a root, and the number has been achieved in his regard.

If instead of them there were five daughters, then there are two ordered faces (wajhān murattabān), and it is more fitting that it not be established, because the milk is not from him such that we could say he is as if the wet nurse, and they are as vessels for his milk—for the daughters are like a single daughter in one respect. And the sisters are like the daughters. When prohibition is established with his two daughters, it extends to him.

If they were diverse—like a mother, a sister, a daughter, a grandmother, and a wife—then the apparent (al-ẓāhir) ruling is that it does not effect prohibition, because from this aggregate no single kinship is produced that could be expressed by a single term. And it was said: it does prohibit, for if each one had completed five, it would have been prohibitive.

### | Branch

The interposition of a separation is required between the sucklings of the wives. If they suckled in a single continuous act, then there are two faces:
- One: it is multiple due to the multiplicity of the wet nurses.
- The second: it is single, like the multiplicity of breasts from one woman, because the infant suckled in a single act. On this basis, if one of them returned and suckled four more times, she becomes prohibited to him, because she completed the five. There is a face that it does not prohibit, because the first suckling was not counted as a complete suckling; had it been counted, prohibition would have been achieved by the aggregate. But this is weak.

— Peace be upon him — The Second Chapter: On Those Who Are Prohibited by Fosterage — Peace be upon him —

By fosterage, the roots and branches are prohibited. The roots are three:
- The wet nurse, who is the mother.
- Her husband, who is the father.
- The suckling, who is the child.

From them, the prohibition spreads to the peripheries, such that whatever is prohibited by consanguinity is prohibited by fosterage. Its clarification: when the wet nurse is prohibited to the suckling, then her mothers are prohibited to him—by lineage and by fosterage—for they are his grandmothers. Her sisters are prohibited to him—by lineage and by fosterage—for they are his maternal aunts. The daughters of her sisters and brothers are not prohibited to him, for they are the daughters of maternal aunts and maternal uncles. Her daughters are prohibited to him—by lineage and by fosterage—for they are the sisters of the suckling. The children of the wet nurse's daughters are prohibited, whether near or far, by lineage and by fosterage, for he is their maternal uncle. Just as the wet nurse is prohibited to the suckling, she is prohibited to his children—by lineage and by fosterage—for they are her grandchildren. She is not prohibited to the suckling's father. If his father married her, it is as if he married the mother of his son, and there is no impediment. If his brother married her, there is no impediment; it is as if he married the mother of his brother, which is permissible. It is only impermissible in consanguinity because she is the wife of the father, and that is forbidden by the rule of affinity (muṣāharah).

This very analogy runs between the suckling and the male progenitor. When he is a father to the suckling, then his father is a grandfather, his brother is a paternal uncle, and his son is a brother—and on this analogy.

The foundational principle regarding the male progenitor is that ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, veiled herself from Aflaḥ, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let him enter upon you, for he is your paternal uncle." She had been suckled from the wife of his brother. Fosterage does not differ from consanguinity except regarding the brother's mother by fosterage and the son's mother by fosterage—these two are not prohibited by fosterage; they are only prohibited by consanguinity due to affinity and marriage.

### | Section on Matters Specific to the Male Progenitor

We say: prohibition from the male progenitor is only established when she suckled with his milk. The attribution of milk attributes the child to him. Every child disowned by him—the milk produced by his cause is disowned from him, like the child of fornication (walad al-zinā) and the child disowned by imprecation (liʿān).

As for the milk of a child born from doubtful intercourse (waṭʾ al-shubhah), the correct (al-ṣaḥīḥ) ruling is that it is attributed to him, like the child. A saying has been transmitted therein, and its rationale is that lineage is established out of necessity, and there is no necessity in fosterage. Likewise, they extended this saying to affinity (al-ṣihr).

### | Two Branches

أحدهما أنه لو وطئت المنكوحة بالشبهة وأتت بولد بحيث يعرض على القائف
وفرعنا على الصحيح في ثبوت الرضاع بوطء الشبهة فالرضاع تبع للنسب فإذا
أرضعت صغيرا فهو ولد من ألحق القائف به المولود فإن لم يكن قائف وبلغ
المولود وانتسب إلى أحدهما تبعه المرتضع في الرضاع فإن مات قبل الإنتساب
ففي الرضيع ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه ينتسب بنفسه كالولد لأنه تابع والآن مات
المتبوع فقام مقامه ولكن هو ينتسب عند عدم الولد
والثاني أنه لا ينتسب لأن الولد يبني على ميل في الطبع تقتضيه الخلقة
وذلك لا يتحقق في الرضاع فعلى هذا نسبه في الرضاع مبهم بينهما فيحرم عليه
مواصلتهما جميعا وهذا هو الأصح
والثالث أن الأمر موقوف والحرمة قائمة وعليه أن لا يواصلهما جميعا ولكن
له مواصلة أحدهما وإذا فعل تعين ولم يجز له بعد ذلك مواصلة الثاني وإن طلثق
الأول وفيه وجه أن له مواصلة الثاني مهما طلق الأول وإنما يحرم عليه الجمع
لأن يتيقن التحريم عند الجمع لا عند الإفراد وفي المسألة قول آخر أنه يثبت
نسبه في الرضاع منهما لأنه يحمل أبوان من الرضاع ولا يحمل من النسب وهذا
ضعيف إلا أن يراد  به شمول التحريم وذلك صحيح
الفرع الثاني إذا طلق زوجته ولبنها دار فهو منسوب إليه أبدا وكذلك لو
انقطع وعاد ما لم تضع حملا من واطىء آخر وقيل إنه يتقدر بأربع سنين وهو
أقصى مدة الحمل وهو فاسد لأن اللبن لا تتقدر مدته ومهما وضعت حملا من واطىء
لخر شبهة أو نكاح انقطع نسبة اللبن عنه اما في مدة الحمل في النكاح الثاني
فهو منسوب إلى الأول إن قال أهل البصر لم يدخل وقت درور اللبن من الثاني
فإن قالوا دخل ففيه نظر
فإن كان اللبن لا ينقطع ففيه ثلاثة أقوال
أحدهما أنه للأول استصجابا
والثاني أنه لهما
والثالث أنه إن زاد اللبن فلهما وإلا فهو للأول
وأما إذا كان قد انقطع وعاد بالحمل فثلاثة أقوال
أحدهما أنه للأول إذ لم يطرأ قاطع معلوم فلا نبالي بقول أهل البصر إن ذلك
جائز ولا بانقطاع اللبن
والثاني أنه للثاني لأن الحمل ناسخ
والثالث أنه لهما جميعا والله أعلم
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثالث في بيان الرضاع القاطع للنكاح وحكم
الغرم فيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
ويشتمل هذا الباب على غوامض الكتاب ولا بد من تقديم أصلين
أحدهما في الغرم
والثاني في التفاف المصاهرة بالرضاع
الأول في الغرم فإذا كان تحته صغيرة فأرضعتها أمه أو امرأته بلبانه حرمت
زوجته الصغيرة وانقطع النكاح وعلى الزوج نصف المسمى قبل المسيس وجميعه حيث
ينقطع النكاح بمثله بعد المسيس وأما المرضعة فقد فوتت ملك النكاح عليه فلا
بد وأن تغرم وقد نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه أن عليها قبل المسيس نصف مهر
المثل ونص في شهود الطلاق إذا رجعوا أنهم يغرمون جميع مهر المثل فقيل قولان
في المسألتين بالنقل والتخريج ينظر في أحدهما إلى أن المستقر هو النصف توفي
الثاني وهو الأصح أن الملك بكماله مستقر وإنما يسقط الشطر بالطلاق فيجب
جميع المهر ومنهم من فرق بأن الشهود لم يقطعوا باطنا ملكه وإنما أوقعوا
حيلولة والإرضاع قطع النكاح والقطع قبل المسيس لا يوجب إلا النصف  ومنهم من
أقر النص في الشهود وخرج منه قولا إلى الرضاع أنه يجب التمام وهو متجه في
القياس وذكر بعض أصحابنا قولين آخرين
أحدهما أنه يغرم نصف المسمى لأنه الذي فات على الزوج متقوما أما البضع
فلا
يتقوم وهو مذهب أببي حنيفة رحمه الله
والثاني كمال المسمى لأنه الذي بذل الزوج إذ التشطير خاصية الزوج
وفي الشهود قول خامس أن الزوج إن كان بذل كمال المسمى وجب كمال المسمى
لأن الزوج منكر للطلاق فلا يمكنه استرداد شطر المسمى
أما إذا جرى بعد المسيس بأن كان تحته كبيرة وصغيرة فأرضعت أم الكبيرة
الصغيرة حتى صارتا أختين فحرم جميعهما اندفعا على الصحيح وفيما تغرم لأجل
الكبيرة الممسوسة قولان
الصحيح المقطوع به أنها تغرم كمال مهر المثل
والثاني أنها لا تغرم شيئا لأن الزوج بالوطء استوفى ما يقابل المهر وكذلك
إذا ارتدت بعد المسيس لم تغرم شيئا
وهذا كله إذا كان الرضاع منها قصدا فلو كانت المرضعة نائمة فدبت الصغيرة
إليها وامتصت فالفسخ محال على الصغيرة حتى يسقط كمال المسمى ولا تغرم
المرضعة لعدم القصد
ولا خلاف في أن فعلها في الإرتضاع لا يعتبر مهما كانت المرضعة قاصدة بل
يحال على جانب المرضعة وذكر الشيخ أبو علي في النائمة وجهين آخرين
أحدهما أنه يحال على المرضعة لأنها صاحبة اللبن فتنسب إليه وهذا ضعيف
والثاني أنها لا تغرم لأنها لم تقصد وتستحق الصغيرة نصف المسمى إذ لا
عبرة بفعلها
أما إذا قطرت قطرة من اللبن فطيرها الريح إلى فم الصغيرة فلا غرم على
صاحبة اللبن والصغيرة تستحق شطر المهر إذ لا فعل لها ويرجع وجه في النظر
إلى صاحبة اللبن
الأصل الثاني في التفاف المصاهرة بالرضاع
فنقول إذا أرضعت امرأة صبية فنكح الصبية رجل حرم عليه المرضعة لأنها أم
زوجته والأمومة سابقة على الزوجية فلو نكح صبية وأبانها فأرضعتها كبيرة
حرمت الكبيرة على المطلق لأنها صارت أم صغيرة كانت زوجته إذ لا ينظر إلى
التاريخ والتقديم والتأخير وهذا متفق عليه والمطلقة أو المستولدة إذا  نكحت
صغيرا ثم أرضعته بلبان الزوج أو السيد حرما على المطلق والسيد لأن الرضيع
صار ابنا وهي كانت زوجته قبل أن صار ابنا فصارتا أم الزوجة
وكذلك لو نكح زيد كبيرة وعمرو صغيرة ثم طلقاهما ونكح كل واحد زوجة صاحبه
فأرضعت الكبيرة الصغيرة حرمت الكبيرة عليهما لأنها صارت أم صغيرة هي
زوجتهما وأما الصغيرة فإن لم يكن زيد قد دخل بالكبيرة لما كانت تحته فنكاح
الصغيرة باق لأنها صارت ربيبة امرأة لم يدخل بها فإن كان قد دخل بالكبيرة
حرمت الصغيرة وانفسخ النكاح لأنها ربيبة مدخول بها
فإن تمهد هذان الأصلان انشعب منهما صور
الصورة الأولى إذا كان تحته صغيرة وكبيرة فأرضعت الكبيرة الصغيرة بلبان
الزوج حرمتا عليه على التأييد لأن الكبيرة صارت أم الزوجة والصغيرة صارت
ولد الزوج فإن أرضعتها بلبان غيره وكان بعد الدخول بالكبيرة حرمتا على
التأييد لأن الكبيرة صارت أم الزوجة والصغيرة ربيبة مدخول بها وإن كان قبل
الدخول حرمت الكبيرة مؤبدة لما سبق وانفسخ نكاح الصغيرة لأنها اجتمعت مع
الأم في النكاح ولا يحرم تجديد نكاحها لأنها ربيبة غير مدخول بها أما الغرم
فإن ظهر فعلها يسقط مهرها قبل الدخول وغرم مهر الصغيرة كما سبق
الصورة الثانية لو كان تحته كبيرة وثلاث صغار فأرضعتهن دفعة بأن حلبت
اللبن فأوجرتهن دفعة حرمت هي على التأييد لأنها أم زوجاته وانفسخ نكاح
الصغار لمعنيين
أحدهما ثبوت الاخوة بينهن
والثاني اجتماعهن مع الأم في النكاح
ولم يحرمن مؤبدا لأن تحريمهن بسبب الإجتماع ولكن بشرط أن لا يكون
الإرتضاع بلبان الزوج وأن يكون قبل دخوله بالكبيرة حتى لا يصرن ربائب مدخول
بها
وإن أرضعت الأوليين ثم الثالثة انفسخ نكاحها مع الأوليين ولم ينفسخ نكاح
الثالثة إذ لم يبق في نكاحه امرأة حتى يمتنع الإجتماع فلو أرضعت واحدة
فواحدة على الترتيب انفسخ نكاح الكبرى مع الأولى ولم ينفسخ نكاح الثانية في
الحال وهل ينفسخ مع نكاح الثالثة وقد أرضعتها وتحته الصغيرة الثانية فيه
قولان
أحدهما نعم وهو القياس لأنهما أختان فليست  إحداهما بالإندفاع أولى من
الأخرى
والثاني أنه تختص الثالثة باندفاع نكاحها لأن سبب الجمع وجد بإرضاعها
وكذلك لو أرضعت أجنبية صغيرتين تحت زوج واحد على التوالي اندفع نكاح
الثانية وفي الأولى قولان
وكذلك لو أرضعت أم إحدى الصغيرتين الأخرى انفسخ نكاح المرتضعة وفي الأخرى
القولان والأصح في الكل التدافع وهو اختيار المزني رحمه الله
ولو كان تحته أربع صغار فجاء ثلاث خالات للزوج من جهة الأب والأم وأرضعت
كل واحدة واحدة لم ينفسخ نكاحهن لأنهن صرن بنات الخالات فلو جاءت بعد ذلك
أم أم الزوج أو امرأة أب لأم الزوج وارتضعت الرابعة حرمت هي مؤبدا لأنها
صارت خالة للزوج وصارت خالة للصغائر الثلاث إذ صارت اختا للخالة التي
أرضعتهن وأخت الخالة خالة فينفسخ نكاحها وفي انفساخ نكاح الثلاث وهي بنات
أختها وقد اجتمعن في النكاح معها قولان لأن سبب الجمع محقق منها

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ض-ع (raḍaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Suckling, the act of an infant drawing milk from the breast; the milk itself is termed *laban*.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Fosterage as a legal cause (*sabab*) that creates kinship-like prohibitions, analogous to lineage (*nasab*), but distinct in its evidentiary and temporal modalities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of suckling vs. metaphorical extension to the legal ruling (*ḥukm*) of prohibition; the term *raḍāʿ* is used *ḥaqīqatan* for the physical act and *majāzan* for its juristic effect.
- Root: ن-س-ب (nasaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Attribution, lineage, relation by blood.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Genealogical descent as the primary anchor for inheritance, marriage prohibitions, and fosterage following suit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal blood relation vs. metaphorical extension to foster-kinship (*nasab riḍāʿī*).
- Root: غ-ر-م (gharima)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pay a debt or indemnity; financial liability for damage caused.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Restitution (*ghurm*) as a compensatory obligation arising from tortious causation (*itlāf*), distinct from contractual debt.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal payment vs. metaphorical use for legal responsibility imposed by causation.
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥaruma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be forbidden, sacred, or inviolable.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Prohibition (*taḥrīm*) as a divine legal category rendering an act or union impermissible.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sanctity vs. metaphorical legal prohibition in marriage and fosterage contexts.
- Sībawayh Rule: *Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab* (Coordination on the Cause) — When multiple legal consequences are coordinated, the syntactic structure mirrors the causal chain, requiring precise parsing of conditional clauses (e.g., "if X, then Y; but if Z, then W") to avoid ambiguity in juristic deduction.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the first of the two [branches] is that if a woman lawfully married is penetrated under a mistaken claim of right (*shubhah*) and gives birth to a child, such that the child is presented to a lineage-examiner (*qāʾif*), and we have built upon the sound opinion regarding the establishment of fosterage by penetration under *shubhah* — then fosterage follows lineage (*al-raḍāʿ tabaʿun lil-nasab*). Thus, if she suckles a young child, that child becomes a son of the one to whom the *qāʾif* attributed the newborn. If there is no *qāʾif* and the newborn reaches maturity and attributes himself to one of the two [potential fathers], the suckled child follows him in fosterage. If he dies before attribution, then concerning the suckled child there are three opinions: First, that he attributes himself independently, like a [true] son, because he is a dependent (*tābiʿ*), and now the principal (*matbūʿ*) has died, so he stands in his place — but he attributes himself only in the absence of a [true] son. Second, that he does not attribute himself, because a son's attribution is built upon a natural inclination (*mayl fī al-ṭabʿ*) necessitated by innate constitution (*khilqah*), and that is not realized in fosterage. On this view, his lineage in fosterage remains ambiguous between the two, so it is forbidden for him to have marital relations with both of them — and this is the most sound (*al-aṣaḥḥ*). Third, that the matter is suspended (*mawqūf*) and the prohibition stands, but he may have relations with one of them; when he does so, that one becomes determined, and thereafter it is not permissible for him to have relations with the second, even if he divorces the first. There is a face (*wajh*) that he may have relations with the second whenever he divorces the first; prohibition only applies to combining them, because certainty of prohibition arises at combination, not at isolation. There is another saying in this matter that his lineage in fosterage is established from both of them, because one can have two fathers in fosterage but not in lineage — but this is weak, unless what is meant is the comprehensiveness of prohibition, which is sound.

The second branch: If a man divorces his wife and her milk is still flowing (*darr*), it is attributed to him forever. Likewise, if it ceases and then returns, [it remains his] as long as she does not give birth to a pregnancy from another penetrator. It was said that it is limited to four years, which is the maximum duration of pregnancy — but this is corrupt (*fāsid*), because the duration of milk is not limited. Whenever she gives birth to a pregnancy from a penetrator, whether by *shubhah* or lawful marriage, the attribution of the milk to him ceases. During the pregnancy in the second marriage, it is attributed to the first if the experts in vision (*ahl al-baṣar*) say that the time of milk-flow from the second had not yet entered. If they say it had entered, then there is a consideration (*naẓar*). If the milk does not cease, then there are three opinions: First, that it belongs to the first, by presumption of continuity (*istiṣḥāb*). Second, that it belongs to both. Third, that if the milk increased, it belongs to both; otherwise, to the first. As for when it had ceased and then returned due to pregnancy, there are three opinions: First, that it belongs to the first, since no known cutter (*qāṭiʿ*) has intervened, so we do not heed the experts' claim that this is possible, nor the cessation of milk. Second, that it belongs to the second, because the pregnancy is abrogating (*nāsikh*). Third, that it belongs to both — and God knows best.

— Peace be upon him — The Third Chapter: On the Fosterage That Cuts Off Marriage and the Ruling on Indemnity Therein — Peace be upon him —

This chapter encompasses the subtleties of the book, and it is necessary to present two principles: First, on indemnity (*ghurm*); Second, on the intertwining of affinity (*muṣāharah*) with fosterage.

The first principle, on indemnity: If a man has a minor wife under him, and his mother or his [other] wife suckles her with his milk, his minor wife becomes forbidden to him, and the marriage is cut off. Upon the husband is half the specified dower (*mahr musammā*) before consummation (*masīs*), and the full amount where the marriage is cut off by such [an act] after consummation. As for the wet-nurse, she has caused the loss of the marital right (*milk al-nikāḥ*) over him, so she must indemnify. Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — explicitly stated that upon her, before consummation, is half the equivalent dower (*mahr al-mithl*). He also explicitly stated regarding the witnesses of divorce, when they retract, that they indemnify the full equivalent dower. Thus two sayings were reported in the two matters, by transmission (*naql*) and by derivation (*takhrij*): One looks to the fact that what is settled (*mustaqarr*) is only half, so she pays half. The second — which is the more sound — is that the right (*milk*) in its entirety is settled, and only the half is dropped by divorce, so the full dower is obligatory. Among them, some distinguished by saying that the witnesses did not cut off his right inwardly; they merely caused a hindrance (*ḥaywalah*), whereas suckling cuts off the marriage, and cutting off before consummation necessitates only half. Among them, some affirmed the text (*naṣṣ*) regarding witnesses and derived from it a saying for suckling that the full amount is obligatory — and this is consistent with analogy (*qiyās*). Some of our companions mentioned two other sayings: First, that she indemnifies half the specified dower, because that is what was lost to the husband as a valued property; the vulva (*budʿ*) itself is not valued — and this is the doctrine of Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him. Second, the full specified dower, because that is what the husband pledged, since the halving is a special characteristic of the husband [in divorce]. Regarding the witnesses, there is a fifth saying: If the husband had pledged the full specified dower, the full specified dower is obligatory, because the husband denies the divorce, so he cannot reclaim the half of the specified dower.

As for when [the suckling] occurs after consummation — such as a man having a major and a minor wife, and the mother of the major suckles the minor until they become sisters — then both become forbidden, and both are repelled (*indafaʿā*) on the sound opinion. Regarding what she indemnifies for the major who was consummated: there are two sayings. The sound and definitive one is that she indemnifies the full equivalent dower. The second is that she indemnifies nothing, because the husband, by intercourse, has already received what corresponds to the dower. Likewise, if she apostatizes after consummation, she indemnifies nothing. All this applies when the suckling was from her intentionally (*qaṣdan*). If the wet-nurse was sleeping and the minor crept to her and sucked, then the annulment (*faskh*) is attributed to the minor, such that the full specified dower is dropped, and the wet-nurse does not indemnify due to lack of intent. There is no disagreement that the minor's act in suckling is not considered whenever the wet-nurse was intentional; rather, it is attributed to the wet-nurse's side. Shaykh Abū ʿAlī mentioned two other faces regarding the sleeping woman: First, that it is attributed to the wet-nurse because she is the owner of the milk, so it is attributed to her — but this is weak. Second, that she does not indemnify because she did not intend, and the minor deserves half the specified dower, since her act is not considered. As for when a drop of milk is dripped and the wind carries it into the minor's mouth, there is no indemnity on the milk's owner, and the minor deserves half the dower, since she has no act — and a face in consideration (*naẓar*) reverts to the milk's owner.

The second principle: On the intertwining of affinity with fosterage. We say: If a woman suckles a young girl, and then a man marries that young girl, the wet-nurse becomes forbidden to him because she is the mother of his wife — and motherhood precedes marriage. If he marries a young girl and divorces her, and then a major woman suckles her, that major woman becomes forbidden to the divorcer because she became the mother of a young girl who was his wife — for no regard is given to chronology, precedence, or delay. This is agreed upon (*muttafaq ʿalayh*). If a divorced woman or a *mustawlada* (a slave-mother of her master's child) marries a young boy and then suckles him with the milk of the husband or the master, both become forbidden to the divorcer and the master, because the suckled child became a son, and she was his wife before he became a son — thus she becomes the mother of the wife. Likewise, if Zayd marries a major woman and ʿAmr marries a minor girl, then both divorce them, and each marries the other's former wife, and the major woman suckles the minor girl — the major woman becomes forbidden to both, because she became the mother of a minor girl who is their wife. As for the minor girl: if Zayd had not consummated with the major woman when she was under him, then the minor's marriage remains valid, because she became a step-daughter (*rabībah*) of a woman not consummated with. If he had consummated with the major woman, the minor becomes forbidden and the marriage is annulled, because she is a step-daughter of one consummated with.

Now that these two principles are established, from them branch forth scenarios.

The first scenario: If a man has a minor and a major wife, and the major suckles the minor with the husband's milk, both become forbidden to him forever (*taʾbīd*), because the major became the mother of his wife, and the minor became his daughter. If she suckles her with another's milk, and this occurs after consummation with the major, both become forbidden forever, because the major became the mother of his wife and the minor a step-daughter of one consummated with. If before consummation, the major is forbidden forever for what preceded, and the minor's marriage is annulled because she is combined with the mother in marriage — but renewing her marriage is not forbidden, because she is a step-daughter of one not consummated with. As for indemnity: if her act is established, her dower drops before consummation, and she indemnifies the minor's dower as previously stated.

The second scenario: If a man has a major wife and three minor wives, and she suckles all of them at once — e.g., she milks the milk and administers it to them at once — she becomes forbidden forever because she is the mother of his wives, and the marriages of the minors are annulled for two reasons: First, the establishment of sisterhood among them; Second, their combination with the mother in marriage. They are not forbidden forever, because their prohibition is due to combination — but on the condition that the suckling was not with the husband's milk and that it occurred before his consummation with the major, so that they do not become step-daughters of one consummated with. If she suckles the first two, then the third, the marriage of the first two is annulled but not the third's, since no woman remains in his marriage to prevent combination. If she suckles one after another sequentially, the major's marriage is annulled with the first, and the second's marriage is not annulled at that moment. Regarding whether it is annulled with the third's marriage, when she has suckled her while the second minor is still under him — there are two sayings: First, yes, which is the analogy, because they are sisters, so neither is more deserving of repulsion than the other. Second, that the third is specifically repelled, because the cause of combination (*sabab al-jamʿ*) arose by her suckling. Likewise, if a foreign woman suckles two minor girls under one husband sequentially, the second's marriage is repelled, and regarding the first there are two sayings. Likewise, if the mother of one of the minor girls suckles the other, the suckled one's marriage is annulled, and regarding the other there are the two sayings. The most sound in all of this is mutual repulsion (*tadāfuʿ*), which is the choice of al-Muzanī — may God have mercy on him. If a man has four minor wives, and three paternal and maternal aunts (*khālāt*) of the husband come and each suckles one, their marriages are not annulled, because they became daughters of the aunts. If thereafter the mother of the husband's mother, or the wife of the father of the husband's mother, comes and suckles the fourth, she becomes forbidden forever, because she became an aunt (*khālah*) of the husband and an aunt of the three minors, since she became a sister of the aunt who suckled them — and the sister of an aunt is an aunt. Thus her marriage is annulled. Regarding the annulment of the three minors' marriages, as they are daughters of her sister and are combined in marriage with her — there are two sayings, because the cause of combination is realized from her. The same matter, if the aunts were disparate — one paternal, one maternal, one both paternal and maternal — and the mother of the husband's mother comes and suckles the fourth, her marriage is annulled. As for the three minors: the one suckled by the paternal aunt — her marriage is not annulled, because the aunt-hood (*khūlah*) of the fourth arose from the side of the mother of the husband's mother, and the paternal aunt does not connect to her. The same matter, if the wife of the father of the husband's mother comes and suckles the fourth with the milk of the father of the husband's mother, her marriage is annulled because she became a paternal aunt (*ʿammah*) of the husband. Regarding whether the three minors' marriages are annulled: as for the one suckled by the paternal aunt or the both-paternal-and-maternal aunt, there are two sayings on her annulment; the one suckled by the maternal aunt is not annulled, because she is foreign to her — since the maternal aunt-hood was established for her from the side of the father of the husband's mother, and she is an aunt from the side of the mother of the husband's mother. Upon this rule are derived three paternal aunts, combined or disparate, with the supposition of suckling the fourth by the mother of the husband's father or the wife of the father of the husband's father.

The third scenario: A man has a major wife and three minor wives, and the major has three adult daughters. Each adult daughter of the major suckles one minor. If after consummation, the major becomes forbidden forever because she became a grandmother (*jaddah*) of the minors, and the minors become forbidden forever because they are step-daughters of one consummated with. If before consummation, their marriages are annulled but not forbidden forever except the major, for she is the mother of the wives. Annulment occurs only if the suckling happened at once without succession. If it happened sequentially, the first's marriage is annulled with the mother, but not the second's or third's. If they milk the milk into one vessel and suckle at once, all marriages are repelled. The wet-nurses share in the indemnity of the minors' dowers in this scenario due to the mixing of milk. If each suckles individually at the same time, each is individually liable for her own dower, and they share in the indemnity of the major's dower, since each produced a complete cause (*ʿillah*) for repelling her marriage.

The fourth scenario: A man marries two major women and two minor girls. One major suckles the two minors with his milk sequentially, and the second major does likewise. Both majors and both minors become forbidden forever. However, when the first major suckled the first minor, she corrupted her own marriage and that minor's, because she became the mother of the wife and the minor became a daughter. When she suckled the second, the second's marriage was corrupted because she too became a daughter. Thus the first major's dower drops if before consummation, and she indemnifies the dowers of the two minors as previously stated. As for the second major, she corrupted only her own marriage, so she has no dower and owes nothing. If it was not with the husband's milk, the minor does not become a daughter but a step-daughter — and her ruling before and after consummation is not hidden, and the ruling of the verse {«وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَائِكُمْ»} (And the mothers of your wives) stands by consensus before consummation.

— Peace be upon him — The Fourth Chapter: On Disputes — Peace be upon him —

And the consideration of claims (*daʿwā*), oaths (*ḥalf*), and testimony (*shahādah*). As for the claim: if both parties agree on the suckling, the repulsion of the marriage is adjudged, and nothing is obligatory except the equivalent dower if consummation occurred. If one of them claims it, judgment is given according to his statement regarding what is against him, and he is required to produce proof (*bayyinah*) regarding what is for him. If the husband claims it, the marriage is repelled but her dower is not dropped by his statement. If the woman claims it, her dower drops if she had not received it; if she had received it, the husband cannot reclaim it, because he denies the suckling.

As for the oath: the denier swears to negate knowledge of the occurrence of suckling, because suckling is the act of another — and no regard is given to her act in suckling, because she was minor. If she refuses (*nukulat*), the husband swears with certainty (*al-batt*) on the occurrence of suckling. Al-Qaffāl said he swears on knowledge of its occurrence, to match the returned oath with its opposite. The sound view is that this was mentioned by way of recommendation (*istiḥbāb*); otherwise, if he swears on the suckling definitively, it suffices.

As for testimony, it has two aspects. The first: the number and qualification of witnesses. Four women are required. Mālik — may God have mercy on him — said two suffice, and the testimony of women alone is accepted. Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said two men or one man and two women are required. If the woman's mother and daughter testify, it is not accepted if she is the claimant; if she is the denier, it is accepted against her. If testimony is initiated without a claim, by way of *ḥisbah* (voluntary attestation for public right), it is accepted, for it may be against her or for her — and *ḥisbah* testimony is accepted in suckling as in divorce. The testimony of the wet-nurse is accepted even if she testifies to her own act, for she does not intend to establish the act but the delivery of milk — unless her purpose is the fee, in which case it is not accepted. Al-Fūrānī said: if she testifies that "she suckled from me," it is accepted; but if she says "I testify that I suckled her," it is not accepted due to the corruption of the formulation (*ṣīghah*).

The second aspect: on bearing testimony (*taḥammul*). This is realized by observing the minor latch onto the breast, swallowing, and his larynx moving as he draws — a movement by which one gains knowledge of the milk's arrival into his stomach from circumstantial evidence (*qarīnah al-ḥāl*) and prevailing presumption (*al-ẓann al-ghālib*), like certainty — as in testimony over ownership. However, at the time of rendering testimony, one should state definitively that between them is a prohibiting suckling. If he testifies to the suckling, let him mention its conditions of time and number. Whether he must mention the arrival of milk into the stomach — there is a disagreement. There is no doubt that if the judge asks for more detail, he must do so. But if the witness dies before detailing, there are two faces on whether the judge may suspend. Those who suffice without it reason that the arrival into the stomach is not seen, unlike the entry of the organ in adultery (*zinā*), which is seen. There is no disagreement that if he merely narrates the circumstantial evidence he observed in the suckling, it is not accepted if that was the basis of his knowledge.

= The Book of Expenditures (Nafaqāt) =

And the causes that necessitate expenditures are three: marriage (*zawjiyyah*), kinship (*qarābah*), and ownership of a slave (*milk al-yamīn*).

chapters.title_en: The First Cause: Marital Union (al-Sabab al-Awwal: al-Zawjiyyah)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | السبب الأول الزوجية

ويجب على الزوج النفقة بالاتفاق وهي خمسة أشياء الطعام والإدام والكسوة
والسكنى وآلة التنظيف كالمشط والدهن والخادم إن كانت ممن تخدم
ثم الخادم تستحق الطعام والأدم والسكنى والكسوة وتستحق الخف لترددها في
الخروج والمرأة لا تستحق  الخف بل المكعب للتردد في المسكن
ولا تستحق الخادمة آلة التنظيف ولا تستحق الزوجة المعالجة بالداء والفضد
والحجامة
وشرح هذه الأمور مع مسقطات النفقة في ثلاثة أبواب
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الأول في قدر النفقة وكيفية الإنفاق - صلى
الله عليه وسلم -
وشرحه في فصلين

### | الفصل الأول في المقدار

والكلام في هذه الاشياء المذكورة وهي ستة أشياء
الواجب الأول هو الطعام وهو مد على المعسر ومدان على الموسر ومد ونصف على
المتوسط وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله إنه لا يقدر بل الواجب قدر الكفاية كنفقة
القريب ونقل الشيخ أبو محمد قولا غريبا على موافقته ونقل صاحب التقريب قولا
أن الزيادة على المد لا مرد له فهو إلى فرض القاضي والمذهب هو الأول
ومستنده أن اعتبار الكفاية لا يصح مع أنها تستحق في يوم مرضها وشبعها فإذا
بطلت
الكفاية فأقل طعام أوجبه الشرع المد في الكفارات وهو القدر الذي يجتزىء
به الزهيد ويتبلغ به الرغيب وأقصاه مدان إذ أوجبهما الشرع في الفدية والوسط
ما بينهما وقد ثبت أن ذلك يختلف لقوله تعالى {على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر
قدره} فتقدير الله تعالى أولى من تقدير القاضي وأحسن مستند لتقدير القاضي
تقدير الشرع وإنما ينظر إلى حال الزوج عندنا في العجز والقدرة لا إلى حالها
والمعسر هو الذي لا يملك شيئا أصلا فعليه مد ولا يزيد فإن كان قادرا على
كسب الزيادة فإن خرج عن حد استحقاق سهم المساكين بملك مال نظر فإن كثر فهو
موسر وإن كان بحيث لو ألزمناه المدين أوشك أن يرجع إلى حد المساكين فهو
متوسط فعليه مد ونصف
وليس على المكاتب والعبد إلا نفقة المعسرين وكذلك من نصفه عبد ونصفه حر
وقال المزني رحمه الله عليه نصف نفقة المعسرين ونصف نفقة الموسرين هذا حكم
المقدار
أما جنس الطعام فغالب قوت البلد فإن اختلف فما يليق بالزوج وإن كان حال
الزوج يخالف الغالب فهو في محل التردد
الواجب الثاني الأدم وقد قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه مكيلة زيت أو  سمن وهذا
تقريب إذ لا تقدير في الشرع فيه وإنما الواجب ما يكفي مع المد أو المدين
والرجوع في الجنس إلى الغالب في البلد أو إلى اللائق بحال الزوج
وأما اللحم فقد قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه رطل من اللحم في الأسبوع إن كان
الواجب مدا ورطلان للمدين قال العراقيون بنى الشافعي رضي الله عنه هذا على
عادة بلدة ألفها فإن اقتضت عادة بلدة أخرى زيادة على ذلك فينبغي أن يزاد
وقال القفال رحمه الله لا زيادة عليه لأنا نقتصر على الأقل كما في الطعام
فرعان
أحدهما لو كانت تزجى الوقت بالخبز القفار فلا يسقط حقها من الأدم كما إذا
لم تأكل أصل الطعام فإنها تستحق الطعام
الثاني لو تبرمت بجنس واحد من الأدم فيجب على الزوج إبداله على وجه ولا
يجب في وجه بل عليها الإبدال إن شاءت
الواجب الثالث الخادمة وتجب نفقة خادمتها إذا كان منصبها يقتضي أن تخدم
وإن كان لا يليق بمنصبها وإنما تخدم لمرض فلا يجب إذ لا تجب أسباب المعالجة
وإن كان بها
زمانة ومرض دائم فهي كذلك تحتاج إلى الخادمة فهذا يحتمل لأن هذا العذر
الدائم لا ينقص عن مراعاة الحشمة
ثم على المعسر للخادمة مد وعلى الموسر مد وثلث كذلك قاله الشافعي رضي
الله عنه وهو تقريب لا تقدير إذ لا تقدير للشرع فيه نعم هو رطلان وهو لائق
بالعادة في حق الخادمة
والصحيح أنه ينظر إلى كفايتها إلا أن هذا القدر قدر الكفاية في الغالب
وفي استحقاق الأدم وجهان
أحدهما نعم كالمخدومة ولكن يجوز أن يكون أدمها في الجنس أخسر وفي المقدار
ما يليق بقدر طعامها
والثاني أنه لا تستحق بل تكتفي بما تفضله المخدومة في بعض الأحوال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ف-ق (nafaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Expenditure, spending; what is consumed and depleted; maintenance (al-nafaqah) as that which sustains life.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Obligatory provision owed by one party to another as a right (ḥaqq), tied to the divine command of kindness (maʿrūf) in marital relations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "spending"; here it is a technical legal term (ḥaqīqah sharʿiyyah) for mandated sustenance, not metaphorical.
- Root: ق-و-ت (qūt)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sustenance, food sufficient for survival; the measure that keeps one alive.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The minimal provision that preserves the body's constitution (qiwām al-badan), distinct from luxury.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: staple food; metaphorical extension to all necessities of maintenance.
- Root: ك-ف-ي (kafā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sufficiency; that which suffices without excess or deficiency.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The standard of adequacy (kifāyah) in maintenance, debated against fixed measures (taqdīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to spare need; legal usage: the benchmark for discretionary rulings.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text uses conditional clauses (in kānat, law kāna) and exceptions (illā) to delineate legal categories, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis for correct juristic inference.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first cause [of obligatory maintenance] is marital union (al-zawjiyyah).

Maintenance (al-nafaqah) is obligatory upon the husband by consensus (al-ittifāq). It comprises five things: food (al-ṭaʿām), condiment (al-idām), clothing (al-kiswah), lodging (al-suknā), and implements of cleanliness (ālat al-tanẓīf) such as the comb and oil. Also [included is] a servant (al-khādim) if she is of a station that is served.

Then the servant is entitled to food, condiment, lodging, and clothing, and she is entitled to shoes (al-khuff) due to her frequent going out. The wife, however, is not entitled to shoes; rather, she is entitled to [the cost of] a sandal (al-mukaʿʿab) for her movement within the dwelling. The servant is not entitled to implements of cleanliness, nor is the wife entitled to medical treatment by cupping (al-ḥijāmah), cautery (al-kayy), or bloodletting (al-faṣd).

The elaboration of these matters, along with the causes that nullify maintenance (musqiṭāt al-nafaqah), [is presented] in three chapters.

CHAPTER ONE: On the Measure of Maintenance and the Manner of Expenditure

Its elaboration is in two sections.

SECTION ONE: On the Quantity [of Maintenance]

The discussion concerns the aforementioned items, which are six things.

The first obligatory item is food (al-ṭaʿām): one mudd (mudd) for the destitute (al-muʿsir), two mudds for the affluent (al-mūsir), and one and a half mudds for the middle-class (al-mutawassiṭ). Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It is not fixed by measure; rather, the obligatory [amount] is the measure of sufficiency (qadr al-kifāyah), like the maintenance of a relative. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad transmitted an odd opinion (qawl gharīb) agreeing with him. The author of al-Taqrīb transmitted an opinion that there is no limit beyond the mudd; rather, it is referred to the judge's discretion (farḍ al-qāḍī). The established doctrine (al-madhhab) is the first [view].

Its basis is that the consideration of sufficiency (al-kifāyah) is invalid, for she is entitled [to maintenance] even on the day of her illness and her satiety. When sufficiency is nullified, then the least food that the Law (al-sharʿ) has mandated is the mudd, [as established] in expiations (al-kaffārāt). It is the quantity that suffices the frugal eater (al-zahīd) and sustains the one with a hearty appetite (al-ragīb). Its maximum is two mudds, for the Law mandated both in the redemption [for breaking fast] (al-fidyah). The middle [amount] is what lies between them. It is established that this varies, for Allah the Exalted says: {«عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ»} ("Upon the affluent is his measure, and upon the constrained is his measure") [Q 2:236]. Thus, Allah's determination (taqdīr Allāh) takes precedence over the judge's determination. The best basis for the judge's determination is the Law's determination.

In our view, consideration is given to the husband's condition regarding incapacity and capacity, not to her condition. The destitute (al-muʿsir) is one who owns nothing at all; upon him is one mudd, and no more. If he is capable of earning more, then [we examine further]: if he has exited the limit of eligibility for the share of the poor (sahm al-masākīn) by owning wealth, then if it is abundant, he is affluent (mūsir). If he is such that were we to obligate two mudds upon him, he would likely revert to the level of the poor, then he is middle-class (mutawassiṭ); upon him is one and a half mudds.

Upon the mukātab (slave under contract of manumission) and the [ordinary] slave, only the maintenance of the destitute is obligatory. Likewise, upon one who is half slave and half free. Al-Muzanī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Upon him is half the maintenance of the destitute and half the maintenance of the affluent. This is the ruling on the quantity.

As for the type (jins) of food, it is the dominant staple of the land (ghālib qūt al-balad). If [staples] differ, then [it is] what befits the husband. If the husband's condition differs from the dominant [staple], then it is in a position of deliberation (maḥall al-taraddud).

The second obligatory item is the condiment (al-idām). Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A measure (makīlah) of oil or clarified butter (samn). This is an approximation (taqrīb), for there is no fixed measure in the Law for it. Rather, the obligatory [amount] is what suffices with the mudd or the two mudds. Reference regarding the type is to the dominant [custom] of the land or to what befits the husband's condition.

As for meat (al-laḥm), al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: One raṭl of meat per week if the obligatory [food] is one mudd, and two raṭls for [the recipient of] two mudds. The Iraqis said: Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) based this on the custom of his town (ʿādat baladihi) which he was familiar with. If the custom of another town requires more than that, then it should be increased. Al-Qaffāl (may Allah have mercy on him) said: There is no increase upon it, for we restrict ourselves to the minimum, as in the case of food.

Two subsidiary points (farʿān):

First: If she were to pass her time with dry bread (al-khubz al-qifār), her right to the condiment is not nullified, just as if she did not eat the staple food at all, she would still be entitled to the food.

Second: If she becomes weary (tabarramat) of a single type of condiment, then it is obligatory upon the husband to replace it in one respect, and not obligatory in another respect. Rather, upon her is to replace it if she wishes.

The third obligatory item is the servant (al-khādimah). The maintenance of her servant is obligatory if her station (manṣib) requires that she be served. If being served is not befitting her station, and she is served only due to illness, then it is not obligatory, for the causes of medical treatment are not obligatory. If she has a chronic affliction (zamānah) and permanent illness, then she likewise needs the servant. This [case] is subject to deliberation (yaḥtamil), for this permanent excuse is no less [worthy] than the observance of dignity (murāʿāt al-ḥishmah).

Then, upon the destitute [husband] for the servant is one mudd, and upon the affluent is one and a third [mudds]. Thus said al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him). It is an approximation, not a fixed measure, for there is no fixed measure in the Law for it. Indeed, it is two raṭls, which befits custom in the case of the servant.

The correct [view] is that consideration is given to her sufficiency (kifāyatuhā), except that this amount is the measure of sufficiency in most cases.

Regarding her entitlement to the condiment, there are two views (wajhān):

First: Yes, like the one served [i.e., the wife]. However, it is permissible that her condiment be inferior in type and, in quantity, what befits the measure of her food.

Second: She is not entitled to it; rather, she suffices with what the mistress leaves over (tafḍuluhu) in some circumstances.
