chapters.arabic_text:
الأول اختلفت نصوص الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الصابئين وهم فرقة من النصارى
وفي السامرة وهم  فرقة من اليهود فمنهم من قال إنه تردد لتردده في أنهم
مبتدعة عندهم أو كفرة فإن صح كفرهم بأن قالوا مدبر العالم النجوم السبعة أو
قالوا بقدم النور والظلمة فلا يقرر لأنه يناقض موجب الكتب المنزلة ومنهم من
قال وإن كانوا مبتدعة فالقولان جائزان إذ تضعف بالبدعة حرمتهم
وهذا الخلاف إنما ينقدح في نكاحهم لأن مبتدعة الإسلام يناكحون لأخبار
منعت من التكفير فلا يعد في التغليظ على مبتدعة أهل الكتاب
الثاني قلو قبلنا جزيته فأسلم منهم رجلان عدلان شهدا أنه كافر بدينهم
تبين انتقضا العهد ونغتاله لتلبيسه علينا وإنما تثبت علقة الأمان عند جهلهم
الثالث المتولد بين وثني وكتابية وبعكسه في مناكحته قولان الصحيح
أنه يقرر ومنهم من طرد القولين
الرابع إذا توثن نصراني وله أولاد صغار فإن كانت الأم نصرانية استمر حكم
تنصرهم بعد البلوغ وإن كانت وثنية فقولان أحدهما أنه تبقى علقة التنصير لهم
فيقررون بعد البلوغ
والثاني أنهم يتبعون في التوثن أيضا لكن لا يغتالون وفي اغتيال أبيهم
خلاف
الخامس الولد الحاصل من المرتدين في إسلامهم لأجل علقة الإسلام في المرتد
خلاف فإن قضينا به فإن لم يصرحوا بعد البلوغ فهم مرتدون وإن لم نقض به فلا
يقرون إذ لم يثبت دين آبائه قبل المبعث وفيه وجه بعيد لا اتجاه له إذ تخرم
القاعدة في مراعاة تقديم الدين على المبعث ولعى هذا يتجه التردد في نكاحهم
والصحيح المنع
والصحيح أنه لا يحل وطء سبايا غوراء إذ صح أنهم ارتدوا بعد الإسلام نعم
ينقدح التردد في استرقاقهم بناء على أنهم كفار أصليون فإن عبدة الأوثان لا
يمتنع إرقاقهم على ظاهر المذهب وفيه وجه أنه يمتنع لأن فيه أمانا مؤبدا
لوثني
القيد الثاني العقل فلا يؤخذ من المجنون جزية بل هو تابع كالصبي ولو وقع
في الأسر رق بنفس الأسر كالصبي وإن كان يجن يوما ويفيق يوما ففي وجه يعتبر
آخر الحول وفي وجه تلفق أيام الإفاقة سنة ويؤخذ لها دينار وهو الأقيس وهو
مذهب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله  وفي وجه ينظر إلى الأغلب وفي
وجه لا نظر إلى جنون منقطع بل هو كالغشية بل تجب جزية كاملة وفي وجه أنه
لا ينظر إلى عقل منقطع فلا جزية عليه أصلا والوجهان الأخيران ضعيفان وإن
وقع مثل هذا في الأسر فالصحيح أنه ينظر إلى وقت الأسر
القيد الثالث الصغير فلا يؤخد منه جزية بل هو تابع أبيه ثم إذا بلغ عاقلا
ففيه وجهان
أحدهما أنه لا حاجة إلى الإستئناف بل يلزمه مثل ما التزم أبوه وكأنه عقد
لنفسه ولولده بعد البلوغ والثاني أنه يستأنف لنفسه
فلو بلغ سفيها والتزم زيادة نفذ لأنه يحقن به دمه كما لو كان عليه قصاص
فصالح على أكثر من الدية فليس للولي المنع لأن حقن الدم أهم من المال ولو
عقد له الولي بزيادة لم يكن للسفيه المنع كما يشتري له الطعام في
المخمصة قهرا لصيانة روحه
وإن قلنا لا يستأنف فإن كان الأب قد التزم زيادة لزمه بعد البلوغ وكان
امتناعه كامتناع أبيه من الزيادة
القيد الرابع الحرية فالعبد تابع فلا جزية عليه وكذا من نصفه حر ونصفه
رقيق
القيد الخامس الذكورة فلا جزية على المرأة إذ لا تتعرض للقتل بل هي تابعة
وللرجل أن يستتبع بدينار واحد جمعا من النساء الأقارب والزوجات ولا يشترط
المحرمية أما الأصهار والأحماء فمنهم من ألحقهن بالأجانب ومنهم من ألحقهن
بالأقارب والصبيان والمجانين الأقارب أيضا يجوز استتباعهم
هذا فيه إذا شرط في العقد فإن أطلق لم يتبع الأقارب والأصهار أما أولاده
الصغار فوجهان وفي زوجاته طريقان أحدهما أنهن كالأولاد والثاني أنهن
كالأقارب
والأصح أن الزوجة والولد مما يقتضيه الإطلاق فلا حاجة إلى الشرط
ثم إذا دخل صبي أو امرأة دارنا من غير أمان وتبعية أوقفناهما وكذلك
المجنون والحربي يتخير فيه بين القتل والإرقاق
فرع إذا حاصرنا قلعة وليس فيها إلا النسوان فإن فتحناها جرى الرق عليهن
بمجرد الظفر وإن بذلن الجزية لدفع الرق فالصحيح أنه لا يجب القبول إذ لو
جاز لها دفع الرق بالجزية كما يجوز للرجل  دفع القتل لما كانت تابعة في
الجزية بل صار أصلا كالرجل ولكان إذا دخلت دارنا لم يجز إرقاقها إن بذلت
الجزية وهو بعيد
والثاني أنه يجب القبول وإنما التبعية إذا كان معها رجل قريب أو زوج
وإنما لا تستقل إذا وقعت في الأسر لأنها رقت بمجرد الأسر
أما إذا كان فيهن رجل واحد وبذل الجزية كان عصمة لجميع النسوان إن كن من
أهله وإن كن أجانب فلا وقد أطلق الأصحاب عصمة الجميع ولعل هذا مرادهم
القيد السادس المتأهب للقتال واحترزنا به عن الزمني وأرباب الصوامع ومن
ذكرنا خلافا في قتلهم فمنهم من قال إذا منعنا قتلهم فهم كالنسوان فلا جزية
عليهم ومنهم من قطع بأخذ الجزية للجنسية وهو الأصح
القيد السابع القدرة واحترزنا به عن الكافر الفقير الذي ليس بكسوب ففيه
ثلاثة أقوال أحدهما أنه يخرج من الدار ولا يقرر مجانا والثاني أنه يقرر
مجانا لأنه معذور والثالث أنه يقرر بجزية تستقر في ذمته إلى أن يقدر
الركن الرابع في البقاع التي يقرر بها الكافر ويجوز تقريرهم بكل بقعة إلا
الحجاز فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو عشت لأخرجت اليهود والنصارى من جزيرة
العرب ثم لم يعش صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يتفرغ له أبو بكر رضي الله عنه
فأجلاهم عمر رضي الله عنه وهم زهاء أربعين ألفا
ونعني بجزيرة العرب مكة والمدينة واليمامة ومخاليفها والطائف ووج وما
ينسب إليها منسوب إلى مكة وفي بعض الكتب التهامة ولعله تصحيف اليمامة وخيبر
من مخاليف المدينة
وقال العراقيون جزيرة العرب تمتد إلى أطراف العراق من جانب وإلى أطراف
الشام من جانب وعلى هذا تلتحق اليمن بالجزيرة فتحصلنا فيه على خلاف
هذا في المخاليف والبلاد أما الطرق المعترضة بينهما فهل يمنعون من
الإقامة بها وفيه وجهان أحدهما لا لأن المراد المنع من الإختلاط بالعرب
حرمة لهم والثاني أنهم يمنعون لأن الحرمة للبقعة
ثم لا خلاف أنهم لا يمنعون من الإجتياز لسفارة أو تجارة ولكن بشرط أن لا
يقيمون في موضع أكثر من  ثلاثة أيام ولا يحسب يوم الدخول والخروج إلا في مكة
فإنه يمنع ولا يمكن الكافر من دخولها مجتازا ولا برسالة بل يخرج إليه من
يستمع الرسالة لقوله تعالى {فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا} ولا
يجري هذا التغليظ في المدينة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes recompense, requital, or payment in return for protection; jizyah is the tax exacted from non-Muslims in exchange for security and exemption from military service.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological-juridical terms, jizyah signifies the contractual tribute that establishes the covenant of protection (dhimmah), symbolizing the subordinate status of the non-Muslim under Islamic sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to payment; metaphorical extension applies to any obligation incurred as a condition of a pact, distinguishing the contractual nature from mere tribute.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if we accept his jizyah...") and exceptions (e.g., "except the Hijaz") requiring precise parsing to preserve legal distinctions between general rules and their qualifications.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first [issue]: The texts of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, differ concerning the Ṣābiʾūn, who are a sect of the Christians, and concerning the Samaritans, who are a sect of the Jews. Some [jurists] said that [his ruling] is hesitant due to his uncertainty as to whether they are innovators (mubtadiʿah) in their own religion or disbelievers (kuffār). For if their disbelief is established — such as their saying that the seven planets direct the world, or their asserting the eternity of light and darkness — then they are not to be confirmed [in their religion], because this contradicts the import of the revealed scriptures. Others said: Even if they are innovators, both opinions are permissible, for their inviolability is weakened by their innovation. This disagreement only arises concerning marriage with them, because innovators among the Muslims are married [to Muslims] due to reports that prohibit declaring them disbelievers; thus, severity is not extended to innovators among the People of the Book.

The second [issue]: If we accept his jizyah, and then two just men from among them embrace Islam and testify that he is a disbeliever in their religion, it becomes evident that the covenant is annulled, and we may treacherously kill him (naghtālahu) for his deception of us. The bond of safety (amān) is only established when they are ignorant [of the truth].

The third [issue]: Concerning one born between a pagan father and a scriptuary mother, and vice versa, there are two opinions regarding marriage with him. The correct [opinion] is that he is confirmed [in his father's religion]. Some [jurists] extended both opinions [to this case].

The fourth [issue]: If a Christian becomes a pagan and has young children, then if the mother is Christian, the ruling of their Christianity continues after they reach maturity. If the mother is pagan, there are two opinions: One is that the bond of their Christianity remains, so they are confirmed [as Christians] after maturity. The second is that they follow [the father] in paganism as well, but they are not to be treacherously killed. Concerning the treacherous killing of their father, there is a disagreement.

The fifth [issue]: Concerning a child born from apostates, regarding his Islam due to the bond of Islam in the apostate, there is a disagreement. If we rule [that he is Muslim], then if they do not explicitly [revert] after maturity, they are apostates. If we do not so rule, then they are not confirmed [in any religion], since the religion of their forefathers before the mission [of the Prophet] is not established. There is a remote opinion with no basis, as it breaches the principle of considering the precedence of religion before the mission; upon this [remote view] the hesitation in their marriage would be directed, but the correct [opinion] is prohibition.

The correct [opinion] is that it is not lawful to have intercourse with female captives from Ghawrāʾ, since it is established that they apostatized after Islam. Indeed, hesitation arises concerning their enslavement, based on the view that they are original disbelievers, for idolaters are not prevented from being enslaved according to the apparent [position] of the school. There is an opinion that it is prevented, because there is in it a perpetual safety (amān muʾabbad) for a pagan.

The second condition: Sanity (al-ʿaql). No jizyah is taken from the insane person; rather, he is a dependent (tābiʿ), like a child. If he falls into captivity, he is enslaved by the mere fact of capture, like a child. If he is insane one day and lucid the next, there is an opinion that the end of the year is considered; and an opinion that the days of lucidity are aggregated to complete a year, for which one dinar is taken — and this is the more analogical (al-aqyas), and it is the school of Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him. There is an opinion that the predominant [state] is considered; and an opinion that intermittent insanity is not considered, being like a fainting spell, so a full jizyah is obligatory; and an opinion that intermittent lucidity is not considered, so no jizyah is due at all. The last two opinions are weak. If such a case occurs in captivity, the correct [opinion] is that the time of capture is considered.

The third condition: Minority (al-ṣighar). No jizyah is taken from the minor; rather, he is a dependent of his father. Then, when he reaches maturity as a sane person, there are two opinions: One is that no renewal is needed; rather, the like of what his father undertook is incumbent upon him, as if the contract were made for himself and his offspring after maturity. The second is that he renews [the contract] for himself. If he reaches maturity as a spendthrift (safīh) and undertakes an increase [in jizyah], it is executed, because he thereby preserves his blood, just as if he had a liability for retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and settled for more than the blood-money (diyah); the guardian has no right to prevent it, because preserving blood is more important than wealth. If the guardian contracts an increase on his behalf, the spendthrift has no right to refuse, just as food is purchased for him in famine by compulsion, for the preservation of his soul. If we say he does not renew, then if the father had undertaken an increase, it becomes incumbent upon him after maturity, and his refusal is like his father's refusal of the increase.

The fourth condition: Freedom (al-ḥurriyyah). The slave is a dependent, so no jizyah is upon him. Likewise, one who is half free and half enslaved.

The fifth condition: Masculinity (al-dhukūrah). No jizyah is upon the woman, for she is not subject to killing; rather, she is a dependent. A man may include as dependents, with a single dinar, women who are relatives and wives, without requiring a degree of consanguinity that prohibits marriage (maḥramiyyah). As for in-laws and paternal relatives' wives, some have likened them to strangers, and others to relatives. Young children and insane relatives may also be included as dependents. This [applies] if stipulated in the contract; if left absolute, relatives and in-laws are not included. As for his young children, there are two opinions; and concerning his wives, there are two paths: one that they are like children, and the second that they are like relatives. The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that the wife and child are implied by the absolute [contract], so no stipulation is needed. Then, if a child or a woman enters our territory without amān or dependency, we detain them; likewise the insane person. The hostile [male] is given the choice between killing and enslavement.

A branch: If we besiege a fortress in which there are only women, then if we conquer it, enslavement applies to them by the mere fact of victory. If they offer the jizyah to repel enslavement, the correct [opinion] is that acceptance is not obligatory, for if it were permissible for her to repel enslavement by jizyah, just as it is permissible for a man to repel killing, then she would not be a dependent in jizyah but would become a principal (aṣl) like a man; and if she entered our territory, it would not be permissible to enslave her if she offered jizyah — which is far-fetched. The second [opinion] is that acceptance is obligatory, and her dependency [applies] only when there is with her a male relative or husband; she is not independent only when she falls into captivity, because she is enslaved by the mere fact of capture. As for when there is among them a single man who offers jizyah, it is a protection (ʿiṣmah) for all the women if they are of his household; if they are strangers, then not. The [authoritative] scholars (al-aṣḥāb) have stated absolutely the protection of all, and perhaps this is their intent.

The sixth condition: Readiness for fighting (al-taʾahhub li-l-qitāl). By this we exclude the chronically ill (zamānā), the monks in their cells, and those regarding whose killing we mentioned a disagreement. Some said: If we prevent their killing, they are like women, so no jizyah is upon them. Others decisively affirmed taking jizyah from them due to their [male] gender — and this is the more correct.

The seventh condition: Capability (al-qudrah). By this we exclude the poor disbeliever who is not a wage-earner. Concerning him, there are three opinions: One is that he is expelled from the territory and not confirmed for free. The second is that he is confirmed for free, because he is excused. The third is that he is confirmed with a jizyah that remains as a debt in his liability until he becomes capable.

The fourth pillar: Concerning the places in which the disbeliever may be confirmed. It is permissible to confirm them in every place except the Hijaz, for the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: {«لو عشت لأخرجت اليهود والنصارى من جزيرة العرب»} — "If I lived, I would expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula." Then he, peace be upon him, did not live [to do so], and Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him, did not have the opportunity; so ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, expelled them, and they numbered nearly forty thousand. By the Arabian Peninsula (Jazīrat al-ʿArab) we mean Mecca, Medina, al-Yamāmah and its districts, al-Ṭāʾif, Wajj, and what is attributed to Mecca; in some books [it is said] al-Tihāmah, and perhaps it is a corruption of al-Yamāmah. Khaybar is among the districts of Medina. The Iraqis said: The Arabian Peninsula extends to the borders of Iraq on one side and to the borders of Syria on the other; upon this, Yemen is annexed to the Peninsula, so we have a disagreement concerning it. This concerns the districts and towns. As for the intervening roads, are they prevented from residing there? There are two opinions: One is no, because the intent is to prevent mixing with the Arabs, as an honor to them. The second is that they are prevented, because the sanctity belongs to the place itself. Then, there is no disagreement that they are not prevented from passing through for embassy or trade, but on the condition that they do not stay in any place more than three days, not counting the day of entry and exit. Except in Mecca, for they are prevented, and a disbeliever cannot be permitted to enter it even as a passer-by or with a message; rather, one goes out to him to hear the message, due to His saying, the Exalted: {«فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا»} — "So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs." This severity does not apply to Medina.

chapters.title_en: On the Transfer of the Deceased from the Sacred Precinct and the Quantum of the Poll-Tax (Jizyah)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو دخل مكة ومرض وخيف من نقله الموت فلا يبالي وينقل ولو دفن نبش قبره
وأخرج عظامه تطهيرا للحرم وإن مات على طرف الحجاز وأمكن نقله نقل قبل الدفن
وإن دفن ففي نبش قبره وجهان
ولو مرض في الحجاز لم ينقل إن خيف موته فإن كان يشق النقل ولا يخاف الموت
ففي وجوب نقله وجهان فإن مات في غير مكة ودفن وعظمت المشقة في نقله تركناه
ولم نرفع نعش قبره

### | الركن الخامس في قدر الجزية الواجبة والواجبات عليهم خمسة

الأول نفس الجزية وأقلها دينار في السنة على كل محتلم كما سبق أو اثني
عشر درهما نقرة ويخير الإمام بينهما والتخيير مستنده قضاء عمر رضي الله عنه
وإلا فلم يرد في الخبر إلا الدينار وشبب بعض الأصحاب بأن النقرة نقومها
بالذهب كما في نصاب السرقة
ثم إن لم يبذلوا إلا دينار وجب القبول وللإمام أن يماكس في الزيادة فإن
بذل زيادة ثم علم أن الزيادة لم تكن واجبة لم ينفعه وكان كمن اشترى بالغبن
نعم لو نبذ إلينا العهد ثم رجع وطلب العقد بدينار وجبت الإجابة
وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله على الفقير دينار وعلى الغني أربعة وعلى
المتوسط ديناران وعندنا لا فرق
ولو أسلم أو مات بعد مضي السنة استوفي عندنا ولو تكرر سنون لم تتداخل
خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله في المسألتين ولو كان عليه ديون ومات قدمت
الجزية على وصاياه وديونه ومنهم من قال بل الجزية من حقوق
الله فتقدم على حق الآدمي في قول وتؤخر في قول وتستوي في قول

### | فرع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ق-ل (na-qāf-lām)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to move, transport, or transmit" something from one locus to another; also used for "transcription" of speech or text.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the physical relocation of a body or obligation, carrying implications of ritual purity (ṭahārah) and respect for sacred space (ḥurmat al-ḥaram).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical conveyance; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to transferring legal liability or rulings across contexts.
- Root: ج-ز-ي (jīm-zāy-yā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root signifies "sufficiency" or "recompense"; the noun jizyah derives from the idea of a payment that suffices as a tribute or compensation for protection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the annual tribute levied on non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimmah) in exchange for security and exemption from military service—a contractual obligation, not a punitive exaction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for "payment that fulfills"; metaphorical extension to "what suffices" in legal obligations, distinguishing it from ṣadaqah (voluntary alms).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs layered conditionals (law, in) and exceptions (illā) requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve legal precision, especially in the phrase "لو نبذ إلينا العهد ثم رجع" where the temporal sequence (thumma) governs the ruling.
chapters.translation:
### | Branch

If one entered Mecca and fell ill, and it was feared that moving him would cause death, then no heed is paid [to that fear], and he is moved. And if he was buried, his grave is exhumed and his bones are extracted to purify the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram). And if he died on the edge of the Ḥijāz and it was possible to move him, he is moved before burial. But if he was buried, then concerning the exhumation of his grave there are two positions (wajhān).

And if he fell ill in the Ḥijāz, he is not moved if his death is feared. But if the moving is burdensome and his death is not feared, then concerning the obligation of moving him there are two positions. And if he died in a place other than Mecca, was buried, and the hardship of moving him became great, we leave him and do not raise the bier of his grave.

### | The Fifth Pillar: On the Quantum of the Obligatory Poll-Tax (Jizyah), and the Obligations upon Them Are Five

The first is the poll-tax itself. Its minimum is one dīnār per year upon every adult male (muḥtalim), as previously stated—or twelve dirhams of pure silver (naqrah). The Imām has the choice between the two, and the basis of this choice is the judgment of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him. Otherwise, nothing has been reported in the tradition (khabar) except the dīnār. Some of our companions (al-aṣḥāb) have suggested that the silver (naqrah) be valued in gold, just as in the nisāb of theft.

Then, if they offer nothing but a dīnār, acceptance is obligatory. And the Imām may bargain for an increase. But if they offer an increase, and it then becomes known that the increase was not obligatory, it does not benefit them—he is like one who purchased with an overpayment (ghabn). Yes, if they cast the covenant back to us (nabadha al-ʿahd), then returned and sought the contract with a dīnār, the response is obligatory.

Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: Upon the poor man is one dīnār, upon the wealthy is four, and upon the middle-class is two. But in our view, there is no distinction.

And if one converted to Islam or died after the passage of the year, we collect it in our view. And if years repeat, they do not overlap (lā tadākhal), contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, in both matters. And if one had debts and died, the poll-tax is given precedence over his bequests and his debts. Among them are those who said: Rather, the poll-tax is among the rights of God (ḥuqūq Allāh), so it takes precedence over the right of a human being—in one saying it is advanced, in another it is deferred, and in another they are equalized.

### | Branch

chapters.title_en: Section 524 — On the Obligations of the Protected People (Ahl al-Dhimmah): The Jizyah, Hospitality, Humiliation, Tithe on Merchants, and Land Tax (Kharāj)
chapters.arabic_text:
لو مات في أثناء السنة ففي وجوب قسطه قولان
أحدهما أنه لا يجب إلا لتمام السنة كالزكاة والثاني أنه يجب كالأجرة
ويشير هذا إلى  تردد في أنها هل تجب بأول السنة لكن تستقر بتمامها أو تجب
شيئا شيئا وبنوا على هذا أن الإمام لو طلب شيئا في أثناء السنة هل يجوز
مع استمرار الحياة والظاهر المنع لأنه على خلاف سير الأولين
الواجب الثاني الضيافة وقد وظف عمر رضي الله عنه الضيافة لمن يطرقهم من
أبناء السبيل فاتفقوا على جواز ذلك بشرط أن نبين لكل واحد عدد الضيفان وقدر
الطعام والأدم وجنسه وعلف الدابة ومنازل الضيفان وليفاوت بين الغني والفقير
في عدد الضيفان لا في جنس الطعام كي لا يؤدي إلى التزاحم على الغني ويبين
مدة إقامة الضيف من يوم إلى ثلاثة أيام فقد ورد أن الضيافة ثلاثة أيام فما
زاد صدقة ويقال إجازة يوم وليلة أعني ما يعطي الضيف ليتزود في الطريق إذا
رحل
ثم هذا محسوب لهم من نفس الدينار إذ كان عمر رضي الله عنه لا يطالبهم
بالجزية مع الضيافة ومنهم من أبى ذلك لأن الإطعام ليس بتمليك وهو كالتغدية
في الكفارة
فإن قلنا إنه من الجزية فما نقص من الدينار يجب أن يكمل ولو أراد نقلهم
عن الضيافة إلى الدنانير بعد ضربه بغير رضاهم ففيه وجهان وكأنه تردد في أن
ضربه هل ينقعد لازما
والصحيح أنه إن قلنا إنه من الدينار فيجوز الإبدال وإن قلنا إنه أصل فلا
بد من رضاهم في الإبدال
ثم إذا أبدلت فقد كانت الضيافة لجميع الطارقين فهل يصرف البدل إلى جميع
المصالح أم يختص بأهل الفيء فيه وجهان والظاهر أنه لأهل الفيء لأن ذلك
احتمل في الضيافة لعسر الضبط
الواجب الثالث الإهانة والتصغير عند الأخذ لقوله تعالى {حتى يعطوا الجزية
عن يد وهم صاغرون} قيل معناه أن يطأطىء الذمي رأسه ويصب ما معه في كف
المستوفي فيأخذ المستوفي بلحيته ويضرب في لهازمه
وهذا مستحب أو مستحق فيه وجهان
فإن قلنا إنه مستحق لم يجز له توكيل المسلم في التوفية ولم يصح ضمان
المسلم للجزية فإنه يجب قبولها إذا أسلم وتسقط الإهانة
ولكن الصحيح أنه مستحب إذ  يجوز إسقاطها بتضعيف الصدقة كما فعل عمر رضي
الله عنه فإن جماعة من نصارى العرب أنفوا من اسم الجزية والصغار فقالوا نحن
عرب فخذ منا ما يأخذ بعضكم من بعض يعني الزكاة فقال عمر رضي الله عنه إنها
طهرة ولستم من أهلها فقالوا خذ بذلك الإسم وزد ما شئت فضعف عليهم الصدقة
وحط اسم الجزية والإهانة ولا شك في أن المأخوذ جزية حتى لا تؤخذ من النساء
والصبيان
ولا بد أن يفي بقدر الجزية إذا وزع على رءوس البالغين وله أن يأخذ ثلاثة
أمثال الصدقة وله أن يأخذ نصف الصدقة إن وفى بالجزية ولكن لا يترك الإهانة
إلا لغرض ظاهر
فإن كثروا ولم يمكن عدهم لتبيين الوفاء ففي جواز أخذه بغالب الظن وجهان
والفقراء هل يدخلون في الحساب يخرج على القولين في العقد وهل يجوز ذلك مع
غير العرب فيه وجهان والظاهر جوازه للمصلحة
ثم صيغة العقد أن يقول الإمام ضعفت عليكم الصدقة فيلزمه عليكم الصدقة
فيلزمه الوفاء فيأخذ من خمس من الإبل شاتين ومن عشر أربع شياه ومن خمس
وعشرين بنتي مخاض ولا يضعف المال فيجعله كالخمسين ويأخذ حقه بل نضعفه
الصدقة ونأخذ الخمس مما سقته السماء والعشر مما سقي بدالية ومن عشرين
دينارا دينارا واختلفوا في مسألتين
إحداهما أنه هل يحط لهم الوقص فيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه يحط كالصدقة
والثاني لا لأن ذلك تخفيف عن المسلمين والثالث
أنه يأخذ إن لم يؤد إلى التجزئة فيأخذ من سبعة ونصف من الإبل ثلاث شياه
وقد حكي عن الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه قال يأخذ من عشرين شاة شاة ومن مائة
درهم خمسة دراهم
الثانية لو ملك ستا وثلاثين من الإبل وليس في ماله بنت لبون فيأخذ بنتي
مخاض وجبرانين لكل جبران واحد شاتين أو عشرين درهما ولا يضعف الجبران ثانيا
ومن قال بذلك فقد غلط وكذلك إذا أخرج حقتين فعلى الإمام الجبران
الواجب الرابع العشر من البضاعة التي مع تجارهم إذا ترددوا في بلادنا
والنظر فيمن يعشر ماله وفي  قدر المأخوذ
أما من يؤخذ منه فهو كل حربي يتجر في بلادنا ضرب عمر رضي الله عنه عليهم
العشر أما الذمي فلا شيء عليه إذا اتجر ولا على الحربي إذا دخل لسفارة أو
سماع كلام الله تعالى
أما لو تردد في الحجاز لا للتجارة ففي أخذ شيء منه خلاف فقيل إنه لا يمكن
تعشير ماله
ولا بد من تعظيم الحجاز فيؤخذ دينار وهو أقل الجزية والذمي إذا اتجر في
الحجاز أخذ منه نصف العشر كذلك فعل عمر رضي الله عنه
ثم هذا إذا جرى الشرط وقبلوا فإن دخلوا بأمان من غير شرط فأصح الوجهين
أنه لا شيء عليهم والثاني أن قضاء عمر رضي الله عنه بذلك قضاء على من سيكون
منهم إلى يوم القيامة فيتبع
أما المقدار فلا مزيد على العشر وقل للإمام أن يزيد إن رأى وأما النقصان
فجائز إلى نصف العشر وذلك في الميرة وكل ما يحتاج المسلمون إلى كثرة
المكاسب فيه كذلك فعل عمر رضي الله عنه ولو رأى رفع هذه الضريبة أصلا
ففيه وجهان أحدهما أنه لا بد من قبول شيء والثاني أن هذا الجنس يتبع فيه
المصلحة إذ عمر رضي الله عنه فعل ذلك برأيه واستصوابه وقد يتغير الصواب
ثم إذا أخذ العشر مرة فلا يأخذه ثانيا في تلك السنة بل يعطى جوازا حتى لا
يطالبه عشار أصلا إلا إذا جوزنا الزيادة فعند ذلك يجوز أخذه في دفعات
أما إذا جرى ترديد مال واحد إلى الحجاز في سنة واحدة فهل يكرر العشر
لتعظيم الحجاز فيه خلاف وهذا إذا خرج من الحجاز وعاد وما دام يتردد فيه فلا
ولو بذل اللسان عند المشارطة بزيادة فالظاهر أنه لا يلزم إذ ليس ذلك عقدا
أصليا بخلاف عقد الجزية
الواجب الخامس الخراج وذلك قد يكون أجرة فلا يسقط بالإسلام كما إذا ملكنا
أراضيهم ثم رددناها إليهم بخراج كما فعله عمر رضي الله عنه وهذا واجب وراء
الجزية
أما إذا صالحناهم على عقارهم بخراج يؤدونه فملكهم مطرد والمأخوذ في حكم
جزية
ومن أسلم سقط الخراج عنه في المستقبل خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "equity" and "portion" — the fair share or apportioned part of a whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the proportional obligation that is due, often tied to the concept of distributive justice in fiscal duties.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (Ḥaqīqah) for a measured share; metaphorical (Majāz) when applied to time, indicating a temporal fraction of an annual duty.
- Root: ض-ي-ف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "hosting" or "receiving a guest" — the act of providing shelter and provision to a visitor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the context of communal obligations, it signifies the mandatory provision of hospitality as a collective duty toward travelers (Ibn al-Sabīl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical act of hosting; metaphorical when extended to the fiscal sphere, where it becomes a form of in-kind taxation.
- Root: ص-غ-ر (ṣ-gh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "smallness" or "lowness" — diminution in stature or rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, it signifies the state of subjugation and humility that the Quranic verse imposes upon the People of the Book in their payment of the jizyah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical lowering; metaphorical for the legal and social status of subordination.
- Root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "ten" — a tenth part.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fiscal jurisprudence, it is the tithe levied on the merchandise of traders, distinct from the alms-tax (zakāh) on Muslims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the numerical fraction; metaphorical when applied to the levy itself, indicating a fixed proportional tax.
- Root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "going out" or "emergence" — that which is extracted or produced.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In land-tenure law, it is the land tax imposed on conquered territories, distinct from the jizyah on persons.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for extraction from the earth; metaphorical for the fiscal extraction of revenue from land.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jazā') — In the sentence "لو مات في أثناء السنة ففي وجوب قسطه قولان" (If he dies mid-year, there are two opinions on the obligation of his portion), the particle "لو" (if) introduces a hypothetical condition, and the response (Jazā') is the legal ruling that follows. The construction requires careful parsing to distinguish the protasis from the apodosis, especially where the apodosis is a nominal sentence indicating a legal disagreement.
chapters.translation:
I say: If he dies in the midst of the year, then concerning the obligation of his apportioned share there are two opinions. One of them is that it is not obligatory except upon the completion of the full year, like the alms-tax (zakāh). The second is that it is obligatory like a rental payment (ujrah). And this points to a hesitation concerning whether it is obligated at the beginning of the year but only becomes firmly established (yastaqirr) upon its completion, or whether it is obligated portion by portion. And upon this they built the question: if the Imam were to demand something in the midst of the year, is that permissible while life continues? And the apparent view is the prohibition, because it contravenes the practice (sīrah) of the early predecessors (al-awwalīn).

The second obligation is hospitality (ḍiyāfah). And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, imposed hospitality upon those whom the wayfarers (abnā' al-sabīl) would visit. They agreed upon the permissibility of that, on the condition that we specify for each one the number of guests, the quantity of food and condiment (udm) and its type, the fodder for the animal, and the lodgings of the guests. And one should differentiate between the rich and the poor in the number of guests, not in the type of food, so that this does not lead to crowding upon the rich. And one should specify the duration of the guest's stay, from one day to three days. For it has been reported that hospitality is three days, and whatever exceeds that is charity (ṣadaqah). And it is said: a license (ijāzah) of a day and a night — I mean, that which is given to the guest as provision (tazawwud) for the road when he departs.

Then this is reckoned for them from the very dīnār, since ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, would not demand from them the jizyah along with the hospitality. And among them (the scholars) was one who rejected that, because feeding is not a transfer of ownership (tamlīk), and it is like the feeding in the expiation (kaffārah).

If we say that it is from the jizyah, then whatever falls short of the dīnār must be completed. And if he (the Imam) wished to transfer them from hospitality to dīnārs after imposing it (the jizyah) without their consent, then there are two faces (wajhān). And it is as though he hesitated concerning whether his imposition (ḍarb) becomes a binding contract (lāzim).

And the correct view is: if we say it is from the dīnār, then substitution (ibdāl) is permissible; and if we say it is an independent obligation (aṣl), then their consent is indispensable for substitution.

Then, when it has been substituted, hospitality was for all those who arrive (al-ṭāriqīn). So is the substitute (badal) to be spent upon all public interests (maṣāliḥ), or is it restricted to the people of the fay' (the public treasury)? There are two faces. And the apparent view is that it is for the people of the fay', because that (i.e., generality) was tolerated in hospitality due to the difficulty of precise control (ʿusrat al-ḍabṭ).

The third obligation is humiliation (ihānah) and belittlement (taṣghīr) at the time of collection, due to His saying, the Exalted: {حَتَّى يُعْطُوا الْجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ} (Until they give the jizyah out of hand while they are humbled). It is said that its meaning is that the dhimmī lowers his head and pours what he has into the palm of the collector (al-mustawfī), and the collector takes him by his beard and strikes him on his jawbones (lahāzim). And this is either recommended (mustaḥabb) or obligatory (mustaḥaqq) — there are two faces.

If we say it is obligatory, then it is not permissible for him (the dhimmī) to appoint a Muslim as his proxy in the payment (tawkiyyah), and the guarantee (ḍamān) of a Muslim for the jizyah is not valid, for it must be accepted when he (the dhimmī) embraces Islam, and the humiliation falls away.

But the correct view is that it is recommended, since it is permissible to drop it by doubling the alms-tax (taḍʿīf al-ṣadaqah), as ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, did. For a group of the Arab Christians were averse to the name of jizyah and humiliation (ṣaghār), and they said: "We are Arabs, so take from us what some of you take from others" — meaning the zakāh. So ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "It is a purification (ṭuhrah), and you are not of its people." They said: "Take it under that name, and increase whatever you wish." So he doubled the alms-tax upon them and removed the name of jizyah and the humiliation. And there is no doubt that what is taken is jizyah, such that it is not taken from women and children.

And it is indispensable that it fulfill the measure of the jizyah when distributed upon the heads of the adult males. And he (the Imam) may take three times the alms-tax, and he may take half the alms-tax if it fulfills the jizyah. But he should not abandon the humiliation except for a manifest purpose (gharaḍ ẓāhir).

If they are numerous and it is not possible to count them to ascertain the fulfillment, then concerning the permissibility of taking according to predominant conjecture (ghālib al-ẓann) there are two faces. And do the poor enter into the calculation? This branches out upon the two opinions concerning the contract (al-ʿaqd). And is that permissible with non-Arabs? There are two faces. And the apparent view is its permissibility for the public interest (maṣlaḥah).

Then the formula of the contract is that the Imam says: "I have doubled the alms-tax upon you." So the alms-tax becomes incumbent upon them, and he (the Imam) is bound to fulfill it. So he takes from five camels two sheep, from ten four sheep, and from twenty-five two she-camels in their second year (bintā makhāḍ). And he does not double the wealth itself, making it like fifty and taking his due; rather, we double the alms-tax and take a fifth from what the sky waters, and a tenth from what is watered by a waterwheel (dāliyah), and from twenty dīnārs one dīnār. And they differed on two questions.

One of them: whether he reduces (yuḥiṭṭ) for them the exempt amount (al-waqṣ). There are three faces: one, that he reduces it like the alms-tax; the second, that he does not, because that is a concession (takhfīf) for the Muslims; and the third, that he takes — if it does not lead to fragmentation (tajzi'ah) — so he takes from seven and a half camels three sheep. And it has been narrated from al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "He takes from twenty sheep one sheep, and from one hundred dirhams five dirhams."

The second question: if one owns thirty-six camels and there is no she-camel in his wealth that is a bint labūn (a two-year-old), then he takes two bintā makhāḍ and two compensations (jabrānān), for each compensation one of two sheep or twenty dirhams. And the compensation is not doubled a second time. And whoever said that has erred. Likewise, if he brings forth two ḥiqqah (three-year-old she-camels), then the Imam must exact the compensation.

The fourth obligation is the tithe (ʿushr) on the merchandise (biḍāʿah) that is with their merchants when they circulate (taraddud) in our lands. And the consideration is in two matters: who is subject to the tithe on his wealth, and the measure of what is taken.

As for who is taken from: it is every ḥarbī (one from the abode of war) who trades in our lands. ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, imposed the tithe upon them. As for the dhimmī, there is nothing upon him if he trades; nor upon the ḥarbī if he enters for an embassy (sifārah) or for hearing the word of God, the Exalted.

As for if he circulates in the Ḥijāz not for trade, then concerning taking anything from him there is a disagreement. For it was said: it is not possible to tithe his wealth. And the Ḥijāz must be venerated, so a dīnār is taken, which is the minimum of the jizyah. And the dhimmī, if he trades in the Ḥijāz, half the tithe is taken from him. Thus did ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, do.

Then this applies when the condition is stipulated and they accept. But if they enter with a safe-conduct (amān) without a stipulation, then the sounder of the two faces is that nothing is upon them. The second is that the judgment (qaḍā') of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, in that matter is a judgment upon whoever will be among them until the Day of Resurrection, so it is followed.

As for the measure: there is no increase beyond the tithe, and it is not said that the Imam may increase if he sees fit. As for decrease, it is permissible down to half the tithe, and that applies to provisions (mīrah) and everything in which the Muslims need an abundance of profit. Thus did ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, do. And if he saw fit to lift this tax entirely, there are two faces: one, that it is indispensable to accept something; the second, that this kind of matter follows the public interest, since ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, did that by his own judgment (ra'y) and his approval (istiswāb), and what is sound may change.

Then, if the tithe is taken once, it is not taken a second time in that year. Rather, a permit (jawāz) is given so that no tithe-collector (ʿashshār) may demand it from him at all, except if we permit the increase — at that point it becomes permissible to take it in installments.

As for if the same wealth circulates to the Ḥijāz multiple times in one year, is the tithe repeated for the veneration of the Ḥijāz? There is a disagreement in this. And this applies when it leaves the Ḥijāz and returns; but as long as it remains circulating within it, then no. And if one pledges verbally at the time of stipulation (mushāraṭah) to an increase, the apparent view is that it is not binding, for that is not an original contract, unlike the contract of jizyah.

The fifth obligation is the land tax (kharāj). And that may be a rental payment (ujrah), so it does not fall away with Islam — as when we came to own their lands and then returned them to them with a kharāj, as ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, did. And this is an obligation beyond the jizyah.

As for if we made peace with them (ṣālaḥnāhum) over their properties with a kharāj that they pay, then their ownership is continuous (muṭṭarid), and what is taken is in the ruling of jizyah.

And whoever embraces Islam, the kharāj falls away from him in the future, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him.

chapters.title_en: The Second Consideration: The Rulings of the Covenant of Protection (ʿAqd al-Dhimmah)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | النظر الثاني في أحكام عقد الذمة

وهو يقتضي وجوبا علينا وعليهم أما ما علينا فيرجع إلى أمرين الكف عنهم
وذب الكفار دونهم
أما الكف فمعناه أنا لا نتعرض لأنفهسم ومالهم ونعصمهم بالضمان ولا نريق
خمورهم ولا نتلف خنازيرهم ما داموا يخفونه ولا نمنعهم من التردد إلى
كنائسهم القديمة ولو أظهروا الخمور أرقناها ومن دخل دارهم وأراقها فقد تعدى
ولا ضمان عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله ولو غصبها وجب مئونة الرد وفيه
وجه أنه لا يجب إلا التخلية ولو باع خمرا من مسلم أريق على المسلم ولا ثمن
للذمي والظاهر أنه يجب رد الخمر المحترمة على المسلم إذا غصب
أما الذب عنهم فمعناه دفع الكفار عنهم ما داموا في دارنا وهو ذب عن الدار
ولو دخلوا دار الحرب فلا مطمع للذب ولو انفردوا ببلدة غير متصلة ببلاد
الإسلام ففي وجوب ذب أهل الحرب عنهم وجهان أحدهما أنه لا يجب إذ لم نلتزم
إلا الكف
والثاني أنه يجب إذ بذلوا الجزية لنسلك بهم مسلك أهل الإسلام فعلى هذا لو
شرطنا أن لا نذب عنهم لم يلزمنا ومنهم من ألغى هذا الشرط وعلى الأول لو
شرطنا الذب لزمنا ومنهم من ألغى ذلك الشرط وكذلك لو ترافعوا إلينا هل يجب
الحكم بينهم فيه خلاف ويرجع حاصله إلى دفع أذى بعضهم عن بعض
أما الواجب عليهم فهو الوفاء بالجزية والإنقياد للأحكام والكف عن الفواحش
وعن بناء الكنائس ومطاولة المسلمين بالبنيان والتجمل بترك الغيار وركوب
الخيول وسلوك جادة الطرق هذه مجامعها
الأول حكم الكنائس وتفصيله أن للبلاد ثلاثة أحوال
الأولى بلدة بناها المسلمون فلا يكون فيها كنيسة وإذا دخلوا وقبلوا
الجزية منعوا من إحداث الكنائس قطعا وفي معناها بلدة ملك المسلمون عليهم
رقبتها قهرا فإنه ينقض كنائسهم لا محالة ولو أراد الإمام أن ينزل منهم
طائفة بجزية ويترك لهم كنيسة قديمة قطع المراوزة بالمنع وذكر العراقيون
وجها في جوازه أما الإحداث فلا  خلاف في المنع
الثانية بلدة فتحناها صلحا على أن تكون رقبة الأبنية للمسلمين وهم
يسكنونها بخراج يبذلونه سوى الجزية فإن استثنى في الصلح البيع والكنائس لم
تنقض وإن أطلق فوجهان أحدهما انها تنفض لأنها ملك المسلمين فلهم التصرف في
ملكهم والثاني لا وفاء بشرط التقرير فإنه يمنع عليهم القرار من غير متعبد
جامع
الثالثة أن تفتح على أن تكون الرقاب لهم ويضرب عليهم خراج فهذه بلدتهم
وليس عليهم نقض الكنائس ولو أحدثوا كنائس فالمذهب أنهم لا يمنعون وقيل يمنع
لأنها على الجملة تحت حكم الإسلام
ولا خلاف أنهم لا يمنعون من ضرب الناقوس وإظهار الخمور وإن كان المسلمون
يدخلون على الجملة لأنها كعقر دارهم ولا نتعرض لما يجري في دورهم

### | فرع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "blame" and its opposite "covenant of protection" — the dhimmah is that which renders one's blood and property inviolable through a binding pact.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological-juridical usage, al-dhimmah denotes the sacred obligation (ʿahd) that secures the protected status of non-Muslims under Islamic sovereignty, entailing reciprocal duties.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the pact itself; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the protected people (ahl al-dhimmah) as a collective.
- Root: ذ-ب-ب (dh-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repel, drive away, or defend against an aggressor — active protective intervention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, it signifies the obligation to shield dhimmīs from external enemies, a subset of the general duty of defense (jihād).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical repulsion of attackers; metaphorical — any act of safeguarding, including legal protection.
- Root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To recompense, pay what is due, or suffice — the jizyah is the tribute that fulfills the obligation of the covenant.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, it is the compensatory payment that secures the dhimmī's right to protection and residence, distinct from kharāj (land tax).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — financial payment; metaphorical — the entire system of reciprocal obligations between the Islamic state and protected communities.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if they reveal wine, we spill it") and exceptions ("except the old churches"), requiring precise parsing to distinguish general rulings from specific qualifications.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second consideration concerns the rulings of the covenant of protection (ʿaqd al-dhimmah). This covenant entails obligations incumbent upon us and upon them. As for what is incumbent upon us, it reverts to two matters: refraining from them (al-kaff) and repelling the disbelievers on their behalf (al-dhubb).

As for refraining (al-kaff), its meaning is that we do not molest their lives or their wealth, and we render them inviolable through liability (al-ḍamān). We do not spill their wines, nor do we destroy their pigs, as long as they conceal them. And we do not prevent them from frequenting their ancient churches. However, if they openly display their wines, we spill them. And whoever enters their abode and spills their wine has transgressed, yet there is no liability upon him — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him. And if one wrongfully seizes their wine, the cost of returning it is obligatory; yet there is a position that only vacating (al-takhlīyah) is obligatory, not the cost of return. And if one sells wine to a Muslim, the wine is spilled upon the Muslim, and the dhimmī has no claim to its price. The apparent position is that it is obligatory to return the respected wine (al-khamr al-muḥtaramah) to the Muslim if it was wrongfully seized.

As for repelling (al-dhubb) on their behalf, its meaning is the repulsion of the disbelievers from them as long as they are within our abode — and this is a defense of the abode itself. But if they enter the abode of war (dār al-ḥarb), there is no expectation of defense. And if they are isolated in a town not contiguous with the lands of Islam, then regarding the obligation of repelling the people of war from them, there are two positions: one is that it is not obligatory, since we have only undertaken the obligation of refraining (al-kaff); the second is that it is obligatory, since they have paid the jizyah so that we may treat them in the manner of the people of Islam. Upon this second position, if we stipulated that we would not defend them, it would not be incumbent upon us — yet among the scholars there are those who nullify this stipulation. And upon the first position, if we stipulated defense, it would be incumbent upon us — yet among them there are those who nullify that stipulation as well. Likewise, if they bring their disputes to us, whether it is obligatory for us to adjudicate between them — there is a divergence of opinion therein, and its upshot reverts to repelling the harm of some of them from others.

As for what is incumbent upon them, it is the fulfillment of the jizyah, submission to the rulings (al-aḥkām), refraining from lewd acts (al-fawāḥish), refraining from building churches, from vying with Muslims in lofty construction, from adorning themselves by abandoning the distinguishing mark (al-ghiyār), from riding horses, and from traversing the main thoroughfares. These are the summary of their obligations.

The first [detailed matter]: The ruling on churches. Its elaboration is that lands have three states:

The first state: A town built by Muslims — therein there can be no church. And if they [the dhimmīs] enter it and the jizyah is accepted from them, they are absolutely prevented from initiating new churches. In the same category is a town whose land was forcibly conquered by the Muslims — for their churches are demolished without fail. And if the Imām wished to settle a group of them therein with a jizyah and leave them their ancient church, the scholars of Marw cut off [the permissibility] by prohibition; yet the scholars of Iraq mentioned a position permitting it. As for initiating new churches, there is no divergence in prohibiting it.

The second state: A town we conquered by treaty (ṣulḥ) on the condition that the ownership of the buildings belongs to the Muslims, while they reside therein in exchange for a kharāj they pay apart from the jizyah. If the treaty stipulated an exception for the shops and churches, they are not demolished. But if the treaty was left unqualified, there are two positions: one is that they are demolished, because they are the property of the Muslims, and they have the right to dispose of their property; the second is that they are not demolished, for the fulfillment of the condition of settlement (al-taqrīr) — for it would prevent their stable residence without a congregational place of worship.

The third state: That the land be conquered on the condition that the ownership of the lands belongs to them, and a kharāj is imposed upon them — for this is their own town, and they are not obligated to demolish churches. And if they initiate new churches, the [authoritative] school (al-madhhab) is that they are not prevented; yet it was said they are prevented, because they are, in general, under the rule of Islam.

There is no divergence that they are not prevented from striking the bell (al-nāqūs) or from openly displaying their wines, even though Muslims may enter their abodes in general — for their homes are like their own courtyard (ka-ʿaqar dārihim), and we do not molest what transpires within their houses.

chapters.title_en: The Intermediate Compendium in Jurisprudence — Section 526: Regulations Concerning Dhimmīs (Protected Non-Muslim Subjects)
chapters.arabic_text:
حيث قضينا بإبقاء كنيسة قديمة والمنع من الإحداث فلا نمنعهم من العمارة
إذا استرمت والأصح أنا لا نكلفهم إخفاء العمارة وقيل يجب الإخفاء حتى لو
زال الجدار الخارج فلا وجه إلا بناء جدار داخل الكنيسة
نعم لو انهدمت الكنيسة ففي إعادتها وجهان من حيث إن هذا كالإحداث من وجه
وإن قلنا لهم الإعادة ففي جواز زيادة في الخطة وجهان أصحهما المنع لأن هذا
إحداث
وأما النواقيس فإنا نمنعهم في كنائسهم أن يظهر صوته فهو كإظهار الخمر
وقيل لا يمنع فإنه تابع للكنيسة
الواجب الثاني ترك مطاولة البنيان فلو بنى دارا أرفع من دار جاره منع ولو
كان مثله فوجهان ولو لم يكن بجنبه إلا حجرة ضعيفة منخفضة فعليه أن لا
يعلوها بنيانه ولو كان في طرف بلد حيث لا جار أو كانت لهم محلة فلا معنى
للمطاولة فلا حجر وقيل إنهم على الجملة يمنعون من رفع فيه تجمل
وهذا كله في البناء فلو اشترى دارا مرتفعة لم ينقض بناؤها وهذا المنع
مستحب أو حتم فيه وجهان
الواجب الثالث يمنعون من التجمل بركوب الخيل ولا يمنعون من الحمار النفيس
وليكن ركابهم من الخشب وقال الشيخ أبو محمد لا يمنع من الفرس الخسيس
كالقتبيات ويمنع من البغال الغر
الواجب الرابع لا  بد من الغيار ولون الصفرة باليهود أليق والكهبة
بالنصارى والسواد بالمجوس والمقصود أن يتميزوا حتى لا نسلم عليهم ويضطرون
إلى أضيق الطرق ويمنعون من سرارة الجادة إذا كانت مشغولة بالمسلمين وإن
كانت خالية فلا منع ويخرج الكافر من الحمام إذا لم يكن عليهم غيار لأنه
ربما ينجس الماء من حيث لا نعرف
والمرأة هل يلزمها الغيار في الحمام وخارجه فيه وجهان ثم أصل الغيار وترك
ركوب الخيل حتم أو مستحب فيه وجهان
الواجب الخامس الإنقياد للأحكام بأن يذعن للحد والضمان إذا تعلقت الخصومة
بمسلم أو زنا بمسلمة أو سرق مال مسلم أما ما لا يتعلق بمسلم ولم يعتقد
تحريمه فلا يحد على الصحيح فيه كالشرب وما اعتقد تحريمه وترافعوا إلينا وجب
عليهم الإنقياد فإن قيل فلو خالفوا في شيء من هذه الجملة فهل ينتقض عهدهم
قلنا هذه الأمور على ثلاث مراتب
الأولى وهي أخفها إظهار الخمر وضرب الناقوس وترك الغيار وإظهار معتقدهم
في المسيح عليه السلام وفي الله تعالى بانه ثالث ثلاثة وما يضاهيه مما لا
ضرر على المسلمين فيه فلا ينتقض به العهد بل نعزرهم ولو شرط الإمام انتقاض
العهد بذلك قال الأصحاب يحمل على التخويف شرطه ولا ينتقض به
الرتبة الثالثة وهي أغلظها القتال ومنع الجزية والأحكام والمشهور أن
العهد
ينتقض بهذه الثلاث وهو ظاهر في القتال
أما منع الجزية فلا يبعد أن يجعل كمنع الديون فتستوفى قهرا ولا يبعد من
حيث إنه ركن الأمان فكأن منعه إسقاط أمانه بخلاف سائر الديون ويحتمل أن
يكون مراد الأصحاب منه أن يكون المنع بالتغلب فيؤدي إلى القتال
وأما منع الحكم فلا ينبغي أن ينقض إن كان بالهرب فإن كان بتمرد حملناه
عليه وإن أدى إلى القتال انتقض عهده وعلى الجملة لا يظهر انتقاض العهد إلا
بالقتال
الرتبة الثالثة ما هو محظور وفيه على المسلمين ضرر كالزنا بالمسلمة
والتطلع على عورات المسلمين أو افتتان المسلم عن دينه ففي هذه الثلاثة
ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه ينقض العهد كالقتال والثاني لا ينقض بل  يعاقبون عليها
كإظهار الخمر
والثالث أنه إذا جرى شرط الإنتقاض انتقض وإلا فلا
وأما قطع الطريق والقتل الموجب للقصاص فمنهم من قال هو من هذا القسم
ومنهم من قطع بإلحاقه بالقتال وكذلك في تعرضهم لرسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم بالسوء طريقان ومنهم من قال كالقتال ومنهم من قال على الأوجه الثلاثة
أما إذا كان الطعن على وفق اعتقادهم كقولهم إنه لي رسول الله والقرآن ليس
بمنزل فهذا كقولهم إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وإنما الخلاف في السب والطعن في
النسب وما لا يوافق عقيدتهم فإن قيل وما حكم انتقاض العهد قلنا أما في
القتال فحكمه الإغتيال وأما في الرتبة الثالثة فقولان أحدهما الإغتيال وصار
العهد كالمعدوم
والثاني أنا نلحقهم بالمأمن ولا اغتيال
ولو نبذ الذمي عهده إلينا من غير جناية فالصحيح أنه يلحق بالمأمن وقيل
يخرج على القولين إذا كان يقدر على الخروج من غير
مجاهرة بنبذ العهد
فإن قيل فالمسلم إن طول لسانه في الرسول فما حكمه قلنا إن كذب عليه عذر
وإن كذبه فهو مرتد فيقتل إلا أن يتوب وكذلك كل تعرض فيه استهزاء فهو ردة
ولو نسبه إلى الزنا فهذا القذف كفر بالإتفاق فلو تاب ففيه ثلاثة أوجه
أحدهما وهو اختيار الفارسي أنه يقتل إذ حد قذف الرسول قتل فلا يسقط الحد
بالتوبة وفي الخبر من سب نبيا فاقتلوه ومن سب أصحابه فاجلدوه والثاني وهو
اختيار القفال والأستاذ أبي إسحاق أنه لا شيء عليه لأن القتل صار مغمورا في
الكفر فيسقط أثره بالإسلام والثالث وهو الذي ذكره الصيدلاني رحمه الله أنه
يسقط القتل وتبقى ثمانون جلدة للحد وهذا يلزمه أن يجلد قبل القتل إذا لم
يتب كالمرتد إذا قذف والإلتفات إلى هذا القياس الجروي في مثل هذا المقام
بعيد
ثم إن قلنا ثبت حد القذف فلو عفا واحد من بني أعمامه ينبغي أن يسقط أو
نقول هم لا ينحصرون فهو كقذف ميت لا وارث له وكذلك في قتل مثله قولان
أحدهما أنه لا قصاص إذ في المسلمين  صبيان ولأنه إن وجب على الإمام
الإستيفاء ضاهى الحد وبطل خاصية القصاص وإن جاز له العفو فهو بعيد والثاني
أنه يجب إذ يؤدي إلى إبطال عصمة من لا وارث له فينقدح أيضا القولان في قذف
من لا وارث له

- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Building, cultivating, populating; the act of constructing and maintaining a dwelling or place of worship
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Maintenance and preservation of what sustains communal life; in legal context, the distinction between original construction (inshāʾ) and repair (tarmīm)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical construction; metaphorical extension to "revival" of land or structures
- Root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, defect; covenant of protection (dhimmah) as a binding obligation
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The contractual bond of security (amān) between Muslim polity and non-Muslim subjects
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal blameworthiness; metaphorical transfer to the legal covenant that removes blame
- Root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Change, alteration; distinguishing mark (ghiyār) imposed on dhimmīs
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The visible differentiation (tamyīz) required to maintain communal boundaries in Islamic law
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal transformation; legal-technical sense of mandated distinctive clothing
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text employs complex conditional structures (law, in, idhā) requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve legal precision in multi-clause rulings.
chapters.translation:
I say: Since we have ruled upon the preservation of an ancient church and the prohibition of its new construction, we do not prevent them from repairing it when it falls into disrepair. The soundest position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that we do not oblige them to conceal the repair; yet it was said that concealment is obligatory, such that if the outer wall collapses, there is no recourse except building an inner wall within the church.

Yes, if the church were entirely demolished, then concerning its rebuilding there are two positions (wajhān), on the grounds that this is akin to new construction in one respect. And if we say to them that rebuilding is permitted, then concerning the permissibility of adding to the original plot there are two positions, the sounder of which is prohibition, because this constitutes new construction.

As for the bells (nawāqīs), we prevent them in their churches from making their sound audible, for this is like the public display of wine. And it was said that they are not prevented, for the bell is subsidiary to the church.

The second obligation: the abandonment of raising buildings higher (muṭāwalah). Thus, if one builds a house higher than his neighbor's house, he is prevented. If it were equal to it, there are two positions. And if adjacent to him there is only a weak, lowly hovel, then he must not raise his building above it. If he were at the edge of a town where there is no neighbor, or if they had their own quarter, then there is no meaning to "raising higher," so no restriction applies. And it was said that they are, in general, prevented from raising anything that involves ostentation.

All of this concerns construction. Thus, if one purchased an already elevated house, its structure is not demolished. And whether this prohibition is recommended (mustaḥabb) or mandatory (ḥatm) — therein are two positions.

The third obligation: they are prevented from beautifying themselves by riding horses, but they are not prevented from riding a valuable donkey. Their saddles should be of wood. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: they are not prevented from riding a lowly horse, such as the Qaṭabiyyāt (pack-horses), but they are prevented from riding fine mules.

The fourth obligation: the distinguishing mark (ghiyār) is indispensable. The color yellow is most fitting for the Jews, the dun-gray (kahbah) for the Christians, and black for the Magians. The purpose is that they be distinguished, so that we do not greet them with salām, and they are compelled to walk on the narrowest paths. They are prevented from the middle of the road when it is occupied by Muslims; but if it is empty, there is no prevention. And the unbeliever is expelled from the bathhouse if they bear no distinguishing mark, because he might defile the water in a manner we do not perceive.

As for the woman — is the distinguishing mark incumbent upon her in the bathhouse and outside it? Therein are two positions. Then, whether the principle of the distinguishing mark and the abandonment of horse-riding is mandatory or recommended — therein are two positions.

The fifth obligation: submission to the legal judgments (al-inqiyād li-l-aḥkām), namely that they acquiesce to the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) and to civil liability (ḍamān) when a dispute is connected to a Muslim, or when they commit fornication with a Muslim woman, or steal the property of a Muslim. As for what is not connected to a Muslim and which they do not believe to be prohibited, they are not subjected to the prescribed punishment according to the sound position (al-ṣaḥīḥ) — such as drinking wine. But what they believe to be prohibited, and they bring their dispute to us, then submission is incumbent upon them.

If it is said: "If they violate any of these matters, is their covenant (ʿahd) annulled?" — I say: These matters fall into three ranks:

The first rank, which is the lightest: the public display of wine, striking the bell, abandoning the distinguishing mark, and publicly proclaiming their belief concerning the Messiah (peace be upon him) and concerning God Most High — that He is the third of three — and what resembles this, wherein there is no harm to the Muslims. The covenant is not annulled by this; rather, we administer discretionary punishment (taʿzīr). Even if the Imām stipulated the annulment of the covenant on account of this, the Companions (al-aṣḥāb) said: this stipulation is interpreted as intimidation (takhwīf), and the covenant is not annulled thereby.

The third rank, which is the gravest: fighting (qitāl), refusing the jizyah (poll tax), and refusing the legal judgments. The well-known position (al-mashhūr) is that the covenant is annulled by these three. This is evident concerning fighting.

As for refusing the jizyah — it is not far-fetched to treat it like the refusal of debts, so it is exacted by force. Nor is it far-fetched, from the standpoint that it is the pillar of security (amān), that its refusal is tantamount to the abrogation of one's security — unlike other debts. And it is possible that the intent of the Companions (al-aṣḥāb) herein is that the refusal occurs through overpowering, which leads to fighting.

As for refusing the legal judgment — it should not annul the covenant if it is by flight. But if it is by rebellion (tamarrud), we hold him to it; and if it leads to fighting, his covenant is annulled. In general, the annulment of the covenant does not become manifest except through fighting.

The third rank: that which is prohibited and in which there is harm to the Muslims — such as fornication with a Muslim woman, spying upon the private matters (ʿawrāt) of Muslims, or causing a Muslim to be seduced away from his religion. Concerning these three, there are three positions: One — that the covenant is annulled, as with fighting. The second — that it is not annulled; rather, they are punished for them, as with the public display of wine. The third — that if the stipulation of annulment was made, it is annulled; otherwise, not.

As for highway robbery and killing that necessitates retaliation (qiṣāṣ) — some said this belongs to this category, and some definitively attached it to fighting. Likewise, concerning their harming the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) with evil, there are two paths: some said it is like fighting, and some said it follows the three positions.

As for when the attack conforms to their belief — such as their saying, "He is not the Messenger of God, and the Qurʾān is not revealed" — this is like their saying that God is the third of three. The disagreement concerns only insult (sabb) and attack upon lineage, and what does not conform to their belief.

If it is said: "What is the ruling on the annulment of the covenant?" — I say: As for fighting, its ruling is covert killing (ightiyāl). As for the third rank, there are two sayings: One — covert killing, and the covenant becomes as if non-existent. The second — we grant them the status of those in a place of safety (maʾman), and there is no covert killing.

And if a dhimmī casts off his covenant toward us without any offense — the sound position is that he is granted the status of one in a place of safety. And it was said that it follows the two sayings, when he is able to depart without openly proclaiming the casting off of the covenant.

If it is said: "As for the Muslim who extends his tongue against the Messenger — what is his ruling?" — I say: If he attributes falsehood to him, he is excused; but if he denies him (takdhīb), he is an apostate (murtadd) and is killed unless he repents. Likewise, every attack involving mockery is apostasy. And if he attributed fornication to him — this is slander (qadhf) constituting unbelief (kufr) by consensus. If he then repents, there are three positions:

One — which is the choice of al-Fārisī — that he is killed, for the prescribed punishment for slandering the Messenger is death, and the punishment is not dropped by repentance. And in the report: "Whoever curses a prophet, kill him; and whoever curses his Companions, flog him."

The second — which is the choice of al-Qaffāl and the Master Abū Isḥāq — that nothing is upon him, because the death penalty has become submerged within unbelief, so its effect is dropped by Islam.

The third — which is what al-Ṣaydalānī (may God have mercy on him) mentioned — that the death penalty is dropped, and eighty lashes remain as the prescribed punishment. This entails that he be flogged before the killing if he does not repent, like the apostate who commits slander. And turning to this juristic analogy (qiyās jarawī) in such a context is far-fetched.

Then, if we say that the prescribed punishment for slander is established — if one of his paternal cousins (banī aʿmāmihi) pardons him, should it be dropped? Or do we say they are not limited in number, so it is like slandering a dead person who has no heir? Likewise, concerning killing someone like him, there are two sayings:

One — that there is no retaliation (qiṣāṣ), because among Muslims there are minors, and because if exacting it were incumbent upon the Imām, it would resemble the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) and the specific character of retaliation would be nullified; and if pardon were permissible for him, that is far-fetched.

The second — that it is obligatory, since otherwise it would lead to the nullification of the inviolability (ʿiṣmah) of one who has no heir. Thus the two sayings also arise concerning slandering one who has no heir.

### | العقد الثاني مع الكفار المهادنة

والنظر في شروطه وأحكامه أما الشروط فأربعة
الأول أن هذا العقد لا يتولاه إلا الإمام لأنه يرجع حاصله إلى صلح جمع من
الكفار على ترك قتالهم والكف عنهم من غير مال نعم لآحاد الولاة عقد ذلك مع
أهل القرى والأطراف المتعلقة بهم فأما مهادنة إقليم كالهند والروم فليس إلا
للإمام
الشرط الثاني أن يكون للمسلمين إلى ذلك حاجة فإن لم تكن حاجة ولا مضرة
وطلبوا ذلك لم يجب على الإمام الإجابة على الصحيح بل يتبع الأصلح وفيه وجه
مخرج أنه تجب الإجابة وفي الجزية وجه مخرج من المهادنة أنه لا تجب الإجابة
والوجهان ضعيفان والصحيح الفرق فإن عقد الذمة كف بمال وهذه مسامحة
الشرط الثالث أن يخلو العقد عن شرط يأباه المسلم كما لو شرط أن يترك في
أيديهم مال مسلم أو شرط أن يرد عليهم أسيرا مسلما أفلت منهم أو شرط لهم على
المسلمين مالا فكل ذلك فاسد مفسد نعم لو كان على المسلمين خوف جاز التزام
مال لدفع الشر كما يجوز فداء الأسير المسلم إذا عجزنا عن انتزاعه مجانا
الشرط الرابع المدة وهو يتقدر بأربعة أشهر إن لم يكن بالمسلمين ضعف وهو
مدة السياحة قال الله تعالى {فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر}
ولا يجوزو أن تبلغ سنة وهذه المدة للجزية لأن الكف سنة إنما جاز بعوض أما
فيما دون السنة وفوق أربعة أشهر فقولان أحدهما الجواز للقصور عن مدة الجزية
وهذا يستمد من قولنا إن طلب قسط من الجزية في بعض السنة لا يجوز والثاني
المنع للزيادة على مدة التسييح أما إذا كان بالمسلمين ضعف وخوف جازت
المهادنة عشر سنين هادن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل مكة عشر سنين ولا
مزيد عليه  وفيه وجه أنه تجوز الزيادة بالمصلحة

### | فرع

لو أطلق الإمام المهادنة ولم يذكر المدة فالصحيح أنها فاسدة وقال
الفوراني في حال القوة وجهان أحدهما أنه ينزل على الأقل والثاني على الأكثر
وهو ما يقارب السنة
وإن كان في حالة الضعف فينزل على عشر سنين إذ لا يتقدر أقله وسببه أن
مقتضى المطلق التأبيد فنحذف ما يزيد على المدة الشرعية
ولو صرح بالزيادة على المدة فالزيادة مردودة وفي صحتها في المدة قولا
تفريق الصفقة وأصحهما الصحة إذ ليس فيها عوض تحدد جهالته
ثم حكم الفاسد أن ننذرهم ولا نغتالهم وحكم الصحيح وجوب الكف عنهم إلى
انقضاء المدة أو إلى جناية تصدر منهم تناقض العهد فنغتالهم إن علموا أنها
جناية وإن لم يعلموا ففي اغتيالهم من غير إنذار وجهان
ولو بنينا تطويل المدة على خوف لم ترتفع بزوال الخوف بل لا بد من الوفاء
ولو استشعر الإمام جناية فله أن ينبذ إليهم عهدهم بالتهمة وذلك لا يجوز
في الجزية نعم لا يبتدىء عقد الجزية مع التهمة

### | النظر الثاني في أحكام العقد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: هـ-د-ن (h-d-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "calmness, stillness, cessation of agitation" — a truce is a mutual quieting of hostilities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes a temporary cessation of fighting (kuff) in exchange for a stipulated term, distinct from permanent dhimmah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical tranquility; metaphorical (majāz) = contractual suspension of warfare.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning "safety, peace, surrender" — from which "musālamah" (peacemaking) derives.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic context, it contrasts with ḥarb (war) and implies a binding pact of non-aggression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = being free from harm; metaphorical = the legal covenant of security.
- Root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To recompense, to pay what is due" — the jizyah is a compensatory payment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fiqh, it is the poll-tax exacted from dhimmīs as a quid pro quo for protection and exemption from military service.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = requital; metaphorical = the contractual payment that legitimizes the kaff (cessation of fighting).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīr (Ellipsis Restoration) — In "فليس إلا للإمام" (it is only for the Imam), the predicate is ellipted and restored as "مشروع" or "جائز" (permissible), governing the exclusivity clause.
chapters.translation:
### | The Second Contract with Unbelievers: The Truce

The examination concerns its conditions and its rulings. As for the conditions, they are four.

**The first** is that this contract is undertaken only by the Imam, because its ultimate outcome reverts to a peace settlement with a group of unbelievers, upon abandoning fighting them and refraining from them, without [the payment of] wealth. Yes, individual provincial governors may contract this with the inhabitants of villages and outlying districts that pertain to them. As for the truce of a whole clime, such as India and Rome, that is only for the Imam.

**The second condition** is that the Muslims have a need for this. For if there is no need and no harm [threatening them], and they request it, it is not obligatory upon the Imam to respond, according to the correct [opinion]. Rather, he follows what is most beneficial (al-aṣlaḥ). And there is a face, derived [by analogy], that responding is obligatory. And in the matter of the jizyah, there is a face derived from the truce that responding is not obligatory. Both faces are weak, and the correct [opinion] is the distinction: for the contract of dhimmah is a cessation [of fighting] in exchange for wealth, whereas this [truce] is an act of indulgence (musāmaḥah).

**The third condition** is that the contract be free of any stipulation that Islamic law rejects — such as stipulating that a Muslim's wealth be left in their hands, or stipulating that a Muslim captive who had escaped from them be returned to them, or stipulating for them wealth [to be paid] by the Muslims. All of that is corrupt and vitiating [of the contract]. Yes, if the Muslims are under fear, it is permissible to undertake [the payment of] wealth to repel evil, just as it is permissible to ransom a Muslim captive when we are unable to extract him without payment.

**The fourth condition** is the duration. It is limited to four months if the Muslims are not in a state of weakness — and this is the period of "safe-conduct" (siyāḥah). God Most High said: {«فَسِيحُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ»} ("So travel freely in the land for four months"). And it is not permissible for it to reach a year. This duration [of one year] belongs to the jizyah, because the cessation of fighting is only permitted in exchange for compensation. As for what is less than a year and more than four months, there are two opinions: one is permissibility, because it falls short of the jizyah duration — and this is derived from our statement that demanding a portion of the jizyah for part of the year is not permissible. The second is prohibition, because it exceeds the duration of the "safe-conduct" (tasyīḥ). However, if the Muslims are in a state of weakness and fear, the truce is permissible for ten years. The Messenger of God ﷺ made a truce with the people of Mecca for ten years, and there is no exceeding that. And there is a face that exceeding [ten years] is permissible by [consideration of] public interest (maṣlaḥah).

### | Branch

If the Imam issues an absolute truce and does not mention a duration, the correct [opinion] is that it is corrupt (fāsidah). Al-Fūrānī said that in a state of strength there are two faces: one is that it is construed as the minimum [four months], and the second as the maximum — which is what approaches a year. And if it is in a state of weakness, it is construed as ten years, since its minimum is not fixed. The reason for this is that the purport of the absolute [expression] is perpetuity, so we delete what exceeds the legal duration.

And if he explicitly stipulates an excess over the duration, the excess is rejected. Regarding its validity within the [legal] duration, there are the two opinions of "division of the transaction" (tafrīq al-ṣafqah); the more correct of the two is validity, because there is no compensation (ʿiwaḍ) in it whose ignorance would render it indeterminate.

Then, the ruling of the corrupt [truce] is that we warn them [of impending attack] and do not take them by surprise (lā naghtāluhum). And the ruling of the valid [truce] is the obligation of refraining from them until the expiry of the duration, or until an aggression (jināyah) issues from them that contravenes the covenant — whereupon we may take them by surprise if they know that it is an aggression. But if they do not know, then there are two faces concerning taking them by surprise without warning.

And if we had based the prolongation of the duration upon fear, it is not lifted by the removal of the fear; rather, fulfillment [of the covenant] is obligatory. And if the Imam senses an impending aggression, he may cast their covenant back at them (yanbidhu ilayhim ʿahdahum) on grounds of suspicion (tuhmah) — and this is not permissible in the case of the jizyah. Yes, one does not initiate the contract of jizyah when suspicion exists.

### | The Second Consideration: The Rulings of the Contract
