chapters.translation:
I say: One of the two [positions] is that regarding the dome, the vaulted passage, the bathhouse, and whatever does not admit of physical partition, the correct [ruling] is temporal division (muhāyāʾah) among them by mutual consent. Whoever withdraws before completing his turn has that right. But if he completes his turn and then withdraws, there are two [scholarly] views. The more analogically sound of the two is that he may withdraw but must compensate [the partners] for what he exclusively enjoyed. The second [view] is that he may not, because this is a transaction upon which the predecessors proceeded, so it should not be disturbed. Ibn Surayj said: He is compelled to accept temporal division, because one of the partners who is independent due to his wealth may leave [the property] idle to the detriment of the partners. The correct [view] is that if they dispute and become obstinate, they are left until they reach a settlement.

Second: If a group comes forward and requests from the judge the partition of property among them without establishing proof that it is their property, the correct [view] is that the judge partitions it and writes in the legal document: "I have partitioned it based on their statement." Likewise, if one of them comes alone and makes the request. There is another view that he should not respond, because perhaps [the claimant] is disposing of another's property without evidence. But this is far-fetched, because possession (al-yad) is theirs in the present moment.

= THE BOOK OF TESTIMONIES =

It contains six chapters.

Chapter One: On what confers eligibility for testimony and its acceptance from among the qualities.

These are six: three of them do not require lengthy examination — namely, legal capacity (taklīf), freedom, and Islam. Thus, the testimony of a minor is not accepted, nor that of an insane person, nor is the testimony of an unbeliever accepted — neither against an unbeliever nor against a Muslim. Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) said: It is accepted against an unbeliever. Nor is the testimony of a slave accepted at all; Dāwūd said: It is accepted. And three [qualities] require lengthy examination — namely, probity (ʿadālah), preservation of honor (murūʾah), and freedom from accusation (ittihām).

The First Quality: Probity (ʿadālah)

Al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) said: There is no one among mankind that we know — except a few — who purifies his obedience entirely so as not to mix it with disobedience. By this he indicated that immunity from sins is not a condition, for that would seal off the door of testimony entirely. But whoever commits a major sin or persists upon a minor sin, his testimony is not accepted, because that indicates negligence regarding the matter of religion, and such a person is deserving that the evil consequence of lying not be feared. As for one who occasionally commits a minor sin due to a lapse in the vigilance of piety, or a slip that occurs to the soul in departing from the rein of scrupulousness (al-waraʿ), while he does not cease to feel remorse and a sense of fear — such a person's testimony is not rejected thereby. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «لَا يَخْلُو الْمُؤْمِنُ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ يُصِيبُهُ الْفَيْنَةَ بَعْدَ الْفَيْنَةِ» — "The believer is not free from sin that befalls him from time to time," meaning from one time to another. Rather, wickedness (fisq) is persistence upon disobedience, even if it be minor.

The distinction between minor and major sins is lengthy, and we have exhausted it in the Book of Repentance from the books of Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn. Now I shall indicate some of the customary minor sins, which are six:

The First: Playing chess. It is not forbidden (ḥarām) but is disliked (makrūh). If we say it is permissible (mubāḥ), we mean that there is no sin in it, not that there is no dislike in it. Thus testimony is not rejected by it, unless gambling is mixed with it — namely, taking the money of the one defeated and stipulating it — or a false oath. It has been narrated that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr (may God be pleased with him) used to play it while turning his back to it and not looking at it. And the saying of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him): "What are these images to which you are devoted?" — perhaps it was in the context of inquiry, as the form of those shapes was unclear to him and what they were. As for persistence upon it, that detracts from honor (murūʾah) and neglects important matters, and rejection of testimony may arise from this — and this will come later.

The Second: Playing dice (nard) is forbidden (ḥarām), because it is narrated that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Cursed is the one who plays with nardshīr," and he said: "The player of dice is like the worshipper of an idol." It is transmitted from Ibn Khayrān and Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī that it is like chess — and this is the analogical [view] — but the report (khabar) prevents it. Then, even if we say it is forbidden, persistence upon it rejects testimony, unlike a single occurrence. And it was said: A single occurrence is wickedness (fisq) that rejects testimony.

As for playing with pigeons, it is not forbidden. The Iraqis differed regarding its dislike and the rejection of testimony by it; rejection only arises from the angle of honor (murūʾah) in the case of one whose honor it detracts from.

The Third: Al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) said: The Ḥanafī who drinks nabīdh (date wine) — I would administer the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) to him and accept his testimony. As for the punishment, it is for deterrence so that he does not return to it, since it leads to corruption. As for our acceptance of his testimony, it is because his undertaking to drink it did not indicate negligence on his part, since he believed it permissible. Al-Muzanī deemed this distinction far-fetched. Among the companions [of al-Shāfiʿī], some said: He is punished but his testimony is not accepted. And among them, some said: He is not punished and his testimony is accepted. Thus we arrive at three positions. If we say the Ḥanafī is not punished, then regarding the Shāfiʿī there are two views due to the ambiguity of the disagreement concerning permissibility.

The Fourth: Musical instruments and strings (maʿāzif wa-awtār) are forbidden, because they incite desire toward drinking, and they are the emblem of drinking; thus resembling them is forbidden. As for the duff (tambourine), if it has no jingles, it is lawful — it was struck in the house of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). If it has jingles, there are two views. Regarding the reed flute (al-yirāʿ), there are two views, and the more correct is that it is not forbidden. The Iraqi mizmār (pipe) is forbidden, because it is the custom of drinkers. All drums are permissible except the kūbah — namely, the drum of effeminate men, which is a long drum with wide ends and a narrow middle. The reason for its prohibition is resembling them. Likewise, striking with two clappers (ṣafāqatayn) is forbidden, because it is their custom.

I have already mentioned the bases of these prohibitions in the Book of Ecstasy and Audition (Kitāb al-Wajd wa-l-Samāʿ), and I detailed what is lawful and what is forbidden. Then Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: Hearing strings once does not reject testimony; rejection only occurs through persistence. The Iraqis said: It is a major sin that necessitates rejection of testimony by a single occurrence. There is no doubt that this varies by region — where its matter is grave, a single occurrence indicates the rupture of the witness's honor.

The Fifth: Composing poetry, reciting it, and listening to it — with melodies or without — is not forbidden, unless the poetry contains satire (hijāʾ), description of a specific woman, or obscenity — whatever is forbidden in prose is forbidden in verse. For poetry is speech: its good is good and its bad is bad. Poems were recited before the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and he did not disapprove of them. If one exaggerates in praise until reaching the limit of falsehood, it is said to be forbidden. The correct [view] is that this is not falsehood, because it is not intended for belief and affirmation, but rather it is a display of artistry in speech.

Listening to singing (ghināʾ) is permissible, because whatever is permissible without melody is permissible with melody — unless it is taken as a habit, for then it may detract from honor. Dancing is also permissible, but when it becomes habitual, or singing becomes a means of livelihood, it detracts from honor.

Chanting the Qurʾān with melody is permissible — rather, commendable — unless it reaches the elongation that disrupts the composition. Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may God be pleased with him) was excellent in melodious recitation of the Qurʾān, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «إِنَّ هَذَا قَدْ أُوتِيَ مِزْمَارًا مِنْ مَزَامِيرِ آلِ دَاوُدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ» — "Indeed, this one has been given a pipe from the pipes of the family of David (peace be upon him)."

The Sixth: Wearing silk and sitting upon it is forbidden, and testimony is rejected by persistence upon it, not by a single occurrence. Likewise, wearing a gold ring. Some companions erred and said: If the witnesses to a marriage contract were upon silk, the marriage would not be contracted by their testimony.

The Second Quality: Honor (murūʾah)

Whoever commits from among permissible things what is unbefitting for his peers — such as eating in the road, urinating in the street, or a jurist wearing the qabāʾ (short cloak) and pointed cap in our lands, and other such things that diminish one — this indicates either a defect in his intellect or a dissolution in his soul that voids confidence in his truthfulness, thus his testimony is defective. It is not hidden that this varies by persons and circumstances. Thus, a person of rank who carries goods to his home for his son has no honor, though if his action can be interpreted as piety and emulation of the early generations, it does not detract from him.

Attached to this category is devotion to permissible things that prevent important matters — such as persistence in chess, playing with pigeons, dancing, and singing — for that also indicates dissolution. They also differed regarding base professions. Among them are those who do not accept the testimony of the tanner, the sweeper, the cupper, the masseur, and one who handles filth, because his choice of this profession indicates his baseness. Among them are those who say: It is accepted if it is the craft of his forefathers and befitting his peers. Regarding the weaver, there are two paths: Al-Qaffāl said there is no difference between him and the tailor; some said that custom has degraded them, so his choice of it is like choosing sweeping and cupping.

The Third Quality: Freedom from Accusation (ittihām)

There is no disagreement that the testimony of a just person is not accepted in every context. I say: The causes of accusation are [several]:

The First: That the testimony entails drawing benefit (jarr) or repelling harm (dafʿ).

As for drawing benefit: It is that one testifies against the one who wounded his testator — such testimony is rejected, because the compensation for the wound accrues to him through inheritance, and the wound is the cause of death leading to inheritance. There is no disagreement that if one testifies during a deathbed illness in favor of the testator regarding property, it is permissible, and we do not give place to accusation there. The testimony of wounding is only rejected because its validation (tazkiyah) redounds to him.

As for repelling harm: It is that two members of the ʿāqilah (kinsmen liable for blood-money) testify to the wickedness of the witnesses of accidental homicide — it is as if they testify for themselves.

chapters.title_en: Section 571 — On Testimony Involving Partiality and Kinship
chapters.arabic_text: ### | ### | فرع ان الأول لو شهد أحد الابنين على أخيه بألف درهم دين على المورث وقلنا لا يجب عند الإنفراد بالإقرار إلا حصة المقر قبلت هذه الشهادة إذ لا دفع فيها وإن قلنا إنه يلزمه تسليم جميع الألف من حصته لو أنكر الآخر فلا تقبل شهادته لأنه دافع وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله إن أقر ثم شهد لم تقبل كما لو قذف ثم شهد ولو أنشأ الشهادة ابتداء قبل كما لو شهد على الزنا الثاني لو شهد شاهدان لرجلين بالوصية لهما في تركة فشهدا للشاهدين أيضا بوصية قال صاحب التقريب لا تقبل للتهمة وهذا فاسد لأن كل شهادة منفصلة عن الأخرى ليس فيها جر وقد قطع الأصحاب بأن رفقاء القافلة إذا شهد بعضهم لبعض في قطع الطريق قبل إذا لم يتعرض في شهادته لنصيب نفسه السبب الثاني البعضية الموجبة للنفقة تمنع قبول الشهادة فلا تقبل الشهادة للولد والوالد وسائر الفروع والأصول لأنه ليس له من ماله إلا قدر حاجته ومال أصوله وفروعه معرض لحاجته فكأنه شهد لنفسه وفي شهادة الزوجين ثلاثة أقوال كما ذكرناه في القطع بالسرقة ولا خلاف أن شهادة الزوج على إنسان بأنه زنى بزوجته لا تقبل وكذلك إن شهد على زوجته بالزنا مع ثلاثة من العدول لأنها أوغرت صدره فنشأ منه عداوة ولأنه يشهد بالخيانة على محل حقه وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تقبل وقال مالك رحمه الله تقبل شهادة الولد لوالده ولا تقبل شهادة الوالد لولده وللشافعي رضي الله عنه قول قديم أنه تقبل الشهادة للولد وللوالد أما الشهادة عليهم فمقبولة لأنها أبعد عن التهمة وفيه وجه أن شهادة الإبن لا تقبل على الأب بالعقوبات إذ لا يكون الإبن سبب عقوبة الأب وهذا بعيد لأنه مظهر لا موجبا وفي حبس الأب بدين ولده ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه لا يحبس لأنه عقوبة والثاني أنه يحبس لأنه ليس مقصودا وعليه أن يؤدي الحق ليتخلص وقال صاحب التلخيص يحبس في نفقته ولا يحبس في سائر ديونه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be present, to witness, to testify; presence of the mind and body in attesting a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) as a legal conveyance of certainty regarding another's right, requiring probity (ʿadālah) and absence of imputation (tuhmah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: juridical attestation bearing legal effect.
- Root: د-ف-ع (d-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repel, push back, ward off; defense against a claim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Repulsion of a legal obligation; a witness who stands to repel liability from himself is tainted.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical pushing; metaphorical: legal avoidance of detriment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with implied apodosis (sharṭ muqaddar) — the ruling hinges on the dichotomy of the two positions (ʿalā al-qawlayn), requiring precise disambiguation of the protasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the first branch — if one of two brothers testifies on behalf of his brother that he has a claim of one thousand dirhams as a debt against the deceased (the testator), and we hold the position that upon solitary acknowledgment (al-iqrār) one is not obligated except for his own share — then this testimony is accepted, for there is no repulsion (dafʿ) in it. But if we hold that he is obligated to surrender the entire thousand from his own share should the other brother deny it, then his testimony is not accepted, because he is a repeller (dāfiʿ). Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he acknowledged first and then testified, it is not accepted — just as one who commits slander (qadhf) and then testifies [is rejected]. But if he initiates the testimony ab initio, it is accepted — just as testimony regarding fornication (zinā) [is accepted from one who did not previously accuse].

As for the second branch — if two witnesses testify on behalf of two men regarding a bequest (waṣiyyah) to them in an estate, and then those two also testify on behalf of the two witnesses regarding a bequest, the author of al-Taqrīb said: It is not accepted due to imputation (tuhmah). But this is corrupt, because each testimony is separate from the other, containing no self-benefit (jarr). The verified scholars (al-aṣḥāb) have decisively ruled that if fellow travelers of a caravan testify for one another regarding highway robbery (qaṭʿ al-ṭarīq), it is accepted — provided that in his testimony he does not touch upon his own share.

The second cause: Partiality (al-baʿḍiyyah) that entails maintenance (nafaqah) prevents the acceptance of testimony. Thus testimony is not accepted on behalf of one's child, one's parent, or the rest of one's descendants and ascendants — because he possesses of his wealth only the measure of his need, and the wealth of his ascendants and descendants is exposed to his need, so it is as though he testified for himself. Regarding the testimony of spouses, there are three positions (aqwāl), as we mentioned in the chapter on amputation for theft.

There is no disagreement that a husband's testimony against a man that he committed fornication with the husband's wife is not accepted. Likewise, if he testifies against his own wife for fornication along with three upright witnesses (ʿudūl), it is not accepted — because she has inflamed his breast, giving rise to enmity from that, and because he testifies to treachery against the locus of his right. Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It is accepted. Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The testimony of a child on behalf of his parent is accepted, but the testimony of a parent on behalf of his child is not accepted. And for al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) there is an old position (qawl qadīm) that testimony is accepted both on behalf of the child and on behalf of the parent.

As for testimony against them, it is accepted, because it is more remote from imputation. And there is a face (wajh) that a son's testimony against his father is not accepted in penal matters (ʿuqūbāt), since a son should not be the cause of his father's punishment. But this is far-fetched, because he is merely a manifestor (muẓhir), not an obligator (mūjib).

Regarding the imprisonment of a father for his son's debt, there are three faces (awjuh):
One: He is not imprisoned, because it is a punishment.
Two: He is imprisoned, because it is not intended [as punishment], and he is obligated to discharge the debt to free himself.
The author of al-Talkhīṣ said: He is imprisoned for his maintenance (nafaqah) but is not imprisoned for his other debts.

chapters.title_en: Section 572 — Grounds for Rejection of Testimony (Sharḥ al-Wasīṭ fī al-Madhhab)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

إذا شهد بحق مشترك بين ولده وأجنبي ورد في حق ولده ففي الرد في حق
الأجنبي وجهان لأجل تبعيض الشهادة في نفسها
السبب الثالث العداوة فلا تقبل شهادة العدو على العدو خلافا لأبي حنيفة
رحمه الله وسلم أن شهادة المخاصم في الحال لا تقبل
أما شهادة المخاصم بعد انقطاع  الخصومة فمقبولة بالإتفاق إذ يؤدي ذلك إلى
أن من
يستشعر من غيره إقامة شهادة عليه ينشيء معه خصومة
ورد شهادة العدو مشكل لأنه إن أخرجته العداوة إلى فسق فترد للفسق وإن لم
تخرجه إلى معصية فلا يبقى إلا مجرد تهمة
ولا خلاف أن الشهادة للصديق مقبولة وكذا الأخ والأقرب ولكن المعتمد فيه
قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تقبل شهادة خصم على خصم
وإنما ترد الشهادة بعداوة ظاهرة موروثة أو مكتسبة بحيث يعلم أن كل واحد
منهما يفرح بمساءة صاحبه ويغتم بمسرته ويبغي الشر له وهذا القدر لا يفسق به
فترد الشهادة به وإن عرف ذلك من أحدهما خصت شهادته بالرد دون شهادة صاحبه
وقد يكون سبب العداوة التعصب للأهواء والمذاهب إذ المعتزلة وسائر
المبتدعة لا يكفرون وأنه تقبل شهادتهم وإن ضللناهم قال الشيخ أبو محمد ترد
شهادة من يطعن في الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم ومن يقذف عائشة رضي الله
تعالى عنها فإنها محصنة بنص الكتاب مبرأة عن الفواحش وما ذكره صحيح وإنما
تقبل شهادة المخالفين في
الإعتقادات فإن من يرى أن الكبيرة الواحدة توجب الخلود في النار فقوله
أوثق
السبب الرابع التغافل
فرب عدل مغفل كثير السهو والغلط وإن لم يكذب عمدا وربما لا يفطن لحقائق
الأشياء ويكثر سبقه إلى الإعتقاد بالتوهم فمثل هذا لا تقبل شهادته المرسلة
إلا في أمر جلي يستقصي الحاكم فيه ويكثر فيه مراجعته حتى يتبين تثبته وأنه
لا يسهو في مثله
السبب الخامس التغير يرد الشهادة
فالفاسق المستسر بالفسق إذا ردت شهادته ثم حسنت حالته فأعاد تلك الشهادة
بعينها لم تقبل وتقبل سائر شهاداته إذ المكذب تنبعث فيه داعية طبيعية
لإثبات صدق نفسه فيصير ذلك من أهم حظوظه
والكافر والصبي والعبد إذا ردت شهادتهم ثم أعادوها بعد الأهلية قبل إذ لا
عار عليهم في الرد أما الفاسق المعلن والعدو والسيد إذا شهد لمكاتبه فردت
شهادتهم فأعادوها بعد
هذه الأعذار ففيه وجهان
أحدهما لا ترد لأن أسباب الرد ظاهرة فلا يتعيرون بها  كالصبي والعبد
والثاني أنه ترد لانهم اتهموا والمتهم يتعير فيدفع العار بالإعادة
السبب السادس الحرص على الشهادة بأدائها قبل الاستشهاد
وذلك مردود إن كان قبل الدعوى وإن كان بعد الدعوى وقب الإستشهاد ففي
القبول وجهان وإن لم تقبل فهل يصير به مجروحا فيه وجهان
وهذا فيما لا تجوز فيه شهادة الحسبة أما مالله تعالى فيه حق كالطلاق
والعتاق وتحريم الرضاع والعفو عن القصاص فيثبت بشهادة الحسبة من غير تقدم
دعوى وترددوا في الوقف والنسب وشراء الأب
أما الوقف فالصحيح أنه لا يثبت إلا بالدعوى إذا كان له مستحق معين فأما
على المساجد والجهات العامة فيثبت وأما شراء القريب الذي يعتق عليه فيشبه
الخلع من وجه والطلاق البائن يثبت بالشهادة على الخلع وفي شراء القريب
وجهان
أحدهما يثبت كالخلع وقال القاضي لا يثبت دون الدعوى لأن العوض مقصود في
الشراء وإثباته دون العوض محال وبيع العوض محال إذ لا مدعي له وأما النسب
فقال القاضي لا يثبت دون الدعوى وقال الصيدلاني من أتت بولد وادعى الزوج
أنه لدون ستة أشهر قبلت البينة على أنه لستة أشهر وإن سكتت المرأة وهذا يدل
على القبول من غير دعوى فقد تحصلنا فيه على تردد من حيث إن النسب متعلق
بكثير من حقوق الله تعالى كالطلاق
ولا خلاف في أن من اختفى في زاوية لتحمل شهادة فلا يحمل ذلك على حرصه على
الشهادة ولا ترد لأن الحاجة قد تمس إلى ذلك للأقارير وقال مالك رحمه الله
هذه الشهادة مردودة وقيل إنه قول للشافعي ضعيف
هذه مجامع ما ترد به الشهادة أما شهادة القروي على البدوي والبدوي على
القروي فمقبولة خلافا لمالك رحمه الله
وشهادة المحدود في القذف إذا تاب مقبولة خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله
وشهادة
الفاسق الذي لا يكذب ويوثق بقوله لا تقبل عندنا خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه
الله لأن من لا يخاف الله تعالى إنما يصدق لغرض وإذا تغير غرضه لم يبال
بالكذب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, witnessing, giving testimony; the act of being present and attesting to what one has observed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) as a legal conveyance of truth regarding another's right (ḥaqq), requiring moral probity (ʿadālah) in the witness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical presence; metaphorical (majāz) — bearing witness as a juridical act of attestation.
- Root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Transgression, enmity, hostility; to exceed bounds against another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Enmity (ʿadāwah) as a moral corruption of the heart that vitiates impartiality, thus undermining the evidentiary value of testimony.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical aggression; metaphorical — entrenched animosity that renders the witness suspect (mutahham).
- Root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neglect, heedlessness, inattention to details.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Heedlessness (ghaflah) as a deficiency in cognitive reliability, making the witness prone to error in testimony.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — absence of attention; metaphorical — habitual carelessness in legal attestation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (idhā... fa-) and exceptions (illā) requiring precise parsing to distinguish general rules from their qualifications, especially in the enumeration of the six causes of rejection.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the subsidiary branch — when a person testifies to a right shared between his son and a stranger, and his testimony is rejected regarding his son, then regarding its rejection concerning the stranger there are two positions (wajhān), owing to the partial division of the testimony (tabʿīḍ al-shahādah) within itself.

The third cause is enmity (al-ʿadāwah). Thus, the testimony of an enemy against his enemy is not accepted — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him. It is affirmed that the testimony of one engaged in active litigation (al-mukhāṣim) at the moment is not accepted. As for the testimony of one who had been litigating, after the cessation of the dispute, it is accepted by consensus — for if it were otherwise, this would lead to a situation wherein a person who anticipates that another will give testimony against him would initiate a dispute with him [to disqualify him].

The rejection of an enemy's testimony is problematic, because if enmity has driven him to immorality (fisq), then it is rejected on grounds of fisq; but if it has not driven him to disobedience, then nothing remains except mere suspicion (tuhmah). There is no disagreement that testimony on behalf of a friend is accepted, and likewise that of a brother and a close relative. However, the relied-upon basis in this matter is the saying of the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: {«لَا تُقْبَلُ شَهَادَةُ خَصْمٍ عَلَى خَصْمٍ»} — "The testimony of an adversary against an adversary is not accepted."

Testimony is only rejected due to manifest enmity — whether inherited or acquired — to the extent that it is known that each of the two rejoices at the other's misfortune, grieves at the other's joy, and seeks evil against him. This degree [of enmity] does not render one immoral (lā yafsuq bihi), yet testimony is rejected on account of it. If this [enmity] is known from only one of the two, then his testimony alone is singled out for rejection, not the testimony of his counterpart.

The cause of enmity may be partisanship for passions and doctrinal schools (al-ahwāʾ wa al-madhāhib). For the Muʿtazilites and the rest of the innovators (al-mubtadiʿah) are not deemed unbelievers, and their testimony is accepted even though we declare them to be in error (ḍallalnāhum). Shaykh Abū Muḥammad said: The testimony of one who impugns the Companions — may God be well pleased with them all — is rejected, as is the testimony of one who slanders ʿĀʾishah — may God be well pleased with her — for she is protected (muḥṣanah) by the text of the Book, declared innocent of all indecencies. What he mentioned is sound. Rather, the testimony of those who differ in doctrinal beliefs is accepted; for one who holds that a single major sin necessitates eternal abiding in the Fire — his statement is more trustworthy.

The fourth cause is heedlessness (al-taghāful). For there may be an upright person (ʿadl) who is heedless, prone to much forgetfulness and error — though he does not deliberately lie — and perhaps he does not perceive the realities of things, and frequently leaps to conviction based on conjecture (al-tawahhum). Such a person's unqualified testimony (shahādatuhu al-mursalah) is not accepted, except in a clear matter wherein the judge thoroughly investigates and repeatedly reviews him, until his carefulness (tathabbutuhu) becomes evident and that he does not err in similar matters.

The fifth cause: change of condition (al-taghayyur) rejects the testimony. Thus, a sinner (fāsiq) who conceals his immorality — if his testimony is rejected, then his condition improves, and he repeats that very same testimony, it is not accepted; but his other testimonies are accepted. For the one who has been discredited (al-mukadhdhab) has a natural inclination aroused within him to prove his own truthfulness, and this becomes among his most important aims.

As for the unbeliever, the child, and the slave — if their testimony is rejected, then they repeat it after [acquiring] legal capacity (al-ahliyyah), it is accepted, for there is no disgrace upon them in the rejection. As for the open sinner (al-fāsiq al-muʿlin), the enemy, and the master who testifies for his mukātab (slave under contract of manumission) — if their testimony is rejected, then they repeat it after [the removal of] these impediments, there are two positions (wajhān):

One of them: it is not rejected, because the causes of rejection are manifest, so they are not disgraced by them — like the child and the slave.

The second: it is rejected, because they are suspected (ittuhimū), and the suspected person is disgraced, so he repels the disgrace by repeating [the testimony].

The sixth cause: eagerness for testimony (al-ḥirṣ ʿalā al-shahādah) by giving it before being called upon (qabl al-istishhād). This is rejected if it occurs before the lawsuit (al-daʿwā). If it occurs after the lawsuit but before being called upon, then there are two positions regarding its acceptance. And if it is not accepted, is he thereby rendered defective (majrūḥ)? There are two positions.

This applies to matters in which testimony of voluntary attestation (shahādat al-ḥisbah) is not permissible. As for matters in which God — exalted — has a right, such as divorce (al-ṭalāq), manumission (al-ʿitāq), prohibition of fosterage (taḥrīm al-riḍāʿ), and pardon from retaliation (al-ʿafw ʿan al-qiṣāṣ) — these are established by testimony of voluntary attestation without prior lawsuit. They hesitated regarding the endowment (al-waqf), lineage (al-nasab), and the purchase by a relative [of a person who would be manumitted upon his acquisition].

As for the endowment, the correct [position] is that it is not established except through a lawsuit, if it has a specific beneficiary. As for endowments upon mosques and general charitable purposes (al-jihāt al-ʿāmmah), it is established [without a lawsuit]. As for the purchase by a relative who would be manumitted upon acquisition — it resembles khulʿ (divorce at the wife's initiative) in one respect, and irrevocable divorce (al-ṭalāq al-bāʾin) is established by testimony regarding khulʿ. Regarding the purchase by a relative, there are two positions:

One of them: it is established like khulʿ. And al-Qāḍī said: it is not established without a lawsuit, because the consideration (al-ʿiwaḍ) is intended in a purchase, and establishing it without the consideration is impossible, and selling the consideration is impossible since there is no claimant for it.

As for lineage, al-Qāḍī said: it is not established without a lawsuit. And al-Ṣaydalānī said: if a woman brings forth a child and the husband claims that it was born in less than six months, the evidence (al-bayyinah) is accepted that it was born at six months, even if the woman remains silent. This indicates acceptance without a lawsuit. Thus we have obtained in this matter a hesitation (taraddud), arising from the fact that lineage is connected to many rights of God — exalted — such as divorce.

There is no disagreement that whoever hides in a corner in order to obtain testimony (li-taḥammul al-shahādah) — this is not construed as eagerness for testimony, nor is it rejected, because necessity may require this for [obtaining] acknowledgments (al-aqārīr). Mālik — may God have mercy on him — said: this testimony is rejected. And it was said that this is a weak position attributed to al-Shāfiʿī.

These are the collective grounds by which testimony is rejected. As for the testimony of a villager (al-qarawī) against a Bedouin (al-badawī), and a Bedouin against a villager — it is accepted, contrary to Mālik — may God have mercy on him. And the testimony of one who has been flogged for false accusation (al-ḥadd fī al-qadhf), if he repents, is accepted — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him. And the testimony of a sinner who does not lie and whose word is trusted is not accepted in our school — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — because one who does not fear God — exalted — only speaks truthfully for some purpose, and when his purpose changes, he does not care about lying.

chapters.title_en: Conclusion Containing Two Principles, and the Second Chapter on Numerical Requirements and Male Gender of Witnesses
chapters.arabic_text: ### | خاتمة بذكر قاعدتين إحداهما أن هذه الأسباب إذا زالت قبلت الشهادة ولا يطول النظر في زوال الصبي والرق وأمثاله وإنما يطول في زوال الفسق والعداوة فإن التوبة مما يخفى ولا يكفي قول الفاسق تبت بل لا بد من الإستبراء مدة حتى يظهر بقرائن الأحوال صلاح سريرته وقدر بعضهم بسنة لتنقضي الفصول فإن العزائم تتغير فيه وقيل ستة أشهر والكل تحكم بل يختلف ذلك بالأحوال والأشخاص والمطلوب غلبة الظن أما القاذف فتوبته في إكذابه نفسه كذلك قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه وهو مشكل لأنه ربما كان صادقا فالمعني به تكذيبه نفسه في قوله أنا محق بالإظهار والمجاهرة دون الحجة فيكفي أن يقول تبت ولا أعود وهل يكفي مجرد ذلك دون الإستبراء إذا لم يظهر منه فسق آخر فيه نصوص مضطربة والحاصل أنه إن أقر على نفسه بالكذب فيستبرأ لأن هذا الكذب كبيرة وإن لم يقر وجاء شاهدا وما تمت الشهادة فقولان وإن جاء قاذفا فقولان مرتبان وأولى بأن يستبرأ والصواب أن نقول إن علم أن ذكر ذلك حرام فهو فاسق فيستبرأ وإن ظن أن هذا القذف مباح فلا حاجة إلى الإستبراء ويكفي قوله تبت فإن أقام الحجة على صدق نفسه ففي بقاء عدالته وجهان أحدهما أنه تقبل شهادته إذ ظهر صدقه والثاني إذ لا نمكن له أن يقذف ثم يثبت إلا أن يجيء مجيء الشهود القاعدة الثانية أن القاضي إذا غلط فقضى بشهادة هؤلاء ثم عرف بعد القضاء فينقض القضاء إن ظهر كون الشاهد عبدا أو صبيا أو كافرا وإن ظهر كونه فاسقا فقولان أقيسهما أنه ينقض إذ قال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه شهادة العبد أقرب من شهادة الفاسق إذ نص القرآن يدل على رد الفاسق حيث قال {إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ} وقوله {ممن ترضون من الشهداء} والثاني أنه لا ينقض لأنه أهل على الجملة وربما صدق وهذا ضعيف على مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه ولهذا قطع بعض الأصحاب بالنقض ورد تردد القول إلى ما إذا فسق بعد القضاء واحتمل الإستناد وأول عليه نص الشافعي رضي الله عنه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثاني في العدد والذكورة - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والعدد مشروط في كل شهادة فلا يثبت بشهادة واحد إلا رؤية الهلال لرمضان على رأي إذ يسلك به مسلك الأخبار لتعلقه بالعبادات أما هلال شوال فلا يثبت إلا باثنين ثم الشهادات في العدد على مراتب المرتبة الأولى الزنا ولا يثبت إلا بشهادة أربعة رجال لقوله تعالى {لولا جاؤوا عليه بأربعة شهداء} ويقول كل واحد رأيته يدخل فرجه في فرجها كالمرود في المكحلة فإن الشاهد الرابع على زنا المغيرة لما قال بين يدي عمر ورأيت نفسا يعلو واستا ينبو ورأيتهما يضطربان تحت لحاف ورجلاها على عاتقه كأنهما أذنا حمار فقال عمر الله أكر وجلد سائر الشهود ولم يكتف بهذا وهل يشترط على الإقرار بالزنا أربعة فيه قولان واللواط إن قلنا إنه كالزنا أو يوجب القتل فهو كالزنا وإن لم يوجب إلا التعزير فهل يشترط فيه أربعة فيه قولان وهل يجوز للشاهد النظر إلى الفرج أو إلى العورات لتحمل الشهادة فيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها نعم لأن الشهادة أمانة والثاني لا لكن إن وقع البصر تحمل الشهادة وإلا فلا والثالث لا يجوز لأجل الزنا فإن الحدود مبنية على الدفع أما لعيوب النساء وغير ذلك من الأحكام يجوز ### | ### | فرع لا تمنع الشهادة بتقادم العهد في الزنا ولا بأن يشهد أربعة في أربعة مجالس خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله في المسألتين فإنه قال إذا انفرد واحد في مجلس حد ولا ينفعه من يشهد في مجلس آخر المرتبة الثانية النكاح والرجعة لقوله تعالى {وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم} ولقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا نكاح إلا بولي وشهود الحق الشافعي رضي الله عنه به كل ما ليس بمال كالقصاص والعتق والإستيلاد والكتابة والوصايا والوكالة والعفو عن القصاص والجرح والتعديل والترجمة في مجلس القضاء وإثبات الردة والإسلام والنسب والبلوغ والولاء والعدة والموت ولا ينظر إلى رجوع الوكالة والوصايا إلى مال لأنها في نفسها سلطنة وولاية وليس بمال وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ينعقد النكاح بشهادة رجل وامرأتين وخصص اعتبار الذكورة بالعقوبات المرتبة الثالثة الأموال وحقوقها وأسبابها تثبت بشهادة رجل وامرأتين بدليل آية المداينة ويدخل فيه الشركة والإجارة وإتلاف الأموال وعقود الضمان والقتل خطأ وكل جراحة لا توجب إلا المال وحق الخيار والشفعة وفسخ العقود وقبض نجوم الكتابة إلا النجم الأخير فيتعلق به العتق ففيه وجهان ويثبت المال في السرقة بشاهد وامرأتين دون القطع والصحيح أن الأجل من حقوق المال وقيل إنه نوع سلطنة فيضاهي الوكالة ثم ليعلم أن النكاح إن لم يثبت برجل وامرأتين يثبت في حق المهر وكذا الوكالة تثبت في حق البيع وتثبت الوصية وإن لم تثبت الوصاية

- Root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cessation, departure, removal of a state or attribute
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Termination of an accidental quality (ʿaraḍ) from a subject, contrasted with essential non-existence
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in physical displacement; metaphorical (majāz) in cessation of legal disqualifications (ʿadālah, riqq)
- Root: ق-ذ-ف (q-dh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Throwing, casting; legally, false accusation of fornication (qadhf)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic crime of slanderous accusation requiring prescribed punishment (ḥadd) and special repentance conditions
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal throwing of an object; metaphorical for casting accusation against chastity
- Root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Breaking, demolishing, undoing a construction
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Annulment of a legal ruling (ḥukm) due to discovered defect in its basis
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical demolition; metaphorical for judicial reversal (naqḍ al-qaḍāʾ)
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with In + Perfect Verb (الشّرط بـ"إن" والفعل الماضي) — The protasis (sharṭ) with "in" + past tense indicates a hypothetical condition whose fulfillment triggers the apodosis (jawāb), used here for legal rulings contingent on discovered facts.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is a conclusion mentioning two principles.

**The First Principle:** When these disqualifying causes cease, testimony is accepted, and scrutiny is not prolonged regarding the cessation of minority, slavery, and the like. Rather, prolongation occurs only regarding the cessation of transgression (fisq) and enmity. For repentance is something hidden, and the mere statement of a transgressor, "I have repented," is not sufficient. Rather, it is necessary to observe a period of probation (istibrāʾ) until the soundness of his inner state becomes manifest through circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl). Some scholars estimated this period as one year, so that the four seasons may complete their cycle, for resolutions change within that span. It was also said: six months. All of this is discretionary (taḥakkum), rather it varies according to circumstances and persons, and what is sought is preponderance of conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann).

As for the slanderer (qādhif), his repentance consists in his declaring himself a liar. Thus said al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him. And this is problematic, because perhaps he was truthful. What is meant by his declaring himself a liar is his saying, "I am deserving of punishment," by way of public declaration and open admission, not by way of establishing proof. So it suffices for him to say, "I have repented and will not return." Is mere that sufficient without probation, when no other transgression has appeared from him? There are conflicting texts (nusūṣ muḍṭaribah) on this. The upshot is: if he confesses against himself of lying, then he must undergo probation, because this lying is a grave sin (kabīrah). If he does not confess, and comes as a witness, and the testimony is not completed, then there are two opinions (qawlān). If he comes as a slanderer, then there are two opinions arranged in order, and he is more deserving of probation. The correct view is that we say: if it is known that he deemed mentioning that (accusation) forbidden, then he is a transgressor and must undergo probation. If he thought that this slander was permissible, then there is no need for probation, and his statement "I have repented" suffices. If he establishes proof of his own truthfulness, then there are two aspects (wajhān) regarding the survival of his uprightness ('adālah):
- One of them: his testimony is accepted, since his truthfulness has become manifest.
- The second: we cannot permit him to slander and then prove it, unless he comes in the manner of witnesses (coming forward with proof).

**The Second Principle:** When a judge errs and renders judgment based on the testimony of such persons, then discovers (the defect) after the judgment, the judgment is overturned (yunqaḍ) if it becomes manifest that the witness was a slave, a minor, or an unbeliever. If it becomes manifest that he was a transgressor, then there are two opinions:
- The more analogically sound of the two (aqyasuhumā) is that it is overturned, for al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, said: "The testimony of a slave is closer (to acceptance) than the testimony of a transgressor," since the text of the Qurʾān indicates the rejection of the transgressor where He said: {«إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ»} ("If a transgressor comes to you with news") and His saying: {«ممن ترضون من الشهداء»} ("From those you approve among the witnesses").
- The second: it is not overturned, because he is qualified in a general sense, and perhaps he was truthful. And this is weak according to the school (madhhab) of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him. For this reason, some companions (aṣḥāb) definitively ruled for overturning, and referred the fluctuation of the opinion to the case where he became a transgressor after the judgment, and the possibility of the judgment being based on (his earlier state). And upon this, the text of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — is interpreted.

**The Second Chapter: On Numerical Requirements and Male Gender** — may Allah bless him and grant him peace —

The numerical requirement is stipulated in every testimony. Nothing is established by a single witness except the sighting of the crescent moon for Ramaḍān, according to one view, since it is treated in the manner of reports (akhbār) due to its connection with acts of worship. As for the crescent of Shawwāl, it is not established except by two (witnesses).

Then testimonies, regarding numerical requirements, are on levels (marātib):

**The First Level:** Fornication (zinā) — it is not established except by the testimony of four men, due to His saying, the Exalted: {«لولا جاؤوا عليه بأربعة شهداء»} ("Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?"). And each one must say: "I saw him insert his glans into her vulva like the kohl-stick into the kohl-container." For when the fourth witness (came forward) regarding the fornication of al-Mughīrah, and said before ʿUmar: "I saw a breath rising and a buttock sinking, and I saw them both moving under a blanket, and her two legs upon his shoulder like the ears of a donkey," ʿUmar said: "Allah is Greater!" and flogged the rest of the witnesses, and did not deem this sufficient.

Is the requirement of four (witnesses) stipulated for confession (iqrār) to fornication? There are two opinions. As for sodomy (liwāṭ): if we say it is like fornication, or that it necessitates killing, then it is like fornication. If it necessitates only discretionary punishment (taʿzīr), then is the requirement of four stipulated in it? There are two opinions.

Is it permissible for a witness to look at the private parts (farj) or at the pudenda (ʿawrāt) in order to bear testimony? There are three aspects (awjuh):
- One of them: Yes, because testimony is a trust (amānah).
- The second: No, but if the gaze falls (accidentally), then he bears testimony; otherwise not.
- The third: It is not permissible for the sake of fornication, for the ḥudūd punishments are built upon repulsion (deflection). As for the defects of women and other legal rulings, it is permissible.

### | Branch

The testimony is not prevented by the lapse of time (taqādum al-ʿahd) in fornication, nor by four (witnesses) testifying in four separate sessions — contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, in both matters. For he said: If one (witness) is alone in a session, he is flogged (for slander), and the one testifying in another session does not benefit him.

**The Second Level:** Marriage (nikāḥ) and return (rujʿah), due to His saying, the Exalted: {«وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم»} ("And call to witness two just men from among you"), and due to his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "No marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses." Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, held the correct view (al-ḥaqq) regarding everything that is not property (māl), such as retaliation (qiṣāṣ), manumission (ʿitq), umm walad (istīlād), kitābah (contract of manumission), bequests (waṣāyā), agency (wakālah), pardon from retaliation (ʿafw ʿan al-qiṣāṣ), jarḥ (discrediting witnesses) and taʿdīl (crediting witnesses), translation in the court session, establishing apostasy (riddah) and Islam, lineage (nasab), puberty (bulūgh), clientage (walāʾ), waiting period (ʿiddah), and death. No consideration is given to the fact that agency and bequests revert to property, because in themselves they are authority (sulṭānah) and guardianship (wilāyah), not property. Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Marriage is contracted by the testimony of one man and two women, and he specified the consideration of male gender to the penal punishments (ʿuqūbāt).

**The Third Level:** Properties (amwāl) and their rights and their causes are established by the testimony of one man and two women, by the evidence of the verse of debt (āyat al-madāyanah). Included in this are partnership (shirkah), lease (ijārah), destruction of properties (itlāf al-amwāl), contracts of guarantee (ʿuqūd al-ḍamān), homicide by error (qatl khaṭaʾ), and every wound that necessitates only property (compensation). Also included: the right of option (khiyār), preemption (shufʿah), rescission of contracts (faskh al-ʿuqūd), and receipt of the installments of kitābah — except the final installment, for manumission is attached to it, and there are two aspects (wajhān) regarding it. Property is established in theft by one man and two women, but not the amputation (qaṭʿ). The correct view is that the term (ajal) is among the rights of property. It was said: it is a type of authority, so it resembles agency (wakālah).

Then let it be known that if marriage is not established by one man and two women, it is established with respect to the dower (mahr). Likewise, agency is established with respect to sale, and bequest is established even if executorship (waṣāyah) is not established.

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Rank of Testimony: Matters Hidden from Men, and the Effect of a Single Witness
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فرع

لو قال لزوجته إن غصبت فأنت طالق أو إن ولدت فثبت الغصب أو الولادة
بشهادة النسوة وجب المال ولحق النسب ولم يقع الطلاق المعلق بهما وكذا لو
علق برؤية الهلال وشهد واحد ولو شهد أولا على غصبها رجل وامرأتان فقضى
القاضي بالضمان فقال إن كنت غصبت فأنت طالق قال ابن سريج إنه يقع بخلاف ما
إذا تقدم التعليق وفيه وجه آخر أنه لا يقع
المرتبة الرابعة ما لا يطلع عليه الرجال غالبا ويثبت برجل وامرأتين
وبأربع نسوة
كالولادة والبكارة وعيوب النساء والرضاع وما يخفى عن الرجال غالبا وقال
أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تثبت الولادة بشهادة القابلة وحدها عند قيام الفراش أو
ظهور مخايل الحمل بعد الطلاق
فإن قيل فهل يتعلق بشاهد واحد حكم قلنا من أقام شاهدين على مال فخاف
فواته فله التماس الحيلولة قبل التزكية ويجب ذلك على القاضي في الأمة إذا
أقامت شاهدين على الحرية ويجب في العبد إن طلب العبد والعبد ينفق من كسبه
في مدة الحيلولة وإن لم يكن فمن بيت المال ثم يرجع إلى السيد إن لم يثبت
العتق وكذا لو أقام شاهدين على
زوجية امرأة منعنا المرأة عن الإنتشار قبل التزكيه وفي العقار هل يجاب
إلى الحيلولة مع أنه لا خوف فيه خلاف
في هذه المسائل الشاهد الواحد هل ينزل في اقتضاء الحيلولة منزلة الشاهدين
فيه قولان
أحدهما نعم  لأن تمامه متوقع كالتعديل
والثاني لا لأن الواحد ليس بحجة والتعديل يبين أن ما أقامه من قبل كان
حجة فإن قلنا يؤثر في الحيلولة فقد ظهر له فائدة على الجملة
ولو جرى في دين فهل للمدعي أن يلتمس الحجر خوفا من أن يبيع ماله فيه
طريقان منهم من طرد القولين ومنهم من قطع بالمنع لأن ضرر الحجر عظيم وقال
القاضي إن كان الخصم معروفا بالحيلة وخاف القاضي حيلته حجر عليه
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الثالث في مستند علم الشاهد وتحمله وأدائه
- صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وفيه فصلان

### | الفصل الأول في مستنده
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ص-ب (gh-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To take something wrongfully, usurpation; core sense of seizing property or right by force or fraud.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, denotes unlawful appropriation (ghaṣb) entailing liability (ḍamān) and restitution.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical seizure; metaphorical (majāz) for violating rights or honor.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, witnessing, testifying; from presence at an event to bearing evidence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) as a legal proof (ḥujjah) establishing rights and obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for ocular presence; metaphorical for attestation of certainty in legal rulings.
- Root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Turning, changing, interposition; also means to prevent or interpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudence, ḥaywalah refers to the court's interim seizure or restraint of property pending verification of evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical interposition; metaphorical for legal sequestration or protective custody.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) with Suspended Ruling — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are syntactically linked such that the ruling (e.g., divorce) is contingent upon the verification of the condition, not merely its utterance.
chapters.translation:
I say: A branch [of this discussion].

If a man says to his wife: "If you commit usurpation (ghaṣb), then you are divorced," or "If you give birth, then [you are divorced]" — and the usurpation or birth is established by the testimony of women [alone], then the financial liability is incumbent, and the lineage (nasab) is affirmed, but the divorce suspended upon these [conditions] does not occur. Likewise, if he suspends [the divorce] upon the sighting of the crescent moon, and a single [male] witness testifies [to it], [the divorce does not occur].

But if witnesses first testify to her usurpation — a man and two women — and the judge rules for liability (ḍamān), then [the husband] says: "If you committed usurpation, then you are divorced" — Ibn Surayj holds that it does occur, contrary to the case where the suspension was made beforehand. There is another opinion that it does not occur.

The Fourth Rank: [Matters] upon which men are not normally able to gain knowledge, and which are established by one man and two women, or by four women — such as childbirth, virginity, defects of women, and suckling (riḍāʿ), and whatever is generally hidden from men. Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) said: Childbirth is established by the testimony of the midwife alone, when the marriage bed (firāsh) is established, or when signs of pregnancy appear after divorce.

If it is asked: "Is any ruling attached to a single witness?" — I say: If a man brings two witnesses concerning property, and fears its loss [before verification], he may seek the interposition (ḥaywalah) [of the court] before the examination of the witnesses' integrity (tazkiyah). This is obligatory upon the judge in the case of a slave-girl (umm walad) who brings two witnesses to her freedom. It is also obligatory in the case of a male slave, if the slave requests it. The slave is maintained from his own earnings during the period of interposition; if he has none, then from the public treasury (bayt al-māl). Then [the expenditure] is reclaimed from the master if the emancipation is not established.

Likewise, if [a man] brings two witnesses to the marriage of a woman, we prevent the woman from disposing of herself before the tazkiyah. Concerning real estate (ʿaqār) — whether one is granted interposition, given that there is no fear of loss therein — there is a difference of opinion.

In these matters [concerning] the single witness: Does he occupy, in requiring interposition, the station of two witnesses? There are two opinions:
One: Yes — because his completion [by a second witness] is anticipated, like the completion of [a witness's] integrity (taʿdīl).
The second: No — because a single [witness] is not a proof (ḥujjah), whereas taʿdīl clarifies that what [the witness] had previously established was a proof.

If we say that [a single witness] is effective in interposition, then a benefit has appeared for him in general.

And if [the dispute] concerns a debt, does the claimant have the right to seek a judicial interdiction (ḥajr) [upon the debtor], fearing that he might sell his property? There are two paths [of transmission]: Among them, some extend the two opinions [from the previous case]; and among them, some definitively hold the prohibition, because the harm of interdiction is grave. Al-Qāḍī said: If the opponent is known for trickery (ḥīlah), and the judge fears his deceit, he may place him under interdiction.

— Peace be upon him — The Third Chapter: On the Basis of the Witness's Knowledge, Its Acquisition, and Its Performance.
— Peace be upon him —
It contains two sections.

### The First Section: On Its Basis [i.e., the source of the witness's knowledge]

chapters.title_en: The Foundation of Testimony: Certainty, Necessity, and the Blind Witness
chapters.arabic_text:
والأصل فيه اليقين قال الله تعالى {ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم} وقال رجل
لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بم أشهد فقال أرأيت الشمس طالعة فقال نعم
فقال على مثل هذا فاشهد وإلا فاسكت هذا هو الأصل لكنا قد نلحق الظن به
للحاجة فنقول
المشهود عليه ينقسم إلى ما يحتاج إلى البصر دون السمع وإلى ما يحتاج إلى
السمع دون البصر وإلي ما يحتاج إليهما
الأول ما يحتاج إلى البصر دون السمع وهو الأفعال إذ البصر يدرك الفعل
والفاعل جميعا
القسم الثاني ما يحتاج إليهما وهو الأقوال إذ الأقوال تدرك بالسمع
والقائل لا
يتعين إلا بالبصر وليس للأعمى أن يعتمد الأصوات فإنها تتشابه بالتلبيس
وقال مالك رحمه الله له ذلك إذ يحل له وطء زوجته فإذا سمع إقرارها في حالة
الوطء كيف لا يشهد عليها فنقول في غيره من الشهود غنية أما حل الوطء
والمعاملات فتبنى على الحاجات
وقد اختلف الأصحاب في سبع
الأول إذا تعلق الأعمى بشخص فصاح في أذنه بالإقرار فجره إلى القاضي
متعلقا به وشهد ففيه وجهان
أصحهما القبول للثقة
والثاني لا لأن فتح هذا الباب عسير ودرجات التعلق والملازمة تختلف ولا
تنضبط
الثانية في رواية الأعمى خلاف لأنه يعجز عن تمييز المروي عنه ولكن قال
بعضهم
يجوز وكان الصحابة يسمعون من عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها من وراء الستر
فهم في حقها  كالعميان أما ما سمعه قبل العمى فيروي بل ما تحمل من الشهادة
قبل العمى على معروف النسب تقبل فيه شهادته
والقاضي إذا سمع بينة ولم يبق إلا الحكم فانعزل بالعمى ففي ذلك الحكم
وجهان من حيث إن العزل يبعد أن يتجزأ
الثالثة في المترجم الأعمى وجهان
أحدهما أنه يجوز لأن القاضي يشاهد المترجم كلامه
والثاني لا حسما للباب
الرابعة في انعقاد النكاح بحضور الأعميين وجهان لأنه ليس فيه إثبات لكن
المقصود الإثبات
الخامسة إذا تحمل البصير شهادة على شخص فمات ولم يكن معروفا بالنسب فلا
بد وأن يحضر ميتا حتى يشهد على عينه بمشاهدة صورته فإن كان قد دفن لم ينبش
قبره إلا إذا عظمت الواقعة واشتدت الحاجة ولم يطل العهد بحيث تتغير الصورة
فإن كان يعرفه باسمه واسم أبيه دون جده فليقتصر عليه في الشهادة وإن عرف
القاضي بذلك جاز وإن افتقر إلى اسم الجد فليس له أن يسأل عن اسم جده ويذكره
وحكي أن القفال ورد عليه كتاب من قاض ليزوج فلانة من خاطبها أحمد بن عبد
الله وكان جار القفال فقال أنا إنما أعرفك بأحمد لا بأحمد بن عبد الله فلم
يزوج وفي مثل هذه الصورة لو أقام
عنده بينة على أنه أحمد بن عبد الله لم تنفع لأنه لم يفوض إليه سماع
البينة كيف والصحيح أن البينة إنما تسمع بعد تقدم دعوى وإنكار
السادسة تحمل الشهادة على امرأة منتقبة بتعريف عدلين غير جائز إلا على
مذهب من يرى أن التسامع من عدلين كاف في معرفة النسب بل الطريق ما فعله
القفال رحمه الله إذ كتب في مثل هذه الشهادة أشهدني فلان وفلان أنها فلانة
بنت فلان وأنها أقرت وامتنع عن الأداء فقال وكيف أشهد والشاهدان في السوق
يعني أن شهادتي شهادة الفرع لكن طريق تحمل الشهادة أن تكشف عن وجهها حتى
ينظر إليها ويحفظ حليتها ثم إنها عند أداء الشهادة تكشف ثانيا فإن عرفها
شهد وإلا فيسكت
ويجوز النظر لحاجة التحمل وإن كانت في غاية الجمال  وللقاضي عند الشهادة
إن رابه أمر أن يحضر معها نسوة في قدها وكسوتها ويمتحن الشاهد فإن لم
يميزها عنهن لم تقبل شهادته وقد فعل ذلك بعض القضاة
السابعة إذا وقعت الشهادة على عينها كما ذكرناه بمال فطلب الخصم التسجيل
ولم يعرفها القاضي بنسبها لم يكن له ذلك إلا أن يسجل على حليتها وصورتها
ولا يكفي قولها إني فلانة بنت فلان إذ لا يسمع مجرد قولها ولا أن يقيم
الخصم بينة لأنها إنما تقام بعد تقدم دعوى في النسب ولكن لو نصب قيما حتى
يدعي عليها دينا وأنها بنت فلان فتنكر المرأة وتقام البينة جاز ذلك فعله
القاضي حسين في مثل هذه الواقعة وفيه إشكال من حيث إنها ربما كانت أقرت عند
القاضي بالنسب فكيف تنكره ولا دعوى إلا على منكر ومن حيث إن القاضي عالم
بأن هذه الدعوى كذب لكن قال القاضي حسين هذه حيلة جائزة للحاجة كما جاز بيع
ثمار خيبر بالدراهم ثم شراء نوع آخر به والمسألة محتملة
القسم الثالث ما لا يحتاج إلى البصر وهو الذي يثبت بالتسامع إذ لا يدركه
البصر
كالإعسار فإنه إنما يدرك بالخبرة الباطنة وقرائن الأحوال في الصبر سرا
على الضر والجوع ولا يعلم بيقين لكن إذا حصل ظن قريب من اليقين جازت
الشهادة
أما الذي يثبت بالتسامع فالنسب والملك المطلق واختلفوا في الولاء والوقف
والنكاح والعتق لأن هذه أمور يدرك بالبصر أسبابها لكن قد يستفيض بين الناس
ويدوم التفوه به وتتوفر الطباع على ذكره بخلاف البيع والهبة وأمثاله ففي
اعتماد التسامع به وجهان منهم من منع لإمكان المشاهدة ومنهم من ألحق بالنسب
لحصول الظن بالإستفاضة وكذا الخلاف في النسب من جانب الأم فإنه يمكن مشاهدة
الولادة ولكن يؤثر فيه التسامع أيضا ومنهم من قطع بأن جانب الأم كجانب الأب
وفي الموت أيضا طريقان والمشهور أنه كالنسب يثبت بالتسامع ومنهم من ألحقه
بالنكاح لأنه يمكن مشاهدته ثم إذا قضى به فالنظر في النسب والملك أما النسب
وما يلحق به ففي حد التسامع فيه  وجهان أحدهما أنه يسمع من قوم لا تجمعهم
رابطة التواطؤ كما في أخبار التواتر والثاني ذكر العراقيون أنه يكفي أن
يسمع من عدلين ثم لا يكون شاهدا على شهادتهما وهو بعيد ثم زادوا عليه
وقالوا لو رآه يحمل صغيرا وهو يستلحقه أو قال الكبير هذا ابني وهو ساكت شهد
على النسب وهذا غلط إلا أن يشهد على الدعوة فلقد يثبت النسب بمجرد الدعوة
أما الملك فلا يحصل فيه تعيين لأنه وإن شاهد الشراء فمن أين يعلم ملك
البائع أو شاهد الإصطياد فمن أين يعلم أنه لم يفلت من غيره لكن يعتمد الظن
الغالب الذي لو
كلف مزيد بحث لتعذر إثبات الأملالك ويحصل ذلك باجتماع ثلاثة أمور اليد
والتصرف والستامع أعني تفاوض الناس بإضافة الملك إليه فإن هذا إذا دام مدة
بلا منازع غلب على الظن الملك
وهل يكفي مجرد اليد والتصرف دون تفاوض الناس بالإضافة المشهور أن ذلك كاف
وقال القاضي لا يكفي لأن المنازع إنما يظهر إذا سمع الإضافة من الناس لكن
يقابله أنه لو كان تصرفه بالعدوان لظهر التفاوض بعدوانه في الجيران وأهل
المحلة فعدم ذلك دليل على عدم الخصم
وأما مجرد اليد دون التصرف أو التصرف دون اليد فلا يكفي وهل يكتفي بمجرد
التسامع دون اليد والتصرف وتصور ذلك في ملك معطل قال العراقيون يكفي ذلك
وهو بعيد فكأنهم يظنون أن الملك أيضا يشتهر كما يشتهر الوقف
ثم إنما نعني بالتصرف الهدم والبناء والبيع والفسخ والإجارة والرهن ولو
لم نر إلا مجرد الإجارة ولكن مرة بعد أخرى ففيه خلاف والصحيح أنه لا يدل إذ
المستأجر مدة طويلة قد يؤاجر مرارا
هذا بيان ما يعتمده الشاهد فتحل له الشهادة أما الخط فقد ذكرنا أنه لا
يعتمد للشهادة ويعتمد للحلف ومما يجب ذكره هاهنا أن من شهد على أن فلانا
مات ولا وارث له سوى فلان فهذا يسمع وإن كان على النفي كبينة الإعسار ولكن
يسمع ممن خبر باطن أحواله وعلم شعب نسبه ويكفي فيه عدلان يقولان لا نعلم  له
وارثا سواه مع الخبرة الباطنة
فإن لم تكن بينة سلم إلى الحاضر قدر اليقين فقط ولا يقين إلا في فرض من
لا يحجب عائلا كربع الثمن عائلا للزوجة وأما الأب فلا يستيقن له مقدار معين
فإن لم تكن بينة بحث القاضي ونادى بأني قاسم ميراثه فمن عرف له وارثا
فليذكر فإن لم يظهر سلم المال إلى الحاضر وهل يطلب له كفيلا للقدر المشكوك
فيه قولان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ي-ق-ن (ya-qāf-nūn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm establishment, absence of doubt; certainty as unshakeable cognitive state
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Certainty (yaqīn) as the epistemic ideal in juridical matters; contrasted with conjecture (ẓann) which may suffice only under necessity (ḥājah)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage — certainty as direct apprehension; metaphorical extension — "certainty" applied to overwhelming probability (ghalabat al-ẓann) when necessity dictates
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Exceptive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The text repeatedly employs "إلا" to carve exceptions from general rules, requiring precise parsing of the excepted clause's scope
chapters.translation:
I say: The foundational principle in testimony is certainty. Allah the Exalted has said: {«And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge»} (Quran 17:36). A man said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him: "By what shall I testify?" He replied: "Do you see the sun rising?" The man said: "Yes." He said: "Upon the like of this, testify; otherwise, remain silent." This is the foundational principle. However, we may attach conjecture (ẓann) to it out of necessity (ḥājah), and so we say:

The one testified against (al-mashhūd ʿalayh) divides into: that which requires sight without hearing; that which requires hearing without sight; and that which requires both.

The first category — that which requires sight without hearing — is actions (al-afʿāl), for sight perceives both the action and the agent together.

The second category — that which requires both — is utterances (al-aqwāl), for utterances are perceived by hearing, while the speaker is not identified except by sight. A blind man may not rely upon voices, for they resemble one another through dissimulation (talbīs). Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, held that he may do so, arguing: since it is lawful for him to have intercourse with his wife, if he hears her confession during the act of intercourse, how should he not testify against her? We respond: there is sufficiency in other witnesses besides him. As for the lawfulness of intercourse and transactions, these are built upon necessities.

The companions (al-aṣḥāb) have differed on seven subsidiary questions:

**The First:** If a blind man clings to a person who then shouts a confession into his ear, and he drags him to the judge while clinging to him, and then testifies — there are two positions (wajhān). The more correct of them is acceptance, due to the reliability (thiqa) attained. The second is rejection, because opening this door is difficult, and the degrees of clinging and accompaniment vary and cannot be regulated.

**The Second:** Concerning the blind man's narration (riwāyah) of hadith, there is disagreement, because he is incapable of distinguishing the one narrated from. However, some said it is permissible, for the Companions used to hear from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with her, from behind a curtain — they were, in her regard, like blind men. As for what he heard before becoming blind, he narrates it. Indeed, whatever testimony he undertook before blindness concerning a person of known lineage, his testimony therein is accepted. And if a judge heard the evidence (bayyinah) and nothing remained but the ruling, then he was removed from office by blindness — concerning that ruling there are two positions, on the grounds that removal from office is unlikely to be divisible.

**The Third:** Concerning the blind interpreter (al-mutarjim al-aʿmā), there are two positions. One is that it is permissible, because the judge observes the interpreter's speech. The second is rejection, to seal off the door (ḥasman li-l-bāb).

**The Fourth:** Concerning the validity of marriage (nikāḥ) contracted in the presence of two blind men, there are two positions, because there is no affirmation (ithbāt) involved — rather, the purpose is affirmation.

**The Fifth:** If a sighted man undertook testimony against a person who then died without being known by lineage, he must present the deceased person until he testifies upon his very identity (ʿayn) by observing his form. If he has been buried, his grave is not exhumed — except if the incident is grave, the need is intense, and the time has not been so long that the form would have changed. If he knows him by his name and his father's name but not his grandfather's, let him confine himself to that in his testimony; if the judge thereby recognizes him, it is permissible. But if he needs the grandfather's name, he may not ask about his grandfather's name and mention it. It is related that al-Qaffāl, may Allah have mercy on him, received a letter from a judge asking him to marry off a certain woman to her suitor, Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who was al-Qaffāl's neighbor. Al-Qaffāl said: "I know you only as Aḥmad, not as Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh," and he did not perform the marriage. In such a case, if evidence were presented before him that he was indeed Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, it would not avail, because he had not been delegated to hear evidence. How could it, when the correct view is that evidence is only heard after a prior claim (daʿwā) and denial (inkār)?

**The Sixth:** Undertaking testimony against a veiled woman (muntaqibah) through the identification of two just witnesses is not permissible — except on the view of one who holds that widespread hearsay (tasāmuʿ) from two just men suffices for knowing lineage. Rather, the proper method is what al-Qaffāl, may Allah have mercy on him, did: in such a case he wrote in the testimony document: "So-and-so and so-and-so made me witness that she is so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, and that she confessed," and he refrained from performing the testimony. He said: "How shall I testify when the two witnesses are in the market?" — meaning that my testimony would be subordinate testimony (shahādat al-farʿ). Rather, the method of undertaking testimony is that she uncover her face so that he may look at her and memorize her distinguishing features (ḥilyah). Then, when performing the testimony, she uncovers a second time; if he recognizes her, he testifies; otherwise, he remains silent. It is permissible to look at her for the need of undertaking testimony, even if she is of the utmost beauty. And the judge, at the time of testimony, if something suspicious occurs to him, may bring women of her stature and dress and test the witness; if he cannot distinguish her from them, his testimony is not accepted. Some judges have done this.

**The Seventh:** If testimony falls upon her very identity (ʿayn) as we have described, concerning property, and the opposing litigant requests official registration (tasjīl), but the judge does not know her by lineage — he may not do so, except that he register upon her distinguishing features and form. The mere statement of the woman "I am so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so" is not sufficient, for her bare statement is not heard; nor may the litigant present evidence, because evidence is only presented after a prior claim concerning lineage. However, if he appoints a guardian (qayyim) so that he may claim against her a debt and that she is the daughter of so-and-so, and the woman denies it, and evidence is then presented — this is permissible. Judge Ḥusayn did this in such a case. There is a difficulty (ishkāl) in it: first, because she may have confessed to the lineage before the judge — how then does she deny it, and there is no claim except against one who denies? Second, because the judge knows that this claim is false. But Judge Ḥusayn said: "This is a permissible legal stratagem (ḥīlah) for necessity, just as it is permissible to sell the fruits of Khaybar for dirhams and then purchase another type with them." The question is open to consideration.

**The Third Category:** That which does not require sight — namely, that which is established by widespread hearsay (tasāmuʿ), since sight cannot perceive it. Such is insolvency (iʿsār), for it is only perceived by inner acquaintance (khubrah bāṭinah) and circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl) — enduring harm and hunger in secret — and it is not known with certainty. But when a conjecture close to certainty is attained, testimony is permissible.

As for that which is established by widespread hearsay: lineage (nasab) and absolute ownership (milk muṭlaq). They differed concerning clientage (walāʾ), endowment (waqf), marriage (nikāḥ), and manumission (ʿitq), because these are matters whose causes are perceived by sight, yet they may become widely diffused among people, continuously spoken of, and natures disposed to mention them — unlike sale, gift, and their like. Concerning reliance upon hearsay in these, there are two positions: some prohibit it, due to the possibility of direct observation; others analogize them to lineage, because conjecture is attained through widespread diffusion (istifāḍah). Likewise, there is disagreement concerning lineage from the mother's side, for birth can be observed, yet hearsay also affects it. Some held definitively that the mother's side is like the father's side. Concerning death (mawt), there are also two paths: the well-known view is that it is like lineage, established by hearsay; some analogize it to marriage, because it can be observed. Then, when one rules by it, the consideration is in lineage and ownership.

As for lineage and what attaches to it — concerning the limit of hearsay therein, there are two positions. One is that it is heard from a group not united by any bond of collusion (rābiṭat al-tawāṭuʾ), as in reports of mass transmission (akhbār al-tawātur). The second, mentioned by the Iraqis, is that it suffices to hear from two just men, without his then testifying upon their testimony — but this is remote. They then added further, saying: if he saw him carrying a small child while claiming him, or the adult said "This is my son" while the other remained silent, he testifies upon the lineage. This is an error — unless he testifies upon the claim itself (daʿwah), for lineage may indeed be established by mere claim.

As for ownership, no specification (taʿyīn) is attained therein, for even if one observes the purchase, how does he know the seller owned it? Or if he observes the hunting, how does he know it had not escaped from someone else? Rather, one relies upon the prevailing conjecture (al-ẓann al-ghālib) — for if one were tasked with further investigation, the establishment of properties would become impossible. This is attained by the conjunction of three things: possession (yad), disposition (taṣarruf), and hearsay — meaning people's mutual discussion attributing the property to him. For if this continues for a duration without any claimant, ownership prevails in conjecture.

Does mere possession and disposition suffice without people's mutual discussion of attribution? The well-known view is that it suffices. Al-Qāḍī said it does not suffice, because the claimant only appears upon hearing the attribution from people. But this is countered by the fact that if his disposition were by aggression, discussion would appear concerning his aggression among the neighbors and the people of the district; the absence of that is evidence of the absence of any adversary.

As for mere possession without disposition, or disposition without possession, it does not suffice. Is mere hearsay sufficient without possession and disposition — conceivable in the case of an idle (muʿaṭṭal) property? The Iraqis said it suffices, but this is remote, as if they suppose that ownership becomes as widely known as endowment does.

Then, by disposition (taṣarruf) we mean: demolition (hadm), construction (bināʾ), sale (bayʿ), rescission (faskh), lease (ijārah), and pledge (rahn). If we observe nothing but mere lease, but repeatedly, one time after another — there is disagreement therein, and the correct view is that it does not indicate ownership, for a lessee over a long period may sublease repeatedly.

This is the exposition of what the witness relies upon, such that testifying becomes lawful for him. As for handwriting (khaṭṭ), we have mentioned that it is not relied upon for testimony, but it is relied upon for oath (ḥalaf).

Among what must be mentioned here: whoever testifies that so-and-so died with no heir other than so-and-so — this is heard, even though it is a negative (nafy), like the evidence of insolvency. But it is heard from one who has inner acquaintance with his circumstances and knows the branches of his lineage. Two just men suffice therein, saying: "We know of no heir for him other than him," along with inner acquaintance.

If there is no evidence, the estate is surrendered to the present claimant only to the extent of certainty (qadr al-yaqīn). And there is no certainty except in the case of one who is not veiled from inheritance by a dependant (ʿāʾil) — like the wife's quarter of an eighth. As for the father, no specific amount is certain for him. If there is no evidence, the judge investigates and proclaims: "I am dividing his inheritance; whoever knows of an heir for him, let him mention it." If none appears, the property is surrendered to the present claimant. Whether a guarantor (kafīl) is required of him for the doubtful portion — there are two sayings (qawlān).

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في وجوب التحمل والأداء

أما الأداء فهو واجب على كل متحمل متعين دعي إلى الأداء من مسافة دون
مسافة العدوي فهذه ثلاثة قيود

في غيبة الأصل إلى هذا الحد
ثم الشاهد لا يستحق الأجرة لأنه التزم هذه الأمانة بخلاف الكاتب نعم
يستحق الشاهد أجرة المركوب عند طول الطريق ثم إذا أخذها فله أن لا يركب
ويمشي فكأنه أجرة نصبه في المشي
ولو تعين شاهدان فامتنع أحدهما وقال احلف مع الثاني لم يجز بالإتفاق
أما التحمل فيما لا يصح دون الشهادة كالنكاح فالإجابة إلى التحمل فيه من
فروض الكفايات ومن امتنع لا يأثم لأنه غير متعين

والثاني نعم لحاجة الإثبات عند النزاع وكذا الخلاف في كتبه الصك لأنه لا
يستغنى عنه في عصمة الحقوق
- صلى الله عليه وسلم - الباب الرابع في الشاهد واليمين - صلى الله عليه
وسلم -
وكل واقعة يقضى فيها برجل وامرأتين فيقضى بشاهد ويمين إلا عيوب النساء

لم يجز

أحدها أنه باليمين والشاهد يعضد جانب الحالف كاللوث
والثاني أنه بالشاهد لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قضى بالشاهد
واليمين

بمسائل أربع

هل يجب إعادة الشهادة فيه وجهان وكذا لو جاء الوارث بشاهد آخر هل يجب على
الأول الإعادة فيه قولان مأخذهما أن هذه دعوى جديدة أو في حكم البناء ولو

الورثة فإنه إنما يثبت أولا لشخص واحد وهو الميت

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح م ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To carry, bear, or undertake a burden; implies physical or moral responsibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for 'bearing witness' (taḥammul) as the initial reception of testimony, distinct from 'performance' (adāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of carrying a load; metaphorically, the assumption of a legal duty.
- Root: ع د و (ʿ-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To exceed, transgress, or cross a boundary; also distance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, 'distance of transgression' (masāfat al-ʿadwā) — the travel distance permitting prayer shortening.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal spatial distance; metaphorical for exceeding legal limits.
- Root: ق ص ر (q-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shorten, restrict, or limit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for shortening prayer (qaṣr) during travel.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal shortening; metaphorical for legal limitation of obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) govern legal hypotheticals, as in 'if he did not bear witness...' (law lam yataḥammal).
chapters.translation:
I say: As for testifying (adāʾ), it is obligatory upon every specific bearer of testimony (mutḥammil) who is summoned to testify from a distance less than the distance of transgression (masāfat al-ʿadwā). These are three restrictions.

If he did not bear witness (yataḥammal), but his sight fell upon the act and he became specifically designated, there are two opinions (wajhān):
One: It is not obligatory, because the bearer has undertaken a commitment, whereas this one has not undertaken anything.
The second: It is obligatory, for the preservation of rights (ṣiyānatan lil-ḥuqūq).

If he is not specifically designated, then if they all refuse collectively, the hardship (ḥaraj) encompasses them all. But if one refuses, there are two opinions on its permissibility, based on the consideration that opening that door might lead to mutual abandonment (takādhul).

If he is summoned from a distance less than the distance of shortening (qaṣr) but greater than the distance of transgression, there are two opinions, like the two opinions regarding the obligation of accepting the testimony of the...

### Branch

...absent principal (ghaybat al-aṣl) to this extent.

Then the witness does not deserve a fee, because he has undertaken this trust (amānah), unlike the scribe. Yes, the witness deserves the hire of a mount (ujrat al-markūb) when the road is long. Then if he takes it, he may choose not to ride and instead walk — as if it were a fee for his exertion in walking.

If two witnesses are specifically designated and one refuses, saying, 'Take the oath with the second,' this is not permissible by consensus (ittifāq).

As for bearing witness in matters that are invalid without testimony, such as marriage (nikāḥ), responding to bearing witness therein is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). Whoever refuses does not sin, because he is not specifically designated.

As for bearing witness in matters of wealth (amwāl) and acknowledgments (iqrārāt) — is it a communal obligation? There are two opinions:
One: No, because one can dispense with it.
The second: Yes, due to the need for proof at the time of dispute. Likewise, the disagreement applies to writing documents (ṣikak), because one cannot dispense with it in safeguarding rights.

— Peace be upon him — The Fourth Chapter on the Witness and the Oath — Peace be upon him —

Every case adjudicated with one man and two women is adjudicated with one witness and an oath, except for defects of women and their chapter. It is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, that he adjudicated with one witness and an oath. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'That applies to matters of wealth.' Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'One witness and an oath are not accepted.'

Then, in our school (ʿindanā), the witness's testimony and his modification (taʿdīl) should precede the oath, for if the oath comes before the strengthening of the swearer's side by evidence (yad) or by circumstantial indication (lawth), it is void of effect. The swearer must affirm the witness's truthfulness in his oath, saying: 'I am right, and he is truthful.' There is no disagreement that if he swore with two women, it is not permissible.

Then this adjudication is by the witness, or by the oath, or by both. The effect appears in the liability for restitution (ghurm) upon retraction (rujūʿ) therein. There are three opinions:
One: It is by the oath, and the witness strengthens the swearer's side like circumstantial indication (lawth).
The second: It is by the witness, because it is reported that he, peace be upon him, adjudicated by the witness and the oath.
The third: It is by both together.

Then if we say it is by the oath, it is possible to impose liability for restitution also upon the witness, since the oath takes effect through his testimony — just as it is obligatory upon the modifier (muzakkī) in one opinion, because the testimony takes effect through his modification. The completion of the chapter is through four issues:

The first: If the heirs produce one witness to a debt owed to their deceased, and they all swear, they are entitled. If only one swears, the swearer is entitled to his share, not the refuser (nākil). If the refuser dies, his heir may not swear, because the right to swear is voided by refusal (nukūl). If he dies before refusing, his heir may swear. But must the testimony be repeated? There are two opinions. Likewise, if the heir brings another witness, must the first repeat his testimony? There are two opinions, whose basis is whether this is a new claim (daʿwā jadīdah) or in the category of continuation (bināʾ). If the heir refuses, and the deceased has a creditor, may the latter swear? There are two opinions, which we mentioned in the chapter on qasāmah (oaths of compurgation). As for when among them there is an absent person or a lunatic — when the absent returns or the lunatic recovers, he swears without needing to repeat the testimony. Rather, that testimony takes effect in the shared right through the claim of one of the heirs. Only the claim and the oath are specific to him, not the witnessing. As for when one bequeaths to two persons, and one swears with a witness while the second is absent — when the absent returns, the testimony must be repeated, because his ownership is separate, unlike the rights of heirs, for those are established first for one person, namely the deceased.
