بقي عليه درهم وقال علي رضي الله عنه يعتق بكل جزء من النجوم جزء من رقبته
وأما الإبراء في الكتابة الفاسدة فلا توجب العتق
الثانية إذا جن السيد فقبض النجوم لم يعتق لأن قبضه فاسد حتى يقبض وليه
وللمكاتب استرداده وإن تلف فلا ضمان لأنه المضيع بتسليمه إليه ولو جن
المكاتب فقبض السيد منه عتق لأن فعل العبد ليس بشرط بل إذا تعذر فعله
فللسيد أخذه هكذا أطلقه الأصحاب وفيه نظر إذ لا يبعد لزوم رفعه إلى القاضي
حتى يوفي النجوم إن رأى المصلحة
أما استقلال السيد فمشكل  عند إمكان مراجعة القاضي
أما الكتابة الفاسدة فظاهر النص أنها تنفسخ بجنون السيد كما تنفسخ بموته
ولا تنفسخ بجنون العبد فاختلفوا في النصين وحاصل ما ذكر نقلا وتخريجا ثلاثة
أوجه
أحدها وهو الأقيس أنه لا تنفسخ لأنه وإن كان جائزا فمصيره إلى اللزوم
كالبيع في زمان الخيار
والثاني أنه ينفسخ لضعف الفساد الثالث أنه ينفسخ بجنون المولى دون العبد
فإن الكتابة أبدا جائزة من جانب العبد فلم يؤثر الفساد في جانبه
ولا خلاف أن موت العبد يوجب فسخ الكتابة الصحيحة أيضا وقال أبو حنيفة
رحمه الله إن خلف وفاء فللوارث أداء نجومه وأخذ الفاضل بالوراثة
فإن قلنا لا تنفسخ بجنون العبد فأفاق وأدى عتق وإن قلنا تنفسخ بجنون
العبد فأفاق وأدى فهل يحصل العتق بمجرد التعليق فيه وجهان والأظهر أنه لا
يحصل كما لو فسخ السيد لأن هذا تعليق في ضمن معاوضة
والثالثة إذا كاتبا عبدا ثم أعتق أحدهما نصيبه نفذ وسرى إلى نصيب شريكه
إن كان موسرا لكن يسري في الحال أو يتأخر إلى أن يعجز المكاتب فيه قولان
أحدهما التأخير إلى أن يعجز إذ السيد قد نصب سبب العتق لنفسه بالكتابة
فكيف يجوز إبطاله
والثاني أنه يسري في الحال ويقدر انتقاله إلى المعتق من غير انفساخ في
الكتابة بل يعتق عن جهة الكتابة عن المعتق حتى يكون الولاء للشريك ولا يؤدي
إلى بطلان الكتابة ومنهم من قال ينتقل وتنفسخ الكتابة إذ العتق أقوى من
الكتابة فيعتق كله على الشريك المعتق ومن هذا الإشكال حكى صاحب التقري
بوجها أن الكتابة تمنع العتق أصلا فلا يسري
فإذا فرعنا على الصحيح وهو أنه يسري فإبراؤه عن نصيبه وقبض نصيبه حيث
يجوز القبض على ما سيأتي كإعتاقه في اقتضاء السراية ولا نقول إنه مجبر
على القبض فلا يسري لأنه مختار في إنشاء الكتابة التي اقتضت إجباره على
القبض نعم إذا مات وخلف مكاتبا فبض أحد الابنين نصيبه عتق نصيبه ولم يسر
لأنه مجبر على القبول ولم يصدر العقد منه
أما إذا ادعى  العبد على الشريكين أنه وفى نجومهما فصدق أحدهما وكذبه
الآخر عتق نصيب المصدق وهل يسري إلى الباقي فيه قولان وجه قولنا إنه لا
يسري مع أنه مختار في التصديق أن مقتضى إقراره عتق الكل فكيف يعمل بخلاف
موجبه ويقدر عتق البعض حتى يسري
الرابعة أحد الإبنين الوارثين إذا أعتق نصيبه من المكاتب نفذ وهل يقوم
عليه الباقي إن قومنا على أحد الشريكين فيه قولان وجه الفرق أن عتقه يقع عن
الميت ولذلك يكون الولاء للميت ويمكن بناء القولين على أن الوارث هل يملك
المكاتب ويحتمل أن لا يملك بناء على أن الدين المستغرق يمنع الملك وكذا
الخلاف في السراية عند إبرائه أما عند قبضه نصيبه فلا سراية لأنه مجبر

### | التفريع

إن قلنا إنه لا يسري ورق النصيب الآخر بالعجز ففي ولاء النصف الأول وجهان
أحدهما أنه بين الإثنين لأن العتق وقع عن الميت فله الولاء ولهما عصوبته
والثاني أنه للمعتق وكأنا بالآخرة تبينا أن العتق وقع عن المعتق وتضمن
انفساخ الكتابة لأن الكتابة لا تقبل التبعيض وقد انفسخ في الباقي وهكذا
الخلاف إن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To write, to prescribe, to decree; kitābah as a written contract of manumission by installments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A contractual obligation (muʿāwaḍah) entailing the slave's purchase of his own freedom, tied to the theology of servitude to God and man.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the written deed; metaphorical (majāz) for the binding covenant of emancipation.
- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be free, to become noble; root sense of release from bondage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal effect (ḥukm) of kitābah—emancipation upon discharge of the debt, a simulacrum of divine liberation from sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical manumission; metaphorical for spiritual release.
- Root: ج-ن-ي (j-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To commit a crime, to incur liability; jīnāyah as tortious act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The slave's tort liability attaching to the master, a nexus of agency and ownership.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for criminal harm; metaphorical for moral transgression.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with Taʿlīq (Suspension) — The apodosis (jazāʾ) is suspended on the protasis (sharṭ), as in "if he pays, he is free," requiring syntactic and juristic precision in determining the moment of emancipation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second examination concerns the rulings of kitābah (manumission contract). Its ruling is emancipation upon the clearing of liability (barāʾat al-dhimmah) through payment, remission (ibrāʾ), or substitution (iʿtiyāḍ), and the slave's independent acquisition (istiqlāl bi-al-iktisāb) immediately following the contract. Branching from this are the subordination of the slave's earnings and offspring, the obligation of compensation (arsh) and dowry (mahr) upon the master in cases of sexual intercourse and tortious acts. Kitābah necessitates the validity of the mukātab's (contracting slave's) dispositions in matters where he is not prevented, and the master's inability to dispose of his person (raqabah). All these details reduce to five rulings.

The First Ruling: On what does not effect emancipation, containing several issues.

The First Issue: If the master remits some of the installments (nujūm) or receives some of them, nothing of the slave is emancipated thereby; rather, he remains a slave as long as even one dirham remains upon him. ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) said: "He is emancipated with each portion of the installments, a portion of his person." As for remission in a corrupt kitābah (kitābah fāsidah), it does not necessitate emancipation.

The Second Issue: If the master becomes insane and then receives the installments, the slave is not emancipated, because the master's reception is invalid (fāsid) until his guardian receives them. The mukātab may reclaim what he paid, and if it perishes, there is no liability upon the guardian, because the slave himself caused the loss by handing it over to the insane master. If the mukātab becomes insane and the master receives from him, emancipation occurs, because the slave's act is not a condition; rather, when his act becomes impossible, the master may take it. Thus did the companions (al-aṣḥāb) state it absolutely, but there is consideration here, for it is not improbable that the matter must be referred to the judge so that he may discharge the installments if he sees benefit. As for the master's independent action, it is problematic when recourse to the judge is possible. As for the corrupt kitābah, the apparent text (naṣṣ) is that it is dissolved by the master's insanity just as it is dissolved by his death, and it is not dissolved by the slave's insanity. They differed regarding the two texts, and the sum of what is transmitted and derived is three positions: One—which is the more analogical (aqyas)—is that it is not dissolved, because although it is permissive (jāʾiz), its end is bindingness (luzūm), like a sale during the option period (khiyār). The second is that it is dissolved due to the weakness of the corruption. The third is that it is dissolved by the master's insanity but not the slave's, for kitābah is always permissive from the slave's side, so corruption does not affect his side. There is no disagreement that the slave's death necessitates the dissolution of even the valid kitābah. Abū Ḥanīfah (may God have mercy on him) said: "If he leaves sufficient payment, the heir may discharge his installments and take the surplus by inheritance." If we say it is not dissolved by the slave's insanity, and he recovers and pays, he is emancipated. If we say it is dissolved by the slave's insanity, and he recovers and pays, is emancipation achieved merely by the suspension (taʿlīq)? There are two positions, and the more apparent is that it is not achieved, just as if the master had rescinded, because this is a suspension within a commutative contract (muʿāwaḍah).

The Third Issue: If two masters contract kitābah with a slave, then one of them emancipates his share, it is effective and permeates (sarā) to the partner's share if he is wealthy (mūsir). But does it permeate immediately or is it deferred until the mukātab becomes unable to pay? There are two positions. One is deferral until he becomes unable, for the master has set up the cause of emancipation for himself through kitābah, so how could its nullification be permitted? The second is that it permeates immediately, and it is deemed that the slave's ownership transfers to the emancipator without dissolution of the kitābah; rather, he is emancipated by virtue of the kitābah from the emancipator, so that the walāʾ (clientage) belongs to the partner, and this does not lead to the nullity of the kitābah. Some said: "It transfers and the kitābah is dissolved, for emancipation is stronger than kitābah, so the whole slave is emancipated upon the emancipating partner." From this difficulty, the author of al-Taqrīb narrated a position that kitābah prevents emancipation entirely, so it does not permeate. If we build upon the correct position—that it does permeate—then his remission of his share and his reception of his share, where reception is permissible as will come, are like his emancipation in necessitating permeation. We do not say he is compelled to receive, so it does not permeate, because he was free in initiating the kitābah which necessitated his compulsion to receive. Yes, if a man dies leaving a mukātab, and one of his two sons receives his share, his share is emancipated but does not permeate, because he was compelled to accept and the contract did not originate from him. As for when the slave claims before the two partners that he has paid their installments, and one affirms him while the other denies him, the share of the affirming one is emancipated. Does it permeate to the remaining one? There are two positions. The basis of our saying that it does not permeate—despite his freedom in affirming—is that the requirement of his acknowledgment (iqrār) is the emancipation of the whole, so how can one act contrary to its implication and deem partial emancipation so that it permeates?

The Fourth Issue: If one of two inheriting sons emancipates his share of the mukātab, it is effective. Is the remaining share valued upon him (taqyīm) if we value it upon one of the two partners? There are two positions. The basis of the distinction is that his emancipation occurs on behalf of the deceased, and therefore the walāʾ belongs to the deceased. The two positions can be built upon whether the heir owns the mukātab, and it is possible he does not own him, based on the view that overwhelming debt prevents ownership. Likewise, there is disagreement on permeation upon his remission. As for upon his reception of his share, there is no permeation because he is compelled.

The Branching (Tafrīʿ): If we say it does not permeate, and the other share reverts (yaruqqu) due to inability, then regarding the walāʾ of the first half there are two positions. One is that it is between the two [heirs], because the emancipation occurred on behalf of the deceased, so he has the walāʾ and they have his ʿaṣabah (agnatic succession). The second is that it belongs to the emancipator, and it becomes apparent in the end that the emancipation occurred on behalf of the emancipator and entailed the dissolution of the kitābah, because kitābah does not admit division, and it was dissolved regarding the remainder. Likewise, the disagreement continues if...

chapters.title_en: Section 607 — On the Effects of Manumission by Kitābah, Its Continuation, and the Rules of the "Iʿtāʾ" (Grant)
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع نا على أن العتق يسري ولكن يتضمن انفساخ الكتابة في محل السراية لأنه قد انفسخ في البعض أما الولاء في محل السراية فينبني على انفساخ الكتابة فإن رأينا أنها تنفسخ بالسراية فالولاء فيه لمن سرى عليه وإن قلنا لا تنفسخ فقد عتق العبد كله عن جهة كتابة الميت فالولاء لهما بعصوبته فرع إذا خلف ابنين وعبدا فادعى العبد أن المورث كاتبه فصدقه أحدهما وكذبه الآخر وحلف صار نصيب المصدق مكاتبا فيستقل العبد بنصف كسبه ليصرفه إلى النجوم ثم إن عتق نصيب المصدق بقبضه النجوم لم يسر لأنه مجبر عليه وإن عتق بإعتاق سرى ولم يمكن تخريجه على الخلاف في السراية إلى المكاتب لأن الشريك يزعم أن نصيبه رقيق فلا بد وأن يسري إليه وإن عتق بالإبراء لم يسر فإن الشريك المكذب يقول الإبراء لاغ إذ لا كتابة فلا يسري حتى يصرح المصدق بلفظ يوجب الإعتاق ثم الصحيح أن المصدق يشهد مع غيره على المكذب فيجوز لأن نصيبه من النجوم قد سلم بإقرار العبد فلا تهمة فيه الخامسة إذا قبض النجوم ثم وجدها ناقصة في الوصف فإن رضي استمر العتق ويكون حصول العتق عند القبض أو عند الرضا فيه خلاف ينبني على أن الدين الناقص يملك عند القبض أو عند الرضا وإن أراد الرد فله ذلك ويرتد العتق على معنى أنه يتبين أنه لم يحصل لعدم القبض في المستحق وهو ظاهر إذا قلنا لا يحصل الملك بالقبض وإن قلنا يحصل فيحصل العتق أيضا بحسبه حصولا غير مستقر بل يندفع عند الرد فلو اطلع على النقصان بعد تلف النجوم فله طلب الأرش ويتبين أن لا عتق حتى يؤدي الأرش فإن عجزه السيد وأرقه جاز كما في نفس النجوم ثم الأرش قدر قيمة نقصان النجوم أو ما يقابله من الرقبة فيه خلاف يجري مثله في المعاوضات المتعلقة بالديون السادسة إذا خرج النجم مستحقا تبين أن لا عتق وليس هو كما لو قال إن أعطيتني ألفا فأنت حر فجاء بمغصوب فيحصل العتق أو الطلاق في مثله على وجه لتجرد حكم التعليق ووجوب صورة الإعطاء أما ها هنا إذا صحت المعاملة فلا يعتق إلا ببراءة الذمة نعم يجري الخلاف في الكتابة الفاسدة إذا صرح بالتعليق على أداء الألف ### | ### | فرع لو قال له عند أداء النجوم اذهب فإنك حر أو عتقت فله رد العتق ولا يؤاخد به فإنه قال بناء على ظاهر الحال كالمشتري فإنه يرجع بالثمن إذا خرج المبيع مستحقا وإن كان قد قال هو ملكي وملك بائعي وقد ذكرنا فيه وجها أنه لا يرجع ويجري ها هنا أيضا إذ لا فرق أما إذا أقر بعتق أو طلاق ثم قال كنت أطلقت لفظة ظننتها نافذة فراجعت المفتي فأفتى بأنه لا ينفذ قال الصيدلاني يقبل قياسا على هذه المسألة وهذا بعيد لأن الإقرار حجة صريحة وفتح هذا الباب يمنع الأقارير إلا أن قوله بعد قبض النجوم أنت حر أو عتقت هو إقرار ولا فرق بين أن يقوله جوابا إذا سئل عن حريته أو ابتداء وبين أن يقوله متصلا بقبض النجوم أو بعده فإنه معذور في الأحوال كلها لظنه فإذا عذر ها هنا فلا يبعد أن يفتح هذا الباب في كلام يجري مجراه الحكم الثاني ما يتعلق بأداء النجوم وفيه سبع مسائل الأولى أنه يجب الإيتاء لقوله تعالى {وآتوهم من مال الله} ولأنه ما كاتب أحد من السلف إلا وضع شيئا ولن المطلقة تنتظر مهرا فإذا لم تسلم تأذت فوجبت المتعة دفعا للأذى فكذا العبد ينتظر العتق مجانا فإذا كان بعوض فيتأذى فلا بد من إمتاعه ثم النظر في محله ووقته وجنسه وقدره أما المحل فهو الكتابة الصحيحة وفي الفاسدة وجهان بناء على أن الأصل في الإيتاء حط شيء من واجب النجوم أو بذل شيء مع أنه لا خلاف أن الوجوب يتأدى بكل واحد منهما فإذا قلنا الأصل هو حط الواجب فلا يجب في الفاسد النجوم بل يجب قيمة الرقبة بعد العتق أما لو باع العبد من نفسه أو أعتقه على مال فالمشهور أنه لا يجب الإيتاء وفيه وجه أنه يجب لأجل العوض ولا خلاف أن العتق مجانا لا يوجب شيئا فإنه عين الإيتاء والإمتاع أما الوقت فلا يجب البدار عقيب العقد وهل يجوز التأخير عن العتق فيه وجهان أحدهما نعم لأن مقصوده أن يكون بلغة بعد العتق والثاني لا لأن مقصوده أن يكون معونة على العتق وأما مقداره فوجهان أحدهما أنه أقل ما يتمول إذ ينطلق عليه اسم الإيتاء بخلاف المتعة فإنه قدر بالمعروف والثاني أنه لا يكفي ذلك إذ الحبة لا يحصل بها لا بلغة ولا معونة بل لا بد من قدر يليق بحال السيد والعبد وقدر النجوم ويظهر له أثر في التيسير والتخفيف وقد كاتب ابن عمر رضي الله عنه عبدا له بخمسة وثلاثين ألف درهم ثم حط عنه خمسة آلاف وهو تسع المال وإن كان السبع إلى العشر لائقا ولكن لا يتقدر به بل يجتهد القاضي عند النزاع فإن شك في مقداره فيتقابل فيه أصلان براءة ذمة السيد وبقاء الأمر بالإيتاء فليرجح ### | ### |
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ر-ي (s-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To travel by night; to spread, permeate, or flow through something continuously.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, the transitive extension of a legal effect (e.g., manumission) from one part to another, as a divinely-ordained consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for nocturnal travel; metaphorical (majāz) for the "flow" of a ruling across parts, here used technically.
- Root: ف-س-خ (f-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To annul, dissolve, or tear apart a binding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Rescission of a contract due to a legal impediment or partial invalidation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tearing cloth; metaphorical for contractual dissolution.
- Root: أ-ت-ي (a-t-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To come, bring, or give.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The obligatory grant (iʿtāʾ) from the master to the mukātab (slave under kitābah), rooted in Quranic command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for giving; here, a specific juristic term for the mandatory financial concession.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muqaddar) — The phrase "if we see that it dissolves" (fa-in raʾaynā) governs a hypothetical whose apodosis is inferred from context, requiring precise parsing of legal alternatives.
chapters.translation:
I say: We hold that manumission (al-ʿitq) does spread (yasrī), but it entails the dissolution (infisākh) of the kitābah in the locus of its spreading, because it has already dissolved in part.

As for the walāʾ (clientage) in the locus of spreading, it is built upon the dissolution of the kitābah. If we hold that it dissolves by the spreading, then the walāʾ therein belongs to the one upon whom it spread. But if we say it does not dissolve, then the entire slave has been freed by virtue of the deceased's kitābah, so the walāʾ belongs to both [heirs] through their ʿaṣabah (agnatic tie).

Branch: If a man leaves behind two sons and a slave, and the slave claims that the testator made a kitābah with him, and one son affirms him while the other denies and takes an oath, then the share of the affirming one becomes kitābah. The slave then independently manages half of his earnings to pay toward the installments (nujūm). Thereafter, if the affirming one's share is freed by the slave's payment of the installments, it does not spread, because it is compulsory upon him. But if it is freed by manumission (iʿtāq), it spreads, and it cannot be derived from the disagreement about spreading to the mukātab, because the [denying] partner claims his share is still enslaved, so it must spread to him. If it is freed by remission (ibrāʾ), it does not spread, for the denying partner says: "The remission is void, since there is no kitābah," so it does not spread—unless the affirming one explicitly utters a word effecting manumission. Then, the correct view is that the affirming one may testify alongside another against the denier, and it is permissible, because his share of the installments has been secured by the slave's confession, so there is no suspicion of bias therein.

Fifth: If he receives the installments, then finds them deficient in description (waṣf), then if he is satisfied, the manumission continues, and whether manumission occurs at receipt or at satisfaction involves a disagreement built upon whether a deficient debt is owned at receipt or at satisfaction. If he wishes to return them, he may do so, and the manumission reverts in the sense that it becomes clear it never occurred, due to the absence of receipt of what is legally due. This is evident if we say ownership is not acquired by receipt. If we say it is acquired, then manumission also occurs correspondingly, but as non-stable acquisition, rather it is repelled upon return.

If he discovers the deficiency after the installments have perished, he may claim the difference (arsh), and it becomes clear there was no manumission until he pays the arsh. If the master then incapacitates him and re-enslaves him, that is permissible, just as with the installments themselves. Then, whether the arsh is the amount of the deficiency's value or its equivalent from the slave's person involves a disagreement that runs similarly in exchanges pertaining to debts.

Sixth: If an installment turns out to be usurped (mustaḥaqq), it becomes clear there was no manumission. This is not like the case where he says: "If you give me a thousand, you are free," and he brings a usurped item, where manumission or divorce occurs in such a case, on one view, due to the pure nature of the conditional and the obligation of the form of giving. But here, when the transaction is valid, he is not freed except by the discharge of liability (barāʾat al-dhimmah). Yes, the disagreement runs in a corrupt kitābah (kitābah fāsidah) if he explicitly conditions upon payment of the thousand.

Branch: If he says to him at the time of paying the installments: "Go, for you are free," or "You are freed," he may reject the manumission and is not held to it, for he said it based on the apparent state of affairs, like the buyer who recovers the price if the sold item turns out to be usurped, even if he had said: "It is mine and my seller's property." We have mentioned a view that he does not recover, and it runs here too, for there is no difference. But if he confesses to manumission or divorce, then says: "I uttered a word I thought was effective, so I consulted the mufti, and he ruled it does not take effect," al-Ṣaydalānī said: He is accepted, by analogy to this case. This is far-fetched, because confession is an explicit proof, and opening this door would nullify confessions. However, his saying after receiving the installments, "You are free" or "You are freed," is a confession, and there is no difference between his saying it in response when asked about his freedom, or as an initiation, or connected to the receipt of installments or after it—for he is excused in all states due to his assumption. So if he is excused here, it is not far to open this door in speech that runs its course.

The second ruling concerns what pertains to the payment of installments, and it contains seven issues.

First: The grant (iʿtāʾ) is obligatory, due to His saying, the Exalted: {«وَآتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ اللَّهِ»} ("And give them from the wealth of Allah"). Also, because no one among the Salaf made a kitābah without waiving something. And since the divorced woman awaits her dower, and if it is not delivered she is harmed, so the mutʿah (consolatory gift) is obligatory to repel harm—likewise, the slave awaits freedom for free, and if it is with compensation, he is harmed, so he must be granted enjoyment (imtāʿ).

Then the consideration is of its locus, time, type, and amount.

As for the locus: It is the valid kitābah. In the corrupt one, there are two views, built upon whether the origin of the iʿtāʾ is a reduction of some obligatory installments or a grant of something—though there is no disagreement that the obligation is fulfilled by either. If we say the origin is reduction of the obligatory, then in the corrupt kitābah, it is not the installments that are obligatory, but rather the value of the slave's person after manumission. But if the slave sells himself or is manumitted for a price, the well-known view is that no iʿtāʾ is obligatory, with one view that it is obligatory due to the compensation. There is no disagreement that free manumission obligates nothing, for it is the very essence of iʿtāʾ and imtāʿ.

As for the time: It is not obligatory to hasten immediately after the contract. Whether delay until after manumission is permissible involves two views: One, yes, because his purpose is that it be a provision after freedom. The second, no, because his purpose is that it be assistance toward freedom.

As for its amount: Two views. One: It is the minimum that counts as wealth (māl), since the name "iʿtāʾ" applies to it—unlike mutʿah, which is measured by what is customary (maʿrūf). The second: That is insufficient, for a single grain achieves neither provision nor assistance; rather, there must be an amount befitting the state of the master, the slave, and the amount of the installments. Its effect appears in facilitation and lightening. Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, made a kitābah with his slave for thirty-five thousand dirhams, then waived five thousand—which is one-ninth of the property—though one-seventh to one-tenth is fitting, but it is not fixed by that; rather, the judge exercises ijtihād at dispute. If he doubts its amount, two principles conflict: the master's immunity of liability (barāʾat al-dhimmah) and the persistence of the command for iʿtāʾ, so let him weigh which to prefer.

chapters.title_en: On the Incapacity of the Mukātab, the Death of the Master, and the Five Causes of the Inability to Pay the Installments
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع لو بقي من النجوم قدر لا يقبل في الإيتاء أقل منه فليس للسيد تعجيزه أصلا بل يرفعه إلى القاضي ليرى فيه رأيه أما الجنس فليبرىء من بعض النجوم أو ليرد عليه مما أخذ منه أو من جنسه فإن عدل إلى غير جنسه فوجهان وجه المنع أنه تعبد فهم من قوله تعالى {وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم} وعنى به النجوم فضاهى قوله تعالى {وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده} والأصح أن هذه معاملة فيتطرق العوض إليها فرع لو مات السيد قبل الإيتاء فهو في تركته لكن النص أنه يضارب به الوصايا وهو مشكل لأن حق الدين أن يقدم فلعله أراد به ما إذا قدر زيادة على الواجب فمات ومنهم من قال وجوب الإيتاء ضعيف فينقلب استحبابا بالموت ومنهم من قال أقل ما يتمول دين والزيادة إذا أوجبناها إنما أوجبنا لأنها لائقة بالحال ولا تليق بما بعد الموت فهو الذي أراد به الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه وأرضاه المسألة الثانية إذا عجل النجوم قبل المحل أجبر السيد على القبول لأجل فك الرقبة كما يجبر في الدين الذي به رهن أما في سائر الديون المؤجلة فوجهان ثم إنما يجبر على قبول النجم إذا لم يكن على السيد ضرر ومؤنة ولم يكن وقت نهب وغارة فإذا كان عليه ضرر لم يلزمه فإن كان النهب مقرونا بوقت العقد ففي الإجبار وجهان وحيث يجبر فلو كان غائبا أو امتنع قبض القاضي عنه وعتق ويقبض النجم الأول وإن لم يكن فيه عتق أيضا لأنه تمهيد سبب للعتق ولو قال لا آخذه فإنه حرام فالقول قول المكاتب ويجب أخذه ويعتق به ثم يجب عليه رده إلى مالكه إن أضافه إلى مالك فإن لم يضف فهل ينتزع من يده فيه وجهان فإن قلنا لا ينتزع فلو كذب نفسه فالظاهر قبوله ويعود تصرفه فيه ### | ### | فرع إذا قال السيد عدل لي بعض النجوم لأبرئك عن البعض فقد نقل المزني رحمه الله في ذلك ترددا وجعل المسألة على قولين ومحل القولين مشكل لأن السيد إن قال إذا عجلت فقد أبرأتك فهو تعليق إبراء فاسد وإن قال العبد خذ هذا بشرط أن تبرئني فأداؤه بالشرط فاسد فلعل محل التردد أن يبتدىء العبد الأداء بالشرط فأداؤه فاسد لكن لو أبرأ السيد واستأنف العبد رضا في دوام القبض صار القبض صحيحا فلو لم يستأنف فهل نقول رضاه الأول كان رضاء بالإضافة إلى حالة الإبراء وقد تحقق فهل يكتفي به يحتمل فيه تردد المسألة الثالثة في تعذر النجوم وله خمسة أسباب الأول الإفلاس عند المحل وللسيد مبادرة الفسخ فإن لم يبادر فله الفسخ متى شاء وليس هذا على الفور ولو استمهل المكاتب لم يلزمه إلا بقدر ما يخرج المال من المخزن فإن كان ماله غائبا فله الفسخ ولو كان له عروض لا تشترى إلا بعد زمان فله الفسخ وقال الصيدلاني لا يفسخ وهو بعيد وإذا عجز عن البعض فله الفسخ والباقي سلم للسيد إلا ما كان من الزكوات فإنها ترد إلى أصحابها الثاني إذا غاب وقت المحل فله الفسخ ولا يحتاج إلى الرفع إلى القاضي على الصحيح ولو كان أذن له في السفر فله أن يرجع ولكن لا يبادر الفسخ حتى يعرفه الرجوع عن الإذن فإن قصر بعد ذلك في الإياب والأداء فسخ الثالث أن يمنع مع القدرة فله ذلك إذ ليس النجوم لازما على العبد بل الكتابة جائزة في جانبه لكن للسيد الفسخ وقال العراقيون ليس للعبد الفسخ لكن له أن لا يؤدي مع القدرة حتى يفسخ السيد وهو متناقض لأن العقد إن كان لازما فليجب الوفاء به الرابع إذا جن العبد وقلنا لا ينفسخ على الأصح فالقاضي إن علم له مالا ورأى مصلحته في العتق أدى عنه وإن رأى أنه يضيع إن عتق فله أن لا يؤدي عنه وكلام الأصحاب يشير إلى أن السيد يستقل بالأخذ إذ ذكروا أن القبض من العبد المجنون يوجب العتق وفيه نظر إذ ربما لم يرضى بالعتق والأداء إذا أفاق إلا أن هذا لا فائدة فيه فإن السيد يقدر على إعتاقه بكل حال فأي فرق بين أن يأخذ كسبه عن جهة النجوم أو عن جهة رالرق الخامس الموت وذلك يوجب انفساخ الكتابة وإن خلف وفاء لتعذر العتق بعد الموت ### |
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Weakness, incapacity, inability to accomplish a task; the opposite of power (qudrah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿajz denotes the absence of the capacity to act, whether by nature or by legal impediment; here it marks the legal status of the mukātab who cannot fulfill the stipulated installments.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to physical incapacity; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to legal incapacity, since the slave may be physically able but legally deemed unable to complete the contract.
- Root: ن-ج-م (n-j-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A star; also a portion of a thing that appears at intervals, like the rising of stars; hence an installment of a debt paid at fixed times.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the context of kitābah (manumission contract), najm refers to the scheduled payments that constitute the consideration for freedom; its plural (nujūm) is a technical term in fiqh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is transferred (majāz) from the celestial sense to the temporal portion of payment, a well-established juristic extension.
- Root: ف-س-خ (f-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To undo, annul, dissolve; to remove a thing from its place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, fasakh is the dissolution of a contract due to a supervening impediment, distinct from ṭalāq (divorce) or iqālah (mutual rescission).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical removal; metaphorical for the annulment of a legal obligation, as the contract is "uprooted" from its binding force.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text frequently employs conditional clauses (law, idhā, fa-in) with apodoses introduced by fa-, requiring careful tracking of protasis-apodosis relations to preserve the legal conditional logic.
chapters.translation:
### | Branch

If there remains of the installments an amount that cannot be reduced further in what is given, then the master has no right whatsoever to declare the slave incapable (taʿjīz). Rather, he must refer the matter to the judge, so that the judge may form his own opinion regarding it.

As for the type (jins) [of payment]: either the master is to grant a discharge (ibrāʾ) from some of the installments, or he is to return to the slave something from what he had taken from him, or from its type. If he deviates to a different type, then there are two views (wajhān). The view of prohibition is that this is an act of devotional worship (taʿabbud), understood from the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«وَآتُوهُمْ مِنْ مَالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ»} ("And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you") — and by it the installments are meant. This is analogous to His saying the Exalted: {«وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ»} ("And give its due on the day of its harvest"). The more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that this is a transaction (muʿāmalah), and thus compensation (ʿiwaḍ) may enter into it.

### Branch

If the master dies before the giving (al-ītāʾ), then it is [a debt] within his estate (tarikah). However, the text (al-naṣṣ) states that it competes (yuḍārabu) with the bequests (waṣāyā). This is problematic, because the right of a debt is to take precedence. Perhaps he meant by this the case where the amount exceeds the obligatory [minimum], and then he died. Among them (the scholars) there is one who said: The obligation of the giving is weak (ḍaʿīf), so it is transformed into a recommendation (istihbāb) upon death. And among them there is one who said: The minimum that constitutes wealth is a debt, and the excess — if we deem it obligatory — we only deem it so because it is befitting to the present state (al-ḥāl), and it is not befitting to the state after death. This is what al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him and grant him His pleasure — intended.

### The Second Issue

If he (the slave) pays the installments before their due time (qabl al-maḥall), the master is compelled to accept, for the sake of freeing the neck (fakk al-raqabah), just as he is compelled [to accept payment] in a debt for which there is a pledge (rahn). As for other deferred debts, there are two views.

Then, the master is only compelled to accept the installment if there is no harm (ḍarar) or burden (muʾnah) upon him, and if it is not a time of plunder (nahb) and raid (ghārah). If there is harm upon him, he is not obliged [to accept]. If the plunder is concurrent with the time of the contract, then there are two views regarding compulsion.

Wherever he is compelled [to accept], if he (the master) is absent, or he refuses, the judge receives it on his behalf, and the slave is freed. And the first installment is received [by the judge], even if there is no freedom in it, because it is a preparation (tamhīd) for the cause of freedom.

If he (the master) says: "I will not take it, for it is unlawful (ḥarām)," then the word is that of the mukātab (the slave), and it (the payment) must be taken, and he is freed by it. Then, he must return it to its owner if he (the slave) attributed it to an owner. If he did not attribute it, then there are two views as to whether it is seized from his hand. If we say it is not seized, then if he (the slave) contradicts himself (kadhdhaba nafsahu), the apparent [view] is that it is accepted from him, and his disposal (taṣarruf) over it reverts.

### | Branch

If the master says: "Defer for me some of the installments, and I will discharge you from some [of the rest]," then al-Muzanī — may Allah have mercy on him — has transmitted hesitation (taraddud) regarding this, and he made the issue subject to two opinions (qawlān). The locus of the two opinions is problematic, because if the master says: "When you pay in advance, I have discharged you," then this is a conditional discharge (taʿlīq al-ibrāʾ), which is invalid. And if the slave says: "Take this on the condition that you discharge me," then his payment with the condition is invalid. Perhaps the locus of hesitation is that the slave initiates the payment with the condition, so his payment is invalid. But if the master grants the discharge, and the slave renews his consent (riḍā) during the continuation of the receipt (al-qabḍ), then the receipt becomes valid. If he does not renew [consent], then do we say that his first consent was a consent in relation to the state of discharge, and that state has been realized — so is it sufficient? This admits of hesitation (taraddud).

### The Third Issue: On the Inability to Pay the Installments (taʿadhdhur al-nujūm), and It Has Five Causes

**The First:** Insolvency (iflās) at the due time. The master has the right to hasten the rescission (fasakh). If he does not hasten, then he has the right to rescind whenever he wishes; this is not [required] immediately (ʿalā al-fawr). If the mukātab requests a delay (istimhāl), he is only granted [a delay] to the extent of the time needed to bring the wealth out of the treasury (al-makhzan). If his wealth is absent (ghāʾib), then he (the master) has the right to rescind. If he (the slave) has goods (ʿurūḍ) that cannot be sold except after a period of time, then he (the master) has the right to rescind. Al-Ṣaydalānī said: He does not rescind — and this is far-fetched. And if he (the slave) is unable to pay some [of the installments], then he (the master) has the right to rescind, and the remainder goes to the master, except for what was from the zakāhs (al-zakawāt), for those are returned to their owners.

**The Second:** If he (the slave) is absent (ghāba) at the due time, then he (the master) has the right to rescind, and he does not need to refer the matter to the judge, according to the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ). If he (the master) had given him permission to travel, then he has the right to revoke [that permission], but he should not hasten the rescission until he informs him of the revocation of the permission. If he (the slave) then falls short (qaṣṣara) after that in returning and paying, then he (the master) rescinds.

**The Third:** That he (the slave) is prevented (mumtaniʿ) despite ability (maʿa al-qudrah). He (the master) has that [right of rescission], for the installments are not binding (lāzim) upon the slave; rather, the kitābah is permissible (jāʾizah) on his side. But the master has the right to rescind. The Iraqis said: The slave does not have the right to rescind, but he has the right not to pay despite ability, until the master rescinds — and this is contradictory, because if the contract is binding, then fulfillment of it should be obligatory.

**The Fourth:** If the slave becomes insane (junna), and we say [the contract] is not dissolved (lā yanfasikh) according to the more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ), then if the judge knows that he has wealth and sees his interest (maṣlaḥah) in freedom, he pays on his behalf. And if he sees that it (the wealth) would be wasted if he is freed, then he has the right not to pay on his behalf. The speech of the [Shāfiʿī] associates (al-aṣḥāb) indicates that the master acts independently in taking [the payment], for they mentioned that the receipt (al-qabḍ) from the insane slave necessitates freedom. But there is consideration (naẓar) in this, for perhaps he (the slave) would not consent to freedom and payment when he recovers — except that there is no benefit in this, for the master is able to free him in any case. So what difference is there between his taking his earnings by way of the installments or by way of slavery (al-riqq)?

**The Fifth:** Death (al-mawt). This necessitates the dissolution (infisākh) of the kitābah, even if he leaves behind sufficient [wealth to pay], because freedom after death is impossible (taʿadhdhur).

chapters.title_en: Section 609: On the Mukātab's Incapacity, the Ordering of Competing Debts, and Joint Kitābah
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع لو استسخر المكاتب شهرا وغرم له أجرة المثل فإذا حل النجم وعجز فله الفسخ وفيه وجه أنه يلزمه أن ينظره مثل مدة الإستسخار لأنه كان يتوقع اتفاق فتوح في ذلك الشهر فيعوضه بمثل تلك المدة فلعله يتحقق توقعه المسألة الرابعة في ازدحام الديون ولها صور الأولى أن يكون الدين للسيد فإذا كان له عليه دين معاملة ونجوم وفي يده ما يفي بأحدهما فلو تطوع السيد وأخذ عن النجوم عتق ودين المعاملة يبقى في ذمته وله أن يأخذ عن جهة المعاملة ويعجزه ولو أراد تعجيزه قبل أن يأخذ ماله عن جهة الدين ففيه وجهان أحدهما له ذلك لان له طلبهما جميعا ويتضمن ذلك عجزه عن بعض النجوم لا محالة والثاني لا لأنه قادر على النجوم وإنما تزول القدرة بإخلاء يده عن المال فرع لو قبض المال مطلقا وقصد السيد الدين وقصد العبد النجوم فالإعتبار بأي قصد فيه وجهان وتظهر فائدته في التحليف عند النزاع فإن القول قول من تعتمد نيته الثانية أن يكون عليه دين معاملة وأرش لأجنبي وليس عليه للسيد إلا النجوم فإن لم يحجر القاضي بعد عليه فله أن يقدم أي دين شاء وإن حجر بالتماس الغير فالنص أنه يوزع على الديون لأن كل واحد لو انفرد لاستغرق تمام حقه والذي ذهب إليه المحققون أن المقدم دين معاملة الأجنبي لأنه لا يجد متعلقا من الرقبة بخلاف الأرش والنجم ثم أرش الأجنبي يقدم على النجم لأنه يقدم على حق المالك حتى يباع فيه العبد الثالثة أن يعجز المكاتب نفسه فتسقط عنه النجوم ويبقى للأجانب الأرش ودين المعاملة وفيه ثلاثة أوجه أحدها وهو الصحيح أنه يقسم ما في يده عليهما بالسوية والثاني أنه يقدم دين المعاملة لتعلق صاحب الأرش بالرقبة والثالث وهو غريب أن يقدم الأرش ويقال لصاحب المعاملة قد قنعت بذمية فاتبعه إذا عتق وهذا يلزم طرده في الصورة الثانية وهو بعيد جدا ### | ### | التفريع إن قلنا يقدم المعاملة فلو مات المكاتب وخلف شيئا فالصحيح أنه يسوى بينه وبين الأرش إذ لم يبق طمع في الرقبة ليتعلق بها الأرش ومنهم من استصحب دين المعاملة فرعان أحدهما أن لمستحق الأرش تعجيز المكاتب حتى يفسخ الكتابة ويبيع الرقبة فلو أراد السيد فداءه لتستمر الكتابة لم يجب على المجني عليه قبوله لأنه إنما يتعلق بالرقبة بعد انفساخ الكتابة وإنما له الفداء عند التعليق وفيه وجه أنه يجب قبوله لغرض السيد في دوام الكتابة وأما صاحب دين المعاملة فليس له التعجيز على المذهب إذ ليس له طمع في الرقبة فلا فائدة له في التعجيز الفرع الثاني لو كان للسيد دين معاملة ونجم فلا يضارب الغرماء بالنجم ويضارب بدين المعاملة لأنه لا يقضي من الرقبة وفيه وجه أنه لا يضارب لأن حقه على عبده ضعيف وعرضة للسقوط المسألة الخامسة إذا كاتبا عبدا فليس للعبد أن يقضي نصيب أحدهما وحده لأن كل ما في يده كالمشترك بين السيدين لكن لو وكل أحدهما صاحبه بقبض نصيبه فإذا قبض الجميع عتق العبد ولو استبد بتسليم الجميع إلى أحدهما لم يعتق منه شيء لأن القابض لا يملك منه شيئا ما لم يملك شريكه مثله وفيه وجه أنه يعتق نصيبه إذ ليس عليه رفع اليد إلا عن النصف ولو رضي أحدهما بتقديم الآخر بنصيبه فهل يصح الأداء فيه وجهان ينبنيان على نفوذ التبرع بإذن السيد وقيل ينبني على أن كتابة أحدهما بإذن صاحبه هل تصح في نصيبه وحده لأن هذا يؤدي إلى أن يعتق البعض وتبقى الكتابة في الباقي ### | التفريع إن قضينا بفساد الأداء فهو رقيق ويسترد منه وإن قلنا صحيح فلا نقول بعتق نصيبه ويسري بل إن كان في يده وفاء أدى نصيب الثاني وعتق كله عليهما وإن عجز عن نصيب الثاني قال ابن سريج لا يشارك الأول فيما قبض بإذنه ولكن عتق على الأول نصيبه وهل يقوم عليه الباقي فيه الخلاف المذكور في سراية عتق الشريك في المكاتب وقال غيره بل يشاركه فيما قبض لأنه أذن في التقديم لا في التكميل ثم إذا شارك فلهما التعجيز بسبب الباقي ويرق العبد ### |
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To employ or press into service; to exact labor from someone against their will.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The imposition of service (taskhīr) upon a mukātab by his master, which interrupts the mukātab's earning capacity during the kitābah period.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual conscription of labor; metaphorical (majāz) — any act that depletes the mukātab's means of acquisition.
- Root: ز-ح-م (z-ḥ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Crowding, pressing together; competition for a limited space or resource.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The concurrence of multiple creditors' claims (tazāḥum al-duyūn) upon a single insolvent estate, requiring a rule of priority or proportional distribution.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical crowding; metaphorical — the juridical competition of claims where the debtor's assets are insufficient to satisfy all.
- Root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone; to compel; to make whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The juristic concept of the injured party's claim (arash) attaching to the slave's person (raqabah) as a coercive lien.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — mending; metaphorical — the legal right of recourse against the slave's body, which outranks mere pecuniary claims.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Ellipsis (Ḥadhf al-Jawā') — In "لو استسخر المكاتب شهرا... فإذا حل النجم وعجز فله الفسخ," the protasis (law) governs the entire ensuing apodosis, with the conditional particle's scope extending over the temporal clause (idhā), requiring the reader to supply the implied consequence of the master's action.
chapters.translation:
### | Subsidiary Branch

If the master conscripted the mukātab's labor for a month and paid him the equivalent wage (ujrat al-mithl), then when the installment (najm) falls due and the mukātab proves unable to pay, he has the option to rescind (faskh). There is a view that the master is obligated to grant him a deferment equal to the period of conscription, because the mukātab had been anticipating the occurrence of some windfall (futūḥ) during that month, so the master compensates him with an equivalent period — perhaps his expectation will then be realized.

### The Fourth Issue: On the Concurrence of Debts (tazāḥum al-duyūn)

This issue has several forms:

**The First Form:** That the debt be owed to the master. If the mukātab owes the master both a debt from commercial dealings (dayn muʿāmalah) and the kitābah installments (nujūm), and the mukātab possesses in his hand what suffices to pay only one of the two — then if the master voluntarily chooses to collect from the installments, the mukātab becomes free, and the commercial debt remains as an obligation in his liability (dhimmah). The master may also choose to collect from the commercial debt and thereby declare the mukātab incapacitated (taʿjīz). If the master wishes to declare him incapacitated before taking his money from the debt — there are two views:

One view: He may do so, because he has the right to demand both claims, and this necessarily entails the mukātab's incapacity with respect to some of the installments.

The second view: He may not, because the mukātab is capable of paying the installments, and capability is only removed by the master's emptying his hand of the money.

**Subsidiary Branch:** If the mukātab received the money absolutely (muṭlaqan), and the master intended it for the debt while the mukātab intended it for the installments — then which intention is given effect? There are two views. Its practical benefit appears in the administration of oaths (taḥlīf) at the time of dispute, for the statement is credited to the one whose intention is relied upon.

**The Second Form:** That the mukātab owes a commercial debt and an indemnity (arash) to a third party (ajnabī), while owing the master only the installments. If the judge has not yet placed a judicial restriction (ḥajr) upon him, the mukātab may give precedence to whichever debt he wishes. But if the judge has imposed a restriction at the request of another party, then the text (naṣṣ) holds that the assets are distributed proportionally among the debts, because each claimant, if alone, would have exhausted the entirety of his right. However, the view adopted by the verifying scholars (muḥaqqiqūn) is that the third party's commercial debt is given precedence, because it has no object of attachment in the slave's person (raqabah), unlike the indemnity and the installment. Then the third party's indemnity is given precedence over the installment, because it takes precedence even over the master's own right — to the extent that the slave may be sold to satisfy it.

**The Third Form:** That the mukātab declares his own incapacity, whereupon the installments fall away from him, but the third parties' indemnity and commercial debt remain. There are three views:

The first — which is the correct one (al-ṣaḥīḥ) — is that what is in his hand is divided equally between the two claims.

The second is that the commercial debt is given precedence, because the indemnity-holder's claim attaches to the slave's person.

The third — which is odd (gharīb) — is that the indemnity is given precedence, and it is said to the commercial creditor: "You have consented to his liability (dhimmah), so pursue him when he becomes free." This view must consistently be applied in the second form as well, and it is very far-fetched.

### | Sub-Derivation (Tafrīʿ)

If we adopt the view that the commercial debt is given precedence — then if the mukātab dies leaving behind some property, the correct view is that equality is made between the commercial debt and the indemnity, since there remains no hope in the slave's person to which the indemnity could attach. Some scholars, however, maintained the continued precedence of the commercial debt.

**Two Subsidiary Branches:**

**The First:** The indemnity-holder has the right to declare the mukātab incapacitated so as to rescind the kitābah and sell the slave's person. If the master wishes to ransom him (fidā') so that the kitābah may continue, the injured party is not obligated to accept, because the indemnity-holder's claim attaches to the person only after the rescission of the kitābah; the master's right of ransom exists only at the time of attachment (taʿlīq). There is a view that acceptance is obligatory, due to the master's interest in the continuation of the kitābah.

As for the commercial creditor, he has no right to declare incapacity on the established doctrine (al-madhhab), since he has no hope in the slave's person — thus there is no benefit to him in declaring incapacity.

**The Second Subsidiary Branch:** If the master has both a commercial debt and an installment claim, he does not compete with other creditors (lā yuḍārib) on account of the installment, but he does compete on account of the commercial debt, because the latter is not satisfied from the slave's person. There is a view that he does not compete at all, because his right against his own slave is weak and subject to being voided.

### The Fifth Issue: When Two Masters Jointly Contract Kitābah with a Slave

It is not permissible for the slave to pay the share of one of them alone, because everything in his hand is as if jointly owned between the two masters. However, if one of them deputizes the other to receive his share, and the latter then receives the entirety, the slave becomes free. But if the slave voluntarily delivers the entirety to one of them alone, nothing of him is freed, because the recipient does not own anything of him unless his partner owns the like thereof. There is a view that his share does become free, since the slave is not obligated to relinquish possession except of the half.

If one of the masters consents to the other's being given precedence with his share — does the payment thereby become valid? There are two views, which build upon whether a gratuitous act (tabarruʿ) is effective with the master's permission. It was also said that they build upon whether one master's kitābah, with the permission of his partner, is valid with respect to his share alone — because this leads to the freeing of a part while the kitābah remains with respect to the remainder.

### | Sub-Derivation (Tafrīʿ)

If we rule that the payment is invalid, then the slave remains in slavery and the payment is recovered from him. If we say it is valid, we do not say that his share is freed and that freedom then carries over (sarāyah); rather, if the slave has in his hand sufficient to pay, he pays the second master's share and is fully freed with respect to both. If he is unable to pay the second master's share, Ibn Surayj said: The second master does not share with the first in what the first received with permission, but the first master's share is freed; whether the remainder is assessed against the slave (taqwīm) involves the aforementioned dispute regarding the carry-over of a partner's manumission in the case of a mukātab. Another scholar said: Rather, the second master does share with the first in what was received, because the permission was for precedence, not for completion (takmīl). Then, when he shares, the two masters may jointly declare incapacity on account of the remaining portion, and the slave reverts to slavery.

chapters.title_en: Section 610 — Disputes Between Master and Mukātab, Joint Kitābah, and Related Branches
chapters.arabic_text: ### | فرع لو ادعى أنه وفاه النجوم فصدقه أحدهما وكذبه الآخر فله أن يشارك المصدق فيما أقر بقبضه وله أن يطالب المكاتب بتمام نصيبه إن شاء ثم لا تراجع بين المكاتب والمصدق فيما يأخذه المكذب منهما إذ موجب قولهما أن المكذب ظالم ولا يرجع المظلوم إلا على ظالم المسألة السادسة إذا كاتب عبدين فجاء أحدهما بمال ليتبرع بأداء نجوم الثاني وقلنا لا ينفذ تبرعه بالإذن فالمال للمؤدي لكن قد نص الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المؤدي لو عتق بمال آخر لم يرجع إلى ذلك المال ونص على أن المكاتب لو عفا عن أرش جناية ثبت له على سيده فإذا عتق رجع فيه فقيل قولان بالنقل والتخريج بناء على أن تصرف المفلس إذا رد للحجر فإذا انقضت ديونه فهل ينفذ بعده ولا خلاف أنه لو استرد قبل العتق ثم عتق لم يكن للسيد استرداده فإنما إنما ينفذ بعد العتق إذا لم يقبضه قبل العتق أما إذا تكفل أحد العبدين بنجوم الآخر لم يصح لأن النجوم ليس بلازم على العبد فلا يصح ضمانه ولو شرط ضمان أحدهما للآخر فسد العقد ### | فرع لو كانا متفاوتي القيمة وجاء المال ثم ادعى الخسيس أنهما أديا على عدد الرؤس وقال الآخر بل على قدر النجوم ففيه نصان مختلفان فقيل قولان أحدهما أن القول قول من يدعي الإستواء لأنه كان في يدهما وهو الصحيح والثاني القول قول الآخر لأن قرينة التفاوت في النجوم تشهد له وقيل بل المسألة على حالين فالقول قول من يدعي الإستواء إلى أن يقتضي ذلك في النجم الأخير استرداد شيء من السيد فالقول قول من ينكره المسألة السابعة في النزاع وله صور الأولى إذا اختلف السيد والمكاتب في قدر النجوم أو في جنسه أو في مقدار الأجل تحالفا وتفاسخا وإن كان بعد حصول العتق بالإتفاق وفائدة الفسخ الرجوع إلى قيمة الرقبة أما رد العتق فغير ممكن وصورته أن يقبض منه ألفين ويدعي العبد أن بعضه وديعة وقال السيد بل النجوم ألفان الثانية أن يختلفا في أصل الأداء أو في أصل الكتابة فالقول قول السيد فلو قال العبد لي بينة على الأداء أمهل ثلاثة أيام فإن أتى برجل وامرأتين قبل إلا في النجم الأخير ففيه وجهان لتعليق العتق به الثالثة لو مات المكاتب وله ولد من معتقه كان ولاؤه لموالي المعتقة فلو قال السيد عتق قبل الموت وجر إلي ولاء أولاده فالقول قول مولى الأم إنه مات قبل العتق لأن الأصل عدم القبض واستمرار الولاء الرابعة كاتب عبدين وأقر بأنه قبض نجوم أحدهما فلكل واحد أن يدعي فإن أقر لأحدهما ونكل عن يمين الآخر حتى حلف المدعي عتق هذا باليمين المردودة وعتق الأول بالإقرار وإن مات قبل البيان فللوارث أن يحلف على نفي العلم بما عناه المورث وإذا حلف استبهم فهل يقرع بينهما فيه قولان أحدهما نعم لأنه عتق استبهم والثاني لا لأنه دين استبهم من عليه ولأنه عتق عبد معين من عبدين وإنما تجري القرعة عند إعتاق العبدين جميعا وقصور الثلث عن الوفاء وإبهام العتق بينهما لكن إذا قلنا لا يقرع فللوارث أن يعجزهما ليحصل تعجيز الرق منهما وبعد ذلك يستبهم عتق بين عبدين فلا تبعد القرعة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Full and complete payment of a debt or obligation; to render in full measure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Fulfillment of a contractual duty (wafāʾ bi-l-ʿahd), particularly the payment of kitābah installments (nujūm) as a condition for emancipation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual delivery of payment; metaphorical (majāz) — completion of any obligation.
- Root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lose, to fall short, to be deficient; a lesser or inferior thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Loss (khusrān) in contractual contexts; the inferior slave (khasīs) in joint kitābah valuation disputes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — deficiency in value; metaphorical — one who suffers loss in a claim.
- Root: ق-ر-ع (q-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cast lots; drawing of arrows or lots for decision.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The procedure of casting lots (qurʿah) to resolve ambiguous entitlements, especially in emancipation cases.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical drawing of lots; metaphorical — any equitable allocation when evidence is inconclusive.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "لو ادعى" (if he claimed) introduces a hypothetical protasis requiring careful parsing of the apodosis, especially where multiple conditional clauses interact with legal consequences.
chapters.translation:
### | Branch

If he [the slave] claimed that he had paid the installments (nujūm) in full, and one of the two [masters] affirmed him while the other denied him, then he [the slave] may partner with the one who affirmed him in what he [the affirming master] acknowledged having received, and he may demand from the mukātab the remainder of his share if he wishes. Thereafter, there is no recourse (murājaʿah) between the mukātab and the affirming master regarding what the denying master takes from him, for the implication of their two statements is that the denier is an oppressor (ẓālim), and the oppressed one does not seek recourse except against the oppressor.

**The Sixth Issue:** If he made a kitābah contract with two slaves, and one of them brought wealth to voluntarily pay the installments of the second — and we hold that his voluntary payment (tabarruʿ) is not valid by mere permission — then the wealth belongs to the one who paid it. However, al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him — explicitly stated that if the payer were emancipated by other wealth, he does not revert to that [previously paid] wealth. And he explicitly stated that if the mukātab forgave the compensation for injury (arsh jīnāyah) established against his master, then when he is emancipated he may revert to it [and claim it]. It was said there are two opinions (qawlān) — by transmission (naql) and by derivation (takhrij) — based on whether the disposition of one under interdiction (muflis), when rejected due to the interdiction, becomes valid after his debts are discharged.

There is no disagreement that if he reclaimed it before emancipation, then was emancipated, the master has no right to reclaim it [again]. Rather, it only becomes effective after emancipation if he had not already received it before emancipation.

As for when one of the two slaves guarantees (takaffala) the installments of the other, this is not valid, because the installments are not a binding obligation (lāzim) upon the slave, so his guarantee (ḍamān) is not valid. And if the guarantee of one for the other were stipulated [in the contract], the contract becomes corrupted (fasada).

### | Branch

If the two [slaves] were of differing values, and the wealth came, then the inferior one (khasīs) claimed that they both paid according to the number of persons (ʿalā ʿadad al-ruʾūs), while the other said rather according to the proportion of installments (ʿalā qadr al-nujūm), then there are two differing transmitted texts (naṣṣān mukhtalifān). It was said there are two opinions: one of them is that the statement is that of the one claiming equality (al-istiwāʾ), because [the wealth] was in their joint possession — and this is the correct (al-ṣaḥīḥ) opinion. The second is that the statement is that of the other, because the indication (qarīnah) of disparity in the installments testifies for him. And it was said rather that the issue has two states: the statement is that of the one claiming equality until that requires, in the final installment, the recovery of something from the master — then the statement is that of the one who denies it.

**The Seventh Issue:** Concerning dispute (al-nizāʿ), and it has several forms:

**The First Form:** If the master and the mukātab differ over the amount of the installments, or over their type (jins), or over the length of the term (ajal), they both take oaths (taḥālafā) and rescind the contract (tafāsakhā) — even if this occurs after emancipation has been established by mutual agreement. And the benefit of the rescission is the return to the value of the slave's person (qīmat al-raqabah). As for reversing the emancipation, that is impossible. Its example is: he [the master] received two thousand from him, and the slave claims that part of it was a deposit (wadīʿah), while the master says rather the installments were two thousand.

**The Second Form:** If they differ over the very fact of payment (aṣl al-adāʾ) or over the very fact of the kitābah contract (aṣl al-kitābah), then the statement is that of the master. If the slave says, "I have a witness (bayyinah) for the payment," he is granted a respite of three days. If he brings a man and two women, it is accepted — except in the final installment, where there are two aspects (wajhān), because emancipation is attached to it.

**The Third Form:** If the mukātab dies and has a child from a woman who is herself a mukātabah (muʿtiqah), then his walāʾ (clientage) belongs to the patrons (mawālī) of the mother. If the master says, "He was emancipated before death, and the walāʾ of his children is drawn to me," then the statement is that of the mother's patron (mawlā al-umm) that he died before emancipation, because the default (al-aṣl) is the non-receipt [of payment] and the continuation of the walāʾ.

**The Fourth Form:** He made a kitābah contract with two slaves and acknowledged that he received the installments of one of them. Then each of them may make a claim. If he acknowledged for one of them, and refused to take the oath (nakala) regarding the other until the claimant took the oath, then this one is emancipated by the returned oath (al-yamīn al-mardūdah), and the first is emancipated by the acknowledgment (al-iqrār). And if he [the master] dies before clarification, then the heir (al-wārith) may take an oath denying knowledge of what the deceased intended. When he takes the oath, the matter remains ambiguous (istabhama). Then, is lots cast (qurʿah) between them? There are two opinions:

One of them: Yes, because it is an emancipation that has become ambiguous.

The second: No, because it is a debt (dayn) that has become ambiguous as to who owes it, and because it is the emancipation of a specific slave from two slaves — and lots are only cast when both slaves are emancipated together and the third [of the estate] falls short of full payment, and the emancipation is ambiguous between them.

But if we say that lots are not cast, then the heir may declare both of them incapable (yuʿajjizuhumā) so that the declaration of incapacity (taʿjīz) of both is achieved. After that, the emancipation becomes ambiguous between two slaves, and then casting lots is not far-fetched.

chapters.title_en: The Third Ruling: The Legal Dispositions of the Master and the Mukātab
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الحكم الثالث حكم التصرفات

أما تصرفات السيد ففيها خمس مسائل
الأولى بيع المكاتب كتابة فاسدة صحيح وهو رجوع وإن كانت الكتابة صحيحة
فهو باطل على القول الجديد لأن العبد استحق عتقا عليه وفي بيع العبد نقل
الولاء إلى غيره والقول القديم أنه يصح ويكون مكاتبا على المشتري إن أدى
إليه النجوم عتق وله الولاء وإن عجز رق له
الثانية بيع نجوم الكتابة باطل لأن ضمانه أيضا باطل لعدم لزومه وفي
الإستبدال عنه وجهان وخرج ابن  سريج قولا أنه يصح بيعه
ثم إذا منعنا بيعه فقبض المشتري النجوم لم يعتق ويرد على المكاتب وفيه
وجه أنه يعتق لأنه مأذون في القبض من البائع فكأنه وكيله فعلى هذا ترد
النجوم على السيد إذا عتق عليه
الثالثة للسيد معاملته بالبيع والشراء ويأخذ الشفعة منه ويأخذ هو من
السيد ويلتزم كل واحد الأرش عند الجناية على صاحبه فلو ثبت له على السيد
دين مثل النجوم في قدره وجنسه عتق حيث نوى وقوع التقاص وفي أصل التقاص عند
تساوي الدينين أربعة أقوال
أحدها أنه لا يقع مع الرضا لإنه إبدال دين بدين
والثاني يقع إن رضينا جميعا وكأنه يشبه الحوالة
والثالث أنه يقع إن رضي أحدهما كما يجبر أحد الشريكين على القسمة عند طلب
أحدهما
والرابع أنه يقع التقاص لأن طلبه منه إذا كان هو مطالبا بمثله عنت ولعله
الأصح وقال صاحب التقريب إن أجرينا التقاص في النقدين ففي ذوات الأمثال
وجهان فإن أجرينا ففي العروض المتساوية وجهان ولا شك في أنه لا يجوز
التقاص بين المكسر والصحيح والحال والمؤجل
الرابعة لو أوصى برقبة المكاتب لم يصح وإن عجز إلا أن يضيف إلى العجز
فيقول إن عجز فقد أوصيت به لفلان ففيه وجهان مرتبان على ما لو قال إن ملكت
ذلك العبد فقد أوصيت به لفلان وهذا أولى بالصحة لقيام أصل الملك
ولو أوصى بالنجوم لإنسان جاز فيما يخرج من الثلث فإن عجز فللوارث التعجيز
وإن أنظر الموصى له وحيث تصح الوصية برقبته إذا عجز فللموصى له تعجيزه وإن
أنظر الوارث وإنما يتعاطى القاضي تعجيزه إذا تحقق ذلك عنده
الخامسة إذا قال ضعوا عن المكاتب أكثر ما عليه ومثل نصفه والنجوم ثمانية
مثلا فيوضع لأجل الأكثر أربع وشيء ولقوله مثل نصفه نصف الأربعة والشيء
فيجوز أن يبقى عليه درهمان إلا شيئين
ولو قال ضعوا عنه ما شاء فشاء الكل لم يوضع بل لا بد من إبقاء شيء وإن قل
وفيه وجه أنه يوضع الكل بخلاف ما لو قال ضعوا من  نجومه ما شاء فإن من تقتضي
التبعيض
أما تصرفات المكاتب فهو فيه كالحر إلا ما فيه تبرع أو خطر فوات
أما التبرع كالهبة والعتق والشراء بالعين والبيع بالمحاباة والضيافة
والتوسع في المطاعم والملابس
وأما الخطر فهو كالبيع بالنسيئة وإن استوثق بالرهن فإنه لا يدري عاقبته
وقد يجوز مثل ذلك في مال الطفل بالمصلحة ولكن ها هنا لا تطلب مصلحة المكاتب
بل مصلحة العتق واليد ولذلك لا ترفع يد السيد عن المبيع قبل قبض الثمن ولا
يهب بثواب مجهول ولا يكاتب ولا يتزوج لأنه يتعرض للنفقة والمهر ولا يتسرى
إذ تتعرض الجارية للهلاك بالطلق
ولا يشتري من يعتق عليه ولا يتهب أيضا من يعتق عليه إلا إذا كان كسوبا لا
تجب نفقته
وأما إقراره فيقبل كالمريض وكل ما منع إذا استقل فلو أذن فيه السيد
فقولان
أحدهما الجواز لأن الحق لا يعدوهما
والثاني المنع لأن حق العتق ملحوظ أيضا وإذن السيد لا أثر له وقد استقل
المكاتب بنفسه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ص-ر-ف (taṣarruf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To manage, conduct, or execute an affair with authority; turning something about in one's control.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Juridical acts of disposition (taṣarrufāt) that produce legal effects, whether valid (ṣaḥīḥ) or void (bāṭil), contingent upon capacity (ahlīyah) and authority (wilāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of "turning" (taṣrīf) a thing; metaphorically extended to legal acts that "turn" rights or obligations from one party to another.
- Root: ك-ت-ب (kataba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To write; the kitābah contract is a written manumission agreement, hence "the writing" (al-kitābah) as a technical term.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The contract of manumission by installments (mukātabah), wherein the slave purchases his freedom by paying a stipulated sum (nujūm, lit. "stars" = installments).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "writing"; metaphorical for the binding written covenant between master and slave.
- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿitaq)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become free, to be released from bondage; root denotes nobility and liberation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Manumission (iʿtāq) as a legal act effecting the slave's freedom, a primary goal (maqṣad) of the Sharīʿah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal release from physical servitude; metaphorical for spiritual liberation from sin.
- Root: و-ل-ي (walā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Proximity, guardianship, patronage; the bond of clientage (walā') established between the manumitter and the freed slave.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The right of inheritance and allegiance (walā' al-ʿitāq) that transfers to the manumitter, a legal consequence of freeing a slave.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "nearness"; metaphorical for the legal bond of patronage that "attaches" the freed slave to his liberator.
- Root: ق-ب-ض (qabaḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To take, seize, or receive possession of something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal taking of possession (qabḍ) as a condition for the transfer of ownership in sales and debts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical grasping; metaphorical for legal receipt of payment or goods.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnā') — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if he pays the installments, he is freed") and exceptive phrases (e.g., "except what involves gratuitousness or risk"), requiring precise parsing to distinguish the protasis (condition) from the apodosis (result) and to identify the scope of exceptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the legal dispositions of the master [over the mukātab], there are five issues therein.

The first: The sale of a mukātab under a corrupt kitābah (kitābah fāsidah) is valid, and it constitutes a revocation [of the kitābah]. But if the kitābah is valid, then [the sale] is void according to the new opinion (al-qawl al-jadīd), because the slave has become entitled to manumission (ʿitq) against him [the master], and in selling the slave, the transfer of the walā' to another [party] occurs. The old opinion (al-qawl al-qadīm) holds that it is valid, and he becomes a mukātab to the purchaser: if he pays him the installments (nujūm), he is freed and the walā' belongs to him [the purchaser]; but if he fails [to pay], he becomes his slave.

The second: The sale of the installments of the kitābah is void, because the guarantee (ḍamān) of them is also void, due to their non-binding nature (ʿadam luzūmihi). Regarding substituting for them [with another contract], there are two opinions (wajhān). Ibn Surayj derived an opinion (qawl) that its sale is valid.

Then, if we prohibit its sale, and the purchaser takes possession (qabaḍa) of the installments, the mukātab does not become free, and [the installments] are returned to the mukātab. There is an opinion that he does become free, because he [the mukātab] is authorized to receive payment from the seller, as if he were his agent (wakīl). On this basis, the installments are returned to the master if he [the mukātab] is freed upon him.

The third: The master may transact with him [the mukātab] in buying and selling, and he [the master] may take preemption (shufʿah) from him, and he [the mukātab] may take it from the master. Each one is liable for the diminution in value (arsh) upon an injury (jināyah) inflicted on the other. So if a debt is established for him [the mukātab] against the master, similar to the installments in amount and type, he becomes free if he intends the occurrence of set-off (taqāṣ). Regarding the principle of set-off when the two debts are equal, there are four opinions (aqwāl):

One: It does not occur even with mutual consent, because it is an exchange of a debt for a debt.
The second: It occurs if we all consent, and it resembles a transfer of debt (ḥiwālah).
The third: It occurs if one of them consents, just as one of two partners is compelled to partition (qasmah) upon the request of the other.
The fourth: It occurs, because his claim against him, when he [the other] is claiming the like from him, is an act of oppression (ʿanat), and perhaps this is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ). The author of al-Taqrīb said: If we apply set-off in the case of the two monetary metals (naqdayn), then regarding fungible items (dhawāt al-amthāl) there are two opinions. If we apply it [there], then regarding equivalent commodities (al-ʿurūḍ al-mutasāwiyah) there are two opinions. There is no doubt that set-off is not permissible between broken and whole [currency], nor between immediate and deferred [debts].

The fourth: If he bequeaths the corpus (raqabah) of the mukātab, it is not valid, even if he [the mukātab] becomes incapacitated (ʿajaza), unless he attaches [the bequest] to the incapacity, saying: "If he becomes incapacitated, I have bequeathed him to so-and-so." There are two opinions (wajhān) therein, arranged upon [the case of] one who says: "If I come to own that slave, I have bequeathed him to so-and-so." And this [latter] is more deserving of validity, due to the establishment of the basis of ownership.

And if he bequeaths the installments to a person, it is permissible with respect to what exits from the one-third [of the estate]. Then if he [the mukātab] becomes incapacitated, the heir may declare his incapacity (taʿjīz). And if the legatee grants him a delay, then wherever the bequest of his corpus is valid upon his incapacity, the legatee may declare his incapacity, even if the heir grants him a delay. The judge (qāḍī) only undertakes the declaration of his incapacity when that is verified before him.

The fifth: If he says: "Remit from the mukātab more than what is upon him, and the like of half of it," and the installments are, for example, eight [dirhams], then for the sake of "more" (al-akthar), four and something (shay') are remitted, and for his saying "the like of half of it," half of the four and the something [is remitted]. Thus it is permissible that there remain upon him two dirhams minus two somethings (illā shay'ayn).

And if he says: "Remit from him whatever you wish," and he [the agent] wishes the entirety, it is not remitted; rather, it is necessary to leave something, however little. There is an opinion that the entirety is remitted, unlike the case where he says: "Remit from his installments whatever you wish," for "from" (min) necessitates partiality (tabʿīḍ).

As for the legal dispositions of the mukātab, he is therein like a free man, except what involves gratuitousness (tabarruʿ) or the risk (khaṭar) of loss.

As for gratuitousness, it is like gift (hibah), manumission (ʿitq), purchase with ready cash (al-ʿayn), sale with favoritism (muḥābāh), hospitality (ḍiyāfah), and extravagance in foods and garments.

As for risk, it is like credit sale (al-bayʿ bi al-nasī'ah), even if he secures it with a pledge (rahn), for he does not know its outcome. Such [transactions] may be permitted in the wealth of a minor for the sake of benefit (maṣlaḥah), but here the benefit of the mukātab is not sought; rather, the benefit of manumission and [the preservation of] the hand [of ownership]. For this reason, the master's hand is not lifted from the sold item before receipt of the price, nor does he [the mukātab] give a gift for an unknown recompense (thawāb majhūl), nor does he enter into a kitābah [with his own slave], nor marry, because he exposes himself to the expenditure [of maintenance] and the dowry (mahr), nor does he take a concubine (tasarrā), because the slave-girl is exposed to destruction through childbirth (ṭalaq).

Nor does he purchase one whose manumission would be incumbent upon him (man yaʿtiq ʿalayhi), nor does he accept as a gift one whose manumission would be incumbent upon him, unless he [the latter] is a wage-earner (kasūb) whose maintenance is not obligatory [upon the mukātab].

As for his acknowledgment (iqrār), it is accepted like [that of] the sick person (al-marīḍ). And everything that is prohibited [to him] when he acts independently (istaqalla), if the master grants permission for it, there are two opinions (qawlān):

One: It is permissible, because the right does not go beyond the two of them.
The second: It is prohibited, because the right of manumission is also considered, and the master's permission has no effect, for the mukātab acts independently with respect to himself.

chapters.title_en: Section 612 — Subsidiary Branches on the Mukātab (Contract Slave)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فروع

الأول نكاحه بإذنه فيه القولان وقيل إنه يصح قولا واحدا لأنه من حاجته
وهو ضعيف إذ لو كان كذلك لاستقل به ولجاز التسري ولأن للكتابة آخرا فإن
الصبر إليه ممكن
الثاني في تزويج المكاتبة طريقان
أحدهما التخريج على القولين
والثاني الجواز قطعا إذ تستحق المه روالنفقة ولا يلزمها تسليم نفسها
نهارا بل تكتسب كالأمة لا كالحرة وقيل إنه لا يجوز قولا واحدا وهو ضعيف
الثالث ذكر العراقيون في مسافرة المكاتب دون الإذن وجهين ثم منهم من طرد
في كل سفر ومنهم من خصص بالسفر الطويل وقال هو انسلال عن لحاظ السيد
بالكلية
الرابع لو وهب من السيد شيئا خرج على القولين وقيل يصح قطعا كما يعجل
النجم الأول إليه ولا يعجل الدين إلى غيره
الخامس لو اتهب المكاتب نصف من يعتق عليه فكاتب عليه حتى يعتق بعتقه ويرق
برقه فإن عتق فعتق النصف قال ابن الحداد يقوم عليه الباقي إن كان موسرا عند
العتق لأنه مختار فيه وقال القفال لا يسري لأنه  لم يسر عند حصول الملك فلا
يسري بعده وهو الأصح
السادس لو اشترى من يعتق على سيده صح ثم إن عجز وانقلب إلى السيد عتق
عليه ولو اتهب العبد القن دون إذن السيد ففيه وجهان فإن جوزنا فاتهب من
يعتق عليه وهو غير كسوب لم يجز إلا بالإذن لأجل النفقة
وإذا اتهب نصف قريبه ففي وجه يصح ولا يسر وفي وجه لا يصح حذرا من السراية
وفي وجه يصح ويسري لأن اختيار العبد كاختياره
ثم إذا صححنا قبول العبد فهل للسيد رده فيه وجهان فإن قلنا له رده فهو
دفع لأصل الملك أو قطع من حين الرد فيه وجهان
السابع إعتاق المكاتب عبده بإذن سيده فيه طريقان
أحدهما التخريج على القولين
والثاني القطع بالمنع لما نذكره من إشكال الولاء
فإن قلنا ينفذ ففي الولاء قولان
أحدهما أنه للسيد لأن المكاتب رقيق وفائدة الولاء الميراث والتزويج وتحمل
العقل وكل ذلك ينافيه الرق
والثاني أنه موقوف فإن عتق المكاتب يوما ما فهو له وإن مات رقيقا فهو
للسيد
فعلى هذا لو مات المعتق بل موت المكاتب وعتقه وهو في مدة التوقف ففي
ميراثه وجهان
أحدهما يوقف حتى يتبين أمر الولاء فيصرف إلى من يستقر عليه من السيد أو
من المكاتب
والثاني أنه لبيت المال لأن ما يتبين من بعد لا يسند الولاء إلى ما مضى
فإن قلنا يثبت الولاء للسيد في الحال فإذا عتق المكاتب فهل ينجر إليه فيه
وجهان

### | فرع

كتابة المكاتب عبده كإعتاقه فإن قلنا ينفذ فلو عتق والعبد الأول رقيق بعد
ففي ولائه القولان المذكوران في الإعتاق
الثامن ليس للمكاتب أن يكفر إلا بالصوم فإن أذن السيد في الإطعام فعلى
القولين وقيل يجوز إذا قلنا إن القن لا يملك والمكاتب أيضا لا يملك وإنما
تصرفه بحكم الضرورة فلا يصح التكفير بالمال وهو ضعيف بل الصحيح أن المكاتب
يملك
التاسع إذا استولد المكاتب جارية فولده مكاتب عليه وهل يثبت للأم علقة
أمية الولد حتى تصير مستولدة إذا عتق فيه قولان  والأصح أنه لا يثبت لأنها
علقت بولد رقيق

### | الحكم الرابع حكم ولد المكاتبة إذا كان من نكاح أو زنا

وفيه قولان كما في سراية التدبير إلا أن ولد المدبرة لا يعتق بإعتاق الأم
وهذا يعتق لأن أمة تعتق عن جهة الكتابة إذا عتقت ولذلك يستتبع الولد
فإن قلنا يسري فلحق الملك في الولد للسيد أو المكاتبة فيه قولان
أحدهما أنه للسيد كالأم
والثاني أنه للأم لأنه من كسبها
ويتفرع على هذا النفقة والكسب ولا شك أنه ينفق عليه من كسبه والفاضل منه
يصرف إلى الأم إن قلنا لها الحق وإن قلنا للسيد لم يصرف إليه لأنه كسب
مكاتبة فيوقف فإن عتق الولد تعتق الأم فالكسب له وإن رق سلم للسيد وفيه وجه
أنه يصرف في الحال إلى السيد
فإن قلنا الكسب للأم فعليها نفقته إذا لم يكن كسب وإن قلنا موقوف للسيد
فهي على السيد وقيل إنه على بيت المال لأنه يتضرر إن توقفنا في الكسب إذ
يطالبه بالنفقة وكذلك إعتاق السيد ينفذ إن قلنا له حق الملك وإن قلنا للأم
فلا كما لا ينفذ في عبد مكاتبه
وأما أرش الجناية عليه فهو كالكسب إلا أن يكون على روحه فإنه لا يمكن
التوقف لانتظار العتق ففيه قولان
أحدهما أنه للسيد
والآخر أنه للأم
أما ولد المكاتب من جاريته فهو ككسب المكاتب فلا يتصرف السيد فيه لكن لو
جنى
الولد لم يكن للمكاتب أن يفديه لأنه لا يتصرف فيه بالبيع ويتصرف في مال
الفداء وفيه ضرر وفداؤه كشرائه
إذا وطىء السيد المكاتبة فلا حد ولكن عصى ووجب المهر للشبهة فإن أحبلها
وولدت وهي مكاتبة بعد فعليه قيمة الولد لها إن قلنا إن بدل ولدها القتيل
يصرف إليها
ثم هي مستولدة ومكاتبة فإن عتقت بأداء النجوم فذاك وإلا بقيت مستولدة
فتعتق بموت السيد ومهما أتت بالولد بعد العجز أو بعد العتق فليس لها قيمة
الولد قولا واحدا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To write, to prescribe, to record; kitābah as a written contract of manumission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The contractual bond (ʿaqd) by which a slave purchases his freedom through agreed installments (nujūm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the written deed; metaphorical (majāz) — the legal status of the mukātab as a hybrid between free and slave.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — governing the apodosis of hypothetical rulings (e.g., "if he is incapacitated... then..."), requiring precise temporal sequencing.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first branch — his (the mukātab's) marriage without the master's permission: therein are the two opinions (qawlān). It was said that it is valid by unanimous agreement because it is among his necessities. But this is weak, for if that were so, he would be independent in it, and concubinage (tasarrī) would likewise be permitted. Moreover, the kitābah has an end, for patience until it is possible is feasible.

The second branch — concerning the marriage of the mukātabah (female contract slave): there are two paths (ṭarīqān). One of them is the derivation (takhrīj) from the two opinions. The second is that it is valid categorically, since she is entitled to the dower (mahr) and maintenance (nafaqah), and she is not obliged to surrender herself during the day; rather, she earns like a slave-woman (amah), not like a free woman. It was said that it is invalid by unanimous agreement, and this is weak.

The third branch — the Iraqis mentioned two aspects (wajhayn) regarding the mukātab's traveling without permission. Then among them, some applied this to every journey, and some restricted it to the long journey, saying it is a complete withdrawal from the master's oversight.

The fourth branch — if something is gifted (wahab) to the mukātab from the master, it is derived from the two opinions. It was said that it is valid categorically, just as the first installment (najm) is advanced to him, whereas a debt is not advanced to other than him.

The fifth branch — if the mukātab is gifted half of a relative who would be manumitted by him (man yaʿtiq ʿalayh), and he contracts kitābah with him so that he is freed by his (the mukātab's) freedom and enslaved by his enslavement — then if he (the mukātab) is freed, the half is freed. Ibn al-Ḥaddād said: the remainder is assessed against him (the mukātab) if he is wealthy at the time of freedom, because he is free in his choice. Al-Qaffāl said: it does not carry over (lā yasrī), because it did not carry over at the moment of acquiring ownership, so it does not carry over afterward — and this is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ).

The sixth branch — if he purchases one who would be manumitted by his master, it is valid. Then if he is incapacitated and reverts to the master, he is manumitted by him. And if the mere slave (al-ʿabd al-qinn) is gifted one who would be manumitted by him without the master's permission, there are two aspects therein. If we permit it, then if he is gifted one who would be manumitted by him while he is not a wage-earner (ghayr kasūb), it is not valid except with permission, due to maintenance. And if he is gifted half of his relative, there is one aspect that it is valid and does not carry over, one aspect that it is invalid out of caution against the carry-over (sarāyah), and one aspect that it is valid and carries over, because the slave's choice is like his (the free man's) choice. Then, if we validate the slave's acceptance, does the master have the right to reject it? There are two aspects.
